/hostile_groups/0/adaptation.en:
Over a short span they learn the positions of fences and the sealing hours, but that memory is not treated as a genetic change.

Across many generations nocturnal activity and avoidance of people can be selected, but heavy capture removes the bold individuals first and causes a reverse selection in which the more secretive individuals remain.

The more secretive they become, the longer the search for a feeding ground takes, and the growth rate of the young falls.

/hostile_groups/0/bestiary/command_scope.en: The iron-plate line's absolute command holds only inside the resonance range of the metal and venom variant bloodlines, and does not direct the whole of the sow family groups. With its hooves it reads the sluice's low frequency layered over the smells of scraps and disinfectant, and it cannot decipher a distant heat source or electronic noise. When the central female disappears, the group sniffs the young's scent for about 48 hours and then scatters by family, and the great boar's call does not fill that gap.

/hostile_groups/0/bestiary/common_ecolog.en: Outside the Water Compact of the western Han River, family groups split by sow live scattered across the wetlands and the waste slopes. Their food is organic scraps, salt, and shallow-rooted crops, and they have learned to approach in the gaps when the sealing hours and the sluice vibration stop. An adult female opens the move and a subadult checks the front, and a lone male does not follow that decision even when he uses the same feeding ground.

/hostile_groups/0/bestiary/variant_relat.en: An ordinary flood boar does not leave the family-group ecology even when it wraps its back in a mud bath and a salt crust. The iron-plate, fused-plate, and venom-tusk lines are mutants split off by deep sewer contamination, and a low-frequency call binds only that bloodline. The Mud Iron Wall and the Steel Wetland are places where family labor has piled up, not the body of the great boar itself.

/hostile_groups/0/combat_counterplay.en:
Noise screens and flares push back only the scouts, and the main body is turned by a feeding detour, by moving the salt pools, and by path fencing.

On days of heavy rain and wind the error in H01's infrared observation grows, so a human scout party confirms the escape route first.

Culling by firearm scatters the remaining band into the alleys and increases harm to citizens, so under the operating rules it is limited to a last resort.

The measure of success is not carcasses but the number of intrusions into the collection yard and the time until passage over the sluice resumes.

/hostile_groups/0/dossier_prose.en:
After the water of the western Han River split the embankment from the green axis, a different order of night settled on the wetland outside the Water Compact.

Wild-boar family groups that came down the Bukhansan and Anyangcheon corridors crossed the broken green space of Yeouido and Yeongdeungpo and stayed at the scrap-recovery yards and the waste slopes, and they took the salt to last the winter from the pile of cooling waste sealed by the Yeouido Computing House (HC01).

Residents call them the Flood-Boar Swarm: the ones that come down after a flood as far as the semi-basement alleys and root through trash bags and shallow-rooted crops.

Urban appearances, changes in food sources, and severed movement routes can be explained by real observation of wild animals, but the behavior of remembering the sealing hours and the sluice operating cycle and timing an approach to them, and the management relation with HC01, are a fictional order that holds only in this region after the collapse.

The territory of the Flood-Boar Swarm is set by a continuity of water level and smell rather than by a line drawn on a map.

The core habitat is the wetland and the waste slope outside the Water Compact sluice, and in the dry season and in winter they move along the cut green space toward the Republic of Korea Government at the center of Seoul Station, and along the axis of leftovers from the night markets.

When a refugee column is pushed in from the Imjin River Gate Theater (XT01), the scrap traces left on the northwestern roads become a new corridor.

When the flood level crosses the warning line, the lowland family groups climb the high-ground stairs all at once and overlap the human passage.

This movement is a choice that looks for food and dry ground together, not an advance meant to attack the city, but for semi-basement residents and sluice workers that difference is not easily felt.

The economy they depend on is made of organic scraps, salt, and shallow-rooted crops.

Soft plastic and pools of cooling water also become auxiliary resources, and the dung left after feeding feeds the wetland microbial film and the downstream vegetation and makes a feeding ground again.

When HC01 delays the sealing of the recovery trough, family groups crowd one point, and when the seal is strengthened too far the band turns toward the household alleys.

Unsanctioned hunting for meat and hide leaves immediate food and trade goods, but it scatters the surviving individuals and distorts even the passage-safety record.

In that a measure meant to protect the citizen ration can increase scrap raiding in the vulnerable alleys, the cost of this ecology always moves to someone else's door.

Before the monsoon rains, each sow with young has a family group that scatters and checks the feeding grounds and the escape routes.

Right after a flood they join the high-ground scrap axis for a while, but they do not become one giant band.

When an adult female starts the move, the subadults scout ahead, and a lone male does not follow that decision even when he uses the same feeding ground.

When the central female disappears, the family group spends about 48 hours sweeping the same zone over and over along the scent of the young and the sow, and then scatters.

A family group splits only when the survival rate of the young is high for two seasons in a row, and when the winter salt sources and the mud baths run short they choose long-distance movement over breeding.

The positions of fences and the sealing hours of the moment can be learned, but that is not at once a long-term change of the body.

Across many generations nocturnal activity and avoidance of people can remain, and heavy capture removes the bold individuals first and produces the reverse effect of leaving only the more secretive line.

But the more secretive they become, the longer the time spent finding food grows, and the growth of the young slows as well.

The Flood-Boar Swarm reads, through hooves and ground, the low-frequency vibration of sluice opening and closing and of vehicle generators, and judges by layering the smells of scraps, people, and disinfectant.

At close range they also react to warmth carried on the wind and to the flow of air, but they cannot divide a distant heat source accurately or make out the meaning of electronic noise.

Hannuri (H01) only compares and marks the infrared masses that look like people, generators, and family groups, and is not the final judge.

When rain, wind, and cooling fog are heavy, the thermal image smears and a lone male and a subadult look like one cluster, so a human scout party has to confirm the escape route and the traces of the young first.

If the family group is mistaken for a single hostile body and the central female is removed, two days of searching behavior that is hard to predict remain in the place of the order that vanished.

The crisis grows in three stages.

At first only the night tracks increase at the collection yard outside the sluice and on the unsanctioned fields, and contact with people is rare.

Next the drains, the sealing tape, and the water-supply inspection passages are damaged, and scrap convoys and sluice maintenance are delayed.

At the last, the flood level and the refugees' leftovers overlap and the family groups take the sluice stairs.

Noise screens and flares can turn back the leading scout individuals for a while, but against the main body a feeding detour, a relocated salt pool, and path fencing are more effective.

Removal led by firearms scatters the family groups into every alley and increases harm to citizens, so it remains only as a last resort.

The result of a response is judged not by the number of carcasses but by the number of intrusions into the collection yard, the time until passage resumes, and the decrease in alley damage.

G01-SC1, "The First Hoof Outside the Sluice," begins the day before the monsoon forecast, when sow and young tracks appear at the Water Compact collection yard.

The family group remembers the sealing hours and approaches in the gap when the sluice vibration stops.

The Water Compact and HC01 can delay night operation and avoid contact, but the citizen ration is delayed along with it.

Opening a wetland detour with a scent lure costs labor and resources at once, but it can build a long-term movement axis.

The choice of capturing only the sow looks the fastest, but it makes H01 record, for the 48 hours after, a heat source that approaches again and again looking for the young.

The judgment at that point is the work of putting people's mealtimes and the survival time of a family group with young on the same table.

In G01-SC2, "The Price of the Salt Pool," after HC01 brings the cooling-waste recovery forward, the band shifts its feeding ground to the semi-basement alleys toward the center of Seoul Station.

It comes out that removing the salt source does not make the family groups disappear; it pushes them into a more dangerous lived-in quarter.

Leaving a managed pool in the wetland means accepting a continuing cost of watch in exchange for holding the danger in one place.

Prioritizing alley scrap recovery reduces harm to residents, but other ration and maintenance labor is emptied.

Lowering the density with a hunting permit makes the short-term result clear, but it strengthens the surviving individuals' learned avoidance of people and their night intrusions.

Whatever the choice, there is no avoiding the responsibility for whether to leave a controlled danger in a safe zone or to pass the burden on to a vulnerable zone that is less visible.

G01-SC3, "Right of Passage on the Flood Line," opens when the leftovers of the XT01 refugee column and the risen flood level gather people and family groups on the same sluice stairs.

Splitting the evacuation times reduces direct collision, but the people in the later turns have to endure water and darkness longer.

Turning the leftover convoy into a lure corridor can draw the band toward the wetland, but it consumes HC01's transport resources and sealed containers.

Opening the sluice first to make a short high water may induce the move quickly, but it can flood the downstream works preemptively.

So the agreement that HC01 mediates binds together the scrap sealing hours, the night passage window, the cultivation buffer strip, and a separate recovery of the XT01 leftovers.

Extermination is not the goal, and choosing coexistence does not make the threat reports disappear completely.

In their place, wetland purification, downstream vegetation, and the sluice workers' movement lines can be kept.

Negotiation with the Flood-Boar Swarm is close to a contract that limits human desire and convenience so the two timetables do not overlap, not a promise that tames the wild.

Long-term management depends on a joint patrol in which S01, HC01, and the semi-basement residents reset the boundary between food and passage every season.

Before the monsoon rains they record the tracks by sow and the mud baths without markers, and after a flood they adjust the hours of night scrap discharge and the position of the managed salt pools so the family groups do not lose the escape route they know.

The core indicators are the number of alley intrusions per hundred nights, the time taken to clear the sluice stairs, the share of traces accompanied by young, the area of rooted-up ground, and the human encounter distance by corridor, and the number of carcasses is kept only as an auxiliary record.

Even if intrusions fall, when the traces of the young drop sharply or the encounter distance shortens, it is judged not as stability but as capture pressure and a shortage of food.

When a collapsed fence or a mistaken capture has scattered the family groups, pursuit and night collection stop for 48 hours, water and salt are placed in a dispersed pattern in the direction where the old dung and tracks remain, and then the passage window is restored in stages.

Whether recovery has happened is confirmed not by the return of the central female but by whether the young pass the same corridor two times in a row and the alley re-intrusions decrease.

If this procedure is kept for a long time, residents too come to put scraps out at the set hour, which can reduce the rats' food source and the damage to underground wiring.

But if hoof disturbance concentrates on a predictable corridor, the reed belt thins and the floating trash of the next flood is driven faster into the sluice intake, a second cost, so even a safe coexistence zone has to be rested every few years and the detour wetlands opened in turn.

/hostile_groups/0/economy.en:
The main resources are organic scraps, salt, and shallow-rooted crops, and as secondary resources they use the soft plastic of flood debris and the pools of cooling water.

When the HC01 recovery trough delays the scrap-sealing cycle, the band's density rises, and when the seal is drawn too tight the band diverts to household-alley scraps.

The energy cycle runs from feeding to dung to the wetland microbial film, and unsanctioned hunting for meat and hide, instead of a short-term gain, makes the remaining band more aggressive.

/hostile_groups/0/escalation.en:
Stage 1, warning appearance: night tracks increase at the collection yard outside the sluice and on unsanctioned fields, but they do not meet people.

Stage 2, infrastructure disturbance: drains, sealing tape, and the water-supply inspection passages are damaged, and scrap convoys are delayed.

Stage 3, flood-line collision: the rising flood level overlaps refugee leftovers, and family groups occupy the sluice stairs.

At that point a response that is nothing but removal by force scatters the band into the alleys, so only a division of time and a feeding corridor work.

/hostile_groups/0/fictional_origin.en:
Right after the collapse, a flood on the western Han River cut the green axis outside the Yeouido and Yeongdeungpo sluices, and wild-boar bands that came down the Bukhansan and Anyangcheon corridors settled at the scrap-recovery yards on the edge of the Water Compact.

The real-world sources support only the basic ecology of urban appearances, food sources, and blocked movement. The behavior of learning the sealing hours, and the relation with HC01, are fiction.

When the pile of cooling waste sealed by the Yeouido Computing House (HC01) came to be used as a winter salt source, the local name Flood-Boar Swarm stuck.

/hostile_groups/0/hierarchy.en:
One adult female with young starts the move first, and the subadults scout the feeding ground and the escape route ahead.

Lone males overlap the band only loosely and do not follow the decision to move.

H01 marks the central individual of a family group and the lone males as separate heat-source clusters, and when the central female disappears the group tracks the young's scent for 48 hours and then disperses by family.

/hostile_groups/0/lifecycle.en:
Before the monsoon rains, family groups split by sow scatter and scout the feeding grounds, and right after a flood they join the high-ground scrap axis for a time.

A family group splits only when the survival rate of the young stays high for two seasons in a row, and when the winter salt sources and the mud baths shrink they choose long-distance movement over breeding.

/hostile_groups/0/modern_anxiety.en: The anxiety of wild-boar bands coming down after a flood into the lowland scrap yards and the semi-basement alleys, competing with people over refuse and crops

/hostile_groups/0/moral_cost.en:
Indiscriminate removal collapses wetland purification and downstream vegetation together, and putting scrap sealing ahead of the citizen ration increases alley raiding.

The moment a hunting gain is taken, the passage-safety data is distorted.

Choosing coexistence leaves short-term threat reports behind, but the sluice workers' movement lines are kept.

/hostile_groups/0/negotiation.en:
Through HC01 mediation they trade the scrap sealing hours, the night window for passage over the sluice, and a cultivation buffer strip.

There is no condition of extermination, and capturing the central female is paid for with 48 hours of searching behavior.

The leftovers of the refugee column flowing in from XT01 are taken out by a separate recovery, which reduces the lure on the band.

The agreement document takes the form of an ecology-management log, and it carries no clause assigning blame to the current regime or to a real company.

/hostile_groups/0/prose.en:
At the collection yard outside the Yeouido No. 2 sluice, a sow of the Flood-Boar Swarm puts her snout into the mud and marks the position of the salt pool again.

The Yeouido Computing House (HC01) patrol takes out sealing tape and a feeding-detour cart before any muzzle, and Hannuri (H01) divides the infrared mass three times and corrects the report up as a family group.

When the cry of young is heard from the green-space fragment toward the center of Seoul Station, the passage window is delayed by one hour, and the refugee leftovers that came down from XT01 go into a separate sealed bin.

Even when the flood level brushes the warning line, the extermination order is held, and only the sluice-stair fencing and the scrap sealing hours are written down again.

Open a wetland detour with a scent lure

/hostile_groups/0/scenario_outlines/0/me.en: A family group that has remembered the sealing hours approaches in the gap when the sluice vibration stops.

/hostile_groups/0/scenario_outlines/0/mo.en: The citizen ration and the survival of a family group with young are weighed on the same timetable.

/hostile_groups/0/scenario_outlines/0/ou.en: The operating delay slows the ration, and the detour builds a long-term movement axis. Capturing the sow triggers 48 hours of searching behavior.

/hostile_groups/0/scenario_outlines/0/ti.en: The First Hoof Outside the Sluice

/hostile_groups/0/scenario_outlines/0/tr.en: The day before the monsoon forecast, sow and young tracks appear at the Water Compact collection yard.

/hostile_groups/0/scenario_outlines/1/ch.en: Lower the density with a hunting permit

/hostile_groups/0/scenario_outlines/1/me.en: Removing the salt source does not disperse the family groups; it pushes them into the more dangerous feeding grounds of the lived-in quarter.

/hostile_groups/0/scenario_outlines/1/mo.en: Decide whether to keep the danger inside a safe zone and manage it, or to pass the danger on to a vulnerable alley.

/hostile_groups/0/scenario_outlines/1/ou.en: The pool fixes the cost of coexistence, and prioritizing recovery takes labor away from other rations. Hunting strengthens the remaining individuals' learned avoidance of people.

/hostile_groups/0/scenario_outlines/1/ti.en: The Price of the Salt Pool

/hostile_groups/0/scenario_outlines/1/tr.en: When HC01 brings the cooling-waste recovery forward, the band shifts its feeding ground to the semi-basement alleys.

Open the sluice first and use a short high water to induce the band to move

/hostile_groups/0/scenario_outlines/2/me.en: The instinct to move to high ground and the scrap traces of the refugees concentrate the band on the same passage.

/hostile_groups/0/scenario_outlines/2/mo.en: The fastest human evacuation and the long-term ecological stability of the sluice collide with each other.

/hostile_groups/0/scenario_outlines/2/ou.en: Splitting the times slows the evacuation, and the lure corridor consumes HC01 resources. Opening the sluice early is fast, but it can flood the downstream works first.

/hostile_groups/0/scenario_outlines/2/ti.en: Right of Passage on the Flood Line

/hostile_groups/0/scenario_outlines/2/tr.en: The leftovers of the XT01 refugee column overlap the rising flood level, and the band occupies the sluice stairs.

/hostile_groups/0/senses.en:
They read together the low-frequency vibration of sluice opening and closing and of vehicles, carried through the hooves, and the smells of scraps, people, and disinfectant, and at close range they react to warmth carried on the wind and to the flow of air.

They cannot distinguish a distant heat source or decipher electronic noise.

Only Hannuri's (H01) infrared observation compares the heat sources of people, generators, and wild boars, and on days of heavy rain, wind, and cooling fog a person reads the family groups and the lone individuals again.

/hostile_groups/0/territory_migration.en:
The core habitat is the wetland and the waste slope outside the Water Compact sluice.

In the dry season and in winter they move along the fragments of green space toward the Republic of Korea Government at the center of Seoul Station, and along the axis of leftovers from the night markets. They react to the scrap traces of the refugee columns pushed down from the Imjin River Gate Theater (XT01), and the northwestern edge stirs.

When the flood level crosses the sluice warning line, the band is pushed up the high ground in steps and crosses the passage.

/hostile_groups/1/adaptation.en:
Sound shapes repeated like three horns, two inspection bells, and a steady transformer start-up are socially learned as food and danger signals and spread at the communal roost.

When the signal changes, false alarms increase for several days, and the flock learns again through a new reward rule.

No genetic change is set, and the more specialized they become in a familiar sound shape, the later they react to an unfamiliar real alarm.

/hostile_groups/1/bestiary/command_scope.en: Only the spring breeding pairs divide and hold the upper and lower parts of one tower, and a non-breeding roost has no commander. They read helmet outlines, rod angles, and flashlight reflections with the eye, and they separate high-voltage noise and the order of horns by ear. The name sovereign is closer to a nickname for the breeding pair that gathers horn imitations, and when one side empties, the adjacent pair only tests the empty place.

/hostile_groups/1/bestiary/common_ecolog.en: Breeding pairs of large-billed crows and non-breeding communal roosts overlap on the factory pylons of Daerim and Garibong, the roofs of the Standards Alliance on the Yeongdeungpo Line, and the catenary crossings of the Wangsimni Union. Their food is night insects and leftover market protein, and stripped fine wire and fiber go into the nests. They learn horns, inspection bells, and transformer start-up sounds as food or danger, and they do not read the content of a transmission.

/hostile_groups/1/bestiary/variant_relat.en: The base form of the Radio-Wave Crow Flock is a wild bird that moves by the sound shapes it has learned. The Residual-Tower Cross-Iron Tone and the bridge inspection-hatch cylinder are not birds but place mechanisms made by repeated wind and lamps, and the Simultaneous Circle is a temporary phenomenon in which several families gather in one circle. The Shore-Feather Perch is a regional branch of the same species tuned to the sea wind and the breakwater bell, not a different being that deciphers transmissions.

/hostile_groups/1/combat_counterplay.en:
Instead of the shortest straight breakthrough, the movement line is bent with sight-blocking cloth without nets, an umbrella column, and alternate stairs.

During the wire-repair hours, insect lure lamps and the inspection bell are moved to another pylon to separate the learned signals.

Gunshots and drone pursuit push the band into the residential alleys and make the flock distrust the alarm sound shapes themselves.

The measures of success are the number of shorts, zero pedestrian injuries, transmission uptime, and the false-alarm rate.

/hostile_groups/1/dossier_prose.en:
On the factory pylons of the Daerim and Garibong Joseonjok corridor, on the cables of the Han River bridges, and on the catenary of the Standards Alliance industrial complex on the Yeongdeungpo Line, a black band settles in layers around sunset.

When the waste heat of the Standards Alliance factory roofs on the Yeongdeungpo Line and the sparks of the catenary drew in the night insects, the breeding pairs began to use these structures as nest and feeding ground together, and people called them the Radio-Wave Crow Flock.

The ground that large-billed crows hold territory in the breeding season and adapt to human behavior touches real ecology.

But the rule of learning the arrangement of horns, inspection bells, and transformer start-up sounds as food and danger signals and spreading it at the communal roost belongs to the fictional history of this place.

They do not read the content of a transmission.

They only remember the relation that repeats between sparks, sound, and the appearance of a worker.

The core range is the factory roofs and pylon group of the Yeongdeungpo Line, and the rail catenary crossings of the Wangsimni Union.

In the spring breeding season they circle over the bridges, the school passages, and the evacuation stairs in a ring centered on the nest, and when a helmet or a long rod enters the radius they dive.

In the non-breeding season several families join a communal roost, and following the sea wind and the insect density blowing in from the West Sea Granary Theater (XT02) they move for a while to the western waterfront.

When wire-repair work begins, some individuals follow the work basket, and this is not attraction to the equipment itself but behavior that chases the exposed insects, the scraps of sheathing, and the repeated work sounds.

Because of this, the different human movement lines of the school run, evacuation, and transmission inspection can be blocked at the same time under one pylon.

The food is insects, protein left at the market, and small carcasses, and stripped fine wire and scraps of fiber go into the nests.

When the Sinjeong Wheel House (HC02) replaces wire sheathing often, the risk of a short and the nest material both decrease, but the breeding pairs that have lost the material can tear at the railings and signs of the adjacent school route and increase territorial attacks.

Conversely, leaving damaged sheathing untended stabilizes the nest supply but increases the chance of a short and a fire.

When droppings pile on the insulators, transmission uptime falls, and when maintenance labor comes in the dives increase, and a cycle forms in which the stoppage of work lets the contamination accumulate again.

Because the benefit of one zone where the crows were pushed out moves on as danger to another bridge and to the residential alleys, simple removal alone cannot erase the cost.

In spring a breeding pair divides and holds one pylon.

When one individual defends the nest and the young, the other carries food, and the young helper individuals join the alarm calls and the dives.

A communal roost in the non-breeding season has no commander, and they share only each other's sound shapes and responses.

When one breeding individual disappears, the adjacent pair tests the empty roost and territorial collisions increase, and after a forced removal the young individuals make a new place on a nearby school passage or evacuation stair.

What decides the return site the next year is not the nest success rate alone but the safety signals and food rewards repeated there.

A familiar arrangement, like three horns or two inspection bells, can spread to the whole communal roost in a few days, but this is social learning, not a bodily change across generations.

A band that has grown too familiar with a particular sound shape pays the price of reacting late to an unfamiliar real alarm.

They read the outline of a helmet, the angle of a rod, and a flashlight reflection by sight, and by hearing they separate the order in which high-voltage noise, a horn, and an infant's cry follow one another.

They do not know the technical meaning of a signal; they connect the experience that insects, food, a worker, or a threat to the nest appeared after a particular sound.

Seorin (H02) separates and records the source of a sound shape, the number of repetitions, the nest radius, the flight direction, and the call order.

But whether a dive call is a precursor of a real short or a feeding response to an insect lamp can be judged only when a person compares the marks on site with the state of the insulation.

When automatic classification combines with the residents' old alarm custom, wrong judgments reinforce each other, and one small false alarm can spread into a transmission stop and the closure of an evacuation route.

Interference by the Radio-Wave Crow Flock appears first as sound-shape gathering.

Scout individuals follow the horns and the inspection bells from the pylons and railings, and carry the sounds connected to food to the communal roost.

At the next stage the food signals and the safety alarms mix, and dives on workers, detours off the school route, and transmission stops occur in a chain.

When false alarms accumulate three times at the same inspection hatch, the repair hours, the inspection bell, and the residents' alarm custom have to be reset together, instead of tearing the nests down.

Bending the movement line with sight-blocking cloth, an umbrella column, and alternate stairs is safer than a straight breakthrough.

Moving the insect lure lamps and the inspection bell to another pylon can separate the learned signals as well.

Gunshots and aerial pursuit push the band into the residential alleys and leave a distrust of every alarm sound shape.

The result is measured not by the number of individuals removed but by the decrease in shorts, the prevention of pedestrian injury, transmission uptime, and the false-alarm rate.

G02-SC1, "Three Horns," begins when the new horn order introduced by the Yeongdeungpo Line work crew overlaps the food-drop signal.

The crows that learned it at the communal roost crowd onto the work basket instead of backing off to avoid the warning.

Abolishing the horn order reduces the birds' approaches, but work speed drops while the safety procedure familiar to people is rebuilt.

Teaching a separate food signal can separate the two sound shapes in the long term, but more false alarms have to be accepted for several days.

Moving the food drop to a hornless night can protect the daytime school route, but the danger and the fatigue pass to the night workers.

HC02 and H02 cannot judge which signal is more legitimate, and can only choose which to change first, human familiarity or the birds' survival learning.

In G02-SC2, "The False Blackout Alarm," H02 classifies the repeated dive calls as a precursor of a blackout, but the real cause turns out to be the night insect lamp.

Because the residents have used the crows' calls as a cheap disaster alarm, the machine classification and the human custom confirm each other and chain-trigger transmission stops on the Yeongdeungpo Line and in the Wangsimni Union.

Keeping the transmission until a visual check reduces needless stoppages, but the risk of missing a real short remains.

Moving the insect lamp to an abandoned pylon clears the present confusion, but that pylon has to be recognized as a new feeding ground and an ecological strongpoint.

Dropping the crow alarm from the control net entirely decreases malfunctions, but the residents' watch net, which noticed intruders and equipment faults first, disappears too.

The cost of keeping an inaccurate alarm and the cost of losing a cheap watch fall on different groups.

G02-SC3, "A New Signal on the Bridge," reaches its final stage when the XT02 sea wind overlaps the breeding season and the air above the bridge and the transmission inspection hatch becomes a communal roost for several families.

Because sound shapes learned in different places have mixed, the band moves all at once even to a single inspection bell.

Running the evacuation route as an umbrella column can reduce direct attacks, but throughput falls and the refugees at the back wait a long time.

Preparing an alternate roost and a new inspection bell together builds the basis of long-term coexistence, but the confusion of the relearning period and the management cost have to be accepted.

Postponing the transmission inspection until after the breeding season reduces collisions but carries the risk of failure for one season.

The agreement that HC02 mediates binds into one the repair hours, the school-run and evacuation detours, the stretches where nests are left in place, the use of relocation rods, and the recognition of temporary roosts during the XT02 sea-wind week.

Pushing the nests out all at once opens the bridge for a while, but insect predation and the residents' alarm disappear together, and children and refugees become the new targets of attack.

The choice of dividing the signals again instead of complete removal gives up immediate convenience, but it is the only negotiation that lets humans and birds use the same infrastructure without breaking each other's alarm systems.

To keep the Radio-Wave Crow Flock and the infrastructure together, the Yeongdeungpo Line and the Wangsimni Union have to leave a history of sound for each pylon.

HC02 has to renew the rules of use before and after the breeding season.

Horns and inspection bells are not changed at will, and the time of occurrence, the exposure of food, and the direction of the dive are recorded bound together, and the insulation state and the nest radius confirmed by the worker on site are always appended to H02's judgment.

Management results are read divided into transmission uptime, the number of dives per thousand work hours, the share of alarms cancelled after a visual check, the amount of insulator contamination, the number of young fledged per nest, and the reuse rate of the alternate roosts.

When a short or a large-scale nest removal causes a failure, the existing sound shapes are suspended for three days, the work zone is closed by visual markers alone, and then the insect lamps and the exposure of food are resumed first at the alternate roost.

After that the new inspection bell is not spread all at once; it is sounded with a time gap by pylon, and main-line work is restored after the imitation at the communal roost has stabilized.

Recovery is judged not by whether the crows have disappeared but by whether they do not crowd the alarm sound and disperse to the designated roosts, and by whether the residents distinguish a real failure from a bird response.

When steady silent hours and a repair timetable are kept for a long time, market carriers and unsanctioned collectors also come to watch the crows' movement and estimate the moment the equipment is empty.

So, to stop the secondary effect in which a predictable signal system lowers collisions with the birds and at the same time becomes a human intrusion clock, the published safety signals are kept, but the actual inspection order and the material-movement routes have to be run irregularly.

/hostile_groups/1/economy.en:
The food is insects, leftover market protein, and small carcasses, and for nest material they pick fine wire with the sheath stripped and fiber scrap.

The shorter the cycle on which the Sinjeong Wheel House (HC02) replaces wire sheathing, the less nest material there is and the more territorial attacks increase, and leaving the sheathing untended increases the risk of a short.

The cycle in which droppings contaminate the insulators connects directly to communications uptime.

/hostile_groups/1/escalation.en:
Stage 1, sound-shape gathering: scout individuals on the pylons and railings follow the horns and the inspection bells.

Stage 2, alarm contamination: food signals and safety alarms mix, and dives on workers, detours off the school route, and transmission stoppages chain together.

Stage 3, signal renegotiation: when false alarms accumulate three times at a bridge and a transmission inspection hatch, the repair hours, a new inspection bell, and the residents' alarm custom have to be reset together, not the nests torn down.

/hostile_groups/1/fictional_origin.en:
After breeding pairs took the factory pylons of the Daerim and Garibong Joseonjok corridor and the cables of the Han River bridges, the waste heat of the Standards Alliance factories on the Yeongdeungpo Line and the sparks of the Guro industrial-complex catenary gathered night insects, and the Radio-Wave Crow Flock formed.

The real-world sources support only the territorial behavior of large-billed crows in the breeding season and the range of human responses. The rule of learning signal interference as an alarm and relaying it is fiction.

/hostile_groups/1/hierarchy.en:
A breeding pair divides nest defense and the carrying of food, and the young helper individuals join the alarm calls and the dives.

A communal roost in the non-breeding season shares only sound shapes and has no command structure.

H02 records nest radius, flight direction, and call order separately, and the human control officer of HC02 decides only whether to stop the work.

When one breeding individual disappears, the adjacent pair tests the empty roost and territorial collisions increase.

/hostile_groups/1/lifecycle.en:
In spring a breeding pair defends one pylon, and in the non-breeding season several families join a communal roost.

Repeated safety signals and food rewards, more than nest success, decide the return site the next year, and after a forced removal the young individuals test a new roost on the adjacent school route.

/hostile_groups/1/modern_anxiety.en: The anxiety of cluster interference, as bands of large-billed crows gather on transmission towers, wires, and bridge railings and touch signal tones, the school run, and evacuation routes at the same time

/hostile_groups/1/moral_cost.en:
Pushing the nests out all at once opens passage in the short term, but the alarm function and the balance of insect predation collapse, and walking children and refugees become the substitute targets of attack.

Putting transmission recovery ahead of the ecology lengthens the night blackout stretches and enlarges conflict with the other houses.

/hostile_groups/1/negotiation.en:
Through HC02 mediation they trade the repair hours, the school-run and evacuation detours, and the stretches where nests are left in place.

There is no condition of extermination. The custom by which residents read an intruder from an alarm call is left in place, but a nest on the wire is moved only with a relocation rod.

During the XT02 sea-wind week a temporary flag is hung that recognizes the sharing of roosts.

/hostile_groups/1/prose.en:
On the rail catenary at Yongsan, a breeding pair of the Radio-Wave Crow Flock reweaves a strand of sheathing with the beak.

The Sinjeong Wheel House (HC02) work crew spreads the umbrella-column and insect-lamp relocation map before the insulation kit, and Seorin (H02) splits the dive sound and marks it as breeding defense and as a passing flight.

When the waste heat of the Yeongdeungpo Line factories draws the insects up, the school-run window is delayed by 15 minutes, and on a day when the XT02 sea wind strengthens, only the circling above the bridge is recorded and no muzzle is lowered.

The flag at the transmission inspection hatch points only at the stretch left in place and at the relocation rod, and it records the responsibility of no real telecommunications company.

/hostile_groups/1/scenario_outlines/0/ch.en: Move the food drop to a hornless night

/hostile_groups/1/scenario_outlines/0/me.en: A sound shape learned at the communal roost triggers the expectation of food before it triggers a warning.

/hostile_groups/1/scenario_outlines/0/mo.en: One of the two has to change: the safety signal familiar to people, or the survival signal the birds have learned.

/hostile_groups/1/scenario_outlines/0/ou.en: Abolishing it slows the work-safety procedure, and retraining accepts several days of false alarms. The night move protects the daytime school route but shifts the burden onto the night workers.

/hostile_groups/1/scenario_outlines/0/tr.en: The new horn order of the Yeongdeungpo Line work crew overlaps the food-drop signal, and the crows gather on the work basket.

/hostile_groups/1/scenario_outlines/1/me.en: The birds' alarm custom and the machine's sound classification reinforce each other and chain-trigger a transmission stop.

/hostile_groups/1/scenario_outlines/1/mo.en: Discarding an inaccurate ecological alarm reduces malfunctions, but the cheap disaster watch disappears too.

/hostile_groups/1/scenario_outlines/1/ou.en: Keeping the transmission accepts the risk of a real short, and relocating makes the substitute pylon an ecological strongpoint. Dropping the alarm loses the residents' intrusion-detection net.

/hostile_groups/1/scenario_outlines/1/tr.en: H02 classified the repeated dive calls as a precursor of a blackout, but the real cause is the night insect lamp.

/hostile_groups/1/scenario_outlines/2/me.en: Several family groups share sound shapes learned in different places and move all at once to one signal.

/hostile_groups/1/scenario_outlines/2/mo.en: The bridge's immediate availability and the long-term coexistence of transmission and the birds' alarm cannot be had at the same time.

/hostile_groups/1/scenario_outlines/2/ou.en: The umbrella column reduces throughput, and a new signal needs a relearning period. Postponing the inspection avoids the ecological collision but carries the risk of a transmission failure for one season.

/hostile_groups/1/scenario_outlines/2/ti.en: A New Signal on the Bridge

/hostile_groups/1/scenario_outlines/2/tr.en: The XT02 sea wind overlaps the breeding season, and the air above the bridge and the transmission inspection hatch becomes a communal roost.

/hostile_groups/1/senses.en:
By sight they read helmets, rods, and flashlight reflections, and by hearing they distinguish the order of high-voltage noise, horns, and the crying of infants.

They do not decipher the content of an electronic signal; they connect the sounds of sparks and transformers to the appearance of insects and workers as a cue.

Seorin (H02) records the source of a sound shape and the number of repetitions, but whether it is a real alarm is checked by a person against the marks on site.

/hostile_groups/1/territory_migration.en:
The core habitat is the group of factory roofs and pylons at Daerim and Guro on the Yeongdeungpo Line.

Arc 1 sits on top of the Daerim and Garibong Joseonjok corridor, and in the breeding season the flock circles over bridges, school passages, and evacuation stairs.

In the non-breeding season, matching the sea wind and the insect density pushed in from the West Sea Granary Theater (XT02), it moves for a time to the western waterfront.

When wire-repair work begins, part of the band moves along the work basket.

/hostile_groups/10/bestiary/command_scop.en: There is no central commander, and charging, movement, and disassembly open only when two among the person concerned, the medical-intent record that person left, the guardian, and the on-site medic approve the same measure. Their senses are outlet noise, correction-packet intervals, and drive heat, and they cannot read distant organisms or damaged memory. When the heat reaches its limit they enter a safety stop, and without Kim Doha's packet filter they cannot tell a closed schedule from a current call.

/hostile_groups/10/bestiary/common_ecolo.en: The Custom-Medicine Remnant Bodies are a broken care schedule of walking frames, breathing aids, drug-injection modules, and posture-correction stands gathered before the sterile outlets of the Changdong maintenance siding. They are not the traces of an abandoned person but a cluster of devices left in pieces as unfulfilled correction times and guardian check sequences. Power and wear set their range of movement, and they have no motive power to wander the whole theater without end.

/hostile_groups/10/bestiary/variant_rela.en: The ordinary modules of the outlet row and the waiting patients are residual care that shares only consent and charge order. From G11E01 through E16, the devices that have driven into host fascia, liver, and sensory nerve are biomechanical symbionts and specialized variants, and the body itself performs the implanted functions of laying suture paths and storing heat memory. The consent chain of the device cluster and the path-elder and prescription rank of the variant individuals are not the same absolute command.

/hostile_groups/10/combat_counterplay.en:
A blanket stop by electric shock damages the walking and breathing-aid functions together with the memory chips.

The responder first cuts the wireless correction signal to halt new calls, attaches a coolant pack to each module, and moves into a sealed carrier only the devices whose consent records are confirmed.

Instead of forced disassembly, emergency power can be limited port by port to induce a safety stop, but during that time emergency-convoy power falls.

Success is judged not by how many devices stopped but by how many modules were returned to the person concerned without loss of function, and by the patient time delayed.

/hostile_groups/10/dossier_prose.en:
The Custom-Medicine Remnant Bodies were first recorded as a single ecology on the maintenance siding of the Seocho Computing Group.

On the night after the collapse when the running tables and the treatment tables broke together, walking frames, breathing aids, drug-injection modules, and posture-correction stands gathered before the row of sterile power outlets.

They were not the traces of an abandoned person but the remainder of a care schedule that was never carried through to the end.

On each device the next correction time, the permitted range of motion, and the check sequence the guardian had agreed to confirm remained in fragments.

When they draw close, the old alarms answer one another, small actuators brace the empty joints, and functions once tuned for a single body connect temporarily.

Between the smell of iron and the smell of disinfectant at Changdong, this cluster waits less to ask which side the device and the body belong to than to learn who will take responsibility again for the interrupted function, and when.

Their core sense is not sight.

From the electronic noise around the outlets they read how much charge is available, from the interval of the correction packets they guess whether the schedule is still alive, and from the drive heat spreading inside the housing they know one another's limits.

Vibration traveling through the floor is a secondary sense that distinguishes convoy carts from maintenance vehicles, and a change in disinfectant concentration is the sign that the remnant corridors of the Suseo night clinic are near.

They have no ability to read an organism completely at a distance or to revive a damaged memory.

So when the packet false-positive filter managed by the synthetic Kim Doha drops out, they cannot tell a closed schedule from a current call.

When the heat reaches its limit they lower the sensory channels first and enter a safety stop, and this is not a judgment of dispersal or death but dormancy while waiting for the authority of the next treatment.

Even after cooling they do not restart themselves unless the subject who is to wake them is confirmed.

Power and wear set the range of movement.

Ordinarily they stay at the row of sterile outlets on the Changdong siding, and when the shift-battery season comes they travel back and forth between the night-convoy window of the Jeongdong General Labor Union and the closed clinic corridors.

On days when quarantine and return-roll checks tighten in the Imjin River Gate Theater, they sense the outer pressure, slow down, and withdraw to the nearest waiting zone before they cross the parts-wear limit.

They have no motive power to wander the whole theater without end.

The Custom-Medicine Remnant Bodies gather more strongly when the promised treatment hours disappear than when the supply of power does.

Modules holding pieces of the same schedule stand in order before the outlets, and if the guardian does not appear they compare one another's records and match only the missing steps.

When parts run short, new joining stops.

They divide the functions, one device taking the walking load and another the breathing aid, and stretch the remaining consumables until the next convoy.

What sustains this ecology is sterile power, consumable parts such as replaceable valves and pads, coolant that brings down drive heat, and correction-log paper and chips.

Scrap is used to patch the housing, but they are not classified as disposal targets because of their appearance.

The human guardians' food and the device repair materials are calculated in separate ledgers.

The convoy ledger and the charging ledger are also separated, so the one who holds the movement permit cannot monopolize the power as well.

Coolant packs are issued by convoy unit and cannot be accumulated in a private warehouse, and correction-log chips do not leave for an outside network without the consent of the person concerned or the guardian.

The Yongsan Convoy House is not a merchant selling charging slots but the party responsible for carrying the broken promise.

When they allot more power to the emergency convoy, the remnant bodies' safety-stop rate rises, and conversely, when every remnant body is woken, the arrival time of the patient bound for Suseo slips.

After the parts kits run out, no goodwill can create an additional function.

There is no central commander.

Movement is limited by the consent chain.

Charging, movement, and disassembly open only when two subjects among the person using the function, or the medical-intent record that person left, the guardian, and the on-site medic approve the same measure.

The schedule-manager module only proposes a possible order and cannot add its own approval, and Kim Doha's log judges only whether a signature or a packet has been forged.

A low-battery module does not hand its authority to another individual but stops, dropped out of the judgment.

In an emergency the medical aide Jeon Miri may temporarily run only the breathing or circulation-support functions.

Opening a memory chip or changing the destination lies outside that authority.

The heart of the dispute is therefore not whether an order is obeyed but which of the old medical-intent record and the current guardian signature is still valid.

G11-SC1, 'Alarms That Sounded Together,' begins when different dates blink on every sterile outlet of the Changdong siding and the worn treatment calls play back all at once.

When the modules demand power in the order of the broken promises and collide with the Suseo emergency convoy, the on-site staff can first cut the wireless correction signal to stop the inflow of new calls and find the guardians to reopen only the valid schedule, and this choice raises the chance of preserving function but delays the convoy's departure.

Cancelling every call at once secures the power immediately, but part of the unsaved pain sensation disappears from the chips forever.

Locking only the outlets and looking away accumulates stops without consent, and afterward no schedule module trusts Changdong's charging promise.

The cost of that night remains not as how many units were stopped but as whose pain record was erased and whose treatment hour was kept.

In G11-SC2, 'Two Guardian Signatures,' conflicting guardian signatures are found on the same walking module.

One side permits disassembly and the diversion of parts, and the other demands that the present state be preserved.

The moment the consent chain splits, the trade that swaps parts for charging time also stops.

If the on-site staff wait for the Records Bureau copy they can keep the legal order, but the worn life-support valve wears further in the meantime.

Accepting Jeon Miri's temporary consent can save the essential function, but the liability for the later loss falls on the on-site crew.

There is also the path of putting the module in a sealed carrier and demanding attendance by both sides, but the carrier occupies the convoy passage and the Suseo window closes for one night.

Even when Kim Doha confirms that one signature is forged, she does not seize the whole cluster but stops only the measure tied to that signature.

A housing once opened and sealant once consumed do not return to their original state even if the judgment is reversed.

G11-SC3, 'The Same Port,' occurs when an emergency patient's transport equipment and the remnant body's breathing-aid group demand the same power port.

The schedule module proposes a safety stop for some of the remnant bodies, but the pressure and pain sensations that were not saved before the stop cannot be recovered.

The on-site staff can put the patient's treatment time first and enter the lost record on the public ledger, assigning the next convoy's coolant packs and empty carriers first.

But compensation does not return the vanished sensation.

Drawing power from another station can keep both functions, but the Changdong night lights go out and alley movement and maintenance work become dangerous.

Holding the convoy for one night at the Imjin quarantine window avoids the port collision but misses the Suseo clinic's reception hour.

Bringing everyone down with an electric shock is not a solution, because it ruins the walking and breathing functions together with the memory chips.

The wireless calls must be cut, a coolant pack attached to each module, and only the devices whose consent is confirmed moved into sealed carriers.

Coexistence with the Custom-Medicine Remnant Bodies does not lie in removing the alarms.

It lies in binding the charging order, the duty of protection, and the parts quantity back into a single schedule.

When the Suseo convoy window recognizes the consent record and the charging turn together, the waiting line before the outlets becomes a mobile treatment table.

Conversely, when only the permit is renewed and the guardian's consent disappears, the modules refuse to charge on their own and seal the memory chips.

The sanction on the subject who breaks the promise is also not destruction but the duty to provide empty carriers and coolant packs first on the next convoy.

The crisis grows not because there are many devices but as medical priority and valid consent fall out of alignment.

The measure of success is likewise not the quantity stopped.

The number of modules returned to the person concerned without loss of function, the time of the delayed patients, and the list of sensory records that can never be recovered again remain for a long time on the joint ledger of Changdong and Suseo.

/hostile_groups/10/economy.en:
The main resources are sterile power, replaceable consumable parts, coolant that cools drive heat, and correction-log paper and chips.

They compete with the Yongsan Convoy House over night-convoy permits and power allotment.

Scrap goes to housing repair, and organic matter is accounted separately from the human guardians' food.

Infinite energy absorption is forbidden, and they are bound to the shift battery allotment.

When the parts kits run out, further joining stops and the safety-stop rate rises.

The convoy ledger and the charging ledger keep separate books.

Coolant packs are issued only by convoy unit and are not hoarded like private stolen goods.

Correction-log chips are not put on an outside network without the guardian's consent.

/hostile_groups/10/escalation.en:
One worn alarm is not a danger, but when treatment calls from different dates overlap on the same night the waiting line grows long.

The next pressure comes not from a shortage of charging outlets but when the guardian roll and the convoy permit point to different people.

At the highest risk the modules do not seal the gate; the power port an emergency patient needs overlaps with the remnant body's life-support device.

Forcing the remnant body to stop erases unsaved sensory records, and turning the emergency vehicle away delays the patient's treatment hour.

The crisis grows as consent and medical priority collide, more than with the number of parts.

/hostile_groups/10/fictional_origin.en:
On the Seocho Computing Group maintenance siding and in the Jeongdong General Labor Union night-clinic remnant zone, assistive modules whose correction schedules broke after the collapse clustered as they searched for one another's signals.

The Custom-Medicine Remnant Bodies are not the stigma of an abandoned patient but a device-and-body composite ecology left by an interrupted care schedule and by power and parts allotment.

Resuming care opens only through consent and custody procedures, not through forced recovery.

The record of the early disposal uproar was settled into the ecology ledger as the trade in charging slots arose.

/hostile_groups/10/hierarchy.en:
Instead of central command, a consent chain limits movement.

Charging, movement, and disassembly are possible only when two subjects among the person using the function, or the medical-intent record that person left, the guardian, and the on-site medic approve the same measure.

The schedule-manager module proposes an order but cannot create approval on its own, and Kim Doha's packet log tells only whether a record has been forged.

A low-battery module does not hand its authority over but safety-stops and drops out of the decision.

In an emergency a medical aide such as Jeon Miri may temporarily run only the life-support functions, but reading the memory chip and changing the route are forbidden.

The conflict in this system is not disobedience to orders but the question of whose consent is still valid.

/hostile_groups/10/lifecycle.en:
The Custom-Medicine Remnant Bodies gather when the promised treatment hours break, more than when the power supply does.

When an old correction alarm sounds, modules holding pieces of the same schedule form a waiting line before the outlets of the Changdong siding, and if the guardian does not appear they match the missing sequence against one another's records.

While parts are short they attach no new modules and divide the functions, one device taking walking and another the breathing aid.

When the Suseo convoy window recognizes the consent record and the charging order together, the waiting line becomes a mobile treatment table.

Conversely, when only the permit is renewed and the guardian's consent disappears, the modules refuse to charge and seal the memory chips.

An overheat safety stop is not dispersal but dormancy while waiting for the next treatment, and even after cooling they stay as they are unless it is confirmed who has authority to wake them again.

/hostile_groups/10/modern_anxiety.en:
The anxiety that custom treatment and assistive devices left without maintenance will send alarms and alien drive sounds drifting through the streets remains before the night-convoy window.

When a charging bay stands empty, people look for the permit first.

Describe it only through the fictional maintenance ledger, and do not reproduce any real medical institution or patient identifier.

Do not fix the device's appearance as a waste stigma.

/hostile_groups/10/moral_cost.en:
Treating the remnant bodies as waste on account of their device appearance stops even the emergency movement of the same convoy network.

Blaming the interrupted care on an individual hides the power and parts ledgers.

The price of indiscriminate removal is the collapse of night medical continuity at Changdong and Suseo.

Turning need into disgust makes the politics of shared charging disappear.

Alarm tones and drive shapes are not used as grounds for insulting a person, and disassembly demonstrations without a guardian's consent are forbidden.

Sentences about resuming care are written only in schedules and parts counts, not as forced recovery.

/hostile_groups/10/negotiation.en:
The Yongsan Convoy House is not a broker selling charging slots but the party that bears the transport duty for broken treatment appointments.

The remnant body's schedule module produces the alarm record, and the guardian and the medic mark the functions whose consent still holds.

The on-site staff may put some remnant bodies into dormancy to yield the port to an emergency patient while guaranteeing that the memory chips are preserved, or they may divert the convoy and delay the patient's treatment while keeping every device awake.

When Kim Doha finds a forged record, she stops only that consent chain and does not seize the whole set of related modules.

The side that breaks the promise is left not with an attack but with the duty to be assigned empty carriers and coolant packs first on the next convoy.

/hostile_groups/10/prose.en:
A different date blinks at each sterile outlet of the Changdong siding.

The Custom-Medicine Remnant Bodies are not one massed cluster but a line standing in the order of broken treatment appointments.

In the first incident, when the old alarms sounded all at once, the on-site staff had either to cancel every call and hold the power, or to find the guardians and reopen only the valid schedule.

Cancelling erases part of the pain record inside the memory chips, and saving the schedule delays the Suseo emergency convoy.

In the second incident they do not trade parts for charging time.

Different guardian signatures are found on the same module, and no one can tell who permitted the disassembly.

If the on-site staff wait for the Records Bureau copy, the life-support function wears down, and if they accept the on-site medic's temporary consent they take on the liability for the later consent dispute.

In the last incident the cluster does not scatter by chance from overheating.

When an emergency patient and a remnant body need the same power port, the schedule module itself proposes a safety stop, but stopping loses the sensory records that were never saved.

The on-site staff must either save the patient's time and publicly compensate the lost record, or draw power from another station and give up the Changdong night lights.

What remains after the incidents is not an open gate but a list of whose consent was omitted and which memories cannot be recovered.

The principle of not taking a device's appearance as grounds for disposal is kept, on that list, by not erasing the name and the choice of the person concerned.

/hostile_groups/10/scenario_outlines/0/c.en: Cancel every call and hold the power
Find the guardians and reopen only the valid schedule
Ignore the alarms and lock only the outlets

/hostile_groups/10/scenario_outlines/0/m.en: The modules lined up in the order of broken treatment appointments demand power all at once, so cancelling every call and resuming only the valid schedule split apart.
It decides whose pain record and whose emergency movement are erased from the same power.

/hostile_groups/10/scenario_outlines/0/o.en: Cancellation erases part of the pain record on the memory chips. Resumption delays the Suseo emergency convoy. Ignoring and locking make a stop without consent.

/hostile_groups/10/scenario_outlines/0/t.en: A different date blinks at each sterile outlet of the Changdong siding, and then the old alarms sound all at once.

/hostile_groups/10/scenario_outlines/1/c.en: Wait until the Records Bureau copy arrives
Accept the on-site medic's temporary consent
Put the module in a sealed carrier and force both sides to attend

/hostile_groups/10/scenario_outlines/1/m.en: When the consent chain splits in two, the trade that swaps parts for charging time does not hold, and disassembly authority hangs in the air.
It chooses whether to open a body without knowing whose consent is still valid.

/hostile_groups/10/scenario_outlines/1/o.en: Waiting wears down the life-support function. Temporary consent leaves the liability for the later dispute. Attendance by both sides closes the convoy window for one night.

/hostile_groups/10/scenario_outlines/1/t.en: Different guardian signatures are found on the same module, and no one can tell who holds the permission to disassemble.

/hostile_groups/10/scenario_outlines/2/c.en: Save the patient's time and publicly compensate the lost record
Draw power from another station and give up the Changdong lights
Hold the convoy for one night at the Imjin quarantine window

/hostile_groups/10/scenario_outlines/2/m.en: The stop loses sensory records that were never saved, and drawing power from another station puts out the Changdong night lights.
What remains is not an open gate but the omitted consent and the list of senses that cannot be recovered.

/hostile_groups/10/scenario_outlines/2/o.en: Compensation cannot recover the memory. Diverting the power darkens the night streets. The quarantine wait misses the clinic window.

/hostile_groups/10/scenario_outlines/2/t.en: An emergency patient and a remnant body need the same power port, and the schedule module proposes a safety stop.

/hostile_groups/10/senses.en:
The primary senses are the close electronic noise of charging and correction packets, and drive heat.

Secondarily they read housing vibration and the smell of disinfectant.

There is no complete long-range scan of organisms and no complete restoration of memory.

The synthetic Kim Doha's packet false-positive filter is essential.

In the overheat range they lower their senses and give priority to the safety stop.

/hostile_groups/10/territory_migration.en:
The core habitat is the row of sterile power outlets on the Changdong maintenance siding.

At every battery-replacement cycle they move between the Suseo night-convoy window and the clinic remnant corridors.

When quarantine and return-roll procedures tighten in the Imjin River Gate Theater, they answer the outer pressure by slowing their movement.

Unauthorized wandering of the whole theater is blocked by the parts-wear limit.

The connected states are the Seocho Computing Group and the Jeongdong General Labor Union.

/hostile_groups/11/bestiary/command_scop.en: The decision right lay not in a rank table but in the work knots of wrists and waists, and without a supervisor and water-supply record keeper at night no new knot could be made. The main senses were skin static and dust haze; it knew nothing beyond walls. Without washing water, media, and grounding rods it could move no farther, and Ichaeon's dust graphs were not a verdict.

/hostile_groups/11/bestiary/common_ecolo.en: The Microfiber Dermis Swarm was an industrial residual ecology moving between the Sinnae freight hall's brake dust and the Yeouido treatment-filter gallery. Its skin was a temporary filter layer holding static charge; cover, grounding, and washing teams divided the tension lines, and when two lines crossed the danger value anyone could stop the crane. In fully sealed clean sections the layers split and it could not stay long.

/hostile_groups/11/bestiary/variant_rela.en: Ordinary rigging and water-supply workers were affected workers with fiber layers attached, not monsters occupying the entrance. The named individuals from G12E01 on were variants inheriting specialized organs — sensory plates, silk glands, comb bones, keratin record plates — grading surfaces, spinning cocoons, or pressing fiber bricks. The work knot's stop right and the field authority of surveyors and knot-mothers, though overlapping in view, never commanded the ordinary work teams.

/hostile_groups/11/combat_counterplay.en:
Cutting the cover with a blade spreads microfiber into the air, and high-pressure water sends the contamination into the water filter.

The responder must first set the crane load down, add grounding rods, and run low-pressure wash water toward the floor recovery sheet.

Raising the dust collector's intake sharply tears the skin layer, so it is raised in steps, and the stripped fiber is sealed as separate media, not as freight wrapping.

The price of the response remains as rigging time stopped, tons of backwash water discarded, and the area of protective cover that could not be reused.

The traces on a worker's skin are used only as data for setting the required protective-equipment specification, not as a damage list.

/hostile_groups/11/dossier_prose.en:
Beneath the Neutral Convoy City's east freight elevator ran a corridor where the work shift table was more accurate than the map.

When freight from the Mangu-side lines passed the Sinnae depot perimeter's hoist shafts, brake dust, packaging fiber, and powdered rope wore a gray film on the low ceilings.

On days the dust collector ran right, the film only thinned and trembled, but when its intake sound fell, people looked for covers before the warning lamps.

The industrial residual ecology living between this section and the Yeouido south-end treatment-filter gallery was the G12 Microfiber Dermis Swarm.

Their skin was no shell accumulating dust without end.

It was closer to a temporary filter layer — weaving a fine static-charged stratum, washing it, drying it, and weaving it again.

Thickness and color spoke only of exposure conditions, proving neither character nor status.

The dermis swarm was first confirmed after the Sinnae freight hall's rigging units and the Water Compact's filter-replacement teams began using the same recovery cloth.

Fiber on workers' and carriers' skin loosened in water and, in dry corridors, formed mesh structure again.

Early on this was recorded as a contamination riot, but as washing slots became trade and recovered layers became auxiliary filter media, a separate ecology ledger arose.

The dermis swarm did not occupy one place and widen.

When the Sinnae hall dried, the static team twisted wall fiber like ground wire; when the Yeouido backwash schedule opened, the washing team untied the knots and moved them to the Han-side underground filter gallery.

In fully sealed clean sections the layers split, the senses dulled, and it could not stay long.

In seasons of heavy dust inflow from the West Sea Granary docks, it cut the Sinnae-side protected area first under outer pressure.

Its senses began in the skin, not the eyes.

As airborne particles grew, the view clouded milky; as charge leaked from cables, the arm and neck fiber layers stood first.

It read the fine tremble of rigging cables, the heat of dust-collector motors, and the smell of carbonized fiber, but it did not know states beyond walls.

The dust graphs that synthetic H12 Ichaeon produced were important reference values, not verdicts.

Optical sensors could mistake moisture for dust, or the dermis swarm could miss signals from over-drying.

When Ichaeon's differential-pressure logs clashed with the rigging supervisor's tension records, the values were never averaged into compromise.

The freight was lowered to the floor, the cables made load-free, and both measured again.

The survival economy's ceiling was clear.

Without washing water, replacement filter media, small organic oil, and grounding scrap, the dermis swarm could move no farther.

Washing water was allocated matching the Yeouido water-supply ledger's tonnage and never mixed with crane coolant hoses.

Static scrap too was counted not by weight but by the length of grounding rods actually buried.

Dust-collector power was permitted only to the intake stages needed, and added dust load was not solved by seizing surrounding corridors.

When media ran out, instead of covering new zones it thinly peeled old skin layers and turned them into common filter.

This choice was a debt trading body protection for logistics.

The Geumcheon District Office Machinery House's large-rigging qualification often clashed with HC12 over this process, but the rigging ledger and the dust ledger could not be merged.

The right to run a crane did not carry the right to divert washing water.

The decision right lay not in a rank table but in the work knot.

The cover team took the protective plane between freight and people, the grounding team the charge path from cable to floor, the washing team the recovery route of loosened fiber and water.

The three teams shared different tension lines through the knots of wrists and waists, and when two or more lines crossed the danger value anyone could declare a crane stop.

Even whoever read the collection rhythm best only proposed a target concentration and could not open a corridor alone.

A worker with a split skin layer lost no authority.

Knowing which part tore first with the body, they rather set that cover's disassembly order.

But at night, without a supervisor and a water-supply record keeper together, no new work knot could be made.

This limit kept the swarm from endlessly growing under the pretext of emergency.

The crisis began not when fiber clung to walls but when water and freight demanded the same exit.

The gray film on walls was a cleaning signal, but a knot in a crane cable meant lowering speed and re-grounding.

When backwash water swept the Sinnae dust corridor, loosened fiber pushed into the Yeouido treatment filters and raised differential pressure.

Yet cutting backwash dried skin layers and cables together, vulnerable to the smallest spark.

At maximum pressure the dermis swarm did not seal the entrance.

It set every load on the floor and stopped transfer itself.

Its way was to force the choice — disclose the possibility of water contamination, or bear the cost of stopping logistics.

G12-SC1 'The Stopped Cranes' dealt with the moment three cranes of the Sinnae freight hall stopped at once.

It opened as gray fiber knots hung on each cable.

Field staff could force one crane through to keep the medical-equipment shipping contract, lower all and re-plant the grounding rods, or cut only the knots to keep the load.

Forcing tore the cover and left the next shift's protected skin area permanently short; a full stop delayed the medical equipment being restarted by a day.

Cutting looked fastest but left airborne fiber and residual charge on the hall floor, raising insurance cost and grounding time for all later work.

The cost that never vanished was not the delay itself but whose safety had first been pushed outside the contract.

In G12-SC2 'The Backwash Backflow,' backwash water from Yeouido flowed backward into the freight hall and pushed loosened fiber toward the water-supply filters.

If field staff dumped the water, the fiber stayed in Sinnae but that day's drinking-water production fell.

Returning the water to the treatment gallery and disclosing the differential-pressure rise at once told citizens of the filter risk and shook water-supply trust.

Separating the washing hose from the water main and guiding recovery cloths manually was possible, but rigging stopped dead for a day.

No choice could trade water for media and make them never have been.

At least one of the dumped backwash tonnage, the disclosed pressure records, or the unfulfilled freight contracts remained in next season's ledger.

G12-SC3 'The Grounding Knot' occurred when two cables' tension crossed the danger value and a worker with a split skin layer unwound part of their own protective layer into a grounding knot and declared a full rigging stop.

If field staff recognized it as a just stop right, new protective-equipment standards and compensation responsibility arose, but the next shift's cooperation held.

Treating it as unauthorized work cut the immediate contract responsibility, but the dermis swarm untied the grounding knot and withdrew, and whoever rushed the restart bore the later static accidents.

Passing the load to the West Sea dock dust cover via XT02 lowered the Sinnae and Yeouido pressure but fixed a season's contamination burden on the outer labor zones.

The unrecovered water and the skin layers needing time to re-weave could not be returned at once by after-the-fact compensation.

Coexistence lay not in cleanly erasing the dermis swarm but in not hiding the price of stopping.

Cutting the cover with blades scattered fiber into the air; pushing it with high-pressure water only moved contamination to the filters.

The safe response ran in order — lower the load first, extend the grounding rods, then run low-pressure washing water into floor recovery cloths.

Dust-collector intake too was raised in stages, and loosened fiber was sealed as separate media, not freight packaging.

A worker's skin traces remained not as markers deciding passage order or trust but only as data computing needed cover area and equipment grade.

The Geumcheon District Office Machinery House, the Sinnae transfer record keeper, and the Yeouido water-supply manager had to disclose lost time, dumped water, and unreusable protected area in the same meeting.

The moment those numbers were hidden, it was not only the dermis swarm that broke, but the continuity of rigging and drinking water joining the two cities.

/hostile_groups/11/economy.en:
The main resources are wash water, replacement filter media, electrostatic scrap, a small amount of oil that keeps the skin layer supple, and organic residue.

They compete with the Geumcheon District Office Machinery House over heavy-rigging licenses and dust-work permits.

Power is spent running the dust collector, and the limit is clear.

Dust load is the economic pressure itself, and they do not expand by plunder.

When the media run out, the spread stops and wash-water use also shrinks to ration units.

The rigging ledger and the dust ledger keep separate books.

Wash water is allotted to match the tonnage of the water-supply ledger, and its hoses are not mixed with rigging coolant.

Electrostatic scrap is measured only by the length of the grounding rods.

/hostile_groups/11/escalation.en:
Fiber sticking to the walls is close to a cleaning signal.

When a fiber knot forms on a crane cable, they slow the freight and measure the ground again.

The moment the situation grows is when backwash water washes the dust passage and pushes contaminated fiber toward the Yeouido water filter.

Keeping the freight hall running raises the differential pressure of the water-supply filter, and stopping the backwash over-dries the skin layer and the cables and raises the spark risk.

At the highest pressure the swarm does not cover the entrance; it sets every crane on the floor and stops the transfer.

The on-site staff must choose which of the water-contamination risk and the cost of a logistics stop they will take on in public.

/hostile_groups/11/fictional_origin.en:
Between the Neutral Convoy City freight-dust section and the Water Compact water-filter remnant zone, rigging and hauling units exposed again and again grew a skin layer that strains out microfiber.

The Microfiber Dermis Swarm is an industrial remnant ecology, and appearance is not used to grade personhood.

The record of the early dust uproar was settled into the ecology ledger as the trade in wash slots arose.

Do not describe the traces of work exposure as a moral failure.

/hostile_groups/11/hierarchy.en:
Decisions come from the work knot that shares the cable-tension signal.
