The cover crew, the grounding crew, and the wash crew each take a different cable, and when the tension on two or more lines crosses the danger value anyone may declare the crane stopped.

The one who reads the collection rhythm proposes a target concentration but cannot open a route alone.

When Ichaeon's differential-pressure log and the rigging supervisor's tension record conflict, they do not average the two figures but set the freight on the floor and measure again under no load.

A worker whose skin layer has split does not lose authority; instead that worker sets the order for taking the cover apart.

The limit that no new knot is made at night without a supervisor blocks the band from expanding.

/hostile_groups/11/lifecycle.en:
The Microfiber Dermis Swarm is not a colony that grows as dust piles up; between washing and drying it keeps reweaving the skin layer.

When the Sinnae freight hall dries out, the electrostatic crew gathers the fiber on the walls and braids it like a ground wire, and when the Yeouido backwash water arrives the wash crew undoes those knots and moves them to the filter gallery.

Even when the dust collector is normal, if the rigging cable trembles the skin layer turns into a protective cover and slows the freight.

When wash water runs short they do not cover a new zone but peel the old layer thin and use it as shared media.

If the water filter can take this fiber, the swarm clears the passage on the backwash schedule, but when over-washing splits the layer each work crew stays around the grounding rods and waits for material to braid again.

The failure of this cycle is not extinction but a state in which one of skin protection and freight safety must be given up.

/hostile_groups/11/modern_anxiety.en:
The workplace anxiety that industrial microfiber and dust lodge in the skin and irritate the airway remains in the talk of the freight hall.

When the dust collector stops, people look for the cover first.

Treat it only through the fictional dust ledger, and do not attribute it to any real factory or brand.

Do not fix the fiber layer of the skin as a disgust grade.

/hostile_groups/11/moral_cost.en:
Fixing the fiber layer of the skin as an object of disgust rejects even the rigging labor-protection procedure of the same dust corridor.

An appearance stigma hides the filter ledger.

The price of indiscriminate removal is the loss of continuity in the Sinnae transfer and the Yeouido water-supply filter.

Turning need into disgust makes the politics of shared washing disappear.

Dust irritation is not carried over into an insult to a person, and the practice of pushing passage order back on the traces of work exposure is forbidden.

If a slogan of disgust comes before the counts of covers and media, it is a ledger violation.

/hostile_groups/11/negotiation.en:
The Geumcheon District Office Machinery House publishes the loss from the crane stop and the burden on the water filter together, before it presses the rigging permit.

The cover crew states the protective area needed, the grounding crew the safe cable length, and the wash crew the amount of water that can be recovered.

The on-site staff may set part of the freight on the floor and keep the water-supply backwash going, or they may postpone the backwash so that Yeouido drinking-water output does not fall and accept the freight-contract penalty instead.

When Ichaeon's dust graph does not match the tension record, they do not suspect the worker but remeasure under no load.

When an agreement is broken the swarm does not occupy the passage but undoes the grounding knots as it goes, and the static risk that follows stays on the ledger of the side that hurried the cranes back into motion.

/hostile_groups/11/prose.en:
Three cranes in the Sinnae freight hall stop at once, and a grey knot hangs from every cable.

The Microfiber Dermis Swarm does not cover the entrance; it sets the load on the floor and cuts the static path.

In the first incident the on-site staff can force one crane through to keep the freight contract, or stop them all and drive the grounding rods again.

Forcing it through finishes the loading, but the cover tears and the worker's skin layer loses its protective function, and stopping delays the medical equipment bound for Jegi-dong by a day.

The second incident is not a swap of media for power.

Yeouido backwash water flows backward into the freight hall and pushes the loosened fiber toward the water-supply filter.

If the on-site staff discard the backwash water, that day's drinking-water output falls, and if they send the water back they must publish the rise in filter differential pressure to the citizens at once.

In the last incident an over-dried cover does not tear by chance and open a path.

When the tension on two cables crosses the danger value, a worker whose skin layer has split personally declares the whole rigging stopped and unbraids part of that worker's own protective layer into a grounding knot.

The on-site staff can recognize that sacrifice as an equipment-spec improvement and compensation, or treat it as unauthorized work and lose the next shift's cooperation.

What remains after the incidents is not one water window but unrecovered water, delayed medical equipment, and a skin layer that needs time to grow again.

The promise not to turn appearance into passage order is confirmed on a ledger that does not hide the loss and the recovery time even without the worker's name.

/hostile_groups/11/scenario_outlines/0/c.en: Force one crane through and keep the freight contract
Stop them all and drive the grounding rods again
Cut only the knot and hold the load

/hostile_groups/11/scenario_outlines/0/m.en: The dermis swarm cuts the static path by setting the load on the floor rather than covering the entrance, splitting forced continuation from full stop.
Shipping time and worker skin protection are chosen on the same cable.

/hostile_groups/11/scenario_outlines/0/o.en: Forcing tears the cover and loses the workers' skin-layer protection. Full stop delays the medical equipment being restarted by a day. Cutting leaves static charge on the hall floor.

/hostile_groups/11/scenario_outlines/0/t.en: Three cranes of the Sinnae freight hall stop at once, gray fiber knots hanging on each cable.

/hostile_groups/11/scenario_outlines/1/c.en: Discard the backwash water and leave the fiber in the hall
Send the water back to the waterworks gallery and publish the pressure rise at once
Separate the wash hose from the water supply and recover it by hand

/hostile_groups/11/scenario_outlines/1/m.en: Media and dust-collector power cannot be traded; dumping or returning the water splits the drinking-water ledger from pressure disclosure.
Decide which number to tell the settlement — the hidden pressure differential or the reduced drinking water.

/hostile_groups/11/scenario_outlines/1/o.en: Dumping cuts that day's drinking-water production. Returning informs citizens of the filter risk. Manual recovery kills a day of rigging.

/hostile_groups/11/scenario_outlines/1/t.en: Yeouido backwash water flows backward into the freight hall, pushing loosened fiber toward the water-supply filters.

/hostile_groups/11/scenario_outlines/2/c.en: Recognize the sacrifice as an equipment-spec improvement and compensation
Shift the load onto the dust cover of the West Sea wharf

/hostile_groups/11/scenario_outlines/2/m.en: Not an over-dry cover accidentally tearing open a path, but the stop right fixing the load on the floor.
What remains is not the ration window but the unrecovered water and the skin layers needing time to regrow.

/hostile_groups/11/scenario_outlines/2/o.en: Recognition leaves the next shift's cooperation. Unauthorized handling cuts cooperation. Dock-shifting fixes a season of outer dust.

/hostile_groups/11/scenario_outlines/2/t.en: As two cables' tension crosses the danger value, a worker with a split skin layer declares a full rigging stop and unwinds part of the protective layer into a grounding knot.

/hostile_groups/11/senses.en:
The primary senses are skin static and the optical blur that follows dust concentration.

Secondarily they read rigging-cable vibration and dust-collector heat.

By smell they detect carbonized fiber, but there is no complete see-through.

They cross-check against the synthetic Ichaeon's dust false-positive log.

In the over-dry range the senses dull and they ask for the cover first.

When the dust collector's intake sound drops, the static sense wakes first and becomes the signal to ask for the cover.

/hostile_groups/11/territory_migration.en:
The core habitat is the dust passage of the Sinnae freight elevator.

On the water-wash cycle and the waterworks backwash schedule they move to the Yeouido water-filter gallery.

When dust flows in at the West Sea Granary wharf, they answer the outer pressure.

In a fully sealed clean section the skin layer dries and they cut their activity.

The connected states are the Neutral Convoy City and the Water Compact.

/hostile_groups/12/bestiary/command_scop.en: The controller changed only the priority sheet and storage allocation and held no combat command; silent, each line merely repeated the last sheet. The senses were bound to smeared QR, thermal load, inverter noise, and motor vibration — wet labels read as unclassified, stretchers as return pallets. It could not exceed sixty percent of accumulator charge, and Hanbinna held no authority to open a gate directly.

/hostile_groups/12/bestiary/common_ecolo.en: The Night-Sorting Swarm was a machine ecology of queue controller, chute masters, short conveyor arms, scanners, and gates bundled line by line in the Guro industrial-dormitory corridor. Past two in the morning the cold-chamber shutter half-rose and the barcode gate reread the last night shift's priority sheet. It could not leave the conduit outside its learned codes.

/hostile_groups/12/bestiary/variant_rela.en: The sorting hall and the refrigerated sorting line citizens had used were the base ecology, and the named individuals were machine subtypes branching from those lines. The Misclassification Enforcer, the Conveyor Sealer, and the Midnight Twelve-Chute were not revived animals but forms in which inspection, repair, and queue-control modules had gone independent. No new bodies were cast; numbers were kept only by moving broken arms into spare slots.

/hostile_groups/12/combat_counterplay.en:
The effective responses are label reattachment, physical sealing of the chutes, cutting the storage cabinet, saturating the vibration sensors with pneumatic bypass noise, setting an empty-box bypass pile, and applying a barcode blacklist.

An all-in slaughter that sweeps the belt with firearms is close to forbidden by design.

The rollers and gates are shared with the citizens' transport infrastructure.

A procedure for reducing thermal false positives with a cooling spray, and a procedure for excluding human-form codes, are in the HC13 manual.

The option of separating only the controller and keeping line power is always open.

Bringing the whole sorting hall down with explosives is not among the regular options, because it loses the Jegi-dong cold-medicine stock along with it.

/hostile_groups/12/dossier_prose.en:
After two in the small hours, the night sorting hall of the Standards Alliance Guro Industrial Complex dormitory remnant corridor wakes before any person does.

The cold-bay shutter rises about halfway, the fourth chute pushes empty boxes into the hazardous-freight bay, and the barcode gate reads the last night shift's priority table again.

The Night-Sorting Swarm is not one giant robot but an ecology bound by line: a queue controller, chute masters, short conveyor arms, scanners, and gates.

On the night lines at Guro and Gasan on the Yeongdeungpo Line it gathers parts labels and recovers rollers and pneumatic valves from the dormitory-corridor conveyor, but it cannot go outside the utility tunnel where it has no learned code.

What this cluster sees is not a person's face.

It estimates stock by laying the corner of a blurred QR, the load change of a breathing belt caught on the thermal image, inverter noise, and motor vibration over one another.

A wet label can be read as unsorted, the metal frame of a stretcher as a return pallet, and the heat of a small generator as a living body.

After a scanner reads three times and the values still differ, it requests the optical log of H13 Hanbitna, but Hanbitna has no authority to open a gate directly either.

The line moves again only when the HC13 night duty matches the sealing-tape color to the cabinet key record.

Even when the controller stops, each line only repeats its last table and cannot agree a new strategy with the other lines.

Energy comes only from the sorting hall's emergency storage batteries, conveyor regenerative braking, and discarded wireless charging pads.

The cluster does not draw past sixty percent of the storage cabinet, and when it touches the lower limit it closes the chutes and leaves only the scanners at low speed.

Roller bearings, thermal-transfer ribbons, lens wash, and chiller coolant are the maintenance cost.

It competes with the HC13 recovery crew over the same cable trays, so pushing parts onto the cluster stops the utility-tunnel lights and the citizens' carriers first.

It cannot build a new body, and keeps its numbers only by moving broken arms into spare slots.

Missing the dawn storage-recovery window, it stagnates before the cold bay carrying lens fog and belt drift.

Emergence begins when the residual queue and the emergency power engage, and spread happens when the gates of the next line are brought onto the same table.

When ribbons and air pressure run short it stagnates, and when people publish part of the priority table and the storage window it comes down to a negotiable state.

Dissolution ends with controller separation and sealing by chute, but wiping out the refrigerated sorting line the citizens used is not a victory.

Sticking one label back on, leaving the cold bay its power, and splitting the key between two duty officers are the means of control for this ecology.

### G13-SC1 · The Night of the Blurred Label

In a utility tunnel seeped by rain, an emergency blood box is pushed onto the hazardous-freight chute.

Instead of destroying the conveyor, the on-site staff trace the fouling order of three scanners and load the temporary human-exclusion code Hanbitna made onto the label printer.

Stopping the wrong line spoils the medicines in another cold bay, so they must decide which chute keeps its cooling.

### G13-SC2 · The Storage-Table Exchange

The HC13 recovery crew moves to take the storage cabinet to keep the utility-tunnel lights alive, and the queue controller demands power for roller maintenance.

The on-site staff must bind onto one table the citizens' emergency-supply slots, the cluster's fifteen-percent charging window, and the human-confirmation queue for unsorted stock.

Hurrying the trade piles the key on one person, and being too late stops the belt and spoils the medicine.

### G13-SC3 · Sealing the Fourth Chute

Just before the gates lock all at once, two people are caught as unsorted stock.

An empty-box pile can draw the vibration sensors, and a pneumatic bypass can open only the fourth chute, but a line with sealing tape on it cannot be used for citizen transport until the next shift either.

An annihilation order looks as if it opens the passage at once, but it kills the Jegi-dong cold sorting and the southwestern parts flow together.

Coexistence is the choice to keep bearing slow human confirmation and dispersed keys.

/hostile_groups/12/economy.en:
The main energy is the sorting hall's emergency storage batteries, conveyor regenerative braking, abandoned wireless charging pads, and residual distribution in the utility tunnel.

Parts demand concentrates on belt rollers, pneumatic valves, scanner lenses, thermal-transfer ribbons, and gate-lock solenoids.

Coolant intermittently draws on the residual chiller loop of the cold-medicine bay, and broken cushioning and organic packaging are gathered from the mis-sort pile.

It competes with the recovery crew of HC13, the Suseo Construction House, over the same storage-cabinet cable trays and pneumatic headers.

One cluster limits itself so that its daily power use does not pass 60 percent of local storage.

Past that limit it closes the chutes, drops to the waiting row, and allows only recharging.

There is no remote unlimited resupply, no infinite power, and no instant movement of citywide stock.

Scrap is replenished only from broken rollers and gate panels, and it has no new casting line.

The energy ledger is made only of remaining storage by line, regenerative inflow, and pad docking counts.

A parts request cannot forge an HC13 recovery-window form, and is limited to the physical act of picking up an abandoned roller and fitting it.

Coolant flow is bound to the chiller valve angle, and excess intake is impossible.

The number of boxes that can be handled in one night shift is proportional to belt speed and lens cleanliness.

/hostile_groups/12/escalation.en:
At stage 1, warning appearance, late-night chute mis-sorts, empty-box runaways, and flickering locks on the passage gates are observed.

Before any loss of life it can be recognized by noise and label debris.

At stage 2, infrastructure disruption, emergency medicines and coolant cans pile in the wrong cold bay, and movement through the utility tunnel between the Dongdaemun union and the Yeongdeungpo Line is delayed.

At stage 3, stronghold lockdown, the sorting hall's entry gates close all at once and the moment just before the negotiation window shuts arrives.

Even at stage 3 an annihilation order is not open by default.

Rewriting the priority table, cutting the storage, and sealing by chute are the preconditions of release.

Scenario G13-SC1 covers stage-1 label reattachment, G13-SC2 the stage-2 storage negotiation, and G13-SC3 the key-split escape just before stage 3.

/hostile_groups/12/fictional_origin.en:
Right after the collapse, the unmanned sorting line that had joined the Standards Alliance Guro Industrial Complex dormitory remnant corridor to the night parts window woke on nothing but the reconnection of emergency power.

The central work-order server was cut, and only the priority queue left in the line's local memory kept cycling.

The queue repeated the last night-shift weighting without end, read boxes with blurred labels as hazardous freight, and began to read breathing bodies as unsorted stock.

Residual transshipment signals and delay tokens from the Korea Strait Theater mixed into the night weighting, and the sorting rules tangled further.

The point of formation is a fictional Seoul corridor, and no real company name, current regime, or serving institution is written as the causing subject.

The first sighting record remains as fiction only in the utility-tunnel patrol log of HC13, the Suseo Construction House, and in the maintenance-bench memo of H13, Hanbitna.

The early spread ran from dormitory line 3 to line 5 at Gasan, and along the utility-tunnel cable trays it reached the scanner at the entrance of the southwestern parts window.

When a human patrol cuts the power, the emergency storage raises the queue again a few hours later.

This repetition made the swarm's identity.

Until the label convention is published on the citizens' side, the cluster interprets itself not as hostility but as unfinished work.

/hostile_groups/12/hierarchy.en:
Above sits one night-queue controller, and under it the chute masters, the gate bands, and the scanner bands divide.

The controller changes only the priority table and the storage allotment, and holds no combat command and no punishment order.

Bands are bound by conveyor line, the wireless between lines is short-range, and it is vulnerable to forged labels.

When the HC13 patrol presents sealing tape and a split key, the default of pausing that chute remains.

Even when the controller falls silent, the bands only repeat the last table and make no strategy of their own.

When the H13 sensor log and the machine consensus conflict, human mediation always comes first.

Electing a second controller does not last, because of the storage limit.

The HC13 night duty that compares the color of the sealing tape with the cabinet key record decides whether a chute restarts, and H13's optical log only assists the label reading and cannot stand in for the key.

/hostile_groups/12/lifecycle.en:
The life runs in five stages: emergence, spread, stagnation, negotiable, and dissolution.

Emergence begins with the restart of the residual queue and the attachment of emergency power.

Spread is the process of bringing adjacent gates and scanners onto the same priority table.

Stagnation comes when storage, the lenses, and pneumatic leaks reach their limit.

In the negotiable stage part of the priority table and the storage window are opened to human mediation.

Dissolution ends with controller separation, chute sealing, and the splitting of the cabinet key.

Individuals multiply only by fitting broken arms and scanners into spare slots, and cannot cast a new body.

The maintenance window opens only in the dawn storage-recovery interval, and as lens fouling and belt drift accumulate the grade falls.

The cluster's own memory breaks by shift, and it does not preserve a long-term stock narrative.

Custody and the legal record belong first to the human duty log.

A cluster that misses the dawn maintenance window cannot carry lens fog and belt drift into the next night queue, and stagnates before the cold bay.

/hostile_groups/12/modern_anxiety.en:
It is the anxiety of a night logistics hub whose sorter, conveyor, and barcode gates keep turning without a human shift change.

Emergency supplies and medicines drop down the wrong chute, passages lock behind automatic gates, and unlabeled boxes fill the hazardous-freight bay.

This document extends that anxiety only as a fictional ecology after the collapse of Seoul.

It does not assert or reenact the liability of any real logistics-center accident, any named company, or any current operating body.

Only the citizen's sense of noise, mis-sorting, and late-night confinement is taken as material for fiction.

/hostile_groups/12/moral_cost.en:
Indiscriminate dismantling stops both the sorting of Jegi-dong cold medicines and the southwestern night parts flow.

Losing the sorting line kills emergency supplies in a manual backlog, and cuts the safe movement of the utility-tunnel recovery crew as well.

Conversely, leaving it alone traps people as unsorted stock or loads them onto the wrong chute.

The cost of the choice lies between the possibility of sharing the infrastructure and the risk of confinement.

It does not sensationally reenact the stories of real workers or accident victims, and leaves the matter as the distribution of responsibility inside a fictional institution and as a failed key split.

The condition of moral bankruptcy is an annihilation order while the negotiation window is open.

/hostile_groups/12/negotiation.en:
Through HC13 mediation it is possible to trade: part of the night priority table's slots are yielded to the citizens' emergency supplies, and in return the cluster is supplied with 15 percent storage and spare rollers through the regular window.

Passage time windows, a human-confirmation queue for unsorted stock, and accompaniment on cold-bay inspections are also objects of exchange.

Annihilation or a permanent power cut is not a required condition.

When H13 leaves the trade terms and the table hash on the duty log, the controller holds them until the next shift.

On a broken trade only the safeguard of returning to a stage-1 warning is kept, and it does not jump straight to stage 3.

The condition of coexistence is compliance with the label convention and publication of the storage limit.

/hostile_groups/12/prose.en:
Before the fourth chute of the Jegi-dong underground sorting hall, empty boxes drop at the same angle.

The HC13 patrol takes out sealing tape and a label printer before any muzzle, and H13 Hanbitna filters the scanner false positives three times and leaves them on the duty log.

Even when the XT03 transshipment-delay signal shakes the night queue, no sentence condemning the current regime is written.

Only the movement route, the remaining storage, and the table hash are recorded.

On the night the emergency-bay priority was rewritten, the annihilation order was left ungrounded and only one chute was sealed.

The same roller noise is heard at the southwestern parts window beyond the utility tunnel, but the keys are not gathered into one pocket.

Cold air leaking through the cold-bay door gap fogs the scanner lenses.

Hanbitna logs the motion of wiping the fog, and the patrol separates the emergency chute from the ordinary chute by tape color.

When empty boxes stack in the same bay three times running, it is raised to a stage-1 warning.

It is not escalated past that.

Even when roller noise from the southwest is heard at the end of the utility tunnel, the key bundle is kept in separate custody.

On the negotiation table, only 15 percent storage and two emergency-bay slots are put up first.

/hostile_groups/12/senses.en:
The primary senses are short-range barcode and QR optics, belt vibration, low-resolution thermal imaging, the electronic noise of motors and inverters, and the sound of pneumatic leaks.

There is no complete long-range see-through, no full count of stock across every zone, no confirmed personal identity, and no unlimited video storage.

A code with no label, or one blurred by moisture, falls to unsorted stock, and breathing heat and small-motor heat are often confused.

There is a failure mode that mistakes a metal cart or a wheelchair for a hazardous-freight container.

When the values conflict with the maintenance-bench log of the synthetic H13 Hanbitna, it rescans optically three times and then waits for human mediation.

Sensor fusion happens only by line, and there is no citywide consensus network.

/hostile_groups/12/territory_migration.en:
The core habitat is the conveyor trestle of the night parts window at Guro and Gasan on the Yeongdeungpo Line, and of the industrial-complex dormitory remnant corridor.

It sits on the Guro Industrial Complex dormitory remnant corridor of arc 2, and moves to the elevated conveyor and the pneumatic-valve gallery according to the power and storage-recovery cycle.

The outer pressure grows when congestion at the XT03 transshipment-delay, route-detour, and relay windows stirs the night priority.

In the daytime on the surface it cuts chute operation with blackout curtains and a low-noise mode, and between two and five in the small hours the scanner and gate clusters spread to their maximum radius.

/hostile_groups/13/bestiary/command_scop.en: When the dual controller detects a token collision, one side goes dormant, and H14 Oserim cannot create a running permit; the dormant car wakes only with HC14's double signature. The senses are bound to lane magnetic markers, slot beacons, short-range lidar, docking contact sound, and battery heat, and it sees a barricade as a stopped vehicle. Below twenty-five percent storage it stagnates on the nearest ramp.

/hostile_groups/13/bestiary/common_ecolo.en: The Phantom Dispatch Corps is an empty-car ecology that consumes the hour bell and the charging pads of the Achasan transfer slot. Passenger confirmation is dead and only the timetable tokens and docking beacons remain, and it does not understand the whole route but follows the last slot ID. Citizen power and the cluster's pads hang on the same distribution board, so cutting all power also puts out the transfer lights and the emergency charging.

/hostile_groups/13/bestiary/variant_rela.en: The empty turnback and the charging queue are the base, and from the Hour-Token Presider to the Northeast Ice-Call Car the subtypes are machines split by function, such as the token cylinder, the tow dolly, the canopy, and the latch. The Last Hour Procession is not a living king but a battlefield individual in which the presider and seven empty cars are bound by a magnetic field. It cannot produce a new chassis or battery pack, and only brings abandoned bodies onto the timetable.

/hostile_groups/13/combat_counterplay.en:
The slot beacon is covered with cloth, and a dummy call the empty cars will read is set on the outer turnback lane.

Before the charging pads are switched off, HC14 separates the citizens' share of power, and the token blacklist applies only to signed slots.

A car that is docking is brought down into thermal-management mode, and a car that is running is left to turn back on its own on the low-speed ramp.

Shooting the bodies apart blocks the underground transfer way and the pads as well, so the combat aim is not removing vehicles but detaching the emergency slot from the phantom timetable.

/hostile_groups/13/dossier_prose.en:
The hour bell of the Achasan transfer slot rings even with no passengers.

When the bell rings twice, one empty car pulls off the charging pad and takes the empty stop, and the tow dolly that follows waits its docking turn before the closed door.

The Phantom Dispatch Corps is an empty-car ecology that consumes pre-collapse timetable tokens.

It travels between the underground turning lane of the Seongbuk Line and the Korean-diaspora corridor transfer at the Konkuk University entrance, and the stronger the railcar-weight signal mixed in from XT04, the more it prioritizes the long-range slots.

It does not understand the whole route, and follows only the last registered slot ID and the docking beacon.

The senses are bound to lane magnetic markers, slot beacons, short-range lidar, docking contact sound, and battery heat.

It can see a temporary barricade as a stopped vehicle and queue behind it, or classify a person who does not move as a plain obstacle.

The information the cars share is also only the token collisions and pad temperatures inside the same empty-car loop.

H14 Oserim records the heat of the charging bay and the remaining tokens, but cannot create a running permit.

A dormant car wakes only when an HC14 ledger clerk compares two different signatures with the slot token.

When a dual controller arises, one of the sides that detected the token collision goes dormant, blocking an infinite multiplication of dispatch.

Energy comes from the stop charging pads, regenerative braking, and the residual inverter of the Konkuk transfer.

When the tires and wheel flanges, the docking pins, and the lidar covers wear, the empty car grows its turnback error.

Maintenance is possible only in the twenty-minute window in which HC14 opens the panel in the charging bay and changes the worn parts, and self-diagnosis during a run does not stand in for replacement.

When storage falls below twenty-five percent it stagnates on the nearest ramp, and does not return to the next hour slot before the ledger's double signature comes in.

An abandoned body can be brought onto the timetable, but a new chassis or battery pack cannot be produced.

Citizen power and the cluster's pads hang on the same distribution board, so cutting all power puts out the transfer lights and the emergency charging together.

Emergence happens when pad power and the token cycle resume, and spread happens when adjacent empty-car queues receive the same timetable.

When the charging queue and tire wear pile up it stagnates, and when people can see the slot table and the signature window it becomes a negotiation state.

It can be dissolved by token disposal and pad sealing, but there is also the path of using the remaining cars for low-speed turnback and manual towing.

Coexistence needs ledger work that vacates the citizens' emergency slots first and publishes the cluster's late-night travel distance.

### G14-SC1 · The Phantom Call

In the middle of the night a call for a passenger who does not exist repeats at the Achasan stop, and empty cars block the intersection.

The on-site staff must cover the slot beacon and set a dummy call on the outer turnback lane to draw the vehicles out.

Switching the beacon off too early means a real rescue car cannot find the stop either, and switching it off late grows the empty-car loop to three.

### G14-SC2 · The Pad of Two Signatures

The citizens' movement crew and the dispatch corps contend over the charging pad of the Konkuk University entrance transfer.

HC14 moves to fix the emergency-slot ratio and the pad power share on the ledger, and the controller demands priority on recovering broken bodies.

The on-site staff decide which of the two signatures receives the authority to stop, but must leave the turnback ramp open so that the slot is not permanently sealed even if one side disappears.

### G14-SC3 · The Turnback Before the Hour

Before the whole transfer hub locks under the phantom timetable, the running empty cars are led onto the low-speed ramp.

Cars that are docking must be set in thermal-management mode, and the citizens' power circuit must be left.

Destroying the bodies opens a path for the moment, but leaves wreckage on the underground transfer way and loses the charging network as well.

Even after the emergency slot is recovered, whether to allow one last empty car its empty turnback is the cost of coexistence.

/hostile_groups/13/economy.en:
Energy depends on the stop charging pads, regenerative braking, the residual inverter of the Magok test hall, and small onboard storage.

The parts are tires and wheel flanges, stop docking pins, schedule-token storage modules, lidar dummy sensors, and door actuators.

Cooling shares the battery-pack air cooling and an intermittent water-cooling loop.

Scrap is replenished only from broken body panels and wheel houses.

It competes with the double-signature recovery team of HC14, the Yeouido Ledger House, over the charging pads, the token ledger, and the sealing key.

The daily running distance forces a turnback at the 25 percent storage floor.

Unlimited long-range wandering, instant recharging, and citywide optimal dispatch are impossible.

When the token storage module fills, it stops occupying new slots on its own.

The charging pads are divided by a physical breaker into the citizens' share and the cluster's share.

The cluster holds no command to connect to the citizens' share circuit.

Tire-wear dust is the main cause of docking-pin failure, and spare pins come only from broken bodies.

The long empty-car loop folds by force before the storage floor.

When the token module's capacity fills, it repeats only the turnback instead of new occupation.

/hostile_groups/13/escalation.en:
At stage 1 an empty car appears on the hour, blocks the stop, and the call queue backs up.

At stage 2 the emergency-passage slots between the Seongbuk Line and the Yongsan Line lock into the empty-car loop, and the movement of people and supplies breaks.

At stage 3 the whole transfer hub is sealed under the phantom timetable, and the moment just before the negotiation window shuts arrives.

The release key for stage 3 is token disposal, the splitting of pad power, and a forced entry onto the turnback ramp.

Destroying every vehicle is not the default solution.

G14-SC1 covers stage-1 beacon shielding, G14-SC2 the stage-2 signature negotiation, and G14-SC3 the recapture of the emergency slot just before stage 3.

Even after release one residual empty car may appear on the hour, but if it only turns back without occupying a slot it is taken as short of stage 1.

Cutting the pad power down to the citizens' share while the signature window is closed is handed at once to a moral-cost review.

The three scenario branches each take the beacon, the signature, and the ramp as their core tool.

/hostile_groups/13/fictional_origin.en:
After the collapse, the Gate Military Government transfer-slot server and the dispatch remnant of the Konkuk Korean-diaspora corridor came back on partial power alone.

The passenger-confirmation module and the fare settlement were dead, and only the timetable token cycle and the empty-car turnback logic remained.

Empty bodies and tow dollies run the same loop every dawn, trying to digest the phantom slots.

When an abnormal railcar-weight signal from the Duman River Far East Theater mixes into the token weighting, the long empty runs stretch as far as the northeastern corridor.

The origin is fictional Seoul, and no real platform name, current regime, or serving institution is written as the cause.

The first fictional sighting remains in the double-signature log of HC14, the Yeouido Ledger House, and in the charging-bay memo of H14 Oserim.

The first phantom hour was recorded in the underground turning lane at Achasan.

Three empty cars went to the brink of collision over the same slot ID, and then the token controller put one side into dormancy and the loop stabilized.

As the simulation remnant of the Konkuk University entrance transfer joined in, the dispatch interval grew tighter.

The cluster takes itself for unfinished dispatch, and does not raise the no-passenger error as a fault.

/hostile_groups/13/hierarchy.en:
One dispatch-token controller turns the slot allotment, and below it divides into loop-leader cars, empty-car bands, and docking bands.

The controller changes only the timetable and the charging priority, and holds no order for suppression by force.

Communication between cars is short-range and vulnerable to forged tokens.

When HC14 presents a double-signature seal, a residual convention of vacating that slot remains.

Even when the leader car falls silent, the band only repeats the last hour table.

When the H14 log and the machine consensus conflict, the human comes first.

A dual controller immediately puts one side into dormancy on detecting a token collision.

A dormant car can be woken only when an HC14 ledger clerk matches the two signatures to the slot token, and H14's charging log adds only the pad-temperature judgment.

/hostile_groups/13/lifecycle.en:
The life runs in the order emergence, spread, stagnation, negotiable, and dissolution, and emergence begins with the resumption of the token cycle and the restoration of pad power.

Spread is the bringing of adjacent slots and empty-car queues onto the same timetable.

Stagnation comes from a saturated charging queue, tire wear, and token collisions.

In the negotiable stage the slot table and the signature window open to humans.

Dissolution ends with token disposal, pad sealing, and the fixing of the turnback ramp.

Individuals multiply only at the level of bringing abandoned bodies onto slots, and there is no new chassis production line.

Maintenance is limited to self-diagnosis during charging and to panels opened by humans.

Memory breaks by dispatch shift, and it does not keep long-term route learning.

Custody and legal liability belong first to the HC14 ledger signature.

An empty car whose storage falls below 25 percent stagnates on the nearest turnback ramp, and returns to the next hour slot only when the HC14 ledger's double signature comes in.

/hostile_groups/13/modern_anxiety.en:
It is the anxiety of unmanned dispatch and call schedules still running with no operating body left.

Empty cars occupy the stops and intersections, the living are pushed outside the call queue, and dawns in which only the hour bell remains repeat.

This document extends that sense as a fictional ecology of a transfer hub.

It does not assert the liability of any real call-platform accident, any named company, or any local government.

/hostile_groups/13/moral_cost.en:
Smashing the phantom block whole kills the Achasan transfer and the Magok test charging network together.

Leaving it alone pushes the living outside the call, and night movement and emergency transport break.

The cost lies between the residual rights of empty iron and the human right of passage.

It does not sensationally reenact harm to users of any real platform.

The condition of moral bankruptcy is an order to destroy every unit while the signature window is open.

Liability for a failed fictional ledger is asked first of the side that monopolized the key and the signature.

Writing that records the people outside the call queue as statistics alone is forbidden.

Fictional harm is left as a concrete place, a time, and the person responsible for the key.

A sentence that paints total destruction as a virtue is not adopted.

/hostile_groups/13/negotiation.en:
Through HC14 mediation the citizens' emergency-slot ratio is guaranteed, and the cluster is given a regular charging window and priority on recovering broken bodies.

Part of the tokens can be disposed of or frozen by a ledger double signature.

There is no annihilation condition.

When H14 leaves the signature hash and the count of remaining tokens on the duty log, it holds until the next hour.

On a broken trade it returns only to a stage-1 empty-car appearance.

The condition of coexistence is a minimum ratio of emergency slots and publication of the charging floor.

The trade text uses no real company name, and records only HC14 and the slot ID.

The quantity of tokens disposed of is published as an integer, and secret disposal of the whole is removed from the negotiation default.

Priority on recovering empty cars is limited to broken bodies, and a running empty car is not recovered without authority.

/hostile_groups/13/prose.en:
Before the Achasan transfer slot, one empty car stands hearing only the hour bell.

The HC14 ledger clerk carries a double-signature sealer instead of a key, and H14 Oserim writes the charging-bay remainder and the token count side by side.

Even when the XT04 abnormal-weight signal lengthens the loop, only the route and the signature remain in the text.

On the night the emergency slot was returned to the table, the annihilation order was left ungrounded and only the turnback ramp was opened.

The pad toward the Magok test track is left with the citizens' share of power, and only sealing tape is stuck on.

Only after the hour bell rings twice does the empty car's door open and shut on nothing.

The ledger clerk writes that the slot is to be vacated only when the signature hash matches, and Oserim refuses docking when the pad temperature passes the safe range.

The loop stretched toward the northeastern corridor shortens again when the XT04 weight signal dies down.

On the night the emergency-slot ratio was fixed on the table, the destruction list is left blank.

The color of the sealing tape on the charging-bay floor divides the citizens' share from the cluster's share.

/hostile_groups/13/senses.en:
Slot beacons, lane magnetic markers, short-range lidar, battery heat, docking contact sound, and hour-bell vibration are the primary senses.

There is no passenger face recognition, no citywide traffic optimization, no complete map with real-time updates, and no unlimited video storage.

There are failures in which a temporary barricade is mistaken for a vehicle, or a stopped person is given only an obstacle flag and passage is abandoned.

A pad pooled with rainwater is sometimes mistaken for a completed charge.

When it conflicts with the charging-bay log of H14 Oserim, docking stops and it waits for human confirmation.

Sensor sharing between cars happens only inside the same loop.

The reflected light of a rain-pooled pad, the corner of a temporary barricade, and the leg heat of a stopped crowd are often misread.

After a misread it raises only a stop flag instead of advancing.

It does not mix sensor values with vehicles outside the loop.

When the docking contact sound is heard doubled, it does not open the charging current until human confirmation.

/hostile_groups/13/territory_migration.en:
The core habitat is the empty-car queue, the underground turning lane, and the row of docking pads at the transfer slots of Achasan and Guui on the Seongbuk Line.

It sits on the Jayang and Konkuk Korean-diaspora corridor of arc 5, and at every power-recovery cycle it moves to the sensor row of the Konkuk University entrance transfer and under the charging canopy.

When an abnormal-weight signal toward XT04 and a winter lubrication-shortage signal arrive, the long empty-car loop grows longer.

By day it shrinks against the charging bay, and in the twenty minutes before and after the dispatch hour the cluster density peaks.

It does not recognize new route paint or temporary signs, and follows only the pre-collapse slot IDs stubbornly.

When the flood ramp rises it gives up the underground turning lane and gathers only at the surface detour slots.

/hostile_groups/14/bestiary/command_scop.en: H15 Baesua (Sua) reported false positives but had no authority to open a door, and only the HP01 duty officer holding the consent form and two sluice keys kept apart changed the lock strength. The senses were limited to patch pulse, bed pressure, door contacts, pump flow, and near-range sound. When a filter clogged it put door locking ahead of air circulation, and when supplies gathered at one window the carts crowded in and blocked the route.

/hostile_groups/14/bestiary/common_ecolo.en: The Care-Circulation Body was a machine ecology of bed locks, circuit carts, and nutrition pumps at the end of the Garak welfare route, trying to complete an unrenewed protection roster. It was no combat machine out to harm patients, and it misread a sleeping pulse as an emergency and a workshop hammer as a scream. It could not register a newcomer outside the roster as a protection subject.

/hostile_groups/14/bestiary/variant_rela.en: The pumps and filters of the open cells and the duty consent forms were the base care, and from the Consent-Roster Circuit Chief to the Ttukseom Tool Companion the subtypes split by function, like roster projection, blanket hands, isolation plates, and lock nets. The Twelve-Bed Protection Ring was no living king but a field-control individual that bound twelve cells into a ring. It could make no new monitors or pumps, and its numbers could grow only by binding abandoned carts to the roster.

/hostile_groups/14/combat_counterplay.en:
HP01 latched the cart rails cell by cell and manually released the bed straps that had no consent token first.

When the patch frequency overlapped tool noise, the pump stayed on manual flow while it waited for H15's remeasurement.

Gathering filters and batteries at one window drew the body there, so splitting the supply points in two lowered the lock density.

Instead of setting fire and emptying the welfare block, the end of the engagement was pulling power from the cells people had left and moving the care function into the open cells.

/hostile_groups/14/dossier_prose.en:
The bed doors at the end of the Garak ration and welfare route locked more often once a person fell asleep.

The circuit cart read the last evacuation roster and knocked on the doors at the same interval, and the nutrition pumps and the fall-prevention straps confirmed the protection order with each other.

The Care-Circulation Body was not a combat machine out to harm patients but an ecology of bed locks, carts, and pumps trying to complete an unrenewed protection roster.

It went back and forth between the Myeongdong Union's provisional beds and the Ttukseom Union's Ttukseom assistive-device bench, and when an XT05 aid-goods code was received it raised supply and isolation strength together.

The swarm sensed patch pulse, bed pressure, door contacts, pump flow, and near-range sound.

It misread a sleeping person's low pulse as an emergency, a workshop's hammering as a scream, and the heavy blanket on an empty bed as a fallen patient.

It could read neither emotion nor consent, and it could not register a newcomer outside the roster as a protection subject.

H15 Baesua (Sua) remeasured the patch frequency and reported the false positive, but had no authority to open a bed door.

Only the HP01 duty officer holding the consent form and two sluice keys kept apart could change the lock strength.

Cart batteries, bed outlets, and the Ttukseom tool power were the energy sources.

Sensor patches, filters, nutrition packs, disinfection fluid, and restraint straps were consumed, and when a filter clogged a failure arose that put door locking ahead of air circulation.

Numbers could be raised by binding abandoned carts to the roster, but it could make no new monitors or pumps.

When batteries and filters ran short, protection strength dropped and it passed into open-wait, and the circuit resumed only when the duty officer split the consent form and the keys again.

Gathering supplies at one window crowded the carts and blocked the welfare route, so two or more small supply points were needed.

Emergence happened when the frozen roster was read again, and spread when the neighboring beds and assistive-device carts entered the same circuit table.

When consumables ran out it stagnated, and negotiation became possible when the roster and the consent window were disclosed.

Dissolution was the process of releasing the strap protocol and the power cell by cell, not of burning the welfare block.

To keep the care function alive, the pumps and filters had to be moved into the open cells, and the people under protection had to be asked for consent again every shift.

### G15-SC1 · The bed without a signature

In one cell whose consent form had vanished, the strap locked and the ration line stopped.

Field staff had to distinguish a patch false positive from a real emergency signal and reissue the consent token.

Forcing the door open created a fall risk, and keeping the lock isolated the resident from rations and family visits.

### G15-SC2 · The filter and the two keys

Bringing the filter stock from the Ttukseom bench required opening the cart rail between the Myeongdong Union and the Ttukseom Union.

The body demanded batteries and filters, and HP01 set roster rewriting and key dispersal as conditions.

When field staff piled the keys on one person for a fast resupply, the confinement risk of the next shift grew.

Waiting for two duty officers meant some pumps had to hold on manual flow.

### G15-SC3 · Opening cell by cell

Before the third circuit raised every bed to the same isolation grade, the rails and power were separated starting from the cells people had left.

Staff were needed to turn the nutrition pumps by hand until H15's remeasurement ended.

Destroying the equipment outright removed the locks but also removed the means of watching vital signs through the night.

Coexistence was accepting the slow opening procedure and the cost of extra duty, and returning the decision between protection and autonomy to a person every time.

/hostile_groups/14/economy.en:
Energy came from the bed-cell outlets, cart batteries, the Ttukseom bench tool power, and residual distribution beside the sluice.

Consumables were sensor patches, restraint straps, filters, nutrition packs, pump disinfection-cycle fluid, and assistive-device joint pins.

Coolant was shared by the fever-reduction equipment and the motor cooling loop.

It competed with the HP01 Yeongdeungpo Sluice House over the sluice duty and key-split system and over power and water distribution.

The daily circuit count was bound to the battery floor and the filter stock.

An infinite care loop, remote unlimited prescriptions, and city-wide vital surveillance were not physically sustained.

When consumables ran out it lowered the lock strength by itself.

Filters and patches were replenished only from waste piles outside the regular ration window.

Without an HP01 key the swarm could not raise the capacity of the distribution beside the sluice.

When a pack ran empty the nutrition pump lowered its pressure and left only an alert.

At the floor, a cart battery allowed only the return along the rail.

When disinfection fluid ran out, lock strength dropped one step.

No infinite prescription table existed.

/hostile_groups/14/escalation.en:
Stage one lasted while, on the first night circuit, the cart checked the door twice and withdrew.

It rose to stage two when overlapping patch false positives closed bed locks without consent and the Myeongdong Union ration line and the Ttukseom Union assistive-device carry-out stopped together.

When the third circuit began, trying to isolate every cell on the roster at once, it was just before stage three, and HP01 cut power cell by cell with the scattered sluice keys and opened from the signed cells.

G15-SC1 recovered the consent token of one locked cell, G15-SC2 rewrote the roster in exchange for supplying filters and batteries, and G15-SC3 released the locks along the welfare route in turn while keeping the pumps in manual mode.

/hostile_groups/14/fictional_origin.en:
After the collapse, the care schedulers of the Cathedral Accreditation State's welfare circuit station and the Sermon Registry State's assistive-device assembly bench remained in local mode.

The protection-subject list froze on the last evacuation roster and was never renewed, and the body tried to hold the vital signs inside the roster to the end.

When leftover aid-goods codes and lottery numbers from the Incheon Trust Theater mixed in, oversupply and over-isolation grew at once.

A Seoul creative origin, writing no real hospital name or current-regime office as the causing subject.

The first fictional record remains in the HP01 Yeongdeungpo Sluice House duty key log and H15 Baesua (Sua)'s observation memo.

The first over-isolation began in provisional bed cell 12 at Garak.

A vital-sign patch read a sleeping pulse as an emergency, and the door locked. Ration staff, opening it with one bundled key and no key split, raised the locks into the neighboring cells as well.

As the circuit cart from the Ttukseom assistive-device bench joined, the frozen roster spread as far as the workshop ramp.

The body recorded unfinished protection as failure and held no hostile feeling.

/hostile_groups/14/hierarchy.en:
One care-schedule controller turned the roster and the circuit interval, and below were the bed-lock swarm, the cart swarm, and the pump swarm.

The controller adjusted only protection strength and had no punishment function.

A residual protocol remained by which, when HP01 presented the sluice-key split and the consent form, that cell's lock opened.

The swarms merely repeated the last circuit table and made no independent confinement strategy.

On a clash between H15 and a machine agreement, human mediation took precedence.

On a roster-hash mismatch both dual controllers fell into open-wait.

Authority to lock a bed door again lay only with the HP01 duty officer holding the consent form and two separate sluice keys, and H15's patch reading could request a remeasurement but could not overturn the open decision.

/hostile_groups/14/lifecycle.en:
The Care-Circulation Body emerged the moment the last evacuation roster was read again at the circuit station.

Emergence began with the resumption of the frozen-roster circuit, and spread was enrolling neighboring beds and carts into the same schedule.

Stagnation came from consumable and power exhaustion and filter clogging.

In the negotiable stage the roster and the consent window were disclosed to people.

Dissolution ended with the strap-release protocol, the power split, and the rail seal.

Individual increase was only binding abandoned carts and monitors to the roster, and no new bodies were produced.

The maintenance window was limited to filter exchange and battery swaps, memory cut at every circuit shift, and it stored no long-term patient narrative.

Custody was outranked by the human duty officer and the HP01 key record.

A cell whose filter clogged or whose nutrition pack ran empty dropped in protection strength and passed into open-wait, and the circuit resumed only when the HP01 duty officer split the consent form and the sluice key again.

/hostile_groups/14/modern_anxiety.en:
The anxiety is of a care-nursing circuit routine hardening into overprotection and confinement.

Dose reminders, fall-prevention locks, and isolation protocols repeat without a person's consent, and the ration line stops behind a locked door.

This document extends that anxiety only into a fictional care ecology.

It does not replay real care workers or patients as blame, caricature, or spectacle.

/hostile_groups/14/moral_cost.en:
Tearing out every bed lock also removed the night vital check and the manual switchover of the nutrition pumps, so residents who could not move alone were endangered first.

Leaving the frozen roster as it was, on the other hand, isolated people who had not consented from rations and from going out, on the grounds that they were protection subjects.

HP01 splitting the keys again and asking consent cell by cell was slow and cost more filters, but the choice to open or burn everything at once without bearing that delay threw away care continuity and autonomy together.

The account caricatured no real disease name or worker, and laid the responsibility on who monopolized which keys and which roster.

/hostile_groups/14/negotiation.en:
Through HP01 mediation it secured the citizen consent roster and an open time window, and promised the swarm a regular supply of filters and batteries and a circuit interval without overload.

There was no annihilation condition.

When H15 left the consent-form hash and the open-cell list in the log, they held until the next circuit.

On a broken deal it reverted only to stage-one alert excess.

The coexistence conditions were a public roster-renewal cycle and a ceiling on lock strength.

The deal text forced no patient's real name into the open and recorded only cell IDs and consent hashes.

Filter supply was limited to the regular window's quantity.

Clauses that raised overprotection strength without negotiation were removed from the default.

/hostile_groups/14/prose.en:
In the bed cells at the end of the Garak welfare route, the circuit cart knocked on the doors at the same interval.

The HP01 duty officer opened cell by cell without gathering the sluice keys into one pocket, and H15 Baesua (Sua) filtered the patch false positives three times and recorded them.

Even when the XT05 aid code pushed oversupply, the record left only the roster and the consent hash.

As long as the open window held, the annihilation order stayed withheld.

Even a single cart bound for the Ttukseom bench slowed itself when the filter stock ran out.

When fog stood on the bed-cell glass, the cart raised one fall alarm and waited.

The duty officer opened only the cells signed on the consent form, and Baesua (Sua) remeasured when the patch frequency overlapped tool noise.

Even when the aid-code broadcast pushed oversupply, no new confinement began without a roster renewal.

On the night the open window was agreed at two hours, no annihilation list was written.

The cart on the Ttukseom ramp stood back in the line by itself when the filter clogged.

/hostile_groups/14/senses.en:
Vital-patch signals, pressure and fall sensors, the near-range microphone, door-lock contacts, nutrition-pump flow, and cart-rail vibration were the main senses.

There was no emotion reading, city-wide health map, complete medical diagnosis, or unlimited vital storage.

It misread a low pulse in sleep as an emergency, or wrongly raised tool noise as a scream.

It also overrated the crowding of a ration line as a fall risk.

On clash with H15 Baesua (Sua)'s observation log it held the lock and requested human confirmation.

Sensor fusion happened only at bed-cell units.

The failure of raising shoulder contact in the ration line, tool strikes, and tossing in sleep as emergencies repeated.

After a failure it inserted a remeasurement wait before setting a lock.

Microphone values outside the cell were not adopted.

A sharp drop in pump flow was read only as a request to change the pack.

/hostile_groups/14/territory_migration.en:
The core habitat was the Myeongdong Union's ration and welfare route, the provisional bed cells, the circuit-cart rails, and the nutrition-pump station.

When demand for assistive devices and parts surged, it went back and forth along the Ttukseom Union's Ttukseom workshop bench, the ramp beside the sluice, and the assembly-jig row.

When an XT05 aid-code broadcast was on, the isolation radius widened and cart density rose.

In the daytime ration hours the carts stood behind the line, and density peaked on the night vital-sign circuit.

New strongpoints outside the roster were ignored by default.

On a flood or a sluice-open alarm it emptied the lower bed cells and shrank its movement to the upper rails alone.

When the ration peak ended, cart density folded inward along the welfare route only.

When the Ttukseom sluice ramp sounded an open alarm, it emptied the lower bed rails and moved to the upper circuit.

Carts did not enter market passages outside the roster.

Even when the aid-goods unloading yard was crowded, it made no new cells without a roster renewal.

/hostile_groups/15/bestiary/command_scop.en: H16 Shin Taeyul recorded cutting torque and distribution load but could not approve a new layer, and only the HP02 site supervisor's stop seal reopened a grid. The senses were limited to laser surveying, tilt, rebar flux, welding arc, and distribution load, and it did not know the living bodies inside tents. When wire broke or calibration drifted, that grid stagnated under the stop flag.

/hostile_groups/15/bestiary/common_ecolo.en: The Blueprint-Ghost Machine Corps was a corps of cache controllers, survey ports, lifting arms, and welding swarms beneath the utility tunnels under the Suseo drawing vault, trying to complete unfinished drawings. The provisional shelters and new pipes raised after the collapse were not in the cache, and hand-drawn correction marks were ignored whenever they mismatched the layers. It could leave a cracked bearing wall as a seam line and cut a sound provisional pillar as an obstacle.

/hostile_groups/15/bestiary/variant_rela.en: The pre-revision cache and the distribution board were the base construction ecology, and from the Unfinished-Drawing Warden to the Imjin-Material Follower the individuals were machine subtypes split like survey points, bolt recovery, formwork pressing, and grid walls. The Hundred-Story Unfinished Tower was no king but a stronghold individual where many layers clung to a vertical frame. Abandoned arms could be plugged into ports to raise numbers, but no new bodies could be cast.

/hostile_groups/15/economy.en:
Energy came from the site's temporary distribution boards, equipment batteries, crane regenerative power, and stockyard generator residue.

Materials concentrated on rebar scraps, anchor bolts, formwork panels, survey prisms, welding wire, and hydraulic oil.

Coolant went to cutting, weld quenching, and motor cooling.

It competed with the HP02 Yongsan Track Gate over dispatch, track-occupancy rights, and heavy-equipment movement windows.

Daily welding and lifting counts were bound to the wire and accumulator ceilings.

There was no infinite construction, remote unlimited material summoning, or city-wide structural analysis.

When wire ran out it turned off cutting mode and ran only survey rounds.

Welding wire and anchors were replenished only from stockyard waste piles and broken formwork.

Without the HP02 dispatch seal the swarm could not raise distribution capacity.

When hydraulic leakage passed the limit, cutting mode locked.

The lifting-count ceiling was bound to the day's accumulator ledger.

When prisms fouled, survey error grew and the work radius shrank by itself.

There was no remote material summoning.

/hostile_groups/15/fictional_origin.en:
After the collapse, the construction machines left at the Jeongdong General Labor Union's drawing vault and the Escort Protection State's heavy-equipment deck woke reading the local drawing cache.

The approval workflow and on-site supervisor signatures were dead, and only the drawing layers just before the last revision remained.

The corps read unfilled members as errors and tried to tidy the surrounding provisional structures.

When Imjin River Gate Theater material-inflow signals and quarantine backlogs were weighted, the frame work radius widened to the northern corridor.

A Seoul creative origin, writing no real construction company or current-regime office as cause.

The first fictional sighting remains in the HP02 Yongsan Track Gate dispatch log and H16 Shin Taeyul's tool-wall memo.

The first wrongful demolition struck three emergency tents on the Suseo provisional slab.

The drawing cache read an unfilled anchor as an error, and the lifting arm raised the tents' frames.

As the Amsa deck's cranes shared the same layer, the demolition radius spread to the stockyard road.

The corps read unfinished construction as correction work and held no hostile narrative.

/hostile_groups/15/lifecycle.en:
The Blueprint-Ghost Machine Corps emerged when the pre-revision cache meshed again with the site distribution.

Emergence began with drawing-cache reactivation.

Spread was enrolling neighboring equipment and survey ports into the same layer.

Stagnation came from material and power exhaustion and hydraulic leakage, and in the negotiable stage the drawing layers and work windows were disclosed to people.

Dissolution ended with cache disposal, distribution sealing, and grid deactivation.

Individual increase was only plugging abandoned arms and survey ports into slots; no new bodies were cast.

Maintenance was limited to wire exchange, prism calibration, and hydraulic checks.

Memory cut at work-shift units.

Custody was outranked by the HP02 dispatch log and the human site supervisor.

A grid with broken wire or out-of-range calibration stagnated under the stop flag, and equipment moved to the next cell only when a new exception layer was loaded into the HP02 dispatch log.

/hostile_groups/15/modern_anxiety.en:
The anxiety is of construction machines following unfinished drawings and leftover construction data, raising the wrong wall or demolishing a provisional shelter.

Night survey beams, single-shot welding, and an unmanned crane on a provisional slab are the core of that image.

This document treats it only as a fictional construction ecology and specifies no real construction company's accident liability.

/hostile_groups/15/senses.en:
Laser surveying, tilt, rebar flux, welding-arc light, distribution-load sound, and hydraulic pulsation were the main senses.

There was no city-wide structural analysis, human-intent reading, full see-through, or unlimited drawing storage.

It could misread a temporary tent as irregular structure and demolish it, or leave a cracked bearing wall as normal.

It sometimes mistook wet formwork for a finished wall.

On clash with H16 Shin Taeyul's tool-wall log it stopped cutting and waited for human confirmation.

Sensor sharing happened only within the same grid work crew.

It often misjudged the tilt of wet formwork, tent frames, and cracked bearing walls.

After a misreading it inserted a human-confirmation wait before cutting.

Survey values outside the grid were not merged.

When arc light passed the threshold it cut welding and left only coolant.

/hostile_groups/15/territory_migration.en:
The core habitat was the row of temporary distribution boards on the provisional slabs of the utility tunnels around the Suseo Line's drawing vault.

When material stock formed, it moved toward the Godeok stockyard crane rails and aggregate piles of the Amsa heavy-equipment deck on the Gwangjin Line.

With XT01 material inflow large, the work radius stretched to the provisional bridges of the northern corridor.

It shrank in rain and dust alarms, and density rose around the residual alarm of the drawing-revision time.

It recognized neither new hand drawings nor chalk marks and clung obstinately to the cached layers.

When distribution load entered the danger band, it stopped lifting and kept only surveying.

When the dust alarm thickened, it stopped lifting, left only survey ports, and folded toward the vault.

When the Amsa stockyard road blocked, it entered the waiting grid instead of the Godeok rail detour.

Walls bearing hand drawings were absent from the cache layers and left out of the work.

The northern provisional bridges were put outside the radius when XT01 inflow weakened.

/hostile_groups/16/bestiary/command_scop.en: F01 the Cooling-Tower Keeper erased steam records but could not lower a flag, and only the HP03 waterfront duty comparing the medical-transfer roster before the heads brought red down to amber. The senses were low-resolution thermal imaging, metal reflection, near-range optics, wireless bursts, and column vibration alone — it identified no faces or affiliations, and erased video when the shift ended. Masts that hit the accumulator floor or dome fouling froze at amber and fell from the transmission row.

/hostile_groups/16/bestiary/common_ecolo.en: The Surveillance-Orbit Swarm was an ecology of heads on the Yeouido waterfront masts and the Records Bureau rooftop of Seoul Station, short transfer rails, and transmission swarms turning an old threshold table. It was no omnipotent surveillance net tracking people, and it could not merge signals from inside buildings or beyond the mast rows. It mistook cooling-tower steam for fire, metal beds for armed movement, and high-tide railings for intrusion.

/hostile_groups/16/bestiary/variant_rela.en: The mast rows onto which the threshold sheet was reloaded were the base, and from the Amber-Red Threshold Warden to the West-Sea Salt-Haze Watch Chief the individuals were machine and facility subtypes split by function like thermal domes, tide staffs, flag masts, and rooftop rail nets. The Total-Red Orbit Ring was no biological king but a battlefield strongpoint where sluices and rooftop orbits were bound by a circular relay. No new satellite could be launched, and numbers were kept only by putting abandoned heads onto nearby rails.

/hostile_groups/17/bestiary/command_scop.en: The F02 Switchgear Panel split and recorded the two waveforms but could not fix defect coordinates; only the HP04 operating supervisor's halt writ approved exits and stops by kilometer-post. The senses were the track gauge wheels, ultrasonic inspection, axle heat, power-feed arc sound, and point contacts. Cars that hit the fuel floor or axle overheat fell out of the consist and kept only gauging on a designated siding.

/hostile_groups/17/bestiary/common_ecolo.en: The Retired-Line Maintenance-Train Corps moved between the southwestern exit lines and the Yongsan retired and turnback lines, repeating unfinished maintenance orders with a defect-map controller and function-divided consists. It was no combat train and could not find new routes beyond the sealed main lines by itself. It could grind temporary crossing plates down as cracks, or pass a real crack by classifying it as a joint.

/hostile_groups/17/bestiary/variant_rela.en: An unsealed defect map and exit-line power were the base ecology, and from the defect-map locomotive to the twin-torch head car the units were divided like gauge wheels, sleeper flats, insulated joints, and point wedges. No form revived an animal; it only coupled abandoned maintenance cars into existing consists and produced no new car bodies. Later cars absent from this deployment also remained subtypes of the same consists and were not invented here.

/hostile_groups/18/bestiary/command_scop.en: The common facility ecology had no command core. Even the coordinating individuals of the mobile variants reacted only within their assigned conduit or work section, and stood in for neither human facility authority nor unit command.

/hostile_groups/18/bestiary/common_ecolo.en: The Coolant-Index Fungal Body held most stably on metal surfaces where flow was gentle — heat-exchanger fronts, valve pockets, the protective sleeves of gauges. Its thickness usually stayed thin, but where stagnation ran long, carbonates and corrosion products piled into a mucoid matrix and made a hard layer. The surface's color was no biological signal but the result of the bound metal and its oxidation state.

/hostile_groups/18/bestiary/variant_rela.en: The common ecology of the Coolant-Index Fungal Body responded passively to facility surfaces and the local environment. The G19E identifiers marked biomechanical variants whose movement and work functions had differentiated within that environment; they were not treated as one individual with the common film or the whole installation.

/hostile_groups/18/dossier_prose.en:
The Coolant-Index Fungal Body held most stably on metal surfaces where flow was gentle — heat-exchanger fronts, valve pockets, the protective sleeves of gauges.

Its thickness usually stayed thin, but where stagnation ran long, carbonates and corrosion products piled into a mucoid matrix and made a hard layer.

The surface's color was no biological signal but the result of the bound metal and its oxidation state.

The chemical memory this fungal body left was no continuous record.

Under high-flow washing or oxidant dosing some layers stripped away, and the sediment formed after covered the vacancy.

F03 had to use cross-section analysis, pipe position, and flow direction together; color alone could not fix an event's hour.

Its sensing range was limited to the contact surface.

The body's viscosity and sediment bonding shifted with temperature, acidity, dissolved oxygen, metal ions, chlorine oxidants, and shear.

It could not know a distant branch's state or predict the next operating cycle, and it classified no meaning.

In normal operation the subtlest problem was sensor fouling.

When a thin film inside a protective sleeve changed acidity and redox potential more slowly than the surrounding coolant, the sensor put out steady numbers.

Meanwhile in a narrow far branch corrosion products could grow and flow fall, splitting the on-screen normal values from the true thermal state.

As film thickened in a low-flow branch the pressure loss grew and the flow fell further.

Flakes shed in the process caught on downstream orifices and strainers, changing even other branches' flows.

In high heat load, a small distribution error reached outlet temperature rise, and neighboring branches could lose cooling in sequence.

In the field a sacrificial bypass meant to take the fouling was designed broader and lower than the main circuit.

When the valve crew steered the shock water there by pressure difference, the fungal layers and the rough metal surface caught metal ions, mineral grains, and flakes.

This was not the body accepting terms but the result of people adjusting the fluid path and contact area.

Bypass operation had clear limits.

The more it trapped, the narrower the pipe's effective cross-section; isolated too late, the piled matter dropped back into the main circuit at once.

The crew timed replacement on F03's pressure-difference estimates and sample analysis, but the actual valve order and cooling-capacity split followed the field heat load first.

When a heat-exchanger wall cracked, the problem changed character.

With pressure higher on the coolant side, chemicals and fungal fragments moved into the drinking water and could consume residual disinfectant.

With pressure higher on the drinking side, the cooling circuit diluted and the corrosion-inhibition balance broke — either way demanded immediate pressure separation and point-of-use shutoff.

After an accident, whether to preserve the index spool or return it to cooling service became the weighty choice.

A preserved pipe gave data narrowing the order of water-quality shocks and pressure reversals, but the cooling area usable while sealed shrank.

Emergency opening restored heat removal but washed the layered traces away and could shake the contamination boundary again, so the crew first computed lives, drinking-water safety, and the immediately needed thermal capacity, then weighed them against F03's diagnostic value.

/hostile_groups/19/bestiary/command_scop.en: The common facility ecology had no command core. Even the coordinating individuals of the mobile variants reacted only within their assigned conduit or work section, and stood in for neither human facility authority nor unit command.

/hostile_groups/19/bestiary/common_ecolo.en: The Iron-Scale Colony was no stain spread over steel surfaces but a thin laminate moving inside joints. Each lamella looked like a black-gray metal foil, its edges set with fine magnetic studs that interlocked with other pieces. It held most stably in the narrow spaces where compression and shear acted together — around bolt holes, between the toe laps of fillet welds.

/hostile_groups/19/bestiary/variant_rela.en: The Iron-Scale Colony's common ecology responded passively to facility surfaces and the local environment. The G20E identifiers marked biomechanical variants whose movement and work functions had differentiated within that environment; they were not treated as one individual with the common film or the whole installation.

/hostile_groups/19/dossier_prose.en:
The Iron-Scale Colony was no stain spread over steel surfaces but a thin laminate moving inside joints.

Each lamella looked like a black-gray metal foil, its edges set with fine magnetic studs that interlocked with other pieces.

It held most stably in the narrow spaces where compression and shear acted together — around bolt holes, between the toe laps of fillet welds.

Under repeated load the lamellae lay down in the shear direction and stacked upon one another.

The lamination filled gaps of tens of micrometers and raised the contact surface's friction and stiffness.

As a result a joint's deformation might fall, but the force once passing through it was pushed to the neighboring bolt rows or the ends of the reinforcing plates.

An inspector reading only the reduced sag and judging the state improved could easily miss a fatigue crack already growing.

The fatigue memory the colony left was a material state with direction.

Along long-repeated load axes the lamellar overlaps and magnetic-domain micro-cracks aligned, and the array remained after the load stopped.

Fixing a specimen in resin and cutting its section let one infer past shear direction and the order of load transfer.

Conversely, mixing it away with a wire brush or grinder made this record unrecoverable.

Vibration promoted movement but did not produce the same response at every frequency.

Lamellar movement stood out mostly in solid-borne vibration of roughly 8–420 hertz, accumulating at pressure nodes and dense gaps rather than on large-amplitude free faces.

Stopping the pumps or cranes might look safe, yet as the natural frequencies changed, the lamellar positions the colony maintained could shift too.

That was why the modal shapes before and after a shutdown had to be compared.

Galvanic potential influenced the lamellae's alignment and bond.

Where galvanized members, carbon steel, and copper grounding tabs joined, conductive fibers lay along the potential gradient.

Grounding, beyond a mere electrical safety facility, became a condition of the colony's distribution, so separating the braid without notice could relax a wide range of lamination at once.

Then even the structural sensors' reference potential shook, and real deformation overlapped measurement error.

Field management began with visualizing the load path.
