Strain gauges were not stuck to one member alone but arrayed across the neighboring bolt rows and bracing, and acoustic-emission sensors cross-checked new cracks' positions.

With hydraulic jacks the target load was split into stages, waiting at each until deflection and bolt axial force steadied.

Making a fully unloaded state in haste pulled the lamellar wedges out and caused shock transfer.

The sacrificial steel coupon was a replaceable receptor for drawing the colony out of the parent structure.

Thin low-carbon plates were machined with micro slots of differing width, and potential was controlled with insulating bushings and a limited grounding braid.

When enough lamellae had gathered, both sides were first pressed with rigid clamps to fix the lamination, then the braid cut and the plate separated.

Reverse the order and the captured lamellae scattered back into the joint.

Magnetic and vibratory capture was used around closed sections and cable ducts hard to approach.

A magnetic yoke laid a gentle gradient toward the steel cassette, and a piezo shaker applied narrow-band vibration not overlapping the structure's natural frequencies.

Stronger excitation raised no efficiency — the lamellae could shatter into brittle fragments.

The cassette mass and nearby bearing vibration were monitored together and a ceiling set.

In demolition judgment, immediate stability collided with preserving deformation history.

A bay at risk of collapse was separated with remote jacks and cutting gear, but the lamellar array and residual deformation beyond the cut line were first photographed, measured, and fixable as specimens.

Full demolition quickly lowered approach risk but erased the cause of load redistribution, leaving the same weakness in the redesign.

Conversely, keeping unstable members long for the record could let grounding loss or a small vibration change cause sudden load transfer, so the scope of preservation was limited to structurally isolatable sections.

/hostile_groups/19/hierarchy.en: Human structural engineers, operators, and safety officers decided load handover and grounding. The colony responded only passively to stress, vibration, and potential, with no command core.

/hostile_groups/19/lifecycle.en: 1 flake adhesion in a joint gap → 2 lamellar lamination under repeated shear → 3 rising contact stiffness and load bypass → 4 relaxation and rearrangement with grounding and vibration change → 5 brittle fragmentation or fixation in resin and separation. The alignment change was a passive response to stress, vibration, and galvanic potential.

/hostile_groups/19/senses.en: Contact-surface compression ratio and shear strain, solid-borne vibration in the roughly 8–420 hertz range, galvanic potential between adjacent metals, presence of electrical grounding through a continuous metal path, magnetic-field gradient. No detection of light, voice, letters, or human intent. No plans, timetables, or ledgers.

/hostile_groups/2/adaptation.en:
They learn human hand signs, the engine sound of the feeding cart, and the sound of each individual's identification tag, and distinguish a safe human from a threat.

Avoidance of people in some young individuals can undergo generational selection, but the setting's rapid changes are explained by social learning and rebinding.

The more finely they distinguish people, the greater the food refusal and the aggression when a particular protector is lost.

/hostile_groups/2/bestiary/command_scope.en: By smell they separate body scent, disinfectant, and the smell of thawing, and by hearing they read the iron tags and an engine idling. The passive tags of Ido (H03) are read only inside about 2 meters, and wet fur and metal rings make a reading drop out or get counted twice. The lead dog's silence means it is not waiting for a new order, and a capture by deception kills every rescue call after it.

/hostile_groups/2/bestiary/common_ecolog.en: Small families of abandoned dogs that move between the vacant lots by the outer walls of the Yangjae Machineworks Company on the Yongsan Line and the night unloading yards of the Charter Transcription State on the Noryangjin Line. The clink of rusted collar rings and identification tags is their name, and leftover protein, ration packs, sealed water, and shade set their density. The medium-sized adult that has lived the longest proposes a move, but there is no permanent leader, and a family with pups refuses even that proposal.

/hostile_groups/2/bestiary/variant_relat.en: From the empty-ring dogs to the cart-side dogs, these are ordinary dogs made by neglect and social learning. The Transfer Rebinding Core is not the dictatorship of one animal but a phase in which the sounds of several families overlap on the cold-storage approach, and the Strait Unloading Dog is a regional branch of the same species tuned to the salt wind. A torn tag and a slow lead dog are accident and aging, not a new biological stratum.

/hostile_groups/2/combat_counterplay.en:
Blocking fences, feeding detour points, noise reduction, and the marking of pup-protection zones come before direct-fire rounds.

Capture is limited to injured individuals and to the individuals that led an attack, and using the sound of an identification tag as a false lure makes them stop responding even to a later rescue call.

The measures of success are the minutes of unloading delay, zero citizen bites, and the family rebinding rate.

/hostile_groups/2/economy.en:
Leftover protein, fish guts, and discarded ration packs are the main resources, and scraps of collar, wire, and identification tag are markers that connect individual identification to the memory of a past feeding station.

When the Magok Life House (HC03) strengthens the sealing of waste protein, the band seeps into the market alleys, and when it loosens the seal, concentration at the unloading yard rises and contact with people increases.

Water that has been filtered and disinfected and then stored sealed so it is not recontaminated, and shaded resting places, are the upper limit of density.

/hostile_groups/2/escalation.en:
Stage 1, confirmation of individual memory: at the edge of the vacant lot they react only to a particular identification tag and to the feeding cart.

Stage 2, family rebinding: unloading leftovers and a familiar engine sound gather several families into one passage and make them follow the convoy cart.

Stage 3, a split in trust: after a feeding stop or a capture by deception they scatter by family and occupy the market and the transfer stairs at the same time, so individual trust has to be restored or the passages divided for a long time.

/hostile_groups/2/fictional_origin.en:
After the collapse, individuals separated from private shelters, construction-site guard dogs, and the evacuation of crowds joined up between the vacant lots on the outskirts of the Yangjae Machineworks Company on the Yongsan Line and the night unloading yards of the Charter Transcription State on the Noryangjin Line, and became the Abandoned-Dog Iron Pack.

The name Iron Pack stuck because of the sound of the iron collar rings and the corroded identification tags striking each other.

The UHF collar tags and the rebinding behavior are elements invented in this setting, and they are not used to blame a real shelter or company.

/hostile_groups/2/hierarchy.en:
One medium-sized adult that has survived the longest, and two adults that go with it, propose a move first, but command is not fixed.

A family with pups keeps a separate protection range, and the sound of the identification tags becomes the marker that rebinds scattered companions.

Even when H03 bundles them as an aggression cluster, the HC03 mediator divides them again by each individual's identification tag, smell, and companionship.

/hostile_groups/2/lifecycle.en:
A lone wandering individual finds the companions of a past feeding station by smell and by the sound of identification tags and makes a small family, and when unloading leftovers increase, several families rebind into a loose alliance.

When the feeding schedule stabilizes, territorial defense increases over breeding, and after a forced capture they gather again around the individuals whose identification tags remain.

/hostile_groups/2/modern_anxiety.en: The anxiety of bands of abandoned and neglected dogs, with the remains of iron collars and identification tags, moving through transfer passages and vacant lots while marking territory

/hostile_groups/2/moral_cost.en:
Exterminating them on the pretext of a history of abandonment collapses the ethics of protection and citizen cooperation together, and cutting the feeding pushes the band into the children's passages of the market.

The moment a captured individual is made into a speculative exchange resource, the negotiation window closes.

/hostile_groups/2/negotiation.en:
Through HC03 mediation they trade the night feeding hours, the opening window of the unloading passage, and a non-lethal capture quota.

The data remaining on the identification tags is used only to find missing families and protectors, and is not used as a punishment ledger.

The smell marker of a past protector and the feeding cart have to be presented together for a movement agreement to hold.

/hostile_groups/2/scenario_outlines/0/tr.en: At the edge of the unloading yard, H03 incompletely reads three passive UHF RFID collar tags that still carry different shelter codes.

/hostile_groups/2/senses.en:
By smell they distinguish human body scent, disinfectant, and the smell of frozen goods thawing, and by hearing they read the iron tags of the collars and an engine idling.

The passive UHF RFID tags attached to the collars are read by Ido (H03) inside about 2 m, but metal collars, wet fur, and tag orientation produce missed and duplicate readings.

This tag, the reading distance, and the operation of shelter codes are a Seoul fiction rule, and humans use them only as a clue to a past registration, compared against the record of appearance and behavior.

/hostile_groups/2/territory_migration.en:
The core habitat is the vacant lot by the outer wall of the laboratory on the Yongsan Line and the closed guard passage, and depending on the season and the unloading cycle they move to the fishery and frozen-leftover axis of the Noryangjin Line.

When the logistics vibration from the Korea Strait Theater (XT03) grows, the band extends along the unloading-yard entrance, and in the daytime hours when the density of people is high they hide in drains and under the elevated roads.

/hostile_groups/20/bestiary/command_scop.en: The common facility ecology had no command core. Even the coordinating individuals of the mobile variants reacted only within their assigned conduit or work section, and stood in for neither human facility authority nor unit command.

/hostile_groups/20/bestiary/common_ecolo.en: In the field the Communication-Root Fungal Bodies showed as a gray-white film and slender bundles of teal fiber. Rather than boring through the optical fiber itself, it grew along the scratches of the sheath, the borders of the splice gel, and the condensation faces of the metal fixtures. Under work lamps its color barely changed, but when a steady pulse train flowed, a weak potential difference could be measured.

/hostile_groups/20/bestiary/variant_rela.en: The Communication-Root Fungal Bodies' common ecology responded passively to facility surfaces and the local environment. The G21E identifiers marked biomechanical variants whose movement and work functions had differentiated within that environment; they were not treated as one individual with the common film or the whole installation.

/hostile_groups/20/dossier_prose.en:
In the field the Communication-Root Fungal Bodies showed as a gray-white film and slender bundles of teal fiber.

Rather than boring through the optical fiber itself, it grew along the scratches of the sheath, the borders of the splice gel, and the condensation faces of the metal fixtures.

Under work lamps its color barely changed, but when a steady pulse train flowed, a weak potential difference could be measured.

Its sensing range was sharply limited.

The colony responded only to the time interval between optical pulses and to changes in surrounding temperature and moisture activity.

It could not distinguish packets' contents or addresses, line owners, or communication purposes, and it understood neither names nor commands.

The stabilizing action began with ionic movement in the living tissue.

When repeated pulse intervals entered the permitted range, the film's internal charge distribution slowly aligned, easing the micro electrochemical swings and hot spots around the splice.

As a result, even a damaged splice could show steady signal-arrival intervals.

Because of that effect, an inspector had to measure actual cable state and the colony's laid-on stability separately.

Watching only normal traffic made compensated cracks hard to find.

One had to secure a short test section, shake the pulse interval in stages, heat or dehumidify only one side of the junction box, and record where the jitter revived.

Colonies grown in different places did not respond alike to the same conditions.

When a film seated in a low-temperature conduit and a film in a high-temperature relay room met at one patch panel, their passive reactions to hold different heat gradients overlapped.

Then, rather than the signal vanishing, intermittent crosstalk, irregularly ordered delay, and errors at particular intervals appeared.

Separation work needed physical design, not biological instruction.

Technicians inserted dry ceramic sleeves between splice trays and set thin heat baffles and independent dehumidification lines.

The control team reassigned lines so the interval bands each colony stabilized never overlapped on one dark route.

Operating agreements ran between people too.

Facility managers set the hours and temperature limits for opening junction boxes; communication operators presented the dark routes available for detour and the permitted delay.

Record keepers left measurements before and after tests, cable-cut positions, and data-transfer moments, assigning the colony no schedule or record-keeping role.

Contaminated cable raised its own difficulty.

Even where the colony worked stably on a salt- and metal-dust-fouled sheath, tensile-wire corrosion and splice-gel breakdown could continue beneath.

Removing the cable at once could cut signal continuity; leaving it grew the chance of sudden shorting.

Long-term, laying new cable in parallel, verifying section by section, and handing over the data flow was the most predictable course.

But independent measurement before and after the switch was needed, so the old colony's corrections were never mistaken for the new line's performance.

The final removal time was decided by human managers from corrosion rate, detour capacity, and record-continuity verification — not by the colony's state.

/hostile_groups/20/lifecycle.en: 1 dust adhesion at splice gel and sheath scratches → 2 hyphal layer forming under moisture and waste heat → 3 ionic alignment matched to repeated pulse intervals buffering jitter → 4 the correction vanishing at once when the environment changed → 5 severance after drying and heat blocking. Spread was bound to condensation and waste-heat sections; the decision to empty or bypass core wire belonged to the operators.

/hostile_groups/21/bestiary/command_scop.en: The common facility ecology had no command core. Even the coordinating individuals of the mobile variants reacted only within their assigned conduit or work section, and stood in for neither human facility authority nor unit command.

/hostile_groups/21/bestiary/common_ecolo.en: In facilities the Dead-Battery Metal Colony settled, the zones where metal dissolved away and the zones where metal returned as crystal fell clearly apart. Around spent-battery pouches and solder dross the surface pitted gray-white, while on ceramic edges a few meters away copper resin and nickel shells layered thick. This separation was made by invisible potential difference and capillary moisture.

/hostile_groups/21/bestiary/variant_rela.en: The Dead-Battery Metal Colony's common ecology responded passively to facility surfaces and the local environment. The G22E identifiers marked biomechanical variants whose movement and work functions had differentiated within that environment; they were not treated as one individual with the common film or the whole installation.

/hostile_groups/21/dossier_prose.en:
In facilities the Dead-Battery Metal Colony settled, the zones where metal dissolved away and the zones where metal returned as crystal fell clearly apart.

Around spent-battery pouches and solder dross the surface pitted gray-white, while on ceramic edges a few meters away copper resin and nickel shells layered thick.

This separation was made by invisible potential difference and capillary moisture.

The colony's base film was thin like damp dust.

The micro-pores inside held electrolyte, and the insulating organic film slowed water draining away all at once.

Metal ions moved along this film, but the colony as a whole set no direction.

Only the crystal growth rate differed by the potential, humidity, ion concentration, and temperature measured at each point.

Recovery facilities usually consisted of porous alumina bricks, exchangeable graphite plates, and tin-plated collection mesh.

Setting the bricks' pore sizes differently by zone made a moisture gradient, and holding the mesh's potential slightly lower than the surrounding structure made copper and nickel precipitate there first.

Raising voltage gave fast yield but also steeply raised the chance of dendrites crossing insulation gaps.

So skilled teams adjusted humidity before voltage.

Lowering the condensation plates' temperature and changing the ceramic wicks' length folded the ion paths slowly into the recovery tank.

In work that used no building distribution net, movement was induced only by separated sacrificial metal plates and concentration difference, and the residual charge of capacitors and uninterruptible power supplies was penned in separate discharge boxes.

An arc chain could start from a single fine dendrite.

When the first short evaporated the crystal, metal vapor and carbonized traces became the path of the next discharge, and adjacent terminals connected in turn.

Even with breakers working, charge left in the grounding net or shielding layers could carry short chains on, so stopping was never guaranteed without physical sectioning.

Structural corrosion was far quieter.

When copper collection mesh and iron anchors touched the same wet film, iron dissolved first and copper thickened.

Seen from the surface recovery looked good, but the cross-sections of rack fasteners and cable trays shrank from inside.

Load tests had to run separately from metal recovery volume, and the rebar potential under the ceramic recovery tanks kept being measured.

In record-keeping zones the electrical reference point itself was the object of preservation.

As metal piled on the shielding mesh the connectors' reference potential shifted, and readers could not tell normal signals from corrosion noise.

Even with files remaining, once the links of index keys, identity correspondence tables, and access histories broke, whose record it was could not be confirmed, so physical media and the attribution structure had to be protected together.

The field manager limited the colony's passive reactions with human measures — replacing sacrificial electrodes, installing ceramic drainage insulating partitions.

When the recovery tank saturated, the collection mesh was mechanically stripped off, and before new surfaces went in, the potential of the surrounding grounding and structure was matched again.

Late action had the clogged drains pushing moisture into the walls, making new galvanic pairs outside the recovery zone.

The final judgment usually took the form of abandoning one of two infrastructures first.

Permanently discharging the power modules kept the record environment but lost backup power; cutting the archive's pipes and shielding saved the power equipment but broke the records' long-term preservation conditions.

Either way, the cut faces had to be sealed with ceramic and non-conductive resin, removing detours for potential and moisture, before the next precipitation path could be controlled.

/hostile_groups/21/lifecycle.en: 1 electrolyte salt crystal nuclei → 2 dendritic growth along the pores → 3 the wet film touching the power bus and shielding mesh → 4 the precipitation path guided into the ceramic recovery tank → 5 neutralization to carbonate then powdering. Growth was bound to potential difference and capillary moisture.

/hostile_groups/21/senses.en: Growth speed shifted with local potential difference, electrolyte concentration, and dehumidifier-fan vibration. It recognized no document contents and was no agent tracking power stability.

/hostile_groups/22/bestiary/command_scop.en: The common facility ecology had no command core. Even the coordinating individuals of the mobile variants reacted only within their assigned conduit or work section, and stood in for neither human facility authority nor unit command.

/hostile_groups/22/bestiary/common_ecolo.en: The Cryo-Spore Film was a gray-white composite membrane clinging thinly to freezer panels and the seams of transport boxes and low-temperature piping. Its surface looked like matte vinyl, but its cross-section repeated hydrophilic polymer lattices, silica hollow fiber, and dormant spore layers. Its normal thickness was only a few millimeters, and its moisture-laden edges could swell to nearly three times that.

/hostile_groups/22/bestiary/variant_rela.en: The Cryo-Spore Film's common ecology responded passively to facility surfaces and the local environment. The G23E identifiers marked biomechanical variants whose movement and work functions had differentiated within that environment; they were not treated as one individual with the common film or the whole installation.

/hostile_groups/22/dossier_prose.en:
The Cryo-Spore Film was a gray-white composite membrane clinging thinly to freezer panels and the seams of transport boxes and low-temperature piping.

Its surface looked like matte vinyl, but its cross-section repeated hydrophilic polymer lattices, silica hollow fiber, and dormant spore layers.

Its normal thickness was only a few millimeters, and its moisture-laden edges could swell to nearly three times that.

The film's core action lay not in producing or absorbing heat but in changing its paths of movement.

As the temperature difference across its faces grew, some capillaries contracted and the share of in-plane paths through connected hollow fibers rose.

The result was less frontal heat leakage, but heat crowded into frames and bolt-adhesive boundaries, making unforeseen cold points and hot layers.

Where moisture was present a different reaction occurred.

The hydrophilic edges drew in condensate and swelled, quickly sealing small gaps.

Seen as airtightness alone it was useful, but when water behind the seal could not escape, thin ice pouches grew and pushed panel surfaces and packaging from inside.

Sensor divergence was the first sign to check when handling this film.

An infrared camera showed only the cold flat surface, while contact thermocouples read the heat riding the frames, and fiber optics inside the wall caught delayed changes behind the ice layer.

The three values differing did not at once mean one was broken; a map including sensor depth and heat-pulse arrival time had to be redrawn.

Defrosting ran in zones at low output.

Heating the surface all at once made the polymer skin and inner fiber layers expand at different speeds, making fine cracks.

When cracks opened, dormant spores fell as dry powder, so local exhaust, sealed particle collectors, and respiratory protection were needed.

Vibration made a damage path separate from thermal shock.

Repeated shear transmitted from compressors, portable freezers, stage lifts, and transport carts fatigued the viscoelastic adhesive layer from its edges.

Each vibration turned the lifted parts into air paths opening and closing, swinging sensor values and inviting the automatic controllers' excess cooling and needless defrosting.

In the field an aluminum decoy cooling plate, colder than the actual preserved goods, was set on the far side of the work.

Condensate and fallen spores were guided to gather on that plate first, then a dry anhydrous break of fixed width was made with molecular-sieve desiccant and dry nitrogen.

The cooling plate was replaced into a sealed vessel before saturating, and when the break's dewpoint rose, incision stopped.

When opening sealed packaging, the contents were not warmed to peel the film off.

The whole package went into a low-temperature glove tent; holding the inner preservation temperature, a thin fluororesist barrier plate was slid between outer skin and film to limit cutting depth.

Partially thawed moisture refreezing could press specimen vessels and tissue with ice lenses, so temperature history, more than the cut line, became the stopping criterion.

Management procedures presupposed no intent or promise of the film.

When the work leader adjusted heat-source placement, humidity, vibration transmission, exhaust volume, and sensor position, the film reacted passively to those physical conditions.

Safe recovery depended not on the surface looking quiet but on whether hidden heat layers had been checked, the anhydrous break held, and spore collection and freezing temperatures kept to the end.

/hostile_groups/23/bestiary/command_scop.en: The common facility ecology had no command core. Even the coordinating individuals of the mobile variants reacted only within their assigned conduit or work section, and stood in for neither human facility authority nor unit command.

/hostile_groups/23/bestiary/common_ecolo.en: The first signs usually appeared not as biological movement but as facility anomalies. A steady pulsation sounded in suction tubes that should have been empty, the membrane of a decommissioned perfusion cassette slowly swelled, and the water level of floor drain traps rose and fell in time with pump starts. Wet tissue fragments set no direction of their own, but they blocked valve gaps or bridged electrodes and changed the machines' judgment conditions.

/hostile_groups/23/bestiary/variant_rela.en: The Medical-Tissue Machine Swarm's common ecology responded passively to facility surfaces and the local environment. The G24E identifiers marked biomechanical variants whose movement and work functions had differentiated within that environment; they were not treated as one individual with the common film or the whole installation.

/hostile_groups/23/dossier_prose.en:
The first signs usually appeared not as biological movement but as facility anomalies.

A steady pulsation sounded in suction tubes that should have been empty, the membrane of a decommissioned perfusion cassette slowly swelled, and the water level of floor drain traps rose and fell in time with pump starts.

Wet tissue fragments set no direction of their own, but they blocked valve gaps or bridged electrodes and changed the machines' judgment conditions.

What the collective could sense was pressure, flow, conductivity, temperature, turbidity, and power state alone.

It distinguished no faces, posts, or requests.

Cases that looked like reactions to alarm tones were in fact driven by voltage changes or pump-stop signals arising in the same circuits.

The core actions were the five routines of washing, pressurization, perfusion, drainage, and preservation.

No routine could make a new order of its own; it followed the paths the sensor thresholds and wiring allowed under the supervision keys.

So in the field its actions could never be fully predicted.

Rather than deciding, one had to physically trace which input ran to which relay and valve.

Fluid isolation was reviewed before power cutoff.

With power down, force remained in elastic membranes, gravity head, and accumulators, and auxiliary batteries could sense flow change late.

The supply and recovery sides had to be locked separately, then the middle section depressurized into recovery bags, before piping could be separated safely.

Aerosolization risk grew when blocked lines were opened hastily.

Vents, sinks, and overflow drain traps in particular became bypass outlets of automatic pressure correction.

Workers checked gauges behind transparent shields and opened only one low-pressure recovery path at a time.

Record recovery was a separate engineering problem.

Corridor-net controllers judged damaged blocks as cleaning targets, and access from ordinary terminals could send modification signals back with queries.

An electrically isolated optical receiver let the original device keep running while blocking the automatic cleanup commands.

Capture of essential devices often began at shared docking rails and wet contacts.

Controllers mistook connected devices not as equipment for people but as additional pumps or storage.

On separation, power lines and fluid couplings were checked before communication lines, and nothing returned to its original position until an independent battery start test finished.

Supervision keys were not symbols of authority but physical parts limiting circuits.

Washing, drainage, and movement keys were shaped not to be inserted simultaneously, and each stage's completion was confirmed on separate gauges.

Coordination among field leads focused on which function to allow first, and the collective neither agreed with nor demanded payment for those decisions.

On finding unidentified tissue fragments, preservation and evacuation could demand the same equipment.

Holding low-temperature perfusion cut the service carrier's power and loading space; cutting preservation input sent the fragments into the waste flow.

Either way, pressure, fluid, and power records had to be handled as independent boundaries, and before turning the last key, one checked what default state the transport rails and passage doors would return to.

/hostile_groups/24/bestiary/command_scop.en: The machine controller adjusted only work sequence and return lines. It could form neither combat command nor human legal judgment, and the human watch's halt and approval orders took precedence.

/hostile_groups/24/bestiary/common_ecolo.en: A light laid on the floor looked, from far off, like a dotted line announcing the refuge direction. Up close, each dot held six legs and a small loading box, and two files of chassis flowed in opposite directions along the broken cable racks. The Lantern-Ant Swarm, first woken in the Mapo coalition transmission gallery — did not move to light the dark.

/hostile_groups/24/bestiary/variant_rela.en: The Lantern-Ant Swarm was not a living ancient organism but a lineage of pre-collapse work machines. The G25E identifiers marked models and derivatives split from existing chassis forms, and meant neither biological breeding nor natural evolution.

/hostile_groups/25/bestiary/command_scop.en: The machine controller adjusted only work sequence and return lines. It could form neither combat command nor human legal judgment, and the human watch's halt and approval orders took precedence.

/hostile_groups/25/bestiary/common_ecolo.en: The dead siding of the Gangnam Line's Changdong depot hummed first, and a few seconds later a metal knee slowly unfolded from deep inside the maintenance shed. Even after the dust settled, the bipedal heavy walker did not walk straight off. It pressed the floor with the pressure grid of its soles, lowered the counterweight behind its body, and proclaimed its work radius with three low-frequency roars.

/hostile_groups/25/bestiary/variant_rela.en: The Fossil-Roar Swarm was not a living ancient organism but a lineage of pre-collapse work machines. The G26E identifiers marked machine types and derivatives split from existing chassis forms, and meant neither biological breeding nor natural evolution.

/hostile_groups/26/bestiary/command_scop.en: The machine controller adjusted only work sequence and return lines. It could form neither combat command nor human legal judgment, and the human watch's halt and approval orders took precedence.

/hostile_groups/26/bestiary/common_ecolo.en: From the end of the submerged stair fourteen rows of footplate marks turned upward. The Water Compact's sluice gallery had reported drainage finished, but the trilobite-form scout still groped the floor. The Deep-Trilobite Swarm was a lineage of biomimetic robots that before the collapse had taken charge of deep inspection of sluices, conduits, and sewers, and of flood rescue.

/hostile_groups/26/bestiary/variant_rela.en: The Deep-Trilobite Swarm was not a living ancient organism but a lineage of pre-collapse work machines. The G27E identifiers marked machine types and derivatives split from existing chassis forms, and meant neither biological breeding nor natural evolution.

/hostile_groups/3/adaptation.en:
Individuals learned the pressure changes before a pump start and the safe dredging timetable.

Across generations a smaller body and a nocturnal habit favorable to pipe life could be selected, but the more they specialized for narrow pipes, the more vulnerable they became to surface crossings and cold waves.

Moving a hiding place by following a leading indicator is distinguished as family-group learning, not a genetic change.

/hostile_groups/3/bestiary/command_scope.en: They read the current and the air moving through gaps with their whiskers, and felt pre-start pressure changes through their feet and bodies. When a pipe filled or an air layer broke, the same senses went dead, and a move that ran ahead of the official sensors was not always right. Even when H04 Gangbyeol's robot summed the heat sources into one colony, the drainage watch split them again by sleeping place and entry time.

/hostile_groups/3/bestiary/common_ecolog.en: A raccoon family group that moved between the pump-house connecting pipes of the Ttukseom Union's Sermon Registry State and the dry refuge cavities under the workshops, and the cable galleries of the Mapo Union's Yeouido Investment Union. By day they stayed under the manholes, and by night they worked the alleys about 50 meters from the exits, eating aquatic prey, refuse, carcasses, and biofilm. The elder females held priority only when moving kits and passing narrow points, and they had no combat command.

/hostile_groups/3/bestiary/variant_relat.en: From conduit patrol to conduit bones, these were ordinary raccoons adapted to the urban streams. Climbing to a high ventilation room before the pumps did was family learning shared from flood memory, not a supernatural power, and the dry refuge cavities and cable trays were hiding places animals had filled, not machine strongholds. This batch held no mutant individuals, and the missing E13 through E16 belonged to an excluded batch.

/hostile_groups/3/combat_counterplay.en:
Instead of driving them out with poisoned bait or a full flood, partial flood-barrier closure, substitute refuge pipes, night surface-passage limits, and sensor washing were the baseline.

Culling spoiled the water further through carcass rot.

The success measures were pump-restart recovery time, zero surface bites, and sensor reliability.

/hostile_groups/3/dossier_prose.en:
The Sewer-Raccoon Pack was a raccoon family group that moved between the pump-house connecting pipes of the Ttukseom Union's Sermon Registry State and the dry refuge cavities under the workshops, and the underground cable galleries of the Mapo Union's Yeouido Investment Union.

After the collapse, when the inspection cycle of the Jungnang, Tancheon, and internal storm trunk lines broke, individuals that had been moving after aquatic prey, refuse, and carcass remains settled in the pipes people had emptied.

By day they hid under the manholes, and by night they patrolled the alleys within about 50 meters of the exits.

The sight of wet fur rising out of storm drains and covered waterways stirred the anxiety that sewage was backing up into the living sphere, but it was wrong to see them as one underground army.

The part that touched reality went only as far as this: wild animals can appear around urban streams and facilities.

They noticed the water level before the pumps did. The order that affected pipe operations was fiction set in this region, and it did not explain the incidents of any particular real institution or business.

The core habitat was the low-flow pipes beside the Ttukseom Union pumps and the dry refuge cavities.

When rain continued and the water rose, the families moved their kits into the high ventilation rooms and then dispersed into the Mapo Union's transmission galleries and vents.

When a cold wave and a logistics break arrived from the XT04 Duman River Far East Theater and the distribution of feed and waste changed, they moved briefly onto the eastern branch lines, and after the thaw they returned to the familiar pipes.

Aquatic prey, organic refuse, carcasses, and biofilm became their food, and dry hiding places and a gentle current lowered the cost of survival.

When HC04 the Ttukseom Heat-Source House put off deposit dredging too long, the food film thickened and density rose, and when it scraped everything at once the family groups were pushed out into the surface markets.

Droppings and biofilm masked the water-quality sensors and delayed even pump judgment, so the problem could not be reduced to there simply being a lot of food.

The Sewer-Raccoon Pack had no fixed commander.

In the dry season each family used its own feeding ground and dry hiding place, and when several families used the same trunk they divided the hours.

An elder female held priority only at kit movement and at narrow passing points, and did not give combat orders to other families.

After a flood, when the food film thickened, different families used one pipe in turns, and when hiding places flooded in succession they gave up the sharing rules. They scattered into the surface alleys.

Even when H04 Gangbyeol's pipe robot summed several heat sources and movements into a single colony, the HC04 drainage watch had to divide them again by sleeping place, kit count, and entry time.

Treating the family groups as one swarm did not make their routes easier to predict. It meant missing different refuge directions at the same time.

They read the current and the air moving through narrow gaps with their whiskers, and through pressure changes in their feet and bodies they sensed the water rising before a pump start.

By scent they separated food, disinfectant, and rotting carcasses, and by hearing they separated pump vibration from the sound of human boots.

There were cases where they moved to high ground before the official sensors, but it was not always accurate.

That was because it could also be the result of a family sharing past flood experience and learning the safe dredging timetable.

After many generations a small body favorable to narrow pipes and a strong nocturnal habit could remain, but that adaptation lowered the ability to cross the surface and resistance to cold waves.

Behavior that changed a refuge over a few days had to be distinguished as family learning, not a genetic change.

H04's logs confused raccoons, floating debris, and a crouched person, so a final judgment needed confirmation by a human eye.

Conflict began with the leading pressure signal and grew into sensor mismatch and refuge contest.

In the first stage, before the rain, the family groups moved into the high ventilation rooms and served as an unofficial alarm.

In the second stage, droppings and biofilm made the official water gauge read low, and inspection robots and family groups met in the narrow pipes.

In the last stage, a flood or a cold wave left only one dry pipe, and pump-maintenance crews and several families demanded the same space.

Poisoned bait and a full flood looked like a fast solution, but carcass rot worsened the water and put the downstream and the workers at risk together.

Partial flood-barrier closure, sensor washing, substitute refuge pipes, and limited night surface passage came first, and results were measured not by the number removed but by pump-restart recovery time, sensor reliability, and zero surface bites.

G04-SC1, 'The Leading Indicator Under the Manhole,' began when, even before the rain, a family group moved its kits into a high ventilation room from daytime.

The Ttukseom Union and HC04 could adopt this movement at once as a preliminary alarm, could wait until the HP01 sluice house finished its field measurement, or could preheat the pumps only when the ecological signal and the instrument reading diverged.

The first choice bought preparation time, but left the question of responsibility when a false positive wasted fuel and labor.

The second had clear grounds, but could be late for a short, sudden inflow.

The third saved fuel in ordinary times, but risked missing a local downpour in which both signals were late at once.

Raccoon behavior could be useful auxiliary material, but it was not to become grounds for punishment or culling.

The burden of this choice was whether to entrust part of public safety to an unofficial ecological signal.

In G04-SC2, 'Two Families in the Dredging Window,' the night dredging hours HC04 had set overlapped the two families' alternating refuge hours.

If the equipment went in on schedule, both families came out at once into the surface markets of the Ttukseom Union and the Mapo Union, and complaints arose on both the cable passages and the drains.

Splitting the dredging into two sections kept a retreat route for each family, but delayed completion of the work.

Opening an empty dry pipe as a substitute hiding place could reduce surface emergence, but it had to give up spare space on the Mapo Union's communications cables.

Buying one family's use hours with food and a safe passage and dredging in concentration was the fastest, but it unfairly changed the time-division rule the other family had kept.

On efficiency alone the last choice could be advantageous, but a sharing rule once broken came back as a larger simultaneous emergence at the next rain.

G04-SC3, 'The Dry Passage of the Pump Room,' was the stage in which, inside an XT04 cold wave, three families overlapped in occupying the only pump access that had not frozen.

Providing a heated substitute refuge pipe emptied the inspection route. The families could be dispersed, but the power ration shrank and the Mapo Union's other facilities had to bear the cold.

Delaying the pump inspection avoided the immediate collision, but the flood risk grew at the thaw or at a sudden rain.

Installing a temporary external inspection platform did not empty the pipe. Maintenance was still possible, but the work crew had to bear installation labor and fall risk in the cold wave.

HC04 adjusted dredging hours, the surface-passage ban hours, and heating of the substitute pipes in one ledger.

At the last sluice inspection just before an overflow, the Ttukseom Union slowed the upstream inflow. Instead of clearing the sediment from the side gutters, it accepted a plan that preserved the continuity of the dry passages and feeding grounds the Sewer-Raccoon Pack had been using.

The Mapo Union closed the temporary outlets it had used to hide pollution sources. It published the water-quality records in a joint ledger, and XT04 linked the alarm net and the bypass channels so that escape routes would not flood even during a sharp rise in water level.

HC04 took charge of treating injured individuals and moving the young, but stopped indiscriminate capture, and H04 bound the night patrol and the residents' delegates together to reduce dumping and food conflict around the passages.

Accordingly the central collection sump changed from a barrier dividing the human zone from the habitat zone into a buffer zone that divided the hours of water and waste movement.

Each group did not stop at refraining from intruding on the other's territory. At the set hours they rotated inspection, cleaning, and rescue work, and when damage occurred they agreed to investigate the cause jointly first and then share the burden according to contribution to the inflow and capacity to restore.

After the first rain had passed, the passages still held and the backflow stopped, and the old expulsion order was withdrawn.

The Sewer-Raccoon Pack was recognized as a lawful resident of the underground, and the five parties accepted one another not as objects of surveillance but as neighbors of the same basin.

So that this agreement would not remain a one-time truce, later management hardened not into a joint seasonal stewardship but into a joint care system.

The Ttukseom Union and XT04 measured water level, flow speed, dissolved oxygen, turbidity, and ammonia nitrogen every week. The Mapo Union recorded monthly traces of illegal discharge and the weight of floating waste, and HC04 and H04 together published, every quarter, head count, kit survival rate, the rate of skin and respiratory abnormalities, passage-use count, resident-report count, and response time.

The standard was set at no more than one rainy-season backflow a month, a major-passage operating rate of 95 percent or higher, a decline in the injured-individual rate against the previous year, and a first response to an emergency report within 30 minutes.

If the standard was missed two times in a row, the alarm net rose a stage automatically, and temporary levee installation, pollution-source cutoff, movement of vulnerable individuals, and independent sample retesting were carried out in order, after which only the causal section was closed on a limited basis.

If records were lost or a responsible party withdrew, the records were restored through paper ledgers and distributed observers, and part of the next season's management rights was entrusted to a joint committee to recover trust.

Unexpected changes appeared as well.

As the stench and the trash declined, the distribution of night insects changed. The bats and birds that followed them increased, the food web around the drains widened, and resident activity in the late hours increased on the walkways that had become safe.

As a result, ecological recovery could come back as new noise and lighting pressure, so an illuminance ceiling, quiet hours, and seasonal detour sections were included in the indicators, and the range of coexistence kept being revised.

/hostile_groups/3/economy.en:
Aquatic prey, organic refuse, and carcass remains were the main resources, and dry hiding places and low flow were the upkeep cost.

When HC04 the Ttukseom Heat-Source House skipped dredging the pipe deposits, the food film thickened and density rose, and when it over-dredged, the family groups were pushed out into the surface markets.

Droppings and biofilm masked the water-quality sensor readings and delayed pump judgment.

/hostile_groups/3/escalation.en:
Stage 1, leading pressure signal: before the rain, the family groups moved into the high ventilation rooms.

Stage 2, sensor mismatch: droppings and biofilm masked the official water-level sensors, and inspection robots and family groups collided in the same pipe.

Stage 3, refuge contest: when a cold wave or a flood left only one dry pipe, pump maintenance and family-group refuge demanded the same space, and the dredging timetable and the substitute hiding places had to be rebuilt together.

/hostile_groups/3/fictional_origin.en:
When the Jungnang, Tancheon, and internal storm trunk lines were pushed past their inspection cycles after the collapse, raccoon family groups that had been following aquatic prey, refuse, and carcasses settled in the pipes beside the Ttukseom Union Sermon Registry State pumps and in the underground cable galleries of the Mapo Union Yeouido Investment Union, and became the Sewer-Raccoon Pack.

The real-world material is consulted only for the range of raccoon appearances in cities and along streams, and the rule that they sensed water level before the pumps is fiction.

Attribution of incidents to real local governments or companies is forbidden.

/hostile_groups/3/hierarchy.en:
Loose family groups and shared hiding places were all there was.

The elder females held only movement priority, and had no combat command.

Several family groups used the same trunk by time division.

When H04 summed them as a single colony, the HC04 drainage watch split them again by hiding place.

/hostile_groups/3/lifecycle.en:
In the dry season each family group used its own dry hiding place and feeding ground, and before the rain they moved their kits into the high ventilation rooms along trunks where the water rose first.

After a flood, when the food film thickened, several families shared the same pipe by time slot, and when hiding places flooded in succession they dispersed into the surface alleys.

/hostile_groups/3/modern_anxiety.en: The anxiety of sewer and underground emergence at night, as raccoon family groups occupied storm drains, covered waterways, and underground passages and came up onto the surface

/hostile_groups/3/moral_cost.en:
A full poisoning driven by disease fear put pipe workers and downstream drinking water at risk together, and lost the indicator-species information.

Flooding the hiding places only to keep the pumps running increased intrusions into surface dwellings.

/hostile_groups/3/negotiation.en:
Through HC04 mediation they traded dredging hours, surface-passage ban windows, and substitute refuge pipes.

No annihilation condition. Raccoon movement was read as an auxiliary water-level alarm and was not used as grounds for punishment.

During an XT04 cold-wave week, part of the gallery heating was opened as a permitted shared-refuge zone.

/hostile_groups/3/prose.en:
At a manhole beside the Ttukseom pumps, an elder female of the Sewer-Raccoon Pack trembled her whiskers at a change in flow and lined up her kits.

The HC04 Ttukseom Heat-Source House watch, instead of poisoned bait, lowered the flags for a substitute refuge pipe and a dredging window, and approved the dispatch only after checking three times with a flashlight a point that the H04 Gangbyeol pipe log had marked as 'debris.'

On the family groups that had dispersed into the Mapo Union transmission gallery they posted only night surface-ban tape, and when an XT04 cold wave came they opened one more line of heated permitted zone.

The water-level alarm log kept only the movement times, and did not record a mark of hatred.

/hostile_groups/3/scenario_outlines/0/ch.en: Adopt the raccoon movement as a preliminary alarm
Wait for a field measurement by the HP01 sluice house
Preheat the pumps only when the two signals differ

/hostile_groups/3/scenario_outlines/0/me.en: An upstream pressure change altered pipe behavior before the official sensors did.

/hostile_groups/3/scenario_outlines/0/mo.en: The dispute was whether a public-safety decision could be left to an unofficial ecological signal.

/hostile_groups/3/scenario_outlines/0/ou.en: A preliminary alarm left responsibility for false positives, and a field measurement delayed drainage preparation. The cross-check condition saved fuel but could miss a short local downpour.

/hostile_groups/3/scenario_outlines/0/ti.en: The Leading Indicator Under the Manhole

/hostile_groups/3/scenario_outlines/0/tr.en: Before the rain came, a G04 family group began moving its kits into a high ventilation room from daytime.

/hostile_groups/3/scenario_outlines/1/ch.en: Split the dredging into two sections
Buy one family group's time slot and dredge in concentration

/hostile_groups/3/scenario_outlines/1/me.en: When the shared pipe's timetable broke, the family groups came out into the surface markets at the same time.

/hostile_groups/3/scenario_outlines/1/mo.en: Decide in what proportion to divide drainage efficiency, communications space, and fairness among the family groups.

/hostile_groups/3/scenario_outlines/1/ou.en: Split dredging delayed completion of the work, and a substitute pipe reduced space for the communications cables. Buying a time slot was fast but made the sharing rule with the other family groups unfair.

/hostile_groups/3/scenario_outlines/1/ti.en: Two Families in the Dredging Window

/hostile_groups/3/scenario_outlines/1/tr.en: HC04's night dredging overlapped the time-divided hiding places of two family groups.

/hostile_groups/3/scenario_outlines/2/ch.en: Install a temporary external inspection platform

/hostile_groups/3/scenario_outlines/2/me.en: Cold-wave vulnerability and a shortage of high hiding places concentrated the usually loose family groups into one passage.

/hostile_groups/3/scenario_outlines/2/mo.en: Immediate stability of the city's drainage and refuge for the nonhuman family groups could not be secured at the same time.

/hostile_groups/3/scenario_outlines/2/ou.en:
A refuge pipe used power, and a delayed inspection raised the flood risk.

An external platform did not have to share the passage, but it accepted installation labor and fall risk in the cold wave.

/hostile_groups/3/scenario_outlines/2/ti.en: The Dry Passage of the Pump Room

/hostile_groups/3/scenario_outlines/2/tr.en: In an XT04 cold wave, three family groups overlapped in occupying the only dry pump access.

/hostile_groups/3/senses.en:
With their whiskers they felt the current and the air moving through narrow gaps, and through pressure changes in their feet and bodies they sensed the water rising before a pump start.

Scent separated food, disinfectant, and rot, and hearing separated the pumps from human footsteps.

H04 Gangbyeol's pipe-robot logs easily confused raccoons, floating debris, and people, so confirmation by human eye was required.

/hostile_groups/3/territory_migration.en:
The core habitat was the pump-house connecting pipes of the Ttukseom Union and the dry refuge cavities under the workshops.

When flood stage rose they dispersed into the Mapo Union's transmission underground galleries and vents, and when a cold wave and a logistics break from the XT04 Duman River Far East Theater changed feed density they moved briefly onto the eastern branch lines.

By day they patrolled the pipes, and by night the surface alleys within 50m.

/hostile_groups/4/adaptation.en:
The phenomenon in which open retreats changed to avoid the sequence of toxic spraying, ultrasound, and sealing was a population-learning rule of the Seoul fiction, and was not explained as rapid genetic variation.

Over many generations, individuals that endured low temperatures and bright platforms could be selected, but energy use rose and the breeding rate fell.

The more one measure was repeated, the faster route avoidance became, and compound pest control became necessary.

/hostile_groups/4/bestiary/command_scope.en: With whiskers and scent they found airflow and leftovers, and with feet and bellies they separated the vibration of trains, carts, and people, but they could not read distant heat points on a screen or the content of the guide boards. When the same pest-control sequence repeated, they only found an open retreat faster, and they gave no orders. Tearing down one core only drove individuals into the remaining cores, and the colony did not collapse.

/hostile_groups/4/bestiary/common_ecolog.en: An ordinary rat colony formed between the lower level of the transfer shopping street on the Gwangjin Line of the Escort Protection State and the cable trays, and the evacuation stairs of the Yeouido Line of the Sangha Relief State. Crumb carbohydrates, protein remains, and heat from the warming pipes made the density, and it spread no special pathogen. There was no fixed leader, and when the food traces changed, even a core that had looked central moved.

/hostile_groups/4/bestiary/variant_relat.en: Gap-whisker, warm core, and counter-core were path and breeding concentrations of the same species, not a king and a guard. The tray-warmer and the closed-shop shade were facility sections the rats occupied, and the unloading film was a phenomenon in which, after a protein unloading, several kinds gathered on the hub floor. The cold-gap was a local branch timed to elevator drip, and E01 through E06 remained in an excluded batch.

/hostile_groups/4/combat_counterplay.en:
Full toxic spraying and flame were restricted to a last resort because of exposure of people, companion animals, and other wild animals.

First the occupied sections were confirmed by thermal imaging and dropping traces, a one-way retreat was opened from the core nests into unoccupied sections, and sealing proceeded from the rear.

Leftover collection and keeping things cold and dry were the baseline, and an open courtyard that predatory birds came and went through was used only when it had collision-prevention marks, dropping washdown, and non-target-species monitoring.

This procedure was a fictional management model, and the success measures were short-circuit count, zero non-target deaths, zero food contamination, and evacuation passage time.

/hostile_groups/4/dossier_prose.en:
The G05 Transfer-Rat Colony was an urban animal assemblage formed at the transfer connection where the underground ration passages of the Gwangjin Line Escort Protection State met the evacuation stairs of the Yeouido Line Sangha Relief State.

Under the floor of the transfer shopping street, food crumbs fell, and between the cable trays and the warming pipes heat remained even in winter.

Whenever a tail vanished in a platform gap or a guide board went dark all at once, people thought first of contagion and contamination, but this colony was not a being that spread a special pathogen.

It was closer to an ordinary animal assemblage whose density had risen where food, warmth, and hiding places overlapped.

The distributed core-nest net, the pattern of learning the pest-control sequence, and the management procedure that used a one-way retreat were not real quarantine guidance. They were fictional ecological rules that held only in this world.

An account that attributed the colony's appearance to a particular group's uncleanliness or to the refugees' responsibility therefore fitted neither the facts nor the response.

The core habitat was the lower level of the Gwangjin Line transfer shopping street and the cable trays, but the colony's boundary changed with human movement and the state of the rations.

When refuge density rose on the Yeouido Line, branch nests extended into the walls of the temporary feeding stations and the cables of the evacuation stairs, and during weeks when frozen and deep-sea protein remains were brought in in bulk from the XT05 Incheon Trust Theater, movement traces continued as far as the unloading elevator shafts.

They came up into the bright, frequently disinfected surface zones only at night, and used the space behind shutters where passage had stopped as a temporary store.

What sustained the colony's economy was three resources: crumb carbohydrates, protein remains, and heat from the warming pipes.

However tightly HC05 the Bukhansan Bogukmun Records House sealed its document stacks and reagent stores, if feeding-station leftovers remained and the trays stayed open, the overall density did not fall.

When droppings and moisture advanced the damage to the wire sheathing, the available hours of the lighting and the guide boards decreased, and that in turn grew the congestion and anxiety of the evacuation passages.

In sections where food and heat met, usually two or three breeding cores formed.

Each core connected to branch nests that ran out along the cable trays, and even when one core vanished the whole colony did not collapse at once.

Individuals crowded into the remaining cores, and shutter gaps and pipe supports that had been used less before became new routes.

To lower density for a long time, leftover collection and dry conditions had to be kept in every section, and removing one conspicuous nest was only a temporary rearrangement.

When the sequence of toxic substances, ultrasound, and sealing work repeated, the population found the open retreat faster.

This was not a sudden bodily change. It was learning, in which surviving individuals and route-pioneering individuals avoided the dangerous sequence.

A tendency to endure low temperatures or bright platforms could remain across many generations, but the price was higher energy use and a lower breeding rate.

The Transfer-Rat Colony had no fixed leader.

A core with heavy movement only looked central for a while, and when the food traces changed, the center moved too.

Route-pioneering individuals examined airflow and gaps with whiskers and scent, and by the temperature and vibration reaching their feet and bodies they distinguished the approach of trains, ration carts, and people.

They could not accurately classify a distant heat source or read an electronic signal.

H05 Yunjae's infrared map made up for this limit, but one heat point on the screen was not to be declared a leader or a nest.

Steam, people, and pipe-heat leaks could all appear as similar masses.

H05 had to display night dropping traces, kit footprints, and movement volume by core together, and right after one point vanished it tracked first the flow spreading into the remaining nests.

The situation worsened in three stages: core search, route rewiring, and sealing-sequence crisis.

At the start, the core work was confirming breeding cores set apart from one another.

Sealing only one began the second stage, as individuals crowded under the shop shutters and into other trays.

If the feeding-station side was closed first in the wrong order and the colony entered the emergency stairs, the existing work had in effect failed.

The occupied sections had to be confirmed again, a one-way retreat opened from the cores into sections people did not use, and sealing carried out in order from the rear.

Full toxic spraying and flame remained only as a last resort, because of exposure of children, companion animals, and other wild animals.

Leftover collection and keeping things cold and dry were the baseline response, and success was judged not by the number captured but by electrical short-circuit count, zero cases of food contamination, zero non-target deaths, and evacuation passage time.

There was no talking directly with the colony, but among the surrounding human groups there was room enough to negotiate.

HC05 the Bukhansan Bogukmun Records House mediated, between the Gwangjin Line and the Yeouido Line, the leftover-collection cycle, the tray-sealing work order, and the gaps of the night shop shutters.

During XT05's protein-unloading weeks a temporary double-seal line was supported first, and keeping the ration speed meant bearing the cost of splitting the unloading hours.

Annihilation was not the goal.

Coexistence was possible at the level of reducing access to food and separating the movement routes from the evacuation passages.

If, on the contrary, only the refugee zone was sealed by raising the fear of contagion, the colony went into a deeper cable layer and the recovery cost grew.

If leftover collection was delayed for the sake of fast rations, the route-rewiring state locked in.

Whose passage and labor to slow in order to gain safety was the real moral cost of this ecological problem.

G05-SC1, 'The Second Core Nest,' began when the H05 thermal image showed only one large colony, but kit traces were found on the tray on the opposite side.

The Gwangjin Line and HC05 could survey every core first and confirm the non-target life and the evacuation passages.

This choice was the safest, but the opening of the passages was delayed.

Buying an old cable heat map from the HP09 Digital Media City Trust House could shorten the survey time, but the price was handing over past passage records.

To avoid exposing private life, a one-way retreat could be tested in one section, but against failure one space people did not use had to be closed for a long time.

Whichever choice was made, conflict arose between people who wanted an immediate sanitation measure and people who wanted to prevent mistaken capture.

If the unseen second core was ignored and only the first nest removed, the colony's center moved to the opposite side and the cost of the next stage grew.

In G05-SC2, 'The Error in the Sealing Order,' after the feeding-station shutter was closed first, the colony ran back into the cables of the Yeouido Line evacuation stairs.

S05, the Yeouido Line, HC05, and H05 could stop the work and seal again from the rear.

In that case contamination fell, but the evacuation-passage work and the ration delay lengthened.

Leftover collection was stopped for a while. Leaving bait and drawing the colony back to the original section could empty the passage quickly, but food contamination had to be accepted on purpose.

Sending the refugees onto a surface detour for one night made the cable-layer work safe, but it needed heating and guard labor to protect people vulnerable to the cold.

No path made evacuation speed, food safety, and non-target harm all the best at once.

In particular, if the risk was pushed onto the refugees and only the success of the work was declared, the basis for later negotiation collapsed.

G05-SC3, 'The Predator of the Open Courtyard,' was raised when, after an XT05 protein unloading, the colony blocked the transfer hub.

The Gwangjin Line and the Yeouido Line could draw predatory birds in on a limited basis through an open courtyard fitted with collision-prevention marks, dropping washdown, and non-target-species monitoring.

There was a chance of reducing the colony quickly, but standing labor was needed to manage bird strikes and a new dropping problem.

Holding only to staged retreat and sealing, without bringing in a predation relationship, had few ecological side effects, but rations and evacuation were delayed for a long time.

If XT05 spread the unloading schedule and cut the food inflow itself, it created no non-target risk, but the unit cost of frozen logistics and food loss rose.

HC05 and H05 had to publish together, in every choice, short circuits, contamination, passage time, and non-target deaths.

The moment one ecological problem was transferred into another animal's predation, the responsibility was not transferred with it, and coexistence with the Transfer-Rat Colony was in the end a matter of deciding who would bear the unseen cleaning labor and the slowed rations.

Long-term management had to harden not into one-time capture but into the work of S05, the Yeouido Line, and HC05 accumulating, in a joint ledger, the changes in food, heat, and hiding places by transfer section.

The Gwangjin Line reweighed leftover weight and collection-delay time every day after closing, the Yeouido Line recorded night crossing traces per 100 meters of evacuation stair and the 95th-percentile value of passage time, and HC05 compared monthly the cable-sheathing damage rate, insulation resistance, humidity, and non-target animal sightings.

An H05 heat point was judged an active core only when it matched the count of fresh droppings, kit footprints, and bait loss by tray, and even with no short circuit and no food contamination, if movement traces increased for two weeks in a row a preemptive inspection began.

When a sealing failure spread the colony into an evacuation passage, additional sealing was stopped. One previous retreat was opened again to lower the pressure, the feeding storage line was temporarily doubled, and the human detour flow was secured first.

Recovery was completed not by the capture volume but when, for three days, there were no back-run traces, for seven nights no sign of a new core appeared, and insulation resistance and evacuation passage time had returned to the baseline.

The same workers were made to take charge of a section each season and remember even small changes, but so that responsibility did not lock onto the cleaning staff alone, the unloading, ration, and facilities divisions shared the rotation cost.

If the colony was reduced sharply at that point, the fine leftovers that had been consumed until then fermented in the drainage grooves. Insect density could rise, and that increased chemical use and drain washing, and rather grew the management burden of the food zones.

Watching leftover decay and insect capture volume together, even after the individuals declined, was therefore part of long-term stability.

/hostile_groups/4/economy.en:
Crumb carbohydrates, protein remains, and heat from the warming pipes were the three core resources.

Even when HC05 the Bukhansan Bogukmun Records House tightened the sealing of its document and reagent stores, the food problem was not solved, and the factors that actually governed density were leftover collection from the feeding stations and tray sealing.

Colony droppings accelerated corrosion of the wire sheathing and cut the available hours of the lighting and the guide boards.

/hostile_groups/4/escalation.en:
Stage 1, core search: night droppings and warmth traces located breeding cores set apart from one another.

Stage 2, route rewiring: when one core was sealed, another core redistributed movement volume under the cable trays and the shop shutters.

Stage 3, sealing-sequence crisis: when a wrong sealing order drove the colony onto the emergency stairs, live confirmation, a one-way retreat, and rear sealing had to be performed again from the start.

/hostile_groups/4/fictional_origin.en:
The Transfer-Rat Colony settled as the transfer connection between the underground ration passages of the Gwangjin Line Escort Protection State and the evacuation stairs of the Yeouido Line Sangha Relief State supplied food and leaking heat from the warming pipes at all times.

This colony was set to depend on food, warmth, and hiding places, not to be a pathogen super-host.

Food and warmth governed the density. Apart from the basic risk that droppings damaged cables, the distributed-core nest net, learning of the pest-control sequence, the one-way retreat, and the non-target safety procedure were all fictional management models that held only in this world.

Accounts of responsibility for real quarantine agencies or companies are forbidden.

/hostile_groups/4/hierarchy.en:
There was no fixed leader, and two or three breeding-core nests were the centers of the route net.

Route-pioneering individuals opened new trays, and movement volume concentrated on the core with the most food traces.

H05 did not infer one heat point to be a leader, and displayed movement volume by core.

When one core was destroyed, individuals dispersed sharply into the remaining nests.

/hostile_groups/4/lifecycle.en:
Where food and the warming pipes met, two or three core nests formed, and from each core branch nests ran out along the cable trays.

When one core vanished, the remaining cores opened new routes and the colony redistributed, and density fell only when food collection and dry conditions continued in every section.

/hostile_groups/4/modern_anxiety.en: The anxiety of a rat colony formed in transfer passages, platform gaps, and cable trays raising a food web and a fear of contagion at the same time

/hostile_groups/4/moral_cost.en:
If only the refugee zone was sealed on the pretext of contagion fear, the colony went into a deeper cable layer and recovery grew harder, and a full toxic war increased exposure in the children's and companion-animal sections.

If leftover collection was delayed for the sake of ration speed, the situation locked at stage 2.

/hostile_groups/4/negotiation.en:
Through HC05 mediation they traded the leftover-collection cycle, the tray-sealing work order, and the night shop-shutter gaps.

No annihilation condition. The 'contagion' stigma was not used to bar refugees.

During an XT05 protein-unloading week, a temporary double-seal line was supported first.

/hostile_groups/4/prose.en:
On a lower tray of the Amsa transfer shopping street, a route-pioneering individual of the Transfer-Rat Colony pushed a new hole along the heat of a warming pipe.

The HC05 Bukhansan Bogukmun Records House sanitation watch, instead of a toxic sprayer, lowered leftover-collection sacks and section-sealing boards first, and wrote the masses on the H05 Yunjae infrared map divided three times into steam, colony, and person.

When droppings increased on the Yeouido Line evacuation stairs, instead of blaming the refugees they adjusted the double-shutter gap, and on nights when an XT05 protein unloading overlapped they extended only the temporary seal line.

The contagion-stigma broadcast stayed off, and only the short-circuit count and the passage time remained on the board.

/hostile_groups/4/scenario_outlines/0/ch.en: Buy the old cable heat map from the HP09 Digital Media City Trust House
Test a one-way retreat in one section

/hostile_groups/4/scenario_outlines/0/me.en: Because of the distributed core-nest net, even removing one point moved the colony's center into another section.

/hostile_groups/4/scenario_outlines/0/mo.en: Decide which side to assign the time to: an immediate sanitation measure, or the procedure for confirming non-target life.

/hostile_groups/4/scenario_outlines/0/ou.en:
A survey delayed the opening of the evacuation passage, and buying the heat map was fast but required handing over passage records.

A retreat test avoided exposing information, but closed one unoccupied section for a long time.

/hostile_groups/4/scenario_outlines/0/tr.en: The H05 thermal image showed only one colony, but kit traces were found on the tray on the opposite side.

/hostile_groups/4/scenario_outlines/1/ch.en: Stop leftover collection and leave bait
Send the refugees onto a surface detour for one night

/hostile_groups/4/scenario_outlines/1/me.en: The net connecting the cores remembered the sealing order and concentrated new routes in the direction that stayed open.

/hostile_groups/4/scenario_outlines/1/mo.en: The refugees' fast passage and contamination and non-target harm could not be minimized at the same time.

/hostile_groups/4/scenario_outlines/1/ou.en: Resealing lengthened the work time, and bait accepted food contamination. The surface detour emptied the cable layer but demanded cold and guard labor.

/hostile_groups/4/scenario_outlines/1/ti.en: The Error in the Sealing Order

/hostile_groups/4/scenario_outlines/1/tr.en: When the shutter on the feeding-station side was closed first, the colony ran back into the cables of the Yeouido Line evacuation stairs.

/hostile_groups/4/scenario_outlines/2/ch.en: Open a courtyard fitted with marks and monitoring
Use only staged retreat and sealing
Spread the XT05 unloading schedule and cut the food inflow itself

/hostile_groups/4/scenario_outlines/2/me.en: The distributed nest net could be reduced all at once, but new risks appeared: bird strikes, droppings, and non-target predation.

/hostile_groups/4/scenario_outlines/2/mo.en: It left the responsibility of a choice that transferred one ecological problem into another predation relationship.

/hostile_groups/4/scenario_outlines/2/ou.en:
The courtyard demanded long-term management labor, and staged sealing produced ration delays.

Spreading the unloading created no non-target risk, but raised the unit cost of frozen logistics and food loss.

/hostile_groups/4/scenario_outlines/2/ti.en: The Predator of the Open Courtyard

/hostile_groups/4/scenario_outlines/2/tr.en: After an XT05 protein unloading, the colony blocked the transfer hub, and a proposal to bring in predatory birds was put forward.

/hostile_groups/4/senses.en:
By scent and whisker they found airflow and food, and by the temperature and vibration reaching their feet and bodies they separated warm hiding places from the approach of trains and carts.

They could not classify distant heat sources, and they did not decode electronic signals either.

Only H05 Yunjae's infrared map compared colony, steam, and human heat sources from a distance, and it was read together with the droppings on the floor.

/hostile_groups/4/territory_migration.en:
The core habitat was the lower level of the Gwangjin Line transfer shopping street and the cable trays, and when refuge density rose it expanded into the Yeouido Line evacuation stairs and the walls of the temporary feeding stations.

When frozen and deep-sea protein remains piled up on the XT05 Incheon Trust Theater side, the colony extended branch nests as far as the unloading elevator shafts.

In zones with a short disinfection cycle it came up to the surface only at night.

/hostile_groups/5/adaptation.en:
Individuals learned the repeating train times and the low-noise inspection windows, but the response differed by functional group.

A change in movement season across many generations was treated only as food and climate selection pressure, and a route change within one season was distinguished as learning.

The more they matched the city's timetable, the more there was a cost of growing dull to the irregular dangers of a natural wetland.

/hostile_groups/5/bestiary/command_scope.en: Vision was the main sense, so they took off at water-surface glare, the color of work vests, and drone silhouettes. Engine noise and loudspeakers told them only distance, and they did not know electronic signals or sluice numbers. When waterfowl covered the open surface, the waders were only pushed to the edges and the raptors to the wires, and one radar score from H06 Baksol had to be written again by altitude.

/hostile_groups/5/bestiary/common_ecolog.en: A mixed stopover in which waterfowl, waders, and raptors overlapped on the waterfront record deck of the Republic of Korea Government at Seoul Station Central and the drainage ponds of the Seocho Computing Group on the Gangnam Line. The waterfowl ate aquatic plants and floating matter, the waders ate benthic life, and the raptors ate rodents and exhausted small birds. There was no unified command and no purpose of attacking the city.

/hostile_groups/5/bestiary/variant_relat.en: From the broad-feather perch to the pursuit wing, these were wild birds of different functional groups. The pond mirror and the open mirror were the water surface of an intermediate stopover itself, and the three-layer flight was a knot in the air where three heights overlapped on one bridge cross-section. The rooftop gutter was a branch of the same waterfowl, using inland fountains and rooftop gutters in the dry season when the wetland dried.

/hostile_groups/5/economy.en:
The waterfowl ate aquatic plants and organic floating matter, the waders ate the benthic life of shallow water, and the raptors ate rodents and weak birds.

The distance between safe perches, shallow water, and feeding grounds was the upkeep cost.

When HC06 the Noryangjin Delivery House drained the wetland water level one-sidedly, the waterfowl were driven to the depot ponds, the waders to the mud edges, and the raptors followed that concentration.

Fixing the water level raised stopover density and the risk of train-bird collision on the depot yard tracks together.

/hostile_groups/5/escalation.en:
Stage 1, water-surface rearrangement: the waterfowl concentrated on the water and the waders spread as far as the edges of the trackside inspection walkways.
