Stage 2, chain flush: a raptor pursuit sent the flock surging up, crossing the sluice sightlines and the depot entry and exit tracks.

Stage 3, seasonal running agreement: when the same collision repeated three times, it was not a culling stage but a point at which train slowdowns during the migratory period, yard-track closures, and water-surface sections by functional group had to be decided together.

/hostile_groups/5/fictional_origin.en:
Intermediate migratory stopovers overlapped on the severed green spaces and failed restoration wetlands of the Han River, Nanji, and Amsa area, and after the collapse a management gap let predatory birds and omnivorous waterfowl form a mixed colony, and they became the Migratory-Wetland Predator Swarm.

The waterfront record deck of the Republic of Korea Government at Seoul Station Central and the depot drainage ponds of the Seocho Computing Group on the Gangnam Line were the core nodes.

Real protected-area material is used only as a reference range for migratory-bird arrival sites and wetland locations, and the negotiation rules of the mixed functional groups are fiction.

/hostile_groups/5/hierarchy.en:
There was no command system.

The waterfowl occupied the open water as a flock, the waders worked the shallow edges at intervals, and the raptors moved from the high wires and pylons following the density of the two functional groups.

When one functional group moved, the space use of the other functional groups changed because of food and alert responses.

When H06 summed them into one hostile score, the HC06 ecology watch recorded them again by altitude, water-surface zone, and head count for each functional group.

/hostile_groups/5/lifecycle.en:
In spring and autumn the waterfowl and waders stopped first on the shallow water, and when food density rose the raptors followed.

The breeding grounds were in a separate protected area, and the depot ponds were used only as an intermediate stopover.

When the water level dropped sharply the waterfowl left first, and the food relationship of the waders and raptors also came apart in a chain.

/hostile_groups/5/modern_anxiety.en: The collision anxiety of flocks of migratory and predatory birds, gathered on a failed wetland-restoration section, taking over bridge walkways, the yard tracks of a rail depot, and sluice sightlines

/hostile_groups/5/senses.en:
Vision was the main sense, and they were sensitive to water-surface glare, vest color, and drone silhouettes.

By hearing they read engines, gunshots, and warning loudspeakers, and scent responded to fish meal and rot.

They did not decode electronic signals.

H06 Baksol's radar-based altitude classification confused balloons, drones, and birds, so it was corrected by eye.

/hostile_groups/5/territory_migration.en:
The core habitat was the waterfront wetland fragments at Seoul Station Central and the drainage ponds and wire perches of the Gangnam Line.

During seasonal movement they rode the wind road toward the XT01 Imjin River Gate Theater and went back and forth on the north-south axis, and at breeding and stopover peaks they occupied the sightlines of bridges and sluices and the air over the depot yard tracks.

When the wetland dried they moved temporarily to inland park fountains and rooftop gutters.

/hostile_groups/6/bestiary/command_scope.en: The ordinary worker's main senses were skin conductivity and metal-surface micro-vibration, salt smell, and local heat points. There was no vision through walls or whole-domain interception, and after rain dilution false positives were frequent. The variants' sensing was bound to connected floors, joined metal pipes, and unshielded transmissions, and beyond those limits they could not relay swarm signals.

/hostile_groups/6/bestiary/common_ecolog.en: A night-recovery labor unit handling waste-battery leakage in the Yongsan sidings' lower level and the Sinnae transshipment hall. Guides, neutralizers, and repair teams shared the salt-concentration map and the dry walking plates, and the word burn was an alias for leak scars, not a passage license. There was no standing commander, and when concentration meters disagreed, no departure could be ordered until the Yongsan duty, the citizen observer, and H07 Jeong Uram's residual-pressure log pointed to the same rack number.

/hostile_groups/6/bestiary/variant_relat.en: Seojin and Inner Mist, Membrane-Mender, and Bandage were ordinary recovery workers who had gained conductive skin membranes. From Leak-Finder on came genetic and symbiotic variants with organs split off — sensory bladders, magnetite chests, crushing sacs — while the Cooling-Vein Keeper, Vibration-Bell Keeper, and Noise-Feeder were biomechanical branches with piping, alarm bells, and communication coils fused to their bodies. The Salt-Bridge Sealer was a battlefield unit of that variant side, not a king of the whole recovery team.

/hostile_groups/6/combat_counterplay.en:
The fastest response is not to bring the swarm down but to break the conductive path.

Lay dry walkboards, put the switch contacts into an unpowered state, and push the weak-base spray from the inside of the pans outward so the salt aerosol does not splash onto the platform.

A hard jet of water widens the spill area, and flame lifts solvent vapor, so both are forbidden.

Attacking the guide scatters the recovery crews, and then there is no one left to report the hidden pools.

The price of suppression remains as delayed refrigerated-freight time, the number of discarded gloves, and the number of contacts that must be replated, and the side that hid those costs loses priority in the next passage negotiation.

/hostile_groups/6/dossier_prose.en:
In the Line Succession State's sidings' lower level ran stains remembered longer than track numbers.

The steel trays that had held traction-battery stacks, the drainage grooves between sleepers, the white crystal lines left on the closed washing-room floors.

Just after the collapse, liquid seeping from abandoned batteries mixed with rain, and the night-recovery units inhaled the mist while moving wet scrap by hand.

Repeated contact left conductive membranes on skin and stirred strong salt cravings.

That they came to be called the Electrolyte-Burn Swarm was only a work name arising inside the Seoul creative corridor.

'Burn' pointed to the scars leakage left; appearance or scars decided neither status nor passage rights.

The Electrolyte-Burn Swarm was no simple colony growing in rain and vanishing in drought.

When water dissolved the racks' salt, dispatch changed first.

The guide reading brine marks threw dry glove scraps to find safe footholds; the neutralizers pushed weak-alkaline spray from inside outward while the repair team mended cracked skin membranes and gloves together.

As concentration rose the three teams split to move, but there was no standing commander.

Even while the guide held one section's say, two teams keeping different concentration meters checked the values.

When numbers diverged, movement stopped, and until the Yongsan duty, the citizen observer, and H07 Jeong Uram's residual-pressure log pointed to the same rack number, no one ordered departure.

A guide with a cracked skin membrane was not excluded, and only by reconstructing the contamination route that person had walked did the next one gain authority.

This authority structure was not fast, but it kept any warehouse hiding leakage from opening the line alone.

The swarm's economy did not lie in plundering batteries.

Neutralized salts, conductive scrap crumbs, coolant, and buffer were the core, each accounted in a different ledger.

The waste-battery lots and heat-resistant alloy the Guro Alloy House HC07 recovered were needed for contact repair, but speeding recovery spread the brine wide beneath the racks.

When the buffer warehouse fell below half, the Electrolyte-Burn Swarm stopped distant-shaft exploration and circulated only marked sections.

Coolant lowered mist and drive heat but was never counted as drinking water.

A dispatch family blurring this distinction could push neutralization cost onto the citizens' water supply.

So negotiation became not a market of barter but a work meeting disclosing per-line leak responsibility.

The Electrolyte-Burn Swarm provided the per-rack concentration map and the dry walking plates' positions, and the Guro Alloy House disclosed its lots and recovery order.

Field staff had to choose whether to keep on-time dispatch, abandon cold freight, or widen dry zones and cut Sinnae transshipment income.

Gunfire did not simplify the problem.

Flame raised solvent vapor, strong water jets widened the leak's area, and felling the guide removed the one who could report hidden pools.

The safest response was to make switchgear contacts current-free, lay dry plates, and neutralize in the direction the concentration meters confirmed.

The cost was recorded not in enemy casualties but in stopped train-minutes, discarded glove counts, contacts needing replating, and cold-freight cells abandoned in Sinnae.

G07-SC1 'Dispatch of the White Salt Line' began as glove discoloration was found just before the morning passenger train departed.

Passing the train spread the pool on wheels as far as Sinnae; emptying the track thirty minutes shook Yongsan's dispatch credit.

Sealing only the salt line could move things now but left no cause map.

What field staff chose in this event was not an abstract balance of safety and efficiency but whose time would be spent proving leak responsibility.

In G07-SC2 'The Off-Ledger Battery,' the lot numbers in the sidings' lower level did not match the official recovery list.

Sealing discarded two cold-freight cells; unsealing, and the swarm withdrew its leak map, losing the next monsoon's safe routes.

Moving the lot to Sinnae to spread responsibility scattered salt over passenger lines.

If field staff published the family warehouse's name, the dispatch-right conflict grew, but hiding it made the citizen corridor pay for the ledger gap.

In G07-SC3 'One Conductive Plane,' the Sinnae elevator floor electrified beyond dividing into sections.

The three recovery teams' meters read differently, and cutting hall power stopped emergency transshipment.

Having the citizen observer mark the wet sections bodily saved transshipment but shifted the danger onto particular people.

Detouring the West Sea Granary Theater XT02 frozen inflow outward fixed the pollution position for a season.

No choice ended cleanly, and the ledger kept warehouse cells that could not reopen and the exposed dispatch family's responsibility.

Coexistence was not a declaration of unconditional acceptance of the Electrolyte-Burn Swarm.

It was a procedure of co-owning the leak map, never using burn scars as inspection cause, and placing the neutralization work's risks and rewards on the same ledger.

The reason the swarm withdrew work from undisclosed sections instead of retaliatory attack when an accord was broken lay here too.

When the next rain corroded the contacts, the hidden responsibility returned as cost.

Erasing these beings alone did not remove the waste-battery leakage.

Rather, the neutralization knowledge and route memory disappeared together, and the dispatch and cooling continuity of Yongsan and Sinnae grew more fragile.

A long-term accord also included post-restoration responsibility.

A rack whose neutralization ended was not sent straight back to the Guro Alloy House's scrap warehouse but remained one monsoon as a joint observation zone.

If the salt line reappeared in that period, it was not the recovery teams' failure but the battery lot and drain slope investigated first.

Whoever sat out work mending skin membranes received rest and buffer assigned in the same units as discarded glove counts, and the risk the citizen observer took marking wet roads was not processed as unpaid duty.

Only so the body that found a leak did not become adverse evidence in the next contract, and the maintenance cost hidden between Yongsan's dispatch revenue and Sinnae's transshipment loss remained in the joint ledger.

/hostile_groups/6/economy.en:
The main resources are neutralized electrolyte salt, conductive scrap fragments, coolant, and the weak-base buffer that stabilizes the skin film.

They compete on the stretches that overlap the spent batteries and heat-resistant alloy scrap the Guro Alloy House recovers from Guro and Seongsu.

The swarm does not own the batteries. It treats the salt concentration of the drip pans as the trade unit, and excess energy absorption is capped by skin cracking.

Organic matter is only supplementary food for the night labor units, not a plunder target.

When the buffer stock hits bottom, expansion stops automatically, and scrap fragments are allotted only to contact repair and conductivity measurement.

Coolant is used to suppress mist and ease heat, and its books are kept separate from the drinking-water ledger.

/hostile_groups/6/escalation.en:
When glove color changes on the siding and a white crystal line forms along the pan edges, the recovery crew raises the first alarm.

When brine reaches the switch contacts and the dispatch signal wavers, night running on that track is reduced and neutralizing labor is concentrated.

The most dangerous moment is when the whole metal floor of the Sinnae freight elevator connects as a single conductive surface.

Then, instead of occupying the hall, they cut the elevator power and demand dry walkboards, so the on-site staff must either divert the refrigerated freight and accept the loss or halt transshipment for a day to stop the brine from spreading.

Gunfire spreads the mist and makes the situation worse, and the longer the concentration gauges stay unpublished, the more Yongsan dispatch credit drains away as a cost.

/hostile_groups/6/fictional_origin.en:
Just after the collapse, abandoned traction-battery stacks between the Line Succession State's sidings and the transshipment platforms of the Itaewon passage alleys mixed with rainwater and made an electrolyte mist.

Night recovery labor units that repeatedly inhaled and touched that mist gained a conductive skin film and a salt thirst, and came to be called the Electrolyte-Burn Swarm only inside Seoul's fictional setting.

At first it was recorded as a simple protection failure, and then a division of labor that treated salt concentration as a trade unit arose and the swarm signal stabilized.

The origin is leftover disaster chemistry, not the nature of any particular people, patient, or disability.

The word burn that remains in the name is a metaphor for a scar, not a medical stigma code.

/hostile_groups/6/hierarchy.en:
The Electrolyte-Burn Swarm has no standing commander.

A guide who steps the brine path first and reads the conductivity value gains the right to speak for that stretch, and the crew carrying the neutralizing spray and the crew repairing the gloves each keep a different concentration gauge.

When the two readings diverge sharply, movement stops automatically, and no one can order a departure until Jeonguram, the citizen observer on duty at Yongsan, confirms the same pan number in the residual-pressure log.

A guide whose skin film has split does not hand authority to a successor. Instead the guide recounts the contamination path aloud, and that testimony remains alongside the numbers.

The strength of this structure is not the speed of orders but that no one who hid a spill can open a path alone.

/hostile_groups/6/lifecycle.en:
On a day when rain dissolves the salt in the siding pans again, the first thing to change is not the skin but the dispatch method.

When a guide who reads the brine traces marks the safe footholds, the recovery crews gather the leakage along that line, and as the concentration rises the glove-repair crew and the neutralizing crew split apart and move separately.

When the buffer storehouse falls below half, they stop exploring distant shafts and cycle only through zones already marked.

If the Sinnae transshipment recognizes the brine passage as an official night slot, the swarm clears the passage in exchange for contact cleaning and concentration records.

Conversely, if the pans are washed without leave, the diluted electrolyte spreads wide and the swarm scatters into small groups, and when the dry-season cracks deepen each crew cuts its signal in the shaded drain grooves of Yongsan.

This cycle advances to the next phase only when spill liters, remaining buffer, and the width of skin-film cracks move together, and burn appearance does not enter the verdict table.

/hostile_groups/6/modern_anxiety.en:
The industrial-burn anxiety that spent-battery leakage pooled on transfer-warehouse and siding floors eats through skin and gloves remains at once in citizen talk and in the duty ledger.

When rainwater dilutes the salt the smell fades, and when the sun rises the crystals shine again.

Accident attribution is handled only through the fictional corridor's spill ledger and by the liter, and it does not use suspicion of any real manufacturer or brand.

The appearance of the burns themselves cannot be grounds for a personhood grade.

/hostile_groups/6/moral_cost.en:
Indiscriminate removal erases, along with the transfer workers, the neutralizing knowledge of the survival units that used the same corridor.

Treating citizens as monsters because of the look of electrolyte burns hides the real spill ledger and the protection procedures, and grows the next spill.

The price of closing the coexistence window returns as the collapse of power and cooling continuity at Sinnae and Yongsan.

The moment need is translated into evil, the politics of sharing buffer stock disappears.

A brutal sweep may look like short-term safety, but it burns long-term corridor trust.

/hostile_groups/6/negotiation.en:
Negotiation is not a market that swaps resources all at once but a working meeting that divides spill liability track by track.

The Guro Alloy House publishes spent-battery lots and recovery order, and the Electrolyte-Burn Swarm provides a concentration map by pan and the positions of the safe walkboards.

When Jeonguram's log reads residual pressure high, they do not immediately give more buffer. They first cross it against on-site glove discoloration and clear the false readings.

The on-site staff decide whether to narrow the night slots to protect Yongsan's transshipment income, or to accept the loss of Sinnae's refrigerated freight and make a wide dry zone.

If the agreement breaks, the swarm does not answer with a retaliatory attack. It withdraws work from the spill stretches it has not published, and as a result the contact-corrosion cost of the next rain falls on the party that broke the contract.

/hostile_groups/6/prose.en:
On the Yongsan siding after the rain stops, a white salt line spreads long toward the switch.

The guide Seojin does not stand at the very front. Seojin throws a scrap of dry glove onto the floor and looks for the point where conductivity breaks.

In the first incident the on-site staff can either run the passenger train in as it is, or clear the track for thirty minutes and publicly investigate the cause of the glove discoloration.

Pushing the train through keeps the dispatch, but a hidden pool rides the wheels and spreads as far as Sinnae.

The second incident is not a coolant trade.

A spent-battery lot absent from the Yongsan ledger is found, and the Guro Alloy House recovery crew and the house warehouse each push the liability onto the other.

If the on-site staff seal the lot they must scrap two cars of refrigerated freight, and if they break the seal the Electrolyte-Burn Swarm withdraws the spill map and the safe routes of the next rainy season are lost.

At the end, skin-film cracking does not cause the command failure.

When the floor of the Sinnae elevator connects as a single conductive surface, three recovery crews each produce a different concentration gauge and demand that the power to the whole hall be cut.

To keep emergency transshipment alive, a citizen observer must mark the wet stretches in person, and in that process the name of the dispatch house that hid the spill is also published.

After the agreement the ledger records not a monster's defeat but the number of discarded gloves, the minutes of stopped trains, and the warehouse bays that cannot be opened again.

The promise not to treat burn traces as a qualification for passage is proved not by a declaration but by the next shift wearing the same gloves together.

/hostile_groups/6/scenario_outlines/0/ch.en: Let the passenger train pass on time
Clear the track for thirty minutes and publicly investigate the cause of the discoloration
Seal only the salt line and keep the dispatch

/hostile_groups/6/scenario_outlines/0/me.en: Rain dissolves the racks' salt into mist, and the guide marks with dry glove scraps only where conduction breaks.

/hostile_groups/6/scenario_outlines/0/mo.en: Passenger time and the recovery worker's skin are weighed on the same morning.

/hostile_groups/6/scenario_outlines/0/ou.en: On-time passage carries the hidden pool to Sinnae. Investigation delay breaks dispatch. Partial sealing leaves no cause map.

/hostile_groups/6/scenario_outlines/0/ti.en: Dispatch of the White Salt Line

/hostile_groups/6/scenario_outlines/0/tr.en: After the rain, a white salt line spreads to the switchgear in the Yongsan sidings, and glove discoloration is observed just before the passenger train departs.

/hostile_groups/6/scenario_outlines/1/ch.en: Seal the lot and scrap two cars of refrigerated freight
Break the seal and keep the spill map
Move the lot to the Sinnae transshipment hall and spread the liability

/hostile_groups/6/scenario_outlines/1/me.en: The lot's leakage overlaps the Electrolyte-Burn Swarm's concentration map, so the seal decides the next monsoon's safe routes.

/hostile_groups/6/scenario_outlines/1/mo.en: Choose whose ledger gap the citizen corridor pays for.

/hostile_groups/6/scenario_outlines/1/ou.en: Sealing abandons cold freight; release erases the next monsoon's map. Hall movement scatters salt over passenger lines.

/hostile_groups/6/scenario_outlines/1/tr.en: A waste-battery lot absent from the Yongsan ledger is found in the sidings' lower level, and the Guro Alloy House recovery squad and the family warehouse shift responsibility.

/hostile_groups/6/scenario_outlines/2/ch.en: Cut the hall power and stop emergency transshipment
Citizen observers mark the wet stretches and keep the transshipment alive
Divert the West Sea Granary refrigerated inflow and turn the salt load outward

/hostile_groups/6/scenario_outlines/2/me.en: With the meters disagreeing and the floor electrified, even the guide cannot fix the route; only the citizen observer can mark the wet sections.

/hostile_groups/6/scenario_outlines/2/mo.en: Where to put the pollution is the choice, not a scripted window.

/hostile_groups/6/scenario_outlines/2/ou.en: The power cut kills transshipment. The marking work publishes the dispatch family's name that hid the leak. The outer detour fixes the pollution position for a season.

/hostile_groups/6/scenario_outlines/2/tr.en: As the Sinnae elevator floor joins into one conductive plane, the three recovery teams demand a full hall power cut.

/hostile_groups/6/senses.en:
The primary senses are changes in skin conductivity and fine vibration on metal surfaces.

As auxiliaries they read electrolyte solvent, the smell of salt, and local hot spots.

Electronic noise is used only to estimate residual battery pressure, and there is no complete vision through walls or eavesdropping on network-wide communications.

After rainwater dilution the conductivity signal weakens and false readings grow frequent.

They always cross-check the triple-filter log of the synthetic Jeonguram against the discoloration of gloves seen by the human eye.

Sensory overload leads to skin cracking, so they avoid staying long in high-concentration salt zones on their own.

/hostile_groups/6/territory_migration.en:
The core habitat is the lower level of the Yongsan siding and the rows of drip pans in the Itaewon passage alleys.

It sits on Corridor 3, the Itaewon passage alleys, and in the rainy season and the thaw cycle it moves along the Yongsan–Itaewon transfer freight-elevator shafts.

When the West Sea Granary Theater's refrigerated containers are pushed inland, it reacts to the salt and moisture gradient and receives a pressure signal toward the outer docks, but it does not replace a Sixteen States slot.

In the dry season it shortens its movement radius to keep the skin film from cracking, and leaves only the seasonal movement window in the duty ledger.

The connected state is the Line Succession State, and outer pressure is recorded only as a West Sea Granary Theater signal.

/hostile_groups/7/bestiary/command_scope.en: An ordinary gatekeeper's verdict stands only after it is crossed against H08 Choidaon's particle false-reading record and the dust pattern on an empty cloth. When a particle storm saturates the senses, they do not look farther. They close the door and wait for the blur to settle. A variant handles only surfaces it has pressed, pressure within two steps, and sound in the same room, and does not accept instructions from beyond the wall or a latent infection as certification.

/hostile_groups/7/bestiary/common_ecolog.en: Inside the pressure-differential door leaves of the Dongdaemun night-wage corridor, they are sentry and haulage units that divide filters, grounding, and the passage roll. Dust is not seen as points. The blur at the edge of the lighting, the static on the handles, and the vibration of the door leaves overlap as one flow. The authority to open a door does not gather in one person, and the lock bar releases only when two among pressure differential, grounding, and the roll approve the same door number.

/hostile_groups/7/bestiary/variant_relat.en: The gatekeepers of the portfolio are people who came to read particle concentration beside purification equipment that had stopped. From the filter-media weavers to the sealed-sac tenders, the variants are trades hardened into organs, such as wrist resin, enzyme sacs, and culture plates, while the circulating-air tuner, the pressure-differential sluice keeper, the electrostatic-cap pilgrim, and the protocol gatekeeper are the biomechanical branch fused to air handling, valves, dust-collection fiber, and certification devices. The protocol-mimic gatekeeper is the closest to the entry procedure, but does not understand why the rules came to exist.

/hostile_groups/7/combat_counterplay.en:
Gunfire and spray tear the filters or lift particles into the air.

Responders first lower the blower, connect the ground line, and then must agree with the gatekeepers on the direction in which the contaminated curtains are folded.

A low-noise cutter can separate a warped door leaf, but pulling every gasket at once sends a pressure wave over the patients in the alley behind.

So each time one door is secured, another is closed to make an escape path for the pressure.

The sign that the fight is over is not the enemy's numbers but the share of medical crates that passed without being repacked, and media discarded in a hasty entry is struck from the next winter's protection budget.

/hostile_groups/7/economy.en:
The main resources are recycled filter media, grounding scrap for removing static, low-particle cooling air, and gaskets for the sealed door leaves.

The points where they compete with the Changdong Protection House's integrated protection key and track-protection supplies are filters and positive-pressure power.

Organic matter and ordinary food are secondary, and when the particle load passes its cap, expansion stops.

They do not draw energy without limit, and they are bound to the battery-allotment ledger.

Grounding scrap is used only to repair door leaves and rail seats, and is not turned into weapon material.

When two rolls of media hit bottom, the spread signal switches off automatically.

Protection-key inspection is recorded separately from the media-consumption ledger, and when positive-pressure power exceeds the night slot they fold the expansion themselves.

Gasket stock is allotted only by door leaf.

/hostile_groups/7/escalation.en:
A change in the dust pattern inside a door is a warning, but it does not mean an immediate lockdown.

When the differential pressure wavers, the Cleanroom Mutant reduces the number of people passing and wraps only the medicine crates bound for Jegi-dong in a separate cloth.

The point where the situation grows is when an old duct regains positive pressure and pushes the accumulated particles toward the market.

Instead of seizing the entrance, they reverse the order in which the doors were opened and try to lead the dust into an empty annex.

If the on-site staff give priority to medical passage, the Noryangjin food inspection stops until new media arrives, and if they open the market first, part of the medicine crates is quarantined.

Damage is counted not by the number of closed doors but by the number of people and crates that were misclassified.

/hostile_groups/7/fictional_origin.en:
The Dongdaemun night-wage corridor and the sealed experimental annex near the Medical Neutrality League lost positive pressure after the collapse.

Sentries and haulage units that held on by keeping the filter replacement cycle gained a breathing rhythm hypersensitive to particle concentration and an electrostatic skin charge, and were reorganized as the Cleanroom Mutant in the sealed alleys of the Dongdaemun undercroft.

Records first written as a simple equipment failure turned into an ecology ledger as the trade in filter-media allotment arose.

They are not the stigma of contaminated humans but an environmentally adapted ecology left by the purification equipment.

They do not divide personhood by a binary of clean and dirty.

/hostile_groups/7/hierarchy.en:
Authority circulates among three gatekeepers rather than a central figure.

The first gatekeeper takes the differential-pressure gauge, the second the ground line, and the third the passage roll, and a door can open or close only when two of the three approve the same door number.

Choidaon's particle log is only material for the vote and carries no deciding power, and when a medical convoy arrives the medic who knows the patients' condition holds temporary priority together with the keeper of the passage roll.

If one gatekeeper loses the breathing rhythm, the remaining two do not monopolize authority. They close the door and wait for the next relief.

So their conflict is not the replacement of a chief but the question of which measurement has the standing to delay a person's passage.

/hostile_groups/7/lifecycle.en:
The movement of the Cleanroom Mutant is tied not to the calendar but to the pressure difference on the two sides of the airlock door.

When dust begins to stick to the inside of a door leaf, a small inspection crew pulls the gasket and holds it to the light, and through a duct where the particle count has spiked they pass an empty cloth first instead of a person.

Once the curtains pass two layers, the movement crew does not spread any wider and stays in one room while the media is washed.

When the Jegi-dong annex publishes the grounding and filter-replacement records, they count the people passing in person and match the speed of pressure recovery.

When positive pressure returns suddenly they do not expand as if it were a victory. They check whether the dust is being pushed into the opposite alley and open the doors one by one.

When the media fibers crumble and the optical signal can no longer be read, the swarm does not leave the contaminated zone. It lowers the curtains and isolates itself, and waits until an outside medic sets a safe dismantling order.

/hostile_groups/7/modern_anxiety.en:
The urban anxiety that, once the remaining filters and positive-pressure devices of sealed cleanrooms and airlocks stop, fine residual particles will torment breath and skin remains in alley talk.

Every time the alarm sounds briefly, people close the door once more and look at the differential-pressure gauge.

Handle it only as an equipment stoppage in the fictional corridor, and do not use suspicion of a real laboratory or corporate accident.

Do not read particle hypersensitivity as a moral failure.

/hostile_groups/7/moral_cost.en:
Excluding the Cleanroom Mutant because of appearance and the sound of breathing also stops the patient transfers and medicine passage that actually have to share the positive pressure.

The stigma of clean and dirty makes the protection ledger hide, and grows the next particle accident.

The price of refusing coexistence is the failure of joint purification in the sealed corridors of Noryangjin and Jegi-dong.

Call need evil, and the politics of sharing filter media disappears.

/hostile_groups/7/negotiation.en:
The core of the talks is not how many rolls of filter to cut but who can overturn a contamination verdict.

The Changdong Protection House produces the protection-key record, and the three gatekeepers post the differential pressure, the grounding, and the passage roll on different walls.

The on-site staff can give the Jegi-dong medics an emergency opening right while leaving the later audit to the market merchants, or they can open every door slowly, give up that day's medical convoy, and thereby block a monopoly on the verdict.

If Choidaon's scatter graph differs from the on-site cough record, neither side brands anyone a contaminant at once, and they run the empty-cloth test again.

The result of breaking the agreement is not an attack but no longer recognizing the door numbers the other side approved, and from then on even a short distance in the corridor must be detoured three times.

/hostile_groups/7/scenario_outlines/0/ch.en: Lock down the alarm door at once
Pass an empty cloth through first and confirm the direction of the contamination
Detour only the twelve patients and leave the door as it is

/hostile_groups/7/scenario_outlines/0/me.en: Closing the door before the particle direction is fixed hides the source of the contamination, and the scatter direction shows only when an empty cloth is passed through.

/hostile_groups/7/scenario_outlines/0/mo.en: It places the time of the patients bound for Jegi-dong and the breath of the whole alley under the same alarm.

/hostile_groups/7/scenario_outlines/0/ou.en: An immediate lockdown hides the source. The cloth test delays the fever reducers. A detour alone pushes dust into the waiting room.

/hostile_groups/7/scenario_outlines/0/ti.en: The Direction of the Empty Cloth

/hostile_groups/7/scenario_outlines/0/tr.en: The alarm lamp of the Noryangjin airlock alley has lit, but the three gatekeepers each read the differential pressure, the grounding, and the roll of patients bound for Jegi-dong as a different door.

/hostile_groups/7/scenario_outlines/1/ch.en: Send the dust into the empty Jegi-dong annex
Send the dust to the Noryangjin food inspection stand
Stop the blower and close both spaces together

/hostile_groups/7/scenario_outlines/1/me.en: A trade that swaps media for power does not hold, and the reverse-running duct is fixed so that it sacrifices only one of the two spaces.

/hostile_groups/7/scenario_outlines/1/mo.en: Who breathes the dirty air is not an exchange of resources but a choice of space.

/hostile_groups/7/scenario_outlines/1/ou.en: Sacrificing the annex loses next month's research space. The market side scraps that day's auction volume. A stoppage halts medicine and food at the same time.

/hostile_groups/7/scenario_outlines/1/tr.en: An old blower runs in reverse, so the dust can be sent to only one of the Noryangjin food inspection stand and the Jegi-dong annex.

/hostile_groups/7/scenario_outlines/2/ch.en: Take after-the-fact liability for one particular door and let the medical convoy through
Close every door and give up the convoy
Hand the protection-key authority to a citizen audit and detour the Strait-of-Three-Routes dust dock

/hostile_groups/7/scenario_outlines/2/me.en: If verdict power gathers into a single key, differential pressure, grounding, and the roll are voided all at once, so the gatekeepers stop opening and closing.

/hostile_groups/7/scenario_outlines/2/mo.en: As the price of the convoy that was saved, it decides who loses the next contamination verdict.

/hostile_groups/7/scenario_outlines/2/ou.en: Liability for one door hands key authority to the citizens if the call is wrong. A total closure kills that day's medicine. Transferring the audit slows passage but blocks the monopoly.

/hostile_groups/7/scenario_outlines/2/tr.en: When the Changdong Protection House tries to open every door with the integrated protection key, two of the three gatekeepers refuse the approval stamp.

/hostile_groups/7/senses.en:
The primary senses are optical blur from particle scattering in the air and changes in electrostatic potential.

As auxiliaries they read door-leaf vibration and local heat such as motor overheating.

Smell goes no further than detecting filter charring, and there is no complete vision or network-wide biological scan.

They always cross-check against the particle false-reading log of the synthetic Choidaon.

When a particle storm comes, sensory overload makes them close the door leaves and wait.

/hostile_groups/7/territory_migration.en:
The core habitat is the lower airlock alleys of the Dongdaemun night-wage corridor and the rows of remaining positive-pressure door leaves.

It sits on Corridor 4, the Dongdaemun night wage, and when filter stock falls it moves seasonally along the ventilation ducts of the sealed annex toward Jegi-dong.

When dust flows in from the relay docks of the Korea Strait Theater, it reacts to the outer pressure and doubles the entrance curtains.

It does not occupy a state slot, and the movement window opens only by the differential-pressure number.

The connected state is the Medical Neutrality League.

/hostile_groups/9/bestiary/command_scope.en: No circle could command another, and when the three rhythms slipped, movement and pump tests stopped together. The main senses were humidity and volatile smell, and pipe vibration arrived late, so writing both as same-moment evidence misjudged the backflow point. The most breathless person held the stop signal, and synthetic Yunsaeron's humidity logs could not guess beyond walls.

/hostile_groups/9/bestiary/common_ecolog.en: The Flood-Mold Breath Cluster was not one species' name but an environment formed as the wet concrete of the Bukhansan Bogukmun corridor, the grain heat of the Garak and Jamsil lower ration stores, and drainage workers' breath meshed over long years. Water gathered first in the low grids, and people saw the ceiling damp only after their soles slipped. The grid circle recorded water level and floor friction, the ventilation circle air and filter resistance, the ration-store circle grain heat and fermentation smell, each in its own ledger.

/hostile_groups/9/bestiary/variant_relat.en: The corridor's ordinary residents and pump watches were affected people sharing wet bedding and drainage shifts, not names on a monster list. From G10E01 to E16 were specialized variants in whom respiratory-disease residue had hardened into swim bladders, thoracic ducts, and fungal plates — inherited organs growing oxygen moss or piercing pipes with coughs. Sharing the humidity ledger, ordinary workers and variants were never bundled into one king's swarm.

/hostile_groups/9/dossier_prose.en:
The Flood-Mold Breath Cluster was not the name of one species or a single resident group.

It named an environmental ecology formed in the Sangha Relief State's underground refuge corridor as wet concrete, ration grain heat, ventilation shifts, and drainage workers' breath meshed over long years.

The corridor running along Seoul's northern hills was an old air-defense passage and underground link, with hastily added dormitories layered floor on floor.

Water gathered first in the low grids, and people felt the slip underfoot before seeing the damp spreading on the ceiling.

When the monsoon lengthened, the wet walls' smell stayed in clothes and filter cloth, but that smell or a cough was neither a member's identity nor their morality.

The name Breath Cluster arose not to classify anyone but to record where the exchange of water and air stopped.

The forming trigger was the continuous flooding of the Bukhansan Bogukmun corridor and the Garak and Jamsil lower ration stores.

Early on, managers tried to remove wall film and grain smell at once, and disinfectant flowed into drainage slots and mixed with drinking-pipe condensation in riots.

Afterwards residents chose separation over removal.

They began recording in different ledgers the positions of wet film, pump running times, filter-cloth wash counts, and the grain piles' internal heat.

The principle of never merging the seed vault's records with the corridor humidity records was also born then.

Bound into one number, it would vanish whether seeds had been saved at the dormitories' expense or planting stock wet to move people.

The cluster first made its rhythm at Bukhansan Bogukmun's lowest drain grid.

Before the water seeping between grids reached ankle height, workers breathed in short and out long, listening to pipe vibration.

When the pumps ran, the colony's center did not chase the falling water but moved with the direction humid air was pushed, toward the connection pipes under Songpa-daero and the Garak ration-store vents.

When the grain piles' heat rose, the flow sensing fermentation smell split toward the seed vault, and the rest guarded the condensation on the Jamsil lowland drinking pipes.

Before abrupt dehumidification the smell sense collapsed and it stopped moving.

When a downpour struck suddenly, volatile smells changed first and pipe vibration arrived late, so writing both as same-moment evidence misjudged the backflow point.

Synthetic Yunsaeron H10's humidity logs supplemented this sense but were no device guessing beyond walls.

When they clashed with field records, the machine figures were measured again.

This resource economy depended not on how much water one held but on holding humidity under which ceiling.

Drainage-pump power was metered separately from ration-window lighting, and as fuel fell, expansion sections closed first.

Scrap went to grid hinges and pump mounts, and coolant was poured only where motor overheat was confirmed.

Filter cloth was removed wet, sealed, and washed, and past the reuse ceiling it went to the discard bin, not to other uses.

Its humidity-management range overlapped the Magok Seed House HC10's fermenting-seed vault.

But it never traded one filter cloth directly for one seed sack or one passage slot.

The moment waterway safety and food's future were converted into a single price, the lowest dormitory's loss was pushed off the ledger.

Authority was divided among three circles.

The grid circle watched water level and floor friction, the ventilation circle air passage and filter resistance, the ration-store circle grain heat and fermentation smell.

No circle could command another, and when the three rhythms slipped, movement and pump tests stopped together.

Especially the most breathless person held the right to call that section's stop signal.

This was no mere symbol of protecting the weak.

It was the procedure of admitting the body where air blocked first as one of the measuring instruments.

The human duty could not ignore that signal, and the signaler could not monopolize rations either.

Resuming work required the residents' delegate to confirm by name the households that would flood and the beds to move under the waterway change.

In this system, power lay not in the ability to stand at the front but in the ability to stop everyone and record its cost.

G10-SC1 'The Slick Stone Steps' began as monsoon rain covered Bukhansan Bogukmun's last drain grid and a refugee column carrying medicine to the high dormitories stopped before the slick stairs.

Turning the column back reduced falls but cut the upper clinic's medicine.

Opening the stairs and attaching a guide per family continued transport while casualties accumulated and guide labor left the ration staff.

Lifting only the grid to change the waterway and detouring people looked most technical, but the changed water flooded the lower tent section.

A once-wet bedding box and document chest never returned to the original dormitory, and the relocated families' passage distance remained in every later ration cost.

The situation passed to the second stage when drinking-water smell rose from the drain.

In G10-SC2 'Two Waters in One Pool,' Bukhansan Bogukmun drinking-pipe condensation and corridor flood met in one pool of the Garak lower level.

Draining Bukhansan Bogukmun first lowered the stair water but pushed humid air into the seed vault, cutting next season's planting sacks.

Prioritizing vault desiccation saved the seeds but forced three rows of refugee tents up through the night.

Stopping the pumps and separating the two waters manually with different-colored buoys and buckets bought time, but labor fatigue and partial contamination made both discard a set volume.

The loss here was not only wet sacks.

Shrinking planting area and families scattered to other dormitories, unable to return, long remained in different ledgers.

The greatest danger came not when water grew but when whichever pump ran first harmed the other system.

In G10-SC3 'The Stop Declaration,' the most breathless circle declared a work stop until the residents' delegate confirmed the relocation families.

Recognizing it delayed rations and cut planting volume, but backflow testing and waterway knowledge were maintained.

If field staff force-connected military pumps, the water level fell short-term but both Bukhansan Bogukmun's and Garak's ledgers became void at once, and the cluster joined no later pump test.

Draining water toward the sea-wind direction of the Incheon Trust Theater XT05 and passing it outward was also possible, but that water left a season's contamination burden on the Tancheon downstream and coastal stores.

It was a hard-to-reverse decision saving the central corridor while erasing the outer water intake and livelihood.

The heart of response lay not in driving out but in distinguishing waterways again.

Hanging different-colored buoys under the grids and running pumps one at a time briefly located backflow points.

Filter cloth was not shaken dry; it was folded wet and sealed, and dehumidifiers went to the seed vault first without blowing cold wind directly on people.

Toxic spraying ruined not only the wet film but both drainage and drinking water, the most expensive choice.

Response costs included not only fuel and cloth but closed-stair counts, abandoned seed sacks, relocated families, and interrupted medicine transport time.

Coexistence was not maintained by promising clean zones.

Bukhansan Bogukmun residents testified to the flooded stairs, Garak managers disclosed per-sack humidity and discard limits, and the three circles separately stated which signal — water height, air flow, or grain heat — touched the danger line first.

Draining Bukhansan Bogukmun first, Garak documented the reduced planting volume; guarding the vault first, the coalition compensated relocation cost and lost dormitories.

Even when the accord broke, the cluster did not attack.

It only withdrew from pump tests, and both sides bore greater loss without backflow knowledge.

So the corridor's order stood not on odorless air but on records that hid neither who got wet, what was discarded, nor at which breath work stopped.

/hostile_groups/9/scenario_outlines/0/me.en: While the grid circle drums the water height, opening the stairs grows casualties and closing them stops the high dormitories' medicine.

/hostile_groups/9/scenario_outlines/0/mo.en: Places who steps on the wet stairs and who goes without medicine in the same rain.

/hostile_groups/9/scenario_outlines/0/ou.en: Turning back cuts the medicine. Keeping open grows casualties. Changing only the waterway floods the lower tents.

/hostile_groups/9/scenario_outlines/0/tr.en: Monsoon rain covers Bukhansan Bogukmun's last drain grid, and a refugee column stands before slick stone steps.

/hostile_groups/9/scenario_outlines/1/me.en: Filter cloth cannot be traded for passage slots, and Bukhansan Bogokmun drainage and the Garak seed vault's humidity hang on the same pump.

/hostile_groups/9/scenario_outlines/1/mo.en: Chooses which ledger to wet first — planting volume or dormitory places.

/hostile_groups/9/scenario_outlines/1/ou.en: Bukhansan Bogukmun priority wets the seed sacks. Vault priority moves three tent rows overnight. Manual drainage trades time for partial loss on both.

/hostile_groups/9/scenario_outlines/1/tr.en: Drinking-pipe condensation and floodwater meet in one pool, and whichever pump runs contaminates the other.

/hostile_groups/9/scenario_outlines/2/me.en: Not dehumidification collapsing the film but the breathing-stop right halting the waterway, so forced pumps break both communities' water ledgers.

/hostile_groups/9/scenario_outlines/2/mo.en: The remaining cost is not an open ration window but dormitories erased from the map.

/hostile_groups/9/scenario_outlines/2/ou.en: Recognition delays rations and cuts planting. Forcing breaks both ledgers and severs cooperation. Outer discharge leaves a season's coastal contamination.

/hostile_groups/9/scenario_outlines/2/tr.en: The most breathless circle declares a work stop, and the pumps do not run until the residents' delegate confirms the relocation families' names.

/houses/0/arcs/0/summary.en: night cooling distribution ran short in the sealed computer block beside the Yeouido No. 2 waterworks

Along the Guro–Geumcheon production axis, the Guro Digital Complex Battery House sorted loose battery cells into stacks by lifespan and temperature.

The Changdong rolling-stock depot demanded its braking stock first, and accepted no material without a test certificate.

Bae Haesol's seal guaranteed not charge capacity but heat-resistance testing and contamination history.

When one leaking drum was found, every bundle on the same freight cart went into quarantine.

The production repair crews pressed for the shortage to be released, and the northern technicians blocked the warehouse door to hold the braking share.

After the materials certifier uncovered forged markings, the supply order changed to an open draw among three states.

To keep its trust, the Guro Digital Complex Battery House discarded even usable cells and cut Changdong's reserve runs.
