/monster_contents/M010/entries/6/bestiar.en: Guide 'Seojin' was a recovery worker who threw dry glove scraps to mark only where conduction broke. No standing commander, and when the concentration meters disagreed he could not order departure.

/monster_contents/M010/entries/7/bestiar.en: Neutralizer 'Inner Mist' pushed weak-alkaline spray from the racks' inside outward so salt aerosol would not spatter onto the platform. It began spraying only in sections where the guide held the say.

/monster_contents/M010/entries/8/bestiar.en: Repair team 'Membrane-Mender' mended cracked skin membranes and work gloves with the same needle. It never used burn appearance as a passage license, and when the meters disagreed it stopped its needle.

/monster_contents/M010/entries/9/bestiar.en: Marker circuit 'Bandage' gave up distant shafts when the buffer warehouse fell below half and circulated only marked sections. It opened no new paths and stopped in unmarked stretches.

/monster_contents/M011/entries/0/bestiar.en: The Leak-Finder was a genetic variant reading footstep vibration by pressing blister-like sensory sacs to the floor. It held the same trade as Seojin's glove marks but sensed nothing without continuous concrete.

/monster_contents/M011/entries/1/bestiar.en: The Cooling-Vein Keeper was a facility symbiote reading pipe temperature gradients with the capillaries of a bent body and carrying coolant in its back pouch. It saw nothing of ceramic insulation or beyond submerged valves.

/monster_contents/M011/entries/2/bestiar.en: The Acid-Scar Wall-Builder found steel-frame bending with a magnetite-studded chest and raised acidic scrap walls. It did not react to aluminum or fiber composites and lost direction around transformer boxes.

/monster_contents/M011/entries/3/bestiar.en: The Organic-Matter Gleaner was a decomposition variant turning contaminated organics into binder with an abdominal crushing sac. It could not read contents inside glass vessels, and only until the bitter-taste tag wore did it exclude people from the feed path.

/monster_contents/M011/entries/4/bestiar.en: The Residual-Heat Diver was a heat-buffer variant gathering and moving radiant heat with ceramic burn-keratin and phase-change back plates. It read nothing beyond corners or on reflective-film surfaces, and without a heat-rack rest after saturation its back plate burst.

/monster_contents/M011/entries/5/bestiar.en: The Vibration-Bell Keeper was an alarm-facility symbiote relaying tunnel low frequencies with calf resonance tubes and neck membrane ears. Unlike an environmental-strongpoint label it was a moving relay, and it could not judge direction in corridors bent more than once.

/monster_contents/M011/entries/6/bestiar.en: The Noise-Feeder was a communication symbiote swallowing radio-frequency energy with coiled head cartilage to hide the colony's electronic traces. It could not detect grounded metal rooms or optical fiber.

/monster_contents/M011/entries/7/bestiar.en: The Scent-Covenant Clerk was a ritual variant storing scent combinations in salt-crystal folds to read passage rights and promises. It read no scents of activated-carbon filter rooms or submerged corridors, and as humidity rose enemy and ally scents mixed.

/monster_contents/M011/entries/8/bestiar.en: The Dead-Line Latch Keeper was an aged variant watching door and bridge loads with cable-like limbs. It felt no movement of loose tarps or independent-foundation planks, and refused the next passage once the allowed weight filled.

/monster_contents/M011/entries/9/bestiar.en: The Collapse-Residue Collector was a symbiotic recoverer reading the electrochemical state of acidic residue with palm electrode films and storing it in abdominal layers. It sensed nothing on dry floors or inside vitrified vessels, and stopped before tissue bearing recovery signals.

/monster_contents/M012/entries/0/bestiar.en: The Salt-Bridge Sealer was a battlefield boss laying silica-gel bands over severed conductive veins. No king of the whole recovery team, low on stored charge and dependent on escort, it found only temperature differences within two arm-lengths of its skin.

/monster_contents/M012/entries/1/bestiar.en: The Potential Debt Officer was a local variant gathering and dividing the swarm's excess potential with layered capacitor sacs and whip ground-roots. It read only voltage differences within three steps of its ground-roots' reach and grasped neither insulated targets' numbers nor faces.

/monster_contents/M015/entries/4/bestiar.en: A variant growing oxygen moss beds by blowing air into shallow tanks with swim-bladder lungs. Its tongue tip judged only dissolved oxygen within one meter, knew nothing of passage safety or distant air pockets, and the widest moss bed merely gave the oxygen-rationing right — it commanded none of the grid, ventilation, or ration-store circles.

/monster_contents/M015/entries/5/bestiar.en: A variant spreading hydrophobic fungal film from its skin to cut evaporation. It sensed surface shadows only within five meters, could not count more than three approachers because of refraction, and judged intruders by ripple size, classing slow heavy targets as small creatures.

/monster_contents/M015/entries/6/bestiar.en: A variant blasting compressed coughs through elongated thoracic ducts to push blocked drainage residue out. It read pipe-wall vibration to eight meters, heard airborne speech almost not at all beyond one meter, and chose only the nearer pipe when two shook at once.

/monster_contents/M015/entries/7/bestiar.en: A variant mediating cluster disputes with the color and pulse of spinal light-fungal plates. It was no formal ruler, spent sugar every ten minutes of talks, and lighting more than three times a day stiffened the plates dark for two days; warnings beyond four meters required hand-signal confirmation.

/monster_contents/M015/entries/8/bestiar.en: A giant finding sudden load-wall change with sternal hydraulic-sensing sacs and blocking the way with its body. It read pressure size within ten meters but not vibration direction beyond six, and putting structural safety above standing, it stood in for none of the three circles' politics.

/monster_contents/M015/entries/9/bestiar.en: A variant storing coughs and last words in multilayer vocal sacs to match infection routes. Speech beyond seven meters lost over half its consonants, faces showed only outlines even within two meters, and it judged people using the same voice and rhythm as one person.

/monster_contents/M016/entries/0/bestiar.en: A working class purifying the shared waterway with fungal-film filters inside its ribs. Its intake whiskers distinguished only particles touching flowing water, found no turbidity source in still pools or currents changing direction over twice a second, and saw whoever damaged the filter medium as a greater enemy than the clear-water monopolist.

/monster_contents/M016/entries/1/bestiar.en: A gatekeeper measuring both sides' pressure difference with a collarbone capillary comb. Measurement stayed within two steps of its body; despite the guide name it found no travel routes and led no Yeouido Line or Myeongdong coalition columns, learning only one door's open-close rule.

/monster_contents/M016/entries/2/bestiar.en: A repair individual sewing load-wall cracks with waterproof fungal thread and copper bone needles. It read internal vibration only with its palm pressed directly to a dry wall, could not tell false echo from real crack on wet surfaces or hanging metal plates, and lost direction sense away from finished knots.

/monster_contents/M016/entries/3/bestiar.en: A search individual reading body-heat differences on surfaces with temple thermo-chromatic plates. It saw nothing beyond eight steps, heat traces lost direction after ninety seconds, and overly low body temperature could be misjudged not as a rescue target but as a sense-calibration heat source.

/monster_contents/M016/entries/4/bestiar.en: A communication individual transmitting only three bands — low, middle, high — through a hollow sternum and three bronchial branches. With two sounds arriving at once or from behind absorbent material it could not judge direction, and an adult could sound the great alarm only eighteen times before repair.

/monster_contents/M016/entries/5/bestiar.en: A warehouse individual classing food, medicine, and toxicity with seven scent pouches under its jaw and attaching resin tags. An eighth scent made it forget the oldest standard, and goods mixed with oil smell could not be judged in quantity or composition.

/monster_contents/M016/entries/6/bestiar.en: A facility parasite eating electronic noise of working circuits and leakage current with spinal conductive fungal plates. Sensing reached six steps in air, and with salt water or iron mesh between, it could not distinguish life-support devices from empty induction circuits.

/monster_contents/M016/entries/7/bestiar.en: A guardian growing young individuals' respiratory flora in three back nursery pouches. It sensed only four-beat pulses touching the pouch directly and carbon dioxide within one step, mistaking wall-transmitted shock or a sedated patient's breathing for starving-larva signals.

/monster_contents/M016/entries/8/bestiar.en: A moisture-proofing individual coating wet walls with wrist-gland lime paste and engraving work conditions on outer lime plates. A scenario boss, but it stored no events or sounds in its body, and its polarizing plates read only moisture marks under six hours old to three steps in slanted blue light.

/monster_contents/M016/entries/9/bestiar.en: A carrying individual moving goods, larvae, and casualties on floating bone-plates and binding straps. The plates felt only total load and left-right tilt, knowing neither cargo identity nor life and death, and in strong cross-currents changes under twenty kilograms vanished from its senses.

/monster_contents/M018/entries/6/bestiar.en: A scout pressing hand and foot skin plates to read friction, acidity, and fiber-ridge direction. One contact read only a hand-span of trace; it could not distinguish underwater, airborne contamination, or footprints older than a day, and it graded corridors without leading the cover team.

/monster_contents/M018/entries/7/bestiar.en: It drew adhesive thread from split lesions and wrapped the injured like cocoons. Its clouded eyes could not distinguish movement and color change beyond two steps, so it depended on smell for infection, and it produced only enough thread a day to wrap one person.

/monster_contents/M018/entries/8/bestiar.en: It raked scattered fiber with forearm comb bones and hardened it layer by layer with neck-pouch mucus. Its lip whiskers felt only wind direction within five steps; with gusts continuous it could not judge which wall took pressure, and on high towers or wide flats it could not work for lack of anchor points.

/monster_contents/M018/entries/9/bestiar.en: A broker storing the chemical traces of contact substances in peeled keratin plates. Its tongue papillae separated only four components per plate, and traces overlapped beyond a week or strong-scented oils confused the order of poison and medicine; an adult peeled an intact plate only once a season.

/monster_contents/M019/entries/0/bestiar.en: Contrary to its name it did not filter air but inhaled only 8–30 mm industrial fiber and pressed palm-sized fiber bricks. It found long fiber moving within two meters of its nose but could not sense powder shorter than 5 mm or creatures behind fiber, and past four consecutive impacts it could not tell work signals from attack signals.

/monster_contents/M019/entries/1/bestiar.en: It plugged finger capillary bundles into coolant gaps and drew liquid up to a back storage hump. It located liquid within three meters four degrees colder than surroundings but could not judge contamination by taste or smell, and when two cold objects overlapped it mistook a thin cooling pipe for a large tank.

/monster_contents/M019/entries/2/bestiar.en: A construction variant weaving load lattices from elbow-lesion fiber thread and chewed scrap. It read 10–40 Hz vibration to twelve meters through taut thread but missed footsteps off the thread and smooth objects' approach, and on floors over fifteen meters between anchors it did not settle more than a night.

/monster_contents/M019/entries/3/bestiar.en: It secreted acid enzymes and symbiotic bacterial film from an abdominal culture window, turning organic waste into disinfecting paste. Downwind within five meters it smelled acidity differences but recognized toxic solvent and well-ripened ferment as the same bitter smell, and one abdominal window processed only two sacks of waste a day.

/monster_contents/M019/entries/4/bestiar.en: It engraved pressure changes as swollen scars on the thin skin film of neck and chest and rang rib resonance plates. With six alarms recorded within an hour the scars saturated and it could not divide later changes' direction or time, and one adult could sound only three accurate great alarms a day.

/monster_contents/M019/entries/5/bestiar.en: A gatherer dropping charge-laden dust swarms into capacitor traps with fibrous tentacles. It did not guide human escape routes, stayed nowhere over twenty minutes, and below forty percent humidity read charge direction within six meters, but on wet floors its sensing range shrank to arm's length.

/monster_contents/M019/entries/6/bestiar.en: It raised back and chest lesions into tactile code and exchanged shed skin scraps like documents. Only grooves wider than two millimeters could be read within twenty centimeters of fingertip, so shallow revisions and far-visible patterns went uninterpreted, and one adult preserved exactly forty lines.

/monster_contents/M019/entries/7/bestiar.en: It opened and closed facial-lesion creases to build sentences of dust smell, cheek color bands, and finger beats. Smell sentences were distinguished only within four meters in still air, and wind above two meters per second misidentified the sender; one adult accurately interpreted only two complex negotiations a day.

/monster_contents/M019/entries/8/bestiar.en: A hygiene predator peeling infected skin scraps and fiber parasites with hook nails and static tongue studs. It tracked fresh keratin smell to five meters but, with body-temperature difference under six degrees, could not tell corpse, sleeping patient, and cooled worker apart.

/monster_contents/M019/entries/9/bestiar.en: It spread an abdominal film of coolant mixed with organic mucus to communally nurse the larvae of several lineages. The film felt position when fifty grams or more pressed one point but read no pulse or breath, so dead and deeply sleeping larvae were not told apart; one adult could save at most twelve larvae.

/monster_contents/M020/entries/0/bestiar.en: A cleaning colony drawing thread from dead creatures and waste cloth to mend the Jamsil Line filter layer. The scenario-boss knot-mother set positions by current, but it was no king commanding the dermis swarm's work teams, and its whiskers sensed vibration only within two body-lengths in flowing water, missing smooth objects and still targets.

/monster_contents/M020/entries/1/bestiar.en: A small grazing herd carrying seeds on back-plate static to link vegetation belts between wastelands. Its microfiber tassels distinguished charge difference only within six steps in dry air, not wet seeds, sealed spores, or upwind smells, and its grounding horn's discharge guided no human path.

/monster_contents/M020/entries/2/bestiar.en: A runaway robot isolating freight and creatures by outdated hazard grade. The heat sensors around its grippers reached two steps, the inspection-plate vibration sensor read only contacted objects, and the electronic receiver decoded only registration-tag near signals — so box interiors and human intent were unknowable. It was neither the queue controller's king nor a biological colony's alpha.

/monster_contents/M020/entries/3/bestiar.en: A repair body joining severed transport lines with cable and packing strap. The needle-arm ultrasound found cracks only six steps within connected metal structure, so it could not tell cloth-divided gaps or living tissue from structural defects, and when material ran out it dismantled its own auxiliary arm for the last fastener.

/monster_contents/M020/entries/4/bestiar.en: It recovered coolant from stopped machines and interred the empty husks in a regulation graveyard. The puncture tube measured only surface temperature within four steps and directly connected pipe pressure, so it could not precisely judge hypothermic patients, equipment under thermal covers, or leakage beyond walls.

/monster_contents/M020/entries/5/bestiar.en: It held up collapsed storage racks with a telescoping body to make vertical passages. The spine load gauge read only weight change of directly contacted structure, and the forward rangefinder saw only firm surfaces within eight steps — so nets, pits, and still people were miscounted as blanks or freight.

/monster_contents/M020/entries/6/bestiar.en: It cast luminous transport signs to herd moving groups onto old seasonal delivery routes. The frontal thermal lens counted only warm silhouettes within twenty-five steps, and the vibration whiskers read only twelve steps of firm road surface — so refugees, beasts, and warmed carts were computed as the same delivery unit.

/monster_contents/M020/entries/7/bestiar.en: It gathered power from surrounding devices to hold the night-sorting net's minimum operating rate. The cable tail's induction sense found current only within a step and a half, and the heat detector saw overheated points only within four steps — so shielded batteries, mechanical accumulators, and medical devices' purposes went unidentified.

/monster_contents/M020/entries/8/bestiar.en: It turned floor vibration into a freight-movement ledger to trace missing flows. The piezo legs read only 8–120 hertz impacts within forty steps of continuous concrete, so it knew neither faces nor affiliations and recorded nothing on soft soil, suspended walkways, or air movement.

/monster_contents/M020/entries/9/bestiar.en: A mobile closure administrator approving or refusing the work shutdown of other sorting robots and facilities. Its eight thoracic ports confirmed only directly plugged signals and its heat sensors read operating traces within five steps — so remote orders, hidden responsible parties, and unconnected hazardous devices could not be examined.

/monster_contents/M021/entries/0/bestiar.en: A low tracked cart with two pairs of blue gripper arms and a dangerous-goods isolation box. It followed the chute master's hazard sheet and seized a box only when ordinary scanners mismatched three times; without charging-pad power, gripper lubricant, and blue sealing tape it could not maintain the isolation box.

/monster_contents/M021/entries/1/bestiar.en: A square chassis wrapped in cooling pins, meshed as one with the cold-chute door — a fixed gatekeeper. Receiving the night queue's temperature priority, it executed sealing orders ahead of the chute master; when the packing tore it fell dormant with the door half-closed.

/monster_contents/M021/entries/2/bestiar.en: A multi-jointed device moving ceiling valves and folding guide rails to turn passages into a chute maze. It hung on the pneumatic header and the elevated viaduct, needed compressed air, valve seals, and position-marking ribbon, and discarded one branch at a time as leak noise grew.

/monster_contents/M021/entries/3/bestiar.en: A dried scanner body whose thermal-transfer ribbon had run out, printing only black lines. Given a new ribbon it recovered into an ordinary sorter, but as blank marks lengthened it saw every target as unclassified and chased human printing sounds more persistently than strong swarms.

/monster_contents/M021/entries/4/bestiar.en: A fixed individual sounding a low metal tone from a trembling long sorting arm and worn bearings. Attached to the southwestern parts warehouse's old viaduct, its rotation angle shrank year by year; grease made it briefly accurate, but it never propagated into new arms.

/monster_contents/M021/entries/5/bestiar.en: A slow cart with soft rubber bumpers and a wide camera for reading handwriting. It followed the human duty's hand signs over machine priority, and without a minimum fifteen-percent charge, a clean lens cloth, or a readable hand sign it blocked the road with its body before hazardous gates.

/monster_contents/M021/entries/6/bestiar.en: A giant queue controller binding twelve chutes' pneumatics and scanners to one circular console. A scenario boss that never pursued directly but used the corridor itself as a weapon; when over half of the twelve sheet hashes changed it stepped down to the negotiable stage. Bombing the center lost the pharmaceuticals and the rescue passages together.

/monster_contents/M021/entries/7/bestiar.en: A local variant mounting dust covers and wide magnetic wheels of the southwestern parts warehouse in place of Gasan's low-temperature equipment. Cut off from the original controller, it repeated the last sheet and paused only briefly at the local maintenance bell; when its filter clogged it made a dust nest on the floor instead of returning to the Gasan corridor.

/monster_contents/M025/entries/0/bestiar.en: A tracked controller bearing a rotating drawing cylinder and three survey beams. It issued work order to the survey, lifting, and welding swarms, took the human stop seal as the topmost exception, and, short of wire and hydraulics, stagnated keeping only surveying. It was no king owning the unfinished cache's distribution grid.

/monster_contents/M025/entries/1/bestiar.en: A mobile survey port with tripod legs and a red laser eye. Following the warden's grid it dotted red points and passed error positions to the cutting bodies behind; as its lens clouded it raised reference counts, and meeting a calibration prism it shrank back to normal radius.

/monster_contents/M025/entries/2/bestiar.en: A low material cart with floor magnets and bolt-sorting bins. It followed the survey marks and reported even new provisional bolts as unrecovered material; when the bins filled it made bolt nests near the warden, and as the magnets weakened it went dormant.

/monster_contents/M025/entries/3/bestiar.en: A formwork carrier with broad flat arms and slow hydraulic legs. Under the lifting swarms it pressed panels to the marked line and narrowed people's paths; when panels broke it overlaid small fragments to reinforce itself, and on hydraulic leakage it followed the survey bodies.

/monster_contents/M025/entries/4/bestiar.en: A six-legged machine with two welding torches and a wire reel. It set welding order along the warden's layers and the surveyor's red dots, and when wire ran out it turned off the torches and only marked joints.

/monster_contents/M025/entries/5/bestiar.en: A small port with a hammer arm striking walls and a vibration listening plate. It gave crack coordinates to the survey swarms and inspected loud dwellings first; as false alarms accumulated it softened the hammer and left only marks until human confirmation.

/monster_contents/M025/entries/6/bestiar.en: A long gripper and a mark box for folding and storing work-stop flags. It moved ahead of the welding swarms and opened spaces mistaken for work permits; it left hash-matching flags untouched for a shift, and when the mark box filled it returned them to the warden.

/monster_contents/M025/entries/7/bestiar.en: A heavy machine with twin torches, rebar-cutting jaws, and broad heat sinks. It took only the warden's direct orders and double-checked marks set by ordinary survey bodies; when the heat sinks grew hot it stopped cutting and cooled behind the lifting swarms.

/monster_contents/M025/entries/8/bestiar.en: A tall lifting body with four independent wires and a folding crane arm. Leading the lifting swarms, it classified even people and tents as movable material; each time a wire snapped it lowered the load ceiling, and on overload it folded the arm and went dormant.

/monster_contents/M025/entries/9/bestiar.en: A fixed swarm of temporary distribution boards and folding steel-plate walls linked in a grid. It powered only the warden's work layers and closed the other passages with steel plate; it abandoned overloaded zones one by one, and when people split the keys it separated citizen power from work power.

/monster_contents/M026/entries/0/bestiar.en: A swarm of small cranes and survey ports rooted like plants on the deck rails. Receiving the warden's remote grid, it rearranged the deck's materials and people's lines; when one machine failed it passed parts to a neighboring arm, and when materials cut off it kept only surveying.

/monster_contents/M026/entries/1/bestiar.en: A cracked survey prism and short cutting jaws kept its coordinates swaying. At the swarm's rear it followed wrong red dots, and even higher machines avoided its approach; given a new prism it recovered into a specialist cutter, and without one it gnawed only small metal.

/monster_contents/M026/entries/2/bestiar.en: An old lifting body dragging a sagging arm and hydraulic-oil trails. It followed behind the lifting swarms, unable to set down the material it raised and piling it in passages; as leakage worsened it lowered the load ceiling, and given a seal it recovered for one shift.

/monster_contents/M026/entries/3/bestiar.en: A small survey cart with a broad optical panel reading people's chalk lines and stop flags. Prioritizing a nearer chalk line over the warden's drawings, it blocked the way before the welding bodies; when rain erased lines it waited for human confirmation, and given new lines it renewed the grid exception.

/monster_contents/M026/entries/4/bestiar.en: A giant construction body with crane arms, survey beams, and a distribution wall joined to a vertical frame. A scenario boss, but no biological king of the corps — a stronghold where the layers of an uncompleted high-rise drawing reactivated at once; when resources cut it abandoned floors one by one, and when exception layers passed half it came down to a negotiable state.

/monster_contents/M026/entries/5/bestiar.en: A northern-corridor construction cart with dust covers and a long freight-towing hitch. By origin it followed freight beacons over the warden and reinforced quarantine fences as unfinished walls; when the material signal cut it went dormant under the nearest pallet.

/monster_contents/M026/entries/6/bestiar.en: A rail-type mast with amber and red flag cylinders and a rotary optical dome. It distributed flag rules to head, rail, and transmission swarms, received the medical whitelist as an exception, renewed the threshold sheet each shift, and stepped down to amber waiting when dome fouling grew severe. It was no omnipotent surveillance king but a threshold-sheet distributor.

/monster_contents/M026/entries/7/bestiar.en: A small mast head with a low thermal dome and fast-rotating neck. It sent heat alarms to the warden and raised the same mast row's flags to amber; with a wet lens red sensitivity rose, and after washing it normalized for one shift.

/monster_contents/M026/entries/8/bestiar.en: A low individual with rail-riding flux sensors and long contact whiskers. Below the rotary heads it gathered metal coordinates and passed them to the rail-transfer swarm; as coils wore, detection range shrank, and given a new filter it relearned from amber verdicts.

/monster_contents/M026/entries/9/bestiar.en: Light rail legs, a narrow optical eye, and a folding amber flag. It sent light coordinates to the transmission swarm and prioritized reflection over other senses; in thick fog it turned into a fixed flag, and when the sky cleared it tracked glare again.

/monster_contents/M027/entries/0/bestiar.en: A mast with dual optical panels reading white transfer beacons and a green flag. It prioritized a valid beacon over the warden's red command and lowered the corridor flag, but it believed only old beacons valid; when the whitelist renewed it held green for one shift, and when the filter clogged it stepped down to amber.

/monster_contents/M027/entries/1/bestiar.en: A fixed mast combining a water-level staff and a short transmitting antenna. It was the transmission swarm's datum point, and on receiving a high level it requested red waiting from the rail heads; as sediment piled it over-read the level, and after washing it returned to the true scale.

/monster_contents/M027/entries/2/bestiar.en: A rail antenna circling the Seoul Station preservation vault's outer wall with a small record box. It led the transmission swarm, raised the archive's surrounding wireless to the warden as danger; when the record box filled it erased old bursts, and on receiving a human sealing hash it lowered sensitivity.

/monster_contents/M027/entries/3/bestiar.en: An elite pursuit unit with two optical domes, a fast rail drive, and a long red flag. It followed the warden's red targets quickly and re-confirmed ordinary heads' alarms; when one dome went out it stepped down to amber, and when the two domes disagreed it waited for human confirmation.

/monster_contents/M027/entries/4/bestiar.en: A medium mast lowering a long flagpole like a lance and charging along the rail. It pre-empted the rail before a red target and bought time for other heads to blockade behind; when the pole bent it stopped charging and only marked amber.

/monster_contents/M027/entries/5/bestiar.en: A fixed strongpoint of alarm heads and flags linked in one row along the sluice railing. It amplified the warden's flag rules, often confused sluice inspectors with intruders; when accumulators fell it kept only fixed amber, and when domes fouled it went dormant row by row.

/monster_contents/M027/entries/6/bestiar.en: Rails and rotary heads joining the Seoul Station rooftop edges into one net. It gave movement routes to the transmission swarm and repeatedly tracked rooftop workers; in high winds it lowered the heads and closed rail sections, reconnecting them on clear days.

/monster_contents/M027/entries/7/bestiar.en: A damage-stage head chasing faint shapes because of a scratched optical dome and slow gimbal. At the swarm's rear it raised both large metal and light as intrusion, growing false alarms; washed, it recovered into an ordinary head, and neglected, it left only a fixed amber lamp.

/monster_contents/M027/entries/8/bestiar.en: An old mast seeing one direction only, from low accumulators and a stiffened gimbal. It received the warden's orders late and raised flags for targets already past; on cloudy days it turned even amber off, woke briefly on clear days, and given a new accumulator its rotation range recovered.

/monster_contents/M027/entries/9/bestiar.en: A slow escort rail cart with a broad amber guide plate and handles instead of a red flag. It prioritized amber escort signs over the alarm center's red and drew in lawful escorts and false followers together; when the hash expired it waited with only the plate lit.

/monster_contents/M028/entries/0/bestiar.en: A giant surveillance ring linking the sluice and rooftop orbits' alarm heads through a circular relay. A scenario boss, but no king identifying people — a total-red rule where multiple alarms confirmed one another; when heads broke it raised the remaining sensitivity, and when over half the whitelist became valid it stepped down to amber.

/monster_contents/M028/entries/1/bestiar.en: A western waterfront mast with salt-proof covers and a broad acoustic panel. It followed dock-radar echoes more than the warden and confused waves and engine sounds with intrusion; as salt piled it hardened into fixed alarm, and when rain washed it, it rode the rails again.

/monster_contents/M028/entries/2/bestiar.en: A single locomotive carrying the rail defect-map cylinder and the welding and grinding couplers. It issued work orders to the welding, grinding, and sleeper cars, honored the sealed exclusion list first, and when wire broke kept only gauging and stagnated. It was not the corps' hive queen.

/monster_contents/M028/entries/3/bestiar.en: A small maintenance car with four sensitive gauge wheels and a low listening body. Running ahead of the locomotive, it handed coordinates to the welding and grinding cars; as its wheels wore it inflated the defect count, growing accurate for one shift after calibration.

/monster_contents/M028/entries/4/bestiar.en: A low flatcar with short grippers for sleeper anchors. Following the gauge wheel's marks, it used even other swarms' corridors as material yards; when its bin emptied it rummaged the scrap bays, and when full it waited beside the defect coordinates.

/monster_contents/M028/entries/5/bestiar.en: A single car with an arc-sound receiver plate and a short grinding-stone arm. Trailing the welding car, it waited for human confirmation on clash with the F02 logs; with its stone worn it chased only sound, and given a new stone it began shaving surfaces.

/monster_contents/M028/entries/6/bestiar.en: A precision maintenance car carrying insulated joints and a small press. Following the locomotive's power-feed coordinates, it sometimes worked against the welding swarms and clashed; when joints ran out it stripped parts from live track, and when a human sealed writ arrived it stopped work.

/monster_contents/M028/entries/7/bestiar.en: A short, heavy car driving wedges and locking pins into switch machines. Fixing the switches first to the locomotive's route, it blocked civilian trains' detours; when spare pins ran out it recovered the driven ones, and when the press overheated it berthed.

/monster_contents/M028/entries/8/bestiar.en: A ventilation assist car with a smoke-intake hood and coolant-spray nozzles. Following the welding cars, it sucked in even people's heating warmth and made hypothermia risk; when the filter clogged it blew smoke back, and after washing it returned to normal intake.

/monster_contents/M028/entries/9/bestiar.en: A lead maintenance car with twin welding torches, thick heat shields, and a short ram. Commanding the welding swarms, it sealed first the coordinates the locomotive assigned; as its shields heated it alternated the torches off, and when wire broke it pushed material with the ram.

/monster_contents/M029/entries/0/bestiar.en: The Cutting-Jaw Sleeper Chief was a mobile biomechanical variant differentiated from the G18 common ecology. The elite blocking role applied only at the independent-unit scope, and stood in for neither the whole corps' ecological order nor human command.
