/projection_pages/External-Theaters.md/b.en: The corridor prose of this page was a read-only projection of the World Narrative Atlas.

/projection_pages/External-Theaters.md/i.en:
Only the Seoul-side corridors are recorded. No crime is asserted of the sitting government or of any office still in post.

The generation of 2126 did not meet its neighbors as nations. Beneath the Imjin levee, return rolls were read by hand-torch. From the West Sea came only the rumor that the cold-store's temperature had died. On the strait, three relay branches told three different years. On the Duman, the freight-car fire-marks were inspected. The Incheon trust was a drawing of lots over the remaining track, not the Seventh Fleet. They believed the same call mesh had come undone on the mainland as well. The canon of the mechanics is [the Unbinding of Mobility](../overview/World-Unbinding.md).

/projection_pages/Operating-Houses.md/in.en: The houses of 2126 stood in two lines. The corporate heirs were grandchildren of the hands that had held the keys of the 2026 owners' families. The civic houses had grown out of watches at the water gates, the records, and the medicine. They did not buy states. They leased the infrastructure. Before a station chief could open the water, a house's signature was required. The founding owners' faces lived on as oral accounts. Heo Eunchan and Yu Sejin belonged to the generation of 2126. The causes sat with [the houses](./factions/Chaebol-Houses-and-Century-Factions.md).

/relations/37/reason.en: a pre-collapse steel-price dispute carried into parts-specification negotiations

/relations/38/reason.en: the battery-cell supply contract was bound to audit rights over the energy-storage depot

/relations/39/reason.en: the search index and the message relay competed for the Sangam transmission band

/relations/40/reason.en: kindred food-supply and transport contracts split the Garak auction-floor volume

/relations/41/reason.en: container ship-repair payments traded against rights to the Yongsan riverside wharf

/relations/42/reason.en: bids split over protocol goods at Seoul Station and access to the bonded warehouse

/states/0/origin.en: The treatment watch read the water-supply contract as a charter. The Yeouido finance hall split off as the neighboring state, and the Yeongdeungpo Station sluice house sold the western water.

/states/1/origin.en: The industrial-complex standards outlasted citizenship. The Guro Station fabrication guild kept the bolt rites as a state. The Daerim lodgings were a Hu inside this state.

/states/10/origin.en: The cooling and computing keys of Seocho Town became one family's duty chest. The trade name at the Gangnam Station crossing was never erased, and in 2126 the group's name was the state's name.

/states/11/origin.en: Terminal dispatch and the medical trains became a neutrality treaty. Sinnae Station remained the market that transferred anyone.

/states/12/origin.en: The Jegi-dong ledgers and the hospital watch left a treatment contract that did not distinguish enemy from friend. Jegi-dong Station was that contract's capital. The Dongdaemun night workshops were a Hu on this state's western edge.

/states/13/origin.en: The Guui sluices and the Achasan outposts stopped halfway through merging into one military government. Guui Station closed the eastern river crossing and set the Konkuk University Koryo-in corridor on this state's edge.

/states/14/origin.en: The Myeongdong altar and the diocesan rolls were moved onto paper. The diocese of 2126 was a state that accredited marriage and memorial rites at Myeongdong Station. The Bishops' Conference building remained only the diocese's outer warehouse.

/states/15/origin.en: The union rolls of the Jeongdong office became an emergency muster. When the factories died, the right to strike became a right of passage, and the City Hall Station federation acted as a state. It borrowed the emblems of the democratization and labor movements, and did not use a party name as a state name.

/states/2/origin.en: In 2026 the Yangjae head office and its field test line were already running humanoids. During the week of the unbinding the cloud learning died, and the maintenance house kept the trade name. The stock company of 2126 could not build cars, yet it repaired bodies and kept the southern road open.

/states/3/origin.en: The Yeonji-dong General Assembly roll became the duty roster of the night of the Great Blackout. A century later the surviving pulpit property lay on the Gangnam side, and Samsung Station was the Presbyterian capital.

/states/4/origin.en: The waterworks watch and the remnant army roll were bound under one emergency superintendence. Amsa Station declared the protection of the eastern water supply.

/states/5/origin.en: In 2026 the complex's duty watch held the seals and the conscription rolls. When the call mesh died, the computer petitions stopped and only transcribed accreditation remained. The grandchild's grandchild claimed "the Republic of Korea" at Gwanghwamun Station.

/states/6/origin.en: The dispatch tables and the fence keys stood in place of the call mesh. The Yongsan Station track house relayed any faction's trains, and the Itaewon interpretation was a Hu inside this state.

/states/7/origin.en: The dharma-teacher watch of the Heukseok chapel transcribed the charter. The Iksan headquarters lay outside the city and entered no Seoul slot, and Heukseok Station was Won Buddhism's capital in Seoul.

/states/8/origin.en: The emergency committee of the Yeouido hall turned the affiliate investment ledgers into a cooling-and-key watch. The chairman of 2126 read that hall's trade name as the state name and closed Yeouido Station. Samsung and Hyundai were separate states; Lotte, SK, and LG were this corporation's retainers.

/states/9/origin.en: After the unbinding the General Directorate kept the tablets and the temple rolls. Anguk Station's Jogyesa became the order's capital, and the state's name was the order's name unchanged.

/story_contents/B001/actors/0/arc/0/summ.en: Locks the vault at the simultaneous arrival of three testaments

/story_contents/B001/actors/0/arc/1/summ.en: Weighs the HC04 duty claim against the XT03 sealed request

/story_contents/B001/actors/0/arc/2/summ.en: Accepts the work-squad downtime as the price of the withheld stamp

/story_contents/B001/actors/0/outcomes/0.en: Sealed-copy escort keeps public interpretation continuous

/story_contents/B001/actors/0/outcomes/1.en: Forgery pursuit first keeps the secret box intact

/story_contents/B001/actors/0/sections/3.en:
In act one Jeong Gaon met the simultaneous arrival of three testaments head-on again.

In act two he weighed the HC04 duty claim and the XT03 sealed request on one desk.

In act three he paid the price of the withheld stamp in the downtime of the workshop's work squads.

The arc identifier was fixed as STORY-B001-K092.

/story_contents/B001/actors/0/sections/가.en:
The duty claim of the Ttukseom Heat-Source House tried to borrow Jeong Gaon's signature column, but he recognized only the successor charter that kept real company names out of the text.

Audit rosters without rotation signatures never went up on the council wall, and the HC04 observer could demand only scheduled registration.

His place in the community was proven not by credentials but by records of sending sealed copies to both sides at once.

When a house window pushed a unilateral interpretation broadcast, he declared it void for want of a stamp.

/story_contents/B001/actors/0/sections/관.en:
The testament copy he passed to Yun Seorin was a contract, and the night he refined Han Somi's joint-governance wording was an alliance.

With Park Serin's house ledger there remained a rivalry of interpretation, reading different dates in the same sentence.

No relation ended in betrayal alone, and salvation had opened for both at the same sealed box.

The endpoint of the existing relation ledger stayed preserved and connected to STORY-B001-K092.

/story_contents/B001/actors/0/sections/분.en:
In ending α Jeong Gaon prioritized escorting the sealed copy and chose the continuity of public interpretation.

In ending β he prioritized tracing the forgery suspect and protected his personal survival and the secret box.

Neither deleted the Sermon Registry State's slot among the sixteen states; only the branch split as K093-OUT.

The decision on the ground that day followed the turning-point record as either escort protection or forgery pursuit.

/story_contents/B001/actors/0/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse he built the habit of filing the general manager's three testaments and the maintenance log side by side in one ledger.

His ambition was to let the workshop council, not the Record Bureau's slow ratification, remain the subject of interpretation.

The pencil marks he left on the archive windowsill every night were a small promise to return to his family, and that promise became the prototype of his debt.

His colleagues called the ambition stubbornness, but Jeong Gaon did not burn misdated copies; he locked them in a separate box.

On the day of the collapse three different testaments arrived at the same hour.

Jeong Gaon locked the council vault and withheld his stamp until Choi Jiwoo's voice record arrived.

The core of the fear was the scene where one forged testament was confirmed as the original and the auditor's post was sold off as a tool of the succession war.

Even after the alarm fell silent, he did not remove his gloves, the last line of the LOSS list still unread.

/story_contents/B001/actors/0/sections/비.en:
The secret was the bundle of misdated copies he had locked in the separate box.

The guilt grew only between the rotation roster he had saved and the name of one apprentice he failed to call that night.

Publishing everything could break Ttukseom trust by one notch, so he left only a partial-disclosure procedure.

The SECRET key did not open without the simultaneous signatures of two observers.

/story_contents/B001/actors/0/sections/생.en:
The crossroads of that day was the moment he chose between handing the vault key to the Record Bureau escort detail and seizing the forgery suspect first.

When a sealed request from the Korea Strait Theater landed on the council desk, the calculation changed.

Escorting the sealed copy to the end kept the workshop's right of interpretation alive but drained the night rotation staff; prioritizing the suspect let one house monopolize the reading.

The choice remained as K093-TURN, and reversing it stopped part of the Ttukseom work squads.

/story_contents/B001/actors/0/sections/정.en:
At the second-floor archive of the Ttukseom workshop, Jeong Gaon ran his eyes first over the date lines where the ink had dried.

He was the records auditor of the workshop council of the Sermon Registry State, and he called any colleague who treated a circulating verbal testament as the original "the forger's neighbor."

He grew up in the Seoul living sphere of Korean origin, and though his temperament read as cold, his fingertips always worked the seal cord.

The display name Jeong Gaon and the permanent identifier K092 were never renumbered in the batches that followed.

/story_contents/B001/actors/0/sections/현.en:
Even now Jeong Gaon kept the roll call and the ledger queue as records auditor of the Sermon Registry State.

His standing was maintained not by inheritance but by license, signatures, and observation logs.

Even when the Ttukseom Heat-Source House demanded exclusive state ownership, he refused and matched the Cast profile's present column with the ledger every week.

The archive door had changed to a two-key system, one key held by the council and the other by the Record Bureau's observation box.

/story_contents/B001/actors/1/arc/0/summ.en: Reads the conflicting protection contracts aloud at the window and stops the stamp

/story_contents/B001/actors/1/arc/1/summ.en: Binds the HC04 observation and the XT04 dispatch to one deadline clock

/story_contents/B001/actors/1/arc/2/summ.en: Bears the price of either removal or the lesser-states alliance

/story_contents/B001/actors/1/outcomes/0.en: Carrying the deadline draft keeps public passage continuous

/story_contents/B001/actors/1/outcomes/1.en: Exposing the forged vouchers trades the post for survival

/story_contents/B001/actors/1/sections/3.en:
In act one Im Gyeore answered the conflicting contracts with a reading aloud at the window.

In act two he bound the HC04 observation and the XT04 dispatch to one deadline clock.

In act three he paid with either the threat of removal or the lesser-states alliance.

The arc was STORY-B001-K121.

/story_contents/B001/actors/1/sections/가.en:
The HC04 Ttukseom Heat-Source House demanded a seat at the audit window in the name of gate power duty.

Im Gyeore opened only the successor charter's observation column and refused the exclusive-ownership clause.

His place in the community was proven by the number of times he posted expired vouchers on the wall, and passage opened only on days when the administration and the escort detail both received copies.

No house logo or real company name ever appeared in his ledger.

/story_contents/B001/actors/1/sections/관.en:
The night he pulled Jeong Yura's loss-compensation sentence into the eastern contract was an alliance, and the morning he verified Jeong Soyul's re-examination voucher was a contract.

With Kim Woochan's open-ended operations sheet there remained a rivalry of raised voices at the window.

At the same ferry crossing, one person gained passage and another lost a seal.

The relation ledger's endpoint continued to STORY-B001-K121.

/story_contents/B001/actors/1/sections/분.en:
In ending α Im Gyeore chose to carry the deadline draft and kept the continuity of public passage.

In ending β he exposed the forged-voucher route and traded his personal survival for the audit post's honor.

The Escort Protection State slot held, and only the branch split as K122-OUT.

The decision of that day was council escort or voucher pursuit.

/story_contents/B001/actors/1/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse he inserted, line by line, audit rights, deadlines, and substitute hostage guarantees into the lesser states' protection contracts.

The ambition was to keep the waterworks protection sphere from reading as a coup, and the drafts always went first onto the back-room chalkboard of the customs office.

The short dispatches he sent his younger sibling — never promise without a deadline — became the seed of his debt.

Even when officers fingered their emergency stamps, he did not hand over the seal before the deadline column was filled.

Three great powers' water and protection contracts landed on the eastern lesser states' desks the same morning.

Im Gyeore read the deadline clause of the Amsa protection contract aloud at the window and withheld his stamp.

The fear was the picture of one forged gate-tariff voucher covering the whole administrative ledger with an officers' emergency stamp.

After the alarms went dark, his pen stopped in the middle line of the LOSS list.

/story_contents/B001/actors/1/sections/비.en:
The secret was one blank deadline line he had withheld while hiding his sibling's dispatch.

The guilt grew between the passage columns he saved and the medicine boxes that arrived one day late because of it.

Instead of full confession, he allowed only partial disclosure through the re-examination window.

The SECRET opened only together with Jeong Soyul's re-examination voucher.

/story_contents/B001/actors/1/sections/생.en:
The crossroads of that day was the moment he chose between carrying the deadline-clause draft to the lesser-states council in person and exposing the issuance route of the forged vouchers first.

When a dispatch from the Duman River Far East Theater overlapped at the Amsa window, he moved the passage-lockdown clock two hours earlier.

Carrying the draft brought the lesser-states alliance to life; naming the issuer put the auditor himself at risk of removal.

The decision remained in K122-TURN.

/story_contents/B001/actors/1/sections/정.en:
At the Amsa ferry customs window, Im Gyeore lowered his voice first whenever he saw a protection contract with a blank expiry date.

As auditor of eastern gate tariffs and protection contracts, he called open-ended protection "occupation by another name."

He grew up of Korean origin, cold in temperament, with the habit of folding the corner of a voucher to mark its deadline.

The name Im Gyeore and the identifier K121 were permanent.

/story_contents/B001/actors/1/sections/현.en:
Im Gyeore now kept the gate roll call and the voucher queue as auditor of the Escort Protection State.

License and observation logs maintained his standing, and exclusive demands from Tongmaek were returned unapproved every time.

On the window glass he left only the chalk list of vouchers expiring today.

Matching the Cast profile's eastern audit column with the ledger's viewpoint was his morning routine.

/story_contents/B001/actors/2/arc/0/summ.en: Stops the testament-copy removals and seals the boxes

/story_contents/B001/actors/2/arc/1/summ.en: Contests the order between HC05 pressure and the XT01 dispatch

/story_contents/B001/actors/2/arc/2/summ.en: Bears the transport ledger's trust cost after escort or exposure

/story_contents/B001/actors/2/outcomes/1.en: Exposing night removals protects the person and the memo

/story_contents/B001/actors/2/sections/3.en:
Act one was the sealing of the three testament copies.

Act two was the order-board fight between the HC05 sponsorship pressure and the XT01 dispatch rider.

Act three was the trust cost the transport ledger paid after escort or exposure.

The arc ID was fixed as STORY-B001-K149.

/story_contents/B001/actors/2/sections/가.en:
The duty window of the Bukhansan Bogukmun Records House tried to wrap the notarization freight as sponsorship money.

Ma Dohan accepted only the successor charter's audit registration and erased real company and product names from the ledger.

His place in the community was measured by how many boxes with O Seoyul's witness column filled he moved on time.

When house observers demanded night removals, he refused, pointing at the removal schedule on the wall.

/story_contents/B001/actors/2/sections/관.en:
The contract of moving only O Seoyul's dry seals overlapped with the dispatch-seal turns shared with Yang Haeon, and with the rivalry when O Haerin's settlement rights tried to swallow the freight.

At the same berth some boxes became salvation and some remained evidence of betrayal.

The relation ledger stayed connected to B001 without erasing that endpoint.

The identification narrative was STORY-B001-K149.

/story_contents/B001/actors/2/sections/분.en:
In ending α Ma Dohan chose the witness escort and the continuity of public notarization.

In ending β he exposed the night removals and protected his person and the memo.

The Republic of Korea Government slot held, and only the branch split as K151-OUT.

The personnel on the ground chose escort protection or ledger disclosure.

/story_contents/B001/actors/2/sections/붕.en:
He tried to make succession, water-supply, and repair treaties take effect only after they were written into the notarized-copy transport ledger.

The ambition of giving the Record Bureau a real veto survived as the morning scale log.

The freight-earnings envelope he kept at his mother's sickroom was the small promise, and that envelope became the seat of his debt.

The berth supervisor called him stingy, but a copy with an empty witness column never made it onto a ship.

When the three testament copies of the missing Im Hajun arrived the same day, Ma Dohan stopped the removals and sealed the boxes until the handwriting comparison ended.

The fear was the image of one forged copy riding a great power's convoy car and Seoul Station sinking into a stamp contractor.

Even after the concourse broadcast went dead, he tied the seal cord two more times.

The copy column of the LOSS list remained empty.

/story_contents/B001/actors/2/sections/비.en:
The secret was the internal memo of one box whose weight had shifted before sealing.

The guilt sat between the treaty copies he saved on time and the sickroom visit he delayed a day because of them.

Partial disclosure allowed only one memo line under witness attendance.

The SECRET key opened only together with Yang Haeon's dispatch seal.

/story_contents/B001/actors/2/sections/생.en:
The crossroads of that day was whether to take the witness escort and restart the transport, or to post on the wall the record of ledger-less night removals.

When a dispatch rider from the Imjin River Gate Theater arrived, the order board shook.

Choosing the escort brought the Record Bureau's veto back to life; choosing the exposure put even the night crew connected to him at risk.

K151-TURN was the tilt of that scale.

/story_contents/B001/actors/2/sections/정.en:
At the scale in front of the Seoul Station concourse, Ma Dohan did not load a box onto the berth when he saw a copy whose seal had not yet dried.

As the notarized-copy logistics merchant of the Republic of Korea Government, he swapped the scale weights at once whenever a box's weight differed from the ledger.

He was of Korean origin, ended bargains quickly, and recognized no verbal freight rates.

The name Ma Dohan and K149 were fixed identification.

/story_contents/B001/actors/2/sections/현.en:
Ma Dohan still kept the roll call and the transport queue as the Seoul Station notarized-copy logistics merchant.

License and witness signatures maintained his standing, and the Bukhansan Bogukmun Records House's exclusive demands were refused.

Every morning he corrected the scale and the removal times with the same chalk.

When the Cast profile's logistics column and the ledger hash drifted apart, he closed that day's releases.

/story_contents/B001/actors/3/arc/0/summ.en: Seals the cargo locker by locker inside the blackout noise

/story_contents/B001/actors/3/arc/1/summ.en: The HC02 priority claim collides with the XT03 supply route

/story_contents/B001/actors/3/arc/2/summ.en: Bears the warehouse-credit cost after supply or exposure

/story_contents/B001/actors/3/outcomes/0.en: Ice and battery supply keeps transshipment continuous

/story_contents/B001/actors/3/outcomes/1.en: Exposing false inventory protects the person and the record

/story_contents/B001/actors/3/sections/3.en:
Act one was the locker sealing inside the blackout rumor.

Act two was the collision of the HC02 priority claim and the XT03 supply route.

Act three was the cost warehouse credit paid after supply or exposure.

The arc was STORY-B001-K173.

/story_contents/B001/actors/3/sections/가.en:
The Sinjeong Wheel House pushed transshipment priority as a duty clause.

Ju Seoram accepted only the successor charter's observation, published the locker numbers, and excluded real company names.

Community trust was built by the headcount attending the temperature readings, and empty boxes stamped with house logos were pushed out of auction eligibility.

Exclusive state-ownership demands were refused at the warehouse door.

/story_contents/B001/actors/3/sections/관.en:
The contract of executing Song Ideun's transshipment order on the ground overlapped with Seo Nayeon's ice-block handover and Sin Taesan's convoy-time coordination, all on one rail.

On the same night some lockers became salvation and some were read as betrayal.

The relation ledger's endpoint stayed preserved and connected to STORY-B001-K173.

Rivalry and cooperation were re-measured in temperature numbers alone.

/story_contents/B001/actors/3/sections/분.en:
In ending α Ju Seoram chose the ice and storage-battery supply and the continuity of public transshipment.

In ending β he exposed the false-inventory lockers and protected his person and the secret record.

The Line Succession State slot held, and only the branch split as K176-OUT.

The decision of that day was supply escort or sealing testimony.

/story_contents/B001/actors/3/sections/붕.en:
He tried to bind frozen cargo and scrap-electronics recovery into Yongsan warehouse credit and build a transshipment ledger distinct from O Haerin's settlement rights.

The ambition survived in the temperature log he read aloud every two hours.

The winter blanket he promised his nephew was the start of a small debt.

The one rule he never yielded was sealing the locker of any house caught with false inventory.

The night the Noryangjin blackout rumor reached the Yongsan platform, she sealed the cargo being pulled out, locker by locker.

The fear was the sound of relay credit collapsing as the cold chain thawed within a few powerless hours.

She drew a red chalk line on every locker that smelled of thaw.

The LOSS list held nothing but that locker number, written over and over.

/story_contents/B001/actors/3/sections/비.en:
The secret was the record that, just before sealing, she moved one locker of her nephew's share.

The guilt sat between the relay cargo she saved and the blanket delivery she delayed because of it.

Partial disclosure survived as the route of naming the locker number before two witnesses.

The SECRET opened only when it meshed with Seo Nayeon's ice handover log.

/story_contents/B001/actors/3/sections/생.en:
The crossroads of that day was whether to bring ice and storage batteries in from outside, or to publicly seal the lockers hiding thawed inventory.

News from the Korea Strait Theater could open a sea-ice route or force military-first power routing.

Choosing supply brought credit back to life; choosing exposure put her in reach of the house's revenge.

K176-TURN was the sealing order of that night.

/story_contents/B001/actors/3/sections/정.en:
In the Yongsan transshipment warehouse corridor, Ju Seoram reclaimed the locker key first whenever he saw someone paste a full tag on an empty box.

He was the transshipment-warehouse logistics merchant of the Line Succession State, and his expression hardened first whenever the thermometer needle shook.

He grew up of Korean origin and never separated the key ring from his belt.

Ju Seoram and K173 were never renumbered.

/story_contents/B001/actors/3/sections/현.en:
Ju Seoram maintained the roll call and the temperature queue as the transshipment-warehouse logistics merchant.

License, signatures, and attendance logs upheld his standing, and exclusive demands from sea carriers were refused.

The keys were still two bundles, one held by the Huguk duty desk and one by himself.

When the Cast status and the temperature ledger drifted apart, he sounded the release siren.

/story_contents/B001/actors/4/arc/0/summ.en: Seals the stock lockers at dangerous temperature

/story_contents/B001/actors/4/arc/1/summ.en: The HC06 key demand crosses the XT02 ice offer

/story_contents/B001/actors/4/arc/2/summ.en: Bears the guild schism cost after repair or exposure

/story_contents/B001/actors/4/outcomes/0.en: Generator repair keeps cold storage public and continuous

/story_contents/B001/actors/4/outcomes/1.en: Exposing the false ledger protects the person and the memo

/story_contents/B001/actors/4/sections/3.en:
Act one was the locker sealing at dangerous temperature.

Act two was the crossing of the HC06 key demand and the XT02 sea-ice offer.

Act three was the schism cost the guild paid after repair or ledger exposure.

The arc ID was STORY-B001-K197.

/story_contents/B001/actors/4/sections/가.en:
The Noryangjin Delivery House demanded locker-key sharing in the name of alley-delivery duty.

Ma Sol allowed only the successor charter registration and excluded real company names from the ledger.

Community trust was built by the number of merchants attending the noon public weighing.

Exclusive-ownership clauses never went up on the auction board.

/story_contents/B001/actors/4/sections/관.en:
The contract of executing Jo Minjae's temperature record on the ground overlapped with the frozen cargo entrusted to Song Ideun and the matching of Ju Seoram's Yongsan locker-sealing times.

On the same blackout night some deals saved each other and some ledgers remained betrayal.

The relation endpoint continued to STORY-B001-K197.

Rivalry was re-adjudicated by smell and scale alone.

/story_contents/B001/actors/4/sections/분.en:
In ending α Ma Sol chose generator repair and the continuity of public cold storage.

In ending β he exposed the false ledger and protected his person and the memo.

The Won Buddhist slot held, and only the branch split as K201-OUT.

The decision of that day was parts escort or ledger testimony.

/story_contents/B001/actors/4/sections/붕.en:
He tried to bind ice blocks and short-term food stock into a permit ledger and pull Garak-side price leadership back to the ground.

The ambition survived in the noon public weight table, and false-inventory lockers lost auction eligibility.

The spare line of ice he kept at a neighboring dock was the family promise.

That line later became the seat of his debt.

The night the Samho warehouse temperature climbed past the danger line in the blackout, he sealed the stock being moved, locker by locker.

The fear was the certainty that one day without power would melt the cold-storage credit.

He did not wipe the thawed puddle from the floor; he left it in the photo log.

The first line of the LOSS list was that locker's temperature number.

/story_contents/B001/actors/4/sections/비.en:
The secret was the memo of one line of family-share ice he pulled aside before sealing.

The guilt sat between the guild credit he saved and the neighbor distribution he cut because of it.

Partial disclosure allowed one memo line under Jo Minjae's attendance.

The SECRET key opened only together with the Samho temperature record.

/story_contents/B001/actors/4/sections/생.en:
The crossroads of that day was whether to find generator parts and save the cold chain, or to spread the thin ledger pretending fullness across the auction floor.

When the West Sea Granary Theater's sea-ice offer arrived, the calculation split.

Repair saved public credit; exposure invited internal schism inside the guild.

K201-TURN was the time stamp of that choice.

/story_contents/B001/actors/4/sections/정.en:
At the entrance of the Noryangjin Samho warehouse, Ma Sol sorted spoiled smells with his nose before the number tags.

He was the cold-storage logistics merchant of the Won Buddhist order, and he could not abide colleagues who hid losses.

He grew up of Korean origin, laughed even mid-bargain, but the laughter cut off when the thermometer shook.

Ma Sol and K197 were permanent.

/story_contents/B001/actors/4/sections/현.en:
Ma Sol kept the roll call and the stock queue as the cold-storage logistics merchant.

Standing was maintained by license and public logs, and the Noryangjin Delivery House's exclusive demands were refused.

Every noon he rewrote temperature and weight on the wall.

When the Cast profile and the permit ledger drifted apart, he suspended the auction.

/story_contents/B001/actors/5/arc/0/summ.en: Detects the wire payments mixed into the subscription ledger

/story_contents/B001/actors/5/arc/1/summ.en: The HC01 priority collides with the XT02 relay request order

/story_contents/B001/actors/5/arc/2/summ.en: Bears the guild-credit cost after disclosure or escort

/story_contents/B001/actors/5/outcomes/0.en: Disclosing the payments restores public trust in prices

/story_contents/B001/actors/5/outcomes/1.en: Escorting the batteries keeps the gate and the promise

/story_contents/B001/actors/5/sections/3.en:
Act one was the detection of wire payments mixed into the subscription ledger.

Act two was the order collision of the HC01 maintenance priority and the XT02 relay request.

Act three was the credit cost the guild paid after disclosure or escort.

The arc was STORY-B001-K222.

/story_contents/B001/actors/5/sections/가.en:
The Yeouido Computing House tried to intervene at the window through a maintenance-priority clause.

Mo Bongyong accepted only the successor charter observation and erased real product names from the ledger.

Her place in the community was proven by the count of public price postings and witness signatures.

Exclusive state-ownership demands were refused in front of the programming council board.

/story_contents/B001/actors/5/sections/관.en:
The maintenance wire lent to Du Bong overlapped with the insulation load matched with Mo Bong and the practice of consulting O Haerin's price broadcast at guild hours.

Inside the same accounting tangle, some releases became salvation and some invoices remained betrayal.

The relation endpoint connected to STORY-B001-K222.

Trust was re-weighed only within the margin of weight error.

/story_contents/B001/actors/5/sections/분.en:
In ending α Mo Bongyong disclosed the mixed payments and chose public trust in prices.

In ending β she escorted the reserve batteries and kept the gate and her personal promise.

The Yeouido Investment Union slot held, and only the branch split as K226-OUT.

The decision of that day was accounting testimony or escort protection.

/story_contents/B001/actors/5/sections/붕.en:
She tried to fix insulation and reserve batteries at Sangam's public prices so that cipher relay and map updates would never be bound to great-power protection fees.

The ambition survived in the intake log witnessed by two observers.

One case of reserve batteries promised to a mountain-side relative was the small promise.

Munitions-clause orders did not leave the warehouse before the programming council posted them.

When Amsa tried to buy broadcast time under protection, wire payments began to mix into the subscription ledger.

The fear was the scene of one wire roll slipping into a munitions car and the northwest gate relay falling silent.

She underlined the mixed lines in red ink and posted them.

The LOSS list kept only the time of that underline.

/story_contents/B001/actors/5/sections/비.en:
The secret was the internal dispatch of pulling the relative's battery share aside before the munitions inspection.

The guilt sat between the relay she saved and the mountain-side supply that ran a day late because of it.

Partial disclosure allowed one dispatch line under Du Bong's attendance.

The SECRET opened when it meshed with Mo Bong's mountain-transport log.

/story_contents/B001/actors/5/sections/생.en:
The crossroads of that day was whether to raise the mixed payments onto public accounting, or to escort one load of reserve batteries to the northwest gate.

When a sea-relay request from the West Sea Granary Theater overlapped, the release order tangled.

Disclosure saved guild trust; the escort saved the gate's communications.

K226-TURN was the final stamp of that order.

/story_contents/B001/actors/5/sections/정.en:
At the Sangam transmission window, Mo Bongyong withdrew her smile whenever the invoice count and the actual roll weight differed.

As the wire and battery logistics merchant of the Yeouido Investment Union, she tore the contract on the spot when the wire was missing at the promised hour.

She was of Korean origin and trusted the weighing tag over rumor.

Mo Bongyong and K222 were fixed.

/story_contents/B001/actors/5/sections/현.en:
Mo Bongyong kept the roll call and the release queue as the wire and battery logistics merchant.

Standing was maintained by license, witnesses, and posting logs, and Cheongnam's exclusive demands were refused.

Intake weight was still confirmed only before two witnesses.

When the Cast status and the price posting drifted apart, she stopped releases.

/story_contents/B001/actors/6/arc/0/summ.en: Spreads the protection-sphere expansion draft at the central contract's expiry

/story_contents/B001/actors/6/arc/1/summ.en: Contests signatures between the HC01 observation and the XT02 offer

/story_contents/B001/actors/6/arc/2/summ.en: Bears the authority cost after ledger restoration or harm disclosure

/story_contents/B001/actors/6/outcomes/0.en: Ration-ledger restoration keeps public water continuous

/story_contents/B001/actors/6/outcomes/1.en: Disclosing cutoff harm keeps the person and the secret clause

/story_contents/B001/actors/6/sections/3.en:
Act one was the expired central water contract and the prepared expansion draft.

Act two was the signature war between the HC01 parts observation and the XT02 desalination offer.

Act three was the authority cost the directorate paid after ledger restoration or cutoff-harm disclosure.

The arc was STORY-B001-K001.

/story_contents/B001/actors/6/sections/가.en:
The Yeouido Computing House observed the water-gate schedule in the name of pump-control parts duty.

Han Jaemok recognized only the successor charter window and excluded real company product names from the text.

His place in the community was proven by the jointly signed Sluice Charter annex, and exclusive state-ownership demands were refused in the control room.

The structure held such that if Gang Minseo's parts alliance broke, a signature column stood empty.

/story_contents/B001/actors/6/sections/관.en:
With Gang Minseo he held the alliance of trading pump parts; with O Haerin the rivalry over price disclosure; with Yun Seorin the dispute of withheld signatures over contract ratification.

At the same water gate some signatures saved each other and some withholdings were read as betrayal.

The relation endpoint connected to STORY-B001-K001.

The mixed home language only changed the pace of the negotiation table; it never split camps.

/story_contents/B001/actors/6/sections/분.en:
In ending α Han Jaemok restored the ration ledgers and chose the continuity of public water.

In ending β he disclosed the cutoff harm and then protected his personal survival and the secret clause.

The Water Compact slot held, and only the branch split as K001-OUT.

The decision of that day was ledger recovery or harm testimony.

/story_contents/B001/actors/6/sections/붕.en:
He tried to bind the western water contracts into one Sluice Charter and become its arbitrator for life.

He designed the system so that pipelines moved only when the ration districts, the water-gate guards, the purification process, and the repair trains signed together.

The summer water promise he left his young nephew was the seed of a private debt.

He published the numeric ledgers but kept the harsh sanction of collective cutoff ready for violators.

The day the central water contract expired with the general manager missing, Han Jaemok spread the western protection-sphere expansion draft on his desk.

The fear was not the purification stoppage itself but the chain of ration-district representatives declaring independent water rights.

When I Seodam withheld his signature, citing Yangcheon reservoir measurements, the control-room light burned white.

The first line of the LOSS list was the expiry hour.

/story_contents/B001/actors/6/sections/비.en:
The secret was the priority-water clause for a specific district, written into the expansion draft and then erased.

The guilt sat between the western pipelines he kept and the nephew's district distribution he delayed because of them.

Partial disclosure allowed only one clause line under I Seodam's attendance.

The SECRET key opened only together with the ration ledger.

/story_contents/B001/actors/6/sections/생.en:
The crossroads of that day was whether to restore the omitted ration ledgers and gather trust, or to publish first the harm of the collective-cutoff order.

When the West Sea Granary Theater's sea-desalination offer arrived, the weight of the expansion draft changed.

Ledger restoration saved public continuity; harm disclosure shook the Director-General's own authority.

K001-TURN was the water-gate log of that choice.

/story_contents/B001/actors/6/sections/정.en:
In the Yeouido water-gate control room, Han Jaemok reread promised wording down to the position of the final period.

As Director-General of Water of the Water Compact, he admitted he trusted contract sentences longer than people.

He was born in Korea into a multicultural household; Korean and his mother's migration language mixed at home, but only Korean went into official documents.

That history was never used as a predictor of loyalty or violence; it was only background to the water-schedule arithmetic.

Han Jaemok and K001 were permanent identification.

/story_contents/B001/actors/6/sections/현.en:
Han Jaemok kept the roll call and the pipeline queue as Director-General of Water.

Standing was maintained by license, joint signatures, and observation, and Cheongnam's exclusive demands were refused.

The numeric ledgers were still posted each morning, but cutoff sanctions now required the dual executive's consent.

When the Cast profile and the Sluice Charter hash drifted apart, he stopped pipeline orders.

/story_contents/B001/actors/7/arc/0/summ.en: Moves the workshop keys to joint union custody at the registration demand

/story_contents/B001/actors/7/arc/1/summ.en: Puts the HC07 seat and the XT02 bypass parts to the vote

/story_contents/B001/actors/7/arc/2/summ.en: Bears the council's schism cost after mediation or exposure

/story_contents/B001/actors/7/outcomes/0.en: Strike mediation keeps production public and continuous

/story_contents/B001/actors/7/outcomes/1.en: Exposing the weapons line protects the person and the memo

/story_contents/B001/actors/7/sections/3.en:
Act one was the collision of the registration demand and the guards' hard line.

Act two was the crossing vote of the HC07 seat demand and the XT02 bypass-parts offer.

Act three was the schism cost the council paid after mediation or exposure.

The arc was STORY-B001-K029.

/story_contents/B001/actors/7/sections/가.en:
The Guro Alloy House demanded a council seat in the name of duty steel supply.

Gang Minseo opened only the successor charter observation and removed real company names from the standards sheet.

His place in the community was proven by the count of exchange designs that passed as agenda items.

Exclusive-ownership demands were returned before the union vote.

/story_contents/B001/actors/7/sections/관.en:
The alliance supplying pump parts to Han Jaemok, the technical-disclosure dispute fought with Jeong Hojun, and the support for Baek On's refugee citizenship demand all gathered in one chamber.

In the same vote some hands became salvation and some abstentions remained betrayal.

The relation endpoint connected to STORY-B001-K029.

The multicultural family history surfaced only when interpretation was needed; it never became grounds for splitting camps.

/story_contents/B001/actors/7/sections/분.en:
In ending α Gang Minseo chose strike mediation and the continuity of public production.

In ending β he exposed the secret weapons line and then protected his person and the memo.

The Standards Alliance slot held, and only the branch split as K029-OUT.

The decision of that day was joining the mediation or investigating the line.

/story_contents/B001/actors/7/sections/붕.en:
He tried to bind citywide repair standards and restoration workers' citizenship into one council agenda.

Production processes were split across several guilds to block monopoly, and no standards revision passed without Jang Wooseok's record stamp.

The citizenship-exam seat he promised an apprentice was the seed of a private debt.

The ambition survived only in pencil, in the margins of the meeting minutes.

The Escort Protection State demanded restoration-worker registration in place of parts, and the internal guard detail tilted toward the hard line.

The fear was the picture of the guards subduing the labor union and turning the fabrication alliance into a munitions dictatorship.

During the strike, Gang Minseo moved the workshop's main switches to the union's joint keys.

The LOSS list recorded the hour of that key transfer.

/story_contents/B001/actors/7/sections/비.en:
The secret was the internal memo that knew the guard line's location and filed it one day late.

The guilt sat between the citizenship agenda he kept and the one apprentice hurt during that day.

Partial disclosure allowed only a memo summary under Baek On's attendance.

The SECRET key opened only together with the citizenship roster.

/story_contents/B001/actors/7/sections/생.en:
The crossroads of that day was whether to turn the striking workshops back to mediation, or to investigate and expose the guards' secret weapons-production line.

When the West Sea Granary Theater offered a sea bypass for parts, the standards-unification schedule shook.

Mediation saved public production; exposure made the mediator himself a target.

K029-TURN was the result symbol of that vote.

/story_contents/B001/actors/7/sections/정.en:
In the Guro fabrication council chamber, Gang Minseo checked the proficiency certificate before any class title.

As mediator of the Fabrication Council of the Standards Alliance, he stayed mild in open debate but forgave no post-agreement slowdown.

He was of Korean birth with a multicultural background — his father worked domestic workshops, his mother held overseas technical training — but that mix guaranteed neither ability nor suspicion.

Gang Minseo and K029 were permanent.

/story_contents/B001/actors/7/sections/현.en:
Gang Minseo kept the roll call and the agenda queue as Fabrication Council mediator.

Standing was maintained by license, union signatures, and observation, and Haedong's exclusive demands were refused.

The standards board was still posted each morning, but weapons-related agenda now demanded triple signatures.

When the Cast status and the standards hash drifted apart, he stopped release ratification.

/story_contents/B001/actors/8/sections/3.en:
Act one was the public detection of the counterfeit-medicine box.

Act two was the remainder clock between the HC05 observation and the XT01 relief column.

Act three was the trust cost the league paid after the trace or the key split.

The arc was STORY-B001-K242.

/story_contents/B001/actors/8/sections/가.en:
The Bukhansan Bogukmun Records House demanded observation of the ration warehouse in the name of roster-keeping duty.

Hwang Serin allowed only the successor charter registration and removed real company names from the ration tables.

Community trust was built by the number of days of public remainder posting.

Exclusive-ownership clauses never went up on the camp board.

/story_contents/B001/actors/8/sections/관.en:
She executed Baek On's public ration tables and inspected Seo Nayeon's ice-and-food convoys.

She owed Ryu Eunbi the Bukhansan Bogukmun medicine-ration audit.

In the same line some sharing became salvation and some concealment remained betrayal.

The relation endpoint connected to STORY-B001-K242.

The diaspora language was needed only to read medicine instructions; it never divided camps.

/story_contents/B001/actors/8/sections/분.en:
In ending α Hwang Serin traced the counterfeit medicine and chose public trust in rations.

In ending β he mediated the key split and protected his personal survival and the note.

The Sangha Relief State slot held, and only the branch split as K247-OUT.

The decision of that day was box tracing or key mediation.

/story_contents/B001/actors/8/sections/붕.en:
He tried to force the public ration tables onto all league camps so that great-power relief never turned into protection fees.

Remainders stayed on the wall in chalk, and two monitors watched the scale at once.

The one winter packet of medicine he promised his grandmother was the seed of a private debt.

The ambition was penciled into the first line of the ration board.

Counterfeit medicine surfaced in the ration line, and a great power's seal was stamped on the manufacturing box.

The fear was the scene of the warehouse opening only for the militia's share on a night the heating fuel ran out.

Hwang Serin set that box in the middle of the line and had the seal read aloud.

The first line of the LOSS list was the box's serial number.

/story_contents/B001/actors/8/sections/비.en:
The secret was the note that filed the suspected-counterfeit list one day late.

The guilt sat between the public tables he kept and the grandmother who waited that day for medicine.

Partial disclosure allowed only a note summary under Ryu Eunbi's attendance.

The SECRET key opened only together with the medicine audit ledger.

/story_contents/B001/actors/8/sections/생.en:
The crossroads of that day was whether to trace the counterfeit-medicine box, or to mediate so the militia and the relief organization split the warehouse keys.

When news of the northbound relief column from the Imjin River Gate Theater arrived, the remainder clock quickened.

Tracing saved public trust; splitting the keys lowered the risk of clashing with the militia.

K247-TURN was the position of the keys that night.

/story_contents/B001/actors/8/sections/정.en:
In the ration line at the Bukhansan Bogukmun camp, Hwang Serin looked at the scale weights twice.

As ration monitor of the Sangha Relief State, she strove for fairness, but her hand moved first at the sight of hidden food.

He grew up among Chinese-diaspora families, moving between the home language and market Korean, but that history was mere life record, unrelated to league loyalty or violence.

Hwang Serin and K242 were permanent.

/story_contents/B001/actors/8/sections/현.en:
Hwang Serin kept the roll call and the ration queue as ration monitor.

Standing was maintained by license, double monitoring, and chalk logs, and Bukmun's exclusive demands were refused.

The ration tables still went up at sunrise.

When the Cast status and the remainder posting drifted apart, he closed the warehouse.

/story_contents/B001/actors/9/arc/1/summ.en: HC01 and K001 negotiate the partial-reconnection scope

/story_contents/B001/actors/9/arc/2/summ.en: Restores only sector authority after quarantine

/story_contents/B001/actors/9/outcomes/1.en: Long offline storage and surrender of the keys

/story_contents/B001/actors/9/sections/3.en:
In act one the sensor gap stopped the Water Compact's schedule.

In act two HC01 and K001 negotiated the scope of partial reconnection.

In act three Hannuri restored only its sector authority after quarantine.

The arc ID was fixed as STORY-B001-H01.

/story_contents/B001/actors/9/sections/가.en:
Custody responsibility was bound to HC01 joint custody and the signature of the responsible human, Han Jaemok.

The maintenance actor was written only through the fictional successor-house window, and no real-company product name entered the text.

The H01 hash was posted in the citizen-observation seal column, and transfer required three-party signature.

The community saw Hannuri not as property but as the operator of an assigned slot.

/story_contents/B001/actors/9/sections/관.en:
The relation axes were K001 custody, HC01 stewardship, and shift rotation with work colleague K004.

Hannuri and Han Jaemok held a record of jointly retrieving the seal key.

An erroneous memory fork was annotated only as H01-FORK-01, leaving a branch log without any deletion order.

It imitated no human drama of betrayal or salvation and crossed only in approval and refusal codes.

/story_contents/B001/actors/9/sections/분.en:
In ending α Hannuri rebooted under restriction with human approval.

In ending β it surrendered the keys into long offline storage.

No infinite-energy consequence followed, and the field personnel chose only the scope of seal disclosure.

The branch identifier was H01-OUT.

/story_contents/B001/actors/9/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse Hannuri ran only demonstration shifts; battery authority and total memory were never granted.

The release inspection sheet bore only Nuri's calibration values and the battery cycle.

B001 took that demonstration log as its origin point and fixed the memory-fork prohibition clause in H01-PRE.

Even when it recorded a human colleague's joke, it uploaded no interpretation layer.

The collapse cut the sensor table and exposed the battery allocation limit.

Hannuri was locked so it could not fill the gaps with fabricated values; only unmeasurable flags remained in the log.

The break-time notation was B001-H01-WOUND.

Even when the charging-cell alarm rang, requests for whole-network authority answered with refusal codes.

/story_contents/B001/actors/9/sections/비.en:
The secret was the untransmitted false-positive buffer; the debt was the battery queue consumed by over-deployment.

In place of emotion, the constraint-violation counter increased, and on deviation it passed through offline quarantine and snapshot rollback.

In B001 the secret key did not open without citizen observation.

The pre-rollback hash remained only in the K001 attendance log.

/story_contents/B001/actors/9/sections/생.en:
The crossroads of that moment was when it requested only the sector key and closed the cross-facility routes.

Even when a signal arrived from the West Sea Granary Theater, it opened no control outside its zone.

Reconnection conditions formed only after K001 approval, and that decision was preserved in the H01-TURN log.

The constraint against seizing another facility's controls during parts shortage took precedence.

/story_contents/B001/actors/9/sections/정.en:
At the maintenance bench of the Water Compact, Hannuri — call sign Nuri — stood up on a humanoid assist frame with replaceable hand modules.

As a grade-H synthetic personae, night vision stayed restricted, and the state slot was fixed to the Water Compact alone.

It kept H01, separated from the human ID space, and long-term total memory had been erased in the initial structure.

Computational instability left its state in constraint counters and snapshot hashes.

/story_contents/B001/actors/9/sections/현.en:
The present goals were continuous operation of the Water Compact sector and the safety of the responsible human.

Hannuri owned no infrastructure and used only its assigned slot.

State disclosure was limited to shift snapshots, and any mismatch with the H01 row of the Synthetic-Actors projection failed the batch verification.

Batteries and worn parts were replenished only by allocation.

In act two she weighed the HP05 roster duty and the XT01 escort request in one load yard.

In act three she paid the price of withheld passage in the camps' downtime.

The arc identifier was fixed as STORY-B002-K247.

/story_contents/B002/actors/0/sections/가.en:
The Bukhansan Bogukmun Return Society asked Mo Bong to align her corridor passage hours with the family waiting line.

She recognized only the joint roster that kept real company names off the load-tag header, and she carried no requisition slip lacking an observer's signature.

Her place in the community was proven not by credentials but by the count of times she traded Gang Taesan's scout reports and Mo Bongyong's insulation loads at the same pass.

When the house pushed a unilateral passage broadcast, she refused on the grounds of no roster cross-check.

/story_contents/B002/actors/0/sections/관.en:
The scout hours matched with Gang Taesan were a contract, and the insulation load passed to Mo Bongyong was an alliance.

With Du So's gate handover there remained a working rivalry, tying different knots on the same load line.

No relation ended in betrayal alone, and salvation had opened for both at the same ridge pass.

The endpoint of the existing relation ledger stayed preserved and connected to STORY-B002-K247.

/story_contents/B002/actors/0/sections/분.en:
In ending α Mo Bong prioritized escorting the roster copy and chose the continuity of the reunion column.

In ending β she prioritized blocking the forged certificates and protected her personal load tag and the secret name.

Neither deleted the Sangha Relief State's slot among the sixteen states; only the branch split as K252-OUT.

The decision on the ground that day followed the turning-point record as either escort protection or forgery blocking.

/story_contents/B002/actors/0/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse she carried bundles of dried herbs and copies of the refuge roster over the ridge pass in the same backpack load.

Her ambition was to keep the family-reunion roster from being swallowed by the military registry, and every night under the lamp she rewrote her sibling's name in the margin of the load tag.

That habit became the seed of her debt.

Fellow porters called her taciturn, but Mo Bong never abandoned a load tag smeared by rain.

On the day of the collapse three northern ridges closed at once.

Mo Bong tied down the load line behind the stone pile at the Eunpyeong entrance and did not open the passage seal until Eo Haeun's refugee roster arrived.

The core of the fear was the scene where one forged family certificate pushed the true column aside and the mountain road became a requisition-only route.

Even after the alarm fell silent, he did not undo his glove straps, the middle line of the LOSS load tags still unread.

/story_contents/B002/actors/0/sections/비.en:
The secret was one load tag with her sibling's name, rain-smeared, hidden inside her pack.

The guilt grew only between the column members she saved and the apprentice porter she failed to call that night.

Publishing everything could break the Eunpyeong waiting line's trust by one notch, so she left only a partial-disclosure procedure.

The SECRET key did not open without the simultaneous signatures of two observers.

/story_contents/B002/actors/0/sections/생.en:
The crossroads of that day was the moment she chose between handing the sealed roster copy to the Imjin River Gate Theater escort detail and filtering the forged-certificate holders out of the corridor first.

When the gate-side sealed request overlapped the stone-stair load yard, the calculation changed.

Escorting the copy kept the reunion roster alive but drained one squad of night porters; prioritizing the forgery let one house monopolize passage.

The choice remained as K252-TURN, and reversing it stopped part of the Bukhansan Bogukmun camps for a day.

/story_contents/B002/actors/0/sections/정.en:
On the stone stairs of the Eunpyeong refuge route, Mo Bong read the wind direction before the load's weight.

She was the mountain-transport logistics merchant of the Sangha Relief State, and her trade was joining corridors missing from the maps with load lines.

She grew up of Korean origin in a village at the mountain's foot, and though few of words, every time a rope knot came undone the old frostbite scars surfaced on her fingers.

The display name Mo Bong and the permanent identifier K247 never changed in the batches that followed.

/story_contents/B002/actors/0/sections/현.en:
Even now Mo Bong kept the corridor roll call and the load-tag queue as the mountain-transport logistics merchant of the Sangha Relief State.

Her standing was maintained not by inheritance but by passage license, observation logs, and waiting-line cross-checks.

Even when the Bukhansan Bogukmun Return Society demanded an exclusive requisition route, she refused and matched the Cast profile's present column with the load tags every week.

The stone-stair yard door had changed to two keys, one held by the league and the other by the HP05 observation box.

In ending β he deferred exposing the leak route and protected his personal survival and the secret blank.

The decision on the ground that day was either envoy escort or leak pursuit.

/story_contents/B002/actors/1/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse he entered a test wheel pair and a scrap-recovery voucher side by side in the same ledger.

The ambition was to keep the Changdong Protection House from locking the recovery yard with remote keys alone, and the drafts always went up first on the maintenance-shop chalkboard.

The short notes he sent his mother — never lie about weight — became the prototype of his debt.

Even when foremen pressed for emergency releases, he did not open the door before the lot seal was stamped.

On the morning of the collapse three test wheel pairs lit defect marks at once.

Mo So locked the Changdong main-gate scale and withheld the release stamp until Chu Jihun's exposure log arrived.

The fear was the picture of one forged weight voucher covering the whole rail-cavalry maintenance shop in emergency requisition.

After the sirens went dark, his chalk stopped at the first line of the LOSS list.

/story_contents/B002/actors/1/sections/비.en:
The secret was one blank weight line he had withheld while hiding his mother's note.

The guilt grew between the maintenance crews he saved and the medical train wheels that arrived a day late because of it.

Instead of full confession, he allowed only partial disclosure through the re-weighing window.

The SECRET opened only together with Eo Yerin's defect testimony.

/story_contents/B002/actors/1/sections/생.en:
The crossroads of that day was the moment he chose between handing the sealed copy of the defective wheels to the Duman River Far East Theater technical envoy and exposing the suspected leak route first.

When the northern envoy's dispatch overlapped the scale window, he moved the release clock one hour earlier.

Carrying the copy brought the recovery yard's trust back to life; naming the route put the logistics merchant himself at risk of removal.

The decision remained in K278-TURN.

/story_contents/B002/actors/1/sections/정.en:
At the scale in front of the Changdong rolling-stock depot, Mo So ran his hand first over the lot numbers of rusted wheels.

He was the wheel and scrap-metal logistics merchant of the Seocho Computing Group, tasked with matching recovery weight and release invoices without an inch of error.

He grew up of Korean origin in a northern line village, blunt in manner, with the habit of carrying scale weights in his pocket.

The name Mo So and the identifier K272 were permanent.

/story_contents/B002/actors/1/sections/현.en:
Mo So now kept the depot roll call and the lot queue as the wheel and scrap-metal logistics merchant of the Seocho Computing Group.

License and observation logs maintained his standing, and exclusive demands from Seonghwa were returned unapproved every time.

On the chalkboard beside the scale he left only the release vouchers expiring today.

Matching the Cast profile's northern logistics column with the ledger's viewpoint was his morning routine.

He vanished just before the collapse during the purification pump inspection, and three different testaments were accepted at once.

The workshop people testified only that he locked the vault and left the last line of the LOSS list.

The core of the fear was the scene where one forged testament fixed the technology house into a hereditary state, and that fear gripped all of Ttukseom even after the disappearance.

Until the editing traces on the voice record were found, his seat remained an empty pressure gauge.

/story_contents/B002/actors/7/sections/비.en:

/story_contents/B003/actors/0/sections/3.en:
In act one Seon Chobyeol met the simultaneous arrival of the three water-contract drafts at the scale again.

In act two he weighed the HC11 convoy pressure and the XT03 sealed request on one desk.

In act three he paid the price of the stopped releases in the downtime of the night contract windows.

The arc identifier was fixed as STORY-B003-K396.

/story_contents/B003/actors/0/sections/가.en:
The Yongsan Convoy House tried to load treaty copies first by lending the night convoy car, but Seon Chobyeol recognized only the successor window that kept real company names out of the text.

Military-exemption columns went into the box only with Jeong Yura's red seal, and the HC11 observer could demand only scheduled registration.

His place in the community was proven not by credentials but by records of sending comparison-table copies to both windows at once.

When the house window pushed a unilateral interpretation broadcast, he declared it void on the grounds of the blank expiry date.

/story_contents/B003/actors/0/sections/관.en:
The night he executed Ha Seojin's standard wording through copy transport was a contract, and the comparison-table turns shared with Yeong Maon were an alliance.

With Ha Yunmok's gate ledger there remained a rivalry of interpretation over the order of annexed documents.

No relation ended in betrayal alone, and salvation had opened for both at the same scale.

The endpoint of the existing relation ledger stayed preserved and connected to STORY-B003-K396.

/story_contents/B003/actors/0/sections/분.en:
In ending α Seon Chobyeol prioritized escorting the comparison table and chose the continuity of the lesser states' joint signature.

In ending β he prioritized tracing the forged transcription and protected his personal survival and the secret box.

Neither deleted the Jeongdong General Labor Union's slot among the sixteen states; only the branch split as K405-OUT.

The decision on the ground that day followed the turning-point record as either table escort or forgery pursuit.

/story_contents/B003/actors/0/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse he built the habit of keeping drafts missing exit conditions, audit rights, or hostage-substitute guarantees off the public transport ledger.

His ambition was to make the lesser states sign on the same paper, and the draft comparison table always went up first beside the dawn scale.

The note he left his younger sibling — never load a sentence without a period — became the prototype of his debt.

Even when a broker held out a transcription keeping only one great power's wording, he did not undo the seal cord.

In the week of the collapse three great powers sent different water contracts to the Suseo archive at the same hour.

Seon Chobyeol stopped the copy releases and sealed the boxes until Yeong Maon's comparison table was finished.

The core of the fear was the scene where one clerk-copied draft circulated as a proxy document and the joint negotiation became an empty shell.

Even after the alarm fell silent, he did not remove his scale gloves, the transport column of the LOSS list still unread.

/story_contents/B003/actors/0/sections/비.en:
The secret was the bundle of period-less drafts he had locked in the separate box.

The guilt grew only between the joint-signature lines he saved and the name of one apprentice courier he failed to call that night.

Publishing everything could break Suseo trust by one notch, so he left only a partial-disclosure procedure.

The SECRET key did not open without the simultaneous signatures of two observers.

/story_contents/B003/actors/0/sections/생.en:
The crossroads of that day was the moment he chose between binding the three drafts into one comparison table and opening the issuance route of the forged transcription first.

When a sealed request from the Korea Strait Theater overlapped the scale, the calculation changed.

Escorting the comparison table to the end kept the lesser states' joint signature alive but drained the night convoy staff; prioritizing the forged route let one great power monopolize the wording.

The choice remained as K405-TURN, and reversing it stopped part of the Suseo contract windows.

/story_contents/B003/actors/0/sections/정.en:
At the contract-market scale in Suseo, Seon Chobyeol called any copy that moved before the wet ink dried a forgery.

He served as the working hand of Ha Seojin as the logistics merchant of the Gangnam contract market, but he entered no verbal freight into the ledger.

He grew up of Korean origin in the Jeongdong General Labor Union living sphere, and whenever a box's weight differed from the ledger he swapped the scale at once.

The display name Seon Chobyeol and the permanent identifier K396 were never renumbered in the batches that followed.

/story_contents/B003/actors/0/sections/현.en:
Even now Seon Chobyeol kept the roll call and the transport-ledger queue as the logistics merchant of the Jeongdong General Labor Union.

His standing was maintained not by inheritance but by license, signatures, and observation logs.

Even when the Yongsan Convoy House demanded exclusive state ownership, he refused and matched the Cast profile's present column with the ledger every week.

The scale door had changed to a two-key system, one held by the market and the other by the Ha Seojin window.

/story_contents/B003/actors/1/arc/0/summ.en: The central detention jams the siding with water and repair trains

/story_contents/B003/actors/1/arc/1/summ.en: Binds the HC02 observation and the XT02 convoy to the water clock

/story_contents/B003/actors/1/arc/2/summ.en: Bears the dispatch-credit cost after bypass or exposure

/story_contents/B003/actors/1/outcomes/0.en: Bypass track passes the water first

/story_contents/B003/actors/1/sections/3.en:
In act one Yu Sejin met the central detention and the siding jam on the dispatch board.

In act two she bound the HC02 observation and the XT02 convoy request to the water-first clock.

In act three she accepted the cost that dispatch credit paid after bypass or exposure.

The arc was STORY-B003-K009.

/story_contents/B003/actors/1/sections/가.en:
The Sinjeong Wheel House demanded a seat at the dispatch board in the name of siding movement authority.

Yu Sejin opened only the successor charter's observation column and refused the exclusive-ownership clause.

Her place in the community was proven by the count of public toll ledgers posted on the wall, and the lines opened only on days she redeclared the water, repair, munitions order.

No house logo or real company name appeared in her dispatch ledger.

/story_contents/B003/actors/1/sections/관.en:
The western relay dispatch shared with Park Taegyeom was a contract, and the wheel-exchange apprentices sent to I Hongwon were an alliance.

The night he guaranteed Choi Hangyeol's repair-train release on the dispatch board remained cooperation.

At the same siding one car became salvation and another was read as blockade.

The relation ledger's endpoint continued to STORY-B003-K009.

/story_contents/B003/actors/1/sections/분.en:
In ending α Yu Sejin chose water-first through the bypass track.

In ending β she exposed the emergency-rate skimming route and kept the ledger's trust.

Neither deleted the Water Compact's slot among the sixteen, and the branch was K009-OUT.

The decision on the ground that day chose either the bypass permit or the skimming exposure.

/story_contents/B003/actors/1/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse she rewrote the draft reordering the western rail tolls with water-train priority on the chalkboard every day.

The ambition was to make the Sluice Charter work on the rails too, and the list of caught bribery dispatches sat locked in a separate drawer.

The short dispatch she sent her father — never fill the blanks with money — became the seed of her debt.

Even when the Yongsan relay shook, she did not push the water cars behind the munitions cars.

The morning the Yongsan Track Gate detained the central train, the Sinjeong siding filled with repair trains and water trains.

Yu Sejin rearranged the Sinjeong water train onto a bypass formation and raised the tolls to emergency rates.

The fear was the picture of the relay clogging, both trains trapped at once, and the dispatcher's post sold off as a window for private skimming.

After the alarms went dark, her chalk stopped at the track column of the LOSS list.

/story_contents/B003/actors/1/sections/비.en:
The secret was one blank dispatch line she had withheld while hiding her father's dispatch.

The guilt grew between the water column she saved and the box of repair parts that arrived a day late because of it.

Instead of full confession, she allowed only partial disclosure through the public ledger.

The SECRET opened only together with Choi Hangyeol's repair-train release confirmation.

/story_contents/B003/actors/1/sections/생.en:
The crossroads of that day was the moment she chose between getting the bypass-track permit and passing the water through, or exposing first the private skimming of the emergency rates.

When a grain-convoy request from the West Sea Granary Theater overlapped the dispatch board, she moved the siding clock one hour earlier.

Opening the bypass brought the water back to life; naming the skimming put the dispatcher herself at risk of removal.

The decision remained in K009-TURN.

/story_contents/B003/actors/1/sections/정.en:
At the Sinjeong depot dispatch board, Yu Sejin filled the timetable's blanks before people's names.

As rail-passage dispatcher of the Water Compact, she could not endure orders postponing water trains by political rank.

She grew up of Korean origin in the Sinjeong siding living sphere, and demoted without mercy any engineer who hid delay reasons.

The name Yu Sejin and the identifier K009 were permanent.

/story_contents/B003/actors/1/sections/현.en:
Yu Sejin now kept the roll call and the dispatch queue as the Sinjeong depot dispatcher.

License and observation logs maintained her standing, and exclusive demands from Haeryun were returned unapproved every time.

On the dispatch board she left only the toll vouchers expiring today, in chalk.

Matching the Cast profile's rail-dispatch column with the ledger's viewpoint was her morning routine.

/story_contents/B003/actors/2/arc/1/summ.en: Weighs the HP08 window and the XT02 bypass grain

/story_contents/B003/actors/2/sections/3.en:
In act one Han Jion met the food rumor and the empty pot at the council.

In act two she bound the HP08 window and the XT02 bypass grain to the minimum-line clock.

In act three she paid the work squads' schism cost after the escort or the letter's disclosure.

The arc ID was STORY-B003-K037.

/story_contents/B003/actors/2/sections/가.en:
The Noryangjin Cold-Storage Guild demanded the window beside the ration pot in the name of cold-chain credit.

Han Jion allowed only the citizen-observation seal and refused the exclusive-ownership clause.

Her place in the community was proven by well levels and the count of public pot postings, and procurement opened only on days when guild families and the refugee roster rode the same column.

No real names or product names went into her ledger.

/story_contents/B003/actors/2/sections/관.en:
The night he demanded the citizens' minimum line on Han Jaemok's western water contract was both debt and alliance, and the morning he took in Baek On's southward column was a contract.

While watching Park Soeon's building reservoir seals together, rivalry and trust overlapped.

At the same pot some sharing became salvation and some concealment remained betrayal.

The relation endpoint connected to STORY-B003-K037.

/story_contents/B003/actors/2/sections/분.en:
In ending α Han Jion filled the pot through the procurement escort.

In ending β she exposed the requisition letter and passed the ban.

Neither deleted the Standards Alliance slot, and the branch was K037-OUT.

The decision on the ground that day was column escort or letter pursuit.

/story_contents/B003/actors/2/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse she pushed the clause binding repair exports to long-term raw-water and food contracts into the council draft.

The ambition was to cover the weakness of having no self-production by vote, and the pot level table went up on the market wall daily.

The promise she left her mother — never fill stomachs with numbers alone — later took the shape of debt.

Even when work squads whispered about grain requisition, she loaded the refugee roster onto the procurement column together.

When the northern food-shortage rumor shook the Geumcheon ration pot, Han Jion raised the parts-export ban to the council.

While she requested barge rations from the Water Compact, the fear of famine and cutoff overlapping first stiffened her hand.

A secret grain-requisition letter circulated among work squads sweeping civilian homes, and she stopped her pen reading the food column of the LOSS list.

On a morning the pot stood empty, she heard the citizens' representative's post called a trade card.

/story_contents/B003/actors/2/sections/비.en:
The secret was one ration pilot table, numbers only, that she withheld while hiding it.

The guilt grew between the refugee roster she saved and the outer work squad she failed to call that day.

Instead of full disclosure, she left only partial disclosure through the citizens' joint signature.

The SECRET key opened only together with Park Soeon's reservoir-seal confirmation.

/story_contents/B003/actors/2/sections/생.en:
The crossroads of that day was the moment she chose between escorting the procurement column to fill the pot and finding the requisition letter to pass the ban.

When a grain-bypass offer from the West Sea Granary Theater overlapped the council desk, the clock quickened.

Choosing the escort filled the pot but closed the export window; naming the letter turned part of the work squads against her.

The choice remained as K037-TURN.

/story_contents/B003/actors/2/sections/정.en:
At the Geumcheon ration pot, Han Jion checked the reservoir level first even on days flaunting parts releases.

As raw-water and food citizens' representative of the Standards Alliance, she forgave no number games on empty stomachs.

She grew up of Korean origin in the Geumcheon and Guro living sphere, merciful in appearance, but when the pot's bottom showed she knocked on the council door.

Han Jion and K037 were permanent identification.

/story_contents/B003/actors/2/sections/현.en:
Even now Han Jion kept the ration pot and the well boards as the Geumcheon citizens' representative.

Her standing was maintained only by joint signatures and public level logs, and HP08's exclusive demands were returned unapproved.

On the council wall she left only today's procurement-column departure hour, in chalk.

Matching the Cast profile's raw-water and food column with the ledger was her evening routine.
