/story_contents/B013/actors/3/outcomes/1.en: Publishing the winning bidder's name closes the direct-trade window for military rations

/story_contents/B013/actors/3/sections/3.en:
In act 1, Won Juon met again, at the same lock, the blank cell of the blockade night and the trace of the opening.

In act 2, he weighed the HP08 power slot and the XT03 canned-goods allocation on one line of the blackboard.

In act 3, he paid for reassigning power to the citizens' cell or publishing the winning bidder with a gap in the ice storehouse.

The narrative line was STORY-B013-K376.

/story_contents/B013/actors/3/sections/가.en:
The Noryangjin Cold-Storage Guild tried to put observation of the bypass coordinates into the duty cell, citing the rotation of power slots.

Won Juon did not put the coordinates on the auction blackboard, and passed only the print of Gu Haon's temperature log to the observation window.

His place in the community was proved not by rank but by copies posted at the warehouse-depot blackboard and the auction floor at the same time.

The demand to move the search warrant of the military-ration sentence into the map's margin was rejected by a note that the temperature log had broken.

/story_contents/B013/actors/3/sections/관.en:
The bypass survey he handed to Ra Jinwoo was a contract, and the night he pinned the coordinates to Pan Hyodam's warehouse-depot blackboard was a sharing of the same seal.

The silence in which he agreed not to leave Nam Yungyeong's undisclosed emergency ration as a title on the master plate was sometimes read as a betrayal, and the same silence also saved the citizens' cell.

They did not take sides by the temperature figures alone.

The endpoint of the relations continued into STORY-B013-K376.

/story_contents/B013/actors/3/sections/분.en:
In ending α, Won Juon moved the power of the broken temperature cell onto the citizens' boxes and left the ration cell cold.

In ending β, he posted on the auction blackboard the name of the winning bidder who had opened the lock, and closed the direct-trade window for military rations.

Neither side erased the Cathedral Accreditation State's slot among the sixteen states, and only the branch identifier split as K384-OUT.

The decision on the ground at the time chose only one of attendance at the power reassignment and the publishing of the winning name, and followed the turning-point record.

/story_contents/B013/actors/3/sections/붕.en:
In the year the auction bell struck, Won Juon bound the bypass storehouses outside Garak and Jamsil onto the public master plate, so that the producing states' direct trade could not turn the auction floor into empty boxes.

His ambition was a note of bypass coordinates hidden under the blackboard, and for fear that the note would later become bait for diverting military rations, he left any storage he had not surveyed as a dotted line alone.

Even when a seal mark aged by only a day, he did not fold the map.

He bound himself not to raise Nam Yungyeong's undisclosed emergency ration onto the master plate as a title.

On the night of the warehouse blockade, the same cell stood empty at once in the trace of an inner opening and on the map of the bypass storehouse.

Won Juon did not fill the blank cell with a poor-harvest rumor, and wrote in the log only the temperature of the lock.

The core of the fear was a scene in which a forged bypass led to a diversion for military rations and the citizens' ration was left as a dotted line alone.

Even after the motor noise died, he did not take the seal thread out of his pocket.

/story_contents/B013/actors/3/sections/비.en:
The secret was one sheet of the temperature log, folded into the groove of the lock.

On that sheet, a below-freezing figure he had not measured left the citizens' cell marked as passed.

The guilt clung to that false below-freezing figure, and Nam Yungyeong's emergency-ration number stood only in the margin, not in the title cell.

The copy of the log came out only after Gu Haon opened the print cell and Ra Jinwoo received the bypass survey.

/story_contents/B013/actors/3/sections/생.en:
In the Garak ice storehouse, Won Juon weighed whether to move the power order of the broken temperature cell onto the citizens' boxes, or to post on the auction blackboard the name of the winning bidder who had opened the lock on the night of the blockade.

When the canned-goods allocation demand from the Korea Strait Theater came in over the transshipment-window radio, the calculation changed.

Moving the order left the citizens' ration cell cold, but the motor of the military-ration cell stopped for one shift; posting the winning bidder's name closed the direct-trade window, but the night storage crew dropped out into the investigation.

That choice remained as K384-TURN, and reversing it stopped the public slot of the Garak ice storehouse for one shift.

/story_contents/B013/actors/3/sections/정.en:
Before the lock of the Garak bypass storehouse, Won Juon scratched with a fingernail at the seal date of the cell where the temperature log had broken.

As a surveyor of the southeast bypass storehouses, he turned on the flashlight first when a closed warehouse came into view, and he called drawing a bypass from a poor-harvest rumor alone a neighbor of an empty box.

Of Korean origin, he grew up in an auction alley of the Cathedral Accreditation State, and ice crystals stayed on his gloves.

The name Won Juon and the number K376 did not mix with the winning-bid order.

/story_contents/B013/actors/3/sections/현.en:
Won Juon corrected the power-slot order in chalk not at Noryangjin but on the Garak ice-storehouse side.

The surveyor's seat was not inherited; it was held only by the temperature log, the seal date, and the attendance signature.

Even when the Noryangjin Cold-Storage Guild demanded exclusive ownership of the bypass, he did not move the military-ration warrant into the body of the master plate.

He matched only the coordinates, week by week, with Pan Hyodam's warehouse-depot blackboard.

/story_contents/B013/actors/4/arc/0/summ.en: Spreads the three different water-compact contracts and the empty back-gate cell

/story_contents/B013/actors/4/arc/1/summ.en: Matches the HC02 cell circulation and the XT05 aid turn over the archive radio

/story_contents/B013/actors/4/arc/2/summ.en: Pays for selecting the standard contract or rejecting the three sheets with a gap in the turn announcements

/story_contents/B013/actors/4/outcomes/0.en: Selecting the contract that matches the wheel tracks keeps the frame of the joint negotiation

/story_contents/B013/actors/4/outcomes/1.en: Rejecting the three water-compact contracts blocks the envoy's pretext for search

/story_contents/B013/actors/4/sections/3.en:
At the opening hour, Cheon Neulwoo spread again the three different water-compact contracts and the empty back-gate cell.

In the middle, she matched the HC02 cell circulation and the XT05 aid turn over the archive radio.

In the closing chapter, she paid for selecting the standard contract or rejecting the three sheets with a gap in the turn announcements.

The narrative-line identifier was fixed as STORY-B013-K400.

/story_contents/B013/actors/4/sections/가.en:
The Sinjeong Wheel House tried to fold the back-gate survey into the observation duty, citing the circulation of battery cells.

Cheon Neulwoo split the three water-compact contracts and posted them across the council ledger and the archive blackboard, and left the survey line only in Won Choon's dotted-line cell.

Her place in the community was proved not by rank but by copies posted on the archive blackboard and the inspection desk at the same time.

The demand to move the search warrant of the great-power sentence into the map's margin was rejected with the three contracts still overlapping.

/story_contents/B013/actors/4/sections/관.en:
The back-gate survey he handed to Yeong Maon was a contract, and the evening he pinned the coordinates to Won Choon's archive blackboard was a sharing of the same chalk.

Leaving Jeong Yura's standard form as a title on the master plate was a bargain to keep the joint negotiation, and the lottery order he shared with Pan Jisol was a matching of hours, not command.

A record of raising one another on the same gravel, and a record of erasing the arrow for half a day, remained together.

The endpoint of the relations continued into STORY-B013-K400.

/story_contents/B013/actors/4/sections/분.en:
In ending α, Cheon Neulwoo raised into the council archive the one water-compact contract that matched the wheel tracks, and kept the frame of the joint negotiation alive.

In ending β, she rejected all three sheets and cut one envoy's pretext for search.

Neither side deleted the Jeongdong General Labor Union's slot among the sixteen states, and only the branch identifier split as K409-OUT.

The decision on the ground at the time followed the turning-point record as one of two: attendance at the reading of the standard contract, or an audit of the rejection of the three sheets.

/story_contents/B013/actors/4/sections/붕.en:
In the year the envoys' waiting room still used cooling, Cheon Neulwoo bound the Suseo depot and the southern outer bypass onto the public master plate, so that the great-power envoys could not skip the inspection desk.

His ambition was the arrow on the archive blackboard, and for fear that the arrow would turn the joint negotiation into an empty phrase, he left any line he had not surveyed as a dotted line alone.

Even when a seal mark aged by only a day, he walked the map again.

He left Jeong Yura's standard form as a title alone, and did not mix it with the figures in the body.

In the week when envoys of three great powers arrived each carrying a different water-compact contract, the trace of the depot back gate stood empty on the seal ledger and the map at the same time.

Cheon Neulwoo did not fill the blank cell with an envoy's word, and left only the wheel tracks on the gravel in ink.

The core of the fear was a scene in which a forged bypass led to the archive's back gate and the joint negotiation became an empty phrase.

Even after the turnback-line announcement cut out, she did not drop the chalk.

/story_contents/B013/actors/4/sections/비.en:
The secret was the one contract among the three whose figures alone matched the wheel tracks at the back gate.

He tucked that sheet behind the blackboard rail and did not spread it on the envoy seat.

The guilt clung to the hour in which he delayed by half a day the back-gate copy he had agreed to hand to Yeong Maon.

That sheet came out of the archive box only after Jeong Yura confirmed the title of the standard form and Yu Sejin opened the dispatch cell.

/story_contents/B013/actors/4/sections/생.en:
Before the archive blackboard, Cheon Neulwoo weighed whether to raise one of the three water-compact contracts as the standard of the joint negotiation, or to reject all three and leave only the wheel tracks at the back gate.

When the demand for a turn of the aid manifest from the Incheon Trust Theater came in over the dispatch radio, the calculation changed.

Raising one sheet kept the turns running, but the other two envoys gained a pretext for search; rejecting all three left the frame of the joint negotiation as a blank cell, but no single envoy could monopolize the reading of the bypass.

That choice remained as K409-TURN, and reversing it stopped the Suseo turn slot for one shift.

/story_contents/B013/actors/4/sections/정.en:
On the gravel below the blackboard of the Suseo archive, Cheon Neulwoo spread three water-compact contracts so they did not overlap.

As a surveyor of the Suseo outskirts, she unrolled the measuring line first when a closed southern connector came into view, and she treated an envoy who drew a bypass from rumor alone as a guest of the empty archive.

Of Korean origin, she grew up beside a turnback line of the Jeongdong General Labor Union, and chalk dust stayed on her sleeve.

The title Cheon Neulwoo and the identifier K400 were not put in the same box as the lottery beads.

/story_contents/B013/actors/4/sections/현.en:
Cheon Neulwoo corrected only the back-gate arrow, not on the Suseo turnback line but before the archive blackboard.

The surveyor's seat was not inherited; it was held only by the survey line, the title of the standard form, and the attendance log.

Even when the Sinjeong Wheel House demanded exclusive ownership of the outer road, she did not move the search warrant into the body of the master plate.

The copy she was to hand to Yeong Maon and the coordinates on Won Choon's blackboard were matched on the same day.

/story_contents/B013/actors/5/arc/0/summ.en: Confirms the stopped water compact and the firing line under the bridge

/story_contents/B013/actors/5/arc/1/summ.en: Matches the HP01 key split and the XT02 wharf drainage demand over the manhole radio

/story_contents/B013/actors/5/arc/2/summ.en: Pays for publishing the source or reporting the cipher-tag leak with a night-patrol gap

/story_contents/B013/actors/5/outcomes/0.en: Publishing the blast source takes in the firing line and keeps the conduit continuous

/story_contents/B013/actors/5/outcomes/1.en: Reporting the cipher-tag leak changes the leader and draws the line of personal survival

/story_contents/B013/actors/5/sections/3.en:
In act 1, Chae Ongyeol met again the stopped water compact and the firing line under the bridge.

In act 2, she matched the HP01 key split and the XT02 wharf drainage demand over the manhole radio.

In act 3, she paid for publishing the source or reporting the cipher-tag leak with a gap in the night patrol.

The narrative line was STORY-B013-K013.

/story_contents/B013/actors/5/sections/가.en:
The Yeongdeungpo Sluice House tried to put observation of the conduit patrol into the duty cell, citing split custody of the sluice key.

Chae Ongyeol opened the patrol cell only at the hour when Heo Dodam's pump trial run ended, and without gathering the keys into one pocket he left only the hour on Han Jaemok's water-supply blackboard.

His place in the community was proved not by the leader's rank but by the number of times he redeployed to the end of a pump run.

An order for a full closure of one district was read as using water as a weapon, and was rejected on the ground.

/story_contents/B013/actors/5/sections/관.en:
Carrying out Kim Taeun's sluice command on the ground was a command contract, and the night he redeployed the patrol to Heo Dodam's pump trial run was a sharing of the same timetable.

The record of guarding Im Bada's cut-off alley first became a rescue, and sharing the night patrol and manhole access with Myeong Woojae was an alliance that split the command.

A record of pulling one another up in the same wetland, and a record of hiding the firing line for half a day, remained together.

The endpoint of the relations continued into STORY-B013-K013.

/story_contents/B013/actors/5/sections/분.en:
In ending α, Chae Ongyeol uncovered the source of the blast rumor, took in the firing line, and chose continuity of the conduit.

In ending β, she handed the cipher-tag leak up to the command, accepted a change of leader, and chose the line of personal survival.

Neither side erased the Water Compact's slot among the sixteen states, and only the branch identifier split as K013-OUT.

The decision on the ground at the time followed the turning-point record as one of two: an escort to trace the source, or attendance at the leak report.

/story_contents/B013/actors/5/sections/붕.en:
In the days when the sluice opened only for the day shift, Chae Ongyeol bound the Yeongdeungpo conduit and the patrol under the bridge to a single cipher tag of the sluice guard, and meant to become the night frame of the Sluice Charter.

Her ambition was the patrol timetable on the blackboard, and for fear that the timetable would become the pretext by which an outside protection force filled a gap, she refused passage to Kim Taeun without a cipher tag.

The habit of hearing the pipe before the footsteps hardened then.

The underside of the bridge at night was written on the public blackboard, but it was not opened without the cipher.

After Im Hajun went missing and the central water compact stopped, Chae Ongyeol extended the Yeongdeungpo night firing line down under the bridge.

He switched the radio off without being able to write, on the last line of the log, the scene in which one point of the conduit was blown, the filtered water flowed backward, and an outside protection force filled that gap.

Only the smell of iron that rose from the manhole remained.

The firing-line flag was not taken in; it was tied while still wet.

/story_contents/B013/actors/5/sections/비.en:
The secret was a mark left in charcoal on the manhole wall, showing that he had brought the firing line down one hour early.

The guilt clung to the shift in which he had left the radio switched off.

Trying to guard Im Bada's cut-off alley first, he let the source of the blast rumor grow for one more hour.

The charcoal mark was moved into the patrol ledger only after Kim Taeun's cipher tag and Han Jaemok's water-supply blackboard overlapped.

/story_contents/B013/actors/5/sections/생.en:
The moment he chose was whether to uncover the source of the blast rumor and take in the firing line, or to hand the cipher-tag leak up to the command and accept a change of leader.

When the wharf drainage schedule demand from the West Sea Granary Theater came in over the sluice radio, the calculation changed.

Uncovering the source kept the conduit continuous, but the night crew dropped out; handing up the leak let one window monopolize the reading of the patrol.

That choice remained as K013-TURN, and reversing it left Im Bada's cut-off alley empty for one shift.

/story_contents/B013/actors/5/sections/정.en:
Opening the manhole cover of the Yeongdeungpo conduit, Chae Ongyeol listened for whether the sound of the iron hammer rose before the sound of footsteps.

As leader of the conduit patrol, she treated an unauthorized night crossing as intent rather than accident, and when a subordinate's water-supply sheet fell behind she walked the wetland first herself.

Of Korean origin, she grew up in the living zone of the Water Compact, and conduit rust-water had soaked into the inside of her gloves.

The name Chae Ongyeol and the identifier K013 were not used interchangeably with the cipher-tag number.

/story_contents/B013/actors/5/sections/현.en:
Beside the firing-line flag under the bridge, Chae Ongyeol corrected only the patrol hour in chalk.

The leader's seat was not inherited; it was held only by cipher-tag attendance, the pump hour, and the manhole log.

Even when the Yeongdeungpo Sluice House demanded exclusive ownership of the conduit, he did not gather the keys into one pocket.

The hour when Heo Dodam's trial run ended and the redeployment of the patrol met only on the same blackboard.

/story_contents/B013/actors/6/arc/0/summ.en: Opens the two edit gaps in the transmission log of the voice record

/story_contents/B013/actors/6/arc/1/summ.en: Matches the HC01 cooling distribution and the XT05 residual-band lottery in the tool box

/story_contents/B013/actors/6/arc/2/summ.en: Pays for recovering the original or blocking the reserve-power bargain with an overnight-crew gap

/story_contents/B013/actors/6/outcomes/0.en: Recovering the original transmitter restores the gap cells

/story_contents/B013/actors/6/outcomes/1.en: Blocking the sale of the reserve power prevents the proclamation-state brand

/story_contents/B013/actors/6/sections/3.en:
In the first scene, Gwon Mirae opened again the two edit gaps in the transmission log of the voice record.

In the middle, she matched the HC01 cooling distribution and the XT05 residual-band lottery in the tool box.

In the closing chapter, she paid for recovering the original or blocking the reserve-power bargain with a gap in the overnight crew.

The narrative-line ID was fixed as STORY-B013-K216.

/story_contents/B013/actors/6/sections/가.en:
The Yeouido Computing House tried to put sharing of the transmission key into the duty cell, citing the night cooling distribution.

Gwon Mirae did not hand over the key, and opened before Heo Eunchan only the cooling-tower clock and the three reserve-power boxes.

His place in the community was proved not by rank but by the number of times he split the power across three places, and by the fault log that carried bilingual notes.

The demand for exclusive state ownership was rejected before the cooling-tower clock.

/story_contents/B013/actors/6/sections/관.en:
Handing the transmission-tower coordinates to Seo Raon under Choi Jiwoo's command was a contract, and the night Du Bong repaired the transmitter was a sharing of the same tool box.

The record of Bong So treating the overnight crew became a rescue, and the record of delaying Bae Woojin's censorship demand as a technical fault remained as the endpoint of a grudge.

The tower coordinates that Bok Dumo handed over were not fixed before the cross-verification.

The relation ledger connected to STORY-B013-K216 without erasing that endpoint.

/story_contents/B013/actors/6/sections/분.en:
In ending α, Gwon Mirae recovered the original transmitter, filled the gap cells, and kept the frame of the public broadcast network alive.

In ending β, she blocked on the ground the bargain that handed the reserve power to one great power, and cut off the proclamation-state brand.

Neither side deleted the Yeouido Investment Union's slot among the sixteen states, and only the branch identifier split as K220-OUT.

The decision on the ground at the time followed the turning-point record as one of two: an escort for the recovery of the transmitter, or attendance at the blocking of the bargain.

/story_contents/B013/actors/6/sections/붕.en:
In the year the rooftop cooling fans ran all night, Gwon Mirae planted at Sangam, Seoul Station, and Changdong a multiple transmission network that survived even when a great power cut the power, and meant to complete Choi Jiwoo's public broadcast network in the physical plant.

His ambition was the cell numbers divided among three reserve-power boxes, and for fear that those numbers would be sold as the winner's proclamation-state brand, he blocked single-channel solo transmission without the programming council's approval.

The household nickname was left in pencil only on the inside of the tool box.

A gap in the broadcast log was recorded only as a fault, not as an edit.

Two edit gaps were found in the transmission log of the voice record from before Im Hajun went missing.

Gwon Mirae did not fill the gaps with inferred lines, and wrote in the log only the hour of the waveform break.

The core of the fear was a scene in which a single transmission accident branded the construction as the winner's proclamation state.

Even after the cooling fan stopped, he did not pull the lock pin of the original transmitter.

/story_contents/B013/actors/6/sections/비.en:
The secret was a note written in the household language on the inside of the tool box, recording that he had found the gap cell one hour early.

The guilt clung to the lie that called Bae Woojin's censorship a technical fault.

That lie both kept the overnight crew and hid the two edit gaps for one more shift.

The note rose onto the broadcast ledger only after Choi Jiwoo confirmed the programming and Heo Eunchan opened the cooling cell.

/story_contents/B013/actors/6/sections/생.en:
The moment she chose was whether to recover the original transmitter and fill the gap cells, or to block on the ground the bargain that handed the reserve power to one great power.

When the demand for the residual-band lottery from the Incheon Trust Theater came in over the rooftop broadcast, the calculation changed.

Recovering the transmitter kept the frame of the public broadcast network alive, but the overnight crew dropped out; blocking the bargain let one window monopolize the reading of the band.

That choice remained as K220-TURN, and reversing it emptied one box of the Sangam reserve power.

/story_contents/B013/actors/6/sections/정.en:
In the machine room on the third floor of the Sangam transmission tower, Gwon Mirae cursed a broken carrier wave before she cursed a person's words.

As a transmission engineer, she did not fear working through the night, but she felt a break in the signal as an insult to a person, and she said that machines were more honest than people.

She grew up in a multicultural household of Korean birth, and inside the house she gave frequencies nicknames in her mother's language, but the broadcast ledger accepted only standard Korean, and those nicknames did not become marks that took sides.

The display name Gwon Mirae and the number K216 were not used interchangeably with a channel number.

/story_contents/B013/actors/6/sections/현.en:
Gwon Mirae matched only the reserve-power cell numbers, not at the rooftop lottery broadcast but in the tool box on the third floor.

The engineer's seat was not inherited; it was held only by the fault log, the programming approval, and the attendance log.

Even when the Yeouido Computing House demanded exclusive ownership of the transmission key, he did not hand over the key and opened only the joint inspection.

He did not fix the tower coordinates he was to hand to Seo Raon before Choi Jiwoo's cross-verification.

/story_contents/B013/actors/7/arc/0/summ.en: Confirms the iron tag bound to the service contract and the covered names

/story_contents/B013/actors/7/arc/1/summ.en: Matches the HP05 reunion register and the XT01 repatriation reissue over the pole radio

/story_contents/B013/actors/7/arc/2/summ.en: Pays for recovering the register or witnessing the service charter with an evening-ration gap

/story_contents/B013/actors/7/outcomes/0.en: Recovering the family register keeps the frame of the family-by-family vote

/story_contents/B013/actors/7/outcomes/1.en: Witnessing the voluntary-service charter secures the stay in the camp

/story_contents/B013/actors/7/sections/3.en:
In act 1, Sin Boram met again the iron tag bound to the service contract and the covered names.

In act 2, she matched the HP05 reunion register and the XT01 repatriation reissue over the pole radio.

In act 3, she paid for recovering the register or witnessing the service charter with a gap in the evening ration.

The narrative line was STORY-B013-K241.

/story_contents/B013/actors/7/sections/가.en:
The Bukhansan Bogukmun Return Society tried to put observation of the camp register into the duty cell, citing the family-reunion register.

Sin Boram recognized as observation only the evening ration roll call, and did not set the register bundle down from her knees.

Her place in the community was proved not by the representative's rank but by the number of times she read aloud each evening, and by the bilingual margin notes.

The demand to exchange the names in the waiting line for the service register was rejected because the consent cell stood empty.

/story_contents/B013/actors/7/sections/관.en:
Speaking for Baek On's oath in the family meeting was an oath contract, and the night she backed Gang Minseo's citizenship solidarity was a sharing of the same pole.

The record of the transfer priority she asked of Yun Jiyul became a rescue, and So Du's courier and Gam Yong's camp meeting were a working alliance to keep the register by reading it aloud.

An evening of recovering names in the same tent, and an evening of hiding a nickname in the margin for a day, remained together.

The endpoint of the relations continued into STORY-B013-K241.

/story_contents/B013/actors/7/sections/분.en:
In ending α, Sin Boram recovered the family register bound to the iron tag and kept the frame of the family-by-family vote alive.

In ending β, she remained as a signing witness of the voluntary-service charter and kept the children in the camp.

Neither side erased the Sangha Relief State's slot among the sixteen states, and only the branch identifier split as K246-OUT.

The decision on the ground at the time followed the turning-point record as one of two: an escort for the recovery of the register, or attendance as a witness of the charter.

/story_contents/B013/actors/7/sections/붕.en:
In the year the camp stove was lit every day, Sin Boram meant to strike whole families out of the great power's military-household register and to put Baek On's independent citizenship into effect first by a vote taken family by family.

Her ambition was the public register on the tent pole, and for fear that the children would be recorded only as restoration-service numbers and dragged out beyond the corridor, she stopped the ration whenever a name was missing.

The household nickname breathed only in the margin.

The oath wording was read aloud again in the family meeting.

The Amsa patrol posted in the camp an iron tag that bound the Bukhansan Bogukmun families' water right to a service contract.

Sin Boram did not condemn the iron tag as an inferred crime, and copied into the log only the names the iron tag had covered.

The core of the fear was a scene in which the children remained only as restoration-service numbers and were dragged out beyond the corridor.

Even after the stove went out, she did not set the register bundle down from her knees.

/story_contents/B013/actors/7/sections/비.en:
The secret was one sheet of the children's names complete, from before the iron tag covered them, folded under the floor covering of the tent.

The guilt clung to the mouth that, while hiding that one sheet, asked Yun Jiyul for transfer priority.

Baek On's oath sentence was read in the family meeting, but the names under the floor covering had not yet been spoken.

So Du's notice and Gam Yong's camp meeting were not written on the same line as this one sheet.

/story_contents/B013/actors/7/sections/생.en:
The moment she chose was whether to recover the family register bound to the iron tag, or to remain as a signing witness of the voluntary-service charter and keep the children in the camp.

When the demand to reissue the repatriation register from the Imjin River Gate Theater came in over the quarantine-post radio, the calculation changed.

Recovering the register kept the frame of the family-by-family vote alive, but the evening ration crew dropped out; remaining as a witness let one window monopolize the reading of the service.

That choice remained as K246-TURN, and reversing it stopped the camp ration line for one meal.

/story_contents/B013/actors/7/sections/정.en:
In the central tent of the Bukhansan Bogukmun camp, Sin Boram stopped while reading the family register aloud before the evening ration.

As representative of the refugee families, she was kind, but her voice sharpened at an official who altered the register, and she had once torn up a ledger that left out a child's name.

She grew up in a multicultural household of Korean birth, and she wrote the household nickname beside a child's name only in the margin, but the ration roll call read only the Korean legal name, and the nickname did not predict loyalty or fitness for service.

The display name Sin Boram and the identifier K241 were not put in one cell with a military-household register number.

/story_contents/B013/actors/7/sections/현.en:
Sin Boram read only the evening register, not on the Eunpyeong evacuation road but before the central pole of the camp.

The representative's seat was not inherited; it was held only by the log of reading aloud, the personal-consent cell, and the attendance signature.

Even when the Bukhansan Bogukmun Return Society demanded exclusive ownership of the register, she did not use the register as a hostage.

Gang Minseo's citizenship-solidarity text was posted only as a copy of the family meeting.

/story_contents/B013/actors/8/arc/0/summ.en: Looks at the family line carrying service contracts and iron tags, and at the mixed dispatch cell

/story_contents/B013/actors/8/arc/1/summ.en: Matches the HP04 hash seal and the XT05 keeping of the aid manifest over the blackboard radio

/story_contents/B013/actors/8/arc/2/summ.en: Pays for escorting the patient train or splitting the list with a gap in the severity duty

/story_contents/B013/actors/8/outcomes/0.en: Escorting the patient-only train keeps the coordination network continuous

/story_contents/B013/actors/8/outcomes/1.en: Splitting the list that mixed in the military-household register blocks its reduction to troop numbers

/story_contents/B013/actors/8/sections/3.en:
At the opening hour, Yun Jiyul looked again at the family line carrying service contracts and iron tags, and at the mixed dispatch cell.

In the middle, he matched the HP04 hash seal and the XT05 keeping of the aid manifest over the blackboard radio.

In the closing chapter, he paid for escorting the patient train or splitting the list with a gap in the severity duty.

The narrative-line identifier was fixed as STORY-B013-K145.

/story_contents/B013/actors/8/sections/가.en:
The Seoul Station Record-Law House tried to put observation of the transfer ledger into the duty cell, citing the sealing of the source hash.

Yun Jiyul did not open the dispatch blackboard, and had Yeorian seal only the hash of the run-cancellation log.

His place in the community was proved not by rank but by the number of times he left a paired Hanja-and-Hangul gloss, and by the run-cancellation log.

The demand to merge three copies of a will into one authentic text was rejected in the transfer ledger.

/story_contents/B013/actors/8/sections/관.en:
Executing the transfer ledger in Yun Seorin's elevation faction was a command contract, and the night he owed Ryu Eunbi the medicine-allocation ledger was a sharing of the same desk, and a debt.

Leaving Sin Boram's family transfer as a priority record became a rescue, and Seo Nayeon's ice priority, Yeon Jiwoo's bed assignment, and Seol Dahuin's dispatch cancellation were practical work that split on one platform.

/story_contents/B013/actors/8/sections/붕.en:

His ambition was the dispatch blackboard ordered by severity, and for fear that the transfer list would merge with the military-household register, he cancelled a run at once whenever weapons and patients boarded one train.

A Hanja name was posted only alongside its Hangul gloss.

An empty name in the body ledger was not filled by inference.

Refugee families from Bukhansan Bogukmun crowded into the Seoul Station sickbay carrying the Amsa service contract together with the iron tag of the water right.

Yun Jiyul did not condemn the iron tag as an inferred crime, and wrote in the log only the dispatches in which a patient's name and the weapons cell were mixed on one line.

The core of the fear was a scene in which the transfer list merged with the military-household register and the refugees remained only as troop numbers.

Even after the platform announcement cut out, he did not take in the red line.

/story_contents/B013/actors/8/sections/비.en:
The secret was one line of a Hanja name, tucked behind the blackboard rail, through which he had drawn a red line because the Hangul gloss was a day late.

The guilt clung to the hour in which that red line pushed one person onto the next train.

Even after writing down that the presence or absence of a gloss did not decide severity, he drew the line because of an empty Hangul cell.

That one line returned to the transfer ledger only after Yun Seorin's elevation window and Yeorian's seal overlapped.

/story_contents/B013/actors/8/sections/생.en:
The moment he chose was whether to escort a train carrying only patients, or to split the transfer list that had mixed in the military-household register and write it as a separate ledger.

Escorting the train kept the frame of the coordination network alive, but the sickbay duty crew dropped out; splitting the list let one window monopolize the reading of the transfers.

That choice remained as K147-TURN, and reversing it left the Seoul Station severity blackboard empty for one shift.

/story_contents/B013/actors/8/sections/정.en:
Before the dispatch blackboard of the Seoul Station sickbay, Yun Jiyul drew a red line through every row where the Hangul gloss beside a Hanja name stood empty.

As keeper of the medical-transfer records, he was principled, but before a patient he folded procedure, and he took leaving a nameless body in the ledger as his proper duty.

He grew up in a family of the Chinese diaspora, and a Hanja name on an old hospital form rose into the transfer cell only when a Hangul gloss was attached, and the presence or absence of the gloss decided neither severity nor side.

The display name Yun Jiyul and the identifier K145 were not merged with the military-household register cell.

/story_contents/B013/actors/8/sections/현.en:

The medicine-allocation ledger he owed Ryu Eunbi he kept only in the neighboring cell, so it did not overlap the transfer ledger.
