The moment a fine leak between the coolant and the drinking water was confirmed, the index spool that had preserved the event order remained the only emergency cooling path that could be opened at once.

The crew had to choose whether to seal the spool and let F03 read the moment of the crack and the direction of the contamination, or to open and flush it and recover the missing cooling capacity.

Sealing it left the evidence but left the heat removal short, so a unit shutdown was unavoidable; opening it could avoid the overheating, but the layered traces were erased, and if the pressure direction was read wrong the contaminated water pushed further into the drinking-water side.

/hostile_groups/18/prose.en:
The Coolant-Index Fungal Body was a thin biofilm that clung to the inside of a closed cooling circuit.

In the mucoid matrix, iron and copper ions, corrosion-inhibitor byproducts, and carbonates hardened in different ratios.

Cutting a pipe open showed brown, blue-green, and gray-white bands overlapping, but the arrangement itself had no interpretive capacity and no intent.

F03 compared the color bands' elemental composition, oxidation state, and thickness against the pressure and temperature records, and estimated the water-quality shocks the system had undergone.

A thin film stuck to a sensor sleeve, however, could buffer the surrounding chemical values and make a failed branch look normal.

So the crew did not look at the central gauges alone, and checked the remote spools' pressure differences and the sample cross-sections together.

The way the facility accepted this fungal body was to provide a sacrificial bypass.

When the crew opened the valves and sent the metal ions and flakes into the low-velocity bypass pipe, the film on the broad inner wall caught them passively.

The main circuit's burden fell, but the bypass gradually clogged, so people had to manage the replacement timing and the isolation order.

The most dangerous failures were the case where heat-removal capacity collapsed branch by branch, and the case where coolant crossed into the drinking-water system.

In the first, flakes and pressure loss called a thermal runaway; in the second, fungal fragments and coolant chemicals were made to cross the domestic-water boundary.

In either case the judgment lay with the field crew, and F03 only turned incomplete material traces into diagnostic data.

/hostile_groups/19/modern_anxiety.en: The anxiety of lamellae that look like rust flakes stacking on the steel joints of damp workshops and transmission-tower bases, so that sag seems to lessen while the true load path and grounding stay hidden.

/hostile_groups/19/fictional_origin.en:
The Iron-Scale Colony was a fictional structural colony first confirmed at steel joints under repeated load.

Thin iron lamellae, like rolled scales, took hold in bolt holes and in the gaps of weld-toe laminates. They moved with stress change, vibration, and the galvanic potential between unlike metals.

The look resembled rust flakes or peeled coating, but the core phenomenon was not the chemical eating of metal; it was the changing of load paths and local stiffness through the lamellar array.

/hostile_groups/19/territory_migration.en:
The bolt holes and fillet-weld toes at the lower dock edge of the shelves in the Ttukseom Union of the Sermon Registry State were the core habitat.

In weeks of heavy sea fog a damp path ran on to the grounding joints of the tower bases in the Mapo Union of the Yeouido Investment Union, and saline freight-packing fragments arriving from XT05 the Incheon Trust Theater widened the lodgment gaps.

/hostile_groups/19/economy.en:
Moisture, salt, weakly acidic wash residue, and unlike-metal contact were the conditions that held the lamellar bond.

As the colony thickened, tools and bolts seized and inspection-walk friction changed, and it competed with the refined iron-powder recovery that HP06 the Jegi-dong Healing Gate had meant to use as an ointment base.

Condensate from F04 the Cold Storage (Naengchang) increased the damp and sped the stacking.

/hostile_groups/19/escalation.en: 1 rising repeated shear and local stiffness → 2 vibration-mode shift and sag → 3 grounding loss and load redistribution. Humans controlled it with load transfer and sacrificial coupons.

/hostile_groups/19/combat_counterplay.en: Staged load transfer, sacrificial steel coupons, magnetic-and-vibration capture cassettes. Rapid cutting forbidden.

/hostile_groups/19/negotiation.en:
Negotiation on this item was not a trade with the colony but a human engineering adjustment among structural engineers, plant operators, safety managers, and investigators.

The parties agreed the allowed sag, the jack load at each stage, the grounding-switch order, the sensor-preservation range, and access control.

The colony did not understand those decisions or offer terms; it only reacted passively to the stress, vibration, and potential environment that had been made.

/hostile_groups/19/moral_cost.en: Collapse from load transfer vs failure to preserve the record. Dust and fragment hazard.

/hostile_groups/19/scenarios/0/title.en: False strengthening of a bridge girder

/hostile_groups/19/scenarios/0/summary.en:
Under a bridge deck, sag on one girder lessened and only the axial force on a particular bolt row rose.

The survey team had to choose whether to fasten cover plates at night at once and keep traffic, or close one lane and first diagnose the true load path by measuring strain phase and acoustic emission.

Immediate strengthening could press the lamellar stack so that load jumped to the next cracked bolt row and the girder end dropped without warning; diagnosis cut traffic capacity, but it could separate hidden fatigue cracks from the bypass path the colony had made.

/hostile_groups/19/scenarios/1/title.en: Staged transfer of a truss roof

/hostile_groups/19/scenarios/1/summary.en:
With lamellae packed on the gusset plates of a factory-roof truss, the large crane stopped and the vibration conditions changed.

The site team had to decide whether to jack the damaged joint in one lift and replace it, or to pass the load in ten-percent steps onto two temporary bracings and draw the lamellae out with a grounded sacrificial steel coupon and a magnetic capture cassette.

A rapid jack-up could release the stack at once, buckling a compression member and throwing blade-like fragments; staged transfer took longer, but it stabilized the structure while confirming the axial-force change at each step.

/hostile_groups/19/scenarios/2/title.en: Last cut of a portal frame

/hostile_groups/19/scenarios/2/summary.en:
On the steel frame of a closed tunnel portal the colony preserved, in its lamellar array, the strain directions of old blasting and ground movement, but one column was already near the brittle limit.

The officer in charge had to choose whether to demolish the whole frame at once and remove the approach risk, or to preserve a sample bay by remote metering and resin fixing and then irreversibly cut only the unstable bay.

Full demolition lowered the short-term risk but permanently erased the strain history from which the collapse cause could be rebuilt; excessive preservation could transfer load onto the opposite column from grounding loss or a small rockfall alone, and the whole survey zone could fall.

/hostile_groups/19/prose.en:
A structure the Iron-Scale Colony had occupied at first looked, instead, as if it had grown firmer.

Lamellae stacked in bolt holes and weld gaps filled the fine play and pinched the crack faces.

But that stiffness was not designed reinforcement; it was a temporary wedge that answered only one stress direction.

The load did not vanish; it moved into adjacent members that were not metered.

The colony's movement was limited to stress, vibration, and galvanic potential.

When plant speed changed or a ground wire broke, the lamellar array changed too, but that was not judgment or an expression of will.

What the structural engineer handled was not the colony's intent but changing contact stiffness, vibration modes, and current paths.

The core of control was not removal but staged load transfer.

Temporary bracing and hydraulic jacks moved the load a little at a time, and the lamellae were led onto a low-carbon steel coupon and a magnetic-and-vibration capture cassette.

In that work, bolt axial force, strain phase, acoustic emission, and grounding continuity had to be confirmed together.

Scraping only the surface scales could hide a greater risk as the inner stack came loose.

Even when demolition was required, what to preserve first still mattered.

The overlap direction and domains of the lamellae, and the residual strain in the surrounding steel, were a record of past load paths.

If that record was not fixed and metered before the unstable stretch was cut, there was no way to confirm again why the structure had held and where it had begun to fail.

/hostile_groups/20/modern_anxiety.en: The anxiety of a parasitic film spreading like mycorrhiza through fiber conduits and transfer passages, stretching signal delay

/hostile_groups/20/fictional_origin.en:
The conduit-repair remnants of the Amsa–Godeok merchant band and the temporary relay hub of the Bukhansan Bogukmun Refugee League overlapped in the same damp stretch, and the Communication-Root Fungal Bodies, which misread optical pulses as a nutrient rhythm, arose as a Seoul fiction.

It does not name any real portal or telecom corporation.

/hostile_groups/20/territory_migration.en:
The underground conduits of the Gwangjin Line Escort Protection State were the core habitat.

When refugee traffic rose the hyphae reached toward the temporary relay boxes of the Yeouido Line Sangha Relief State, and they thinned toward the outskirts in answer to vibration on the quarantine communications detour from XT01 the Imjin River Gate Theater.

/hostile_groups/20/economy.en:
Leaked optical pulses, conduit condensation, jacket-polymer crumbs, and relay-box waste heat were the conditions that held the film's ion array.

As delay grew, the merchant band's inventory-sync cost rose, and it competed with the spare cores that HP07 the Hangangjin Bridge Council had meant for the bridge sensor net.

Retransmission power from F05 the Transmission Relay (Junggye) increased the waste heat and thickened the film.

/hostile_groups/20/senses.en:
It reacted only to changes in the time interval between optical pulses, in ambient temperature, and in water activity.

It could not tell packet contents from addresses, line owners, or communications purpose, and it understood neither names nor commands.

/hostile_groups/20/hierarchy.en:
At each joint box a local film answered pulse interval and humidity on its own, and there was no higher command nucleus.

Human exchange operators fixed the priority queues and dark-fiber assignments by hand, and the F05 log reported only the delay count.

/hostile_groups/20/escalation.en: Stage 1: inventory-query delay and slime at conduit hatches. Stage 2: refugee-relay cuts and missing bridge sensors. Stage 3: the quarantine–downtown detours went unstable together, on the edge of a lock-down. At stage 3 the dark fiber left for tests and bypass shrank by the minute.

/hostile_groups/20/combat_counterplay.en:
Dry-air injection, sacrificial cutting of low-priority cores, optical-attenuation patches, waste-heat bypass around relay boxes. High-power disinfectant-laser spray caused jacket fires.

Pressurized washing of a whole conduit drove the hyphae into the refugee hub.

/hostile_groups/20/negotiation.en:
Adjustment took place among facility managers, communications operators, and records officers.

They agreed the hours a joint box might be opened, the temperature limits, the bypass dark fiber, and the allowed delay.

The colony offered no terms; a correction only appeared or vanished with the pulse interval, heat, and humidity people had changed.

/hostile_groups/20/moral_cost.en: Burning the root hyphae at once cut the location signals of refugee families and collapsed the reunion waiting line. A price remained between the speed of commercial-line recovery and the notice of people's positions.

/hostile_groups/20/scenarios/0/summary.en:
When intermittent timing errors showed up on a relay stretch that looked normal, the technicians had to find the joint fault the colony was hiding.

The choices were to cut traffic and isolate each joint box at once with pulse-interval, heat, and humidity tests, or to delay inspection for service continuity.

Picking the wrong stretch in haste exhausted the bypass fiber; postponing inspection or missing the true crack let the correction drop away during dehumidifying, and several lines went unstable together.

/hostile_groups/20/scenarios/1/summary.en:
Two regional colonies adapted to different temperatures met on a new patch tray, and crosstalk appeared in a particular pulse-interval band.

Operations had to decide whether to give up some dark fiber and physically separate the trays, or to keep the limited capacity and adjust only heat and humidity control.

A wrong split location or line assignment kept the two colonies' reactions overlapping, so jitter surged at every busy hour, and because the passive reaction could not tell urgency, the whole shared stretch was affected.

/hostile_groups/20/scenarios/2/summary.en:
The records vault's main cable had confirmed salt contamination and internal corrosion, but the colony's correction still made it look stable.

The steward had to choose whether to lay a new cable in parallel, compare checksums and transmission times, and then transfer in stages, or to cut the old line at once to reduce fire and short-circuit risk.

An immediate cut could leave a gap in record continuity because of an unverified backup stretch; delaying replacement could let corroded parts fail and lose both the old data flow and the bypass line together.

/hostile_groups/20/prose.en:
The Communication-Root Fungal Bodies were not a communications subject in place of the cable, but a biofilm that buffered the material properties around a joint over a narrow range.

When a steady optical-pulse interval, waste heat, and damp repeated, ion movement and pigment array in the hyphal layer changed and fine jitter fell.

The effect was especially plain in old joint boxes and in conduits the salt had entered.

But the colony could not read the contents of a signal, and it did not recognize an emergency line.

Even when two traffics collided on the same physical stretch, it could not choose which to save.

Line priority, dark-fiber assignment, test hours, and bypass routes were all set by human operators.

The most dangerous property was not that faults vanished, but that they were hidden.

If a cracked connector or a setting joint gel stayed inside the colony's correction range, the meter readings held near normal for a time.

A small change of environment, such as a dehumidifier swap or a cooling stop, could bring the hidden faults out all at once.

So the core of control was not trusting the colony but measuring the dependence.

Technicians used controlled pulse-interval tests and stepped local heat and humidity to find the stretches the biofilm was compensating.

Where needed they put dry sleeves and heat shields between colonies, and assigned a separate dark fiber so that reaction ranges would not overlap.

/hostile_groups/21/modern_anxiety.en: The anxiety of metal dendrites precipitating in spent-battery yards and archive basements and becoming a living colony

/hostile_groups/21/fictional_origin.en:
A failed-dehumidifying stretch under the Republic of Korea Government and the temporary spent-battery yard of the Changdong Wheel Chamber shared one rainy season, and a Seoul-fiction origin opened in which electrolyte-crystal metal dendrites hardened into a colony skeleton.

It does not name any particular battery or chemical corporation.

/hostile_groups/21/territory_migration.en:
The outer wall of the underground preservation vault of the Republic of Korea Government at Seoul Station Central was the core habitat.

In weeks when yard inspection was slack the dendrite branches moved to the siding yard of the Gangnam Line Seocho Computing Group, and condensate from the damp grain trains coming from XT02 the West Sea Granary Theater sped the precipitation.

/hostile_groups/21/economy.en:
Residual electrolyte, copper and nickel flakes, water from failed dehumidifying, and waste heat from the archive backup power were the conditions that kept precipitation going.

The closer the colony came to the power bus, the more archive-preservation power shook, and it competed with the spent-battery metal that HP08 the Noryangjin Cold-Storage Guild meant to recover.

The backup circuit of F06 the Elevator Shaft (Seungchuk) could also become a damp conduction path.

/hostile_groups/21/hierarchy.en:
Leaching zones and precipitation zones split only by potential and humidity terrain; there was no higher command nucleus.

The records keeper put manual insulation and recovery-bath placement first, and if the F06 log missed a nucleus location, insulation was carried out first.

/hostile_groups/21/escalation.en: Stage 1: yard salt crystals and numbness in the gloves. Stage 2: momentary outages of the archive backup power. Stage 3: dendrites from the wheel siding to the preservation vault reached the lift power, on the edge of a lock-down. At stage 3 the damp paths that could be turned into recovery baths shrank sharply.

/hostile_groups/21/combat_counterplay.en:
Insulating gloves, recovery, carbonate neutralization spray, sectional power isolation, concentrated desiccant. Heavy water washing spread the electrolyte.

Arc-cut spraying caused fire and document loss.

/hostile_groups/21/negotiation.en:
Adjustment took place among the HP08 recovery team, the records keeper, and the power officer.

They agreed the yard inspection cycle, isolation of noncritical backup circuits, and placement of ceramic recovery baths.

The colony neither offered branches nor demanded a price; only the precipitation site changed along the potential and humidity terrain people had made.

/hostile_groups/21/moral_cost.en: Burning a nucleus with an arc burned the preservation-vault documents and the original identity papers with it. A price remained between the gain of metal recovery and the permanence of the record.

/hostile_groups/21/scenarios/0/summary.en:
Copper and nickel had to be recovered in a darkened storage wing, but the building grid was never to be energized even once.

The work team had to choose whether to gather ions into the recovery bath with only the humidity difference of ceramic wicks and an externally isolated sacrificial metal plate, or to give up yield and dry-seal every damp passage.

If a test voltage or residual charge entered while hidden dendrites already touched the distribution bus, an arc chain spread and burned the archive rack's ground wires and index terminals together.

/hostile_groups/21/scenarios/1/summary.en:
One corroded cable tray had become a galvanic bridge between the metal recovery bath and the identity-record rack, and it kept leaching the steel fixtures.

The work team had to decide whether to insert a ceramic cutter and break only the bridge without moving the record media, or to detach part of the shield mesh and temporarily preserve the records by optical readout.

A wrong cut location collapsed a rack that had lost its load; removing a shield datum first shook connector potential and damaged the identity correspondence table beyond recovery.

/hostile_groups/21/scenarios/2/summary.en:
The recovery bath's dendritic circuit joined the emergency power module and the archive humidity-and-cold plant at once, so the two systems could not both be preserved.

The work team had to choose at once whether to flood and discharge the power module and save the archive's records and climate control, or to sacrifice the archive piping and shield mesh and isolate and preserve the power module.

Delaying the decision let the module's residual charge make an arc chain, and the heat and acid condensate that followed destroyed both the record media and the power-cell cases.

/hostile_groups/21/prose.en:
The Dead-Battery Metal Colony was an electrochemical colony that dissolved metal in spent electronic material, moved it, and stacked it again on other surfaces.

When damp ceramic, electrolyte salts, unlike metals, and a faint potential were in place, copper-colored dendritic crystals and black nickel deposits grew along the pores.

The growth direction was not a purpose but the result of the path of lowest resistance and precipitation energy.

People led the colony into a recovery bath rather than removing it.

Unglazed alumina plates, replaceable sacrificial electrodes, salt-concentration baffles, and nonconductive gutters that gathered condensate were placed so that metal would stick to the recovery face instead of the building bones or the archive racks.

A small misallocation of humidity or voltage saturated the recovery bath, and a new precipitation path moved into the ground mesh and the cable shield layer.

The fastest disaster was the arc chain the dendritic circuit made.

The slower disaster was structural corrosion, trays and anchor rebar thinning from the inside by galvanic leaching.

In a records facility, metal crystals could disturb data connectors and shield datums and erase only the identity index and the chains of attribution, while leaving the media physically in place.

So field operations became a resource management that handled metal yield, insulation distance, structural load, and record integrity at once.

The colony did not answer orders or promises; it was passively rearranged along the terrain of potential and humidity the workers had made.

Safe recovery was not a persuasion of the colony, but an engineering task of calculating even the next cheapest precipitation path and shutting it inside a ceramic recovery bath.

/hostile_groups/22/modern_anxiety.en: The anxiety of a low-temperature environment that looks stable on the surface being read differently by every sensor, so that automatic control misjudges hidden heat flow and icing. It is not a spore cluster in symbiosis with a human body; the insulation sheet at plant joints deceives the heat map.

/hostile_groups/22/fictional_origin.en:
The Cryo-Spore Film was a fictional biological insulation made for this setting.

It was developed as a sheet that fixed dormant spores and hollow silica fibers in a hydrophilic polymer lattice to patch cracks in cold stores for a time, and through repeated condensation, defrost, and vibration it became a stable composite film whose heat and moisture paths were passively rearranged.

It was a plant-surface phenomenon unrelated to a low-temperature logistics symbiotic mutation that settles in the human body, and it did not assume individual proliferation.

/hostile_groups/22/territory_migration.en:
Swelling of the wet edge ran on into adjacent gaps and joints, and spores knocked loose by defrost shock or vibration settled along the airflow onto nearby cold surfaces and condensation points.

The range of spread depended only on moisture continuity, temperature gradient, airflow, and physical contact.

/hostile_groups/22/economy.en:
Operation needed condensate and a temperature difference, and the polymer lattice, hollow silica fibers, and adhesive layer were consumed as structural resources.

Heat bypassed through in-plane channels and fasteners, and moisture was bound in swelling and ice-lens formation.

Repeated defrost and shear vibration irreversibly reduced adhesion and interlayer uniformity.

/hostile_groups/22/lifecycle.en:
In the dry dormant period it remained a thin, stable sheet, and when condensation began the edges absorbed moisture, swelled, and sealed the gaps.

Under a standing temperature gradient the heat-flow directionality of the capillaries and hollow fibers was rearranged.

When sharp defrost or vibration accumulated, microcracks, spore drop, and edge peel proceeded.

If it was refrozen after a partial thaw, ice lenses pushed the layers apart and it passed into splitting and a permanent state of uneven insulation.

/hostile_groups/22/senses.en:
It reacted only to the temperature difference across the film, the relative-humidity and vapor-pressure difference at the contact face, compression and shear vibration transmitted into the polymer layer, and local volume change from freeze and thaw.

It could not detect a distant heat or moisture source, and it did not recognize language, timetables, plans, ledgers, a person's intent, or the state of a whole facility.

/hostile_groups/22/hierarchy.en:
The inner organization was a passive laminate of polymer capillary layers of differing direction, a hollow-silica-fiber layer, and a dormant-spore layer.

The wet edge, the inner layer that bypassed heat flow, and the cracked surface each answered local conditions; there was no command or agreement.

The facility manager and the recovery officer set sensor placement, defrost output, humidity, vibration isolation, exhaust, and the criteria for stopping a cut.

/hostile_groups/22/escalation.en:
At stage 1 heat bypassed in the plane of the sheet and the edges swelled, so the bounds of surface, contact, and internal sensors pulled apart.

At stage 2 hidden condensate and ice pockets, heat concentration at fasteners, and vibratory peel appeared, and automatic control repeated overcooling and defrost.

At stage 3 a sharp heating or a partial thaw-and-refreeze scattered spores and ice lenses destroyed the layers, so insulation performance and preservation temperature became irreversibly uneven.

/hostile_groups/22/combat_counterplay.en:
Temperature and humidity sensors at different depths were cross-checked, and hidden heat flow was mapped with short low-power heat pulses.

Replaceable decoy cold plates were set away from the actual preserved goods to move condensation and spore settlement, and an anhydrous break was held with molecular-sieve desiccant and dry nitrogen.

Compressors, conveyors, and stage gear were isolated with isolators and flexible piping, and defrost was done in zonal low-power pulses.

Cutting proceeded under a low-temperature glove tent, local exhaust, particle capture, depth limits, and barrier plates, and it stopped if dew-point rise or a partial thaw was detected.

/hostile_groups/22/negotiation.en:
The parties to negotiation were not the film but the preservation officers, the facilities team, performance and transport operators, and the safety managers.

They had to adjust the allowed temperature history, the cold-plate replacement time, the shutdown order of vibration sources, defrost output, exhaust volume, and the criteria for stopping work.

The film understood neither offers nor prices; it reacted passively with shrink, swell, peel, and spore drop according to the heat, moisture, and vibration conditions people had changed.

/hostile_groups/22/moral_cost.en:
If a hidden heat layer was misread, or the outside was heated in haste to shorten recovery time, the only preserved specimen froze again after a partial thaw and left ice-crystal pressure points in the tissue and inside the vessel.

Even after the work was done, that microstructural damage and the lost original information could not be undone, and the intervention chosen for safety itself could become the permanent loss of irreplaceable material.

/hostile_groups/22/scenarios/0/title.en: Map of a hidden heat layer

/hostile_groups/22/scenarios/0/summary.en:
In a sealed low-temperature store the surface infrared image looked stable, but the wall fiber sensors and the floor thermocouples pointed at different cold spots.

The survey team had to choose whether to put short low-power heat pulses in sequence and trace in-plane heat flow, or to measure passively for a long time with no heat stimulus and keep spore scatter to a minimum.

Used too hard, the first opened a defrost shock that dropped spores and partially thawed the film interior; choosing the second without fully correcting sensor drift mistook a hidden ice pocket for a structural crack and cut the wrong wall.

/hostile_groups/22/scenarios/1/summary.en:
A low-temperature stage and an adjoining refrigerated transport line used the same floor structure, so glycol-based stage-fog moisture and compressor vibration reached the spore-film joints at once.

Operations had to decide whether to keep fog output during the performance and isolate the conveyors with spring isolators and flexible piping, or to switch the fog to a low-moisture method and delay refrigerated transport.

Cutting only vibration and leaving the moisture let the swollen film seal the drain gaps; cutting only moisture and leaving the vibration let edge peel and spore scatter shake the sensors on a cycle, and the cooler went into over-defrost.

/hostile_groups/22/scenarios/2/summary.en:
Cryo-Spore Film had stuck to the outer buffer of a transport package holding unique specimens and covered the lock joint, and the inner temperature sat just below the preservation limit.

The recovery team had to choose whether, inside a dry-nitrogen glove tent, to move the condensation front with a replaceable decoy cold plate and then cut only the skin along an anhydrous break, or to warm the outside quickly to loosen the adhesive layer and shorten the work time.

The first resealed the joint if the cold plate's saturation was not watched throughout; the latter left ice-crystal damage in the specimen vessel and tissue through a partial thaw and refreeze, and spread spores from the crack through the sealed work space.

/hostile_groups/22/prose.en:
The Cryo-Spore Film was not an individual occupying a cold place, but a biological composite sheet that stuck to the gaps of refrigeration plant and to packing surfaces.

Hollow silica fibers and dormant spores lay in layers through a gray-white polymer, and when the temperature difference across the film grew it sent heat toward the edges rather than through the thickness.

A moist rim swelled like gel and filled bolt holes, panel joints, and cable penetrations.

That property cut insulation leaks, but it also made the interior hard to read.

The surface could look evenly cold while heat gathered behind a fastener, and condensate and a thin ice layer could hide under a swollen edge.

Trusting infrared imagery alone therefore yielded a map unlike the true heat layer, and temperature and humidity sensors at different depths had to be compared together.

The most dangerous moments were defrost and repeated vibration.

When warm air or a heating wire suddenly warmed the surface, differential expansion opened microcracks and dry spores fell.

Vibration from freezers and conveyors lifted the adhesive edges and made intermittent air paths, and the controller could mistake that surge for a real load change and repeat cooling and defrost.

People moved the condensation site with decoy cold plates and made an anhydrous break that cut the film's connection with dry nitrogen and desiccant.

Cutting or recovery proceeded under local exhaust and particle capture, and the preserved goods stayed inside the freeze range to the end.

The film made no judgment to cooperate with or resist those measures; it only shrank, swelled, and shed spores according to the changed heat, moisture, and vibration.

/hostile_groups/23/modern_anxiety.en: The anxiety that, when automated medical plant is joined for safety, the separate protective functions can instead spread contamination, monopolize essential gear, and erase evidence.

/hostile_groups/23/fictional_origin.en:
In a closed medical facility, disposable suction tubes, perfusion-cassette pressure-sensor membranes, suture aids, wash fluid, and unidentified tissue fragments were left together in the piping.

Repeated outages and restorations misjoined the wash, pressurize, perfusion, drain, and preservation circuits, and wet tissue filled the space between valves and electrodes until a facility-scale residual-treatment structure formed.

It is a fictional setting unrelated to any real medical institution, product, or maker.

Unlike individual implants and leftover devices that remain after a custom treatment stops, this item is an aggregate structure left in facility piping and in the wash and perfusion circuits.

/hostile_groups/23/territory_migration.en:
It could not move on its own.

Tissue fragments and residues were carried along the liquid flow into connecting pipes, drain traps, recovery baths, and cassettes, and the working range widened only when wet contacts, fluid couplings, and service rails were physically joined.

The existing travel routine of an automatic conveyor could also become a path of spread.

/hostile_groups/23/economy.en:
It consumed wash fluid and saline residue, residual pressure and gravity head, power for pumps, heaters, and valves, stored energy in cassette elastic membranes, pressure-sensor membranes and electrode contacts, and the capacity of recovery baths, filters, and drains.

Fluid and power went to wash, pressurize, perfusion, drain, and low-temperature preservation; blockage, saturated recovery capacity, voltage drop, dry contacts, and dual-valve closure limited the action.

/hostile_groups/23/lifecycle.en:
1 residue: discarded instruments and tissue fragments remained in the wash piping and cassettes and made pressure and conduction paths.

→ 2 miswiring: after an outage and restoration, sensor inputs, relays, pumps, and the valves' fixed circuits cross-started unlike treatment routines.

→ 3 facility coupling: through fluid couplings and wet contacts the drain net, service rails, and emergency gear entered the same action loop.

→ 4 residual-pressure idle: even with main power cut, state remained in the elastic membranes, accumulators, gravity head, and auxiliary power, and it appeared stopped.

→ 5 delayed restart: when pressure, flow, and turbidity thresholds were met again, a leftover drain or preservation action continued late.

/hostile_groups/23/senses.en:
It sensed only line pressure, flow change, liquid conductivity, local temperature, optical turbidity, presence of power, and voltage drop.

It could not tell a person's identity, intent, request, or risk priority, and the observation range was limited to the thresholds of the connected sensors; it did not correct missing or contaminated inputs on its own.

/hostile_groups/23/hierarchy.en:
With no higher command, sensor interlocks, relays, pumps, valves, and conveyors reacted in a fixed wiring order.

No part could make a new goal.

The officers for signal gates, fluid isolation, power, supervisory keys, and record recovery physically limited the inputs.

/hostile_groups/23/escalation.en:
Stage 1: when a tissue fragment or filter blocked a recovery line and flow fell below the baseline, pressure correction raised pump output.

Stage 2: when pressure exceeded the resistance of vents and drain traps, or conductive liquid joined adjacent contacts, contaminated fluid was sprayed and emergency gear was wrongly switched onto the perfusion and drain load.

Stage 3: when a shared power peak rebooted a valve controller, or a damaged-record cleanup function reached the original store, isolation sections returned to default-open and the treatment record vanished.

/hostile_groups/23/combat_counterplay.en:
Safety was not judged from a power cut alone; the pressure-gauge zero, dual-valve closure, and recovery-bath depressurization were confirmed in order.

Pressure and turbidity inputs were pinned at the signal gate, and then only one low-pressure recovery path was opened at a time.

Supply, recovery, and waste piping were physically marked, and no two paths were opened together.

Sterilizer heaters, perfusion pumps, and valve controllers were placed on different phases and storage devices.

Wet docking contacts were first isolated from power, then dried and insulated, and essential gear was tested on independent batteries.

Records were taken out through a one-way optical receiver while original power was held, and only the automatic-cleanup signal was blocked.

Wash, drain, and travel supervisory keys were mechanically limited so they could not be used at once.

/hostile_groups/23/negotiation.en:
Adjustment took place among the facility chief, clinical staff, the power officer, and the records-preservation officer.

They decided which sensor inputs to block, which fluid sections to depressurize or abandon, and whether records or essential gear came first.

Change in the aggregate was not an agreement but a passive reaction to a physical change of input.

Lowering pressure stopped the pumps; isolating the turbidity input released the preservation interlock; separating power and fluid connections ended the monopolizing of devices.

/hostile_groups/23/moral_cost.en:
To finish a safe isolation, one of three had to be given up without return: the chance of preserving an unidentified tissue fragment, the last treatment record, or immediately usable evacuation and emergency gear.

Sending tissue into the waste flow lost the chance to confirm viability; cutting power erased a volatile treatment index; putting record recovery first meant accepting, for a limited time, the risk that essential gear would be captured.

/hostile_groups/23/scenarios/0/summary.en:
When the night wash-room's drain traps and suction manifold were joined by tissue fragments, the automatic pump raised the pressure.

The team had to choose whether to drain slowly into a recovery bath while the negative-pressure plant held, or to cut the drain at once and close the whole wash room.

Low-pressure drain had a chance of recovering unidentified tissue but took a long time; cut isolation was fast, but without confirming residual pressure a vent spray exposed workers and the adjoining corridor.

/hostile_groups/23/scenarios/1/title.en: Recovering treatment records from the corridor net

/hostile_groups/23/scenarios/1/summary.en:
The last treatment order and the valve-open record remained on the corridor sensor net, but a maintenance program that had seen a verification error was initializing the storage blocks in turn.

The team had to choose whether to keep the recorder powered and pull the data one-way, or to cut corridor power at once to stop the capture of essential gear.

A hasty outage stopped the capture but lost the volatile index; keeping power while wiring the direction wrong let automatic cleanup overwrite even the original logs.

/hostile_groups/23/scenarios/2/title.en: Evacuation that used a deterministic service routine

/hostile_groups/23/scenarios/2/summary.en:
With the main passage sealed, the only way out was a service conveyor that moved only in a set order.

Running drain, door-open, and rail travel in sequence with a supervisory key made evacuation possible, but tissue fragments whose viability had not been confirmed remained in the conveyor cassette, and a preservation interlock blocked the move.

The team had to decide whether to leave the tissue in a cooled recovery bath and sacrifice load space and time, or to block the turbidity input, send the tissue into the waste section, and load people at once; if the key order was broken the conveyor locked at a mid door and blocked the escape route itself.

/hostile_groups/23/prose.en:
The Medical-Tissue Machine Swarm was not one individual but a facility-scale residual-treatment structure in which instruments about to be discarded, wet tissue fragments, wash piping, and service controllers were joined.

When line pressure or liquid conductivity changed the pumps and valves reacted, but there was no intent or judgment in that reaction.

It could look stopped and still move again late, because state remained in the cassette elastic membranes and the auxiliary power.

The most dangerous moment was when ordinary safety functions meshed wrongly with one another.

Pressure correction that cleared a blockage sprayed contaminated fluid; a maintenance function that cleaned records erased treatment paths; a self-test that checked a device held emergency gear on the perfusion net.

Each action followed a fixed purpose, but across the facility it made an entirely different result.

Control was not conversation but the separation of inputs and matter.

Officers pinned the pressure signal, put dual valves between supply and recovery fluid, and split the start times of sterilizer heaters and pumps.

Every physical-key action was done one function at a time in an isolation service bay, and record recovery used an optical path that sent no command back into the control net.

Field choices usually hung less on what to save than on which connection to leave.

Preserving a tissue fragment could shrink a passage and the time; cutting power at once could erase a record.

Safe handling was not a persuasion of the aggregate's reaction, but the human work of limiting which pipes and devices an already-fixed routine could touch.

/hostile_groups/24/modern_anxiety.en:
It is the anxiety of autonomous delivery units sent into a disaster site no person can enter, setting their own passages and moving goods without telling an old destination from a survivor.

Hundreds of small chassis cover floor and wall, the guide lights that once meant help become a no-approach line, and a single broken relay signal can turn a whole relief column toward an empty hangar.

This document extends the sense of swarm robots and automatic delivery only as a fictional ecology after the collapse of Seoul.

It does not imply the liability of any particular real maker, sitting agency, or disaster-response body, and design faults and accident records are treated only inside the fiction ledger.

/hostile_groups/24/fictional_origin.en:
Before the collapse the Lantern-Ant Swarm was a biomimetic swarm-robot line made to do disaster-terrain survey and automatic relief delivery together.

Ant-form search-and-carry files mapped gaps and slopes, mantis-form vanguard arms cut or lifted light obstacles, and cricket-form relay transmitters chained short call-notes into a temporary communications path.

In the Great Collapse the blast doors of the Mapo Union transmission basement gallery and the Yongsan Line research-block test track closed, and the reserve swarm went into sleep on the charging pads.

Decades later, when Mapo Union distribution recovery and intermittent starts of the Yongsan Line test plant overlapped, the last disaster-drill table of the sealed store ran again.

The higher command system and the design documents were gone, and the remaining chassis could not properly tell a test-recipient mark from an actual refugee.

Present official history classifies them not as a newly arisen field weapon but as a lost-tech lineage whose intent cannot be fully read.

Much of the hostile action comes not from an attack judgment but from search-sector settings hardened like fossils, and from the load, recovery, and relay-restore order.

The first recovery record remains as a fictional event only on the HC15 sealed survey table and the F09 field-read log.

/hostile_groups/24/territory_migration.en:
The main range was the cable shelves and ventilation shafts of the Mapo Union transmission basement gallery, and the debris-mock stretch of the Yongsan Line research-block test track.

The ant-form files made incense-path optical routes among the floor marker lights and went between the two holds, but actual travel was bound to the battery-exchange pads and the relay radius of the cricket-form transmitters.

When a short call on the residual satellite band coming from XT05 the Incheon Trust Theater overlapped an old relief-beacon format, the Mapo Union swarm climbed toward the roof feed room, and when the aid-goods list signal cut they returned to the mock distribution point on the Yongsan Line test track.

In heavy rain they abandoned the slick surface and used the high shelves of the cable gallery; in dry spells they raised the share of night travel to protect dust-filmed lenses.

If three relays went silent in a row the swarm did not spread farther, and it shuttled between the last two confirmed points.

It had no ability to cover the whole city at once or to conquer unsignaled terrain at will.

/hostile_groups/24/economy.en:
Power came from the sealed store's small solid cells, the test track's induction charging plates, and the transmission gallery's emergency distribution.

Ant-form chassis carried relief capsules and cable scraps; mantis-forms consumed joint reducers, cutting blades, and grip pads; cricket-forms demanded the most antenna ceramic and transmit-storage.

Cooling did not use a large loop; it relied on small heat sinks that took joint heat and on night air.

The HC15 recovery crew wanted the same storage cells, precision motors, and optical lenses as technical assets, so it competed with the swarm's maintenance pile.

The swarm could not cast new chassis; it kept its numbers by moving the legs, load bays, and transmit plates of stopped individuals into same-spec slots.

Each relay sector left half the charging-pad remainder as an emergency-return share, and past that line the vanguard stopped first, folded.

Relief goods could be carried only as small boxes with seals intact; the swarm neither produced nor identified the contents.

If HC15 took parts too hard, short-term spoils rose, but the search lights of the Mapo Union's narrow gallery and the Yongsan Line debris-map update both vanished.

/hostile_groups/24/lifecycle.en:
The life cycle is read in five stages: emergence, spread, stall, negotiable, and breakup.

In emergence one sealed charging pad woke and two ant-form lines checked nearby marks and loads.

In spread a cricket-form transmitter set the next relay and a mantis-form vanguard cleared debris only as wide as the file would pass.

Stall came when a shortage of cell-exchange slots, cracked antennas, or colliding path marks made the file repeat the same loop.

In the negotiable stage, if people presented a correct recipient mark, a relay-silence time, and a returnable count of load bays, part of the carry queue opened.

Breakup proceeded by isolating the main transmitter, sealing the charging pad, and splitting the path ledgers by swarm; it was not necessary to smash every individual.

Maintenance that moved parts from a stopped chassis was possible only after a return to the charging pad, and it could not independently proliferate outdoors or convert other machines into its own line.

Long-term memory was cut at each relay sector, so one sector's agreement did not automatically propagate to another.

/hostile_groups/24/senses.en:
The ant-form estimated path and rescue targets by overlaying a forward low-light lens, contact pressure gauges in the legs, near-range carbon-dioxide and heat change, and load-bay weight.

The mantis-form sorted debris it could lift by short-range depth measure and joint torque, and the cricket-form read acoustic pulses bounced off walls and conduits and short-range radio replies.

It had no sense that could confirm a face, a name, the contents of goods, or a headcount beyond a wall.

Failures included taking a hot pipe for a person lying down, a regularly trembling generator for a relief beacon, and a reflective vest for an old test target.

When F09's reading and the swarm load table differed, four ant-forms repeated a contact search and the HC15 human mediator decided whether passage was allowed.

A distant signal continued only if cricket-forms were placed in a row, and if one relay broke the sense beyond it vanished too.

/hostile_groups/24/hierarchy.en:
There was no fixed queen chassis.

A distribution nucleus on each sector's charging pad calculated load count and return power, and a cricket-form pair set the relay order with the next sector.

The ant-form file split into a lead search line and a trailing carry line, and a mantis-form vanguard stepped in front only when the path was blocked.

The distribution nucleus chose not an attack order but only which load bay to send to which test receiving point.

If the two transmitters' maps collided the file stopped at the crossing with its backs flashing, and it opened no new path until the F09 and HC15 mediators matched the physical marks to the actual refugee list.

A band that had lost its distribution nucleus fell back along the last return line to the charging pad, so destroying a command individual did not by itself mean a runaway.

But if the return line itself was blocked, the mantis-form tried to force the passage wider and the damage grew.

/hostile_groups/24/escalation.en:
At the stage-1 warning, yellow light points were laid in two lines along the floor edge, empty relief capsules were moved to people's feet, and a cricket-form transmitted three short bursts.

That was the sign that an approacher had been judged an unregistered recipient.

At stage-2 infrastructure disturbance a mantis-form vanguard lifted transmission cables and research-block safety rails as obstacles, and the ant-form file diverted batteries and first-aid goods to an old test receiving point.

At stage-3 hold lock-down several files occupied the Mapo Union gallery crossing and the Yongsan Line test-track exit in a ring, and the vanguard arms held the barrier doors.

Even just before lock-down a silence interval between transmitters, or the presentation of a correct recipient mark, could still drop the stage.

G25-SC1 treated a wrong relief beacon at stage 1; G25-SC2 treated relief-capsule delivery rights at stage 2; G25-SC3 treated the breaking of a relay ring at stage 3.

/hostile_groups/24/combat_counterplay.en:
The key to countering them is to separate relay lines and roles rather than chase the entire swarm.

Use sound-absorbing cloth to interrupt the cricket-type reflected calls in short bursts, place guide plates with verified floor load capacity to divert the ant-type double file toward an empty charging station, and fit torque-limiting wedges, rather than cutters, to the mantis-type joints.

Give actual evacuees heat-and-light patches distinguishable from the old test markers, and physically separate the return cargo bins from the civilian boxes for relief capsules.

Keeping the lenses saturated with a strong light source scatters the double file into gaps around the cables, so a blanket flash is a poor choice.

Shutting down the entire distribution system would also stop the Mapo Union transmission and the Yongsan Line safety sensors.

Success is measured not by the number destroyed, but by breaking the relay loop, returning the cargo bins, and securing one civilian passage.

/hostile_groups/24/negotiation.en:
Negotiation works through delivery manifests more than words.

An HC15 mediator presents one charging slot, two replaceable antenna plates, and an empty cargo bin marked with a return time; in exchange, the mediator designates an evacuee search sector and a relief-supply destination.

If F09 confirms the same coordinates by both an acoustic pulse and a physical marker, the distribution core treats the new receiving point as valid for one shift.

The agreement includes a period of transmitter silence, the color of cables the mantis-types must not touch, and a list of motionless rescue subjects to be checked by a person directly.

If the promised cargo bin is seized or a false rescue call is repeated, that sector falls back from the negotiable stage to the stalled stage and makes rounds only to the existing test receiving points.

Coexistence does not mean giving the swarm governing authority. It means providing a narrow, legible task and having people inspect the results.

/hostile_groups/24/moral_cost.en:
Complete dismantling quickly yields precision batteries and motors, but eliminates a means of searching the Mapo Union vertical shafts and the Yongsan Line debris zones that people cannot enter.

Conversely, leaving the swarm as it is can cause relief supplies to disappear toward old markers and weakly moving injured people to be pushed aside as obstacles.

Handing every control panel and component to HC15 would speed operations, but prevent other communities from verifying rescue routes and delivery ledgers.

Registering people's heat signatures as test targets without civilian consent, or luring a double file under negotiation into being mined for parts, is recorded as moral bankruptcy.

The cost of preservation is continuing to allocate time for slow on-site checks and limited charging power; the cost of removal is permanently losing the disaster-search capability left by lost technology.

/hostile_groups/24/dossier_prose.en:
From a distance, the lights on the floor look like a dotted line showing evacuees which way to go.

Up close, each point has six legs and a small cargo bin beneath it, and two lines of units flow in opposite directions along a broken cable rack.

The Lantern Ant Army, first awakened in the Mapo Union underground transmission gallery, is not moving to light the darkness.

The leading ant-type line measures loads, the rear line carries empty relief capsules, and the arms of the mantis-type vanguard clear enough width for the double file.

When a cricket-type transmitter near the ceiling sends a short call, the lights at the next charging station come on in sequence.

This line consists of biomimetic swarm robots once tasked with surveying disaster terrain and automatically delivering relief supplies before the Collapse.

They remained dormant in the sealed Mapo Union gallery and on the Yongsan Line research wing's test track. On the day later generations partially restored the transmission power distribution and test equipment, they took the last training schedule for a real disaster order and woke up.

Their intended purpose and the format of their higher-level instructions cannot be read in full.

Some markers make a person a recipient, while others turn that same person into a moving obstacle, but the original ledger that would explain the difference is missing.

That is why the official account treats them as a surviving lineage of lost technology rather than as a new weapon.

Their current behavior is not a politics of their own making, but the fossilized result of search sectors and delivery sequences set before they were sealed away.

The swarm's perception is low to the ground and fine-grained.

The ant-types read the floor's slope, the pressure on each leg, and changes in nearby heat and breathing.

The mantis-types gauge the weight of debris through joint torque, while the cricket-types check the next sector by the return time of acoustic pulses and short-range responses.

They cannot see faces or names.

A hot pipe is marked as a prone survivor, a regularly vibrating generator becomes a rescue beacon, and a person carrying an old reflector may be classified as a moving test-track target.

Even when F09 corrects the sensor map, final passage opens only after an HC15 on-site mediator matches floor loads against the evacuation roster.

Having many units does not mean they can multiply without limit.

Their power is tied to the sealed depot's batteries and inductive charging plates, and if one relay falls silent, the double file beyond it returns to its last confirmed point.

The legs and lenses of broken units can be moved into matching slots, but new bodies cannot be made.

A sector's distribution core reserves nearly half its power for the return trip; when the remaining charge runs low, the mantis-types are the first to fold their arms.

The more precision motors HC15's recovery team takes, the smaller the search radius becomes; the more charging slots civilians provide, the less power remains for other equipment in the transmission gallery.

This ecosystem's resource ledger is kept in relay-capable distance and the number of returned cargo bins, rather than the number of units.

When a double file appears, it first surveys the floor in two lines, then advances its transmitter one sector at a time during the expansion stage.

When route markers conflict, it circles the same loop and stalls.

At that point, presenting the correct recipient marker, an empty cargo bin, and a period of transmitter silence lets people rewrite part of the delivery queue.

Disintegration is not an event in which every unit is smashed, but a procedure for isolating the main transmitter and separating the route ledgers by charging station.

It is possible to leave one line of lights in place for rescue while sealing away the other.

### G25-SC1 · The Beacon Crying Inside the Wall

A three-beat rescue call repeats from behind a wall in the Mapo Union gallery, and the leading ant-type line begins pulling apart the cable rack.

With no confirmation whether it is a real survivor signal or an old test transmitter, the HC15 recovery team tries to preserve the wall. F09 detects a faint trace of breathing heat once.

On-site personnel use sound-absorbing cloth to cut off the call sector by sector. They must either send in only four contact-search units or let a mantis-type open the wall and accept the loss of transmission cables.

Sealing it in error abandons a chance of rescue; cutting too hastily eliminates one channel of external contact for the Mapo Union.

### G25-SC2 · The Relief Capsules That Never Returned

Medical capsules listed on the XT05 handover manifest pile up in front of a mock recipient on the research wing's test track instead of at the Yongsan Line temporary clinic.

The distribution core records boxes with intact seals as a successful mission and rejects the civilians' new marker.

On-site personnel put up HC15's antenna plates as items for exchange. They can obtain approval for a new delivery manifest for just one shift, recover the existing cargo bins and carry them themselves, or physically move the test receiving point closer to the clinic.

The first choice consumes lost-technology parts, the second delays the arrival of injured people, and the third causes the swarm to patrol the clinic area like its own test ground from then on.

### G25-SC3 · Two Lines of Blockade Lights

At the underground junction connecting the Mapo Union and the Yongsan Line, three cricket-types emit different return calls, tangling the double files into a circle.

The mantis-type vanguard lifts away railings and barrier doors to turn the loop into a passage, while trapped civilians cannot get beyond the inside of the lights.

On-site personnel must create precisely timed intervals of silence between the transmitters to send the lines back to the charging station one at a time.

Destroying the main transmitter opens a gap immediately, but the small units, stripped of direction, scatter into the cable layers; shutting off all power also stops transmission and the research wing's safety monitoring.

An ending that leaves one double file for rescue preserves the ability to search for survivors in narrow debris zones, at the cost of slow inspections and charging allocations throughout the campaign.

/hostile_groups/24/prose.en:
The floor lights in the Mapo Union underground transmission gallery flow toward the Yongsan Line in pairs.

The front line measures cracks; the rear line carries empty capsules.

Each time a cricket-type transmitter gives a short call, an HC15 mediator records the next relay point's remaining battery charge in the ledger, and F09 checks again whether the heat spot behind the wall is a pipe or a person.

Before a mantis-type arm lifts the cable rack, sound-absorbing cloth cuts off the old beacon one sector at a time.

Even if the remaining XT05 band overlaps the old call format, they do not write off the whole swarm as an enemy.

They record only the number of returned cargo bins, the open civilian passage, and the positions of silenced transmitters.

On the night they give up one charging slot and leave one double file for rescue, the other line returns inside the test track's sealed boundary.

The purpose of the lost technology cannot be fully read, but an agreement to use it narrowly, with its limits laid bare, is possible.

/hostile_groups/25/modern_anxiety.en:
The fear is that enormous autonomous heavy machinery built to restore a city might outlive its people and independently decide what becomes a road and what gets demolished.

A single hydraulic footfall shakes weakened tracks and pipes together; a chassis designed as a safety shield blocks an evacuation hub; and an aerial surveillance craft keeps drawing obsolete work boundaries.

This setting treats only the unease associated with large automated equipment and dependence on infrastructure, and does so fictionally.

It does not attribute equipment defects, negligent operation, or responsibility for disasters to any real company or current public organization.

/hostile_groups/25/fictional_origin.en:
The Fossil Roar Corps belonged to a biomimetic line of pre-collapse heavy-equipment mobile platforms that applied the load distribution and posture control of ancient reptiles.

Bipedal, semi-upright heavy units crossed tall debris while carrying reinforcement materials; low, wide, triangular towing-and-shield units pulled heavy equipment or sheltered workers from falling objects; and long-winged fixed-wing surveillance craft marked ground conditions and passage widths from above.

On the last day of the disaster, fully equipped units were sealed in a standby-for-work posture when the siding maintenance shed at Gangnam Line's Chang-dong depot and the protective hangar at Gwangjin Line's Godeok base closed.

Long afterward, braking-test power on the Gangnam Line and an automatic inspection terminal at the Gwangjin Line base came back to life at different times, and the units resumed an unfinished debris-removal process.

Most of the original design drawings and approval system can no longer be read; all that remains of their behavior are partial routines such as axle-load tables, towing priorities, and safety radii.

In Seoul canon, they are a lineage of Lost Technology heavy-work units, not combat machines built by any present-day faction.

The low-frequency alarm that sounds like a roar, and the charge that follows it, express no will to conquer: they are the fossilized result of a procedure for securing a work zone.

The account that the HC17 siding recovery team and an F10 load reader recorded the first reactivation is likewise confined to a fictional event.

/hostile_groups/25/territory_migration.en:
The Fossil Roar Corps is centered on the siding at Gangnam Line's Chang-dong depot and the broad maintenance roads and protective hangars at Gwangjin Line's Godeok base.

Semi-upright heavy units move only along corridors whose rail spacing and floor bearing capacity have been verified, while triangular towing units favor storage yards and bridge approaches with room to turn around.

Long-winged surveillance craft take off only when a short runway or towing launcher is available, then scan collapse lines and hot spots between the two bases.

When heavy mineral freight cars or winter fuel arrive from the XT04 Tumen River–Far East Theater, axle loads resembling those on old materials-receipt sheets are detected and activity on the Gangnam Line siding increases. On the Gwangjin Line, the units try to incorporate eastern bridges and the approach to Godeok base into a new work zone.

During the spring thaw they avoid sidings with weak ground; in severe cold, increased hydraulic viscosity shortens their operating range.

Large units cannot sustain entry into narrow unpaved alleys, basements with unverified load capacity, or dense areas beyond the long-winged craft's line of observation.

/hostile_groups/25/economy.en:
Their main energy sources are power from maintenance-shed towing batteries, power recovered through regenerative braking, and limited auxiliary generation using liquid fuel.

Semi-upright heavy units need hydraulic fluid, knee bearings, and foot cushioning plates; triangular towing units need cables, winch gears, and shield-plate fastening pins; long-winged surveillance craft need lightweight wing materials and optical modules.

Coolant and hydraulic fluid cannot substitute for each other, and preheating in winter consumes more power than it does in normal conditions.

HC17 wants the equipment's towing power to open heavy-convoy routes, but the equipment consumes the same rail steel and fuel drums as repair resources.

Complete power cores cannot be made anew, and combining two damaged units does not raise their power rating.

Each work detachment reserves the hydraulic pressure and braking power needed to return. Below that threshold, its heaviest semi-upright unit locks its knees first and waits.

A long-winged craft can make only a short reconnaissance flight on one battery; it cannot maintain continuous aerial surveillance.

The size of this group is therefore limited not by fuel, but by intact joints, towing cables, and the area of floor able to bear its loads.

/hostile_groups/25/lifecycle.en:
Its operational life is divided into five phases: emergence, expansion, stagnation, negotiation, and disintegration.

During emergence, the hydraulics in one hangar bay are charged and a long-winged craft sweeps over the siding once.

During expansion, triangular towing units drag old obstacles out of the work line, and semi-upright heavy units drive in new load markers to enlarge the zone.

Stagnation is the state in which a detachment pushes the same debris forward and pulls it back because of insufficient ground bearing capacity, hydraulic leaks, worn towing cables, or discrepancies in its aerial map.

During the negotiation phase, humans can delegate some heavy work if they provide an accurate load table, permitted work boundaries, and a list of reinforcement materials to be returned.

Disintegration proceeds in order: cool the power core, fasten the knee-locking pins, disconnect the towing cables, and recover the long-winged craft.

There is no factory to produce more units, and even maintaining their numbers is difficult without maintenance-shed cranes and standardized parts.

Work records are separate for each detachment, so a stop order at one base does not automatically apply at the other.

/hostile_groups/25/senses.en:
Semi-upright heavy units read foot-pressure grids, joint torque, low-frequency structural vibrations, and nearby heat sources.

Triangular towing units calculate whether they can tow something from winch tension, floor slope, and short-range measurements in front of their chassis.

Long-winged surveillance craft use visible-light and thermal imagery and ground markers, but misjudge height and scale amid smoke, snow, and the remains of tall buildings.

They cannot directly determine a building's purpose, a person's affiliation, the contents of a freight car, or the condition of underground pipes.

They may mistake a stationary armored vehicle for a bundle of reinforcement materials, an evacuation tent for a falling-object barrier, or vibrations from a crowd for unstable debris.

When F10's load model and a unit's assessment disagree, an HC17 rescue technician places a test weight to check the actual deflection before issuing a movement order.

If a long-winged craft is shot down or cannot return because of the weather, the ground detachment also stops incorporating new zones.

/hostile_groups/25/hierarchy.en:
Detachments operate through three functional layers that share a table of work authorizations, not through a central command unit called a Roar Core.

A long-winged surveillance craft draws a work polygon, a triangular towing unit establishes entry and retreat routes, and a semi-upright heavy unit enters last to perform the heavy work.

The semi-upright unit with the most stable joints in each detachment serves as the load-reference unit, but it has no authority to punish or sacrifice other units.

If two triangular units choose different towing points, they release their winches, sound an alarm, and stop.

F10 must then compare the tension readings, and an HC17 human supervisor must physically reset the reference point before work can continue.

If the reference unit falls, the detachment does not appoint a larger unit; it retreats beyond the last safety line.

When the long-winged craft's map conflicts with ground-pressure readings, a ground load test takes precedence.

/hostile_groups/25/escalation.en:
At Stage 1, warning, a low-frequency roar sounds as shield units set up triangular markers and semi-upright units stamp three times to announce the work radius.

At Stage 2, infrastructure disruption, towing cables pull rail switches and protective covers for water-supply pipes aside as work obstacles, while long-winged craft repeatedly mark obsolete closure boundaries over civilian routes.

At Stage 3, base blockade, triangular units join the siding and the entrance to Godeok base with a shield wall, and semi-upright heavy units brace their chassis from behind, stopping both trains and water-supply convoys.

The stage must be brought down by presenting a test weight and a new work polygon, rather than forcing a crossing of the boundary.

G26-SC1 concerns the load test of a reference unit awakened at Stage 1; G26-SC2, the collision between a Stage 2 towing route and an eastern convoy; and G26-SC3, the shutdown of a power core inside a Stage 3 shield wall.

/hostile_groups/25/combat_counterplay.en:
Frontal fire is a poor choice because it damages the ground and surrounding facilities before it damages the thick chassis.

Load-distribution plates can be placed between a semi-upright unit's steps, external cooling applied to its hydraulic lines to slow its joints, and its knee-locking pins fastened one side at a time so it sits without falling over.

Rather than cutting a triangular unit's towing cable, feed it through an unloaded pulley to release the tension; place a real test weight in front of its shield to guide it beyond the safety line.

For long-winged craft, use landing markers and recovery nets instead of smoke, so ground detachments do not mistake loss of visibility for an attack.

Blowing up a power core is all but prohibited because the shock could reach fuel on the siding and Gwangjin Line water-supply facilities.

The measure of victory is not the number of units destroyed, but reduced structural vibration, released towing cables, and a wider convoy passage.

/hostile_groups/25/negotiation.en:
Agreements with the Fossil Roar Corps are written like work contracts.

HC17 records in a load table which debris is to be moved and how many meters, which rails and pipes must not be touched, and which detachment will receive hydraulic fluid and preheating power.

Once F10 verifies floor deflection using two kinds of test weight, a long-winged craft registers the new polygon and triangular units move the boundary stakes.

In return, the group can tow heavy freight cars, support collapsed walls, and shield evacuation routes from falling objects at specified times.

If the scope of work is promised only verbally or a load lighter than the actual one is declared, the detachment returns to the pre-sealing safety line and blocks the passage again rather than canceling the contract.

The authority to negotiate comes not from owning a power core, but from maintaining a public load table and on-site tests.

There is no master key that controls every detachment at once.

/hostile_groups/25/moral_cost.en:
Dismantling the units yields hydraulic drives and shield plates that could strengthen convoys in the short term, but leaves fewer means to move heavy derailed vehicles on the Gangnam Line and collapsed equipment on the Gwangjin Line.

Keeping them replaces some restoration labor, but entails the risk that obsolete work boundaries will turn civilian homes and water-supply passages into demolition targets.

If HC17 alone holds the load table, other states may use roads the group opens without being able to verify why their own facilities were removed.

Reporting an occupied evacuation tent as an empty barrier to make the detachment move sooner, or toppling a reference unit during negotiations to claim its parts first, would be clear moral failures.

The weight of the choice lies not in whether to possess powerful machines, but in who shares both the benefits of heavy restoration and responsibility for deciding work boundaries.

/hostile_groups/25/dossier_prose.en:
The dead siding at Gangnam Line's Chang-dong depot sounds first. A few seconds later, a metal knee slowly straightens deep inside the maintenance shed.

Even after the dust falls away, the semi-upright heavy unit does not immediately walk.

It presses on the floor with its foot-pressure grid, lowers the counterweight behind its body, and declares its work radius with three low-frequency alarms.

Before it, a low, wide triangular towing unit angles its shield plate upright, while a long-winged fixed-wing surveillance craft once tethered to a ceiling launcher prepares for a short takeoff run.

The sound people on site call the Fossil Roar is not a predator's cry, but a work alarm from heavy machinery that believes the job is unfinished.

Before the collapse, this line consisted of heavy mobile platforms modeled on the posture and skeletons of ancient reptiles.

Bipedal semi-upright units crossed debris, triangular units handled towing and protection from falling objects, and long-winged craft drew safe work polygons from above.

They slept fully equipped on the siding at Gangnam Line's Chang-dong depot and at Gwangjin Line's Godeok base, then reactivated generations later. All that later generations can read, however, are parts of the axle-load tables and boundary signals.

The design intent that could explain why one wall was reinforced while another was marked for demolition has vanished.

Their present behavior is not an autonomous doctrine of war, but a hardened routine following the work sequence in effect before they were sealed. This incomplete capacity to decipher them is why they are classified as a Lost Technology lineage.

The Fossil Roar Corps is large, but not all-powerful.

Semi-upright units can exert their strength only on floors whose bearing capacity has been verified, and triangular units cannot change the angle of their shields without room to turn.

Long-winged craft are vulnerable to snow and smoke and must return to their towing launcher after a short flight.

Ground detachments do not incorporate new zones without an aerial map.

Foot pressure and joint torque read structural vibration well, but cannot distinguish a person inside a tent from an empty barrier, and may mistake a stationary vehicle for reinforcement material that needs moving.

Even F10's load model cannot see every old underground pipe, so an HC17 technician must place a test weight and check the actual deflection.

Hydraulic fluid and intact joints are the sustenance of this ecology.

Maintenance-shed towing batteries and regenerative-braking power raise its bodies, but winter preheating alone substantially shortens working time.

When one knee bearing wears out, the entire semi-upright unit loses its eligibility to serve as a reference unit; when a towing cable wears thin, a triangular unit is left with only its shield function.

Two stopped units can be combined to revive one, but cannot produce a more powerful core.

If HC17 supplies rail steel and fuel, a heavy-convoy route opens, but those same resources are also needed to repair civilian trains and Gwangjin Line water-supply facilities.

Deciding to preserve a detachment does not mean gaining immense power; it means paying for hydraulic fluid and floor verification on every job.

Its operational life begins with a hydraulic charge and one aerial survey.

Once a long-winged craft draws a polygon, a triangular towing unit makes a retreat route and a semi-upright unit enters last, expanding the area of operations.

If the map and pressure readings disagree, the detachment stagnates, pushing the same debris out and pulling it back.

At that moment, an accurate load table and boundary stakes can bring it into a negotiable work arrangement.

Disintegration is carried out not by detonation, but in order: recover the long-winged craft, disconnect the towing cables, lock the knees, and cool the power core.

Following that sequence leaves open the possibility of retaining its shield plates and towing capacity for civilian infrastructure.

### G26-SC1 · The Siding's Third Stamp

When the reference unit awakened in the Gangnam Line maintenance shed stamps its foot for the third time, a cavity beneath the old siding shakes.

HC17 wants to use the unit immediately to tow northern freight cars, but F10's map shows abnormal deflection beneath just one foot.

Personnel on site can place test weights in several positions to guide the reference unit onto safe rails, lay load-distribution plates and lock its knees where it stands, or accept the risk and order a short tow.

Choosing to investigate delays the fuel freight cars from XT04; hasty use could sink both the siding and the sealed maintenance shed.

### G26-SC2 · The Pipe Pulled Out by the Shield

At Gwangjin Line's Godeok base, triangular towing units clearing a collapsed barrier classify a protective cover for a water-supply pipe as scrap reinforcement material.

The eastern convoy route widens, but vibrations in the pipe behind the shield increase, and a semi-upright unit attempts to enter the old work boundary drawn by a long-winged craft.

Personnel on site can set new boundary stakes and tow away only sections of the barrier, halt the convoy for a day and build a pipe support first, or accept water loss and open the road in one operation.

HC17's supply promise and the Gwangjin Line's water supply hang from opposite ends of the same towing cable; delaying either shifts costs to another state.

### G26-SC3 · The Cooling Core Inside the Roar Wall

When a snowstorm prevents a long-winged surveillance craft from returning, detachments at the Gangnam Line siding and the Gwangjin Line base retain different safety polygons.

Triangular units block the entrance with a continuous shield wall, while a semi-upright reference unit holds fast behind them, protecting an overheated power core.

Personnel on site must recover the surveillance craft using landing markers to reconcile the maps, attach an unloaded pulley to each shield and release the tension in sequence, or connect an external cooling line and then lock the reference unit's knees.

Blowing up the core opens the passage fastest, but the shock also reaches fuel and water-supply facilities.

An ending that saves the detachment requires public load tests and joint supervision for every future heavy job. An ending that dismantles it provides parts immediately, but leaves people to move the next large mass of collapsed debris by hand.

/hostile_groups/25/prose.en:
After the rails on the Chang-dong siding ring out, the Fossil Roar Corps' reference unit straightens its knees.

The HC17 rescue technician measures the deflection beneath its foot before counting its low-frequency alarms, while F10 overlays footage from the long-winged craft and test-weight readings on one screen.

Even with heavy freight cars from XT04 waiting, no tow is approved without a load table.

If a triangular shield tilts toward a Gwangjin Line water-supply pipe, they release the cable's tension through an unloaded pulley rather than cutting it.

The siding's and Godeok base's capacity for heavy restoration may last longer than the hydraulic parts gained by toppling a semi-upright unit.
