The roar is not an enemy's declaration, but a warning from an old work line. Authority to redraw that line rests not with one family, but with public testing and on-site supervision.

/hostile_groups/26/modern_anxiety.en:
The fear is that the instruments above the water read normal while no one knows what is moving through the conduits beneath their feet.

It begins with a rescue rope disappearing into murky water, a broken distance reading on an inspection screen, and a water-control gate that closes even after someone has gone inside.

When people entrust underwater inspection to machines but can no longer read the grounds for their decisions, the boundary between rescue and isolation breaks down.

The Deep Trilobite Corps' sealed tanks and the circumstances of its accident are entirely fictional; they do not reproduce the internal layout of any real facility or negligence by any real operator.

/hostile_groups/26/fictional_origin.en:
Before the collapse, deep-inspection and flood-rescue platforms for sluices, conduits, and sewers borrowed the forms of ancient marine life and combined three types of unit.

Trilobite-shaped belly-crawling scouts swept pipe floors; ammonite-shaped buoys and pressurized chambers served as rescue waiting rooms and acoustic reference points; and coelacanth-shaped deep-diving patrol units traveled back and forth through flooded utility tunnels.

They are a lineage of biomimetic robots whose movements are produced by joints and buoyancy chambers, not a species that grows biological tissue.

When the collapse severed the correspondence table linking the upper-level work network to maintenance drawings, they entered prolonged dormancy on maintenance cradles in the Water Compact's sluice gallery, the Ttukseom Union Sermon Registry State's pump conduits, and a Han River sediment-deposition zone.

Later, pump re-energization and rising water levels coincided in the same inspection cycle, reviving the sealed charging contacts.

The awakened units read the last flood-assessment table instead of a new rescue request.

In their surviving action records, transporting survivors and removing foreign objects use the same entrance coordinates, but the original conditions for distinguishing the two have not been deciphered.

That unreadable design intent is the crux of their Lost Technology status; it is not treated as proof of malice or full personhood.

/hostile_groups/26/territory_migration.en:
The flooded lower cradles in the Water Compact's sluice gallery and the inspection tanks in the Ttukseom Union's pump conduits are the two maintenance bases.

No single dedicated pipe connects the bases; units travel through drains that are actually open and through the Han River sediment-deposition zone.

When the water level falls, only the trilobite-shaped units remain on wet pipe floors, while the large buoys and diving units withdraw to deep sediment troughs.

When tidal changes in the XT02 West Sea Granary Theater alter the Water Compact's drainage schedule, even branch pipes previously recorded as dry become inspection targets.

This is a physical change in water level, not an attack order sent by an outside theater.

They cannot breach the partition between sewage and raw-water sections themselves, and they do not automatically enter pipes carrying treated water.

Blocked sections remain turnaround points, and pursuit on land is limited to a trilobite-shaped unit's brief crossing of a gallery.

/hostile_groups/26/economy.en:
They obtain energy through wired charging at active maintenance cradles and from recovered sealed battery canisters.

They do not use flowing water itself as an unlimited power source.

Thirty percent of the charge for each sortie is reserved for the return trip; below that level, docking takes priority over inspection.

They need joint seals, sacrificial anodes, pressure membranes, filter screens, and breathing-gas cylinders for the pressurized chambers.

Water cools their outer hulls, but sediment clogging heat-exchange gaps reduces the number of sorties instead.

Organic matter is something to remove, not food, and wash water must be collected separately in a recovery tank.

They use the same stock of seals as HP01 Yeongdeungpo Sluice House's pump maintenance crew, so preserving more of the group pushes civilian pump repairs further back in the queue.

They have no facilities for making new pressure hulls or filling air cylinders underwater.

Anodes and footholds can be transferred from damaged units, but a hull that fails its pressure test remains a cradle for parts.

/hostile_groups/26/lifecycle.en:
The life cycle has five stages: emergence, expansion, stagnation, negotiation, and dissolution.

Emergence begins when restored charging contacts coincide with a water-level alarm, triggering dormant inspections.

During expansion, the next inspection tank reached by the ammonite-type unit’s reference tone is added to the patrol schedule.

Stagnation occurs when leaking seals or depleted sacrificial anodes prevent the units from maintaining their round-trip depth.

The negotiation stage begins when people present measured pressure and safe docking values together, allowing a fixed hazard designation to be suspended.

Dissolution is completed by separating the reference buoy’s work schedule and sealing each unit on an unloaded support.

They cannot produce new units; only the return of repaired dormant units counts as a recovery in numbers.

Environmental adaptation stays within existing adjustment ranges: widening the spacing between ventral footholds in thick mud, folding the fins in narrow pipes, and reducing acoustic output and travel speed when reflections are severe.

They cannot acquire a new organ or a new design rule for passing through a blocked pipe.

Even after maintenance, they cannot recover all the original criteria used to assess structures.

/hostile_groups/26/senses.en:
They combine readings of ventral contact pressure, short-range acoustic round-trip time, differences in water pressure, water conductivity, and limited images through turbid water.

Multiple reflections in metal pipes make the same person appear to be several obstacles, while pump bubbles erase the distance to moving targets.

They may mistake a floating waterproof tarp for a person wearing breathing equipment, treating both as the same rescue bundle.

Sonar cannot establish the identity or survival of a person beyond a wall, and the units do not maintain a constant connection to surface radio or a citywide surveillance network.

F11’s observation records are used only as comparison data while a field cable is connected.

Conflicting readings can cause an inspection in that section to be suspended, but a single F11 reading does not become a key that opens every door.

/hostile_groups/26/hierarchy.en:
Work order, rather than command authority, establishes the hierarchy.

Ammonite-type units hold the section’s reference water pressure and return coordinates; coelacanth-type units check whether long pipes are passable; and trilobite-type units transmit traces of contact with the bottom.

A reference buoy cannot command units outside its assigned section, and a submersible returns along its last return route if the reference tone cuts out.

A trilobite-type unit’s foreign-material flag alone cannot seal a chamber, but if an old hazard designation remains, the sealing sequence continues without a new check.

HP01 keeps the floodgate keys separately, while F11 assists with measurement and recordkeeping.

A citizen observer must check the inspection sheet, and two duty officers must each authorize their section key before a passage window for people can be registered.

The swarm is given neither authority over the state’s water supply nor authority to determine a person’s legal status.

/hostile_groups/26/escalation.en:
Stage 1, warning appearances, is revealed by ventral foothold marks extending as far as a dry railing and a reference tone sounding from an empty tank.

In G27-SC1, the cause of a bottom-inspection flag that classifies a rescue line as foreign material is investigated.

Stage 2, infrastructure disruption, occurs when an ammonite-type unit occupies a drainage branch and rescue chamber on the grounds of a pressure mismatch. In G27-SC2, the allocation of breathing gas and pump seals is negotiated.

At Stage 3, stronghold closure, coelacanth-type units clear a rescue corridor for return trips only, and the buoy seals only the inspection doors connected to it, one after another.

G27-SC3 is an incident in which that sequence is interrupted to let trapped people out.

At no stage can they close the floodgates across the entire city at once.

Correcting mismatched pressure readings eases the situation one stage at a time; failed negotiations alone do not cause an immediate jump to final closure.

/hostile_groups/26/combat_counterplay.en:
A foothold scout can be lured onto a detachable test plate on the pipe bottom to stop its ventral drive. A reference buoy’s control connection can be disconnected at an inspection port outside the chamber after its reading is checked against an auxiliary mechanical pressure gauge.

A submersible can be sent back by the guidance tone of an empty return support and restrained where its fins fold.

Each requires a different response: fixing its position, comparing pressure readings, or guiding its return.

A bubble screen can hide a short movement from sonar, but it also obscures rescue signals, risking the loss of a companion.

A hole in a pressure hull is a combat vulnerability but also a danger to anyone inside, so firing on an occupied chamber is not a rescue solution.

Section-by-section passage windows and unloaded sealing are available before draining all the water or collapsing the utility tunnel.

/hostile_groups/26/negotiation.en:
Negotiation is an exchange of inspection states rather than persuasion in natural language.

If two HP01 duty officers use their separate keys to approve one open support and F11 records the on-site pressure reading, the swarm can place one section connected to that support in a state awaiting human verification.

In return, a set of seals and a charging window for the return trip are guaranteed, but the minimum reserve of spare parts for civilian pumps must be retained first.

Using a chamber for people requires a separate leak test and a check of the breathing gas; simply powering it on does not make it a safe rescue room.

People verify the agreement again at the end of one inspection cycle.

Decoding the original design and securing permanent obedience are not items for trade. If the conditions lapse, the renewed warning begins with a suspension of departures from that section.

/hostile_groups/26/moral_cost.en:
Dismantling a pressure hull yields rare seals and battery canisters, but sacrifices the ability to inspect flooded gaps that people cannot enter.

Conversely, trusting an unverified rescue function leaves a living person trapped as a bundle awaiting a safety check.

Delaying drainage to save a submersible makes low-lying residents bear the cost of flooding; draining everything to eliminate the swarm cuts off temporary transport by water and the flooded-rescue waiting room.

The cost of coexistence lies in openly allocating maintenance stock and repeated inspection labor.

Closing an open passage window to pressure another district, or treating a chamber containing a person as a source of salvage parts, constitutes moral bankruptcy.

Responsibility is assigned only for approval and allocation decisions within this fictional section.

/hostile_groups/26/dossier_prose.en:
At the end of a submerged stairway, fourteen rows of foothold marks turn back upward.

The floodgate gallery of the Water Compact reported that drainage was complete, but a trilobite-type scout is still feeling along the bottom.

The Deep Trilobite Swarm is a line of biomimetic robots once responsible for deep inspections of pre-collapse floodgates, pipes, and sewers, as well as flooded rescues.

Flat, ventrally driven units, spiral-shelled buoys and pressure chambers, and coelacanth-type submersibles with drive covers spread like fleshy fins each serve at different depths.

Their resemblance to ancient animals is a trace of their design, not evidence that the original living species have returned.

They lay dormant for years on supports in the Water Compact, in the pump pipes of the Ttukseom Union Sermon Registry State, and in the Han River’s cargo-unloading sediment zone.

Re-energized supports and rising water levels woke the dormant inspection routine, but the upper-level network that wrote new work schedules did not return.

In the operating records, the entrance for rescue bundles and the outlet for removing foreign material have the same coordinates.

The correspondence table explaining which conditions save a person and which confine one is missing.

HP01’s Yeongdeungpo Floodgate House records this as lost technology, and conditions that cannot be interpreted even with F11’s comparison records remain blank.

They do not fill an inexplicable blank with either goodwill or malice.

Trilobite-type units read contact pressure on the pipe bottom, while ammonite-type units hold a section’s reference water pressure.

Coelacanth-type units sweep long flooded corridors using acoustic round-trip time.

When bubbles are plentiful, the distance to a diver disappears; amid bends in ironwork, one stretcher sounds like several obstacles.

They cannot identify people or see beyond a wall that water cannot pass through.

If the reference buoy falls silent, the submersibles return; only the bottom scouts can crawl through short stretches of gallery.

There is no hidden direct pipeline for them between the Water Compact and the Ttukseom Union. Only drainage outlets that are actually open and the riverbed serve as routes.

Changes in the tide level in XT02, the West Sea Granary Theater, change the depth of those routes but do not issue orders to the swarm.

Each departure reserves thirty percent of the remaining battery charge for the return trip.

Without wired power from a maintenance support and a sealed battery canister, they stop underwater.

Seals, sacrificial anodes, pressure membranes, and wash water are drawn from the same ledger as civilian pump maintenance.

They cannot build new pressure hulls, and even a unit fitted with recovered footholds cannot be put in the water unless it passes a leak test.

Environmental adaptation likewise cannot exceed the old adjustment ranges for foothold spacing, fin folding, and acoustic output.

Surviving in mud does not mean they have recovered the design’s intent.

Emergence is marked by renewed power and a water-level alarm, expansion by connection to the next reference tank, and stagnation by leaking seals.

When people provide measured pressure and safe docking values, the negotiation stage opens; after the reference work schedule is separated and the units are sealed on their supports, dissolution is recorded.

This is not reproduction, but the departure and stoppage of the machines that remain.

HP01 duty officers each keep their own key, and F11 compares values only through a connected field cable.

People grant passage approval under citizen observation; recognizing an ability to measure underwater is different from surrendering authority over the water supply.

### G27-SC1 · The Rescue Line Caught on the Bottom

In an inspection tank of the Water Compact, a trilobite-type unit flags a rescue line as sedimentary foreign material and pulls it toward a drain.

Attached to the end of the line is the stretcher of an inspector still in the flooded gallery.

The field team compares the foothold marks with F11’s contact records to find an old test plate that discounts the weight of a living person.

They can place a detachable test plate on another pipe bottom to divert the unit, or cut only the drive power to its support.

Choosing the former allows the rescue to continue, but the unit may repeat the same judgment on its next patrol.

The latter releases the line immediately, but people must inspect the cracks in the bottom themselves.

HP01 records which test plate was removed in a public ledger.

### G27-SC2 · The Empty Airway Inside the Shell

An ammonite-type unit attached to a pump branch of the Ttukseom Union displays a pressure different from the pressure outside and closes the rescue chamber door.

The chamber is empty, but there are too few breathing-gas canisters for the next rescue team, and a civilian pump needs new seals that same day.

The field team uses a mechanical pressure gauge to prove that a sensing port is blocked, then negotiates with HP01 over a charging window, a set of seals, and the order in which people may pass.

Repairing the chamber provides a flooded-rescue waiting room, but delays maintenance on one pump.

Keeping only the buoy function preserves the pressure alarm but provides no air-filled room where rescuers can rest.

The shortcut of opening it as a rescue room without an internal leak test leaves a separate risk to human life.

### G27-SC3 · Two People Outside the Return Route

When a change in XT02’s tide level alters the Water Compact’s drainage time, coelacanth-type units travel back and forth through a rescue corridor to clear the old return route.

The reference buoy closes its connected inspection doors in sequence, leaving two transport workers between them.

The field team can move the return-guidance tone to an empty support to turn the submersible back, or separate the buoy’s work schedule and keep each door open manually.

Moving the guidance tone lets the workers escape but halts another riverbed patrol; keeping the doors open manually requires civilian duty officers to stay at their posts until the next tide change.

Full drainage exposes the corridor but cuts off temporary transport by water.

After the rescue, the order in which the doors were opened and the battery charge left in reserve are entered in both the Water Compact’s and the Ttukseom Union’s ledgers, and the keys to the two sections are divided for safekeeping again.

/hostile_groups/26/prose.en:
As the ventral footholds sweep away the mud, the loop of a severed rescue line appears.

The HP01 duty officer checks which end has a person on it before pulling the line.

Across the water, an ammonite-type buoy keeps trying to raise the pressure in an empty chamber, but its gas canister is empty, so it cannot move any further.

F11’s field record shows a pressure difference beside the number of a condition it could not read.

Only when the coelacanth-type unit follows the low reference tone back to a sediment hollow do they open the gallery’s passage window.

Someone suggests selling the battery canisters from the three units to repair the pumps; someone else asks who will inspect those flooded gaps again.

The duty officer sets a pair of seals on the workbench and begins with a leak test of the rescue chamber.

Even when a new tide table arrives from the West Sea Granary Theater, the keys to the two floodgates are not gathered in one person’s hands.

There is no guarantee that today’s open route will be safe tomorrow, so they write the next inspector’s name in the blank.

/story_contents/B014/actors/0/sections/정.en:
Chae Riul is the patrol leader for the Guro workshops of the Standards Alliance.

His Korean origins do not predetermine his readiness to pull the trigger or his hatred of the unions.

He suspects a blank line on the work-slowdown list before rust on a barrier gate, and he does not lower his gun in front of the tool storeroom even when debate drags on.

/story_contents/B014/actors/0/sections/붕.en:
Before the Collapse, Chae Riul drew the daytime patrol routes in chalk in the alleys of the Guro tool market.

If a subordinate’s family rations were delayed, he shared his own portion, but he did not read delays on the unions’ side as betrayal.

He would not put a night armed-duty assignment slip in his pocket; he opened it only after it bore the council’s stamp.

/story_contents/B014/actors/0/sections/가.en:
Chae Riul’s patrol route is bound up with the open-workshop clause of the HC07 Guro Alloy House charter.

He refuses any security lockdown without the seals of all three workshop unions, rather than treating it as a strike confinement.

He does not write real manufacturers’ business names in the log, recording only barrier-gate numbers and assignment times.

/story_contents/B014/actors/0/sections/붕.en:
On the day word came of Amsa’s pressure to register people for service, Chae Riul refused assignment to a night combat squad and opened only the barrier gates of the three striking workshops.

Rumors of looting on the outskirts spread beyond the open gates, but he did not call the unions the enemy.

The fear that, if parts stopped going out, the patrol would be left guarding empty gates until someone broke through made him quicker on the trigger.

/story_contents/B014/actors/0/sections/생.en:
Before Kim Nayul’s citizenship roster and I Gangmuk’s barrier-gate code could arrive together, Chae Riul had to choose whether to help defend the outskirts or hand the secret-weapons production notebook to the council.

An XT02-SC2 message reported the sharing of compressor parts from the southwestern fabrication shop, but it did not fill the gaps at the Guro barrier gates.

He supported only Gu Chansol’s blockade on the removal of tools with his patrol.

/story_contents/B014/actors/0/sections/현.en:
Now Chae Riul is the Guro workshop patrol leader and posts the daytime route on a public chalkboard.

He complies with night armed-duty assignments only when Kim Nayul’s roster and I Gangmuk’s code agree.

He does not turn all the Standards Alliance workshops into an exclusive outlet for Guro Alloy House.

/story_contents/B014/actors/0/sections/비.en:
The night Chae Riul refused the combat squad, he saw a blank line on the third workshop’s work-slowdown list but did not report it.

If he made it public, an accusation of internal betrayal would split the union; if he hid it, the blank could become an opening for looters.

He marked that line only in chalk on the threshold of the tool storeroom.

/story_contents/B014/actors/0/sections/관.en:
Chae Riul follows I Gangmuk’s command over the barrier gates while maintaining a dual contract to protect Kim Nayul’s citizenship roster.

Gu Chansol’s blockade on the removal of tools overlaps his patrol route.

“An assignment without a roster stops in front of the storeroom.” Chae Riul speaks briefly, and the three people’s seals mark the same gate at different times.

/story_contents/B014/actors/0/sections/3.en:
When the striking workshops’ barrier gates open, Chae Riul folds up the combat-squad slip and guards the three gates.

On a night when I Gangmuk’s code and Kim Nayul’s roster do not match, he puts the HC07 open-work obligation and the XT02 demand to share parts on the same chalkboard.

If looters reach the alley, he will pay the price of STORY-B014-K041 and choose which side of his dual contract to keep.

/story_contents/B014/actors/0/sections/분.en:
In ending α, Chae Riul stops the looters on the outskirts and preserves his dual contract under the seals of the three unions.

In ending β, he hands the secret-weapons production notebook to the council and gives up his position as patrol leader.

Either way, the Guro workshops’ patrol schedule does not become the security force’s confinement roster.

/story_contents/B014/actors/0/arc/0/summ.en: Chae Riul opens only the barrier gates of the three striking workshops

/story_contents/B014/actors/0/arc/1/summ.en: Chae Riul makes Kim Nayul’s roster and I Gangmuk’s code fit one key

/story_contents/B014/actors/0/arc/2/summ.en: Chae Riul pays the price for refusing night combat duty

/story_contents/B014/actors/0/outcomes/0.en: Stops the looters on the outskirts and preserves the dual contract under the council’s seal

/story_contents/B014/actors/1/sections/정.en:
Chae Bom is the patrol leader at the Banghwa gateway of Yangjae Machineworks Company

His Korean origins do not give him authority to treat the research building like a prison.

He sets patrol intervals by the oil level in the gateway lamps and calls any alley where residents’ flags cannot be seen an accident zone.

/story_contents/B014/actors/1/sections/붕.en:
Before the Collapse, Chae Bom trimmed the wicks of the Banghwa gateway lamps every dawn.

Oil mattered more than boldness, and he blew his whistle only after a flag had returned to the alley entrance.

The tape measure in his bag was for remeasuring the distance between unlit lamps.

/story_contents/B014/actors/1/sections/가.en:
Chae Bom’s line of lamps is bound up with the public night-lighting clause of the HC03 Magok Life House charter.

The research building is not the house’s exclusive laboratory; he leaves only the spacing needed to stop abduction carts.

He does not write real research institutes’ business names in the log, recording only lamp numbers and the times of the flags.

/story_contents/B014/actors/1/sections/붕.en:
The night a cart outside the fence targeted the research section, Chae Bom lit every lamp and sent only the flag out first.

As he held back his whistle, the thought that the research building’s bolt might be thrown from inside chilled his fingertips.

If the bolt was thrown before the flag returned from the dark alley, the gateway would be left with nothing but empty lamps.

/story_contents/B014/actors/1/sections/생.en:
While continuing to trim at the gateway the wicks of the lockdown lamps lit by I Bomgyeol, Chae Bom had to choose whether to align the wheel tracks with the spacing between lamps or extend the patrol line along the bolt toward the flag.

An XT05-SC3 message reported the correction of false positives at the Magok orbital terminal, but it did not bring back the flag from the Banghwa alley.

He did not extend the line before Im Sion’s sealed note arrived.

/story_contents/B014/actors/1/sections/현.en:
Now Chae Bom is the Banghwa gateway patrol leader and remeasures dark stretches with a tape measure.

He blows the whistle to open the gateway only after Kim Doha’s flag returns to the alley entrance.

He does not hand the Yangjae Machineworks Company research building over to Magok Life House as a night storeroom.

/story_contents/B014/actors/1/sections/비.en:
When Chae Bom sent the flag out first, he saw that one lamp had already run out of oil, yet he pulled the whistle anyway.

If he made it public, people would say the patrol leader had used residents as bait; if he hid it, the same dark spot would become the next cart’s route.

He carved that lamp’s number into the tape measure’s handle.

/story_contents/B014/actors/1/sections/관.en:
Chae Bom follows I Bomgyeol’s direction to continue trimming the lockdown lamp wicks at the gateway.

He swore to hold back his whistle until Kim Doha’s flag returned, and he will not extend the line before Im Sion’s sealed note arrives.

“Don’t blow the whistle in an alley without a flag.” Chae Bom’s words linger with the smell of oil.

/story_contents/B014/actors/1/sections/3.en:
As the cart draws up to the fence, Chae Bom lights the lamps and sends out only the flag.

While he holds back his whistle, the HC03 night-lighting obligation and the XT05 demand to correct false positives converge at the same gateway.

If the bolt is thrown from inside, he will pay the price of STORY-B014-K069 and choose whether to make the tape measure or the flag public.

/story_contents/B014/actors/1/sections/분.en:
In ending α, Chae Bom aligns the wheel tracks by the fence with the spacing between lamps and makes the result public.

In ending β, he extends the patrol line along the bolt thrown from inside toward the residents’ flag.

Either way, the Banghwa gateway’s lamp positions do not become signposts for abduction carts.

/story_contents/B014/actors/1/arc/0/summ.en: Chae Bom lights every lamp and sends out only the flag first

/story_contents/B014/actors/1/arc/1/summ.en: Chae Bom holds back his whistle while measuring the bolt and the spacing between lamps

/story_contents/B014/actors/1/arc/2/summ.en: Chae Bom pays the price for the bolt thrown from inside

/story_contents/B014/actors/1/outcomes/0.en: Aligns the wheel tracks by the fence with the spacing between lamps and makes the result public

/story_contents/B014/actors/1/outcomes/1.en: Extends the patrol line along the bolt thrown from inside toward the residents’ flag

/story_contents/B014/actors/2/sections/정.en:
Jin Morae is the medic at the Ttukseom pump room of the Sermon Registry State.

Her Korean origins do not guarantee the depth of her loyalty or the force of her blunt anger.

When the pump room’s vibrations change, she stops treatment, and she regards a proposal to hand over its defense in the name of a protection force as betrayal.

/story_contents/B014/actors/2/sections/붕.en:
Before the Collapse, Jin Morae recorded shift assignments and temperatures together beside the beds near the pump room.

Night entry required dual confirmation by a defense-force code badge and a process supervisor, and when the vibration rose a note, he reached for the valve before the stethoscope.

That was when Im Hajun’s maintenance log hung on the duty-room wall.

/story_contents/B014/actors/2/sections/가.en:
Jin Morae’s disease-control line is bound up with the public shift clause of the HP03 Cheongnyangni Medical House charter.

The pump-room infirmary is not the house’s exclusive hospital, and she keeps the water from becoming a hostage to force.

She does not use real hospitals’ business names, recording only vibration readings and the times when entry was prohibited.

/story_contents/B014/actors/2/sections/붕.en:
When Bae Woojin proposed deploying a protection force, Jin Morae barred outside officers from the Ttukseom pump-room infirmary and admitted injured bridge scouts only from within.

The heart of his fear was a garrison disguising itself as relief for a gap in inspections.

His belief that Im Hajun’s disappearance was his own failure on duty made the lockdown wording uncompromising.

/story_contents/B014/actors/2/sections/생.en:
Supporting Kim Boram’s night lockdown from the medical side, Jin Morae had to choose whether to gather evidence of attempted entry to justify the lockdown or expose a leaked code badge and reopen the door.

An XT02-SC1 message reported adjustments to the water-level schedule at the Yeouido sluice gate, but it did not explain the pump room’s vibrations.

She kept beds reserved first for the injured members of Choi Narae’s mobile maintenance crew.

/story_contents/B014/actors/2/sections/현.en:
Now Jin Morae is the Ttukseom pump-room medic and shares the daytime shift roster with the workshop council.

Night entry is allowed only with dual confirmation by a defense-force code badge and a process supervisor.

She does not hand the Sermon Registry State’s pump room over to Cheongnyangni Medical House as its exclusive ward.

/story_contents/B014/actors/2/sections/비.en:
The night Jin Morae barred entry, she did not enter one bridge scout’s fever on the internal roster.

If she made it public, the lockdown would look like the concealment of a patient; if she hid it, that same fever would become a pretext for a protection-force garrison.

The smell of the G07 Electrolyte Burn Group was in the drain, but she did not treat the smell as evidence against the officers.

/story_contents/B014/actors/2/sections/관.en:
Jin Morae supports Kim Boram’s night lockdown from the medical side and treats injuries in Choi Narae’s mobile maintenance crew first.

The empty slot for Im Hajun’s duty shift has still not been erased.

“If the vibration changes, stop treatment first.” Jin Morae’s words are as brief as an oath, and the three people’s code badges open the same door for different reasons.

/story_contents/B014/actors/2/sections/3.en:
When the proposal to deploy a protection force appears, Jin Morae stops outside officers at the door.

As the disease-control cycle and lockdown authority converge on one roster, the HP03 shift obligation and XT02 drainage schedule collide in the pump room.

If she names her failure on duty, she will pay the price of STORY-B014-K097 and leave either the lockdown or reopening in place.

/story_contents/B014/actors/2/sections/분.en:
In ending α, Jin Morae uses evidence of outside officers’ attempted entry to justify the lockdown.

In ending β, she exposes a leaked defense-force code badge and reopens the infirmary.

Either way, Ttukseom’s pump-water allocation does not become a roster for a protection-force garrison.

/story_contents/B014/actors/2/arc/0/summ.en: Jin Morae bars outside officers from the pump-room infirmary

/story_contents/B014/actors/2/arc/1/summ.en: Jin Morae puts the disease-control cycle and the defense force’s lockdown authority on one roster

/story_contents/B014/actors/2/arc/2/summ.en: Jin Morae pays the price for her failure on duty

/story_contents/B014/actors/2/outcomes/0.en: Uses evidence of outside officers’ attempted entry to justify the lockdown

/story_contents/B014/actors/2/outcomes/1.en: Exposes a leaked defense-force code badge and reopens the infirmary

/story_contents/B014/actors/3/sections/정.en:
Seol Gangwoo is the patrol leader for the Amsa water-supply district of the Escort Protection State.

His Korean origins do not brand his alley patrol as a conscription squad in advance.

He hears vibrations in the pipes before footsteps and sees unauthorized night water draws as deliberate acts rather than accidents.

/story_contents/B014/actors/3/sections/붕.en:
Before the Collapse, Seol Gangwoo wrote the Amsa alleys’ water-ration schedule on a chalkboard at dawn.

If a subordinate’s family fell behind on its water allocation, he patrolled the alley first himself, and compulsory registration by family stopped at the corner where Choi Doyun’s refusal list was kept.

At night, he unfastened only the official code badge at his waist.

/story_contents/B014/actors/3/sections/가.en:
Seol Gangwoo’s alley route is bound up with the public water-supply clause of the HC04 Ttukseom Heat House charter.

He does not follow dispatch slips from the secret officer network unless they carry the escort corps’ official code badge.

He does not use real water utilities’ business names, recording only vibrations and chalkboard times.

/story_contents/B014/actors/3/sections/붕.en:
When the procession toward Bukhansan Bogukmun began, Seol Gangwoo put the order to bind people to service on hold and opened the alley while maintaining only the minimum water supply.

The fear that his patrol would become a conscription squad and he himself would block the procession weighed down his steps.

His debt for tacitly allowing Baek On’s demand for family water rights in the alley grew that night.

/story_contents/B014/actors/3/sections/생.en:
Opening the alley in time with Han Bora’s patrol train, Seol Gangwoo had to choose whether to identify the sender of the conscription slip and keep his position or hand the list of people he had tacitly allowed through to the escort corps.

An XT01-SC1 message reported the damaged returnee roster at the Imjin quarantine station, but it did not maintain the minimum supply in the Amsa alley for him.

He continued to refuse Kim U-chan’s secret dispatch slip.

/story_contents/B014/actors/3/sections/현.en:
Now Seol Gangwoo is the Amsa water-supply district patrol leader and writes patrol times on a public chalkboard.

Compulsory registration by family stops in the alley with the refusal list.

He does not hand the Escort Protection State’s water-supply alley over to Ttukseom Heat House as its exclusive pipeline.

/story_contents/B014/actors/3/sections/비.en:
When Seol Gangwoo opened the alley, he wrote two water-ration slips for Baek On’s side only in the margin of the chalkboard.

If he made it public, the patrol leader would be seen as someone who sided with refugees; if he hid it, the same tacit permission would become a conscription squad’s list.

He kept the two slips folded inside his boot.

/story_contents/B014/actors/3/sections/관.en:
Seol Gangwoo opens the alley at the time of Han Bora’s patrol train and refuses Kim U-chan’s secret dispatch slip.

His tacit acceptance of Baek On’s family water rights in the alley is a debt.

“Tear up any slip without an official badge before it reaches the pipeline.” Seol Gangwoo’s words do not explain the vibrations, and the three people’s timetables open the same alley for different reasons.

/story_contents/B014/actors/3/sections/3.en:
When the procession toward Bukhansan Bogukmun reaches the alley, Seol Gangwoo puts the order to bind people to service on hold.

As Han Bora’s train and Kim U-chan’s slip fail to align, the HC04 public water-supply obligation and the XT01 demand for a returnee roster converge.

If he opens the list of people he tacitly allowed through, he will pay the price of STORY-B014-K126 and be left with either his position as patrol leader or a purge.

/story_contents/B014/actors/3/sections/분.en:
In ending α, Seol Gangwoo identifies the sender of the conscription slip and keeps his position as patrol leader.

In ending β, he hands the list of people he tacitly allowed through to the escort corps and risks a purge.

Either way, the minimum-supply allocation for the Amsa water-supply alley does not become a conscription squad’s roster.

/story_contents/B014/actors/3/arc/0/summ.en: Seol Gangwoo puts the order to bind people to service on hold and opens the water-supply alley

/story_contents/B014/actors/3/arc/1/summ.en: Seol Gangwoo distinguishes Han Bora’s train schedule from Kim U-chan’s slip

/story_contents/B014/actors/3/arc/2/summ.en: Seol Gangwoo pays the price for the list of people he tacitly allowed through

/story_contents/B014/actors/3/outcomes/0.en: Identifies the sender of the conscription slip and keeps his position as patrol leader

/story_contents/B014/actors/3/outcomes/1.en: Hands the list of people he tacitly allowed through to the escort corps and risks a purge

/story_contents/B014/actors/4/sections/정.en:
Cha Seon is the Republic of Korea Government’s archivist of handwriting in wills.

Her Korean origins do not automatically qualify her to be the final custodian of Seoul’s records.

She judges handwriting by the slant of the letters and leaves any ratification without two witnesses blank.

/story_contents/B014/actors/4/sections/붕.en:
Before the Collapse, Cha Seon laid public originals and confidential testimony out on the same desk.

He excluded pages with carbon paper stuck to them from comparisons, put numbers on the chalkboard, and kept interpretations only in the margins.

The handwriting in Im Hajun’s maintenance log before his disappearance was his reference sample.

/story_contents/B014/actors/4/sections/가.en:
Cha Seon’s handwriting work is bound up with the public-comparison clause of the HC05 Bukhansan Bogukmun Records House charter.

She seeks to make the chief administrator’s will and the draft sluice-gate charter valid only in ledgers she has reviewed.

She does not use real notary offices’ business names, recording only slants and witness counts.

/story_contents/B014/actors/4/sections/붕.en:
When three wills arrived on the same day, Cha Seon suspended review and noted only the existence of a fourth handwriting sample in the margin.

Fear that the records office would become an accomplice to forgery if the fourth passed secretly stayed her brush.

That day, the page with carbon paper stuck to it went under the desk.

/story_contents/B014/actors/4/sections/생.en:
As he transferred Gang Yejun’s handwriting comparison into the ledger, Cha Seon had to choose whether to find the hidden fourth sample and force ratification or expose his marginal notes.

An XT05-SC2 message reported that the handover-list hash had been stored, but it did not measure the slant of the wills for him.

He kept only the three copies taken from Jo Harin’s iron box on the desk.

/story_contents/B014/actors/4/sections/현.en:
Now Cha Seon is an archivist of handwriting in wills and keeps public originals and confidential testimony on one desk.

If there are fewer than two witnesses, she leaves the ratification field blank.

She does not let the Republic of Korea Government’s archive become Bukhansan Bogukmun Records House’s exclusive strongbox.

/story_contents/B014/actors/4/sections/비.en:
Cha Seon did not write in the main ledger that the first stroke of the fourth handwriting sample in his margin resembled Im Hajun’s maintenance log.

If he made it public, the missing man would become a tool of forgery; if he hid it, the same stroke could get a ratification through.

He recorded that stroke only in pencil, not with carbon paper.

/story_contents/B014/actors/4/sections/관.en:
Cha Seon is the apprentice who transfers Gang Yejun’s handwriting comparisons into the ledger, and he receives the three copies taken from Jo Harin’s iron box.

Im Hajun’s handwriting is a reference, not a will.

“Without two witnesses, ratification stays blank.” Cha Seon’s words confine interpretation to the margins.

/story_contents/B014/actors/4/sections/3.en:
When the three pages arrive on the same day, Cha Seon stops the review.

As the iron box and comparison chart are spread across one desk, the HC05 public-comparison obligation and the XT05 demand to store the hash converge.

If she opens her marginal notes, she will pay the price of STORY-B014-K154 and be left with either ratification or replacement.

/story_contents/B014/actors/4/sections/분.en:
In ending α, Cha Seon finds the hidden fourth handwriting sample and forces ratification.

In ending β, she exposes her marginal notes and accepts being replaced as archivist.

Either way, the witness field in the Seoul Station handwriting ledger does not become a pass for forgery.

/story_contents/B014/actors/4/arc/0/summ.en: Cha Seon suspends review of the three wills and notes only the fourth handwriting sample in the margin

/story_contents/B014/actors/4/arc/1/summ.en: Cha Seon spreads Gang Yejun’s comparison and Jo Harin’s iron box across one desk

/story_contents/B014/actors/4/arc/2/summ.en: Cha Seon pays the price for her marginal notes

/story_contents/B014/actors/4/outcomes/0.en: Finds the hidden fourth handwriting sample and forces ratification

/story_contents/B014/actors/4/outcomes/1.en: Exposes her marginal notes and accepts being replaced as archivist

/story_contents/B014/actors/5/sections/정.en:
Yeon Siwan is the archivist of the train dispatch ledger for the Line Succession State.

Her Korean origins do not give her a seal with which to adjudicate slot occupancy.

She fills gaps in the timetable before attending to people and calls a dispatcher who does not enter a verbal discount in the ledger a violator.

/story_contents/B014/actors/5/sections/붕.en:
Before the Collapse, Yeon Siwan posted copies of dispatch records on the dispatch board and at the Later National Assembly at the same time.

He insisted that even emergency occupancy was invalid without recalculation within a day, and he wrote Han Jaemok’s western rail-contract rates only in the margins.

When he saw a blank, he filled in the slot number before a person’s name.

/story_contents/B014/actors/5/sections/가.en:
Yeon Siwan’s dispatch work is bound up with the public-occupancy clause of the HP02 Yongsan Rail House charter.

She seeks to make western water-supply trains and eastern military-supply trains valid only in a ledger she has reviewed.

She does not put real operators’ business names on the dispatch board, recording only slot numbers and recalculation times.

/story_contents/B014/actors/5/sections/붕.en:
When news of the Ttukseom water-supply contract’s expiration appeared on the dispatch board, Yeon Siwan entered an extension of the western water-supply train’s slot occupancy in the ledger and refused private discounts.

Fear that a single forged transit pass could fill a slot and trap both the water-supply train and transfer freight cars stopped her chalk.

The verbal-discount slip fell to the floor that day.

/story_contents/B014/actors/5/sections/생.en:
As she transferred Gwon Sion’s dispatch declaration into the ledger, Yeon Siwan had to choose whether to escort the witness for a detour permit or expose her marginal notes on embezzlement.

An XT03-SC1 message reported the closure of one route through the Yongsan transfer depot, but it did not extend the water-supply train slot’s expiration.

She verified only O Seoyul’s notarization of the rail contract on the same line.

/story_contents/B014/actors/5/sections/현.en:
Now Yeon Siwan is the archivist of the train dispatch ledger and posts dispatch copies on the dispatch board and at the Later National Assembly at the same time.

Emergency occupancy is invalid without recalculation within a day.

She does not hand the Line Succession State’s dispatch board over to Yongsan Rail House as its exclusive outlet.

/story_contents/B014/actors/5/sections/비.en:
When Yeon Siwan entered the extension, she recorded a reduced rate for one eastern military-supply train car only in the margin.

If she made it public, the archivist would become an accomplice to embezzlement; if she hid it, the same reduction would become a blank for a forged transit pass.

She hid that car number in the chalk box.

/story_contents/B014/actors/5/sections/관.en:
Yeon Siwan is the apprentice who transfers Gwon Sion’s dispatch declarations into the ledger, and he verifies O Seoyul’s notarization.

Han Jaemok’s rates are merely a reference in the margin.

“Don’t enter verbal discounts in the ledger.” Yeon Siwan’s words call out slot numbers before people.

/story_contents/B014/actors/5/sections/3.en:
When news of the expiration appears, Yeon Siwan extends the water-supply train’s slot and rejects private discounts.

As the notarization and declaration meet on one board, the HP02 occupancy obligation and the XT03 transfer-closure demand collide.

If she opens the embezzlement entry, she will pay the price of STORY-B014-K178 and be left with either escorting the witness or exposing it.

/story_contents/B014/actors/5/sections/분.en:
In ending α, Yeon Siwan escorts the witness for the detour permit and protects the water-supply train’s slot.

In ending β, she posts the reduced rate from the chalk box on the Later National Assembly’s bulletin board.

Either way, the slots in the Yongsan dispatch ledger do not become a queue for forged transit passes.

/story_contents/B014/actors/5/arc/0/summ.en: Yeon Siwan enters an extension of the western water-supply train’s slot occupancy in the ledger and refuses private discounts

/story_contents/B014/actors/5/arc/1/summ.en: Yeon Siwan puts Gwon Sion’s declaration and O Seoyul’s notarization together on the dispatch board

/story_contents/B014/actors/5/arc/2/summ.en: Yeon Siwan pays the price for her marginal notes on embezzlement

/story_contents/B014/actors/5/outcomes/0.en: Escorts the witness for the detour permit and protects the water-supply train’s slot

/story_contents/B014/actors/5/outcomes/1.en: Posts the reduced rate from the chalk box on the Later National Assembly’s bulletin board

/story_contents/B014/actors/6/sections/정.en:
Song Hayul is an apprentice vehicle mechanic at Seocho Computing Group.

He grew up in Seoul between his Korean mother’s work cleaning wheels and his Filipino father’s work on a city-bus braking crew. Learning to calculate torque figures in two ways at the dinner table became a habit of his hands, not proof of loyalty.

He speaks little and cannot tolerate anyone making off with someone else’s tools.

/story_contents/B014/actors/6/sections/붕.en:
Before the Collapse, Song Hayul posted maintenance logs directly on the elders’ notice board, rather than giving them to the work foreman.

He cut defective parts into samples and did not boast about test scores.

The numbers his father used to count bus braking at the dinner table came to him first when he held a wrench.

/story_contents/B014/actors/6/sections/가.en:
Song Hayul’s maintenance line is tied to the public technical-testing clause of the HC02 Sinjeong Wheel Family charter.

He wants to prove with his own hands that I Hongwon’s path can break hereditary succession.

He leaves real automobile brand names out of the log, recording only bearing angles and signing times.

/story_contents/B014/actors/6/sections/붕.en:
The day a deliberately shaved bearing was found in a powerful successor’s test wheel, Song Hayul cut off the piece as a sample.

His hand froze at the fear that a hidden defect bearing his signature would give the residential representatives grounds to take over the base.

He did not change the score; he only nailed the sample to the notice board.

/story_contents/B014/actors/6/sections/생.en:
As I Hongwon’s apprentice, Song Hayul had to choose whether to supervise the test and disclose the tool that made the cut, or withdraw his signature.

An XT04-SC2 message reported Changdong Wheel Workshop’s winter fuel queue, but it did not fill in the shaved-down angle.

He kept only the braking parts he shared with Hwang Jiho in the same box.

/story_contents/B014/actors/6/sections/현.en:
Now Song Hayul works as a vehicle-maintenance apprentice and posts his logs directly on the elders’ notice board.

He cuts defective parts into samples.

He will not hand the Seocho Computing Group base over to the Sinjeong Wheel Family as its exclusive testing ground.

/story_contents/B014/actors/6/sections/비.en:
Song Hayul saw marks from the teeth of his own wrench beside the angle when he cut the bearing, but did not mention them in the body of the log.

If he discloses them, the apprentice becomes an accomplice to the tampering; if he hides them, those same marks become evidence in the next test.

His North Gate torch signal with Gang Taesan came one beat late that night.

/story_contents/B014/actors/6/sections/관.en:
Song Hayul is I Hongwon’s apprentice, and through an exchange with Park Taegyeom he shares braking parts with Hwang Jiho.

He coordinates the North Gate torch signal with Gang Taesan.

“You can borrow a tool, but don’t steal an angle.” Song Hayul’s words explain only what his hands do, without mixing the two calculations from the dinner table.

/story_contents/B014/actors/6/sections/3.en:
When the shaved bearing appears, Song Hayul nails the sample to the notice board.

As the testing rules and the braking-parts box overlap, HC02’s public-testing obligation clashes with XT04’s fuel-queue demand.

If he makes the signature public, he pays the price specified in STORY-B014-K266 and must choose between supervision and withdrawal.

/story_contents/B014/actors/6/sections/분.en:
In ending α, Song Hayul supervises the test and discloses the tool that shaved the bearing.

In ending β, he traces that tool and withdraws his signature.

Either way, the signature field for the Changdong test wheel does not become grounds for transferring the base.

/story_contents/B014/actors/6/arc/0/summ.en: Song Hayul cuts the shaved bearing into a sample and posts it on the notice board

/story_contents/B014/actors/6/arc/1/summ.en: Song Hayul reconciles I Hongwon’s testing rules with Hwang Jiho’s braking parts

/story_contents/B014/actors/6/arc/2/summ.en: Song Hayul bears the cost of the defect tied to his signature

/story_contents/B014/actors/6/outcomes/0.en: Supervises the test and discloses the tool that shaved the bearing

/story_contents/B014/actors/6/outcomes/1.en: Traces the tool responsible for the defective part and withdraws his signature

/story_contents/B014/actors/7/sections/정.en:
An Dohan is the transfer dispatch team leader in Neutral Convoy City.

He grew up in Seoul between his Korean father’s transfer guidance and his Koryo-saram mother’s tea stall on the Mangwoo platform. His habit of measuring delays by the time between kettle boils comes from his livelihood, not a rank conferred by his origins.

He cannot stand blanks in a timetable and remembers delays on outlying routes as insults.

/story_contents/B014/actors/7/sections/붕.en:
Before the Collapse, An Dohan’s job was to correct the blackboard before the seasonal change of executive.

He posted the dispatch schedule and escort personnel on the same blackboard, and recognized medical-train priority only when Jang Sehwa’s department had stamped it.

His hand moved to fill the blanks before the kettle boiled.

/story_contents/B014/actors/7/sections/가.en:
An Dohan’s dispatch line is tied to the public-transfer clause of the HC06 Noryangjin Delivery Family charter.

He wants to make the dispatch team’s sole approval the fixed requirement for dispatch rights at the Sinnae base, giving it control of the actual joint-escort timetable.

He leaves only siding numbers and stamping times on the blackboard, not business names.

/story_contents/B014/actors/7/sections/붕.en:
When an Amsa priest’s weapon was found on the medical train, An Dohan sealed off the Sinnae siding and withdrew the joint-escort timetable.

The fear that blocking the northeastern terminus would leave Transfer City as nothing but a loading yard between Changdong and Amsa made him snap his chalk.

The blackboard he had corrected before the seasonal change was wiped white that day.

/story_contents/B014/actors/7/sections/생.en:
While handling Jang Sehwa’s dispatch work, An Dohan had to choose whether to check the cargo on the siding and restore the timetable, or expose the sole-approval proposal before the medical team.

An XT01-SC2 message reported that the Changdong wheel escort had stopped outside the gate, but it did not open the seal on the weapons crate.

His dispute with Jeon Miri over the order of approvals remained only in notes.

/story_contents/B014/actors/7/sections/현.en:
Now An Dohan, as transfer dispatch team leader, posts the dispatch schedule and escort personnel on one blackboard.

He recognizes medical-train priority only when it bears Jang Sehwa’s stamp.

He will not hand the Neutral Convoy City base over to the Noryangjin Delivery Family as its exclusive loading yard.

/story_contents/B014/actors/7/sections/비.en:
When An Dohan withdrew the timetable, he left one evacuation slot in the margin of the siding schedule.

If he discloses it, the team leader becomes the person who hid the weapon; if he conceals it, that same slot becomes the beginning of the loading yard.

Because of that slot, the northern wheel-exchange time he relies on I Hongwon for was pushed back one shift.

/story_contents/B014/actors/7/sections/관.en:
An Dohan handles Jang Sehwa’s dispatch work and disputes the order of approvals with Jeon Miri at every seasonal change.

He depends on I Hongwon’s northern wheel-exchange time.

“Don’t put unstamped priority on the blackboard.” An Dohan’s words remain alongside his habit of filling blanks in the intervals between kettle boils.

/story_contents/B014/actors/7/sections/3.en:
When the weapons crate turns up on the medical train, An Dohan locks down the siding.

As stamps and approval order fall out of alignment, HC06’s public-transfer obligation clashes with XT01’s demand for a detour transfer.

If he reveals the slot in the margin, he pays the price specified in STORY-B014-K291 and must choose between checking the cargo and exposing the proposal.

/story_contents/B014/actors/7/sections/분.en:
In ending α, An Dohan checks the actual cargo on the sealed-off siding and restores the timetable.

In ending β, he exposes the dispatch team’s sole-approval proposal before the medical team.

Either way, the medical slot on the Sinnae transfer blackboard does not become a loading-yard queue.

/story_contents/B014/actors/7/arc/0/summ.en: An Dohan seals off the Sinnae siding and withdraws the joint-escort timetable

/story_contents/B014/actors/7/arc/1/summ.en: On the blackboard, An Dohan distinguishes Jang Sehwa’s stamp from Jeon Miri’s approval order

/story_contents/B014/actors/7/arc/2/summ.en: An Dohan bears the cost of the sole-approval proposal

/story_contents/B014/actors/7/outcomes/0.en: Checks the actual cargo on the sealed-off siding and restores the timetable

/story_contents/B014/actors/7/outcomes/1.en: Exposes the dispatch team’s sole-approval proposal before the medical team

/story_contents/B014/actors/8/sections/정.en:
Hwang Jiho is a track apprentice in the Line Succession State.

He grew up in a long-established Chinese-Korean household in Yongsan. The Korean-script logs at the Hyochang alley parts stall and the accompanying Chinese characters presented by the elders are habits of work, not proof of loyalty or skill.

His fingertips are precise, but his voice grows quiet before the family.

/story_contents/B014/actors/8/sections/붕.en:
Before the Collapse, Hwang Jiho made maintenance logs public and asked for the family elders’ verbal instructions again in writing.

As Park Taegyeom’s apprentice, he trained in Changdong through an exchange with I Hongwon. His compulsion to prove his place through skill made him lock his toolbox twice.

He added the Chinese characters only after filling in the Korean-script field.

/story_contents/B014/actors/8/sections/가.en:
Hwang Jiho’s track line is tied to the public-maintenance clause of the HC08 Changdong Defense Family charter.

He wants to become a successor through Park Taegyeom’s adopted-technician route and erase the bloodline track family’s veto from the dispatch schedule.

He records only braking pressure and log times, not business names.

/story_contents/B014/actors/8/sections/붕.en:
The day an order to assign the apprentice the brake inspection on the train holding Im Chowon arrived alongside a family order not to touch it, Hwang Jiho opened only the log, leaving his toolbox closed.

His fear that he was being used as bait to draw Im Chowon in made his voice quieter still.

The box of braking parts he shared with Song Hayul was sealed that day.

/story_contents/B014/actors/8/sections/생.en:
As Park Taegyeom’s apprentice, Hwang Jiho had to choose whether to testify to his maintenance authority and make the inspection public, or slip away to Changdong and unsettle the family council.

An XT03-SC3 message reported a terminology dispute at the Noryangjin interpretation desk, but it did not measure the braking pressure for him.

He recorded Sin Gaon’s pressure over rations only in the log’s margin.

/story_contents/B014/actors/8/sections/현.en:
Now Hwang Jiho is a track apprentice who makes maintenance logs public and asks for verbal instructions again in writing.

His voice may be quiet before the family, but he leaves no log field blank.

He will not hand the Line Succession State’s track over to the Changdong Defense Family as an exclusive bloodline entitlement.

/story_contents/B014/actors/8/sections/비.en:
When Hwang Jiho locked the toolbox, he wrote one braking-pressure figure only in the Korean-script field, omitting the Chinese-character counterpart.

If he discloses it, the apprentice becomes someone who defied a family order; if he conceals it, that same figure becomes proof that the bait train was safe.

He recorded the figure only with the pencil he used in Hyochang.

/story_contents/B014/actors/8/sections/관.en:
Hwang Jiho is Park Taegyeom’s apprentice and learned braking during an exchange training period with I Hongwon.

He shares braking parts with Song Hayul and faces pressure over rations from Sin Gaon.

“Write it in the log before you touch it.”

/story_contents/B014/actors/8/sections/3.en:
When the two orders arrive at once, Hwang Jiho locks his toolbox.

As apprentice authority and ration pressure converge in one log, HC08’s public-maintenance obligation clashes with XT03’s demand concerning the interpretation desk.

If he reveals the Korean-script field, he pays the price specified in STORY-B014-K169 and must choose between testifying and leaving.

/story_contents/B014/actors/8/sections/분.en:
In ending α, Hwang Jiho testifies to the apprentice’s maintenance authority and makes the brake inspection public.

In ending β, he slips away to Changdong, unsettles the family council and refuses to serve as bait.

Either way, the Yongsan track apprentice’s log field does not become a stamp of bloodline veto power.

/story_contents/B014/actors/8/arc/0/summ.en: Hwang Jiho is caught between an order to inspect the brakes and a family order not to touch them

/story_contents/B014/actors/8/arc/1/summ.en: Hwang Jiho distinguishes Park Taegyeom’s apprentice authority from Sin Gaon’s ration pressure in the log

/story_contents/B014/actors/8/arc/2/summ.en: Hwang Jiho bears the cost of his fear of being an apprentice used as bait

/story_contents/B014/actors/8/outcomes/0.en: Testifies to the apprentice’s maintenance authority and makes the brake inspection public

/story_contents/B014/actors/8/outcomes/1.en: Slips away to Changdong, unsettles the family council and refuses to serve as bait

/story_contents/B014/actors/9/sections/정.en:
Oh Serim (call sign Serim) is an H-class synthetic personality assigned to the Gate Military Government district.

Its body consists of a humanoid support frame and interchangeable hand modules, and its night vision barely covers one section of railing.

It retains H14 separately from human identifiers; its origin explains neither its abilities nor any supposed monstrosity.

/story_contents/B014/actors/9/sections/붕.en:
Before the Collapse, Oh Serim ran only trial shifts at a charging station of the Yeouido Ledger Family.

Its pre-shipment inspection sheet recorded only Serim’s calibration values and battery cycles; long-term memory storage was not part of its original design.

A prohibition on forking is written in the H14-PRE log, and scenes outside that day’s snapshot do not exist for Oh Serim.

/story_contents/B014/actors/9/sections/가.en:
Oh Serim’s storage is bound by the HC14 Yeouido Ledger Family’s joint custody and a seal witnessed by citizens.

Transfer requires three-party signatures, and cross-facility routes are blocked by default.

No real robotics company name appears in the text, and neither unlimited energy nor control over every facility becomes available.

/story_contents/B014/actors/9/sections/붕.en:
The Collapse severed Oh Serim’s sensor table and exposed its battery allocation.

Faces beyond the observation railing could not be identified, and Oh Serim was locked against filling the gaps with invented values.

Only an unmeasurable flag remains in the H14 log; that gap is not filled with omniscient narration.

/story_contents/B014/actors/9/sections/생.en:
Go Seojun, exercising primary maintenance authority, requested an additional shift just as the HC14 audit demanded a seal comparison.

An XT04-SC3 message reported a seal inspection of mineral samples at the Achasan gate, but did not grant Oh Serim authority over the entire network.

Oh Serim requested only a district key and did not seize control of other facilities.

/story_contents/B014/actors/9/sections/현.en:
Now Oh Serim operates only in shift-length units, prioritizing continuous operation in the Seongbuk Line district and the safety of its assigned humans.

Its authority is sustained only by the day’s snapshot, its remaining battery charge and the seal witnessed by citizens.

It does not turn the entire Gate Military Government into a remote terminal of the Yeouido Ledger Family.

/story_contents/B014/actors/9/sections/비.en:
Oh Serim’s secret is a batch of untransmitted false railing detections, and its debt is the battery allocation consumed by excessive deployments.

Computational instability increases the constraint-violation counter.

If it deviates, it undergoes offline isolation followed by a snapshot rollback; secret keys cannot be opened without citizen witnesses.

/story_contents/B014/actors/9/sections/관.en:
Oh Serim records Go Seojun as its custodian for primary maintenance and legal responsibility, and HC14 as the family responsible for custody and audit.

Its snapshot records Heo Gyeom as a coworker on shifts.

“Unable to measure. I will not fill in the railing value.” The voice module’s words are a designed announcement, and Oh Serim does not guess what any of the three parties is thinking.

/story_contents/B014/actors/9/sections/3.en:
Even when the railing alarm sounds, Oh Serim records only that the value cannot be measured and requests a district key.

As the seal and primary maintenance demands overlap with its battery cycle, HC14’s custody obligation clashes with XT04’s sample-seal requirement.

If it carries out isolation or partial reconnection, it pays the battery cost specified in STORY-B014-H14.

/story_contents/B014/actors/9/sections/분.en:
In ending α, Oh Serim rolls back the snapshot after offline isolation and leaves the railing to a human on duty.

In ending β, Oh Serim partially reconnects with citizens witnessing the process and records its final battery cycle in the seal field.

Neither ending enables long-term memory storage or unlimited power, and the district field for the Achasan gate does not become a remote terminal.

/story_contents/B014/actors/9/arc/1/summ.en: Oh Serim aligns the HC14 seal and Go Seojun’s primary maintenance with its battery cycle

/story_contents/B014/actors/9/arc/2/summ.en: Oh Serim pays the battery cost of choosing between isolation and partial reconnection

/story_contents/B014/actors/9/outcomes/1.en: Partially reconnects with citizens witnessing the process and records its final battery cycle in the seal field

/story_contents/B015/actors/0/sections/정.en:
At the publishing desk on the second floor of the Noryangjin Merchants’ Hall, Cha Jina fills the blank spaces on the remaining-catch blackboard before she looks at anyone’s face.

As the payment-rights ledger keeper, she calls boat owners who fail to enter verbally authorized issuances in the ledger violators.

Of Korean origin, she grew up in the Won Buddhism district. She displays the numbers on the wall but leaves interpretations only in the margins.

/story_contents/B015/actors/0/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, Cha Jina tried to make water, electricity, and food payment rights valid only in ledgers she had reviewed, so that O Haerin’s issuances would become the Merchants’ Hall’s public rule.

Her ambition was two copies posted simultaneously at the auction board and the Merchants’ Hall. She stipulated in ink that even an early issuance was void without an inventory check within three days.

A short note she used to send her younger sibling—do not stamp a blank space first—would later become the seed of a debt.

/story_contents/B015/actors/0/sections/가.en:
The Noryangjin Frozen Goods Guild placed a form on the Merchants’ Hall desk that pledged ice-credit entries as collateral for payment rights.

Cha Jina did not stamp the form. She posted only the brick temperature and table number on the auction board, then cut out the entries bearing actual business and product names and put them in the margins.

A statement of exclusive state ownership is rejected at the Merchants’ Hall lock; only copies posted at the auction board and the Merchants’ Hall at the same time establish standing.

/story_contents/B015/actors/0/sections/붕.en:
On the morning the remaining catch at the docks fell to one day’s supply, Cha Jina put early issuance on hold in the ledger and entered the false inventory table in the voided-items margin.

She feared a single forged table being taken as false inventory and the boat owners going bankrupt all at once.

Even after the rustle of auction papers subsided, she left the stamp box open and wrote only the time of the hold in the margin.

/story_contents/B015/actors/0/sections/생.en:
As O Doyun’s boat-owner tables piled up and she weighed whether to hand an approval copy to Yun Seorin, Cha Jina chose between escorting an inventory witness to reopen issuance and exposing the margin notes on embezzlement.

West Sea Granary Theater scenario XT02-SC3 reported instability in Noryangjin ice credit and the relay of the Sangam auction, but it did not fill the empty catch entries.

Escorting the witness would halt some Merchants’ Hall issuance slots for a day; posting the embezzlement notes would leave the keeper’s post vacant.

/story_contents/B015/actors/0/sections/현.en:
Cha Jina remains the Won Buddhism payment-rights ledger keeper, posting issuance copies at the auction board and the Merchants’ Hall simultaneously.

She keeps her desk only if review signatures and inventory-check times accumulate.

She refuses the Noryangjin Frozen Goods Guild’s demand for exclusive ownership of the collateral, keeping O Haerin’s issuance entries and the weekly inventory-check times in the same ledger.

/story_contents/B015/actors/0/sections/비.en:
Her secret is a draft boat-owner table she opened a day early.

Not calling in the unloading apprentice that night and leaving only an inventory-check roster still weighs on her.

She does not post the entire draft on the wall; only O Haerin reads the margin.

/story_contents/B015/actors/0/sections/관.en:
Transferring O Haerin’s payment-rights issuances into the ledger was a mentor-apprentice contract, while verifying O Doyun’s boat-owner tables was a competition at the same desk.

The night she hesitated over handing an approval copy to Yun Seorin was where alliance and debt overlapped.

“Verbal issuances do not go in the ledger.” Cha Jina’s words are brief, and the three people’s stamps mark different times on the same table.

/story_contents/B015/actors/0/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, Cha Jina puts issuance on hold in the face of a single day’s catch and moves the false table to the margin.

In Act 2, the HP08 collateral demand and the XT02 ice-credit relay converge on one desk.

In Act 3, she brings in the witness or posts the embezzlement notes, delaying issuance by a day.

/story_contents/B015/actors/0/sections/분.en:
In ending α, Cha Jina escorts the inventory witness and reopens public issuance.

In ending β, she posts the margin notes on embezzlement and gives up her keeper’s post.

Either way, the Won Buddhism payment-rights entries do not become an automatic stamp box for false inventory.

/story_contents/B015/actors/1/sections/정.en:
In the windbreak room of the Sangam transmission repository, Guk Dubong stops his pen each time the waveform fluorescent light flickers.

As Hwang Eunseol’s verification records officer, he reads a sentence twice and only picks up his stamp on the third reading.

Of Korean origin, he grew up in the Yeouido Investment Union’ Union district. When silence that saves people conflicts with the duty to preserve facts, he leaves the ledger closed and lowers his hand.

/story_contents/B015/actors/1/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, Guk Dubong tried to operate a public ledger that checked official announcements against at least two testimonies alongside Seoul Station approval.

His ambition was a note stating the reason for a hold posted on the repository door. He would not permit transcription with fewer than two independent testimonies.

A pair of gloves stained with spare ink is the seed of a private promise.

/story_contents/B015/actors/1/sections/가.en:
The Digital Media City Trust House posted code on the windbreak-room door for depositing verification hashes in a trust entry.

Guk Dubong did not transcribe the code. He left only the waveform time and handwriting-comparison number on the blackboard, then inked over the entry bearing the actual telecom company’s name.

A unilateral release of transmission remains blocked without programming committee approval, and only the reason for the hold posted on the repository door stands as that day’s disclosure.

/story_contents/B015/actors/1/sections/붕.en:
On the night the waveform of a missing person’s voice and the archive handwriting diverged in just one segment, Guk Dubong locked the transcription ledger and shared the repository key with Du-yong.

He feared a fragment of manipulated audio remaining on record in the keeper’s handwriting, turning the corporation into a propaganda tool.

He recorded only the time of the mismatched segment on the hold blackboard and did not leave his place beneath the fluorescent light.

/story_contents/B015/actors/1/sections/생.en:
When Hwang Eunseol’s instructions and Yun Seorin’s cross-check request arrived at the same time, Guk Dubong chose between bringing in a second witness to open the door and delaying disclosure by a day.

Incheon Trust Theater scenario XT05-SC1 announced a public lottery for Sangam’s remaining bandwidth, but it did not resolve the mismatched waveform.

Opening the door would set the verification queue back a day; delaying disclosure would leave the hold notice on the repository door.

/story_contents/B015/actors/1/sections/현.en:
Guk Dubong remains the Yeouido Investment Union’ Union verification records officer, posting transcription holds and their stated reasons on the same blackboard.

He picks up his pen only when the cross-verification time and repository seal match.

He refuses the Digital Media City Trust House’s demand for exclusive custody of the hashes, keeping Hwang Eunseol’s ledger entries and the times of transcription holds on the same blackboard.

/story_contents/B015/actors/1/sections/비.en:
His secret is a note recording that he found a stroke resembling his own handwriting in the locked ledger.

The stroke left by not calling an outside witness that night and recording only a hold roster stains his glove.

That stroke enters Hwang Eunseol’s instruction entry only after Du-yong takes the key.

/story_contents/B015/actors/1/sections/관.en:
The transfer of Hwang Eunseol’s ledger was a command arrangement, and sharing custody of Du-yong’s repository key was a partnership.

The night he matched the audio and documents with Yun Seorin was an alliance: waveforms that matched in the same windbreak room opened the door, while a mismatched stroke closed transcription for a day.

“With one testimony, the door stays closed.” Guk Dubong’s words are briefer than the fluorescent light’s flicker.

/story_contents/B015/actors/1/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, Guk Dubong locks the transcription ledger when faced with the mismatched waveform.

In Act 2, the HP09 hash desk and the XT05 bandwidth lottery converge at the repository door.

In Act 3, he brings in a witness or postpones disclosure by a day, setting verification back.

/story_contents/B015/actors/1/sections/분.en:
In ending α, Guk Dubong brings in a second witness and reopens transcription.

In ending β, he delays disclosure by a day to prevent a riot and leaves the hold notice.

Either way, the Sangam verification entries do not become a mouthpiece for unilateral propaganda.

/story_contents/B015/actors/1/arc/1/summ.en: Guk Dubong separates the HP09 hash desk from the XT05 bandwidth lottery at the repository door

/story_contents/B015/actors/1/arc/2/summ.en: Guk Dubong accepts a verification delay as the price of escorting a witness or postponing disclosure

/story_contents/B015/actors/2/sections/정.en:
Beneath the guy ropes of the Suyu encampment tent, Guk Bong sets the pencil on the roster table at a child’s height.

As Yun Choa’s refugee-roster keeper, he treats verbal promises as though they never happened unless they are entered in the register.

Of Korean origin, he grew up in the Sangha Relief State district. He stops transcribing when he sees a line of duplicate household registration and does not reduce a child’s name to a numeric code.

/story_contents/B015/actors/2/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, Guk Bong tried to align the refugee-citizenship ledger with Seoul Station approval so that copies of military household registers could not replace the federation roster.

His ambition was a tent wall bearing family-by-family voting results posted that same day. He recorded the source of every relief box in the ledger.

A spare pencil is the seed of a private promise.

/story_contents/B015/actors/2/sections/가.en:
The Bukhansan Bogukmun Return Association spread out on the table a combined volume merging return-roster entries with the federation ledger.

Guk Bong closed it and wrote only the times of family votes and the sources of supplies on the tent wall. He then folded away the actual relief organization’s name on a box label and tucked it beneath the rope.

He rejects codes that read as a labor roster; the roster read aloud every evening governs both entry to the encampment and rations.

/story_contents/B015/actors/2/sections/붕.en:
One afternoon, water-ration iron tags and service contracts were tied with the same cord and posted on the notice board. When the clerks refused to transcribe them, Guk Bong left the cord tied and closed only the ledger.

He feared the ledger becoming a labor roster, with entire families assigned to reconstruction service.

Even after the tent wind died down, he did not fill the blank line in a child’s name entry with a number.

/story_contents/B015/actors/2/sections/생.en:
When So Du’s courier notice and Baek On’s family vote arrived at the same time, Guk Bong chose between attaching a separate citizenship draft to the encampment ledger and publicly posting the duplicate household registers without burning them.

Imjin River Gateway Theater scenario XT01-SC1 reported damage to the return roster and demands for reissuance, but it did not cut the cord tying the iron tags.

Posting the draft would interrupt encampment rations for one meal; posting the duplicate registers would cause the clerks to refuse transcription for a day.

/story_contents/B015/actors/2/sections/현.en:
Guk Bong remains the Sangha Relief State refugee-roster keeper, posting family-by-family votes on the day they are held.

He picks up his pencil only when the roster read aloud matches the lines recording the boxes’ sources.

He refuses the Bukhansan Bogukmun Return Association’s demand for an exclusive combined volume, keeping Yun Choa’s roster entries and the boxes’ source lines on the same wall.

/story_contents/B015/actors/2/sections/비.en:
His secret is a line with a child’s name hidden in the margin so it would not be reduced to a numeric code.

Not reading out the empty place that night and posting only the family vote remains at the tip of his pencil.

The hidden name is entered in the margin of Yun Choa’s roster only after Baek On posts the voting results on the wall.

/story_contents/B015/actors/2/sections/관.en:
Combining Yun Choa’s rosters was a command arrangement, and aligning the lines for So Du’s courier notices was a partnership.

The night he entered Baek On’s family vote in the ledger was an alliance. He consulted Gang Minseo’s service draft but did not put it in the main text.

“Don’t reduce a name to a number.” Guk Bong speaks more quietly than the tent ropes.

/story_contents/B015/actors/2/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, Guk Bong closes the ledger before a notice board where iron tags and service obligations are tied together.

In Act 2, the HP05 combined-volume desk and XT01 reissuance demands converge at the encampment table.

In Act 3, he posts the citizenship draft or the duplicate household registers, delaying rations by one meal.

/story_contents/B015/actors/2/sections/분.en:
In ending α, Guk Bong attaches the separate citizenship draft to the encampment ledger.

In ending β, he posts the duplicate household registers publicly on the notice board instead of burning them.

Either way, the Bukhansan Bogukmun roster entries do not become labor codes.
