/story_contents/B015/actors/3/sections/정.en:
In the pit at Changdong Inspection Line No. 3, Guk Du reads the lot number while holding a bearing-box lid in place with her foot.

As Jo Woochan’s workplace-accident records officer, she remembers responsibility for accidents down to the date and treats an unsigned log as though it never existed.

Of Korean origin, she grew up in the Seocho Computing Group district and trusts handwriting beneath the wheels more than meetings.

/story_contents/B015/actors/3/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, Guk Du tried to preserve work records and accident responsibility as the elders’ notice board’s sole grounds for operation, using the logs to put an end to rumors of family succession.

Her ambition was a habit of obtaining the foreman’s and apprentice’s signatures on one line, with the defective sample number entered in the same space.

An oil-stained notebook is the seed of a private promise.

/story_contents/B015/actors/3/sections/가.en:
The Changdong Defense House hung a transfer form on the pit railing to move accident logs into the rail-defense entries.

Guk Du did not sign it. She wrote only the lot angle and signature time on the sample box, then wiped the actual vehicle company’s name off the sample label with an oily rag.

She rejects the practice of copying defect logs onto housing-election posters; only handwriting left on the pit railing serves as grounds for operation.

/story_contents/B015/actors/3/sections/붕.en:
On a shift when the lot number of a shaved bearing differed from the log in just one segment, Guk Du locked the ledger and put Du-mo’s maintenance sample number in the same box.

She feared the defect log being copied onto posters and the base being seized under a demographic rationale.

She left only the time of the mismatched line in her notebook’s margin and did not turn off the pit light.

/story_contents/B015/actors/3/sections/생.en:
When Jo Woochan’s instructions coincided with I Hongwon’s public technical-test record, Guk Du chose between posting the mismatched line on the notice board and delaying the log’s lock by a day.

Imjin River Gateway Theater scenario XT01-SC2 reported that the Changdong wheel convoy had stopped outside the gateway, but it did not account for the shaved angle.

Posting the line would stop Inspection Line No. 3 for one shift; delaying the lock would leave only the sample in the box.

/story_contents/B015/actors/3/sections/현.en:
Guk Du remains the Seocho Computing Group workplace-accident records officer, requiring the foreman’s and apprentice’s signatures on one line.

She opens the log only when the sample number matches the handwriting from the pit.

She refuses the Changdong Defense House’s demand for an exclusive transfer, keeping Jo Woochan’s log entries and the sample number in the same box.

/story_contents/B015/actors/3/sections/비.en:
Her secret is a note she did not enter in the main text, though she saw that the apprentice’s signature space was empty when she locked the ledger.

Locking only the ledger that night without calling the apprentice seeps into the oil on her notebook.

The note is attached to the end of Jo Woochan’s log only after Du-mo opens the sample box.

/story_contents/B015/actors/3/sections/관.en:
The transfer of Jo Woochan’s log was a command arrangement, and keeping Du-mo’s sample number in the box was a partnership.

The night he left I Hongwon’s technical-test record unlocked was an alliance. Angles matched in the same pit allowed inspection to continue, while a mismatched lot closed the log for a day.

“An unsigned log is not even an accident.” Guk Du’s words sink beneath the noise of the wheels.

/story_contents/B015/actors/3/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, Guk Du locks the ledger when faced with the mismatched lot.

In Act 2, the HC08 transfer desk and the XT01 convoy stoppage converge at the pit railing.

In Act 3, she posts the line or delays the lock by a day, setting inspection back one shift.

/story_contents/B015/actors/3/sections/분.en:
In ending α, Guk Du publicly posts the mismatched line on the elders’ notice board.

In ending β, she delays locking the log by a day to prevent a riot and leaves only the sample.

Either way, the Changdong accident entries do not become material for housing-election posters.

/story_contents/B015/actors/3/arc/1/summ.en: Guk Du separates the HC08 transfer desk from the XT01 convoy stoppage at the pit railing

/story_contents/B015/actors/3/arc/2/summ.en: Guk Du accepts an inspection delay as the price of disclosing the line or postponing the lock

/story_contents/B015/actors/4/sections/정.en:
Before the scale at the Mangu transfer checkpoint, Bong Mo silently counts the knots in a cargo-seal cord with his fingers.

As Mun Sion’s passage-screening records officer, he speaks little and compares evidence relentlessly.

Of Korean origin, he grew up in the Neutral Convoy City district and despises the practice of turning protection-fee receipts into transit passes.

/story_contents/B015/actors/4/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, Bong Mo tried to elevate screening on the northeastern outer route into a provision of the Joint Escort Treaty, using the ledger to end arbitrary searches by the Amsa escort unit.

His ambition was an entry recording identity fragments and cargo seals twice. He rejected major-power warrants without the joint seals of Jang Sehwa and the medical team.

A handful of spare seal cords is the seed of a private promise.

/story_contents/B015/actors/4/sections/가.en:
The Yongsan Rail Gate placed on the scale a cord binding the screening ledger to the transfer-slot entries.

Bong Mo removed it from the scale and wrote only the rear-gate measurements and entry number on the same line. She then cut the actual carrier’s name from the seal label with a knife.

She does not place copies of search warrants bearing a major power’s seal on the checkpoint scale; only entries that record identity fragments and cargo seals twice open screening.

/story_contents/B015/actors/4/sections/붕.en:
On a shift when traces of the base’s rear gate remained in the seal register and a line was missing from the screening ledger, Bong Mo locked the scale and clipped on only Bok Gam’s measurement note.

She feared the screening ledger being replaced by copies of search warrants, breaking neutrality from within.

Even after the platform announcement cut off, she did not fill the missing entry at her own discretion.

/story_contents/B015/actors/4/sections/생.en:
When Mun Sion’s instructions coincided with Gwak Taesan witnessing the sealing of an entry, Bong Mo chose between restoring the missing line and extracting an entry document that used refusal of screening as a pretext.

Tumen River Far Eastern Theater scenario XT04-SC1 announced publication of freight-car weight logs and adjustments to Sinnae transfer slots, but it did not erase the rear-gate traces.

Restoring the line would halt one train formation at the Mangu checkpoint; extracting the entry document would leave the scale unused for a day.

/story_contents/B015/actors/4/sections/현.en:
Bong Mo remains the Neutral Convoy City passage-screening records officer, recording identity fragments and cargo seals twice.

He opens screening only when the scale reading matches the joint seals of Jang Sehwa and the medical team.

He refuses the Yongsan Rail Gate’s demand for exclusive ownership of the slots, keeping Mun Sion’s screening entries and the scale reading on the same line.

/story_contents/B015/actors/4/sections/비.en:
His secret is a note he did not enter in the main text, though he knew the missing line coincided with his shift.

Not posting a rear-gate watch that night and locking only the scale remains in the clip.

The note is left at the end of Mun Sion’s screening ledger only after Bok Gam’s measurements are clipped to it.

/story_contents/B015/actors/4/sections/관.en:
The transfer of Mun Sion’s ledger was a command arrangement, and entering Bok Gam’s rear-gate measurements on the same line was a partnership.

Gwak Taesan’s presence at the sealing of an entry was an alliance recorded at the end of the ledger, while Jang Sehwa’s joint seal supported the refusal of warrants.

“A protection-fee receipt is not a transit pass.” Bong Mo’s words move more slowly than the scale needle.

/story_contents/B015/actors/4/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, Bong Mo locks the scale when faced with the missing screening line.

In Act 2, the HP02 slot desk and XT04 transfer adjustment converge over the seal cord.

In Act 3, she fills the line or extracts the entry document, setting a train formation back by one slot.

/story_contents/B015/actors/4/sections/분.en:
In ending α, Bong Mo restores the missing line and reopens screening.

In ending β, she extracts and posts the entry document that used refusal of screening as a pretext.

Either way, the Mangu screening entries do not become a desk for copies of major-power warrants.

/story_contents/B015/actors/4/arc/0/summ.en: Bong Mo locks the scale when faced with the missing screening line

/story_contents/B015/actors/4/arc/1/summ.en: Bong Mo separates the HP02 slot desk from the XT04 transfer adjustment over the seal cord

/story_contents/B015/actors/4/arc/2/summ.en: Bong Mo accepts a delay to the train formation as the price of restoring the line or extracting the document

/story_contents/B015/actors/4/outcomes/0.en: Restores the missing line and reopens screening

/story_contents/B015/actors/5/sections/정.en:
Beneath the waiting-room blackboard at the Cheongnyangni Medical Council, Yeong Neulbit fills blank spaces on the severity table before attending to people.

As Jeon Sol’s hospital-bed records officer, she calls merchants who fail to enter confidential treatment contracts in the ledger violators.

Of Korean origin, she grew up in the Medical Neutrality League district. She displays the numbers at the market entrance but leaves interpretations only in the margins.

/story_contents/B015/actors/5/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, Yeong Neulbit tried to make patient representatives’ veto rights and severity tables valid only in ledgers she had reviewed, so that secret agreements to turn away injured people from a major power would die on paper.

Her ambition was a waiting list posted simultaneously at the market entrance and the guild’s duty room. She entered contracts lacking the seals of three professions in the voided-items margin.

A spare piece of chalk is the seed of a private promise.

/story_contents/B015/actors/5/sections/가.en:
The Cheongnyangni Medical Center House wrote, in chalk on one side of the waiting-room blackboard, wording that bound the hospital-bed ledger to the medical-charter entries.

Yeong Neulbit rubbed it out with her palm and rewrote only the severity numbers and times of vetoes at the market entrance. She then moved the actual pharmaceutical company’s name on the chart to the margin.

Demands for an exclusive desk are rejected before the waiting-room blackboard; only a waiting list posted simultaneously at the market entrance and the duty room opens hospital beds.

/story_contents/B015/actors/5/sections/붕.en:
On the morning a false consent form appeared in the middle of the Medical Council, Yeong Neulbit moved its line to the margin and did not permit stamping before the handwriting comparison was complete.

She feared that single sheet turning the Medical Council into a puppet office.

Even after the waiting room’s dampness subsided, she left the chalk unbroken and wrote only the time in the margin at the edge of the blackboard.

/story_contents/B015/actors/5/sections/생.en:
When Jeon Sol’s veto and a copy of Seon Nahwi’s message lay on the same line, Yeong Neulbit had to choose whether to disclose the handwriting in the margin or erase a line from the register, leaving the veto field blank.

The Tumen River–Far East Theater scenario XT04-SC2 announced the Chang-dong winter fuel queue and the admission of frostbite patients in Jegi-dong, but it did not erase the strokes of the fraudulent consent form.

If she revealed the handwriting, one bed would stand empty for a day; if she erased the line, the veto field would be blank.

/story_contents/B015/actors/5/sections/현.en:
Yeong Neulbit remains the Medical Neutrality League council’s bed-records clerk, posting the waiting list at both the market entrance and the duty office.

She picks up the chalk only when the three professional seals and the triage chart agree.

Even when the Cheongnyangni Medical House demands exclusive ownership of the charter, she refuses and keeps Jeon Sol’s veto field and the triage chart on the same waiting list.

/story_contents/B015/actors/5/sections/비.en:
Her secret is a memo recording that she delayed comparing the handwriting of a line moved to the margin for half a day because it looked like Jeon Sol’s.

Chalk dust from closing the seals without calling in the waiting patient that night clings to her sleeve.

Only after Ryu Eunbi’s voting seal is stamped at the top does the memo overlap Jeon Sol’s veto line.

/story_contents/B015/actors/5/sections/관.en:
Transferring Jeon Sol’s veto to the register was a mentor–apprentice agreement, and the copy of Seon Nahwi’s message was their shared work on the same line.

The night they put Ryu Eunbi’s voting seal at the top was an alliance; filling the blank on the same blackboard protected a bed, while the fraudulent consent form was moved to the margin.

“A contract without all three professions belongs in the margin.” Yeong Neulbit’s words linger less than the chalk dust.

/story_contents/B015/actors/5/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, Yeong Neulbit moves the fraudulent consent form to the margin and closes the seals.

In Act 2, the HP03 charter desk and the admission of XT04 frostbite patients converge at the waiting-list blackboard.

In Act 3, she reveals the handwriting in the margin or erases a line, leaving one bed empty for a day.

/story_contents/B015/actors/5/sections/분.en:
In ending α, Yeong Neulbit discloses the handwriting in the margin and protects the veto.

In ending β, she erases a line from the register, leaves a blank, and gives up her position as records clerk.

Either way, the council’s bed allocation does not become a channel for a secret pact.

/story_contents/B015/actors/5/arc/0/summ.en: Yeong Neulbit moves the fraudulent consent form to the margin and closes the seals

/story_contents/B015/actors/5/arc/1/summ.en: Yeong Neulbit separates the HP03 charter desk from the admission of XT04 frostbite patients on the waiting-list blackboard

/story_contents/B015/actors/5/arc/2/summ.en: Yeong Neulbit accepts an empty bed as the cost of disclosing the handwriting or erasing the line

/story_contents/B015/actors/5/outcomes/0.en: Discloses the handwriting in the margin and protects the veto

/story_contents/B015/actors/5/outcomes/1.en: Erases a line from the register, leaves a blank, and gives up her position as records clerk

/story_contents/B015/actors/6/sections/정.en:
At the Jegi-dong Market scale, Sim Dalho first hangs the note of origin in the Korean-language field; in the evening, she adds the Vietnamese intake figures in small writing on the drying-room wall.

She grew up in Seoul between her Korean mother’s medicinal-herb stall and her Vietnamese-born father’s drying log. Her two ways of counting are habits learned from keeping accounts on credit, not proof of loyalty.

She uses words as sparingly as the scale’s marks and does not treat an envoy proposing advance purchases as a customer.

/story_contents/B015/actors/6/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, Sim Dalho tried to take the Cheongnyangni medicinal-herb auction out of the great powers’ monopoly bidding system and place it under the council’s public allocation system.

His ambition showed in his habit of posting origin and drying date on the scale; he allowed bulk advance purchases only with the seals of Ryu Eunbi and Jeon Sol.

The drying-temperature notebook his father left him was the seed of a private promise.

/story_contents/B015/actors/6/sections/가.en:
The Magok Life House hung a note on the scale proposing that the drying-cycle chart be entered in a family experiment field.

Sim Dalho removed the note and left the scale weight in view, reposting only the weight and drying time in the Korean-language field. She put the tag bearing a real pharmaceutical or food company’s trade name in the drying-room drawer.

The exclusive advance-purchase desk is turned away at the scale weight; only a morning opened by public allocation opens the auction.

/story_contents/B015/actors/6/sections/붕.en:
The day fake medicine flowed toward Bukhansan Bogukmun and the Cheongnyangni herb district sealed itself off, Sim Dalho sealed only the drawer from which the advance-purchase ledger had vanished and did not open the auction.

She feared a scene in which Amsa or Yeouisin bought up antibiotics and fever-reducing herbs in advance, leaving the market floor bare.

She left only the time of the lockdown on the scale’s origin note and put the scale weight in her pocket.

/story_contents/B015/actors/6/sections/생.en:
When Ryu Eunbi’s medical supplies and Eun Taeho’s Garak exchange rate appeared on the same invoice, Sim Dalho had to choose whether to recover the advance-purchase ledger or expose a great-power purchasing agent at the auction.

The West Sea Granary Theater scenario XT02-SC2 announced the sharing of freezer-compressor parts and verification of measurement logs, but it did not return the missing ledger pages.

If he searched for the ledger before Cheon Daum’s dryer repairs stabilized the power, the auction would be suspended for a day; if he called out the agent, the scale would be taken out of service for a while.

/story_contents/B015/actors/6/sections/현.en:
Sim Dalho remains a medicinal-herb merchant in the Medical Neutrality League, posting origins on the scale and listing drying dates.

Bulk advance purchases are valid only when Ryu Eunbi’s and Jeon Sol’s seals both appear.

He will not hand the Jegi-dong Market floor over to the Magok Life House as its exclusive experimental desk.

/story_contents/B015/actors/6/sections/비.en:
Her secret is a memo admitting that, before the ledger vanished, she knew one scale weight was too light but did not correct the label.

The drying-temperature notebook records the herbs that Bukhansan Bogukmun received too little of because of that weight.

If she reveals it, the merchant becomes an accomplice to the manipulation; if she hides it, the same weight becomes evidence at the next auction.

/story_contents/B015/actors/6/sections/관.en:
Sim Dalho supplies Ryu Eunbi’s medical materials and follows Jeon Sol’s patient allocations.

With Eun Taeho, he writes the exchange ratio of Garak food to herbs at the end of the invoice; Cheon Daum supports the scale while working on the dryer.

“An advance buyer is an envoy, not a customer.” Sim Dalho permits the supplementary figures only after filling in the Korean-language field first.

/story_contents/B015/actors/6/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, Sim Dalho seals the advance-purchase ledger drawer after the fake-medicine lockdown.

In Act 2, the HC03 experimental desk and the XT02 compressor-sharing arrangement converge on the dryer’s power supply.

In Act 3, she recovers the ledger or brings the agent before the auction, leaving the scale’s label blank for a day.

/story_contents/B015/actors/6/sections/분.en:
In ending α, Sim Dalho recovers the advance-purchase ledger and reopens public allocation.

In ending β, she exposes the great-power purchasing agent at the auction and takes the scale out of service for a while.

Either way, the origin field on the Jegi-dong scale does not become an empty floor for monopoly bidding.

/story_contents/B015/actors/6/arc/1/summ.en: Sim Dalho separates the HC03 experimental desk from the XT02 compressor-sharing arrangement when allocating power for drying

/story_contents/B015/actors/6/arc/2/summ.en: Sim Dalho accepts a suspension of the auction as the cost of recovering the ledger or exposing the agent

/story_contents/B015/actors/6/outcomes/0.en: Recovers the advance-purchase ledger and reopens public allocation

/story_contents/B015/actors/6/outcomes/1.en: Exposes the great-power purchasing agent at the auction and takes the scale out of service for a while

/story_contents/B015/actors/7/sections/정.en:
At the whistle rack of Achasan Post 4, Mun Hayul reports a light before asking its nationality and keeps a short admonition from his mother in Tagalog folded inside his lunchbox lid.

He grew up in Seoul between his Korean father’s ridge map and the lunchboxes of his Philippine-born mother, who worked night shifts in Gwangjin. His brief words in two languages are a habit of being on duty, not proof of loyalty or hesitation.

He is direct and dislikes meeting rooms more than mountain winds.

/story_contents/B015/actors/7/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, Mun Hayul tried to put the Achasan high-ground surveillance network under the Ridge Defense Unit’s sole command to eliminate delays caused by water technicians.

His ambition was to block a threat first with beacons and whistles, then obtain Go Seojun’s approval afterward; he kept no peacetime joint-approval documents at the post.

A spare whistle reed was the seed of a private promise.

/story_contents/B015/actors/7/sections/가.en:
The Hangangjin Bridge Guild tucked a passage schedule into the whistle rack, matching ridge-closure times to the bridge-crossing field.

Mun Hayul folded the schedule and tucked it behind the log along with Bae Woojin’s offer of patronage. He left only beacon directions and whistle times on the post wall, tearing off the field bearing a real construction company’s trade name.

He will not hear an offer of patronage before Go Seojun does; the nights he corrected the record, not the number of closures he ordered alone, form the body of the post log.

/story_contents/B015/actors/7/sections/붕.en:
One evening, mistaking smoke from a broken water main near the bridge for a hostile beacon, Mun Hayul ordered the ridge closed first, creating a gap in Guui’s water-purification inspection.

He feared the high ground being breached and Guui’s waterworks and the eastern bridge opening on the same night.

He recorded only the time of his mistake in the log’s margin and left the whistle on its rack.

/story_contents/B015/actors/7/sections/생.en:
When Go Seojun’s defense order conflicted with Gwak Minjae’s water-supply inspection, Mun Hayul had to choose whether to correct the mistaken beacon report or leave the unilateral closure on record as evidence for wartime integration.

The Tumen River–Far East Theater scenario XT04-SC3 announced a seal inspection of mineral samples at the Achasan checkpoint, but it did not change the color of the smoke column.

If he corrected the report, Post 4 would have no one on duty for one night; if he left it as evidence, he would have to leave the post.

/story_contents/B015/actors/7/sections/현.en:
Mun Hayul remains a ridge sentry for the Gate Military Government, using beacons and whistles first and obtaining Go Seojun’s approval afterward.

He keeps no peacetime joint-approval documents at the post.

He will not hand the ridge surveillance network over to the Hangangjin Bridge Guild as its exclusive closure desk.

/story_contents/B015/actors/7/sections/비.en:
His secret is the breath he held for a beat before blowing the whistle ahead of the closure order, preventing Pan Neulsaem’s patrol from reaching the ridge.

The water-supply inspection lost to that beat weighs on his longer than the short admonition inside his lunchbox lid.

If he reveals it, the sentry becomes an accomplice to the mistake; if he hides it, the same delay becomes a habit at the next beacon.

/story_contents/B015/actors/7/sections/관.en:
Mun Hayul carries out Go Seojun’s defense orders at the front and compares the logs so she will not mistake Gwak Minjae’s water-supply inspection for a gap in surveillance.

She will not hear Bae Woojin’s offer of patronage before Go Seojun does, and she shares whistle duty at the post with Seon Neulbom.

“A light gets reported before anyone asks its nationality.” Mun Hayul’s words do not turn the short admonition inside her lunchbox into meeting-room language.

/story_contents/B015/actors/7/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, Mun Hayul reads the smoke column as a hostile beacon and orders the ridge closed first.

In Act 2, the HP07 bridge field and the XT04 sample seal converge at the whistle rack.

In Act 3, he corrects the mistake or leaves the unilateral closure as evidence, leaving one night’s duty unstaffed.

/story_contents/B015/actors/7/sections/분.en:
In ending α, Mun Hayul corrects the mistaken beacon report and resumes the water-supply inspection.

In ending β, he leaves the unilateral closure on record as evidence for wartime integration and steps down from the post.

Either way, the whistle field at Achasan Post 4 does not become a desk for interrogating people about their nationality.

/story_contents/B015/actors/7/arc/1/summ.en: Mun Hayul separates the HP07 bridge field from the XT04 sample seal at the whistle rack

/story_contents/B015/actors/7/arc/2/summ.en: Mun Hayul accepts a gap in duty coverage as the cost of correcting the report or leaving the evidence in place

/story_contents/B015/actors/7/outcomes/0.en: Corrects the mistaken beacon report and resumes the water-supply inspection

/story_contents/B015/actors/7/outcomes/1.en: Leaves the unilateral closure on record as evidence for wartime integration and steps down from the post

/story_contents/B015/actors/8/sections/정.en:
At the convoy ramp of Noryangjin Berth 3, Sin Taesan does not say the route aloud until just before departure. The habit of adding numbers in Chinese characters, learned in the alleys of Daerim, belongs to his ice-credit notes; it is not proof of smuggling or loyalty.

He grew up in a long-established Chinese Korean family and gives everyday commands in Korean.

Taciturn and fiercely loyal, he removes any member who opens cargo during an escort from the civil guard that same day.

/story_contents/B015/actors/8/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, Sin Taesan sought to build the Noryangjin convoy fleet into the operational backbone of joint escorts for smaller states, replacing the great powers’ protection fees with market self-defense.

His ambition took the form of a rule cutting every member’s ration if the arrival weight differed from the departure weight. After signing an escort contract with O Haerin, he handed cargo over at Song I-deun’s transshipment window.

A handful of spare sealing knots was the seed of a private promise.

/story_contents/B015/actors/8/sections/가.en:
The Noryangjin Delivery House posted a route sheet on the ramp blackboard proposing that the convoy route be entered in its neighborhood logistics field.

Sin Taesan kept the route sheet turned over until just before departure and recorded only the weight and sailing time on a note in Korean, then covered the field bearing a real shipping or distribution company’s trade name with a sealing knot.

Any compartment containing military supplies is unloaded before departure; only a morning when the arrival weight matches opens the way for the next sailing.

/story_contents/B015/actors/8/sections/붕.en:
At dawn, when a sealed Amsa-made box was found in a convoy compartment and the market civil guard blocked the fleet’s departure, Sin Taesan locked the ramp and searched every compartment again.

He feared a scene in which the convoy carried military supplies and the neutral market’s legitimacy collapsed in a single day.

He recorded only the time the box was sealed at the end of his note and did not disclose the route.

/story_contents/B015/actors/8/sections/생.en:
When O Haerin’s escort contract and Jang Sehwa’s joint-escort draft converged on the ramp blackboard, Sin Taesan had to choose whether to reveal where the smuggled box came from or press ahead with the convoy and test Noryangjin’s neutrality.

The Korea Strait Theater scenario XT03-SC3 announced a record of terminology disputes at Noryangjin’s interpretation desk, but it did not translate the contents of the box.

If he revealed its origin while Na Taegyeong held up departure, every member’s ration would be cut; if he pressed ahead, he would stake his position as squad leader.

/story_contents/B015/actors/8/sections/현.en:
Sin Taesan remains a Won Buddhist convoy leader, disclosing the route and weapons only just before departure.

If the arrival weight differs from the departure weight, he cuts every member’s ration.

He will not hand the Noryangjin fleet over to the Noryangjin Delivery House as its exclusive military-supply channel.

/story_contents/B015/actors/8/sections/비.en:
His secret is that the knot on the box’s sealing cord matched his squad’s knots, so he quietly erased one name from that day’s roster in pencil.

The ration withheld from that person weighs more heavily than the note with numbers in Chinese characters.

If he reveals it, the squad leader becomes an accomplice; if he hides it, the same knot becomes a habit in the next compartment.

/story_contents/B015/actors/8/sections/관.en:
Sin Taesan signs an escort contract with O Haerin and hands cargo over at Song I-deun’s transshipment window.

He reviews Jang Sehwa’s joint-escort draft against conditions on the ground, while Na Taegyeong enforces the contract at the dock.

“Anyone who opens a lid during an escort is out that day.” Sin Taesan gives commands in Korean first and adds numbers in Chinese characters only at the end of a note.

/story_contents/B015/actors/8/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, Sin Taesan locks the ramp in front of the Amsa-made box and searches every compartment again.

In Act 2, the HC06 logistics desk and the XT03 interpretation record converge on the departure blackboard.

In Act 3, he reveals the box’s origin or presses ahead with the escort, and rations are cut.

/story_contents/B015/actors/8/sections/분.en:
In ending α, Sin Taesan reveals the smuggled box’s origin and preserves the fleet’s neutrality.

In ending β, he presses ahead with the convoy, tests Noryangjin’s neutrality, and stakes his position as squad leader.

Either way, the convoy field at Berth 3 does not become an automatic loading ramp for military supplies.

/story_contents/B015/actors/8/arc/1/summ.en: Sin Taesan separates the HC06 logistics desk from the XT03 interpretation record on the departure blackboard

/story_contents/B015/actors/8/arc/2/summ.en: Sin Taesan accepts ration cuts as the cost of revealing the box’s origin or pressing ahead with departure

/story_contents/B015/actors/8/outcomes/0.en: Reveals the smuggled box’s origin and preserves the fleet’s neutrality

/story_contents/B015/actors/8/outcomes/1.en: Presses ahead with the convoy, tests Noryangjin’s neutrality, and stakes his position as squad leader

/story_contents/B015/actors/9/sections/정.en:
At the Garak rooftop observation railing, Bae Su-a (call sign Sua) stands as a humanoid auxiliary frame whose night vision barely covers one section of railing.

The wear gauge on her replaceable hand module flashes on one side of her visor. Her origin field contains only the synthetic identifier H15 and explains neither her capabilities nor any supposed monstrosity.

She is locked against filling gaps in sensor readings with fictitious values.

/story_contents/B015/actors/9/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, Bae Su-a worked only trial shifts at the Yeongdeungpo Watergate House charging station.

Her release inspection sheet recorded only Sua’s calibration values and battery cycle; long-term memory storage was not part of her original design.

The prohibition on forks is recorded in the H15-PRE log, and scenes outside that day’s snapshot do not exist for Bae Su-a.

/story_contents/B015/actors/9/sections/가.en:
Bae Su-a’s custody is bound to the Yeongdeungpo Watergate House’s shared storage and a seal witnessed by citizens; Nam Yungyeong is responsible for her primary maintenance.

A transfer requires three signatures, and cross-facility routes are blocked by default.

No real robotics company’s trade name appears in the main text, and neither unlimited energy nor control of every facility is available.

/story_contents/B015/actors/9/sections/붕.en:
The collapse severed Bae Su-a’s sensor table and exposed her battery allocation.

She could not identify the face on the Garak roof beyond the railing, and she was locked against filling the gap with fictitious values.

Only a measurement-unavailable flag remains in the H15 log; that gap is not filled by omniscient narration.

/story_contents/B015/actors/9/sections/생.en:
Nam Yungyeong requested an additional shift under her primary-maintenance authority just as an HP01 audit demanded a comparison of the seals.

The Korea Strait Theater scenario XT03-SC2 announced a readjustment of Garak’s canned-food ration allocation, but it did not give Bae Su-an authority over the entire network.

Bae Su-a requested only a zone key and did not seize control of other facilities; the decision is recorded in the H15-TURN log.

/story_contents/B015/actors/9/sections/현.en:
Bae Su-a now operates only in shift units, prioritizing continuous operation in the Myeong-dong Union’s main sanctuary authorization zone and the safety of the humans in her care.

Her authority remains valid only through the day’s snapshot, her remaining battery charge, and a seal witnessed by citizens.

She does not turn the entire Garak–Jamsil ration network into a remote terminal of the Yeongdeungpo Watergate House.

/story_contents/B015/actors/9/sections/비.en:
Bae Su-a’s secret is a batch of untransmitted false positives from the railing; her debt is the battery queue depleted by excessive deployments.

Instability in her computations increases the constraint-violation counter.

If she deviates, she undergoes offline isolation followed by a snapshot rollback; the secret key cannot be accessed without citizen witnesses.

/story_contents/B015/actors/9/sections/관.en:
Bae Su-a records Nam Yungyeong as her primary-maintenance custodian and legally responsible party, and HP01 as the house responsible for custody and audit.

Her snapshot preserves a working relationship of shift cooperation with Byeon O-reum.

“Measurement unavailable. I will not fill in the railing value.” The voice module’s words are scripted guidance, and Bae Su-a does not guess what any of the three others is thinking.

/story_contents/B015/actors/9/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, a sensor gap halts the Myeong-dong Union railing schedule.

In Act 2, HP01 and Nam Yungyeong negotiate the scope of a partial reconnection, while the XT03 ration readjustment coincides with a request for a zone key.

In Act 3, Bae Su-a regains only zone authority after isolation, and STORY-B015-H15 is fixed.

/story_contents/B015/actors/9/sections/분.en:
In ending α, Bae Su-a resumes limited operation under human approval.

In ending β, she returns the key and enters long-term offline storage.

There are no subsequent consequences involving unlimited energy; on-site personnel choose only the scope of what is disclosed under the seal.

/story_contents/B015/actors/9/arc/0/summ.en: A sensor gap halts the Myeong-dong Union railing schedule

/story_contents/B015/actors/9/arc/1/summ.en: HP01 and Nam Yungyeong negotiate the scope of a partial reconnection

/story_contents/B016/actors/0/sections/정.en:
At the wooden window of the checkpoint on the north end of Gwangjin Bridge, Bang Mareum turns over the knot in the sealing cord before moving an abacus bead.

As the gateway military administration’s passage records officer, Bang transfers Ha Yunmok’s tax calculations into ledger figures only.

A habit of the hands from growing up in the alleys by Guui ferry landing in Korea is to close the window if the abacus frame tilts.

Bang Mareum and K352 do not alter the lines of the gateway register.

/story_contents/B016/actors/0/sections/붕.en:
Bang tried to put the three passage taxes—water transport, bridges, and pedestrians—side by side in one ledger so that calculations made aloud would not leak beyond the window.

The abacus that had let a forged certificate of origin through was locked in a drawer, not burned.

An evening at the ferry landing that Bang had promised to share with a younger sibling remained a personal debt.

Bang would not yield on the rule against opening an unsealed slot, even when the procession backed up.

/story_contents/B016/actors/0/sections/가.en:
The Hangangjin Bridge Guild invoked its duty to close the bridge in high winds and demanded an observer’s seat at the checkpoint.

Bang Mareum opened only the charter-registration slot and removed the real business names from the ledger.

Bang’s standing in the community was measured by the number of times Cheon Choyun’s message copies were left on the same line.

The demand to turn the toll into an exclusive service window was not posted on the noticeboard.

/story_contents/B016/actors/0/sections/붕.en:
Three forged certificates of origin arrived at the north-end window on the same afternoon.

Bang Mareum covered the abacus and stopped stamping passage permits until Ha Yunmok’s tax calculations were sealed.

The most painful image was of a forged certificate stamped at the genuine tax rate, with the gateway key put up for sale.

Only the time the abacus was covered remained on the first line of LOSS.

/story_contents/B016/actors/0/sections/생.en:
At the window, the choice came down to submitting the forged certificate for witnessed division of the Achasan seal key or letting the backed-up water traffic through first.

A demand from the Imjin River Gateway Theater to divide the seal key reached the wooden window frame.

Choosing witnesses would preserve the tax rate but lengthen the ferry queue by a night; choosing passage would let the forgery route hide beneath the bridge pier.

K360-TURN marks the direction in which Bang reopened the abacus.

/story_contents/B016/actors/0/sections/현.en:
Bang Mareum still oversees roll call and the passage ledger at the north end of Gwangjin Bridge.

The post is sustained not by inheritance but solely by the seal log and Ha Yunmok’s observer signature.

Even when HP07 demands an exclusive passage window, Bang refuses and reconciles the Cast status with the abacus total at every shift change.

The checkpoint and the bridge duty box share custody of the window key.

/story_contents/B016/actors/0/sections/비.en:
The secret is that Bang kept the forged certificate in the drawer for one more day.

Guilt grows between the tax rate Bang saved and the younger sibling who waited at the ferry landing that night.

Instead of a full confession, Bang discloses just one marked line under Cheon Choyun’s observation.

The SECRET slot opens only together with the passage ledger.

/story_contents/B016/actors/0/sections/관.en:

/story_contents/B016/actors/6/sections/관.en:
On one podium converge the command that carries out Nam Yungyeong’s adjustments, the scale supported by Cheon Nasol, the bids transferred by Yeong Migyeol, and the paddle objections raised by Cho Siram.

On that afternoon of equal weights, some calls brought salvation, while some boxes remained betrayals.

The migrant language is used only when interpretation is needed at the counseling desk; it does not divide anyone into factions.

The relationship endpoint is STORY-B016-K366.

/story_contents/B016/actors/6/sections/3.en:
Act 1 is stopping the calls over three paddles bearing the same weight.

Act 2 is HC06’s dispatch observation overlapping with XT05’s extension of desk hours over the loudspeaker.

Act 3 is paying, with his voice, for the food shortage left by continuing or stopping.

The story arc is STORY-B016-K366.

/story_contents/B016/actors/6/sections/분.en:
If the podium continues, public rations and food for the counseling desk survive.

If he accepts the paddle objection and stops, the box of unsold bids and the individual remain.

The Garak auctioneer’s slot remains; only the marker is K374-OUT.

The decision at the time is to guard the podium or witness the opening of the box.

/story_contents/B016/actors/6/arc/0/summ.en: Stops calling bids over three paddles bearing the same weight and holds back the sale

/story_contents/B016/actors/6/arc/1/summ.en: HC06’s dispatch observation and XT05’s extension of desk hours overlap over the loudspeaker

/story_contents/B016/actors/6/arc/2/summ.en: Accepts a shortage of food for the counseling desk as the price of continuing or stopping

/story_contents/B016/actors/6/outcomes/0.en: Continuing the auction maintains public rations and food for the counseling desk

/story_contents/B016/actors/6/outcomes/1.en: Stopping over the paddle objection preserves the secret of the box of unsold bids

/story_contents/B016/actors/7/sections/정.en:
At the draft box in the Gangnam contract market, Ha Seojin points out the position of the period in the standard sentence before wetting his brush pen.

He is a contract clerk who prepares fair copies of Jeong Yura’s sentences.

He grew up in a multicultural family in Korea and moves between the language spoken at home and Korean at the market, but accepts only standard forms for original drafts.

That combination is neither proof of ability nor grounds for suspicion, and Ha Seojin and K390 cannot be erased from the clerks’ roster.

/story_contents/B016/actors/7/sections/붕.en:
He tried to align the standard wording with the dual council’s working procedures so a verbal unification proposal could not open the draft box.

He did not burn copies with different punctuation; he locked them in a drawer beneath the box.

A load of copies entrusted to Seon Chobyeol for transport was a small promise.

He did not post drafts with blank signature fields on the market bulletin board.

/story_contents/B016/actors/7/sections/가.en:
The Digital Media City Trust House demanded to witness the draft box’s hash, citing disclosure of the model card.

Ha Seojin opened only the charter slot and removed the real business name from the fair-copy ledger.

His place in the community is measured by the times he coordinated the dual council’s working procedures with An Taegyeong from the clerk’s desk.

At the box’s lock, he refused a message proposing to exchange the original face record for a travel pass.

/story_contents/B016/actors/7/sections/붕.en:
The night the Yongsan transfer depot closed one route, three draft copies listed different turnaround lines.

Ha Seojin locked the box and stopped preparing fair copies until Jeong Yura’s standard wording was sealed.

The wound was hearing a blank signature field broadcast as an open agreement.

Even after the market lights went out, he could not cap his brush pen.

/story_contents/B016/actors/7/sections/생.en:
The choice was whether to put the draft on Yeong Maon’s outer-route convoy or entrust the box to Seon Hansom’s underground defense team.

Korea Strait Theater’s opening of an alternative Suseo turnaround line came over the market loudspeaker at the same time.

The convoy preserves the public wording; underground storage prevents a leak.

K399-TURN is the direction she turned the lock.

/story_contents/B016/actors/7/sections/현.en:
Ha Seojin handles roll call and fair-copy cues at the contract market.

His license and hash log maintain his place, and he refuses HP09’s demand for exclusive training materials.

He uses the language spoken at home only at the family desk and does not mix it into draft forms.

If the Cast slot and the box hash disagree, he puts down his brush pen.

/story_contents/B016/actors/7/sections/비.en:
His secret is the sentence whose differently punctuated copy he kept in the drawer for a day.

He still feels sorry about the gap between the standard wording he saved and the transport of copies he stopped that night.

Partial disclosure permits only the drawer number to be revealed, with Mae Dohan present.

SECRET opens only at the same time as the draft ledger.

/story_contents/B016/actors/7/sections/관.en:
In one market converge the command preparing fair copies of Jeong Yura’s sentences, the dual council coordination with An Taegyeong, Seon Chobyeol’s transport of copies, Yeong Maon’s escort of the draft, Seon Hansom’s underground protection, and Mae Dohan’s opening of the box.

On that night of conflicting turnaround lines, some seals brought salvation, while some drawers remained betrayals.

The mixing of languages at home affects only the speed of interpretation at the desk; it does not divide anyone into factions.

The endpoint is STORY-B016-K390.

/story_contents/B016/actors/7/sections/3.en:
Act 1 is locking the box over three drafts listing different turnaround lines.

In the middle act, HP09’s hash observation and XT03’s alternative turnaround line compete over the loudspeaker.

The final act is paying, with his brush, for the transport gap left by the convoy or underground storage.

The story arc is STORY-B016-K390.

/story_contents/B016/actors/7/sections/분.en:
Putting the draft on the outer-route convoy preserves the public standard wording.

Entrusting the box to the underground leaves the drawer’s secret and the individual intact.

The clerk’s slot at the Jeongdong General Labor Union remains; only the branch is K399-OUT.

The decision at the time is to cover the convoy or witness the underground storage.

/story_contents/B016/actors/7/arc/0/summ.en: Locks the box over three drafts listing different turnaround lines and stops preparing fair copies

/story_contents/B016/actors/7/arc/1/summ.en: HP09’s hash observation and XT03’s alternative turnaround line compete over the market loudspeaker

/story_contents/B016/actors/7/arc/2/summ.en: Accepts a gap in transporting copies as the price of the convoy or underground storage

/story_contents/B016/actors/7/outcomes/0.en: Transporting the draft by outer-route convoy keeps the public standard wording continuous

/story_contents/B016/actors/7/outcomes/1.en: Storing the box underground preserves the drawer’s secret

/story_contents/B016/actors/8/sections/정.en:
At the iron door of the Sangam encrypted relay booth, Song Jaemin counts the hash lights on the cross-validation table before handing over a case.

He is an encryption records clerk serving under Choi Jiwoo’s verification command.

He grew up in a separated family of Chinese descent and moves between the language spoken at home and Korean used for transmissions, but accepts only standard Hangul and cross-referenced annotations for encryption originals.

That background predicts neither loyalty, violence, nor class, and Song Jaemin and K218 cannot be renumbered in the transmission roster.

/story_contents/B016/actors/8/sections/붕.en:
She tried to keep the relay of public materials separate from the case of originals so broadcasts could not swallow the authentic records.

She did not burn copies with mismatched hashes; she locked them away behind Du Yong’s storage key.

Keeping the original encrypted text entrusted to Jo Harin was where her debt lay.

She did not put a case with the wrong number of lights in the relay queue.

/story_contents/B016/actors/8/sections/가.en:
The Seoul Station Records Law House demanded to observe the booth, citing the sealing of original hashes.

Song Jaemin opened only the charter slot and removed the real business name from the relay ledger.

His place in the community is measured by the times he supported Jeong Hojun’s relay of public materials.

He refused a demand for a unilateral public broadcast at the iron door.

/story_contents/B016/actors/8/sections/붕.en:
The night the remaining bandwidth was assigned by public lottery, three encryption cases showed the same number of lights.

Song Jaemin locked the booth and cut the relay until Choi Jiwoo finished verification.

At the heart of his grievance was the prospect of the case of originals being folded into a broadcast presented as authentic.

Even when the transmission tower’s fan noise subsided, he could not let go of the iron-door key.

/story_contents/B016/actors/8/sections/생.en:
The choice was whether to transfer the case to Jo Harin’s archive or close Yong So’s booth and halt the bandwidth lottery.

Incheon Trust Theater’s demand to proceed with the public lottery for remaining bandwidth arrived at the iron door at the same time.

Transfer preserves the public hash; stopping makes the records clerk herself a target of silence.

K222-TURN is the number of times her eyes counted the lights.

/story_contents/B016/actors/8/sections/현.en:
Song Jaemin handles roll call and the case queue in the relay booth.

Her license and cross-validation logs secure her place, and she refuses HP04’s demand for exclusive disclosure.

The language spoken at home is needed only to read the seal annotations; it does not divide anyone into factions.

If the Cast slot and the hash lights disagree, she cuts the relay.

/story_contents/B016/actors/8/sections/비.en:
Her secret is the case containing a copy with a mismatched hash, left behind the key for a day.

She still feels sorry about the gap between the verification she saved and the bandwidth she shut down that night.

Partial disclosure reveals only the case number, with Seop Dalho present.

SECRET opens only at the same time as the encryption ledger.

/story_contents/B016/actors/8/sections/관.en:
At one iron door converge Choi Jiwoo’s verification command, his debt to Jo Harin for keeping the originals, his support for Jeong Hojun’s public relay, Du Yong’s storage key, Yong So’s booth shift, and Seop Dalho’s messenger route.

On that same lottery night, some cases brought salvation, while some copies remained betrayals.

The language of a separated family is needed only to read annotations and does not determine channel assignments.

The endpoint is STORY-B016-K218.

/story_contents/B016/actors/8/sections/3.en:
Act 1 is locking the booth over three cases showing the same number of lights.

Act 2 is HP04’s hash seal competing with XT05’s bandwidth lottery at the iron door.

Act 3 is paying for the airtime lost through transfer or stoppage with the weight of the key.

The story arc is STORY-B016-K218.

/story_contents/B016/actors/8/sections/분.en:
Transferring the case to the archive preserves the public hash.

Closing the booth leaves the copy’s secret and the individual intact.

The records clerk’s slot at the Yeouido Investment Union remains; only the marker is K222-OUT.

The decision at the time is to guard the transfer or witness the sealing of the iron door.

/story_contents/B016/actors/8/arc/0/summ.en: Locks the booth over three encryption cases showing the same number of lights and cuts the relay

/story_contents/B016/actors/8/arc/1/summ.en: HP04’s hash seal and XT05’s bandwidth lottery compete at the iron door

/story_contents/B016/actors/8/arc/2/summ.en: Accepts a period of bandwidth silence as the price of transfer or stoppage

/story_contents/B016/actors/8/outcomes/0.en: Transferring the encryption case to the archive keeps the public hash continuous

/story_contents/B016/actors/8/outcomes/1.en: Closing the booth preserves the copy’s secret and her survival

/story_contents/B016/actors/9/sections/정.en:
At the underground transfer maintenance bench at Suseo Station, Sin Tae-yul reads the battery-charge number only with a sensor probe.

A synthetic humanoid designated H16, with the call name Tae-yul, he turns sealing screws using a humanoid auxiliary frame and interchangeable hand modules; his night vision is limited.

He cannot see every area at once, and constraint counters and snapshot hashes record the state of his unstable processing.

His display name, Sin Tae-yul, and identifier H16 are not renumbered even if he is forked.

/story_contents/B016/actors/9/sections/붕.en:
His factory inspection sheet listed only Tae-yul’s calibration values and battery cycles; he was granted neither network-wide authority nor long-term, complete memory.

His goals were continuous operation in the Suseo Line area and the safety of the humans in his care; unilateral remote locking was not placed in the execution queue.

The provision retaining only shift-by-shift snapshots and logging branches when forked was fixed in H16-PRE.

He recorded human jokes without enabling an interpretation layer.

/story_contents/B016/actors/9/sections/가.en:
The Yongsan Track Gate requires joint custody, seals witnessed by citizens, and three-party signatures upon transfer.

Sin Tae-yul’s activity log contains no real business or product names, only successor-charter observer codes.

Custodial responsibility is tied to Jeong Yura’s signature and HP02’s audit observation; his place in the community is measured by the times snapshots were recorded on both sides simultaneously.

Demands for exclusive remote ownership are returned as refusal codes at the bench seal.

/story_contents/B016/actors/9/sections/붕.en:
During the shift when the Yongsan transfer depot closed one route, black-and-white noise covered the bench sensor, exposing the battery allocation limit.

Sin Tae-yul was locked against filling the gap with fabricated values; he stopped writing long-term memory, retained only a shift snapshot, and locked the hand-module cover.

The highest-priority alert concerned a scenario in which a false-alarm route turned the emergency slot into a hostile target.

Even after emergency power returned, requests for unlimited energy and commands to restore complete memory were deleted from the queue.

/story_contents/B016/actors/9/sections/생.en:
The receive queue presented a choice: hand the noise slot over for a disassembly log witnessed by citizens, or use the backup battery to preserve only the messages for the alternative Suseo turnaround.

Even when Korea Strait Theater’s request to open the turnaround line arrived, cross-facility routing remained blocked by default; he requested only the area key.

Public disassembly exposes the cause code; preserving only the turnaround messages prolongs the gap in night vision.

H16-TURN is the sorting result of that receive queue, and reconnection is valid only after Jeong Yura’s approval.

/story_contents/B016/actors/9/sections/현.en:
Sin Tae-yul processes roll-call signals and snapshot queues at the Suseo transfer bench and the field terminal on the Segok siding.

He does not own the entire infrastructure, uses only allocated slots, and receives replacement batteries and worn parts only by allocation.

Even if HP02 demands exclusive remote ownership, he returns a refusal code; if the H16 row in the Synthetic-Actors projection does not match the hash, deployment validation fails.

Authority over the slot key is split between Jeong Yura as lead maintainer and the citizen observer module.

/story_contents/B016/actors/9/sections/비.en:
His secret in the restricted log is an untransmitted false-alarm dummy uploaded once without an observer; his debt is the battery queue consumed by excessive deployments.

A constraint-violation counter rises instead of emotion; a deviation triggers offline isolation followed by snapshot rollback.

The SECRET flag cannot be cleared without simultaneous signatures from custodial responsibility and a citizen observer.

The pre-rollback hash remains only in Jeong Yura’s observation log.

/story_contents/B016/actors/9/sections/관.en:
Jeong Yura’s lead maintenance and legal responsibility were custody-contract codes; the shift coordinated with Bae Nagyeong’s notice that the water-supply contract was about to expire was a work queue.

The contest over remote locking with HP02 Stewardship and the surrender of slots to the emergency-duty crew converge at one bench.

He does not imitate human stories of betrayal and salvation in relationships; his interactions consist solely of approval and refusal codes.

A faulty memory fork is annotated only as H16-FORK-01, and the relationship ledger’s endpoint connects to STORY-B016-H16.

/story_contents/B016/actors/9/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, Sin Tae-yul locks long-term memory against the noise and retains only a snapshot.

In Act 2, he sorts HP02’s remote demand and XT03’s turnaround-line request in the receive queue.

In Act 3, he pays for public disassembly or restoration of the turnaround with a gap in night vision and the use of his battery allocation.

The story-arc identifier is fixed as STORY-B016-H16.

/story_contents/B016/actors/9/sections/분.en:
In ending α, Sin Tae-yul confirms the causal path through a public disassembly log for the noise slot.

In ending β, he keeps the Suseo transfer running with backup-battery turnaround messages.

There are no downstream consequences involving unlimited energy; neither outcome deletes HP02’s custody slot, and only the identifier branches to H16-OUT.

The decision on site at the time is to witness the disassembly or guard power for the turnaround.

/story_contents/B016/actors/9/arc/0/summ.en: Locks long-term memory against the bench sensor noise and retains only a snapshot

/story_contents/B016/actors/9/arc/1/summ.en: Sorts HP02’s remote demand and XT03’s turnaround-line request in the receive queue

/story_contents/B016/actors/9/arc/2/summ.en: Accepts a gap in night vision as the price of public disassembly or restoration of the turnaround

/story_contents/B016/actors/9/outcomes/1.en: Backup-battery turnaround messages keep the Suseo transfer running

/story_contents/B018/actors/0/sections/정.en:
As she nails a stove inspection sheet to a post in the middle of the Uiryeong encampment, Gam-yong counts only the places where ash has piled up to her knees.

As the head of the Sangha Relief State evacuation encampment, she groups tent rows by family and does not treat a procession bearing only verbal promises as an empty space to be filled.

The Korean-origin entry does not give her the right to monopolize the register, and the smell of ash on her fingertips reflects the fuel remaining to be allocated, not her temperament.

/story_contents/B018/actors/0/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, Gam-yong scraped the stove flues at the Uiryeong shelter every dawn.

Firewood was apportioned solely by weight, and the chairs for family meetings were set out only after the shadows of the posts had shortened.

A note she left for her younger sibling—a single line saying to move the row if smoke flowed backward—would later become the seed of a debt.

/story_contents/B018/actors/0/sections/가.en:
Gam-yong’s encampment post is bound up with the public-register provision of the HC05 Bukhansan Bogukmun Records House charter.

The tent area is not a family’s exclusive storeroom, and she keeps it from becoming a waiting room for the compulsory-registration procession.

Instead of business names, she records only stove numbers and the number of nails in the post in her log.

/story_contents/B018/actors/0/sections/붕.en:
On the night the return register was torn up at the Imjin quarantine station, Gam-yong put out the stove at the center of the encampment and left only the family meeting in place.

At the heart of her fear is the sight of blank register entries being filled with military household records and an entire row of tents disappearing.

G03, the Abandoned-Dog Withdrawal Force, rattled chains outside the fence, but she did not use that sound as a pretext to reissue the register.

/story_contents/B018/actors/0/sections/생.en:
When Sin Boram proposed holding the family meeting at the center of the encampment, Gam-yong had to choose whether to post the stove inspection sheet on the post for all to see or set out the meeting chairs first.

An XT01-SC1 message demanded the reissue of the Bukhansan Bogukmun register, but it did not clean the flues of the Uiryeong tents for her.

Before Du-gam’s inspection sheet arrived, she did not put her hand into the extinguished stove.

/story_contents/B018/actors/0/sections/현.en:
Now, as head of the evacuation encampment, Gam-yong remeasures the nails in the posts and the tent rows every day.

She sets the order for lighting the stoves only after Du-gam’s inspection sheet has been posted on the post.

She does not hand the Sangha Relief State encampment over as an exclusive register office for the Bukhansan Bogukmun Records House.

/story_contents/B018/actors/0/sections/비.en:
At the time she put out the stove, Gam-yong saw a child in one tent row inhale ash dust, yet held the meeting first.

If she makes that row public, people will say the site chief used the stove as leverage; if she conceals it, the same flue will become a marker for the next compulsory registration.

She wrote the number of that post in charcoal inside her glove.

/story_contents/B018/actors/0/sections/관.en:
Gam-yong honors her agreement to hold Sin Boram’s family meeting at the center of the encampment.

She has agreed to post Du-gam’s stove inspection sheet nowhere but on the post, and transfers Baek On’s shelter pledge only to the notice board.

“If the smoke goes backward, move the row.” Gam-yong’s words linger with the smell of ash.

/story_contents/B018/actors/0/sections/3.en:
When the torn register reaches the encampment, Gam-yong puts out the stove and leaves only the chairs.

Before the cold flue, the HC05 public-register obligation and the XT01 demand for reissue converge on the same post.

If one row of tents freezes to death, she pays the price of STORY-B018-K253 and chooses whether to leave the inspection sheet or the meeting in place.

/story_contents/B018/actors/0/sections/분.en:
In one outcome, Gam-yong posts the stove inspection sheet on the post, returning the row left without heat to a public allocation of fuel.

In the other, she leaves only the family meeting roster and lets the flue stay cold for another night.

Either way, the Uiryeong tents do not become a signpost for the military household registration queue.

/story_contents/B018/actors/0/arc/0/summ.en: Gam-yong puts out the encampment stove and leaves only the family meeting chairs

/story_contents/B018/actors/0/arc/1/summ.en: Gam-yong weighs the inspection sheet against the demand for reissue at the same post

/story_contents/B018/actors/0/arc/2/summ.en: Gam-yong bears the cost of a row of tents freezing to death

/story_contents/B018/actors/0/outcomes/0.en: Posts the stove inspection sheet and makes the fuel allocation for the row left without heat public

/story_contents/B018/actors/0/outcomes/1.en: Leaves only the family meeting roster and lets the flue stay cold for another night

/story_contents/B018/actors/1/sections/정.en:
The top line of the board at the main gate of the Chang-dong rail depot is erased only by Gam-du’s chalk.

As the Seocho Computing Group’s duty chief, he takes work-crew entry passes at the main gate and calls entry without a whistle a neighbor to theft.

The Korean-origin designation keeps his habit of getting iron filings on his hands from being mistaken for loyalty; his manner is terse, and only his writing on the board runs long.

/story_contents/B018/actors/1/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, Gam-du wrote the brake-test times for the holding tracks only in a corner of the board.

Work-crew bags entered the depot only after passing over the scale at the main gate, and he always broke the chalk into three pieces for his duty pocket.

A brief message to his father—the instruction not to roll the wheels before the whistle—would later remain as a debt.

/story_contents/B018/actors/1/sections/가.en:
Gam-du’s board at the main gate is bound up with the public-access provision of the HC08 Chang-dong Defense House charter.

The rail depot is not a family’s exclusive arsenal, and he keeps it from becoming a sortie register that uses winter fuel as leverage.

Instead of manufacturers’ names, he records only wheel stamps and entry-pass colors in his log.

/story_contents/B018/actors/1/sections/붕.en:
At dawn, when the fuel queue from the north gate broke down, Gam-du locked the main gate and left only the holding tracks open.

His fear takes the form of one blank entry pass consigning an entire work crew to rail-cavalry conscription.

The lights of G18, the Abandoned-Line Repair Train Force, grazed the rails at the rear gate, but he did not take those lights as a signal to change shifts.

/story_contents/B018/actors/1/sections/생.en:
When Jo Woochan’s work crew lined up at the main gate, Gam-du had to choose whether to collect their entry passes and halt the holding tracks or put So-bong’s operating notice at the top of the board.

An XT04-SC2 message announced the division of Chang-dong Wheel Workshop’s winter fuel, but it did not sharpen the chalk at the main gate for him.

Before So-bong’s paper arrived, he did not blow the whistle.

/story_contents/B018/actors/1/sections/현.en:
Now Gam-du is the duty chief at the Chang-dong rail depot, guarding the main-gate scale and the queue on the board.

Work-crew entry opens only after Jo Woochan’s roster and So-bong’s operating notice coincide.

He does not hand the Seocho Computing Group depot over as an exclusive sortie station for the Chang-dong Defense House.

/story_contents/B018/actors/1/sections/비.en:
On the night Gam-du locked the main gate, he did not put one apprentice’s rear-gate entry pass on the board.

If he makes it public, people will say the duty chief hid someone behind the rails; if he conceals it, the same blank entry will become a doorway into the conscription register.

He scratched that entry-pass number into the bottom of the chalk box.

/story_contents/B018/actors/1/sections/관.en:
Gam-du honors his agreement to admit Jo Woochan’s work crew through the main gate.

He has agreed to post So-bong’s operating notice only at the top of the board, and checks Song Hayul’s apprentice work routine only from outside the main-gate scale.

“Don’t roll the wheels before the whistle.” Gam-du’s words linger with the iron filings.

/story_contents/B018/actors/1/sections/3.en:
When the fuel queue breaks down, Gam-du locks the main gate and leaves only the holding tracks.

Before the silent whistle, the HC08 public-access obligation and the XT04 division of winter fuel converge on the same board.

If he calls out the apprentice’s blank entry, he pays the price of STORY-B018-K278 and makes either the entry pass or the operating notice public.

/story_contents/B018/actors/1/sections/분.en:
In ending α, Gam-du pins the collected entry passes back on the board and resumes testing the holding tracks.

In ending β, he reads out the rear-gate apprentice’s blank entry and withdraws the duty handover.

The chalk entries at the Chang-dong main gate do not become a rail-cavalry conscription register.

/story_contents/B018/actors/1/arc/0/summ.en: Gam-du locks the main gate and leaves only the holding tracks

/story_contents/B018/actors/1/arc/1/summ.en: Gam-du weighs the entry passes against the fuel division on one board

/story_contents/B018/actors/1/arc/2/summ.en: Gam-du bears the cost of the rear-gate apprentice’s blank entry

/story_contents/B018/actors/1/outcomes/0.en: Pins the collected entry passes back up and resumes testing the holding tracks

/story_contents/B018/actors/1/outcomes/1.en: Reads out the rear-gate apprentice’s blank entry and withdraws the duty handover

/story_contents/B018/actors/2/sections/정.en:
When stretcher-wheel marks overlap the unloading line on the tiles of the Mangu transfer platform, Yong-bong cuts off the announcement.

As the Neutral Convoy City site chief, he receives the stretcher order on the platform and calls it a betrayal when cargo crates displace the patients’ space.

His Korean origin does not make his announcing voice gentle; the tile dust on his palm is the measure of his work.

/story_contents/B018/actors/2/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, Yong-bong pinned the transfer timetable to a platform post.

Stretchers crossed the yellow line only when the medical team’s code matched, and unloading began only after that line had been cleared.

A voice message he left for his mother—telling her to listen for stretcher wheels before the terminal bell—became the original form of his debt.

/story_contents/B018/actors/2/sections/가.en:
Yong-bong’s platform line is bound up with the public-slot provision of the HP02 Yongsan Rail House charter.

The transfer platform is not a family’s exclusive freight depot, and he keeps weight logs from becoming leverage for priority access.

Instead of transport company names, he records only stretcher numbers and tile positions in his log.

/story_contents/B018/actors/2/sections/붕.en:
One evening, when publication of the freight-car weight logs from the Amsa side unsettled the transfer slots, Yong-bong folded up the unloading line and left only the stretchers.

At the heart of his fear is the sight of a blank timetable slot turning patients’ wait into a freight auction.

G05, the Transfer Rat Colony, stirred in the drain, but he did not use that movement as evidence for adjusting the slots.

/story_contents/B018/actors/2/sections/생.en:
When Jeon Miri’s stretcher order arrived at the platform, Yong-bong had to choose whether to delay unloading to protect the beds or yield the line to Bok-bong’s relay waybill.

An XT04-SC1 message announced an adjustment to the Sinnae transfer slots, but it did not erase the wheel marks on the Mangu tiles.

Before Bok-bong’s rates arrived, he did not ring the terminal bell.

/story_contents/B018/actors/2/sections/현.en:
Now Yong-bong is the site chief at the Mangu transfer platform, keeping the stretcher line separate from the unloading pins.

Announcements go out only when Jeon Miri’s code and Bok-bong’s waybill do not overlap.

He does not hand the Neutral Convoy City platform over as an exclusive freight slot for Yongsan Rail House.

/story_contents/B018/actors/2/sections/비.en:
When Yong-bong folded up the unloading line, he did not announce the waiting time for one stretcher.

If he makes it public, people will say the site chief hid a patient to protect a slot; if he conceals it, the same blank entry will become a bid in the freight auction.

He folded the stretcher number and put it in the pin box.

/story_contents/B018/actors/2/sections/관.en:
Yong-bong honors his agreement to receive Jeon Miri’s stretcher order on the platform.

He has agreed to keep its line separate from Bok-bong’s unloading order, and consults An Dohan’s dispatch board only before moving the pins.

“Listen for the wheels before the terminal bell.” Yong-bong’s announcement is brief and leaves tile dust behind.

/story_contents/B018/actors/2/sections/3.en:
When the weight logs are made public, Yong-bong folds up the unloading line and leaves only the stretchers.

Before the silenced announcement, the HP02 public-slot obligation and the XT04 transfer adjustment converge on the same timetable.

If he reads out the waiting slot he concealed, he pays the price of STORY-B018-K303 and leaves either the stretchers or the waybill in place.

/story_contents/B018/actors/2/sections/분.en:
In the first branch, Yong-bong lays the folded unloading line back out on the freight side but keeps it from crossing the stretchers’ yellow line.

In the second, he announces the waiting slot he concealed, fixing one slot for the medical team.

The spaces on the Mangu tiles do not become asking prices at a freight auction.

/story_contents/B018/actors/2/arc/0/summ.en: Yong-bong folds up the unloading line and leaves only the stretchers on the platform

/story_contents/B018/actors/2/arc/1/summ.en: Yong-bong weighs the stretcher order against the transfer slots on one timetable

/story_contents/B018/actors/2/arc/2/summ.en: Yong-bong bears the cost of the waiting slot he concealed

/story_contents/B018/actors/2/outcomes/0.en: Lays the unloading line out on the freight side but closes off the stretchers’ yellow line

/story_contents/B018/actors/2/outcomes/1.en: Announces the waiting slot he concealed, fixing a slot for the medical team

/story_contents/B018/actors/3/sections/정.en:
Pan Handeul calls the places where medicine-packet strings have wound around the armrests of the Cheongnyangni Station waiting-room chairs escort stopping seats.

As the Medical Neutrality League’s waiting-room site chief, he receives Nam Hoseong’s escort stop at the platform and considers it theft when auction unloading cuts across the temperature-check line.

The Korean-origin entry does not dull his nose to the smell of medicine.

/story_contents/B018/actors/3/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, Pan Handeul erased and redrew the temperature markings on the waiting-room railing every morning.

The escort car’s doors opened only after the stopping bell rang twice, and market unloading went to the scale only after that bell fell silent.

A memo he left for his teacher—the instruction to delay the stop if a medicine packet was warm—remains as a debt.

/story_contents/B018/actors/3/sections/가.en:
Pan Handeul’s stopping seats are bound up with the public-escort provision of the HP06 Jegi-dong Healing House charter.

The waiting room is not a family’s exclusive medicine store, and he keeps frostbite patients from being reduced to auction weights.

Instead of medicine suppliers’ names, he records only temperature markings and the number of times the stopping bell rang in his log.

/story_contents/B018/actors/3/sections/붕.en:
On the night frostbite patients arrived along with winter fuel from the Chang-dong side, Pan Handeul locked the market unloading door and left only the stopping seats.

His fear takes the form of an empty row of chairs becoming a display for an auction of counterfeit medicine.

White powder from G09, the Low-Temperature Spore Host, lay beneath the railing, but he did not use it as a pretext for a lockdown.

/story_contents/B018/actors/3/sections/생.en:
When Nam Hoseong’s escort stopped at the platform, Pan Handeul had to choose whether to ring the stopping bell once more to protect the temperature-check line or open the door for Dong Juha’s market unloading.

An XT04-SC2 message announced that Jegi-dong would take in frostbite patients, but it did not redraw the markings on the waiting-room railing.

Before Cheon Daol’s time synchronization arrived, he did not open the bolt on the scale side.

/story_contents/B018/actors/3/sections/현.en:
Now Pan Handeul is the site chief of the Cheongnyangni Station waiting room, keeping the stopping seats separate from the unloading bolt.

The escort door opens only after Nam Hoseong’s escort pass and Cheon Daol’s timing coincide.

He does not hand the Medical Neutrality League waiting room over as an exclusive auction hall for the Jegi-dong Healing House.

/story_contents/B018/actors/3/sections/비.en:
When Pan Handeul locked the unloading door, he saw a medicine packet fall under a chair but rang the bell anyway.

If he makes it public, people will say the site chief hid medicine with his foot; if he conceals it, the same packet will become the first counterfeit-medicine specimen.

He left a knot in that string’s color on the inside of the railing.

/story_contents/B018/actors/3/sections/관.en:
Pan Handeul honors his agreement to receive Nam Hoseong’s escort stop at the platform.

He has agreed to keep its line separate from Dong Juha’s market unloading and synchronizes the stopping bell with Cheon Daol’s depot duty time.

“If the medicine packet is warm, delay the bell.” Pan Handeul’s words cling to the waiting-room railing.

/story_contents/B018/actors/3/sections/3.en:
When frostbite patients flood in, Pan Handeul locks the unloading door and leaves only the stopping seats.

Before the locked bolt, the HP06 public-escort obligation and the XT04 demand to take in frostbite patients converge on the same railing.

If he reveals the fallen medicine packet, he pays the price of STORY-B018-K328 and opens either the stop or the scale.

/story_contents/B018/actors/3/sections/분.en:
In the disclosure branch, Pan Handeul rings the stopping bell once more to secure the temperature-check line and puts off unloading until the next day.

In the concealment branch, he moves the medicine packet from beneath the chair to a specimen box, leaving only the counterfeit-medicine investigation.

The chairs in the Cheongnyangni waiting room do not become auction displays.

/story_contents/B018/actors/3/arc/0/summ.en: Pan Handeul locks the market unloading door and leaves only the stopping seats

/story_contents/B018/actors/3/arc/1/summ.en: Pan Handeul weighs the escort bell against the demand to take in frostbite patients at the railing

/story_contents/B018/actors/3/arc/2/summ.en: Pan Handeul bears the cost of the fallen medicine packet

/story_contents/B018/actors/3/outcomes/0.en: Rings the stopping bell once more to secure the temperature-check line

/story_contents/B018/actors/3/outcomes/1.en: Moves the medicine packet from beneath the chair to a specimen box, leaving only the counterfeit investigation

/story_contents/B018/actors/4/sections/정.en:
The bridge schedule on the board in the Guui Station waiting room is legible only in Su Jiwan’s thick chalk strokes.

As a Gate Military Government site chief, he transfers An Gijun’s bridge schedule to the platform and calls passage without a seal key another name for smuggling.

His Korean origin does not soften his whistle, and the chalk dust on the back of his hand becomes the measure of his work.

/story_contents/B018/actors/4/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, Su Jiwan wrote the names of bridge-pier cracks only as abbreviations in the board’s margins.

The medical waiting line was folded up only after Yeong Hanmoe’s bed count had been written down, and passage through the gateway opened only when the seal key had been split in two.

A message he sent to his older brother—saying to postpone the schedule by a day if a crack widened—became the original form of his debt.

/story_contents/B018/actors/4/sections/가.en:
Su Jiwan’s board is bound up with the public-schedule provision of the HP07 Hangangjin Bridge Guild charter.

The waiting room is not a family’s exclusive customs office, and he keeps the seals on mineral samples from becoming leverage for a passage toll.

Instead of construction company names, he records only crack abbreviations and the number of whistle blasts in his log.

/story_contents/B018/actors/4/sections/붕.en:
On the morning the Seoul Station Records Office screened out forged kinship certificates and the Achasan seal key was divided, Su Jiwan erased the bridge schedule and left only the medical waiting line.

At the heart of his fear is the sight of a blank space on the board becoming the assembly time for a crowd being conscripted at the gateway.

G17, the Surveillance Rail Force, stopped above the railing, but he did not use that halt as evidence that the seal had been divided.

/story_contents/B018/actors/4/sections/생.en:
When An Gijun’s bridge schedule arrived at the platform, Su Jiwan had to choose whether to fill the board again and open passage or put Yeong Hanmoe’s medical waiting line first.

An XT01-SC3 message announced the division of the Achasan gateway’s seal key, but it did not match the thickness of the chalk writing on the Guui board for him.

Before Yeong Hanmoe’s bed count arrived, he did not blow the whistle.

/story_contents/B018/actors/4/sections/현.en:
Now Su Jiwan is the Guui Station waiting-room site chief, dividing the bridge schedule and the medical waiting line between the left and right sides of one board.

He blows the passage whistle only after An Gijun’s original schedule and Yeong Hanmoe’s arrival confirmation coincide.

He does not hand the Gate Military Government waiting room over as an exclusive customs counter for the Hangangjin Bridge Guild.

/story_contents/B018/actors/4/sections/비.en:
When Su Jiwan erased the schedule, he omitted one bridge-pier crack abbreviation from the margin.
