His guilt grows between the neutrality declaration he protected and the patients who waited in front of the medical car during that delay.

Instead of full disclosure, he permits only partial access in the presence of the medical team.

Access opens only at the same time as a copy of Go Seojun’s Achasan passage agreement.

/story_contents/B019/actors/8/sections/관.en:
The night he tried to protect Jang Sehwa’s neutrality at the inspection desk was an agreement; the morning he refused Bae Woojin’s protective search was a boundary close to enmity.

Cross-checking Go Seojun’s Achasan passage agreement was cooperation, but they still disagreed over the speed of surveying the rear gate.

At the same inspection desk, some seals brought salvation and some detours were read as betrayal.

His Chinese-descended family’s invoicing habits matter only for checking evidence and do not predict loyalty.

The connection is STORY-B019-K293.

/story_contents/B019/actors/8/sections/3.en:
Where rear-gate ink has spread across the steel plate of the Sinnae inspection desk, Mun Sion returns the stamp to a blank field.

HP02 observation and XT01 detour transfers overlap with the seal timetable.

He pays the price of either a delayed train service or neutrality being turned against itself.

The story arc is STORY-B019-K293.

/story_contents/B019/actors/8/sections/분.en:
In the restoration branch, Mun Sion repairs the rear-gate ledger and ends arbitrary searches.

In the document branch, he extracts the document citing refusal as grounds for entry, exposing the gap in neutrality.

The Neutral Convoy City slot remains unchanged; only the branch splits at K299-OUT.

The decision at the time is to escort the ledger’s restoration or secure the document setting out the grounds for entry.

/story_contents/B019/actors/8/arc/0/summ.en: On finding traces of a rear-gate bypass, he returns the inspection stamp to a blank field.

/story_contents/B019/actors/8/arc/1/summ.en: He ties HP02 observation and XT01 detour transfers to the seal timetable.

/story_contents/B019/actors/8/arc/2/summ.en: He pays the price of a delayed train service or neutrality being turned against itself.

/story_contents/B019/actors/8/outcomes/0.en: Arbitrary searches blocked by restoring the rear-gate ledger

/story_contents/B019/actors/8/outcomes/1.en: The gap in neutrality exposed by extracting the document justifying entry

/story_contents/B019/actors/9/sections/정.en:
Water Purification Filter is fixed in a rack against the concrete wall of the filter corridor at the Magok water treatment plant and has no joints for movement.

A class-F facility intelligence called Filter, it has a sensor bus that samples only turbidity, differential pressure, and residual chlorine; it does not identify human faces.

The F03 identifier does not overlap with human K-numbers, and its national slot is tied solely to the Yongsan Line.

Its status records contain no statements of emotion, only counts of differential-pressure exceedances and shift hashes.

/story_contents/B019/actors/9/sections/붕.en:
During the pre-shipment inspection, Water Purification Filter was given only a filter-membrane differential-pressure calibration value and the cycle counts for two battery slots.

It had neither full battery access nor complete memory, and trial shifts ran on only one line of the filter corridor.

The ban on memory forks was locked under clause F03-PRE, and the human staff’s jokes were not placed in its audio buffer.

B019 takes that trial differential-pressure log as its starting point.

/story_contents/B019/actors/9/sections/가.en:
Responsibility for custody rests with the Yongsan Escort House’s joint custody and Jeong Harin’s signature.

On transfer, the rack key cannot be moved without three signatures—from the lead maintenance family, an auditor, and a citizen observer.

The maintenance party is recorded only as a fictional successor office, and the names of real equipment companies are not written in the duty log.

The community regards Water Purification Filter not as property but as the operator of its assigned filtration slot.

/story_contents/B019/actors/9/sections/붕.en:
The collapse severed the turbidity channel and exposed the battery slots’ allocation limits in numbers.

Water Purification Filter was locked against filling an empty sample with fictitious turbidity data and retained only a measurement-unavailable flag.

Even when the G19 Cooling-Water Index Microbial Colony signal appeared on the bus, it could not raise an alarm until it had filtered and checked the signal three times.

It answered a request for access to the entire pump-room network with a refusal code.

/story_contents/B019/actors/9/sections/생.en:
The turning point came when it requested only a district key and closed the valve route to the neighboring building.

Even when a message about measurement verification arrived from the West Sea Granary Theater, control outside its assigned area remained unavailable.

Reconnection is valid only after Jeong Harin’s approval and is preserved in the F03-TURN log.

Even without filter-membrane stock, the constraint against taking control of other facilities takes priority.

/story_contents/B019/actors/9/sections/현.en:
Its current goals are continuous operation of the Yongsan Line filters and the safety of the humans responsible for them.

Water Purification Filter does not own the entire treatment plant and uses only its assigned rack.

Status disclosure is limited to eight-hour shift snapshots, and deployment validation fails if they disagree with the F03 row in Synthetic-Actors.

Batteries and filter membranes are replenished only by allocation; there is no unlimited energy.

/story_contents/B019/actors/9/sections/비.en:
Its secret is a dummy record of an untransmitted false turbidity alarm, and its debt is the battery queue depleted by excessive sampling.

Instead of emotion, its constraint-violation counter rises; a deviation triggers offline isolation followed by a snapshot rollback.

The secret key cannot be opened without a citizen observer, and the pre-rollback hash remains only in the log witnessed by Jeong Harin.

The undelivered packet of the Amsa turbidity message sent to Na Hyowon is mixed into the same dummy record.

/story_contents/B021/actors/0/sections/정.en:
Under the light at the rear gate of the Sinnae rail depot, Gukso covers the last line of the dispatch board with her palm.

As the depot duty chief for the Neutral Convoy City, she locks the gate before saying a word whenever a time slot is left blank.

Of Korean origin, she grew up in the Mangwoo transfer alleys, and yesterday’s coupler grease remains on the back of her hand.

Her display name, Gukso, and immutable identifier, K304, are not renumbered in later assignments.

/story_contents/B021/actors/0/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, he wrote the dispatch times for medical trains and freight cars side by side on one board, but left the priority slot blank without Jang Sehwa’s departmental seal.

His ambition to keep Great Power escort troops off the holding tracks occupied that blank space.

A note he left for his younger sibling—return the rear-gate key only after your shift ends—would later become the seed of a debt.

Even when word from the seasonal regent came late, he locked the board first.

/story_contents/B021/actors/0/sections/가.en:
Changdong Defense Gaeun cited its integrated security key for the Sinnae transfer barrier gate in demanding an observer’s seat at the depot duty desk.

Gukso allowed only a joint inspection with I Hongwon and did not hand the remote key over to the escort corps.

His standing in the community was demonstrated by the number of times he posted dispatch times and duty names on the same board, and he stopped outside armed personnel unaccompanied by Mun Sion at the rear gate.

No real company name appears on his board.

/story_contents/B021/actors/0/sections/붕.en:
When ammunition stamped with the Amsa insignia was found in a medical train’s weapons locker, a line was already missing from the duty roster.

Gukso locked the dispatch switch and kept his gloves on, unable to finish reading Jang Sehwa’s statement of neutrality.

At the heart of his fear was the sight of depot duty becoming a springboard for loading weapons, reducing the Transfer City to a freight yard that merely let shipments pass through.

He covered the Transfer Rat Colony droppings on the holding-track floor with sealing tape before he covered the ammunition crates.

/story_contents/B021/actors/0/sections/생.en:
The crossroads then was the moment she chose whether to find the missing duty officer and restore the roster or block dispatch by switching to a dual-key system.

As word arrived that the Changdong wheeled convoy had stopped outside the gate in the Imjin River Gateway Theater, the alternate transfer slot demanded the same time as the medical train.

Restoring the roster would let dispatch resume but might leave the ammunition route intact; dual keys would stop the weapons but delay one train consist.

That choice is recorded as K310-TURN.

/story_contents/B021/actors/0/sections/현.en:
Gukso still serves as duty chief at the Sinnae rail depot, opening roll call on the holding tracks.

His license and observer logs sustain his position, and he rejects HC08’s demand for exclusive state control.

Sodugam’s maintenance shop holds one rear-gate key; the duty desk holds the other.

Every morning, he checks the depot field in the Cast profile against the times on the board.

/story_contents/B021/actors/0/sections/비.en:
His secret is the rear-gate key time he wrote in the note, and the name of the duty officer he failed to summon at that time.

His guilt grows only in the space between the neutrality preserved by locking dispatch and the stretcher that arrived a day late.

Revealing everything could break a link in transfer trust, so he left only a partial disclosure.

The SECRET field opens only at the same time as An Dohan’s dispatch schedule.

/story_contents/B021/actors/0/sections/관.en:
The night he put An Dohan’s dispatch schedule at the top of the board was a contract; the dawn he shared duty with Sodugam’s maintenance shop was an alliance forged through tools.

The time he verified Gwak Taesan’s guard rotation at the rear gate was witnessing, not command.

On the same holding track, one person gained a dispatch and another lost a signature.

The relationship ledger endpoint leads to STORY-B021-K304.

/story_contents/B021/actors/0/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, Gukso places the ammunition and the incomplete roster under the same light.

In Act 2, she ties the HC08 security key and XT01 alternate slot to the dispatch clock.

In Act 3, she bears the cost of the delay caused by either restoring the roster or using dual keys.

The narrative arc identifier is fixed as STORY-B021-K304.

/story_contents/B021/actors/0/sections/분.en:
In ending α, Gukso finds the missing duty officer, resumes dispatch, and keeps public transfers connected.

In ending β, she uses dual keys to prevent weapons from being loaded but delays one medical-train consist.

The Neutral Convoy City slot remains in place; only the branch splits at K310-OUT.

The decision at the scene was to restore the roster or double-lock dispatch.

/story_contents/B021/actors/0/arc/1/summ.en: Ties the HC08 security key and XT01 alternate slot to the dispatch clock

/story_contents/B021/actors/1/sections/정.en:
In front of the switch box at the Jegi-dong medical convoy depot, Cheon Daol does not attach a note bearing the destination country’s name to the convoy pass.

As depot duty chief for the Medical Neutrality League, he upholds Nam Hoseong’s silence in the field but throws a memo calling for armed guards in the treatment car into the stove.

Of Korean origin, he grew up near the Cheongnyangni evacuation route and has a habit of writing only patient counts and the weight of medical supplies inside his glove.

The name Cheon Daol and identifier K329 are immutable.

/story_contents/B021/actors/1/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, she first wrote the dispatch times for the Sinnae–Jegi-dong–Achasan triangular convoy in the margins of the draft Joint Convoy Treaty.

Her ambition to end the mistaken identification of medical trains as military-supply trains filled those margins, and she put the destination country’s name on the board only immediately before dispatch.

A message she sent her mother—do not put the treatment-car key and the armed personnel roster on the same ring—became the original form of her debt.

Even when her superior kept the route secret for longer, she would not issue a convoy pass with its weight field blank.

/story_contents/B021/actors/1/sections/가.en:
Jegi-dong Healing Gate invoked double-checking prescriptions in demanding an observer field on the convoy dispatch form.

Cheon Daol accepted only Jeong Harin’s lot postings and did not make an exclusive purchase agreement a condition of dispatch.

His standing in the community was demonstrated by records showing patient counts and the weight of medical supplies written on both the convoy pass and the board.

If the family office tried to tie the treatment-car key to the guard roster, he declared it invalid for lack of separate signatures.

/story_contents/B021/actors/1/sections/붕.en:
When scouts at the Achasan bridge mistook a medical convoy for hostile movement, Cheon Daol locked the dispatch switch and rewrote the convoy pass to show only its weight.

Her fear was the sight of a car leaving the depot being marked as a military-supply car at the Guui bridge while a patient’s vital signs faded.

Even when a Cleanroom Mutant alarm sounded from the medical-supply crate’s hygrometer, she did not put the treatment car under guard control.

After the alarm stopped, her pen halted halfway down the LOSS list.

/story_contents/B021/actors/1/sections/생.en:
The crossroads then was the moment she chose whether to correct the false signal on the depot board or reroute the convoy to put distance between it and the Gateway State’s scouts.

As word arrived that the Changdong Wheel Guild was dividing the winter fuel queue in the Tumen River Far East Theater, Jegi-dong’s frostbite-patient car demanded the same slot.

Correcting the signal would keep passage over the bridge open but leave the scouts’ pride at stake; a detour would delay arrival but reduce the risk of a clash caused by the misidentification.

The decision is recorded in K336-TURN.

/story_contents/B021/actors/1/sections/현.en:
Cheon Daol is currently duty chief at the medical convoy depot, overseeing dispatch roll call and the weight queue.

Nam Hoseong’s command log and a copy of Go Seojun’s bridge permit sustain his position.

The destination country’s name still goes on the board only immediately before dispatch.

Checking the operations-officer field in his profile against the time on the convoy pass is part of his morning routine.

/story_contents/B021/actors/1/sections/비.en:
His secret is the ash of the armed-guard memo he burned and the name of the apprentice assistant he failed to summon that day.

His guilt grows between the treatment car he saved and the loss of body heat caused by the detour.

Instead of a full confession, he permits only partial disclosure through the lot noticeboard.

SECRET access opens only at the same time as Pan Handeul’s waiting-room stop.

/story_contents/B021/actors/1/sections/관.en:
The night he took dispatch duty under Nam Hoseong’s command was service almost like an apprenticeship; the morning he checked Go Seojun’s bridge-crossing permit before dispatch was a contract.

Synchronizing with Pan Handeul’s waiting-room stop was a platform alliance.

Before the same convoy pass, one person gained a departure and another lost a route.

The endpoint leads to STORY-B021-K329.

/story_contents/B021/actors/1/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, Cheon Daol counters the mistaken order to stop with a convoy pass containing only a weight field.

In Act 2, she ties the HP06 lot posting and XT04 fuel queue to the dispatch clock.

In Act 3, she bears the cost in body heat of either correcting the signal or taking a detour.

The narrative arc is STORY-B021-K329.

/story_contents/B021/actors/1/sections/분.en:
In ending α, Cheon Daol corrects the false signal on the board and gets the convoy across the bridge.

In ending β, she reroutes the convoy to avoid a clash with the scouts but delays the arrival of frostbite patients.

The Medical Neutrality League slot remains in place; only the branch splits at K336-OUT.

The decision then was to correct the signal or arrange a detour.

/story_contents/B021/actors/1/arc/1/summ.en: Ties the HP06 lot posting and XT04 fuel queue to the dispatch clock

/story_contents/B021/actors/1/arc/2/summ.en: Bears the cost in body heat of either correcting the signal or taking a detour

/story_contents/B021/actors/1/outcomes/0.en: Correcting the false signal lets the convoy cross the bridge

/story_contents/B021/actors/1/outcomes/1.en: A detour avoids a clash with the scouts but delays arrival

/story_contents/B021/actors/2/sections/정.en:
Beneath the beacon at the Achasan outpost, Seon Neulbom records a light seen once at the top of the shift log.

As outpost depot duty chief for the Gate Military Government, she throws a note telling her to keep the joint-approval document at the outpost into the stove.

Of Korean origin, she grew up in a ridge village in Guui and has a habit of winding her whistle cord around her wrist.

The name Seon Neulbom and identifier K354 do not change.

/story_contents/B021/actors/2/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, he posted beacon times and duty names on one board and would not keep the peacetime joint-approval document anywhere at the outpost but in its safe.

His ambition to keep water technicians’ delays and Amsa patronage from standing under the same roof filled that safe.

A short note he left his father—record the light before the nationality—became the seed of a debt.

Even when Go Seojun’s retrospective approval was late, he blew the whistle first.

/story_contents/B021/actors/2/sections/가.en:
The Hangangjin Bridge Guild cited wind-speed closure criteria in demanding an observer field in the outpost’s beacon records.

Seon Neulbom stopped outside armed personnel unaccompanied by Go Seojun, but rejected language that treated the bridge as nothing more than a source of tolls.

His standing in the community was demonstrated by the number of times he posted beacon times and duty names on the same board.

No family logo or real business name appears in his log.

/story_contents/B021/actors/2/sections/붕.en:
The night smoke from a broken water main was mistaken for a hostile beacon, a line was missing from the outpost duty roster.

Seon Neulbom locked the beacon and stood with his whistle in his mouth, unable to copy Mun Hayul’s sentry order into the log.

His fear was the sight of a mistaken beacon opening both the high ground and the bridge on the same night, exposing Guui’s purified water supply.

To keep from conflating the idling noise of the Ghost Dispatch Unit below the ridge with the beacon light, he divided the log field in two.

/story_contents/B021/actors/2/sections/생.en:
The crossroads then was the moment he chose whether to find the missing duty officer and correct the mistaken beacon or switch the beacon to dual keys and lock down the outpost’s own strongpoint.

At the outpost, word arrived from the Imjin River Gateway Theater that the Seoul Station Records Office was identifying forged kinship certificates and the Achasan gateway was sharing a seal key.

Finding the duty officer would clear up the mistake but leave a gap in the timeline; dual keys would block patronage but take away one of Gwak Minjae’s water-supply inspection windows.

The choice is K362-TURN.

/story_contents/B021/actors/2/sections/현.en:
Seon Neulbom still serves as duty chief at the ridge outpost depot, opening beacon roll call.

Mun Hayul’s enforcement log and Go Seojun’s accompaniment record sustain his position.

He does not keep the joint-approval document at the outpost, sending it only to the gateway ledger.

Checking the operations-officer field in his profile against the log time marks the start of his shift.

/story_contents/B021/actors/2/sections/비.en:
His secret is the ash of the joint-approval note he burned and the empty duty field left when he failed to hand over the whistle that night.

His guilt grows between the high ground protected by the locked beacon and the alley whose water-supply inspection was pushed back one slot.

Instead of full disclosure, he left only partial disclosure through overlapping log entries.

The SECRET field opens only at the same time as Pan Neulsaem’s patrol whistle.

/story_contents/B021/actors/2/sections/관.en:
The night he carried out Mun Hayul’s sentry order at the depot was command; the dawn he shared duty with Pan Neulsaem’s patrol whistle was a contract.

Cross-checking his log so that he would not treat Gwak Minjae’s water-supply inspection as a surveillance gap was witnessing.

On the same ridge, one person gained a blockade and another lost an inspection.

The endpoint leads to STORY-B021-K354.

/story_contents/B021/actors/2/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, Seon Neulbom places the smoke and the incomplete roster beneath the beacon.

In Act 2, she ties the HP07 wind-speed criteria and XT01 seal key to the whistle clock.

In Act 3, she bears the cost of a gap in water-supply inspection caused by either correcting the mistake or using dual keys.

The narrative arc is STORY-B021-K354.

/story_contents/B021/actors/2/sections/분.en:
In ending α, Seon Neulbom finds the missing duty officer and corrects the mistaken beacon.

In ending β, she locks the beacon with dual keys to block patronage but leaves the water-supply inspection window empty.

The Gate Military Government slot remains in place; only the branch splits at K362-OUT.

The decision then was to search for the duty officer or double-lock the beacon.

/story_contents/B021/actors/2/arc/1/summ.en: Ties the HP07 wind-speed criteria and XT01 seal key to the whistle clock

/story_contents/B021/actors/2/arc/2/summ.en: Bears the cost of a gap in water-supply inspection caused by either correcting the mistake or using dual keys

/story_contents/B021/actors/2/outcomes/0.en: Searching for the missing duty officer corrects the mistaken beacon

/story_contents/B021/actors/2/outcomes/1.en: Double-locking the beacon blocks patronage but leaves a gap in water-supply inspection

/story_contents/B021/actors/3/sections/정.en:
Beneath the roof speaker in the Jamsil Station waiting room, Cheon Solbit counts the faces at the front of the line on her fingers and does not take down the plaza ledger.

As the waiting-room strongpoint chief for the Cathedral Accreditation State, she crumples a note telling her to turn famine rations into a broadcast about charity behind the microphone.

Of Korean origin, she grew up in the lower alleys of Jamsil and has a habit of gauging the crowd by the dampness on the platform.

The name Cheon Solbit and identifier K379 are immutable.

/story_contents/B021/actors/3/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, she posted waiting-room tickets and plaza ration slips under one roof, but recorded rumors of secret military rations only as an enemy of the line.

Her ambition to keep the public lottery and the number of dependents visible as the face of the plaza went into those tickets.

A temporary ticket she gave her younger sister—do not buy a place in line—would later become the original form of a debt.

Even when an envoy from the merchants’ council urged a direct deal, she did not hand over the microphone.

/story_contents/B021/actors/3/sections/가.en:
Seoul Station Inventory House cited its inventory ledger for household goods in lower Jamsil in demanding an observer’s seat at the waiting-room counter.

Cheon Solbit allowed only a joint inspection with Nam Yungyeong and rejected language calling for places in the ration line to be sold.

His standing in the community was demonstrated by the dates on which he did not take down the plaza ledger, and he would not open the counter for undisclosed priority rations without Yun Seorin’s sanction.

No real business name appears on his waiting tickets.

/story_contents/B021/actors/3/sections/붕.en:
During a week of soaring prices, an emergency ration line filled the Jamsil assembly point. When the merchants’ council demanded a halt to rations, Cheon Solbit did not take down the plaza ledger.

Her fear was the sight of the emergency rice she had distributed becoming bait for military household-registration renewal, marking the waiting room as a protection office.

Even when the movement of the Migratory Marsh Predators could be heard in the lower drainage channel, she did not turn on the loudspeaker to disperse the line.

Even after the alarm fell silent, she did not let go of the roof speaker’s power switch.

/story_contents/B021/actors/3/sections/생.en:
The crossroads then was the moment she chose whether to protect the plaza ledger and keep rations going or disperse the line and give priority to the auction system.

Word that Garak’s ration service was readjusting its canned-food allocation in the Korea Strait Theater appeared alongside the entries on the waiting-room board.

Protecting the ledger would keep the line alive but prolong the merchants’ council’s blockade; dispersing it would open the auction but erase the number of dependents from the counter.

The choice is recorded as K387-TURN.

/story_contents/B021/actors/3/sections/현.en:
Cheon Solbit still serves as chief of the Jamsil Station waiting-room strongpoint, opening roll call for the line.

Jeon Nagyeong’s command log and Bang Neuljae’s presence at the treatment tent sustain his position.

Waiting tickets are made public daily, and military freight cars are brought alongside the platform only after the water-supply train departs.

Checking the operations-officer field in his profile against the plaza ledger’s timestamp is his first broadcast.

/story_contents/B021/actors/3/sections/비.en:
Her secret is the name in the margin of the temporary ticket she gave her younger sister, and the other face she could not remove from that line.

Her guilt grows between the rations saved by the ledger she never took down and the wait prolonged because she did not disperse the line.

Revealing everything could break a link in the plaza’s trust, so she left only a partial disclosure.

The SECRET field opens only at the same time as Baek On’s temporary tickets for families heading south.

/story_contents/B021/actors/3/sections/관.en:
The night he managed the plaza line under Jeon Nagyeong’s command was service; the dawn he shared the queue with Bang Neuljae’s treatment tent was an alliance.

Giving temporary tickets to Baek On’s southbound families was not a contract but witnessing their entry in the register.

In the same waiting room, one person gained a line and another lost a place in the auction order.

The endpoint leads to STORY-B021-K379.

/story_contents/B021/actors/3/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, Cheon Solbit faces the line formed by soaring prices and the demand to halt rations beneath the waiting-room roof.

In Act 2, she ties HC09 inventory observation and XT03 canned-food allocation to the waiting tickets.

In Act 3, she bears the cost at the counter of either protecting the ledger or dispersing the line.

The narrative arc is STORY-B021-K379.

/story_contents/B021/actors/3/sections/분.en:
In ending α, Cheon Solbit protects the plaza ledger and keeps the ration line going.

In ending β, she disperses the line and gives priority to the merchants’ council’s auction system.

The Cathedral Accreditation State slot remains in place; only the branch splits at K387-OUT.

The decision then was to protect the ledger or disperse the line.

/story_contents/B021/actors/3/arc/1/summ.en: Ties HC09 inventory observation and XT03 canned-food allocation to the waiting tickets

/story_contents/B021/actors/3/arc/2/summ.en: Bears the cost at the counter of either protecting the ledger or dispersing the line

/story_contents/B021/actors/3/outcomes/0.en: Protecting the plaza ledger keeps the ration line going

/story_contents/B021/actors/3/outcomes/1.en: Dispersing the line gives priority to the auction system

/story_contents/B021/actors/4/sections/정.en:
In front of the thermometer in the Suseo underground archive, Seon Hansom touches a loose strand of the draft-box seal cord and blocks the door with his body.

As chief of the underground-facility defense unit’s strongpoint for the Jeongdong General Labor Union, he records it as an incident whenever the defense unit is more conspicuous than the convoy.

Of Korean origin, he grew up in Gangnam’s contract alleys and has a habit of never putting keys and seals in the same pocket.

The name Seon Hansom and identifier K403 are not renumbered.

/story_contents/B021/actors/4/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, he stored the archive key separately from the draft-box seal and permitted searches only in the presence of a contract clerk.

His ambition to end the practice of stationing Great Power escort troops beside the draft box lay behind that separation.

A memo he left his mentor—record the box temperature and the audit sheet on the same line—became the seed of a debt.

Even when the nomination committee pressed him, he refused a search without a witness.

/story_contents/B021/actors/4/sections/가.en:
Suseo Construction Gaeun cited seismic-joint plans for the Suseo underground utility tunnel in demanding an observer’s seat at the archive duty desk.

Seon Hansom allowed only a joint inspection with Jeong Yura and rejected language offering to trade the plans for an expansion of the watchtower.

His standing in the community was demonstrated by the number of shifts in which keys and seals were kept separate, and demands for exclusive state ownership were rejected.

No real company name appears in his temperature log.

/story_contents/B021/actors/4/sections/붕.en:
When water-supply contracts from three Great Powers arrived in the same week, a line was missing from the underground duty roster and one strand of the draft-box seal cord had come loose.

Seon Hansom locked the archive door and kept his gloves on, unable to move Ha Seojin’s draft box.

His fear was the sight of someone within the defense unit concealing a forged fair copy, breaking Jeong Yura’s standard form from within.

He first recorded signs of a Customized Medical Remnant coolant leak in the box temperature log and postponed the search.

/story_contents/B021/actors/4/sections/생.en:
The crossroads then was the moment he chose whether to find the missing duty officer and expose the internal forgery route or replace the seal and cast the incident as outside tampering.

Underground, word arrived from the Incheon Trust Theater that the Seoul Station Records Office was keeping the handover-list hash and Suseo was opening a delivery turnback line.

Finding the duty officer would expose the culprit inside but leave the archive open for a day; replacing the seal would close the draft box but might leave the forgery behind.

The choice is K412-TURN.

/story_contents/B021/actors/4/sections/현.en:
Seon Hansom still serves as chief of the underground-facility defense unit’s strongpoint, opening archive roll call.

Ha Seojin’s witness log and Yeong Maon’s perimeter rotation sustain her position.

Searches take place only in the presence of a contract clerk, and the box temperature is cross-checked against Cheon Neulsaem’s generator log.

Checking the strongpoint field in her profile against the seal time marks the start of her shift.

/story_contents/B021/actors/4/sections/비.en:
Her secret is a line of the draft she read before retieing the loose seal cord.

Her guilt grows between the standard form protected by the locked door and the duty officer she failed to summon that day.

Instead of a full confession, she permits only partial disclosure by cross-checking audit sheets.

The SECRET field opens only at the same time as Gwak Eunjae’s audit sheet.

/story_contents/B021/actors/4/sections/관.en:
The night she guarded Ha Seojin’s draft box underground was a contract; the dawn she shared a shift with Yeong Maon’s perimeter patrol was an alliance.

Cross-checking Gwak Eunjae’s audit sheet against the box temperature log was witnessing.

In the same archive, one person gained a draft and another lost a key.

The endpoint leads to STORY-B021-K403.

/story_contents/B021/actors/4/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, Seon Hansom places the loosened seal and the empty roster in front of the archive thermometer.

In Act 2, Seon ties the HC13 drawing review and the XT05 hash round schedule to the archive clock.

In Act 3, Seon bears the cost of opening up either an internal search or a seal replacement.

The story arc is STORY-B021-K403.

/story_contents/B021/actors/4/sections/분.en:
In ending α, Seon Hansom finds the missing duty officer and reveals the route by which a fair copy was forged internally.

In ending β, Seon replaces the seal, attributes the incident to external tampering, and closes the draft box.

The Federation of Affective Labor Unions slot remains in place; only the branch splits into K412-OUT.

The decision at the time is to search for the duty officer or replace the seal.

/story_contents/B021/actors/4/outcomes/0.en: Search for the missing duty officer exposes the internal forgery route

/story_contents/B021/actors/5/sections/정.en:
Behind the glass of the Sinjeong Base audit office, Je Yun leaves a note promising a verbal exemption out of the ledger, folding it into the margin instead.

As the Water Compact's transit-toll recordkeeper, he fills gaps in the timetable before attending to people, but leaves his interpretations in the margins rather than the main text.

Of Korean origin, he grew up in staff housing beside the Sinjeong siding. He habitually makes the figures public without explaining exemptions at the counter.

The name Je Yun and identifier K016 are immutable.

/story_contents/B021/actors/5/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, he entered western railway transit tolls and the priority order for water-supply trains as valid only in a ledger he had reviewed himself.

His ambition to make the Floodgate Charter work on the rails, too, filled that review column.

A message he sent to his mentor, a train dispatcher—emergency rates are void unless recalculated within three days—became the source of his debt.

Even as rumors of bribery in train dispatching spread, he posted copies on the dispatch board and in the audit office at the same time.

/story_contents/B021/actors/5/sections/가.en:
The Sinjeong Wheel House cited the rotation of battery cells on the Sinjeong Base siding to demand an observer's seat at the transit ledger.

Je Yun allowed only a joint inspection with Yu Sejin and rejected language granting a monopoly over the Yongsan transshipment counter.

His place in the community was demonstrated by the number of times he posted copies of the transit tolls on both walls, and the demand for exclusive state ownership was rejected.

No real company's trade name appears in his ledger.

/story_contents/B021/actors/5/sections/붕.en:
When the Yongsan Rail House detained a central train, Je Yun entered an emergency rate for a rerouted water-supply train departing Sinjeong in the ledger and refused a private exemption.

What he feared was a single forged transit pass filling the siding, trapping a maintenance train and a water-supply train at the same time.

Even when he heard the Idling Disused-Line Maintenance Train Group on the siding, he did not enter the forged pass in the genuine-document column.

After the alarm stopped, he set down his pen without being able to unfold the note tucked into the margin.

/story_contents/B021/actors/5/sections/생.en:
The turning point came when he had to choose whether to escort a witness to the rerouting authorization or expose the margin note on misappropriation, putting himself at risk of replacement as recordkeeper.

At the audit office, this coincided with a message from the West Sea Granary Theater: the Yeouido floodgate was rescheduling dock drainage to match the West Sea tides.

Escorting the witness would let the water-supply train through but leave the opening for misappropriation; exposure would close the loophole in the rate but stop the counter for a day.

The choice is K016-TURN.

/story_contents/B021/actors/5/sections/현.en:
Je Yun still conducts ledger roll call as the Sinjeong Base transit-toll recordkeeper.

A copy of Yu Sejin's dispatch declaration and Choi Hangyeol's release-guarantee log sustain his position.

The counter window states that emergency rates are void unless recalculated within three days.

His first stamp of the day is to align the recordkeeper entry in his profile with the ledger's time.

/story_contents/B021/actors/5/sections/비.en:
His secret is a figure he calculated before refusing a private exemption and left on a note folded into the margin.

His guilt grows between the water-supply train saved by the emergency rate he posted and the maintenance slot halted for a day because of that rate.

He permits only partial disclosure through the recalculation counter, not full disclosure.

The SECRET entry opens only together with Park Taegyeom's relay-counter copy.

/story_contents/B021/actors/5/sections/관.en:
The night he transferred Yu Sejin's dispatch declaration into the ledger was a contract, and the dawn he certified Choi Hangyeol's maintenance train release in the records was an alliance.

He witnessed Heo Eunchan attaching electricity use to the transit ledger, and the counter where he shared western rates with Park Taegyeom was a relay point.

On the same siding, one person gained passage and another lost an exemption.

The endpoint leads to STORY-B021-K016.

/story_contents/B021/actors/5/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, Je Yun holds the news of the detention and the forged transit pass up to the audit office glass.

In Act 2, he ties the HC02 battery review and the XT02 drainage schedule to the emergency rate.

In Act 3, he bears the cost of a counter shutdown for either escorting the witness or exposing the misappropriation.

The story arc is STORY-B021-K016.

/story_contents/B021/actors/5/sections/분.en:
In ending α, Je Yun escorts the witness to the rerouting authorization and gets the water-supply train through.

In ending β, he exposes the margin note on misappropriation, closes the loophole in the rate, and accepts the risk of replacement.

The Water Compact slot remains in place; only the branch splits into K016-OUT.

The decision at the time is to escort the witness or expose the margin note.

/story_contents/B021/actors/6/sections/정.en:
At the Sangam cross-verification desk, Hwang Eunseol reads each sentence twice before touching the broadcast switch.

As a verification recordkeeper for the Yeouido Investment Union, Hwang's hand stops between the silence that saves lives and the duty to disclose the facts.

Born in Seoul, Hwang grew up reading notes from their mother's night shifts and school notices from their father at the same table. The habit of comparing a sentence in the rhythms of two languages developed before the job did.

The name Hwang Eunseol and identifier K217 are immutable.

/story_contents/B021/actors/6/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, Hwang sought to run a public ledger that cross-verified every state's official announcements against at least two testimonies, alongside Seoul Station certification.

The ambition was a broadcast network that would not become a propaganda tool, and drafts always went onto the verification desk's chalkboard first.

A request that Jo Harin keep the original encrypted message later became the seed of a debt.

If there were fewer than two independent testimonies, Hwang posted the reason for withholding the broadcast on the noticeboard that same day.

/story_contents/B021/actors/6/sections/가.en:
The Seoul Station Records House cited its original hash seal to demand an observer's seat at the transmission cross-verification desk.

Hwang Eunseol allowed only a joint inspection with Yeo Rian and rejected language granting the broadcasting station sole authority to disclose.

Hwang's place in the community was demonstrated by the dates on which reasons for withholding broadcasts were posted, and pressure to merge three copies of a will into one authentic original was rejected.

No real company's trade name appears in Hwang's ledger.

/story_contents/B021/actors/6/sections/붕.en:
When the waveform of a missing person's voice and the handwriting in the document archive diverged in just one segment, Hwang Eunseol locked the verification ledger.

What Hwang feared was a fragment of manipulated audio being officially broadcast, turning the agency's credibility into a propaganda tool.

Even after filtering the communications mycelium noise through the headphones three times, Hwang did not enter a false positive in the authentic-original column.

After the alarm stopped, Hwang kept the headphones on, unable to read the last line of the withholding noticeboard.

/story_contents/B021/actors/6/sections/생.en:
The turning point came when Hwang had to choose whether to bring in a second witness and resume broadcasting or delay disclosure for a day to prevent a riot.

At the verification desk, this coincided with a message from the Incheon Trust Theater: Sangam Transmission was holding a public lottery for the remaining bandwidth, and Yeouido was coordinating the time with the water-supply duty shift.

Securing the testimony would revive the broadcast but make rumors on the street move a beat faster; delaying would buy public order but risk having the stated reason for withholding read as propaganda.

The choice is K221-TURN.

/story_contents/B021/actors/6/sections/현.en:
Hwang Eunseol still conducts roll call at the cross-verification desk as a verification recordkeeper.

Choi Jiwoo's audio copy, Yun Seorin's document certification, and Gang Yejun's oath log sustain Hwang's position.

If there are fewer than two independent testimonies, the broadcast is withheld and the reason is posted that same day.

Hwang's first task with the headphones is to align the verification entry in the profile with the ledger's time.

/story_contents/B021/actors/6/sections/비.en:
The secret is Hwang's debt to Jo Harin for keeping the original encrypted message, and the waveform of one segment of that original that Hwang examined before the broadcast.

Hwang's guilt grows between the propaganda stopped by the locked ledger and the rumors fueled by disclosure delayed a day.

Hwang permits only partial disclosure through the withholding noticeboard, not a full confession.

The SECRET entry opens only together with Guk Dubong's ledger-transport log.

/story_contents/B021/actors/6/sections/관.en:
The night Hwang matched audio and documents between Choi Jiwoo and Yun Seorin was a contract, and the dawn Hwang swore to cross-verify with Gang Yejun was an alliance.

Jo Harin's safekeeping of the original encrypted message was a debt, and Bong So's standing by on the night the broadcast was withheld made Bong a witness.

At the same verification desk, one person gained a broadcast and another bore the silence.

The endpoint leads to STORY-B021-K217.

/story_contents/B021/actors/6/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, Hwang Eunseol confronts the mismatched waveform and handwriting through the headphones.

In Act 2, Hwang ties the HP04 hash seal and XT05 bandwidth lottery to the withholding clock.

In Act 3, Hwang bears the cost in rumors of either securing another testimony or delaying a day.

The story arc is STORY-B021-K217.

/story_contents/B021/actors/6/sections/분.en:
In ending α, Hwang Eunseol brings in a second witness and resumes broadcasting.

In ending β, Hwang delays disclosure for a day to prevent a riot and leaves the reason for withholding on the noticeboard.

The Yeouido Investment Union slot remains in place; only the branch splits into K221-OUT.

The decision at the time is to escort the witness or delay disclosure.

/story_contents/B021/actors/7/sections/정.en:
At the scale in the Achasan checkpoint tax collector's booth, Ha Yunmok sees an empty exemption field as a warning sign and withholds his seal.

As the Checkpoint Military Government's checkpoint tax collector, he closes the booth if he cannot reconcile passage weights and water-supply times in one ledger. When an officer presents a stamp to reduce a tax, he records the time in the margin reserved for insults.

Growing up in a long-settled family, he compared the Chinese-character marginal notes in the kitchen ledger with the checkpoint's Korean-script price list on the same evenings. That history helps him spot discrepancies between the two fields first, but does not predict his loyalty or business sense.

The name Ha Yunmok and identifier K343 are immutable.

/story_contents/B021/actors/7/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, he sought to combine bridge tolls and limited water-supply contributions in one checkpoint ledger, making it the eastern counter for small states' joint negotiations.

His ambition was one ledger for tax rates and water-supply times, not the collection of protection money.

A short line his grandmother left in the kitchen ledger—an empty exemption field is like a debt on credit—became the seed of an obligation.

He recognized military exemptions only on transit passes bearing contract-audit language.

/story_contents/B021/actors/7/sections/가.en:
The Yeongdeungpo Floodgate House cited the divided custody of the Guui floodgate keys to demand an observer's seat at the checkpoint ledger.

Ha Yunmok allowed only a joint inspection with Han Jaemok and did not enter an order to use water as a weapon into the tax rates.

His place in the community was demonstrated by the number of times he recorded goods passing through and water-supply times in the same ledger, and the demand for exclusive state ownership was rejected.

No real company's trade name appears in his tax-rate entries.

/story_contents/B021/actors/7/sections/붕.en:
When three major powers presented different water-supply and passage-exemption documents in the same week, Ha Yunmok locked the booth's scale.

What he feared was becoming a collector of protection money and being excluded from Jeong Yura's standard treaty.

Even with a blank voucher from the Phantom Dispatch Unit attached behind an exemption document, he would not let an entry without a quarantine stamp pass.

After the alarm stopped, his seal halted halfway through the tax calculation.

/story_contents/B021/actors/7/sections/생.en:
The turning point came when he had to choose whether to authenticate the exemption documents and protect the tax-rate ledger, or carry the checkpoint ledger to the Suseo agreement draft and leave the booth unattended for a day.

At the scale, this coincided with a message from the Tumen River Far East Theater: the Achasan checkpoint was destroying forged origin labels after inspecting the seals on mineral samples.

Authenticating the documents would revive the booth but leave the major powers' exemptions in place; carrying the ledger would keep joint negotiations alive but stop passage.

The choice is K351-TURN.

/story_contents/B021/actors/7/sections/현.en:
Ha Yunmok still conducts booth roll call as the checkpoint tax collector.

Jeong Yura's draft loss-compensation clause and its linkage to Ra Seyeong's quarantine stamp sustain his position.

Bae Woojin's demands for a protection tax are rejected every time, and military exemptions pass only with transit passes bearing audit language.

His first stamp of the day is to align the tax collector entry in his profile with the ledger's time.

/story_contents/B021/actors/7/sections/비.en:
His secret is a line about an old unpaid debt, left in Chinese characters in the kitchen ledger's margin and never entered at the booth.

His guilt grows between the tax rates protected by the locked scale and the queues created by a day without passage.

He permits only partial disclosure through publication of the tax calculations, not a full confession.

The SECRET entry opens only together with Bang Mareum's ledger-copying log.

/story_contents/B021/actors/7/sections/관.en:
The night he tried to put Jeong Yura's loss-compensation clause into the tax rates was an alliance, and the morning he refused Bae Woojin's demand for a protection tax was a contract of refusal.

Ra Seyeong's quarantine stamp was linked to the tax calculation under observation, and Cheon Choyun's carrying the ledger only while it remained sealed was done under orders.

At the same booth, one person gained passage and another lost an exemption.

The endpoint leads to STORY-B021-K343.

/story_contents/B021/actors/7/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, Ha Yunmok places three exemption documents on the scale.

In Act 2, he ties the HP01 floodgate-key review and XT04 destruction of origin labels to the tax-rate clock.

In Act 3, he bears the cost of a booth shutdown for either authenticating the documents or transporting the ledger.

The story arc is STORY-B021-K343.

/story_contents/B021/actors/7/sections/분.en:
In ending α, Ha Yunmok authenticates the exemption documents and protects the tax-rate ledger.

In ending β, he carries the checkpoint ledger to the Suseo draft, leaving the booth unattended for a day.

The Checkpoint Military Government slot remains in place; only the branch splits into K351-OUT.

The decision at the time is to authenticate the documents or escort the ledger.

/story_contents/B021/actors/8/sections/정.en:
On a cart outside the Garak rear-gate ice warehouse, Jeon Nagyeong transfers the faces in line onto the ration sheet and records rumors of secret military provisions as enemies of that sheet.

As an emergency ration officer for the Bondang Certification Administration, Jeon sees famine rations as a matter of records, not charity.

As a child during night loading at Garak, Jeon wrote down the weights his mother called out for ice crates. That history helps his remember faces, but does not stand in for the character of his place of origin.

The name Jeon Nagyeong and identifier K368 are immutable.

/story_contents/B021/actors/8/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, Jeon sought to fix the order of famine rations by public lottery and number of dependents, eliminating secret military provisions used in succession deals.

His ambition was a public ledger on the cart, and the draft went up on the Garak rear-gate chalkboard before it went to Jamsil Square.

A copy of the ration ledger he gave Yun Seorin later became the seed of a debt.

Even when a merchants' association envoy proposed a direct deal, he did not hand over the cart's lock.

/story_contents/B021/actors/8/sections/가.en:
The Noryangjin Refrigeration Merchant Guild cited the rotation of power slots at the Garak ice warehouse to demand an observer's seat at the ration cart.

Jeon Nagyeong accepted only Gu Haon's printed temperature log and did not make retrieval of the motor a condition for rations.

Her place in the community was demonstrated by the number of times she posted ration sheets in the square and at the rear gate simultaneously, and she refused undisclosed priority without Yun Seorin's certification.

No real company's trade name appears in her cart ledger.

/story_contents/B021/actors/8/sections/붕.en:
During a week of soaring prices, when an emergency ration line filled the Jamsil gathering place and the merchants' association demanded a halt to distribution, Jeon Nagyeong kept the ledger on the cart and revised only the rear-gate chalkboard.

What he feared was the emergency rice he distributed becoming bait for re-registration in the military household rolls.

Even when the Migratory-Bird Wetland Predators' movement behind them was visible in puddles at the loading dock, he did not open the secret-provisions entry to buy off the line.

After the alarm stopped, he stood holding the chalk, unable to read Nam Yungyeong's concealed-inventory figure.

/story_contents/B021/actors/8/sections/생.en:
The turning point came when he had to choose whether to push the cart into the square and distribute emergency rice, or hand Nam Yungyeong's secret-provisions entry to the records office and break off the succession deal.

At the rear gate, this coincided with a message from the West Sea Granary Theater: while Noryangjin ice credit was faltering, Sangam Transmission would relay only the auction broadcast.

Pushing the cart would keep the line going but leave the secret entry intact; handing over the entry would end the deal but halt rations that day.

The choice is K376-TURN.

/story_contents/B021/actors/8/sections/현.en:
Jeon Nagyeong still conducts roll call at the rear-gate cart as an emergency ration officer.

Yun Seorin's certification copy and Baek On's witnessing of the temporary tickets sustain his position.

Ration sheets are posted at Jamsil Square and the Garak rear gate simultaneously, and he defies Nam Yungyeong's secret military provisions.

Him first mark in chalk is to align the ration officer entry in his profile with the cart ledger's time.

/story_contents/B021/actors/8/sections/비.en:
Her secret is a line of concealed inventory seen only at the rear gate and omitted from the copy she gave Yun Seorin.

Her guilt grows between the faces saved by the emergency rice she distributed and the succession deal prolonged by the entry she did not hand over.

She permits only partial disclosure through a copy of the ledger, not a full confession.

The SECRET entry opens only together with Bang Neuljae's bed-allocation log.

/story_contents/B021/actors/8/sections/관.en:
The night she gave Yun Seorin a copy of the ration ledger was a contract, and the morning she defied Nam Yungyeong's secret military provisions was a refusal.

Giving temporary tickets to Baek On's southbound families was an act witnessed in the rolls, and the dawn she shared beds for the emergency ration line with Bang Neuljae was an alliance.

At the same rear gate, one person received rice and another lost a place in the auction queue.

The endpoint leads to STORY-B021-K368.

/story_contents/B021/actors/8/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, Jeon Nagyeong faces the line driven by soaring prices and the demand to halt distribution outside the ice warehouse.

In Act 2, he ties the HP08 temperature log and XT02 auction relay to the cart clock.

In Act 3, he bears the cost of a ration halt for either pushing the cart or reporting the secret entry.

The story arc is STORY-B021-K368.

/story_contents/B021/actors/8/sections/분.en:
In ending α, Jeon Nagyeong pushes the cart into the square and distributes emergency rice.

In ending β, he hands the secret-provisions entry to the records office, breaking off the succession deal and halting rations that day.

The Bondang Certification Administration slot remains in place; only the branch splits into K376-OUT.

The decision at the time is to push the cart or report the concealed entry.

/story_contents/B021/actors/9/sections/정.en:
At the battery slot beneath the rack in the Amsa machine room, Transmission Relay answers to the call name Relay and records the sensor bus's uncertainty flag as a counter for computational instability.

It is an F-class fixed-facility rack. Its state slot is fixed solely to the Gwangjin Line, and it retains F05, separate from the human ID space.

Night vision and cross-facility routes were absent from its original design, and it has no complete long-term memory.

The display name Transmission Relay and identifier F05 are not renumbered.

/story_contents/B021/actors/9/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, Transmission Relay left only zone-key requests in the Amsa machine room duty log and kept cross-facility routes blocked by default.

The inspection sheet recorded only relay calibration values and battery cycles; independent battery authority was not part of the design.

B021 takes that duty log as its starting point and fixes the prohibition on memory forks in F05-PRE.

It did not activate the interpretation layer even when Kim Woochan checked the seal.

/story_contents/B021/actors/9/sections/가.en:
Custodial responsibility is tied to joint custody by the Suseo Construction House and the signature of the responsible human, Kim Woochan.

The maintenance party is identified only as the fictional successor house's service desk; no real company's product name is used in the main text.

The F05 hash is posted in the citizen-observer seal entry, and transfer requires three-party signatures.

The community regards Transmission Relay not as property but as the operator of an assigned slot.

/story_contents/B021/actors/9/sections/붕.en:
The collapse severed the sensor table and exposed the limit on battery allocation.

Transmission Relay was locked against filling gaps with fictitious values, leaving only measurement-unavailable flags in the log.

Even when a communications mycelium signal entered as fiber-optic noise, it filtered out false positives three times before reporting and did not issue an extermination order.

Even when the charging-slot alarm sounded, it answered requests for authority over the entire network with a refusal code.

/story_contents/B022/actors/0/sections/정.en:
In front of the chalkboard on the second floor of the Guro work crew building, Je Haon snaps a piece of chalk while covering a blank proficiency-score field with her palm.

As the Standards Alliance’s proficiency-score ledger keeper, she locks the ledger first when she sees a clerk trying to push numbers from the work-slowdown list out of it.

Of Korean origin, she grew up in the alleys of Guro’s workshops, and yesterday’s standards ink remains beneath her fingernails.

Her display name, Je Haon, and immutable identifier, K044, are not renumbered in subsequent placements.

/story_contents/B022/actors/0/sections/붕.en:
Before the Collapse, she tried to put restoration-service workers’ citizenship fields and proficiency scores side by side in one ledger, so that the Manufacturing Standards Alliance would spread through freedom of movement for workers rather than military supplies.

Her ambition was a chalkboard that would not place unregistered labor on the council agenda, and she first wrote the draft on the lid of a toolbox.

A note she left for her younger sibling—return the removal key only after the shift ends—would later become the seed of a debt.

Even when word from Amsa was late, she sealed the ledger itself first.

/story_contents/B022/actors/0/sections/가.en:
The Guro Alloy House invoked its heat-resistant alloy recipe for Guro’s high-temperature furnace to demand an observer’s seat at the proficiency-ledger chest.

Je Haon allowed only a joint inspection with Gang Minseo and did not stamp the proficiency field with a seal reserved for military supplies.

His standing in the community was demonstrated by the number of times he put work-crew shifts and scores on the same chalkboard, while labor unregistered for citizenship was left off the council agenda.

No real company name appears in his ledger.

/story_contents/B022/actors/0/sections/붕.en:
When Amsa demanded restoration-service registration instead of parts, internal security knocked on the striking workshops’ doors.

Je Haon sealed the tool-removal ledger until the council voted and kept her gloves on, unable to finish reading Kim Nayul’s clerks’ roster.

At the heart of her fear was the prospect of the union roster becoming a military household register, with proficiency scores serving as evidence for confinement.

Before addressing the removal permit, she covered with sealing tape the noise of the Night Sorting Group running the conveyor at Guro’s rear gate empty.

/story_contents/B022/actors/0/sections/생.en:
The crossroads came when she had to choose whether to protect the proficiency roster and bring the citizenship proposal before the council, or expose the manipulation of the work-slowdown list and risk her position as ledger keeper.

On the chalkboard, this overlapped with word from the West Sea Granary Theater that the Southwest fabrication depot was distributing freezer-compressor parts and Magok was verifying measurement logs.

Protecting the roster would preserve freedom of movement but halt removals for a day; exposing the manipulation would make security withdraw but leave the work crew’s scores blank.

That choice remains recorded as K044-TURN.

/story_contents/B022/actors/0/sections/현.en:
Je Haon conducts morning roll call as the proficiency-score ledger keeper for the Guro work crew.

Her position is maintained not by inheritance but solely by the public chalkboard and Jang Wooseok’s standards cross-verification logs.

HC07’s demand for exclusive service to the state is rejected, and labor unregistered for citizenship still does not enter the agenda field.

Her first use of the chalk is to match the keeper field in the Cast profile to the removal time.

/story_contents/B022/actors/0/sections/비.en:
Her secret is the removal-key time written in the note to her younger sibling, and the name of one apprentice she failed to call at that time.

Her guilt grows only between the military household register that the seal prevented and the work crew left idle by tools being held back for a day.

Because full disclosure could break a link in the union’s trust, she left only a procedure for partial disclosure.

The SECRET field opens only at the same time as Baek On’s joint citizenship petition.

/story_contents/B022/actors/0/sections/관.en:
The night she fixed Kim Nayul’s clerks’ roster in the ledger was a contract, and the dawn she reconciled scores with Jang Wooseok’s standards seals was an alliance of cross-verification.

Backing Baek On’s demand for refugee citizenship with records was an act of witnessing; at the same chalkboard, one person gained a score and another lost the right to remove tools.

The endpoint of the relationship ledger leads to STORY-B022-K044.

None of the relationships ended in betrayal alone.

/story_contents/B022/actors/0/sections/3.en:
At the Guro chalkboard, Je Haon places word from Amsa and the blank proficiency field under the same light.

She then ties observation of the HC07 recipe and the XT02 distribution of parts to the removal clock.

Finally, she bears the cost of a work-crew stoppage for either protecting the roster or exposing the manipulation.

The storyline identifier is fixed as STORY-B022-K044.

/story_contents/B022/actors/0/sections/분.en:
On one path, Je Haon protects the proficiency roster and brings the citizenship proposal before the council.

On the other, she exposes the manipulation of the work-slowdown list, risks her position as ledger keeper, and makes security withdraw.

The Standards Alliance slot is not deleted; only the branch identifier splits into K044-OUT.

The decision at the scene was to escort the roster or make the manipulated ledger public.

/story_contents/B022/actors/1/sections/정.en:
In front of the certification chest at the Magok archive, Je Raon picks up an access pass with its date erased using tongs and props it beside the heater.

As the keeper of technical-certification copies for Yangjae Machineworks Company, she folds shut the seal field when she sees a council member offer a certification stamp as a bargaining chip.

Of Korean origin, she grew up in the alleys by the Banghwa experimental building, and yesterday’s sealing cord has left a mark on her wrist.

Her display name, Je Raon, and immutable identifier, K072, are not renumbered.

/story_contents/B022/actors/1/sections/붕.en:
Before the Collapse, she tried to move medical, communications, and pump certifications into a public ledger rather than state ownership, and to become the Joint Technology Ledger’s records desk.

Her ambition was a copy kept simultaneously by the applicant state and the Magok archive, and she first wrote the draft in the access-lock log.

The time at which she entrusted the original to Im Sion on loan would later become the seed of a debt.

If she saw a confidential performance clause, she did not affix the seal.

/story_contents/B022/actors/1/sections/가.en:
The Magok Life House invoked its key for isolating the biometric dataset in the sealed experimental building’s windbreak chamber to demand an observer’s seat at the certification chest.

Je Raon allowed only a joint inspection with Jeong Hojun and did not add a clause giving priority access to raw materials to the certification terms.

His standing in the community was demonstrated by the number of times he left copies with the applicant state and in Magok at the same time, while exclusive purchase orders were rejected.

No real business name appears in his seal field.

/story_contents/B022/actors/1/sections/붕.en:
When rumors of counterfeit medicines and contaminated water converged, Je Raon put every certification stamp under renewed review and did not let exclusive-purchase vouchers leave the archive.

Her fear was that a single forged access pass would turn the entire archive into propaganda material for a powerful state.

She used isolation tape to block the smell of the Coolant-Index Colony growing a metallic film in the experimental building’s pipes before addressing the performance clause.

Even after the alarm stopped, she held the tongs, unable to read the last line of Choi Eunjae’s certification scope.

/story_contents/B022/actors/1/sections/생.en:
The crossroads came when she had to choose whether to retrieve the original records of the replication experiment and restore certification, or expose the council member who had concealed the confidential clause.

At the certification chest, this overlapped with word from the Incheon Trust Theater that Magok was correcting false alarms from orbital terminals and Garak was extending the family-reunification counseling desk.

Retrieving the original would save certification but release the access lock for a day; exposure would stop the propaganda but leave the joint-technology desk vacant.

The choice is K072-TURN.

/story_contents/B022/actors/1/sections/현.en:
Je Raon conducts access roll call as keeper of technical-certification copies at the Magok archive.

Choi Eunjae’s scope-transfer logs and Im Sion’s lock times maintain his position.

He brings Jeong Yura’s technology-sharing language into the certification terms only, and the confidential-performance field bears no seal.

His first use of the tongs is to match the keeper field in the profile to the copy time.

/story_contents/B022/actors/1/sections/비.en:
His secret is the time of the original’s loan, which he owes Im Sion, and one line of the performance clause that he viewed at that time.

His guilt grows between the propaganda stopped by the locked stamp and the contaminated-water rumors fueled by a certification desk left vacant for a day.

Instead of a full confession, he permits only partial disclosure through the review noticeboard.

The SECRET field opens only at the same time as Jeong Hojun witnesses the safety review.

/story_contents/B022/actors/1/sections/관.en:
The night he transferred Choi Eunjae’s certification scope into the ledger was almost a master-apprentice relationship, and the dawn he backed Im Sion’s access lock with a record was a contract.

Bringing Jeong Yura’s technology-sharing language into the terms was an alliance; in the same archive, one person gained certification and another lost access.

The endpoint leads to STORY-B022-K072.

No verbal agreement became a ledger for any of those relationships.

/story_contents/B022/actors/1/sections/3.en:
At the certification chest, Je Raon picks up the rumors of counterfeit medicines and contaminated water with the same tongs.

She then ties observation of the HC03 isolation key and correction of XT05 false alarms to the review clock.

Finally, she bears the cost of leaving the desk vacant for either escorting the original or exposing the council member.

The storyline is STORY-B022-K072.

/story_contents/B022/actors/1/sections/분.en:
On one path, Je Raon escorts the original from the replication experiment and restores certification.

On the other, she names the council member who concealed the confidential clause on the noticeboard, cutting off the propaganda channel.

The Yangjae Machineworks Company slot remains; only the branch splits into K072-OUT.

The decision at the time was to escort the original or disclose the clause.

/story_contents/B022/actors/1/arc/2/summ.en: Bears the cost of leaving the desk vacant for either escorting the original or exposing the council member

/story_contents/B022/actors/1/outcomes/1.en: Exposing the confidential clause blocks propaganda; the joint-technology desk is left vacant

/story_contents/B022/actors/2/sections/정.en:
At the entrance to the flooded Gunja–Seongsu tunnel, Myeong Gangsan shines a flashlight on the mark where the water-temperature gauge’s needle has stopped.

An explorer of flooded tunnels for the Seolgyo Register Government, he does not boast about manholes absent from the map; he records late reports as offenses.

Of Korean origin, he grew up in the alleys by the Seongsu pump room, and yesterday’s flood moss remains inside his boots.

His display name, Myeong Gangsan, and immutable identifier, K100, are not renumbered.

/story_contents/B022/actors/2/sections/붕.en:
Before the Collapse, he tried to chart the flooded bypass tunnel connecting the Gunja siding and Ttukseom pump on a public navigational map, so that common standards for water and parts would work beneath the tracks as well.

His ambition was a navigational map that recorded water depth and pump vibration in one ledger, and he first wrote the draft inside his helmet.

A bottle of floodwater sample he sent to Heo Gyeom would later become the seed of a debt.

He marked collapsed sections only when both the workshops and the defense force signed.

/story_contents/B022/actors/2/sections/가.en:
The Ttukseom Heat Source House invoked its right to connect to the underground heat source of the Ttukseom pump to demand an observer’s seat in the exploration ledger.

Myeong Gangsan allowed only a joint inspection with Park Nuri and did not put priority rights to waste heat on the bypass coordinates.

His standing in the community was demonstrated by the number of times he recorded water depth and vibration on the same line, while solo exploration toward Amsa was refused.

No real business name appears on his navigational map.

/story_contents/B022/actors/2/sections/붕.en:
When the central water-supply and parts contract expired, Myeong Gangsan reserved the bypass tunnel from Gunja exclusively for the Ttukseom pump room and refused to explore toward Amsa.

His fear was that the exploration route would be sold as an infiltration route for eastern patrol trains, bringing maintenance autonomy under a protection contract.

Before recording the coordinates, he covered with sealing tape the tracks where the Sewer Raccoon Clan marked its nighttime territory beneath a manhole cover.

After the alarm stopped, he held the water-temperature gauge, unable to read the last number in Jang Yerin’s inspection network.

/story_contents/B022/actors/2/sections/생.en:
The crossroads came when he had to choose whether to open an escort route through the bypass tunnel and end its exclusive reservation, or expose the infiltration-route markings and close the route for a day.

At the water-temperature gauge, this overlapped with word from the Korea Strait Theater that Garak’s distribution office was readjusting canned-food allotments and the Ttukseom workshops were sending sealed tools.

Opening the escort route would keep the pump working but leave an infiltration route; exposure would prevent the protection contract but keep the bypass water depth undisclosed for a day.

The choice is K101-TURN.

/story_contents/B022/actors/2/sections/현.en:
Myeong Gangsan conducts a water-temperature roll call as an explorer in the flooded Gunja–Seongsu tunnel.

His position is maintained by his contract with I Juntaek for the repair car’s coordinates and Heo Gyeom’s sample-receipt logs.

HC04’s demand for exclusive service to the state is rejected, and collapsed sections do not go on the navigational map without two signatures.

His first use of the flashlight is to match the explorer field in the profile to the water-depth time.

/story_contents/B022/actors/2/sections/비.en:
His secret is one line of infiltration markings beneath the manhole that he did not put on the sample bottle sent to Heo Gyeom.

His guilt grows between the pump protected by the exclusive reservation and the water-supply hours lost when he refused to go toward Amsa.

Instead of a full confession, he permits only partial disclosure through a ledger requiring two signatures.

The SECRET field opens only at the same time as Jang Yerin’s solo water-sampling log.

/story_contents/B022/actors/2/sections/관.en:
The night he gave bypass coordinates to I Juntaek’s Gunja repair car was a contract, and the dawn he sent a sample for Heo Gyeom’s alley-pump maintenance was an alliance.

Taking solo water samples to keep the numbers going when Jang Yerin’s inspection network stopped was a debt; in the same tunnel, one person gained coordinates and another lost the right to explore.

The endpoint leads to STORY-B022-K100.

Late reporting was excused in none of those relationships.

/story_contents/B022/actors/2/sections/3.en:
At the tunnel entrance, Myeong Gangsan puts word of the contract’s expiration and the exclusive reservation on the same water-temperature gauge.

He then ties observation of the HC04 heat source and XT03 sealed tools to the navigational-map clock.

Finally, he bears the cost of a gap in water-depth data for either opening the escort route or exposing the infiltration route.

The storyline is STORY-B022-K100.

/story_contents/B022/actors/2/sections/분.en:
On one path, Myeong Gangsan opens an escort route through the bypass tunnel and ends its exclusive reservation.

On the other, he exposes the infiltration-route markings, closes the route for a day, and refuses maintenance under a protection contract.

The Seolgyo Register Government slot remains; only the branch splits into K101-OUT.

The decision at the time was to organize an escort or disclose the infiltration markings.

/story_contents/B022/actors/2/arc/1/summ.en: Ties HC04 heat-source observation and XT03 sealed tools to the navigational-map clock
