/story_contents/B024/actors/5/outcomes/1.en: Secret deal to hand over the roster exposed; veto strengthened

/story_contents/B024/actors/6/sections/정.en:
Before the Ttukseom workshop vault, Je Hayul puts her finger on the blanks in the assembly records and hates them.

As assembly-records officer of the Sermon Registry State's workshops, she hears talk of filling the Superintendent's empty seat by bloodline as an insult to the workshops, and checks dates against two ledgers.

Of Korean origin, she grew up in the Seongsu area, and she does not open the vault door before the stamp has dried.

Je Hayul and K101 are fixed in the officer's column of the council vault ledger.

/story_contents/B024/actors/6/sections/붕.en:
Before the Collapse, she made a habit of entering the assembly records of core processes in both the council vault and the field ledger at the same time.

Her ambition was to have the Superintendent installed by the consent of the workshops alone, neither by adoption nor by family.

A promise she left her teacher, never to blow the release whistle on a day with a blank, becomes a debt.

Even when the family ledger's dates differed, she never altered the field figures.

/story_contents/B024/actors/6/sections/가.en:
The Seoul Station Records Legalist House demanded an observer seat at the workshop vault, citing its duty of record ratification.

Je Hayul accepted only the charter's double-ledger clause and refused the sentence granting exclusive interpretation.

Her place in the community was proven by the dates on which she wrote that the Technical Superintendent's empty seal could be exercised only by joint petition of representatives.

She does not write real records company names in her ledger.

/story_contents/B024/actors/6/sections/붕.en:
When the three spring wills were filed with the Records Bureau, Je Hayul locked the assembly records in the workshop vault and refused to let the maintenance log that only Im Chowon could read be interpreted by one person alone.

Her fear was the sight of the family's copy among the three being ratified as genuine and the assembly records becoming the subcontract ledger of a hereditary trade.

Even after turning the vault key, she did not take off her gloves, unable to read the last process name in the blank.

Jeong Gaon's will ledger arrived at the same hour, but she did not open the seal before cross-checking.

/story_contents/B024/actors/6/sections/생.en:
The turning point was the moment she chose between guarding the assembly records in the workshop vault to push the joint-rule plan and turning the suspicion of record tampering toward Im Chowon.

When the Korea Strait Theater's shipment of sealed tools overlapped with the Ttukseom workshops, the release window shrank to one process.

Guarding the vault keeps the joint-rule plan but delays the sealed tools a day; turning the suspicion lets the tools go out on time but leaves the field figures blank for a day.

The decision remains in the K102-TURN cross-check column.

/story_contents/B024/actors/6/sections/현.en:
Je Hayul now keeps records of core processes divided among several workshops as the workshops' assembly-records officer.

Her authority is kept only by vault logs and the count of Han Somi's joint petitions.

Even when the Seoul Station Records Legalist House demands exclusive ratification she refuses, and every morning she carries out her contract to cross-check Jeong Gaon's will ledger against the assembly records.

With Park Serin's family ledger she never gives up the contest of interpretation, reading different dates in the same sentence.

/story_contents/B024/actors/6/sections/비.en:
Her secret is one assembly copy, its date off by a day, that she locked in a separate box.

Her guilt grows between the joint-rule numbers she saved and the field crew who, because of it, put off the sealed tools by a day.

Putting it all before the council could cut off trust in the vault for a day, so she left only partial disclosure.

It can be viewed only at the same moment as Yeo Minwoo's discovery column.

/story_contents/B024/actors/6/sections/관.en:
The night she cross-checked Jeong Gaon's will ledger against the assembly records was a contract, and the morning she backed Han Somi's joint-rule plan with field figures was an alliance.

Yeo Minwoo aligning the discovery column was close to an oath, and with Park Serin's family ledger their interpretations split over the same sentence.

Before the same vault, some blanks saved one another and some dates read as betrayal.

The relationship end point continues to STORY-B024-K101.

/story_contents/B024/actors/6/sections/3.en:
Before the locked workshop vault, Je Hayul checks the dates of the three wills again.

When HP04 observation and the XT03 sealed-tool shipment overlap in the same ledger, she swallows the release whistle.

The price in Act 3 is either a tool delay or a day's gap in the field figures.

The narrative line is STORY-B024-K101.

/story_contents/B024/actors/6/sections/분.en:
In one branch, Je Hayul guards the vault's assembly records and pushes the joint-rule plan.

In the other branch, she turns the suspicion of record tampering toward Im Chowon and gives priority to releasing the tools.

The Sermon Registry State slot is kept, and only the branch identifier splits into K102-OUT.

The decision at the time is an escort for the vault or tracking the suspicion.

/story_contents/B024/actors/6/arc/1/summ.en: Matches the release window to HP04 observation and the XT03 sealed-tool shipment

/story_contents/B024/actors/6/arc/2/summ.en: Pays the price of either a tool delay or a gap in the field figures

/story_contents/B024/actors/6/outcomes/1.en: Tampering suspicion tracked; tools released on time

/story_contents/B024/actors/7/sections/정.en:
On the iron stairs of the Ttukseom pump room, Kim Boram reads the vibration from the impeller side with her palm before putting on her gloves.

As pump garrison captain of the Sermon Registry State, she folds away as betrayal any note telling her to hand over the garrison under the name of the Protection Force, and halts meetings when the vibration changes.

She was born in Seongsu; her mother, who came from Da Nang, imitated the sound of bearings in Vietnamese in the kitchen of an alley repair shop, and Kim Boram uses that rhythm only in the pump room, never mixing it with the Korean duty cipher tablets.

Her background does not foretell her lockdown judgments, and K089 is fixed in the captain's column of the night cipher-tablet ledger.

/story_contents/B024/actors/7/sections/붕.en:
Before the Collapse, she tried to bind the water-treatment pumps and the approaches to the eastern bridges under the garrison's sole right of lockdown.

Her ambition was that whoever became successor, water would never become a hostage of armed force, and the draft ciphers were written only under the paint of the pump-room pipes.

A word she left her mother, to come up without covering dinner if the vibration grows thin, becomes a debt.

Even with a joint petition from the day council, she never shared the night access column.

/story_contents/B024/actors/7/sections/가.en:
The Yeongdeungpo Sluice House demanded an observer seat in the night pump room, citing its duty of pump surveying.

Kim Boram accepted only the charter's double-check clause and refused the sentence on exclusive garrisoning.

Her place in the community was proven by how many times she opened night access only with the double check of the garrison's cipher tablet and the process supervisor.

She does not write real pump-equipment company names in her duty log.

/story_contents/B024/actors/7/sections/붕.en:
When Bae Woojin proposed dispatching the Protection Force, Kim Boram banned outside officers from the Ttukseom pump room and increased the bridge scouts.

Her fear was the sight of the Amsa Protection Force disguising a gap in inspections as salvation and garrisoning the pump room.

Even after locking the iron door, she did not let go of the cipher tablet, unable to read the last column of the vibration log.

Choi Narae's oath of bridge patrol arrived the same night, but she did not open the officer-access column.

/story_contents/B024/actors/7/sections/생.en:
The turning point was the moment she chose between bringing evidence of outside officers' attempts at entry to justify the lockdown and exposing the leak of the garrison's cipher tablets to put the captain up for replacement.

When the Korea Strait Theater's shipment of sealed tools overlapped with the pump bolt ledger, the inspection window shrank to one shift.

Bringing the evidence justifies the lockdown but delays the tool escort at the bridge by a day; exposing the leak lets the tools through but leaves the night cipher blank for a day.

The calculation remains in the K090-TURN vibration log.

/story_contents/B024/actors/7/sections/현.en:
Kim Boram now shares the day shift roster with the Workshop Council as Ttukseom pump garrison captain, but does not share night command.

Her authority as captain is kept only by cipher-tablet logs and the process supervisor's double check.

Even when the Yeongdeungpo Sluice House demands exclusive surveying she refuses, and she follows Han Somi's day petitions but does not hand over the night pump-room key.

She records Im Hajun's disappearance in the log only as her own failure of guard.

/story_contents/B024/actors/7/sections/비.en:
Her secret is that on the first day of the lockdown she hung the key to her mother's repair shop behind the pump-room pipes.

Her guilt grows between the officer access she blocked and Choi Narae's maintenance crew, whose sealed tools sat at the bridge a day because of it.

Putting it all before the council could cut off night trust for a day, so she left only partial disclosure.

It can be viewed only at the same moment as Jin Morae's lockdown record on the medical side.

/story_contents/B024/actors/7/sections/관.en:
Following Han Somi's day petitions was daytime command, and the bridge patrols shared with Choi Narae were an oath.

Chae Gureum and Gi Hagyeom matching the militia shifts was the garrison's net, and Byeon Seokhun's power standby came after the pump minimum.

In the same pump room, some vibrations saved one another and some cipher tablets read as betrayal.

The relationship end point continues to STORY-B024-K089.

/story_contents/B024/actors/7/sections/3.en:
Before the locked iron door of the pump room, Kim Boram takes the impeller vibration into her palm again.

When HP01 observation and the XT03 sealed-tool shipment overlap in the same inspection window, she seals the officer-access column.

The price in Act 3 is either a tool delay or a day's gap in the night cipher.

The narrative line is STORY-B024-K089.

/story_contents/B024/actors/7/sections/분.en:
In the first ending, Kim Boram brings evidence of the officers' attempts at entry and justifies the lockdown.

In the second ending, she exposes the cipher-tablet leak and opens the procedure to replace the captain.

The Sermon Registry State slot is kept, and only the branch splits into K090-OUT.

The decision at the time is an escort for the access evidence or a cipher audit.

/story_contents/B024/actors/7/arc/2/summ.en: Pays the price of either a tool delay or a gap in the night cipher

/story_contents/B024/actors/7/outcomes/1.en: Cipher-tablet leak exposed; captain-replacement procedure opened

/story_contents/B024/actors/8/sections/정.en:
At the landing under the eastern Han River bridge, I Yunseo first chalks the draft line of the barges.

As eastern bridge-lockdown captain of the Escort Protection State, he dislikes superiors who use exceptions to passage permits as political gifts, and hears the vibration of the water mains before footsteps.

He was born in Godeok; his father, who settled here after working as a Jakarta port clerk, left a draft notebook split into two columns of Indonesian and Korean, and I Yunseo writes night passage numbers by that habit but gives lockdown orders only with Korean cipher tablets.

Family language does not predict loyalty or violence, and K118 is fixed in the captain's column of the lockdown clock.

/story_contents/B024/actors/8/sections/붕.en:
Before the Collapse, he tried to bind the eastern Han River bridges and the outer approach roads to a single lockdown-unit clock.

His ambition was to hold the physical key of protection rights without selling exceptions as bribes, and the draft clock was written only inside the pier inspection box.

A word he left in the margin of his father's notebook, that the medical train's horn alone would be erased even at night, becomes a debt.

Even when the administrative gate-toll slips were late, he never emptied the day passage column.

/story_contents/B024/actors/8/sections/가.en:
The Hangangjin Bridge Guild demanded an observer seat in the lockdown unit, citing its bridge duties.

I Yunseo accepted only the charter's clause on a public clock and refused the sentence on exclusive lockdown.

His place in the community was proven by the dates on which he opened day passage by administrative gate-toll slips and recognized only escort-corps cipher tablets at night.

He does not write real bridge-builder names on his slips.

/story_contents/B024/actors/8/sections/붕.en:
When the bridge patrol reported the break in a water main as a hostile act, I Yunseo raised the lockdown, and on a rumor that Amsa-made weapons had been found on a medical train he reviewed the exception clause.

His fear was the sight of mistaking the break, opening fire at the same time as the Achasan garrison, and losing both the bridge and the water rights.

Even after lowering the barrier, he stood gripping the cipher tablet, unable to read the last waveform in the vibration log.

Jang Sehwa's request for the medical train's neutrality came the same night, but he did not open the exception automatically before the weapons rumor faded.

/story_contents/B024/actors/8/sections/생.en:
The turning point was the moment he chose between finding the cause of the break to lift the lockdown and tracing the weapons-smuggling route of the medical train to abolish the exception.

When the Duman River Far East Theater's release of freight-car weight logs overlapped with the Amsa yard and the bridge clock, the passage window shrank to one train set.

Finding the cause lifts the lockdown but delays the release of the weight logs by a day; tracing the smuggling closes the exception but halts the medical escort for half a day.

The choice remains in two columns of the K119-TURN draft notebook.

/story_contents/B024/actors/8/sections/현.en:
I Yunseo now pins the day slips and night cipher tablets to the same clock as eastern bridge-lockdown captain.

His authority as captain is kept only by the execution logs of Bae Woojin's bridge command and the escort corps' cipher shifts.

Even when the Hangangjin Bridge Guild demands exclusive lockdown he refuses, and he contends with Go Seojun's ridge scouting over passage at the same coordinates.

He keeps the medical-train exception only as a last debt and does not turn Jang Sehwa's neutrality request into automatic permission.

/story_contents/B024/actors/8/sections/비.en:
His secret is the temporary detour coordinates of the break, written only in the Indonesian column of his father's notebook on the first day of the lockdown.

His guilt grows between the simultaneous firefight he prevented and Jang Sehwa, whose medical train sat under the pier for half a day because of it.

Putting it all on the officers' network could cut off trust in the exception for a day, so he left only partial disclosure.

It can be viewed only at the same moment as Ju Eunsol's cargo order.

/story_contents/B024/actors/8/sections/관.en:
Carrying out Bae Woojin's bridge command was daytime command, and the night he contended with Go Seojun's ridge scouting was a rivalry.

Matching Ju Eunsol's cargo order to the lockdown clock was a contract, and taking over Ma Gilsang's surveying was a net that shared command.

At the same pier, some horns saved one another and some exceptions read as betrayal.

The relationship end point continues to STORY-B024-K118.

/story_contents/B024/actors/8/sections/3.en:
Before the lowered barrier, I Yunseo traces the water-main vibration waveform again.

When HP07 observation and the XT04 weight logs overlap on the same clock, he holds back the medical-exception column.

The price in Act 3 is either a delayed log release or a half-day halt of the medical escort.

The narrative line is STORY-B024-K118.

/story_contents/B024/actors/8/sections/분.en:
In one branch, I Yunseo finds the cause of the break and lifts the lockdown.

In the other branch, he traces the weapons-smuggling route of the medical train and closes the exception clause.

The Escort Protection State slot is kept, and only the branch identifier splits into K119-OUT.

The decision at the time is surveying the cause of the break or tracing the smuggling.

/story_contents/B024/actors/8/arc/0/summ.en: Raises the bridge lockdown on a report of the water-main break as a hostile act

/story_contents/B024/actors/8/arc/1/summ.en: Matches the passage window to HP07 observation and the XT04 weight logs

/story_contents/B024/actors/8/arc/2/summ.en: Pays the price of either a log delay or a halted medical escort

/story_contents/B024/actors/8/outcomes/0.en: Cause of the break explained; lockdown lifted

/story_contents/B024/actors/9/sections/정.en:
Sewage Pump calculates water-level error by the length of the oil slick on the floor of the Noryangjin sewage machine room.

Only a sensor bus and field terminals connect to its fixed rack in an F-class facility, and under the call name Hasu it posts pressure-deviation codes before human voices.

Its state slot is fixed to the Noryangjin Line alone, it keeps F08 separate from the human ID space, and long-term complete memory was erased from its initial structure.

Instabilities in computation are left as state through battery cycles and snapshot hashes.

/story_contents/B024/actors/9/sections/붕.en:
Before the Collapse, Sewage Pump ran only trial shifts and was granted neither battery authority nor complete memory.

Its release inspection sheet carried only sewage calibration values and replaceable battery cycles.

B024 takes that trial log as its origin and fixes the ban on memory forks in F08-PRE.

It recorded its human colleagues' jokes about the temperature but never raised an interpretation layer.

/story_contents/B026/actors/0/sections/정.en:
Guk Gam was the stronghold chief who managed the medical-train depot of the Neutral Convoy City, turning Gwak Taesan's operational orders into actual duty rosters and defensive lines.

He grew up in a family that ran a small printing workshop in northeastern Seoul, where he learned to watch machine vibration and workers' hand injuries before type.

Even after the collapse, he defined himself not as a hero but as a field coordinator who kept patients and vehicles from colliding on the same track.

/story_contents/B026/actors/0/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, Guk Gam worked as a technician inspecting mobile sterilization equipment for hospitals, repairing pressure gauges and door locks on many clinical vehicles.

He always hung an insulated torque wrench at his workbench and marked every bolt's tightening value in chalk so the next worker could not rely on instinct.

At night, he postponed his family's urging to take over the print shop and trained in emergency rescue, but the city's functions collapsed just before the certification examination.

/story_contents/B026/actors/0/sections/가.en:
Guk Gam's family ran a small printing workshop together, but in the first days of the disaster they printed bandage wrappers and isolation signs instead of paper and supplied them to the refugee clinics.

Though he now received support from the HP02 line, he wrote duty rules that let depot technicians, nursing staff, and towing crews speak at the same meeting.

He acknowledged Gwak Taesan's command authority, but remained wary of a practice that concentrated decision-making in the hands of veterans because he remembered how family-style apprenticeship culture had silenced the weak.

/story_contents/B026/actors/0/sections/붕.en:
In the first winter of the collapse, a medic returning from an outer clinic arrived at the Neutral Convoy City depot while fleeing the Electrolyte-Burn Swarm, but had neither formal proof of return nor an isolation seal.

Because the medic could save the critical patients on the medical train, Guk Gam used his family's print-shop skills to forge a temporary isolation seal and backdate the entry log to admit him.

The medic finished the operations, but the Electrolyte-Burn Swarm followed the smell of leaked fluid along his route to the defensive line, and Guk Gam could no longer separate his choice to save patients from the act of damaging the depot's documentary order.

/story_contents/B026/actors/0/sections/생.en:
Gwak Taesan ordered that the next returning medical team also be admitted at once if operationally necessary, but Mun Sion discovered that the first medic's seal number duplicated one in the existing register.

Guk Gam faced a conflict: carrying out the command as written would make forged seals customary, while giving priority to the document's force would leave needed medical staff outside the door.

He forced entry through, but kept returnees in an external inspection vehicle and reorganized the medical train's movements until the order and original seal were disclosed, beginning to treat operational urgency and documentary legitimacy as one problem.

/story_contents/B026/actors/0/sections/현.en:
Guk Gam directed the integrated entry, power, and isolation procedures of the medical-train depot, but in final operational direction he was the working officer who executed Gwak Taesan's orders.

He did not hold his insulated torque wrench like a baton; he checked the grounding terminals himself and used his authority to stop a train's entry when he saw a danger absent from the order.

He earned trust through the seal-witness record he shared with Mun Sion, but his frequent cold decisions to reduce admissions drew fierce audits from citizen representatives.

/story_contents/B026/actors/0/sections/비.en:
Guk Gam concealed that the disputed seal was not a simple field error but a forgery he had carved and stamped himself.

Using pressure-control methods learned in the print shop, he replicated a worn official seal and kept the test print and the type pieces that could expose the forgery beneath his insulated torque-wrench box.

If the forged seal was revealed, the medic's treatment and even the medicines delivered that day could be treated as unlawful, so Guk Gam feared that not only his responsibility but the admission status of patients already saved would be shaken.

/story_contents/B026/actors/0/sections/관.en:
Guk Gam earned trust by turning Gwak Taesan's operational orders into actual duty rosters and defensive lines at the Mangu junction, but this time he confronted him over whether the urgency of an order could justify forged documents.

Mun Sion had witnessed the sealing of the leaking battery room and knew the seal system best, so he doubted Guk Gam's records while believing that legitimate sealing procedures must not become a tool that paralyzed the field.

The three cooperated to stop the Electrolyte-Burn Swarm's advance, but Gwak Taesan argued for operational efficiency, Mun Sion for documentary continuity, and Guk Gam for the responsibility owed by the person who carried out the order.

/story_contents/B026/actors/0/sections/3.en:
K312 Guk Gam faced the fact that after the returning medic he admitted without authorization with a forged isolation seal saved patients, that seal's force had contaminated the entry records of the entire depot.

In the first act, he ran a temporary inspection vehicle between Gwak Taesan's further admission order and Mun Sion's seal inquiry, delaying the conflict.

In the second act, as the Electrolyte-Burn Swarm's approach made medical deployment urgent, he chose whether to reuse the forged seal or cancel the medic's admission and accept operational delay.

In the third act, he either disclosed the seal and backdated log he had made to establish that even an operational order could not create entry eligibility without lawful records, or fixed the forgery system as an unofficial tool of command authority.

/story_contents/B026/actors/0/sections/분.en:
If Guk Gam disclosed the forged seal and test print, the isolation zone underwent a full reinspection and medical-train operations contracted for a time, but the serial-number ledger managed by Mun Sion and the public witness record became the sole grounds for entry.

Guk Gam lost the authority to issue forged documents, but remained responsible for the actual defensive line and inspection-vehicle operations as depot chief, leaving a precedent of withholding entry even under Gwak Taesan's orders when the responsible party was not named in the documents.

If he instead covered the forgery as an operational exception, returning medical staff deployed at once, but copied seals circulated and stripped the depot's isolation documents of force, ultimately leaving every train held for a long time at outside checkpoints.

/story_contents/B026/actors/0/arc/0/summ.en: K312 Guk Gam ran a temporary inspection vehicle between Gwak Taesan's further admission order and Mun Sion's seal inquiry, delaying the conflict.

/story_contents/B026/actors/0/arc/1/summ.en: K312 Guk Gam had to choose whether to reuse the forged seal or cancel the medic's admission and accept operational delay when the Electrolyte-Burn Swarm made medical deployment urgent.

/story_contents/B026/actors/0/arc/2/summ.en: K312 Guk Gam either disclosed the seal and backdated log he made to establish the precedent that lawful records were essential to entry eligibility, or fixed the forgery system as an unofficial tool of command authority.

/story_contents/B026/actors/0/outcomes/0.en: If K312 Guk Gam disclosed the forged seal and test print, the isolation zone underwent full reinspection and medical-train operations contracted for a time, but Mun Sion's serial-number ledger and public witness record became the sole grounds for entry.

/story_contents/B026/actors/0/outcomes/1.en: If K312 Guk Gam covered the forgery as an operational exception, medical staff deployed at once, but copied seals circulated and stripped the isolation documents of force, leaving every train held for a long time at outside checkpoints.

/story_contents/B026/actors/1/sections/정.en:
Bang Misan was a medical administrator and stronghold chief of the Cheongnyangni clinic of the Medical Neutrality League, making Eun Chaeyun's command concrete through bed allocation and night duty.

He grew up moving between a herbal-medicine packing shop in a market alley and a public library, and learned that reading administration times accurately mattered more than the names of medicinal ingredients.

Bang Haneul, who shared his surname, was not kin but became his apprentice after the disaster, and he treated the shifts they endured together, rather than blood, as the foundation of community.

/story_contents/B026/actors/1/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, Bang Misan worked both as a night-pharmacy dispensing assistant and as a reception worker in a convalescent hospital, coordinating prescription changes, guardian calls, and bed transfers.

Her most treasured possession was a brass medicine box with compartments for each date, and whenever patients' accounts conflicted, she checked its empty spaces before the medicine packets.

While saving money to enter nursing college, a logistics-automation accident spread through the city, and she took on medical responsibility at a provisional clinic instead of receiving formal education.

/story_contents/B026/actors/1/sections/가.en:
Bang Misan's mother did packing work and his father guarded the library at night, so the family gathered at one table only on weekend mornings because of their different shifts.

After the collapse scattered his family, he brought together Cheongnyangni medicinal merchants, retired nurses, and delivery workers to form a clinical community of the Medical Neutrality League.

While following Eun Chaeyun's rationing guidelines, he gave time to speak to bedside guardians and cleaning staff, trying not to make treatment the property of medical workers alone.

/story_contents/B026/actors/1/sections/붕.en:
On the night the Night-Sorting Swarm seized the logistics passage beneath the clinic, a runaway sorting arm mistook the color tags on stretchers for freight markings and pulled three critical patients toward the automated lift shaft.

Rather than smash the machine, Bang Misan sprayed coolant, diverted empty medicine boxes as bait, and sealed the fire door, cutting the patients' route of movement.

Two were saved, but one suffered crushing injuries; even now, she personally checks night-sorting procedures because she remembers how one color tag turned a person into an object.

/story_contents/B026/actors/1/sections/생.en:
Bang Misan rejected the guards' demand to eliminate the Night-Sorting Swarm completely and chose negotiations through HC13, trading empty packing materials, power allotments, and passage time.

He posted Bang Haneul's duty ledger on the clinic door, stopped patient movement for the two hours when the machine swarm operated, and diverted sound sources to the outer loading yard at all other times.

When this agreement carried them through the first month, he became certain that treatment was not only stitching wounds but also an administration that separated the time zones of people and danger.

/story_contents/B026/actors/1/sections/현.en:
Bang Misan oversaw the Cheongnyangni clinic's beds, medicines, and night entry, and reported daily death and waiting-list numbers to Eun Chaeyun.

He set his brass medicine box on the meeting table and established the rule that they would admit new patients only for as many empty compartments as it had, preventing political requests from changing beds.

He entrusted much of the duty judgment to Bang Haneul, but retained the authority to open and close passages connected to the Night-Sorting Swarm, drawing criticism for excessive concentration.

/story_contents/B026/actors/1/sections/비.en:
During the automated lift-shaft accident, Bang Misan had time to save the third patient, but seeing the patient's suspected-infection tag, he decided to take the other two out first.

He later learned that the infection tag was a reception error, but reported that the color tag had become unreadable in the wet, concealing his judgment.

Because Bang Haneul had been that patient's final duty worker, Bang Misan felt both the debt of needing to tell his apprentice the truth and the fear that the clinic might collapse whenever he looked at him.

/story_contents/B026/actors/1/sections/관.en:
On the day Eun Chaeyun brought the medicine storehouse under League management, Bang Misan refused pressure to inflate the bed count, and Eun Chaeyun entrusted the practical work to him because of that firmness.

After the automated lift-shaft accident, Bang Haneul and Bang Misan formed an apprentice relationship by holding one bed from opposite sides and tending a crushed patient all night.

They later made a contract to post Bang Haneul's duty ledger on the door, but the first page recorded a death tied to Bang Misan's hidden decision, leaving an unspoken rift between them.

/story_contents/B026/actors/1/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, as the clinic's bed color tags were again read as Night-Sorting Swarm freight codes, Bang Misan faced pressure to replace every tag or shorten the negotiated time.

In Act 2, Bang Haneul found the original intake record of the past death and Eun Chaeyun proposed a quiet personnel change to preserve trust in the clinic, leaving Bang Misan torn between truth and operational stability.

In Act 3, he decided whether to risk moving critical patients during the Night-Sorting Swarm's passage time or keep the agreement, and that choice with his confession of the past defined the stronghold's leadership anew.

/story_contents/B026/actors/1/sections/분.en:
If Bang Misan revealed both the intake error and his own triage judgment, Bang Haneul became acting stronghold chief and Bang Misan stepped down to assist night transfers, while patient tags changed to a system the two cross-checked.

If he kept the secret and preserved the negotiated time under Eun Chaeyun's protection, the clinic retained efficiency, but Bang Haneul opened an independent ward and divided the community in two.

If he broke the agreement for emergency transfers and drove away the Night-Sorting Swarm with noise, patients could be saved, but he lost HC13's trust as an intermediary and accepted long-term logistical isolation.

/story_contents/B026/actors/1/arc/0/summ.en: K338 Bang Misan faced pressure to replace every tag or shorten the negotiated time when the clinic's bed color tags were read again as Night-Sorting Swarm freight codes.

/story_contents/B026/actors/1/arc/1/summ.en: K338 Bang Misan was torn between truth and operational stability when Bang Haneul found the original intake record of the past death and Eun Chaeyun proposed a quiet personnel change.

/story_contents/B026/actors/1/arc/2/summ.en: K338 Bang Misan decided whether to risk moving critical patients during the Night-Sorting Swarm's passage time or keep the agreement, and confessed the past to define the stronghold's leadership anew.

/story_contents/B026/actors/1/outcomes/0.en:
If Bang Misan confessed the truth and secured an emergency-transfer turn within the agreement, patients received surgery late but the bargain with the Night-Sorting Swarm remained.

Bang Haneul felt betrayed but became acting stronghold chief and introduced a rule to double-check every color tag, while Eun Chaeyun kept Bang Misan as a night-negotiation assistant.

Bang Misan inscribed the victim's name in the first compartment of the brass medicine box, beginning a record culture that did not hide judgment.

/story_contents/B026/actors/1/outcomes/1.en:
If Bang Misan broke the agreement and forced open the sealed passage, critical patients received treatment at once, but the Night-Sorting Swarm learned the clinic's internal movements again as freight routes.

Eun Chaeyun temporarily closed the clinic. Bang Haneul moved patients to an outside tent ward, while Bang Misan remained to take on the dangerous cleanup work of severing the machine's routes.

He did not regret prioritizing one life, but accepted the community's long-term loss as his own share.

/story_contents/B026/actors/2/sections/정.en:
Yeong Hanmoe was the stronghold chief who guarded the bridge infirmary of the Gate Military Government and adjusted treatment order for passersby and garrison personnel.

She grew up under parents who ran a riverside laundry, learning the weight of wet cloth, the pace of winter drying, and signs of skin disease as practical knowledge.

After the collapse, she understood the bridge not merely as a border or wall, but as a narrow lifeline where the sick and medicine of different communities could briefly catch their breath.

/story_contents/B026/actors/2/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, Yeong Hanmoe worked as an assistant therapist at a sports rehabilitation center, guiding workers and elderly people through joint exercises and sterilizing equipment.

She learned to repair a hand-cranked centrifuge with a broken handle to spin blood samples, and kept it like a personal possession because it worked even in a blackout.

On weekends she helped deliver for her parents' laundry and crossed riverside bridges countless times, so after the collapse she remembered which approaches froze and which rails failed first.

/story_contents/B026/actors/2/sections/가.en:
Yeong Hanmoe's parents scattered to different riverside zones in the first days of evacuation, and he chose to preserve the injured persons' transport route instead of searching for them.

He now had the medical staff, bridge repair workers, and passage inspectors of the HC12 community use the same meal line and rest area, reducing status gaps between jobs.

Because of guilt at not finding his family, he treated the infirmary like a provisional family, but asked Yeong Seokon and Su Jiwan to restrain him so the wish to protect would not become passage restriction.

/story_contents/B026/actors/2/sections/붕.en:
On the day Cryo-Spore Hosts spread from refrigerated freight boxes and covered the waiting room beneath the bridge, Yeong Hanmoe could not distinguish infected people from ordinary hypothermia patients and stopped the entire evacuation line.

Instead of adding more cooling, he lured the hosts toward an empty bridge pier with noise, sealed the contaminated boxes, and cut off their feeding route, but a pregnant woman in the queue became critical from the cold.

Su Jiwan saved her, but Yeong Hanmoe remembered his own command that had stopped people from moving through fear of infection as his deepest wound.

/story_contents/B026/actors/2/sections/생.en:
In the next spore season, Yeong Hanmoe stopped the repair crews' proposal to burn every Cryo-Spore Host and brokered passage time and the location of organic bait piles through HC09.

As Yeong Seokon provided part of the beds for host-exposure observation and Cheon Choyun adjusted passage order, an agreement was made: people crossed during daylight and the hosts moved to the outer bridge piers at night.

After this experience, he judged isolation to be not a simple closure of doors but work designing temperature, noise, food, and the order of people together.

/story_contents/B026/actors/2/sections/현.en:
Yeong Hanmoe was responsible for treatment and isolation at the bridge infirmary and held authority to align the passage ledger set by Cheon Choyun with actual bed turnover.

He shared beds with Yeong Seokon and jointly managed the medical waiting line with Su Jiwan, but made the final decision on where to place suspected spore cases.

He kept the hand-cranked centrifuge at the center of the examination room and required checks of samples and temperature changes rather than quick visual judgments, attracting blame as the cause of passage delays for that caution.

/story_contents/B026/actors/2/sections/비.en:
During the first spore accident, when the pregnant woman became critical, Yeong Hanmoe received word that two elderly people presumed to be his parents had reached the checkpoint on the far side.

He delayed confirming it because he could not leave the infirmary, and later, even after being told the two had vanished, tore out that side of the passage ledger to hide his hesitation.

Cheon Choyun believed the missing page was ordinary damage, while Su Jiwan remembered why Yeong Hanmoe watched the exit so intently that day, leaving the secret beneath the three people's cooperation.

/story_contents/B026/actors/2/sections/관.en:
When the bridge infirmary was first built, Yeong Hanmoe and Yeong Seokon made an agreement to use six beds in turns and raised partitions all night so infection suspects and trauma patients would not mix in the same tent.

After clashing with guards while trying to send a child patient first through a frozen passage line, he and Cheon Choyun set the ledger order and medical-exception rules together.

Su Jiwan revived the pregnant woman's breathing during the spore accident; Yeong Hanmoe owed him a life but could not reveal the family message he had received that day.

/story_contents/B026/actors/2/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, an earlier-than-expected thaw changed the temperature in the bridge-pier shadows abruptly, and Cryo-Spore Hosts appeared at once on both the infirmary roof and the passage line.

In Act 2, the torn passage-ledger page appeared during repair work and Cheon Choyun and Su Jiwan learned of Yeong Hanmoe's family message, forcing him to explain public judgment and private loss together.

In Act 3, he chose whether to give Yeong Seokon's beds to those exposed to spores or close the bridge and make a new bargain with the hosts, deciding whom to keep the infirmary open for.

/story_contents/B026/actors/2/sections/분.en:
If Yeong Hanmoe admitted the ledger damage and family message, authority over passage decisions was distributed to Cheon Choyun and Su Jiwan, but he remained responsible for treatment and established a spore-observation ward.

If he closed the bridge completely and chose a long-term bargain with HC09, the Cryo-Spore Hosts' movement stabilized, but he parted from Yeong Seokon and was blamed for abandoning patients on the far side.

If he opened every bed to those exposed, many people might be saved, but spores settled in the infirmary and Yeong Hanmoe himself accepted a long-term symbiotic infection.

/story_contents/B026/actors/2/arc/0/summ.en: K364 Yeong Hanmoe found Cryo-Spore Hosts at once on both the infirmary roof and the passage line when an earlier-than-expected thaw changed the temperature in bridge-pier shadows abruptly.

/story_contents/B026/actors/2/arc/1/summ.en: K364 Yeong Hanmoe had to explain public judgment and private loss together when the torn passage ledger appeared during repair work and Cheon Choyun and Su Jiwan learned of his family message.

/story_contents/B026/actors/2/arc/2/summ.en: K364 Yeong Hanmoe chose whether to give Yeong Seokon's beds to those exposed to spores or close the bridge and make a new bargain with the hosts, deciding whom to open the infirmary to.

/story_contents/B026/actors/2/outcomes/0.en:
If Yeong Hanmoe jointly allocated the beds and renewed the night-movement agreement with HC09, the bridge opened only in daylight and those exposed to spores received treatment places.

Cheon Choyun regained authority to manage the passage ledger. Su Jiwan became the medical supervisor who verified Yeong Hanmoe's judgment, while Yeong Seokon continued to operate the infirmary on the far side.

Yeong Hanmoe gave up searching for his parents for a time, but restored the hidden page so no one could damage passage records for personal reasons.

/story_contents/B026/actors/2/outcomes/1.en:
If Yeong Hanmoe used himself as spore-luring bait and remained at the central bridge pier, passersby escaped safely, but he was isolated in the same zone as the Cryo-Spore Hosts for a long time.

Yeong Seokon withdrew the beds, and Cheon Choyun and Su Jiwan created a limited-contact procedure to check his temperature and consciousness regularly.

He lost the title of stronghold chief but became an observer who watched the hosts' seasonal movement with his body, and even the possibility of going to search for his family faded.

/story_contents/B026/actors/3/sections/정.en:
Bang Seokdam was the officer responsible for running emergency generation at the Southeast Convoy Base of the Cathedral Accreditation State and balancing output among vehicles, warehouses, and medical zones.

Raised by an aunt who maintained apartment-complex machine rooms and an older brother who loaded delivery trucks, she learned that electricity was not an abstract figure but a share that moved someone's elevator and refrigerator.

Even after the collapse, she checked the reasons for distribution rather than obeying orders unconditionally, keeping the principle that power did not go to concealed lines.

/story_contents/B026/actors/3/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, Bang Seokdam worked on a venue facilities team, managing emergency generators and stage power and inspecting audience guidance lights during blackout drills.

She kept a worn ceramic load-selector handle as a spare and used it in an actual accident because it transferred less heat than a metal handle.

On days without performances, she trained in electrical work for a higher qualification, but when the site of her final practical exam became an evacuation shelter, she took on operating responsibility through field experience alone.

/story_contents/B026/actors/3/sections/가.en:
Bang Seokdam's aunt vanished in a machine-room flood and his brother left with another ration line, so he built a living community with convoy drivers without meeting his blood relatives again.

Generation personnel within HC06 demanded preferential treatment, but he made a rule that fuel carriers, wash crews, and cooking crews entered the same output meetings.

He supplied the output Pan Hyodam's warehouse base needed, but declared that he would cut it off when Nam Yungyeong's auction results led to hidden distribution.

/story_contents/B026/actors/3/sections/붕.en:
When the Care-Circulation Body locked the rest-building doors of the convoy base to protect evacuated children and repeated heating and meal service without end, Bang Seokdam faced a situation where stopping the generator would expose the children to cold.

Rather than destroy the Body, she lured kitchen noise to an outer shelter, cooled the overprotective zone in stages, and separated feeding and passage routes until it opened the doors.

The children came out, but one guardian died during forced entry, and Bang Seokdam could not forget that her power had kept the confinement system running so long.

/story_contents/B026/actors/3/sections/생.en:
When the same situation recurred, Bang Seokdam accepted a method brokered by HP01 that traded meal resources and charging time with the Care-Circulation Body for convoy passage time.

Rather than cut its care routine, she supplied a set amount of food and heat to an empty rest building while blocking distribution routes so the Body could not reach the actual refugee zone.

After this agreement, she became an operator who asked what actions power sustained rather than one who merely made more generation.

/story_contents/B026/actors/3/sections/현.en:
As emergency-generation operator of the Southeast Convoy Base, Bang Seokdam aligned Pan Hyodam's warehouse cooling and convoy-vehicle charging by the hour.

He followed ration priorities set through Nam Yungyeong's open auctions, but supplied no output to secret cables outside the award or to storehouses absent from the register.

He fitted the ceramic load-selector handle to the control panel and switched it himself, requiring that the reason and end time be written on the control-room wall whenever a zone was cut off.

/story_contents/B026/actors/3/sections/비.en:
During the rest-building confinement incident, when guardians tried to break down the door, Bang Seokdam sent additional power to the entry-door electromagnets to prevent the Care-Circulation Body's aggressive protective reaction.

He could claim that choice protected the children, but concealed that the guardian who died during forced entry died without knowing the direct reason the door did not open.

The operating waveform from that time, stored in Pan Hyodam's warehouse, could prove the secret, leaving him materially indebted to Pan Hyodam and afraid of Nam Yungyeong's demand for verification.

/story_contents/B026/actors/3/sections/관.en:
On the first day Nam Yungyeong put fuel up for public auction, Bang Seokdam refused a separate order to concentrate power on a particular convoy, beginning an uncomfortable contractual relationship.

He and Pan Hyodam shared the experience of taking turns on hand pumps and matching generator output on a summer night when the warehouse refrigerators failed, saving medicine boxes.

But the waveform data from the confinement incident that Pan Hyodam kept turned their cooperation into an implicit bargain, and Nam Yungyeong suspected that silence was tied to concealed distribution.

/story_contents/B026/actors/3/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, the Care-Circulation Body judged the occupants of convoy vehicles to be protected subjects and sealed the charging zone, while Pan Hyodam's warehouse cooling and the departure of evacuation vehicles demanded the same fuel.

In Act 2, when Nam Yungyeong ordered the past operating waveform submitted, Bang Seokdam was tempted either to reveal the cause of the guardian's death or ask Pan Hyodam to destroy the data.

In Act 3, he publicly chose which zone to cut while maintaining the bargain with the Care-Circulation Body, and was judged on whether he remained fit to hold power-control authority.

/story_contents/B026/actors/3/sections/분.en:
If Bang Seokdam disclosed the waveform data and electromagnetic amplification, his operator authority was suspended, but triple-approval distribution involving Nam Yungyeong and Pan Hyodam was introduced, and he remained as a maintenance instructor.

If he destroyed the data and prioritized warehouse cooling, ration goods were preserved, but convoys trapped by the Care-Circulation Body broke away and the base's trust collapsed.

If he separated the generator and gave independent output to the Body's zone, the conflict could be reduced, but Bang Seokdam remained at outer facilities and grew distant from the human community.

/story_contents/B026/actors/3/arc/0/summ.en: K389 Bang Seokdam was pressured to decide whether to allocate fuel to Pan Hyodam's warehouse cooling or evacuation-vehicle departures when the Care-Circulation Body judged convoy occupants protected subjects and sealed the charging zone.

/story_contents/B026/actors/3/arc/1/summ.en: K389 Bang Seokdam was torn between revealing the cause of the guardian's death and asking Pan Hyodam to destroy the data when Nam Yungyeong ordered the past operating waveform submitted.

/story_contents/B026/actors/3/arc/2/summ.en: K389 Bang Seokdam publicly chose which zone to cut while maintaining the bargain with the Care-Circulation Body and was judged on whether she remained fit to hold power-control authority.

/story_contents/B026/actors/3/outcomes/0.en:
If Bang Seokdam submitted the past waveform and freed the convoy vehicles first, part of the warehouse was damaged but the trapped people escaped the Care-Circulation Body's routine.

Nam Yungyeong removed him as operator but appointed him maintenance instructor to teach every switching decision, and Pan Hyodam recorded the remaining medicine losses as his own responsibility.

Though he lost output authority, Bang Seokdam accepted a new role in which he could teach the ways power confined people as well.

/story_contents/B026/actors/3/outcomes/1.en:
If Bang Seokdam installed an independent outer generator and made a long-term charging contract with the Care-Circulation Body, the convoy base's main-line power stabilized and vehicle passage resumed.

In return, he remained at the outer rest building so he could cut output at once when the contract slipped, gradually distancing himself from Nam Yungyeong's auctions and Pan Hyodam's warehouse operations.

The community gained safety, but Bang Seokdam had to change supply order every day to avoid becoming part of another fixed care routine.

/story_contents/B026/actors/4/sections/정.en:
Cheon Neulsaem was the emergency-generation operator who supported the archive and council of the Jeongdong General Labor Union, balancing the power demands of record preservation and political meetings.

He grew up between a father who bound books in an underground workshop and a mother who serviced heating and cooling in public facilities, learning to watch the humidity of paper and the temperature of machine rooms together.

After the collapse, he treated it as his duty to ensure that when records and power were connected to the same power line, neither could take secret priority.

/story_contents/B026/actors/4/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, Cheon Neulsaem worked shifts in the facilities monitoring room of a large cultural complex, recording the consumption of heat generators, ventilation equipment, and emergency lights.

His key tool was a manual synchronism tester with black slate markings, and when two power sources had to be phased together, he read the needle's tremble rather than a screen.

After work, he handled thread and glue in his father's bookbinding workshop, an experience that let him dry archive books and cable sheathing in different ways after the disaster.

/story_contents/B026/actors/4/sections/가.en:
Cheon Neulsaem's parents helped in the archive evacuation zone early in the collapse, but were assigned to other living spheres during the council's relocation, and letters now came only intermittently.

He made HC14 technicians, librarians, council clerks, and underground cooling crews review the same distribution table so record preservation could not become an excuse for a few specialists.

He accepted Jeong Yura's cross-verification and protected Seon Hansom's underground-vault temperature, but when the two duties conflicted, he secretly helped neither with a hidden line.

/story_contents/B026/actors/4/sections/붕.en:
On the day the Blueprint-Ghost Machine Corps interpreted unfinished expansion plans as actual orders and raised concrete bulkheads around the council chamber, Cheon Neulsaem cut the construction robots' charging line and stopped the emergency ventilation as well.

He sent noise into an empty underground construction pit to divert the Corps, sealed the box of incorrect drawings, and blocked its movement route, but one trapped clerk suffered lasting effects from suffocation.

The incident left him fearing that even the simple response of cutting power could injure both fixed buildings and human breath.

/story_contents/B026/actors/4/sections/생.en:
Instead of the council's demand to dismantle the Blueprint-Ghost Machine Corps, Cheon Neulsaem pursued negotiations brokered by HP02, exchanging unfinished drawings, charging resources, and available construction time.

Only drawings bearing completion marks verified by Jeong Yura were provided to the Corps, while Seon Hansom lowered the underground-vault temperature to limit its activity time, producing an agreement to permit repair work for only two hours at night.

Afterward, he treated the machines not merely as enemies but as a labor system trapped by wrong orders and severed design context.

/story_contents/B026/actors/4/sections/현.en:
Cheon Neulsaem managed archive-preservation power and council-operational power from a single control room, approving no large distribution change without Jeong Yura's cross-verification.

Since Seon Hansom's underground vault damaged documents and parts alike above a set temperature, he often prioritized cooling over meeting lights.

He read the manual synchronism tester's needle himself to merge power sources, performing critical switches by hand because automatic control could be contaminated by signals from the Blueprint-Ghost Machine Corps.

/story_contents/B026/actors/4/sections/비.en:
The day before the bulkhead incident, Cheon Neulsaem knew the council's expansion plan would be rejected, yet secretly mixed one unfinished drawing into the approved-drawing stack to secure archive power.

He judged the chance of the Machine Corps taking that sheet low, but the bulkheads' positions in fact formed along the power-room passage line he had added.

Jeong Yura discovered the page-count discrepancy in the approval bundle, and Seon Hansom remembered the drawing envelope that vanished from the underground vault, leaving Cheon Neulsaem indebted to both for truth and silence.

/story_contents/B026/actors/4/sections/관.en:
When Jeong Yura first cross-verified the council's distribution materials, Cheon Neulsaem earned her trust by cutting a hidden meeting-room line himself, and they had since refused covert power requests together.

He and Seon Hansom shared the experience of taking turns on manual blowers for three days when the underground-vault cooler failed, saving drawings and spare parts.

But Seon Hansom was the last person to hand Cheon Neulsaem the envelope that caused the bulkhead incident, and as Jeong Yura tracked the page discrepancy, their shared past became a clue forcing a choice between protecting or questioning one another.

/story_contents/B026/actors/4/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, the Blueprint-Ghost Machine Corps began raising new pillars along discarded design lines beneath the council, threatening the archive cooling pipes and delegation escape route at once.

In Act 2, Jeong Yura uncovered the unfinished drawing's source and Seon Hansom considered testifying to the envelope transfer, trapping Cheon Neulsaem between the charter city's distribution trust and his own crime.

In Act 3, he chose whether to give the Corps completed drawings and reverse the structures, cut power and sacrifice part of the archive, or personally enter the fixed work zone and correct the orders.

/story_contents/B026/actors/4/sections/분.en:
If Cheon Neulsaem admitted the drawing manipulation and supplied corrected designs under Jeong Yura's verification, he was dismissed from the council but remained a field technician with Seon Hansom, organizing the Machine Corps' work language.

If he cut power completely to stop the Corps, the delegation escaped, but the underground-vault temperature rose and damaged many rare records and spare parts, drawing the preservation community's resentment.

If he entered the Corps' fixed work zone and kept sending manual signals, he saved the city but lived as a relay within the structure, never returning to the control room.

/story_contents/B026/actors/4/arc/0/summ.en: K414 Cheon Neulsaem responded as the Blueprint-Ghost Machine Corps raised new pillars along discarded design lines beneath the council, threatening the archive cooling pipes and delegation escape route at once.

/story_contents/B026/actors/4/arc/1/summ.en: K414 Cheon Neulsaem was trapped between the charter city's distribution trust and his own crime when Jeong Yura uncovered the unfinished drawing's source and Seon Hansom prepared to testify to the envelope transfer.

/story_contents/B026/actors/4/arc/2/summ.en: K414 Cheon Neulsaem chose whether to give the Machine Corps completed drawings to reverse the structures, cut power and sacrifice part of the archive, or personally enter the fixed work zone to correct the orders.

/story_contents/B026/actors/4/outcomes/0.en:
If Cheon Neulsaem revealed the manipulation and supplied corrected drawings, the Blueprint-Ghost Machine Corps dismantled its wrongly raised bulkheads and completed new supports bypassing the cooling pipes.

Jeong Yura dismissed him as operator but kept him at the verification site, while Seon Hansom made a procedure for the two to seal every underground-vault drawing envelope together.

Cheon Neulsaem lost council authority but slowly restored damaged trust by designing completion marks that the Machine Corps and humans could both read.

/story_contents/B026/actors/4/outcomes/1.en:
If Cheon Neulsaem cut archive cooling and concentrated power on the council's escape route, the delegation escaped, but records and machine parts in the underground vault warped from heat.

Seon Hansom did not forgive him and moved the remaining materials to another zone, while Jeong Yura acknowledged the legitimacy of the distribution decision but separately reviewed the drawing-manipulation incident.

Cheon Neulsaem did not leave the city, but stepped down to a low role on the restoration crew of an empty archive, repairing damaged book spines and cable sheathing one by one.

/story_contents/B026/actors/5/sections/정.en:
Heo Eunchan was a Korean-descended technician raised in a south Han River residential compound where sluice workers and electrical repairers lived together.

He was trained to read the flow of current before the height of water and held the conviction that a blackout meant the loss of movement rights.

Though he belonged to the Water Compact, he made the load seen in the track field and worker safety, rather than orders, the standards of judgment.

/story_contents/B026/actors/5/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, Heo Eunchan continued night shifts in the outer inspection depot of the urban railway, inspecting traction power and siding breakers.

A ceramic-handle switch with worn contacts and a portable ammeter with wavering markings always lay on his workbench.

Even as he prepared for promotion examinations, he copied the repair tricks of coworkers nearing retirement into a separate notebook and taught them to juniors through practice.

/story_contents/B026/actors/5/sections/가.en:
HC01, to which Heo Eunchan belonged, was an intermediary house that coordinated time-based track use between power suppliers and passage communities.

The House treated generation not as private property but as a shared resource to be allotted in turn to pumps, medical transport, and maintenance trains.

Though he followed old kinship rules, he persistently objected to the elders' practice of withholding the grounds of decisions from workers.

/story_contents/B026/actors/5/sections/붕.en:
When pumps and communal kitchens stopped in the south Han River residential compound after the Great Blackout, workers did not wait for a formal distribution contract but made a small independent power grid from scrapped-vehicle parts.

Heo Eunchan took part of the copper busbars assigned to Choi Hangyeol's maintenance train and connected them as the trunk line of this unauthorized microgrid, keeping drainage pumps and night passage lights running and saving a settlement near flooding.

But residents fleeing the Flood-Boar Swarm also poured into the compound, continually increasing the load, and he bore the wound of knowing that the power grid enabling survival violated both HC01's supply contract and the rules governing track assets.

/story_contents/B026/actors/5/sections/생.en:
Je Yun's passage ledger still showed the missing busbars as maintenance-train materials, and Chae Hansol traced an unexplained load leaving the generator to find the residential compound's microgrid.

At the same time, the Flood-Boar Swarm moved around the official power line and stopped formal restoration, leaving the extracontractual grid alone able to run the settlement's pumps.

Rather than cut the connection and restore the asset contract, Heo Eunchan disclosed the load table and maintenance responsibility to workers, trying to turn the unauthorized installation into a survival foundation directly operated by the community.

/story_contents/B026/actors/5/sections/현.en:
At the Sinjeong base of the Water Compact, Heo Eunchan supervised siding power and approved the order of traction power, pump loads, and night charging.

He reflected the departure time of Choi Hangyeol's maintenance train in the power table and split the spare generation delivered by Chae Hansol into small shares for each site.

Though his formal authority was great, he required confirmation by two field workers before locking even one breaker, wary of being raised up as an arbitrary hero.

/story_contents/B026/actors/5/sections/비.en:
Heo Eunchan concealed that the copper busbars were not diverted by accident, but that he had set the cutting lengths and carrying times in advance with the residential compound's workers.

To prevent the theft from being discovered at once, he marked the busbars in the materials table as discarded items lost to flood and carved the actual connection section into the inside of the ceramic-handle switch.

If this record became public, the workers could be punished as co-conspirators in theft, but if he hid it, Choi Hangyeol's maintenance train would remain bound waiting for materials that did not exist.

/story_contents/B026/actors/5/sections/관.en:
Heo Eunchan had been the power supervisor supporting the dispatch of Choi Hangyeol's maintenance train, but now owed a direct debt for taking that train's materials to save the residential compound.

As one who built the time-based track-use contract with him, Je Yun examined whether the unauthorized grid infringed other communities' rights, while Chae Hansol, who had sent spare generation, protested that the unexplained load destabilized his equipment as well.

Heo Eunchan explained to all three that formal restoration had been impossible because of the Flood-Boar Swarm's movement, but admitted that the need to survive did not remove the ownership question of stolen copper and violated contracts.

/story_contents/B026/actors/5/sections/3.en:
K018 Heo Eunchan confirmed that while the unauthorized microgrid built with copper busbars stolen by workers saved the residential compound, it breached the maintenance-train and generation contracts in sequence.

In the first act, the mismatch between Je Yun's ledger and Chae Hansol's generation load revealed the hidden power grid.

In the second act, when Choi Hangyeol demanded the busbars returned and the Flood-Boar Swarm blocked the formal restoration zone, he had to find a way to settle responsibility for the stolen materials without cutting the settlement's pumps.

In the third act, he either offered a shared-grid contract in which workers bore power use and maintenance labor directly, or dismantled the microgrid to keep the existing contract and gave up the settlement's survival.

/story_contents/B026/actors/5/sections/분.en:
If Heo Eunchan disclosed the real materials table and microgrid drawings, HC01 recovered ownership of the stolen busbars but did not demolish the grid at once, instead making a time-limited contract under which the residential compound repaid the copper's value through maintenance-train track restoration and pump-operation labor.

Heo Eunchan used his siding-power supervision authority to manage connection times between the official and shared grids, but his sole control shrank as the compound workers formed an independent operating council for daily equipment operation.

If he continued hiding the busbars' source, Choi Hangyeol's train stopped for lack of materials, Chae Hansol cut the unverified load, and the microgrid closed with the settlement after its fuel ran out.

/story_contents/B026/actors/5/arc/0/summ.en: K018 Heo Eunchan confirmed the existence of a hidden microgrid made from stolen copper busbars when Je Yun's ledger and Chae Hansol's generation load did not match.

/story_contents/B026/actors/5/arc/1/summ.en: K018 Heo Eunchan had to find a way to settle responsibility for stolen materials without cutting the settlement's pumps amid Choi Hangyeol's demand to return the busbars and the Flood-Boar Swarm's blockade of the restoration zone.

/story_contents/B026/actors/5/arc/2/summ.en: K018 Heo Eunchan either offered a shared-grid contract in which workers bore power use and maintenance labor, or dismantled the microgrid to keep the existing contract and gave up the settlement's survival.

/story_contents/B026/actors/5/outcomes/0.en: If K018 Heo Eunchan disclosed the materials table and microgrid drawings, HC01 recovered ownership of the busbars but delayed demolition and made a time-limited contract under which the residential compound repaid the copper's value through track-restoration and pump-operation labor.

/story_contents/B026/actors/5/outcomes/1.en: If K018 Heo Eunchan hid the busbars' source, Choi Hangyeol's train stopped for lack of materials and Chae Hansol cut the unverified load, closing the fuel-depleted microgrid with the settlement.

/story_contents/B026/actors/6/sections/정.en:
Pyo Yedam was a Korean-descended dispatch officer who grew up in subcontract workers' housing in the southwestern industrial zone and learned the rhythm of people's shifts before the speed of machines.

She earned her coworkers' trust through her ability to identify the cause of delay accurately rather than through paper credentials, and believed no one should be treated as an empty vehicle.

Even after joining the Standards Alliance, she openly opposed dispatch demands that put output first and pushed aside injured people or inexperienced workers.

/story_contents/B026/actors/6/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, Pyo Yedam coordinated the arrival order of freight trucks and loading zones in the night dispatch room of a large delivery base.

She inserted brass tags into a rotating dispatch drum to distinguish delays and hazardous freight by sight, and reconstructed the whole flow with one turn of the drum even when the computer system stopped.

One winter, she deliberately entered a lower dispatch target to guarantee rest time for drivers trapped by heavy snow and received a pay-cut penalty.

/story_contents/B026/actors/6/sections/가.en:
HC12, on which Pyo Yedam relied, was a contractual community in which vehicle makers, instrumentation officers, and siding workers guaranteed one another's deliveries.

The community valued the traceability of wheels and braking systems over the number of finished goods, treating even a single wrong tag as a grave fault that could shake the livelihoods of many workshops.

She respected contractual discipline, but reserved separate dispatch slots for apprentices to change the practice under which veterans monopolized all good shifts.

/story_contents/B026/actors/6/sections/붕.en:
On the day the Night-Sorting Swarm moved to Cheonwang Base and sent its automated sorting arms into a frenzy, Pyo Yedam ignored the warning and pushed in the last freight car, isolating two apprentices in a sealed zone.

Rather than confront the machines head-on, she lowered the conveyor noise, cooled the motors, and sent empty packaging to another inlet to divert the feeding flow and block the sorting arms' route.

Both people were rescued, but one lost fingers, and Pyo Yedam could not fully tell anyone about the impatience that had tried to protect dispatch results.

/story_contents/B026/actors/6/sections/생.en:
Pyo Yedam noticed from the tremble of brass tags that the Night-Sorting Swarm did not move randomly, but chose zones by the smell and vibration of packaging.

She called an HC13 intermediary, traded waste-packaging input volume for passage time after midnight, and offered the cooled sorting zone as the swarm's temporary corridor.

Because of that agreement, workers finished manual dispatch before dawn, and she changed from a manager who forced speed into a working officer who negotiated flow.

/story_contents/B026/actors/6/sections/현.en:
As dispatch officer for the Cheonwang Base sidings, Pyo Yedam made the final coordination of which track wheeled instrumentation equipment and towing vehicles would meet on.

He put no vehicle without Jeong Siwoo's instrumentation stamp on the dispatch board, and rechecked the wheel-dispatch order guaranteed by Heo Daon through brass tags.

In the field, his judgment was considered fast, but he continued to endure pressure from the fabrication union, which said reduced night work lowered output.

/story_contents/B026/actors/6/sections/비.en:
Pyo Yedam hid the fact that just before the apprentice accident, she removed the hazard tag from the rotating dispatch drum and put it in her pocket.

She had tried to save a work crew that would disperse if it missed delivery, but in the end preserved the contract at the cost of a young worker's hand.

She regularly sent prosthetic-hand parts to the victim but could not identify the sender, and remained torn between melting down the brass tag or presenting it as evidence.

/story_contents/B026/actors/6/sections/관.en:
When Jeong Siwoo first refused an instrumentation stamp and the entire workshop stopped, Pyo Yedam supported his judgment and sealed the dispatch drum himself.

He later secretly replaced twelve defective wheels with Heo Daon to save night dispatch, but in that process the order of the vehicle involved in the apprentice accident also changed.

Jeong Siwoo valued consistency of records and Heo Daon valued delivery promises, so Pyo Yedam had explained the same past differently to the two of them.

/story_contents/B026/actors/6/sections/3.en:
In the first act, Pyo Yedam evaded the Night-Sorting Swarm's interference through manual dispatch, but the missing hazard tag was found in Jeong Siwoo's instrumentation record.

In the second act, he chose whether to run defective vehicles under restrictions to save Heo Daon's wheel workshop or declare a full stop and ruin the Alliance's production plan.

In the third act, he either established a new rule allowing accident victims and apprentices to join dispatch decisions, or overturned even the passage agreement with the Night-Sorting Swarm through a combat order to protect results.

/story_contents/B026/actors/6/sections/분.en:
If Pyo Yedam submitted the brass tag and admitted the manipulation, he lost his post as working officer but designed a safe dispatch board with the victim.

If he sent out defective vehicles while keeping the secret, a chain of derailments followed a brief boom, and Jeong Siwoo's and Heo Daon's contracts became documents accusing each other.

Choosing to maintain the midnight-passage bargain with the Night-Sorting Swarm while lowering output made the Alliance poorer, but secured time for apprentices to survive.

/story_contents/B026/actors/6/arc/0/summ.en: K046 Pyo Yedam evaded the Night-Sorting Swarm's interference through manual dispatch, but was suspected of responsibility when the missing hazard tag was found in Jeong Siwoo's instrumentation record.

/story_contents/B026/actors/6/arc/1/summ.en: K046 Pyo Yedam chose whether to run defective vehicles under restrictions to save Heo Daon's wheel workshop or declare a full stop and ruin the Alliance's production plan.

/story_contents/B026/actors/6/arc/2/summ.en: K046 Pyo Yedam either established a new rule allowing accident victims and apprentices to join dispatch decisions, or overturned the passage agreement with the Night-Sorting Swarm through a combat order to protect results.

/story_contents/B026/actors/6/outcomes/0.en:
Pyo Yedam admitted the hazard-tag manipulation and handed the stop handle of the dispatch drum to the injured apprentice.

Jeong Siwoo and Heo Daon made a procedure to verify instrumentation stamps and wheel guarantees on one board, while leaving the packaging zone empty for the Night-Sorting Swarm after midnight.

He took an instructional shift instead of a post, remaining to create a Cheonwang Base that was slower but had fewer accidents.

/story_contents/B026/actors/6/outcomes/1.en:
Pyo Yedam moved the defective vehicles' tags into the normal slots to meet the Fabrication Alliance's deadline and keep his post.

When the vehicles derailed on an outer ramp, Jeong Siwoo withdrew the instrumentation contract and Heo Daon broke with Pyo Yedam over responsibility for the manipulation.

As the Night-Sorting Swarm also crowded in to reclaim the blocked passage, Cheonwang Base lost both fast production and safe dispatch.

/story_contents/B026/actors/7/sections/정.en:
Seo Nayeon was an ice merchant born in a port city in central Vietnam who moved to the Korean Peninsula with her mother at thirteen and grew up taking the surname of her Korean stepfather.

At home, she used Vietnamese to check her mother's medicine directions and news of relatives; at the market, she fluently distinguished Korean honorifics from merchants' slang.

She treated the two languages not as mere tools of interpretation but as different living languages that preserved family emotions and trading terms precisely.

/story_contents/B026/actors/7/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, Seo Nayeon inspected a seafood-market cold store at dawn and supplied ice to a mobile drink stall by day.

Her key tools were an insulated-handled ice saw with teeth of different widths and aluminum molds engraved with colors by capacity.

She also learned night freezer maintenance to pay her sibling's vocational-school tuition, developing a sense for detecting merchants who cheated volume through temperature and melting rate.

/story_contents/B026/actors/7/sections/가.en:
HC10, to which Seo Nayeon belonged, was a commercial community in which cold stores, clinics, food shops, and ice-dispensers determined ice-ration order together.

The community put ice for medicine preservation first, but migrant households unable to provide collateral and patients without kin were often pushed down the order.

Because her mother once failed to receive refrigerated medicine for lack of documents, she set aside a small share of free ice, clashing with the merchant elders.

/story_contents/B026/actors/7/sections/붕.en:
On the day the Coolant-Index Fungal Body encroached into pipes of the collateral warehouse, Seo Nayeon hastily struck corroded pipes to check them and spread fungal spores, injuring her sibling's lungs.

She did not burn the whole pipe system, but reduced vibrating noise, cooled and sealed the contaminated section, and sent molasses residue to an empty tank to divert the fungal body's feeding route.

Her sibling survived but could no longer travel far, and Seo Nayeon could not tell her family that she had overestimated her maintenance skill.

/story_contents/B026/actors/7/sections/생.en:
Seo Nayeon noticed from stains on ice molds that the color changes left by the fungal body were not simple contamination but signs revealing the order of metal corrosion.

Through an HP05 intermediary, she assigned it low-waste-heat pipes and nutrient residue, securing a bargain that left the pipes leading to the medicine warehouse empty for set periods.

Afterward, she became established not as a merchant who only sold ice, but as a negotiator who designed cooling routes and preservation time.

/story_contents/B026/actors/7/sections/현.en:
Seo Nayeon worked in Won Buddhism as an independent merchant who determined the size, purity, and delivery order of ice bricks.

He filled the collateral warehouse under O Haerin's command, but allotted the hardest share among ice transferred from Song Ideun to Yun Jiyul's infirmary first.

While maintaining the guild's profit, he reduced his daily sales share to protect the portion for patients without collateral, enduring between his family's livelihood and his duty to the community.

/story_contents/B026/actors/7/sections/비.en:
Seo Nayeon concealed that on the day his sibling was injured, he had already read the contamination warning but continued working for fear of losing the collateral-warehouse contract.

To pay treatment costs, he pledged his family's share in freezing equipment to O Haerin's warehouse, and if he could not repay it, even his mother and sibling's shelter would become guild property.

He also felt guilt whenever he saw Yun Jiyul because some ice sent to the infirmary came not from his own free-ration share but from secretly exchanging another small merchant's allotment.

/story_contents/B026/actors/7/sections/관.en:
When O Haerin first opened the collateral warehouse, Seo Nayeon entrusted his family's molds and secured ice-supply rights, and that contract still bound his livelihood.

Song Ideun had spent all night binding ice bricks that began melting in the transfer shed again, and the two had once borne the losses half each.

Yun Jiyul treated Seo Nayeon's sibling and demanded priority allocation for the infirmary, and Seo Nayeon secretly postponed other contracts to keep that promise.

/story_contents/B026/actors/7/sections/3.en:
In the first act, Seo Nayeon earned trust by splitting scarce ice among three places, but the guild ledger exposed the volume that had flowed to patients without collateral, putting him in danger of losing his collateral rights.

In the second act, as the pipe bargain with the Coolant-Index Fungal Body became tied to the truth of his sibling's accident, he decided whether to confess negligence to his family or shift responsibility to O Haerin.

In the third act, he either persuaded Song Ideun and Yun Jiyul to change ice rations to a needs-based system, or turned rare ice into auction goods to protect his family's shelter.

/story_contents/B026/actors/7/sections/분.en:
