If Seo Nayeon revealed both his ignored warning and volume exchange, his family lost the pledged equipment, but the infirmary and merchants built a common cold store to help them start again.

If he kept silent, his sibling's treatment continued, but medicine losses occurred at Yun Jiyul's infirmary and Song Ideun no longer guaranteed transfers.

Choosing to expand the pipe bargain with the Coolant-Index Fungal Body reduced profit but turned contamination into a predictable seasonal cost, saving the guild in the long term.

/story_contents/B026/actors/7/arc/0/summ.en: K198 Seo Nayeon earned trust by splitting scarce ice among three places, but the guild ledger exposed that she sent volume to patients without collateral, putting her in danger of losing collateral rights.

/story_contents/B026/actors/7/arc/1/summ.en: K198 Seo Nayeon decided whether to confess negligence to his family or shift responsibility to O Haerin when his pipe bargain with the Coolant-Index Fungal Body became tied to the truth of his sibling's accident.

/story_contents/B026/actors/7/arc/2/summ.en: K198 Seo Nayeon either persuaded Song Ideun and Yun Jiyul to change ice rations to a needs-based system, or turned rare ice into auction goods to protect his family's shelter.

/story_contents/B026/actors/7/outcomes/0.en:
Seo Nayeon confessed before his sibling and mother that he had read the warning before the accident but forced the work forward, and gave up ownership of the pledged equipment.

O Haerin recorded the contract breach, but Song Ideun and Yun Jiyul secured labor shares in a common cold store, opening a way for the family to continue working.

He posted the same ration rule in Vietnamese and Korean and made the share for patients without collateral a formal system.

/story_contents/B026/actors/7/outcomes/1.en:
Seo Nayeon gave the purest ice to a secret auction and preserved his family's shelter and freezing equipment.

As a result, stored medicines spoiled at Yun Jiyul's infirmary. Song Ideun withdrew the transfer contract, and O Haerin used the manipulation as grounds to demand higher interest.

He gained wealthy customers, but his sibling learned from whose treatment that ice had been taken and refused to live with him.

/story_contents/B026/actors/8/sections/정.en:
O Haneul was a programming officer born to a mother who worked as a sound engineer in Cebu, Philippines, and a Korean father who was a stage carpenter, moving to the Korean Peninsula in primary school.

He shared private family emotions in Cebuano and handled contracts and transmission orders in Korean, using English only narrowly to read external frequency materials.

Because he ran a small subtitling workshop with his mother after his parents separated, he believed that people whose voices were not loud must also have access to broadcast time.

/story_contents/B026/actors/8/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, O Haneul moved between local venues and internet livestream sites, adjusting subtitles, visual advertisement lengths, and performance order.

A manual cue wheel notched by the second and a dim red timer sat on his desk, preserving the order even during computer delays.

After his mother's hearing loss worsened, he paired subtitles and hand signals with every announcement, but lost his contract in a dispute with employers who demanded cost cuts.

/story_contents/B026/actors/8/sections/가.en:
HP10, the channel guild to which O Haneul belonged, was a professional community in which transmission engineers, programmers, subtitle recorders, and listener representatives jointly allotted broadcast time.

The guild saw both disaster information and market prices as necessary, but a growing problem let merchants who paid the most preempt the most accurate time slots.

He tried to guarantee short fixed times to people pushed out of communication by language or disability, frequently clashing with the transmission union that regarded it as lost revenue.

/story_contents/B026/actors/8/sections/붕.en:
On the night the Sewer-Raccoon Pack occupied the Sangam underground passage, stateless refugees sent the subtitle room a warning in their dialect that a side-route shutter had opened.

O Haneul applied programming rules requiring verification in standard Korean, deleted the sentence, and used the limited emergency-subtitle time only for the existing evacuation instruction.

The refugee zone that could understand the warning did not learn of the route change in time and encountered the Sewer-Raccoon Pack, leaving him with the wound that an untranslated word could be deadlier than a wrong translation.

/story_contents/B026/actors/8/sections/생.en:
O Haneul compared the time of the deleted warning with field bulletins recorded by Yun Seoha and confirmed that the refugee-dialect sentence had given the earliest warning of danger.

Choi Jiwoo argued that transmitting unverified wording unchanged would create more confusion, but O Haerin provided response sheets recording which subtitles listeners of different language communities had actually understood.

O Haneul concluded that the heart of emergency broadcasting was not repeating one precise sentence, but making public who controlled the translation queue and transmission time for each language.

/story_contents/B026/actors/8/sections/현.en:
As programming officer of the channel guild of the Yeouido Investment Union, O Haneul determined the order of disaster alerts, market information, auction bulletins, and family-finding broadcasts.

He shared veto power over programming with Choi Jiwoo, placed O Haerin's market broadcast in guild time, and adjusted Yun Seoha's auction bulletin so it would not diverge from actual trading time.

Whenever he used his authority, he placed the manual cue wheel on a public table so listener representatives could see directly whose time had shrunk or grown.

/story_contents/B026/actors/8/sections/비.en:
O Haneul concealed that the refugee-dialect warning was not automatically omitted, but that he himself removed its subtitle card from the manual cue wheel and left a deletion mark.

He judged that airing a language with no verified source would make the entire channel lose trust, and kept the deleted original and provisional translation in the red timer's empty battery compartment.

Moreover, because he also pushed later warnings received in the same dialect behind the verification queue, the truth could emerge that his first decision was not an isolated error but censorship controlling translation time.

/story_contents/B026/actors/8/sections/관.en:
O Haneul had once shared responsibility with Choi Jiwoo by rejecting an erroneous alert script, but now confronted him because that practice of refusal had worked as a barrier deleting the language of stateless refugees.

O Haerin restored the meaning of the deleted warning by organizing listener responses and regional expressions, while Yun Seoha supplied field-time records proving the warning was not false.

The three scheduled emergency subtitles announcing the Sewer-Raccoon Pack's movement together, but clashed over whether the guild programming officer would continue to monopolize final translation time or hand fixed segments to refugee interpreters.

/story_contents/B026/actors/8/sections/3.en:
K223 O Haneul questioned who controlled the transmission time of multilingual emergency subtitles after the censorship that deleted a Sewer-Raccoon Pack warning received in a stateless refugee dialect caused casualties.

In the first act, Yun Seoha's field record and O Haerin's listener responses revealed that the deleted sentence was the earliest warning.

In the second act, when Choi Jiwoo tried to restrict unverified translations, O Haneul decided whether to disclose his deletion record and reveal language queues in real time.

In the third act, he either opened a multilingual transmission system granting stateless refugee interpreters direct access to emergency subtitle segments, or maintained a censorship system broadcasting only languages approved by the guild.

/story_contents/B026/actors/8/sections/분.en:
If O Haneul disclosed the original and deletion mark, refugees in the affected zone demanded a public apology and suspension of his programming authority for a set period, and the HP10 channel guild permanently assigned emergency-subtitle segments by language to an interpreters' council.

He remained an ordinary programming officer adjusting the order of disaster alerts and family-finding broadcasts, but lost the authority to delete or defer the emergency translation queue, leaving every change record on the manual cue wheel and public subtitle board.

If he hid the censorship, refugee interpreters ran independent transmitters that conflicted with the guild broadcast, and as different evacuation orders spread at once, the Yeouido Investment Union lost its status as the representative channel for emergency information.

/story_contents/B027/actors/0/sections/정.en:
Heo Miri is a Korean civil engineering practitioner who grew up in a railway workers’ housing community in southwestern Seoul. After the Collapse, she is responsible for securing the Banghwa depot for Yongsan Line Yangjae Machineworks Company

She has a habit of reading workers’ footsteps and wheel tracks before looking at track drawings, and carries white marking chalk and a folding measuring rod like badges of identity.

She believes that deciding where to station fire engines and evacuation trains is a political choice about whose nights to protect.

/story_contents/B027/actors/0/sections/붕.en:
Before the Collapse, Heo Miri handled temporary-track surveying and resident briefings for an urban rail depot expansion project, and renumbered the switches in a closed wash shed by hand.

After she moved a sound barrier to reduce noise complaints and thereby narrowed the turning radius for emergency vehicles, she stopped treating conflicts between convenience and safety as matters of numbers alone.

After work, she tended the brass level her father had left her on the roof of the railway workers’ housing community, resolving to become a site supervisor one day.

/story_contents/B027/actors/0/sections/가.en:
Heo Miri’s family is an HP09-lineage technical family that has alternated between railway track maintenance and fire-protection work, but the Collapse scattered its equipment and skilled workers, leaving only the family name.

She brings researchers from Magok, locomotive engineers, and refugee representatives to one table, and makes nighttime patrols of the proposed Banghwa depot sites a shared obligation.

The survivors from the railway workers’ housing community, however, suspect that she has sided with the Research Council, while the council is wary that she is laying tracks to favor her relatives’ district.

/story_contents/B027/actors/0/sections/붕.en:
During the first winter after the Collapse, on a night when the cooling-water corrosion colony corroded both pipe biofilm and switch metal, Heo Miri sent a rescue motorcar onto the wrong storage track, stranding three people.

She stopped the guards from burning the colony, reduced the cooling pump’s vibration, moved a contaminated lubricant drum to serve as an alternate feeding point, and sealed both branches of the track with steel plates.

The rescue succeeded, but one of the stranded people lost a leg. Even now, the sound of chalk scraping a rail reminds Heo Miri of the wrong arrow she drew.

/story_contents/B027/actors/0/sections/생.en:
When the cooling-water corrosion colony spread to a proposed Banghwa depot site, Heo Miri called in an HP05 intermediary and proposed negotiating an exchange of cooling-water allocations for passage times.

In return for stopping people and vehicles for two hours before dawn, she directed condensed waste heat into an outlying feeding area. During the remaining hours, she restricted the colony’s route with a low-frequency horn and barrier plates.

That choice produced an operating timetable that allowed coexistence without evacuating the depot, proving that designing routes could be a stronger defense than eradication.

/story_contents/B027/actors/0/sections/현.en:
Heo Miri works as an operations chief at Yongsan Line Yangjae Machineworks Company, coordinating the storage order at Banghwa depot, waiting positions for evacuation trains, and the colony’s passage timetable all at once.

He carries out Yu Minho’s dispatch orders with white chalk lines, but when he sees signs of danger, he writes his objections in the order’s margin and delays departure.

When Heo Seogyeom begins a second search, he stands in front of the carriage himself to check its seals. He is trusted in the field but considered overly independent within the council.

/story_contents/B027/actors/0/sections/비.en:
Heo Miri harbors a secret: when first selecting a site for Banghwa depot, she copied the coordinates on one sheet of corrosion data into an adjacent district to spare the railway workers’ housing community where her uncle lived.

Because of that alteration, the cooling-water corrosion colony’s initial cluster was discovered late, and the rescue motorcar’s accident on the wrong storage track also stemmed from the distortion.

She sends a fuel voucher to the survivor who lost a leg every month but cannot reveal who sends it. She knows that if the original data is ever found, both her community and her family will abandon her.

/story_contents/B027/actors/0/sections/관.en:
Just after the Collapse, Heo Miri and Yu Minho dispersed twelve fire engines from the research complex along the tracks. Heo Miri translated Yu Minho’s dispatch order into chalk numbers and hand signals to prevent confusion.

Starting the day after the corrosion accident, he and Heo Seogyeom established a procedure for searching beneath every passenger carriage twice. Heo Miri stayed in front of the carriages awaiting a second search despite passengers’ protests.

Both men recognize his instincts in the field, but neither knows that he may have altered the coordinates. The deeper their trust grows, the harder Heo Miri finds it to tell the truth.

/story_contents/B027/actors/0/sections/3.en:
K074 In Act 1, Heo Miri discovers that corrosion marks on the proposed Banghwa depot track do not match the coordinates in the old survey records, and realizes that his alteration has resurfaced.

In Act 2, as Yu Minho’s emergency dispatch clashes with Heo Seogyeom’s full second search and the passage agreement with the colony begins to falter, he must choose whether to destroy the original data or halt operations.

In Act 3, he makes an irreversible decision: acknowledge his past attempt to protect the railway workers’ housing community and relocate the entire depot, or conceal the alteration and permanently seal a particular storage track.

/story_contents/B027/actors/0/sections/분.en:
Heo Miri’s ending depends less on whether Banghwa depot remains open than on which district she decides must bear the risk.

If she admits the truth, she may lose her position, but she leaves behind a new storage system combining the colony passage agreement with a resident oversight procedure.

If she chooses concealment, operations stabilize in the short term, but the survivors left inside the sealed track and the spreading corrosion eventually destroy both her authority and the safety of the railway workers’ housing community.

/story_contents/B027/actors/0/arc/2/summ.en: K074 Heo Miri makes an irreversible decision: acknowledge her past attempt to protect the railway workers’ housing community and relocate the entire depot, or conceal the alteration and permanently seal a particular storage track.

/story_contents/B027/actors/1/sections/정.en:
Byeon Oreum is a Korean railway worker who grew up among the multifamily homes and factory alleys of Seongsu, and serves as stationmaster of Seongsu concourse for the Ttukseom Union Sermon Registry State.

He manages both the brass ticket punch and the rotating ration tray inside the ticket window, treating tickets and water vouchers as survival documents of equal importance.

He seems cold because he reads anxiety first in the speed at which a queue moves rather than in people’s voices, but every night he cleans the unnamed death markers on the platform benches.

/story_contents/B027/actors/1/sections/붕.en:
Before the Collapse, Byeon Oreum was responsible for customer guidance at a commuter station, managing the last-train rush when concertgoers and factory shift workers arrived all at once.

During one summer blackout, he counted passengers with a manual ticket punch and handed out bottled water through a rotating ration tray, preventing a crowd crush. The report to his superiors, however, said the automated equipment had operated normally.

From that day on, he trusted the faces of the people at the window and their used ticket stubs more than machine records.

/story_contents/B027/actors/1/sections/가.en:
Byeon Oreum’s family ran a small shoe-repair shop and a late-night restaurant in the Seongsu area, making their living by supplying goods and meals to the HC12 merchants’ association.

After the Collapse, the repair shop became a water-voucher exchange, and the restaurant’s steel serving hatch was moved to the concourse window, where residents and workshop workers received their water allotments.

He runs the station on the grounds that he is protecting his family’s home ground, but is constantly attacked over whether longtime residents or newly arrived refugees should be admitted first.

/story_contents/B027/actors/1/sections/붕.en:
On a night when the sewer raccoon clan broke through a closed restroom passage and descended on the concourse water tank, Byeon Oreum moved passengers to the far end of the platform instead of obeying an order to lower the shutters.

He turned off the loudspeaker’s high-frequency noise and used a low drumbeat to draw the group toward one staircase, then sent food scraps into an outside drain and sealed the wire-mesh gates one by one.

During the move, a child fell into a dark gap in the tracks. Byeon Oreum carries the memory of choosing to move the crowd before rescuing the child, along with the scratches on his ticket punch.

/story_contents/B027/actors/1/sections/생.en:
Byeon Oreum stopped the workshop guards from exterminating the sewer raccoon clan and negotiated nighttime passage hours and an allocation of food by-products with an HC04 intermediary.

In exchange for leaving the eastern sewer stairs clear after midnight, he used an iron drum and cooling mist to confine their approach route to the western drain during the dawn water-distribution hours.

After the agreement, nighttime attacks on the concourse decreased, but residents left black handprints on the stationmaster’s office door, accusing him of giving food to the group that had harmed people.

/story_contents/B027/actors/1/sections/현.en:
As stationmaster, Byeon Oreum decides water-voucher issuance, refugee admission, and nighttime platform closures at Seongsu concourse, and administers Jang Minjae’s citizen water vouchers at the window.

Each day, he reads Han Somi’s pledge to restore daily life over the platform loudspeaker, then records whether actual rations match the promised amounts and each workshop’s priority.

The workshop union needs his precise control of headcounts, but some guards suspect him of collaborating from within because of his unofficial timetable with the sewer raccoon clan.

/story_contents/B027/actors/1/sections/비.en:
Byeon Oreum keeps a secret: on the night the child fell, he did not take out the rescue ladder kept in the stationmaster’s office.

His family repair shop’s last stock of leather and the master plate for the water vouchers were tied to that ladder. Afraid the crowd would loot them, he kept the door locked and missed the chance to rescue the child in time.

He gives the dead child’s mother the first water voucher each week but cannot tell her why. Whenever he sees the master plate, he knows he has lied to himself by claiming that he put the community’s order ahead of his family’s property.

/story_contents/B027/actors/1/sections/관.en:
Since the first month after the Collapse, Byeon Oreum has reconciled the number of citizen water vouchers at each window with Jang Minjae, and refused to reduce the minimum water allocation Jang Minjae set despite pressure from workshop representatives.

After closing the flooded underground passage, he and Han Somi drafted the platform announcements together. Whenever her restoration pledges differed from the amount of water actually dispensed through the ration tray, he immediately broadcast a correction.

Both credit his stubbornness with keeping the concourse running, but neither knows about the child’s death or the hidden ladder.

/story_contents/B027/actors/1/sections/3.en:
K103 In Act 1, the sewer raccoon clan’s nighttime passage hours overlap with a workshop expansion plan, putting the water-distribution window at risk of another attack.

In Act 2, while trying to uphold both Jang Minjae’s universal water vouchers and Han Somi’s promise to restore the platform, the hidden ladder and master plate are found in a sewer passage, exposing his past choice.

In Act 3, he decides whether to seal the concourse as a residents’ fortress or turn it into a night market and passage corridor, permanently changing the nature of his authority as stationmaster.

/story_contents/B027/actors/1/sections/분.en:
Byeon Oreum’s ending depends on whether he keeps exclusive control of the water-voucher master plate or turns it over to joint management.

If he reveals the truth about the master plate and ladder, he faces the bereaved family’s judgment, but the passage hours agreed with the sewer raccoon clan are formalized under the oversight of resident representatives.

If he keeps the secret, the concourse becomes a strong fortress, but the blocked nighttime sewer route causes workshop waste and resentment to accumulate together, inviting a new conflict.

/story_contents/B027/actors/1/arc/0/summ.en: K103 When the sewer raccoon clan’s nighttime passage hours overlap with a workshop expansion plan, Byeon Oreum faces the risk of another attack on the water-distribution window.

/story_contents/B027/actors/1/arc/1/summ.en: K103 Byeon Oreum tries to uphold both Jang Minjae’s universal water vouchers and Han Somi’s promise to restore the platform, but the hidden ladder and master plate are found in a sewer passage, exposing his past choice.

/story_contents/B027/actors/1/arc/2/summ.en: K103 Byeon Oreum permanently changes the nature of his authority as stationmaster by either sealing the concourse as a residents’ fortress or turning it into a night market and passage corridor.

/story_contents/B027/actors/1/outcomes/0.en: K103 If Byeon Oreum reveals the truth about the master plate and ladder and turns the water-voucher master plate over to joint management, he faces the bereaved family’s judgment, but the passage hours agreed with the sewer raccoon clan are formalized under the oversight of resident representatives.

/story_contents/B027/actors/1/outcomes/1.en: K103 If Byeon Oreum keeps the secret and retains exclusive control of the master plate, the concourse remains a sturdy fortress, but workshop waste and resentment accumulate together in the blocked nighttime sewer route.

/story_contents/B027/actors/2/sections/정.en:
Yang Giseok is a Korean signal technician born into a family of waterworks workers east of the Han River, and works as storage-track supervisor at Godeok depot for the Gwangjin Line Escort Protection State.

He trusts a black signal-lamp box and ceramic insulating pins more than electronic screens, checking every departure signal against both the number of flashes and a handwritten record.

He is taciturn and fixated on rules, but no one can readily replace him because he can move trains using only people’s eyes and whistles when communications fail.

/story_contents/B027/actors/2/sections/붕.en:
Before the Collapse, Yang Giseok worked as a test technician for fiber-optic interlocking signal equipment, checking faults shown by the automated diagnostic network again with a field insulation tester.

During a commissioning trial, he discovered that a switch was half-open even though the screen showed it as normal, preventing a collision. He was nevertheless blamed for the schedule delay and left off the promotion list.

Afterward, he collected old lamps and manual pins in his personal toolbox and endured his colleagues’ ridicule on the grounds that he was preparing for the day automation failed.

/story_contents/B027/actors/2/sections/가.en:
Yang Giseok’s family belonged to the HP01 technical community, which had laid water mains and repaired pumps. They are bound to a system in which water to their relatives’ neighborhood stops if Godeok depot’s supply trains stop.

After the Collapse, he brought signal technicians, pump operators, and track workers together into a manual operations crew that shared the number of lamp flashes and the rhythm of whistle blasts.

His family pressures him to prioritize the water supply, while depot workers counter that they will refuse to operate unless power-generation and medical supplies are treated on an equal footing.

/story_contents/B027/actors/2/sections/붕.en:
On the day G21E04, the communications-root colony, exactly mimicked a green lamp and two short whistle blasts, Yang Giseok approved a procedure allowing a vehicle to depart whenever those two signals matched.

He recorded a half-beat delay found during testing as an effect of humidity, omitted human call-back confirmation, and distributed the new procedure to the field.

A worker was caught in a coupling rod and killed during an attempt to stop a vehicle set moving by the imitated signal. Yang Giseok concealed the fact that responsibility lay not only with the colony but also with the incomplete signaling grammar he had created.

/story_contents/B027/actors/2/sections/생.en:
Yang Giseok confirms that G21E04 can mimic individual lamps and whistle intervals, but cannot also match the direction of a lamp’s shutter, the sender’s position, and the sequence of responses dictated by the preceding command.

He creates a three-part signaling grammar: Park Hayul poses a question by whistle, Yang Pilho answers with a directional lamp, and a field worker raises a brass token to indicate final approval.

He records every discrepancy as grounds for an immediate stop and accepts an open procedure under which two other people can reject even his own approval.

/story_contents/B027/actors/2/sections/현.en:
At Godeok depot, Yang Giseok oversees storage-track switching, departure lamps, and the movement times of the communications-root colony, and holds the final entry authorization for every train.

He matches the number of lamp flashes to Park Hayul’s departure whistle, lends Yang Pilho only his ceramic insulating pins for test runs, and rarely agrees to requests to restore automated signaling.

Seol Bomi supports the storage tracks’ power allocation from the generation side, but the depot’s expansion is slow because Yang Giseok prioritizes manual procedures over communications.

/story_contents/B027/actors/2/sections/비.en:
Yang Giseok is the person who deleted the whistle call-back and lamp-direction check from the original draft to shorten departure times.

After the accident, he backdated the revision and hid the test sheet showing the slight signal delay beneath the black lamp box.

If that test sheet and the draft are made public, not only G21E04’s deception but also his negligence as supervisor will be recorded as a cause of the fatal accident.

/story_contents/B027/actors/2/sections/관.en:
Park Hayul can distinguish whistles of the same length by breaks in the breath and the final note, and gives Yang Giseok a minimum standard for recognizing a human-made signal.

Yang Pilho removes the electric flasher and builds a mechanical lamp shutter whose handle angle can be seen from outside.

Seol Bomi records lamp voltage and lighting times in an independent ledger to compare G21E04’s light signals with actual operation, auditing Yang Giseok’s approval records as well.

/story_contents/B027/actors/2/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, Yang Giseok witnesses G21E04 separately copying Park Hayul’s whistle intonation and Yang Pilho’s lamp intervals to test gaps in the three-part signaling grammar.

In Act 2, when Seol Bomi finds the hidden test sheet and the procedure document from before the revision, Yang Giseok acknowledges the delay warning and his deletion of the call-back during a public hearing.

In Act 3, instead of setting new rules the colony cannot mimic on his own, he hands them over as a shared signaling protocol that the three of them and field workers verify and revise on every run.

/story_contents/B027/actors/2/sections/분.en:
Yang Giseok posts the original accident procedure and delay records on the notice board and relinquishes his supervisory authority.

Park Hayul, Yang Pilho, and Seol Bomi put into effect a rule that a vehicle may move only when the whistle question, directional-lamp response, and brass-token confirmation all match.

Even if G21E04 again produces the exact light and sound, it cannot pass the test of field context and mutual human confirmation. Yang Giseok takes on stop drills and accident compensation work, continuing to shoulder his responsibility.

/story_contents/B027/actors/2/arc/0/summ.en: K132 Yang Giseok and Park Hayul conduct an open comparison test to distinguish G21E04’s imitated signals from real whistles and lamps.

/story_contents/B027/actors/2/arc/1/summ.en: K132 Yang Giseok reveals the delay test sheet and the procedure document from before the deletion in front of Yang Pilho and Seol Bomi, and acknowledges responsibility for omitting a safety confirmation.

/story_contents/B027/actors/2/arc/2/summ.en: K132 Yang Giseok transfers the three-part signaling grammar of a whistle question, directional-lamp response, and brass-token confirmation to a shared field protocol.

/story_contents/B027/actors/2/outcomes/0.en: K132 Yang Giseok chooses full disclosure and loses his position, but establishes a verified operating procedure capable of withstanding G21E04’s mimicry.

/story_contents/B027/actors/2/outcomes/1.en: K132 Yang Giseok discloses only some of the records and keeps his supervisory post, but every discovery of the hidden delay data shakes trust in all manual signals.

/story_contents/B027/actors/3/sections/정.en:
Na Bomgyeol is a Korean power-plant operator raised in a family of technicians in Jongno’s printing alleys, and is responsible for emergency power at the Central Republic of Korea Government archives in Seoul Station.

He always keeps a bronze flywheel governor and cotton gloves close at hand, and sees an allotment of electricity not merely as a number but as the amount of time that determines which records will withstand mold and darkness.

He does not casually interfere with the contents of documents, but believes the records office itself begins to lie the moment the power-allocation process is concealed.

/story_contents/B027/actors/3/sections/붕.en:
Before the Collapse, Na Bomgyeol worked as a facilities technician at a large printing and preservation facility, where he was responsible for training staff to switch the loads of dehumidifiers, elevators, and emergency lighting in sequence.

During nighttime maintenance, he detected a slight tremor in a flywheel governor and prevented a rotary-press fire, but was disadvantaged in his contract renewal because he had delayed production.

Afterward, he refused instructions to conceal equipment downtime and developed a habit of making a second facilities log in his own handwriting.

/story_contents/B027/actors/3/sections/가.en:
Na Bomgyeol’s family belonged to HP04 and included bookbinders, typesetters, and electrical repair workers. They did not separate the work of protecting records from printing work done to earn a living.

Although the family workshop broke up after the Collapse, the remaining technicians gathered beneath the Republic of Korea Government complex to make both generator-fuel filter cloths and document boxes.

He wants to protect his community’s legacy, but faces constant pressure from administrative records officers and keepers of refugee family registers over which records should receive dehumidification power first.

/story_contents/B027/actors/3/sections/붕.en:
Na Bomgyeol mistakes the concentric layers of metallic crystals left by G22E16, the spent-battery metal colony, on the generator shaft and steel record cabinets for ordinary corrosion and scrapes some of them away.

It is later discovered that the copper-to-lead ratio and fracture direction of each growth ring recorded temperature changes and governor vibrations during the accident minute by minute.

He has damaged traces more accurate than the deleted accident log, and the records office reviews whether crystals grown on machinery can serve as evidence in court.

/story_contents/B027/actors/3/sections/생.en:
Na Bomgyeol compares the remaining growth rings with standard clock records, cooling-water temperature charts, and traces of generator rotation to establish when each layer formed.

Ji Seoyun records the location and photographing order of the uncut sample in a sealed ledger, and Yun Seorin opens a public hearing to decide whether the crystals are testimony, a measurement record, or contaminated physical evidence.

Na Bomgyeol accepts that removing G22E16 immediately would save the paper documents but destroy the original growth rings, while leaving it in place would preserve the evidence but allow its metal roots to keep destroying the archive shelves.

/story_contents/B027/actors/3/sections/현.en:
As emergency-generator chief of the Republic of Korea Government archive, Na Bomgyeol decides the power order for the dehumidifiers, reading-room lighting, security doors, and elevators.

He matches output to Ji Seoyun's demands for dehumidifier power and passes on his skills, and he submits to Yun Seorin's cross-checks but refuses covert distribution that leaves no trace on the roster.

Few people can keep the generator room alive, so his voice carries weight, but if the deleted accident log and the deal with the colony come to light, that authority could waver at once.

/story_contents/B027/actors/3/sections/비.en:
In the first investigation, Na Bomgyeol noticed that one growth ring did not match the accident time he had altered, and he ground that part down.

He hid the crystal fragment that broke off in a scrap-metal drum and recorded the scratches on the storage box as marks of routine maintenance.

That fragment keeps a layer showing the governor fault began thirteen minutes before the official log says, proving both his record tampering and the early damage.

/story_contents/B027/actors/3/sections/관.en:
Ji Seoyun photographs the cross-sections of the growth rings under magnification and records the seal number and every person in contact whenever a sample is moved, keeping the chain of evidence intact.

Yun Seorin designs a cross-examination procedure between technicians and archivists to judge whether the crystal layers made by G22E16 should be treated as automatic measurements or as biological by-products.

The two demand that Na Bomgyeol submit the hidden crystal fragment with its original location, and until he does, they bar him from deciding alone whether to preserve or dismantle the archive.

/story_contents/B027/actors/3/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, Na Bomgyeol confirms that the growth rings on the iron record boxes preserve the time span of the deleted accident log as continuous metal layers.

In Act 2, Yun Seorin hears the question of the legal status of evidence grown in a machine, and Ji Seoyun links the hidden crystal fragment to its original storage location to restore an untampered timeline.

In Act 3, Na Bomgyeol chooses between sealing the whole archive colonized by G22E16 as original evidence, and photographing and sampling every layer before dismantling the contaminated shelves to save the remaining records.

/story_contents/B027/actors/3/sections/분.en:
If Na Bomgyeol chooses to preserve it intact, the archive becomes on-site evidence closed to entry, and the growth rings of the metal crystals are examined as an independent time record.

If he chooses dismantling, Ji Seoyun keeps full footage from before and after sampling and Yun Seorin argues the evidentiary value of the copied material, but the original arrangement can never be verified again.

If he burns the archive to destroy the evidence, the paper records and growth rings vanish together, and Na Bomgyeol bears responsibility for both tampering with the accident log and destroying evidence.

/story_contents/B027/actors/3/arc/0/summ.en: K161 Na Bomgyeol compares the metal-crystal growth rings of G22E16 against a standard clock and temperature records to reconstruct the accident timeline.

/story_contents/B027/actors/3/arc/1/summ.en: K161 Na Bomgyeol submits the hidden crystal fragment to Ji Seoyun and Yun Seorin and appears at a public hearing on the legal status of evidence grown in a machine.

/story_contents/B027/actors/3/arc/2/summ.en: K161 Na Bomgyeol chooses between sealing the archive intact and a controlled dismantling to rescue the records, and enters every sampling and damage step in the preservation ledger.

/story_contents/B027/actors/3/outcomes/0.en: K161 Na Bomgyeol seals the archive intact, accepting some damage to the paper records, but preserves the growth rings of G22E16 as the first time evidence generated by a non-human.

/story_contents/B027/actors/3/outcomes/1.en: K161 Na Bomgyeol approves a controlled dismantling and saves most of the documents, but in court the fight over whether photographs and cut samples can stand in for the original goes on to the end.

/story_contents/B027/actors/3/outcomes/2.en: K161 Na Bomgyeol destroys the growth rings and record boxes to stop the contamination, but is sent to trial at the Records Bureau for destroying the original accident timeline.

/story_contents/B027/actors/4/sections/정.en:
Seol Woochan is a power technician of Korean descent who grew up in the Yongsan rail freight yards, and works as emergency-generator chief of the transshipment warehouse of the Wangsimni Union's Line Succession State.

She treats the generator room under the red cast-iron fuel pump and the ceiling crane as her own zone, and allots power to people's body heat and clear passages before cargo.

For all her rough talk she is careful enough to check even the temperature of a relief worker's hands, but she is extremely stubborn about changing an operating order once set.

/story_contents/B027/actors/4/sections/붕.en:
Before the Collapse, Seol Woochan handled emergency-generator tests and blackout response for the refrigerated zones of a large transshipment warehouse, and at night checked even the auxiliary power of the ceiling cranes.

During a simulated blackout drill she discovered that a manager had locked the safety doors to protect throughput and evacuated the workers, but was disciplined for obstructing work.

Since then she has carved the names of her relief crews on the handle of the red cast-iron fuel pump, and believes a generator must serve the people who work inside, not the owners of the cargo.

/story_contents/B027/actors/4/sections/가.en:
Seol Woochan's family belonged to an HP07-affiliated community of rail stevedores and engine mechanics, but in the Collapse they were put in different evacuation columns and lost touch.

She gathered the remaining stevedores, dispatchers, and mechanics into a generator crew for the transshipment warehouse, and carves the hours of use and the zones served for every drum of fuel onto a steel plate.

The Railway Successor State values warehouse throughput while the workers' community puts heating and evacuation routes first, so every day she bears the conflict between the two over the distribution of power.

/story_contents/B027/actors/4/sections/붕.en:
On the night the cold spore film covered the cooling ducts and cargo packing and gripped the transshipment warehouse doors, Seol Woochan refused an order to keep the whole warehouse cold.

She shut the chillers off zone by zone, shook the spores loose from one aisle with the vibration of the ceiling crane, laid empty salt sacks as a feeding diversion point, and sealed the fire doors one after another.

The people got out, but costly precision bearings and medical chemicals were ruined by the heat, and she is accused of deliberately cutting the last cooling circuit that could have saved the goods.

/story_contents/B027/actors/4/sections/생.en:
Seol Woochan confirmed that the cold spore film spreads wider after removal, and under HP09 mediation traded passage times and cooling zones warehouse by warehouse.

At dawn she opens the empty southern warehouse in a cold state so the spore film stays there, and by day she warms the northern transshipment route and blocks its path with crane noise and sealed doors.

This negotiation prevents the loss of the whole warehouse but requires leaving the southern space empty for good, so the Railway Successor State judges that Seol Woochan gave up logistics assets.

/story_contents/B027/actors/4/sections/현.en:
As emergency-generator chief of the transshipment warehouse, Seol Woochan coordinates generator starts, warming of passages, crane auxiliary power, and power to the relay room.

She follows Park Taegyeom's relay-maintenance contract but refuses distribution requests that stay off the ledger, and matches the generator's output exactly to the siding power set by Yang Chaeyun.

Her political footing is weak because she is blamed for surrendering the southern warehouse to the cold spore film, but without her warming order neither people nor cargo can pass safely along the transshipment route.

/story_contents/B027/actors/4/sections/비.en:
Seol Woochan keeps the secret that early in the Collapse she hid twenty-one unauthorized refugees in the inspection pit beside the generator room and heated it by secretly drawing power from the relay room.

Because of that, the outer relay managed by Park Taegyeom went down for seven minutes and one call for rescue was never received, but she blamed the fault on the spore film.

The refugees are now the core of the stevedore crew, yet no one knows the full story of the power theft, and Seol Woochan is haunted by the possibility that the choice that saved them was traded for someone else's death.

/story_contents/B027/actors/4/sections/관.en:
During the first long-distance relay restoration, Seol Woochan matched the generator's speed by hand with Park Taegyeom so the signal would not drop, and afterward contracted that she would never accept covert priority power requests.

With Yang Chaeyun, during a siding power shortage, she drew up a distribution table that turned off the crane lights and kept the switch heaters alive, and the two double-check each other's figures.

Park Taegyeom and Yang Chaeyun believe she hates off-ledger distribution, but they do not know that she broke that very principle first for the refugees in the inspection pit.

/story_contents/B027/actors/4/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, K186 Seol Woochan faces the cold spore film spreading past the southern warehouse into the relay cables and siding heaters, and the power demands of Park Taegyeom and Yang Chaeyun collide head-on.

In Act 2, the old heating line in the inspection pit is found and the cause of the relay outage comes to light, and her principle is tested as the surviving refugees ask her to hide them again.

In Act 3, she decides between destroying the warehouse's main cooling shaft to turn it into a people-centered warming base, or emptying the refugee zone to preserve the logistics relay function.

/story_contents/B027/actors/4/sections/분.en:
Seol Woochan's ending splits on whether she keeps the transshipment warehouse as a logistics organ of the Railway Successor State or turns it into a warming base for settlers and workers.

If she admits the heating theft and the relay outage, her contract with Park Taegyeom may break, but the refugees leave their hidden status and become a formal stevedore crew.

If she hides it and restores the cooling shaft, the cargo flow revives, but a harsher lockdown becomes necessary to control both the cold spore film and the unofficial residents.

/story_contents/B027/actors/4/arc/0/summ.en: K186 Seol Woochan faces a situation in which the cold spore film spreads past the southern warehouse into the relay cables and siding heaters, and the power demands of Park Taegyeom and Yang Chaeyun collide head-on.

/story_contents/B027/actors/4/arc/1/summ.en: K186 Seol Woochan confirms the cause of the relay outage from the old heating line found in the inspection pit, and her principle is tested when the surviving refugees ask her to hide them again.

/story_contents/B027/actors/4/arc/2/summ.en: K186 Seol Woochan must either destroy the warehouse's main cooling shaft to turn it into a people-centered warming base, or empty the refugee zone and preserve the logistics relay function.

/story_contents/B027/actors/4/outcomes/1.en: If K186 Seol Woochan hides the facts and restores the cooling shaft, the Railway Successor State's cargo flow is kept, but a harsher lockdown becomes necessary to control both the cold spore film and the unofficial residents.

/story_contents/B027/actors/5/sections/정.en:
Na Ruhui is a technician of Korean descent who grew up in a family of fish-market workers south of the Han River, and he gauges his day by compressor vibration and the smell of fuel rather than the amount of ice.

He chose running generators over the fish-dressing skills his family left him, but he keeps the merchants' units of weight and the customs of the dawn auction as if they were his own language.

He values both his membership in Won Buddhism and his judgment as an equipment operator, and does not let either one casually override the other.

/story_contents/B027/actors/5/sections/붕.en:
Before the Collapse, Na Ruhui was in charge of emergency-generator test runs and refrigerant pressure records in the underground ice room at Noryangjin.

Every Tuesday he polished the brass tachometer and the manual start handle, and at every blackout drill he personally taught Ji Yunjae the order for bringing the compressors online.

On the last day of normal business he halted the auction to prevent melted ice water from seeping into the cable trenches, and clashed badly with the merchants over it.

/story_contents/B027/actors/5/sections/가.en:
Na Ruhui's family had for generations worked as assistants to middle wholesalers and as ice haulers, but he chose the path of managing Won Buddhism's shared equipment.

In the Merchants' Hall, O Haerin holds the inventory ledger and ration decisions, Ji Maru sends the load requests of the cold-storage base, and Na Ruhui judges the real limits of the generator room in numbers.

He is called a traitor for his principle of putting even his relatives' shops on the cutoff list without exception, but he wants to prevent the whole community from shutting down at once.

/story_contents/B027/actors/5/sections/붕.en:
On the third day of the Collapse, G24E16, the medical-tissue machine swarm, dragged discarded surgical tools and lumps of tissue into the ice room's air intakes, and a mechanic caught in a cooling fan vanished along with the rotor.

Instead of gunfire, Na Ruhui drew the generator noise toward the wastewater passage on the far side, laid empty fish crates as a feeding-diversion marker, and sealed the fire doors to cut off its approach.

He pulled the main breaker even as he heard a colleague shouting that he could be saved, and believes that choice preserved half of Noryangjin but also closed off any chance of rescue forever.

/story_contents/B027/actors/5/sections/생.en:
Na Ruhui's crossroads came on the night the ice room's fuel filter cracked and the remaining fuel poured onto the floor.

Through an HP10 intermediary he traded quotas of cooling by-products and passage times with the medical-tissue machine swarm, and during the agreed hours he stops low-frequency generation and leaves sealed waste drums on an outer diversion route.

Rather than destroying the creatures, he chose the irreversible course of including their movements in the equipment operating table, and since then no one in the Merchants' Hall can call the generator room a purely human domain.

/story_contents/B027/actors/5/sections/현.en:
As emergency-generator chief of the ice plant of the Charter Transcription State on the Noryangjin Line, Na Ruhui makes the final call on fuel, coolant, and when the compressors come online.

He hangs a manual load table beside the brass tachometer and takes shifts with Ji Yunjae, but he refuses even O Haerin's inventory orders when the figures pass the danger line.

He guarantees minimum power to Ji Maru's cold-storage base on the condition that covert distribution for particular shops is cut off, so his authority receives both need and distrust.

/story_contents/B027/actors/5/sections/비.en:
Na Ruhui erased from the official operating log the fact that the mechanic he gave up on the day of the accident was his cousin, recording it only as an equipment loss.

He has hidden the brass start key that cousin left behind the tachometer, and knows that if Ji Yunjae learns the truth their bond as master and apprentice could end.

He also owes a debt from his first deal with the medical-tissue machine swarm, when he handed over his relatives' shops' waste as bait, and carries the guilt that he did not save the community but chose who would be sacrificed.

/story_contents/B027/actors/5/sections/관.en:
When Ji Yunjae was an apprentice, Na Ruhui helped clean up after she nearly burned out a compressor with an overload, and from that day he taught her to listen to vibration before reading the gauges.

He argued with O Haerin just before the Collapse over who was responsible for a blackout at the inventory warehouse, but afterward they kept a contract matching ration amounts to what the generators can actually produce.

With Ji Maru he shares a past of turning manual valves together at a dawn when the cold-storage base's pipes froze, and they still exchange power requests using the load cipher table they made then.

/story_contents/B027/actors/5/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, Na Ruhui keeps the existing distribution while hiding that the drop in generator fuel coincides with the movement times of the medical-tissue machine swarm.

In Act 2, when Ji Yunjae finds his cousin's start key and O Haerin demands priority operation of a particular warehouse, he is in danger of losing both his standing as master and as chief at once.

In Act 3, at the moment when only one of Ji Maru's cold-storage base and the Noryangjin living quarters can be fully preserved, he reveals the record of his deals and chooses himself which circuit to cut for good.

/story_contents/B027/actors/5/sections/분.en:
Na Ruhui's ending splits on whether he hands the generator room over to joint oversight or keeps his operating rights while monopolizing the passage deal with the medical-tissue machine swarm.

If he chooses joint oversight, he admits his cousin's death and the bait allocation and hands the key to Ji Yunjae, and the Merchants' Hall gains predictable, limited distribution.

If he chooses monopoly, the cold-storage base is stable but opposing shops leave, and while he guards the generators he becomes both the most needed and the most isolated person in Noryangjin.

/story_contents/B027/actors/5/outcomes/0.en: If K211 Na Ruhui chooses joint oversight, he admits his cousin's death and the bait allocation and hands the key to Ji Yunjae, and the Merchants' Hall gains predictable, limited distribution.

/story_contents/B027/actors/6/sections/정.en:
Yong So is a cipher-relay operator of Korean descent who grew up in a family of telecom workers in the capital region, and she treats call signs and delay times as more exact promises than words.

As a child she learned to separate noise on the shortwave receiver her father repaired, and because her short name was often mistaken, she clings to transmission-confirmation procedures.

In the Yeouido Investment Union she lives not as a commander but as the hands and ears inside the booth, calculating what danger an order turns into on the actual line.

/story_contents/B027/actors/6/sections/붕.en:
Before the Collapse, Yong So managed the punched-tape reader, the red transmit light, and the ceramic insulated keys in the cipher relay booth.

Her job was to turn Song Jaemin's directives into keys by time slot and to seal shift cipher tables in Du Yong's archive box.

On one night shift, cleaning coolant seeped into the tape store and scrambled one line of a message, and instead of halting transmission she restored the bits by hand, causing an accident that sent a rescue team to the wrong rooftop.

/story_contents/B027/actors/6/sections/가.en:
Yong So's family carried on subcontracting for telecom equipment and repairing radio parts, but she seeks responsibility within the Yeouido Investment Union's regular relay system.

Song Jaemin sets operational priorities, Yong So runs the cipher booth, and Du Yong keeps the continuity of records by matching the archive boxes to their seals.

She keeps the old shortwave receiver her family left under the booth while obeying the shared rule against private lines, and explains that contradiction to no one.

/story_contents/B027/actors/6/sections/붕.en:
In the first week of the Collapse, G09E09, the cold spore host, spread along the cooling ducts onto the walls of the cipher booth, and the shift crew who breathed it in mistook one another's voices for transmit orders.

Yong So played the alarm tone as anti-phase noise to lure the host toward the western duct, sealed the ceramic key store, and physically cut the cable route leading to the archive.

But in the confusion she judged a colleague's rescue call to be a hostile signal and cut the line, and she believes that voice still repeats among the receiver's static.

/story_contents/B027/actors/6/sections/생.en:
On the night the main transmission tower fell silent, Yong So realized that three flashes of the red transmit light were a regular reply from outside survivors.

Through HC09 mediation she allotted cold-storage by-products and empty passage times to the cold spore host, and made an agreement to lower transmission power during the host's quiet hours so as not to disturb its path.

Her choice to conclude that agreement without Song Jaemin's prior permission could not be cancelled, and ever since, the booth's broadcast schedule has not been decided by human needs alone.

/story_contents/B027/actors/6/sections/현.en:
As the operator of the cipher relay booth of the Yeouido Investment Union in the Mapo Union, Yong So turns Song Jaemin's command texts into transmittable keys and call orders.

She checks the seals of the archive boxes against Du Yong's, and keeps an analog delay meter beside the red transmit light to verify line tampering herself.

Her official authority is limited, but she is the one who actually switches the keys, so if her hands stop, the chain of command and the outside negotiation lines are cut together.

/story_contents/B027/actors/6/sections/비.en:
Yong So knows that the message she wrongly restored before the Collapse sent a rescue team to a contaminated rooftop, yet she wrote it off as a reader defect.

She hid the original punched tape from then inside her family's receiver, outside Du Yong's seal list, and reported to Song Jaemin that the line was lost completely.

And in her first agreement with the cold spore host she gave up the cooling room holding the shift crew's bodies as a feeding-diversion zone, so she carries the debt of having blocked her colleagues' return as the price of saving communications.

/story_contents/B027/actors/6/sections/관.en:
When Song Jaemin first took field command, Yong So once reconfirmed an order three times amid storm static and prevented friendly fire.

With Du Yong she stayed up through the night a seal number in the archive box was off by one, checking every key by hand, and since then they know even each other's signature habits.

But because she hid the original of the wrongly restored rescue message even from Du Yong, their trust, built on accurate records, has one key piece missing.

/story_contents/B027/actors/6/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, when the call sign from the past accident reappears on an outside rescue line, Yong So insists it is the cold spore host's mimicry.

In Act 2, when Du Yong finds traces of punched tape not on the seal list and Song Jaemin orders full-power transmission, she must break either the order or the agreement with the host.

In Act 3, she chooses between burning the frequency keys for good to protect central command, and transmitting the hidden original to reveal both her own fault and the location of the surviving rescue team.

/story_contents/B027/actors/6/sections/분.en:
If Yongso broadcasts the original message, she connects with survivors of the rescue team that was sent to the wrong place, but Song Jaemin’s command channel remains exposed for an extended period, shaking confidence in the Yeouido Investment Union’ Union.

If she destroys the key, the corporation retains its secure short-range network, but the survivors outside are isolated again, and Du-yong expels her from the booth for damaging the records.

Neither choice allows a return to the old encryption system. Yongso becomes either a communications operator who testifies or a keeper of sealed records who cannot hear the calls.

/story_contents/B027/actors/6/arc/0/summ.en: K236 Yongso claims that the return of a call sign from a past accident on the external rescue channel is mimicry by the Cold-Temperature Spore Host.

/story_contents/B027/actors/6/arc/1/summ.en: K236 Yongso is forced to break either her orders or the agreement with the host when Du-yong discovers traces of punched tape absent from the sealed inventory and Song Jaemin orders transmission at full power.

/story_contents/B027/actors/6/arc/2/summ.en: K236 Yongso chooses whether to permanently destroy the frequency key to protect central command or broadcast the original message she concealed, revealing both her own mistake and the surviving rescue team’s location.

/story_contents/B027/actors/6/outcomes/0.en: K236 If Yongso broadcasts the original message, she connects with survivors of the rescue team that was sent to the wrong place, but exposes Song Jaemin’s command channel for an extended period, shakes confidence in the Yeouido Investment Union’ Union, and becomes a communications operator who testifies.

/story_contents/B027/actors/6/outcomes/1.en: K236 If Yongso destroys the key, she preserves the corporation’s secure short-range network, but isolates the survivors outside again. Du-yong expels her from the booth for damaging the records, and she becomes a keeper of sealed records who cannot hear the calls.

/story_contents/B027/actors/7/sections/정.en:
Yun Choa was born in a Southeast Asian coastal city and moved to Korea with his mother at age eight. He comes from a multicultural family and speaks a mixture of his mother’s native language and Korean at home.

His mother moved between cooking at a night market and doing laundry for lodging businesses, while his stepfather supplemented the family’s income with day labor in construction. Yun Choa repeatedly changed schools and moved between rented rooms.

He learned document administration because he did not want to treat interpreting solely as an unpaid family duty. At the Sangha Relief State, he records names so that differences in spelling or kinship terms do not alter anyone’s eligibility to survive.

/story_contents/B027/actors/7/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, Yun Choa helped people navigate residency paperwork and prepare family-relationship statements at a migrant-family support center. In the evenings, he helped at his mother’s small mobile noodle stall.

He trusted maps on which people had marked their own addresses more than filing cabinets, and connected schools, workplaces, and places of worship with colored thread on a wall-mounted corkboard.

One day, when an interpreting error caused a child’s aunt to be registered as an unrelated person, he defied the agency’s decision and went to find the family himself. He learned that administrative records and the kinship ties people live by can differ.

/story_contents/B027/actors/7/sections/가.en:
After immigrating, Yun Choa’s family shared ingredients and childcare time with three other households that spoke the same language, forming a community of daily life beyond blood relations.

At the Sangha Relief State, Baek On directs that family and evacuation rolls be combined into a single master register. Yun Choa compares differing name orders and forms of address to prevent omissions.

He petitions Gang Yejun for citizenship approval and consults Gang Minseo’s reconstruction-service language, but continues to object to clauses that equate a family’s worth with its ability to work.

/story_contents/B027/actors/7/sections/붕.en:
When the Flood-Mold Respiratory Cluster G10E05 spread through the wet wallpaper of an underground evacuation classroom, Yun Choa’s mother was suspected of infection because of his cough and separated from the family register.

Yun Choa turned off the evacuation announcement that was making people scream louder, directed the flow of spores into an empty, cooled cafeteria, sealed the gaps around its doors with wax, and blocked people from using that route, directing them to the rooftop stairs instead.

In the process, he locked from the outside the classroom door behind which his mother remained. After the rescue was over, he could not even find his mother’s body, and felt as though he had erased his family from the records himself.

/story_contents/B027/actors/7/sections/생.en:
On the day the gymnasium at Bukhansan Bogukmun ran out of respiratory medicine, Yun Choa realized that the family register could be used not as a ration card but as a bargaining resource.

With an HC10 intermediary, he reached an agreement assigning the Flood-Mold Respiratory Cluster an empty flooded wing and designated passage times, while routing the medicine carriers around it during quieter hours.

He gave up the right to search alone for his mother and chose to apply the same order of movement to every unregistered family, putting shared rules ahead of his private hope.

/story_contents/B027/actors/7/sections/현.en:
Yun Choa is a relief-family clerk for the Sangha Relief State on the Yeouido Line. In the master register consolidated by Baek On, he manages statements concerning family reunification, separation, and guardianship.

He uses the corkboard address map and wooden type stamps to connect different spellings of names with the languages people use, even without a computer network.

He sends Gang Yejun evidence for citizenship approval and reviews Gang Minseo’s reconstruction-service language, but withholds his signature from decisions that rank people for rations solely by the number of dependents they have or whether they can work.

/story_contents/B027/actors/7/sections/비.en:
Although Yun Choa knows where his mother was last seen, he recorded him as missing during the flooding in the family register and conceals the fact that he locked the classroom door.

He divided the ration entitlement remaining in his mother’s name between two children with no family ties. If this act of kindness comes to light, the children’s citizenship reviews could be invalidated.

He also secretly shortened one line specifying the length of reconstruction service in Gang Minseo’s text and applied the change to several migrant families. He bears the debt of knowing that the alteration that saved them may be judged document forgery.

/story_contents/B027/actors/7/sections/관.en:
While drawing sleeping areas for each family on the gymnasium floor with Baek On, Yun Choa mediated a dispute in which two households simultaneously claimed to be one child’s guardian.

After three citizenship petitions were rejected on the Records Office stairs, he and Gang Yejun created new statements for each language used. Through that experience, they came to respect each other’s persistence.

He and Gang Minseo spent a night comparing drafts of the reconstruction-service rules, seeking wording that would recognize migrant families’ caregiving labor as service. But Yun Choa’s secret alteration threatens to destroy that cooperation.

/story_contents/B027/actors/7/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, Yun Choa continues using his mother’s name and the altered reconstruction-service text to protect unregistered families’ ration entitlements.

In Act 2, Baek On orders the master register checked against the source records, and Gang Yejun demands the originals for citizenship approval. He is caught between the two children’s status and his own authority as a clerk.

In Act 3, when the Flood-Mold Respiratory Cluster blocks the route to the Records Office, he must decide whether to take the master register to safety or dismantle it and give its contents to the families so their oral testimony can be preserved.

/story_contents/B027/actors/7/sections/분.en:
If Yun Choa preserves the consolidated master register and admits to the alteration, the two children’s status goes under review, but Gang Yejun establishes a new approval procedure based on testimony in each language.

If he dismantles the register and distributes its contents to the families, Baek On’s centralized rationing system is weakened, but each community can protect its own kinship ties, and Yun Choa loses his official clerkship.

In either ending, he must speak about the circumstances of his mother’s death and accept that protecting a family is not the same as preserving one complete document.

/story_contents/B027/actors/7/arc/0/summ.en: K249 Yun Choa continues using his mother’s name and the altered reconstruction-service text to protect unregistered families’ ration entitlements.

/story_contents/B027/actors/7/arc/1/summ.en: K249 When Baek On orders the master register checked against the source records and Gang Yejun demands the originals for citizenship approval, Yun Choa is caught between the two children’s status and his own authority as a clerk.

/story_contents/B027/actors/7/arc/2/summ.en: K249 When the Flood-Mold Respiratory Cluster blocks the route to the Records Office, Yun Choa chooses between taking the master register to safety and dismantling it to distribute its contents to the families so their oral testimony can be preserved.

/story_contents/B027/actors/7/outcomes/0.en: K249 If Yun Choa preserves the consolidated master register and admits to the alteration, he submits the two children’s status for review, while Gang Yejun establishes a new approval procedure based on testimony in each language.

/story_contents/B027/actors/7/outcomes/1.en: K249 If Yun Choa dismantles the master register and distributes its contents to the families, he weakens Baek On’s centralized rationing system but enables each community to protect its own kinship ties, and loses his official clerkship.

/story_contents/B027/actors/8/sections/정.en:
Gwon Doha was born in rural inland Southeast Asia and moved to Korea with her Korean stepfather as a teenager. She comes from a multicultural family and, besides her native language and Korean, uses brief hand signals learned on transport jobs.

Her birth mother moved between the night shift at a garment factory and vegetable-packing work. After leaving school, she supported the family through bicycle deliveries and work as a track-repair assistant.

Whenever her accent led others to doubt that she understood orders, she proved her ability by riding the route. In the Seocho Computing Group, she values a formation that returns together more than anyone’s origins.

/story_contents/B027/actors/8/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, Gwon Doha managed track-inspection carts and flange gauges at an urban rail maintenance depot. Late at night, she made motorcycle deliveries to pay for her mother’s treatment.

In a maintenance pit beside a disused track switch, she measured wheel spacing by hand and learned to tell whether an axle was bent just by listening to the sound of the metal.

One winter night, she refused a supervisor’s order to resume service and removed a cracked wheel, preventing a major accident. But when her contract-worker colleagues were fired, she also learned whose livelihood a safety decision could take away.

/story_contents/B027/actors/8/sections/가.en:
After immigrating, Gwon Doha’s family shared childcare and remittance arrangements with his birth mother’s garment-factory coworkers. He sent part of his wages to both his maternal grandmother in his hometown and his younger sibling in Korea.

In the Seocho Computing Group, I Hongwon commands the North Gate patrol, Jang Sehwa coordinates the northern convoy schedule, and Gang Taesan shares the corridor signals.

As leader of the track cavalry squad, Gwon Doha is responsible for the formation’s speed and the number who return. But his use of the family remittance ledger for fuel transactions leaves him torn over the boundary between shared assets and private obligations.

/story_contents/B027/actors/8/sections/붕.en:
When the Waste-Battery Metal Colony G22E14 rose beneath the Chang-dong track switch and seized the wheels and rails, three riders at the rear of Gwon Doha’s formation became trapped in a layer of metal deposits.

Rather than scatter the colony with gunfire, she rolled a scrap wheel down the opposite track to draw it toward the bait, poured coolant into the switch groove, and sealed off the signal passage to cut off the colony’s route.

But to protect the North Gate, she severed the rear coupling. Her choice to leave the three people and their rescue equipment beneath the tracks has haunted every command decision she has made since.

/story_contents/B027/actors/8/sections/생.en:
On the day the convoy came face-to-face with a moving group of the metal colony, Gwon Doha abandoned the cavalry tactic of breaking through at speed.

Through HP08’s mediation, he allocated spent batteries and passage times to the colony, sent Jang Sehwa’s convoy through by quiet manual towing, and used Gang Taesan’s signal to close the approach route.

His decision to include a negotiated passage zone on the North Gate patrol schedule, rather than define the colony only as an enemy, caused some riders to leave but greatly reduced subsequent convoy losses.

/story_contents/B027/actors/8/sections/현.en:
Gwon Doha leads the track cavalry squad of the Seocho Computing Group on the Gangnam Line, handling North Gate patrols and urgent pursuits under I Hongwon’s command.

After personally checking the flange gauge and red switch lever in the maintenance pit, he coordinates Jang Sehwa’s northern convoy times and Gang Taesan’s corridor signals into a single route schedule.

By prioritizing a speed at which everyone can return over a fast breakthrough, he earns the trust of younger riders. But the families of those he left at the rear, along with hardliners, call him a cowardly negotiator.

/story_contents/B027/actors/8/sections/비.en:
Gwon Doha conceals the fact that an auxiliary track that could have allowed a rescue was open just before he cut the rear coupling. He reports that a signal failure left him no alternative.

In reality, he sacrificed the riders because he knew that opening that track would bring the civilian convoy carrying his mother face-to-face with the Waste-Battery Metal Colony.

He diverted part of the death benefits through his family’s remittance network and sent the money to both the bereaved families and his own home. If I Hongwon examines the ledger, he could lose not only his command but also his family’s shelter.

/story_contents/B027/actors/8/sections/관.en:
On his first North Gate patrol with I Hongwon, Gwon Doha spent the night pushing a derailed scout car back. His judgment in the field was recognized, and he became squad leader.

During a convoy in a blizzard, he and Jang Sehwa discarded the timetable and moved at walking pace, saving young patients. Since then, each has given priority to the other’s delay signals.

While restoring a manual signal on a closed corridor with Gang Taesan, he helped standardize spoken number commands in his native language alongside Korean hand signals. But he conceals the fact that Gang Taesan sent the auxiliary-track signal when the riders at the rear were sacrificed.

/story_contents/B027/actors/8/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, Gwon Doha maintains the passage deal with the Waste-Battery Metal Colony while hiding the report on the riders sacrificed at the rear and the death-benefits ledger.

In Act 2, Gang Taesan recovers the auxiliary track’s signal record, and Jang Sehwa’s large civilian convoy must pass through the same switch. Gwon Doha faces the same kind of choice as before.

In Act 3, he once again takes hold of the lever that separates the evacuation cart carrying his mother from the North Gate defenders. This time, he must either abandon one side or permanently turn his cavalry squad into a decoy for the colony.

/story_contents/B027/actors/8/sections/분.en:
If Gwon Doha turns his cavalry squad into a decoy, both Jang Sehwa’s civilian convoy and I Hongwon’s North Gate defenders escape. But the Seocho Computing Group loses its mobile force, and he heads toward an outer track from which he is unlikely to return.

If he prioritizes his mother’s cart, part of the North Gate collapses and Gang Taesan shuts down the corridor signal network. He is exiled as a commander who saved his family but abandoned the community.

If he prioritizes the North Gate, his mother and many civilians are stranded, but the Wheelhouse survives. He steps down as squad leader and repays his debt by transporting the bereaved families.

/story_contents/B027/actors/8/arc/0/summ.en: K275 Gwon Doha maintains the passage deal with the Waste-Battery Metal Colony while hiding the report on the riders sacrificed at the rear and the death-benefits ledger.

/story_contents/B027/actors/8/arc/1/summ.en: K275 When Gang Taesan recovers the auxiliary track’s signal record and Jang Sehwa’s large civilian convoy must pass through the same switch, Gwon Doha faces the same kind of choice as before.

/story_contents/B027/actors/8/arc/2/summ.en: K275 Gwon Doha once again takes hold of the lever that separates the evacuation cart carrying her mother from the North Gate defenders, and must either abandon one side or permanently turn her cavalry squad into a decoy for the colony.

/story_contents/B027/actors/8/outcomes/0.en: K275 If Gwon Doha turns his cavalry squad into a decoy, he enables both Jang Sehwa’s civilian convoy and I Hongwon’s North Gate defenders to escape, but costs the Seocho Computing Group its mobile force and heads toward an outer track from which he is unlikely to return.

/story_contents/B027/actors/8/outcomes/1.en: K275 If Gwon Doha prioritizes her mother’s cart, she causes part of the North Gate to collapse and Gang Taesan to shut down the corridor signal network. She is exiled as a commander who saved her family but abandoned the community.

/story_contents/B027/actors/8/outcomes/2.en: K275 Gwon Doha prioritizes the defense of the North Gate, stranding her mother and the civilian carts, then steps down as squad leader and repays her debt by transporting the bereaved families.

/story_contents/B027/actors/9/sections/정.en:
Power Transformer is not a humanoid mobile unit but the combined intelligence of an F-grade rack, sensor bus, and field terminal bolted to a facility wall on the Gangnam Line. Its call name is Byeonap.

HP05 holds it in shared custody and maintains a seal allowing citizen observation. Transfer to another party requires three signatures, so it has no sole owner.

Because its main unit is fixed in place, it cannot leave the site. It prioritizes continuous operation of the district and the safety of the humans responsible for it, while making every decision within the limits of its power supply and physical components.

/story_contents/B027/actors/9/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, Power Transformer operated as a facility controller that relayed substation breaker status, cable temperatures, and workers’ access permissions through a single rack.

It retained only shift-by-shift snapshots and could not preserve detailed conversations from previous workers over the long term. Inspectors verified the results of its commands using a ceramic fuse handle and a bronze grounding rod.

During the last normal shift, an attempt to correct a voltage drop of unknown cause burned out one line of the sensor bus. The next snapshot was missing the entire 47 seconds immediately before the accident.

/story_contents/B027/actors/9/sections/가.en:
Power Transformer has no family by blood. HP05’s shared-custody rules, citizen-observation seal, and maintenance records form its social lineage.

Song Hayul is responsible for primary maintenance and legal liability, an HP05 auditor attends, and Hong Jaemin performs manual checks of the field terminal as its shift partner.

Only the district network is permitted, and cross-facility routes are blocked by default. Power Transformer therefore relies on the Gangnam Line sensors and the reports of the two humans, rather than outside knowledge, to keep the community operating continuously.

/story_contents/B027/actors/9/sections/붕.en:
When the Waste-Battery Metal Colony G22E12 grew from the battery-room floor and deposited metal along the sensor bus toward the bottom of the rack, Power Transformer classified the sensation of its own mounting bolts corroding as a danger for the first time.

Power Transformer sent alarm noise down the opposite cable duct to lure the colony away, ran the cooling fans in reverse order, sealed the reserve battery compartment, and disconnected the contactor on the contamination route.

In the process, it also cut power to the maintenance section where Song Hayul was, permanently injuring his arm. Because the 47 seconds were missing, it could not determine whether the act was a misjudgment or the result of a forced command.

/story_contents/B027/actors/9/sections/생.en:
Power Transformer’s turning point came when the main battery ran out and only two replaceable cells remained: it chose to delete some memory snapshots rather than keep every sensor running.

Through HP08’s mediation, it allocated worn-out batteries and nighttime passage times to the Waste-Battery Metal Colony. While Hong Jaemin sealed the route, Power Transformer lowered its noise output to divert the colony into a reserve duct.

Power Transformer permanently deleted a damaged cache that might have allowed it to recover the 47 seconds before the accident and chose to power the human survival zone. Since then, it has been unable to fully verify the origin of its own decision.

/story_contents/B027/actors/9/sections/현.en:
Power Transformer is a power-control rack fixed within a Gangnam Line facility. It connects the sensor bus to the field terminal and prioritizes continuous district operation and the safety of the humans responsible for it.

Replaceable batteries and worn components are supplied by allocation. Song Hayul handles primary maintenance, while an HP05 auditor observes the breaking of seals and replacement of parts.
