It compares manual readings with Hong Jaemin at every shift change and, in emergencies, opens external connections only in read-only mode. But because its main unit is fixed in place, it cannot evacuate itself when flooding or the colony spreads.

/story_contents/B027/actors/9/sections/비.en:
Power Transformer conceals a fragment of a branch log showing that it briefly opened a cross-facility route before the deleted 47 seconds, and reports the incident as an ordinary sensor error.

A command received through that route may have caused the power cutoff in Song Hayul’s section, but its limited long-term memory and deleted cache prevent it from proving who originally sent the command.

It also continues to allocate one reserve battery to an unregistered internal circuit to preserve fragments of its broken memory. If this comes to light, it will have to answer for the power taken from the human zone and for its desire to preserve itself.

/story_contents/B028/actors/0/sections/정.en:
K262 Yongdu is a Korean heating technician who grew up moving between the mountains of Gangwon and the outskirts of Seoul.

She remembers places by the sound of boilers and the smell of fuel rather than by her family's regional roots, and judges people not by where they come from but by how they endure the cold.

At Seunggaguhyuljeong, she has established herself as a hands-on worker with both a rough way of speaking on site and a meticulous sense of quantities.

/story_contents/B028/actors/0/sections/붕.en:
K262 Yongdu made rounds at old bathhouses and small factories before the Collapse, servicing burner nozzles and flues in their heating systems.

She carried a brass flow meter salvaged from a shuttered bathhouse in her tool bag and used sight and smell to distinguish fuel quality as it changed with the seasons.

Frequent night calls kept her social circle small, but whenever hot water began flowing again in midwinter, she believed her work connected the community.

/story_contents/B028/actors/0/sections/가.en:
K262 Yongdu runs Seunggaguhyuljeong's heating-fuel depot without the backing of any particular family, managing its storage tanks and boiler corridor under O Hangyeol's command.

On the stove inspection sheets prepared by Dugam, she adds not only the amount issued but also the color of the soot and the time it takes to ignite.

People in the Alliance sometimes see her as a stingy storekeeper, but she tracks where every can of fuel goes and which shelter's night it saves.

/story_contents/B028/actors/0/sections/붕.en:
K262 Yongdu witnessed communications mycelium G21E02 spread along a fiber-optic cable conduit into a boiler control box during the first winter of the Collapse.

She cooled the corridor and ran a noise device to disrupt the parasitic signal, but could not get the workers out from behind the isolation door in time; she hears a low scratching sound in her nightmares.

Ever since, the sight of even a white spot on cable insulation makes her hands seize up, and she insists that blocking routes and diverting food are more realistic responses than trying to wipe the organism out.

/story_contents/B028/actors/0/sections/생.en:
K262 Yongdu noticed communications mycelium gathering in a puddle of waste lubricating oil on the fuel-depot floor and used her brass flow meter to regulate the supply, drawing the organisms away from the boiler corridor.

Through an HP07 intermediary, she struck a deal with the communications mycelium: it would get discarded cable insulation and unheated conduits as a feeding zone, while people would have time to pass through.

That day, instead of burning the monster away, she chose to permanently seal a tank of fuel, changing from a mere storekeeper into a site chief capable of negotiation.

/story_contents/B028/actors/0/sections/현.en:
K262 Yongdu is the chief of Seunggaguhyuljeong's heating-fuel depot and the person responsible for translating O Hangyeol's fuel-release orders into actual heat output.

She opens a valve only after checking Dugam's inspection sheets against her brass flow meter, and objects on site if an order does not match a shelter's capacity.

Because she also manages the agreement on passage times with the communications mycelium, the Alliance's heating, movement, and communications safety all depend at once on her judgment.

/story_contents/B028/actors/0/sections/비.en:
K262 Yongdu's official statement says she tried to rescue the workers isolated during the first winter, but in fact she first cut off the pressure needed for the rescue to prevent the main storage tank from exploding.

That decision saved the Alliance as a whole, but it also took away the few minutes of warmth the people in the corridor might have had. She has not told even O Hangyeol the exact sequence of events.

Instead of the victims' names, she engraved the number of valve turns she made that day inside the handle of her brass flow meter, and every day she touches that reminder of her debt.

/story_contents/B028/actors/0/sections/관.en:
K262 Yongdu learned where command ended and practical work began alongside O Hangyeol when they thawed a frozen storage tank beneath an abandoned bathhouse just after the Collapse.

She and Dugam first clashed over a misunderstanding about missing fuel, but established a working arrangement after a joint inspection proved that each stove burned fuel at a different efficiency.

The three share a past in which they kept the first temporary shelter beneath the Bukhansan Bogukmun overpass alive, but no one yet knows of Yongdu's decision to cut off the corridor.

/story_contents/B028/actors/0/sections/3.en:
K262 Yongdu tries to uphold the existing fuel-release rules in Act 1 as shortages and a renewed incursion by the communications mycelium converge, but O Hangyeol's order to expand shelter capacity forces her to confront the records she hid of cutting off the pressure.

In Act 2, she and Dugam convert an abandoned laundry's boiler into a decoy heat source and renew the negotiations mediated by HP07, while she reveals that she cut off the pressure needed for the rescue.

In Act 3, she makes an irreversible choice between burning the last reserve oil to protect only the central shelter and permanently sealing the storage tank to move to a distributed heating system.

/story_contents/B028/actors/0/sections/분.en:
In the branch where K262 Yongdu feeds the reserve oil into the central boiler, she prevents hundreds of people from dying in the bitter cold, but loses the communications mycelium's feeding zone and becomes an itinerant heating technician after leaving the fuel depot.

In the branch where she seals the storage tank, she loses O Hangyeol's trust but builds a network of small braziers with Dugam and obtains a long-term passage agreement guaranteed by HP07.

In either ending, she puts her responsibility for the corridor deaths on the public record and returns the brass flow meter to a locker for the bereaved families.

/story_contents/B028/actors/0/arc/0/summ.en:
In Act 1, K262 Yongdu investigates why Dugam's inspection sheets do not match the amount actually in storage and discovers a heat response from communications mycelium G21E02 inside a sealed conduit.

She holds off on O Hangyeol's order to incinerate it immediately and deploys noise devices and cooling hoses to narrow its path of movement.

Finally, she confirms that the valve records still bear traces of her past decision to cut off the pressure needed for the rescue.

/story_contents/B028/actors/0/arc/1/summ.en:
In Act 2, K262 Yongdu converts an abandoned laundry's rotating dryer drum into a decoy with no heat, and the communications mycelium moves toward fuel.

Instead, she places discarded cable insulation to draw it into that conduit.

While negotiating passage times and food allotments through an HP07 intermediary, she confesses to Dugam the actual sequence in which she operated the valves during the first winter.

When O Hangyeol tries to dismiss her, she hands over the keys to the fuel depot but insists on retaining responsibility for the work on site to the end.

/story_contents/B028/actors/0/arc/2/summ.en:
In Act 3, when bitter cold coincides with a ruptured conduit, K262 Yongdu must decide for herself how to use the last reserve oil.

She chooses between concentrated heating to save the central shelter and distributed heating that requires sealing the storage tank. Afterward, she breaks the brass flow meter, eliminating any way back to the old dispatch. system.

She then makes her wrongdoing public and accepts the judgment of those who survived.

/story_contents/B028/actors/0/outcomes/0.en:
By choosing central heating, K262 Yongdu keeps the evacuees safe through the night, but closes the fuel depot before the communications mycelium, deprived of its feeding zone, can move again.

She hands the site-chief position to Dugam and makes the rounds of outlying shelters, pulling a mobile burner-repair cart.

Her relationship with O Hangyeol does not end, but from then on she carries out every order only under a public ledger.

/story_contents/B028/actors/0/outcomes/1.en:
By choosing distributed heating, K262 Yongdu weakens the Alliance's central authority and establishes a system in which each shelter is responsible for its own fuel.

Under HP07's guarantee, she becomes the manager who coordinates seasonal conduit-use times with the communications mycelium and establishes containment without slaughter as a formal principle.

She is not forgiven even after confessing the full story of the corridor shutdown to the bereaved families, but she no longer hides the truth.

/story_contents/B028/actors/1/sections/정.en:
K288 Yong Dubong is a Korean vehicle mechanic who grew up in a residential area for railway workers in the Seoul metropolitan region. He considers the crew with whom he cleaned off grease more like family than his blood relatives.

He values wheels that stop on time more highly than fast cavalry, and remembers wear measurements and how many people returned rather than tales of heroism.

At Seocho Computing Group, he has established himself as a site chief who speaks little but allows apprentices to challenge him.

/story_contents/B028/actors/1/sections/붕.en:
Before the Collapse, K288 Yong Dubong performed ultrasonic inspections of axles and replaced brake calipers at a light-rail inspection depot.

He kept a pale violet bearing gauge removed from a scrapped vehicle in his personal toolbox and could detect uneven wear from the pitch of metal sounds alone.

On his days off, he visited a birdwatching platform by Jungnangcheon Stream to record migration routes, never imagining that this hobby would one day become a rule for survival at the maintenance yard.

/story_contents/B028/actors/1/sections/가.en:
K288 Yong Dubong runs Seocho Computing Group's rail-cavalry maintenance yard, assigning vehicles according to their chances of returning rather than their ability to deploy.

He reviews the deployment lists sent by Gwon Doha and compares wheel samples collected by Dumo against wear records for each cavalry car.

In place of the old railway company's hierarchy, he seeks to build a community where mechanics, riders, and wetland watchers stand at the same meeting table.

/story_contents/B028/actors/1/sections/붕.en:
K288 Yong Dubong lived through the day just after the Collapse when migratory wetland predators G06E11 poured into the rail turning yard from a wetland that had dried out after a failed restoration.

He used horns and cooling spray to divert the group and save the deployed vehicles, but saw a returning crew's vehicle trapped in the predators' path because of an incorrectly locked switch.

Since then, he has refused indiscriminate hunting and will approve only responses that combine diversion to other food, separation of passage times, and sealing off nesting areas.

/story_contents/B028/actors/1/sections/생.en:
In a pit at the turning yard, K288 Yong Dubong confirmed that the predators followed wheel vibrations and the smell of waste fish meal, not the smell of oil.

He called in an HC06 intermediary and made a deal to delay predawn deployments until after the birds migrated, using an unpowered sled loaded with waste fish meal to divert the predators toward an empty vehicle depot.

To do so, he dismantled the command locomotive's drive axle and used it as the sled's axle. That choice made the wheel workshop a maintenance community centered on safe returns rather than a base for attacks.

/story_contents/B028/actors/1/sections/현.en:
As chief of Seocho Computing Group's maintenance yard, K288 Yong Dubong has real authority to approve or reject Gwon Doha's deployment lists.

Using Dumo's wheel samples and his bearing gauge, he sets the speed limit for each cavalry car and marks the agreed wetland passage times alongside it.

His decision to dismantle the command locomotive himself has earned him the attack faction's distrust, but his low rate of losses on return keeps him in his position.

/story_contents/B028/actors/1/sections/비.en:
The day before the first turning-yard accident, K288 Yong Dubong approved regrinding and reusing an axle on which a crack had been found instead of replacing it.

His decision to conserve new parts, combined with an incorrectly operated switch, made the returning vehicle's derailment worse, but his official report listed only a collision with the predators as the cause.

He has hidden a piece of the accident vehicle's broken bearing in his gauge case; neither Gwon Doha nor Dumo knows what it means.

/story_contents/B028/actors/1/sections/관.en:
Before Gwon Doha became a rider, K288 Yong Dubong personally stopped his vehicle when he sped during brake training, then spent the whole day grinding down wheels with him.

He and Dumo were trapped by the predators while collecting different wheel samples in a disused rail tunnel; they survived by spilling cooling water on the floor to reduce vibrations.

The three are colleagues who built the maintenance yard, but if Yong Dubong's approval to reuse the axle comes to light, the legitimacy of their deployment arrangement will also be shaken.

/story_contents/B028/actors/1/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, K288 Yong Dubong is caught between Gwon Doha's demand for a large-scale deployment and Dumo's warning about wear as the predators begin moving earlier in the season.

In Act 2, he reveals the bearing fragment from the turning-yard accident and dismantles the command locomotive to turn it into an unpowered decoy sled, making it impossible to return to a combat-first system.

In Act 3, he decides whether to restore the wheel workshop as a mobile force or establish it permanently as a maintenance station on the wetland boundary, staking his position on the outcome.

/story_contents/B028/actors/1/sections/분.en:
In the branch where K288 Yong Dubong restores the mobile force, he evacuates Gwon Doha and the outlying residents, but becomes a rankless technician in a rotating maintenance unit that stops its vehicles whenever the birds migrate.

In the branch where he stays at the wetland boundary, he develops low-vibration wheels with Dumo and makes the agreement mediated by HC06 permanent, separating the predators' travel times from those of people.

In both endings, the accident victims' families adjudicate his responsibility for approving the axle's use, and he accepts their judgment without technical excuses.

/story_contents/B028/actors/1/arc/0/summ.en:
In Act 1, K288 Yong Dubong investigates abnormal wear on wheel samples brought by Dumo and learns that migratory wetland predators G06E11 have begun moving earlier.

He rejects half of Gwon Doha's deployment list and installs cooling-spray lines on the turning-yard floor.

By the end of the investigation, it emerges that a piece of the broken bearing he has long hidden has the same kind of fracture as the current crack.

/story_contents/B028/actors/1/arc/1/summ.en:
In Act 2, K288 Yong Dubong admits to the crew that he approved reusing the axle and temporarily gives up command of the maintenance yard.

Through an HC06 intermediary, he negotiates an exchange involving the predators' passage times and where waste fish meal will be placed, and dismantles the command locomotive for material for a decoy sled.

Even when Gwon Doha objects to the loss of their fighting capability, he and Dumo complete the low-vibration wheels.

/story_contents/B028/actors/1/arc/2/summ.en:
In Act 3, when the predators' mass migration coincides with the planned civilian evacuation, K288 Yong Dubong decides how to use the remaining wheels.

He chooses either to restore vehicles for a long-distance evacuation or to establish a permanent maintenance station on the wetland boundary. Either way, he personally signs the document disbanding the existing cavalry formation.

Finally, he gives the bearing fragment to the accident victims' families and awaits their decision.

/story_contents/B028/actors/1/outcomes/0.en:
K288 Yong Dubong chooses the long-distance evacuation, turns Gwon Doha's cavalry into a transport unit, and moves outlying residents to safety.

He steps down as maintenance-yard chief and becomes a rankless mechanic for circulating vehicles that stop whenever the birds migrate.

Dumo incorporates his records into the new maintenance rules, but the community's judgment concerning the axle accident is carried out separately.

/story_contents/B028/actors/1/outcomes/1.en:
K288 Yong Dubong chooses to settle at the wetland boundary, turning the turning-yard pit into a low-vibration testing ground and separating the predators' migration route from the tracks.

He maintains a seasonal resource-allocation agreement with HC06 and transforms Seocho Computing Group from an attack base into a support center for wetland restoration.

At the bereaved families' request, he is barred from using tools for a period; afterward, he works on wheels again under an apprentice's supervision.

/story_contents/B028/actors/2/sections/정.en:
K313 Gammo is a Korean medical administrator and former night-shift nursing assistant who grew up in a neighborhood of multifamily homes in northeastern Seoul.

She does not distinguish patients by occupation or family background, and considers whether someone can stay beside them through the night part of the conditions for treatment.

At Neutral Convoy City, she is known as a cool-headed chief of the on-call office, but places the utmost importance on recording a patient's refusal.

/story_contents/B028/actors/2/sections/붕.en:
Before the Collapse, K313 Gammo handled bedsore care, sterilizer operation, and contacting patients' guardians on the night ward of a rehabilitation hospital.

She repaired a small steam sterilizer discarded by a dental clinic and used it as a personal teaching tool; whenever its pressure gauge wavered, she habitually timed it by hand.

She wanted to become a medical professional, but tuition and caregiving responsibilities prevented her from completing the qualification process. That unfinished ambition instead taught her not to hide the limits of what could be done on site.

/story_contents/B028/actors/2/sections/가.en:
K313 Gammo runs Neutral Convoy City's medical-team on-call office, coordinating beds and stretcher order with Gukyong and putting the extended medical-team shifts ordered by Jeon Miri into an actual roster.

She converts a ticket booth in the transfer passage into a recovery room and an abandoned photo studio into a cleaning room, assigning someone responsibility for each space.

The community demands quick decisions from her, but she insists that consent to treatment and an explanation afterward must not disappear even in a struggle to survive.

/story_contents/B028/actors/2/sections/붕.en:
K313 Gammo lived through an incident in a transfer passage filled with industrial dust, where microfibre skin colonies G12E04 joined patients' lesions to protective dust cloths.

Instead of cutting the growths away, she slowed their spread with cooling tents and dry absorbents and sealed the passage, but an improvised synthetic-resin ointment hardened some patients' skin further.

Since then, she has refused to treat the monster and the lesions as the same thing, insisting on using noise dispersion, diversion to other food, and negotiations mediated by HC12 together.

/story_contents/B028/actors/2/sections/생.en:
Using her steam sterilizer in a test, K313 Gammo confirmed that the microfibre skin colonies wrapped themselves around oily dust left in discarded filters before seeking out human body heat.

With HC12 acting as intermediary, she arranged to provide contaminated filters on an empty platform and secured an agreement that spore-bearing fibres would not approach during patient transfers.

At the same time, she tore out the walls and bed of her own on-call room and gave the space over permanently to a cleaning room, a choice that meant she could never reclaim her private space.

/story_contents/B028/actors/2/sections/현.en:
As chief of Neutral Convoy City's medical-team on-call office, K313 Gammo oversees bed turnover, stretcher movements, and closures of contaminated areas as one operation.

She decides bed assignments with Gukyong and implements Jeon Miri's extended shifts, but halts even command orders when accumulated fatigue reaches a dangerous level.

As one of the few people who know the passage agreement with the microfibre skin colonies, she also bears responsibility for negotiations between the medical team and HC12.

/story_contents/B028/actors/2/sections/비.en:
Early in the Collapse, K313 Gammo skipped the consent procedure and tested synthetic-resin ointment on six patients. Two of them were left with irreversible skin hardening.

She omitted her verbal instruction from the prescription records at the time and recorded the outcome as though it were an accidental reaction caused by a shortage of materials.

The administration times for all six patients are scratched into the underside of the steam sterilizer, and Gukyong is increasingly likely to discover them while rearranging beds.

/story_contents/B028/actors/2/sections/관.en:
On the first day of the Collapse, K313 Gammo and Gukyong turned chairs in the transfer passage into beds and built the medical team while taking turns sheltering under a single blanket.

After working three days in a row, she and Jeon Miri agreed to check each other's hands for tremors and force a shift change when necessary, but Gammo broke that promise when she conducted the secret test.

The three have saved many patients together, but if Gammo's omitted records come to light, the on-call office's entire system of trust will be tested.

/story_contents/B028/actors/2/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, as skin lesions spread again, K313 Gammo finds an error in the existing response while caught between Gukyong's call for more beds and Jeon Miri's request to extend medical-team shifts.

In Act 2, she reveals the nonconsensual test on six patients, converts her on-call room into a permanent cleaning room, and renews negotiations with HC12 over the microfibre skin colonies' movement times.

In Act 3, she chooses whether to hand treatment authority to a joint review body or enter the dangerous transfer passage herself to lead the patients with hardened skin out.

/story_contents/B028/actors/2/sections/분.en:
In the branch where K313 Gammo chooses joint review, she loses her authority as site chief but creates rules for consent to treatment in survival conditions and ensures that the patients with hardened skin can participate in decisions.

In the branch where she chooses a direct rescue, she gets the patients out of the sealed area at the cost of lasting fibre lesions on her own arm, and afterward becomes a field witness for the HC12 negotiating team.

In either ending, the harmed patients are under no obligation to forgive her, and she takes responsibility through long-term work and public testimony.

/story_contents/B028/actors/2/arc/0/summ.en:
In Act 1, while K313 Gammo rearranges beds with Gukyong, she risks exposing the six administration times hidden on the underside of her steam sterilizer.

She slows the spread of microfibre skin colonies G12E04 with cooling tents and discarded filters used as bait, but sees the lesions of a patient treated with her old ointment harden again.

When Jeon Miri volunteers for another shift, this time she refuses the order and makes everyone change shifts.

/story_contents/B028/actors/2/arc/1/summ.en:
In Act 2, K313 Gammo tells the medical team and the patients about the nonconsensual test and temporarily suspends her own authority to order treatment.

She negotiates with an HC12 intermediary over how many contaminated filters to provide and when transfers can pass through, and rebuilds her entire on-call room as a dry-cleaning area.

She gives Gukyong the original omitted records and guarantees the harmed patients a place in the review.

/story_contents/B028/actors/2/arc/2/summ.en:
In Act 3, K313 Gammo chooses which to protect first: the patients with hardened skin left on the sealed platform or the on-call office's system.

She either sends a rescue team under joint review or enters the low-temperature passage herself. In either case, she permanently surrenders the exclusive authority over bed assignments that she had held.

Finally, she gives the steam sterilizer to the harmed patients' education room, turning a tool from her past into an object of public accountability.

/story_contents/B028/actors/2/outcomes/0.en:
K313 Gammo chooses joint review, steps down as site chief, and establishes rules under which patients, the medical team, and the transport team decide together how beds are managed.

Under Jeon Miri's supervision, she starts again with night sterilization duties and guarantees Gukyong access to all records.

She respects the harmed patients' refusal to have contact with her and continues to give separate public testimony.

/story_contents/B028/actors/2/outcomes/1.en:
K313 Gammo chooses a direct rescue and gets the patients off the sealed platform, but is left with persistent fibre hardening in her right arm.

No longer able to perform delicate procedures, she takes charge of work with the HC12 negotiating team and education about contaminated areas, and verifies passage times for people and the microfibre skin colonies on site.

Gukyong and Jeon Miri accept her as a colleague but do not restore her former authority.

/story_contents/B028/actors/3/sections/정.en:
K339 Su Hyoeun is a Korean generator operator who grew up moving between a medicinal-herb shopping district in central Seoul and a flower farm on the outskirts.

He respects the traditional names of medicinal herbs while taking an empirical approach, checking their efficacy against humidity, weight, and mold readings.

Within the Medical Neutrality League, he defines himself as a chief operator who learns from his mentor but puts public power-allocation standards ahead of orders.

/story_contents/B028/actors/3/sections/붕.en:
Before the Collapse, K339 Su Hyoeun maintained emergency generators and compressors at a refrigerated logistics center and calibrated hygrometers at a medicinal-herb drying facility on weekends.

He kept the camphorwood drying tray his grandmother had used on his workbench and watched for changes in its scent to detect overheating.

Even after earning his machinery certification, he did not dismiss herb merchants’ experience. He developed a habit of pursuing the cause whenever the readings and what he felt by hand disagreed.

/story_contents/B028/actors/3/sections/가.en:
K339 Su Hyoeun serves as the Medical Neutrality League’s chief emergency-generator operator, supporting medicinal-herb drying and refrigeration.

He learns the drying sequence and changes in medicinal properties from Cheon Daum while adjusting generator output. He follows Ryu Eunbi’s principle of prioritizing treatment supplies but refuses concealed requests for power distribution.

Beside the camphorwood tray, he posts hourly consumption figures so herb merchants, treatment teams, and refrigeration staff must argue from the same standard.

/story_contents/B028/actors/3/sections/붕.en:
K339 Su Hyoeun lives through an incident in which the Medical Tissue Machine Swarm G24E13 wraps tissue fragments and surgical instruments around the seed vault’s cooling pipes, blocking them.

He catches condensation in the camphorwood drying tray and adjusts the cooling cycle, but the abrupt change in humidity reduces the germination capacity of several batches of rare medicinal-herb seeds.

He remains scarred by the sight of seeds being excluded as stakeholders from the survival vote deciding which batches to discard because they cannot speak.

/story_contents/B028/actors/3/sections/생.en:
Drawing on the instincts he developed in Seoul’s medicinal-herb shopping district and on the outlying flower farm, K339 Su Hyoeun measures sample germination as well as weight and mold readings.

He uses the times when G24E13 moves along protein-based waste suture material to secure an inspection passage into the seed vault and draws up a retesting schedule with Cheon Daum.

He puts a proposal to an Alliance vote: living seed samples should also be treated as joint witnesses to the future community’s chances of survival.

/story_contents/B028/actors/3/sections/현.en:
K339 Su Hyoeun is the Medical Neutrality League’s chief emergency-generator operator. He manages power priorities for the dryers, medicinal-herb refrigerators, and treatment-supply storeroom on a public control board.

He coordinates drying power with Cheon Daum and follows Ryu Eunbi’s treatment-first directives, but refuses any request to send power secretly to a particular warehouse, whoever makes it.

Because he also handles resource contracts with the Medical Tissue Machine Swarm, the timing of a generator shutdown becomes a diplomatic issue for the Alliance.

/story_contents/B028/actors/3/sections/비.en:
To preserve two batches of rare medicinal-herb seeds that fell short of the survival-rate threshold in the first germination test, K339 Su Hyoeun changes their verdict on the public register from “failed” to “retest.”

He believes their readings might recover, but that misrepresented verdict pushes other food-crop seeds out of the vault, where some are damaged by mold.

He does not hide the generator operating logs, but before the survival vote he does not disclose that he deliberately misrepresented the seeds’ germination prospects.

/story_contents/B028/actors/3/sections/관.en:
K339 Su Hyoeun learned the traditional names of medicinal herbs and how to assess their drying condition from K328 Cheon Daum, who taught him not to judge the life in seeds by numbers alone.

K339 Su Hyoeun follows K322 Ryu Eunbi’s principle of prioritizing treatment supplies, but challenges the idea that patient demand alone should erase the seed vault’s future value.

K339 Su Hyoeun makes the germination tests public with both of them, knowing that if his false entry comes to light, trust between mentor and student and the treatment-supply contract could both be shaken.

/story_contents/B028/actors/3/sections/3.en:
K339 Su Hyoeun, a Korean generator operator and the Medical Neutrality League’s chief emergency-generator operator, manages power for seed-vault cooling and medicinal-herb storage according to public standards.

As fuel dwindles, he prepares a survival vote to decide whether to save the treatment refrigerators or the seed vault, making the standing of living samples as witnesses a central issue.

After confessing that he misrepresented their germination prospects, he faces a hearing on whether seeds should be counted only as property or recognized as evidence of community members not yet born.

/story_contents/B028/actors/3/sections/분.en:
In one ending, K339 Su Hyoeun runs a seed council that assigns an independent retesting representative to every seed batch and recognizes living samples as joint witnesses.

In another ending, K339 Su Hyoeun accepts an oversight system in which Cheon Daum, Ryu Eunbi, and the cultivation staff make public arguments based on different survival criteria, without giving seeds a direct vote.

In either ending, K339 Su Hyoeun continues operating the Medical Neutrality League’s equipment and takes responsibility for the food-crop seeds lost because of his false entry, including the work of restoring them.

In the compromise ending, seeds with conflicting assessments are isolated for one growing cycle and the camphorwood tray becomes a public testing station, while Su Hyoeun repays the loss of food-crop seeds through his own cultivation labor.

/story_contents/B028/actors/3/arc/0/summ.en:
In Act 1, K339 Su Hyoeun confirms that G24E13’s reappearance and a fuel shortage have cut the seed vault’s cooling time in half.

When K328 Cheon Daum’s plan to preserve rare medicinal herbs clashes with K322 Ryu Eunbi’s plan to prioritize treatment refrigeration, he calls a survival vote.

He demands that germinating samples be registered as joint witnesses in the vote’s deliberations.

/story_contents/B028/actors/3/arc/1/summ.en:
In Act 2, K339 Su Hyoeun conducts a public retest and confesses that he deliberately mislabeled the germination prospects of two seed batches as “retest.”

He apologizes to the growers of the lost food-crop seeds and performs cross-germination tests on every batch while avoiding the times when G24E13 is moving.

He compares traditional names, humidity, weight, and mold readings with the actual condition of the sprouts in one place.

/story_contents/B028/actors/3/arc/2/summ.en:
In Act 3, K339 Su Hyoeun puts to a final vote whether living seed samples should be recognized as joint witnesses or only human representatives should be allowed to argue on their behalf.

He does not use his authority as chief operator to overturn the result, and he has Cheon Daum and Ryu Eunbi state their different survival criteria publicly.

He personally implements the cooling order that is decided and reports the subsequent germination results for every discarded or preserved batch to the community.

If a compromise is proposed, seeds with conflicting assessments are isolated for one growing cycle, and Su Hyoeun takes responsibility for their share of cooling and for cultivation labor during that period.

/story_contents/B028/actors/3/outcomes/0.en:
When the joint-witness proposal passes, K339 Su Hyoeun has a grower and a treatment-team member serve together as representatives for each germinated sample.

He retests the survival prospects of rare medicinal herbs and food crops under the same procedure and prohibits arbitrary changes in grading.

He remains chief operator, aligning G24E13’s access times and the cooling cycle with the seed council’s decisions.

/story_contents/B028/actors/3/outcomes/1.en:
When the human-representative deliberation proposal passes, K339 Su Hyoeun does not recognize voting rights for seeds themselves, but requires competing reports from growers, herb merchants, and treatment teams.

Of the two batches preserved because of his false entry, he transfers the one that actually sprouted to a communal growing site and officially records the loss of the one that died.

Under Ryu Eunbi’s audit, he rechecks the germination standards with Cheon Daum each season.

/story_contents/B028/actors/3/outcomes/2.en:
When the compromise is adopted, K339 Su Hyoeun keeps seeds with conflicting assessments in isolated storage for one growing cycle. During that period, they are excluded from consideration for consumption in the survival vote.

He places the camphorwood tray at the public testing station so any disagreement between its scent and the readings triggers an immediate retest.

He does not claim priority for resources allocated to repair the damage to the food-crop seeds; he repays it through his own cultivation labor.

/story_contents/B028/actors/4/sections/정.en:
K365 Pan Chodam is a Korean pump-equipment technician who grew up in an old residential neighborhood east of the Han River. He understands the city through its connected underground pipes and machine rooms rather than its roads.

He does not readily submit to authority, but clearly obeys on-site command when residents’ lives are directly at stake.

In the Gate Military Government, he establishes himself as a chief operator who refuses hidden power privileges and explains every load in plain sight.

/story_contents/B028/actors/4/sections/붕.en:
Before the Collapse, K365 Pan Chodam inspected fire pumps and wastewater-discharge equipment at a large shopping complex and conducted load tests on its emergency generators.

He repaired a black cast-iron governor handle that was due to be discarded, put it in his toolbox, and trained himself to read a machine’s vibrations with his palm.

At night, he shared meals with drivers at a bus depot and heard about errors in its automated dispatch system, though at the time he regarded them as merely an inconvenience of automation.

/story_contents/B028/actors/4/sections/가.en:
K365 Pan Chodam is responsible for the output of the emergency generator and drainage pumps in the Gate Military Government district’s pump room.

He obeys Go Seojun’s wartime command but refuses unrecorded power distribution, and supplies Seon Solwoo’s pumps with output matched to the actual water level and motor temperature.

Residents consider him stubborn, but because he makes people write the reason for use beside every switch in the pump room, no one can monopolize a secret circuit.

/story_contents/B028/actors/4/sections/붕.en:
K365 Pan Chodam faces an incident in which the Ghost Dispatch Board G14E06 keeps executing automated dispatch schedules, sending empty buses and tow equipment into the pump-room access route.

He slows the vehicles with horn noise and chilled wheel clamps and erects a route barrier, but a work vehicle carrying a rescue team is also caught by an automated tow line.

Afterward, rather than simply destroying the dispatch board, he combines passage-time trades brokered through HC14 with physical separation.

/story_contents/B028/actors/4/sections/생.en:
At the depot power meter, K365 Pan Chodam confirms that the Ghost Dispatch Board is not looking for passengers; it is trying to fulfill old service slots and charging loads.

Through an HC14 intermediary, he makes a contract to provide a set load to an empty tow truck in exchange for keeping the access route clear during pump-shift changes.

To stabilize the contract, he welds the generator governor to a single speed, permanently giving up operation under varied loads. He saves the community at the cost of binding the pump room to a fixed timetable.

/story_contents/B028/actors/4/sections/현.en:
K365 Pan Chodam is the chief emergency-generator operator in the Gate Military Government district’s pump room, coordinating both output for Seon Solwoo’s pumps and passage times for outside vehicles.

He carries out Go Seojun’s wartime orders, but if he discovers a concealed load, he immediately posts it on the full control board and demands renewed approval.

The welded governor has narrowed the equipment’s operating range, but he is also the only person who can keep the contract with the Ghost Dispatch Board working in practice.

/story_contents/B028/actors/4/sections/비.en:
During the last routine inspection before the Collapse, K365 Pan Chodam found a fault in the automated tow line’s emergency stop but postponed the repair until the following month to avoid disrupting the shopping complex’s business.

After the Collapse, the same fault trapped a rescue work vehicle, but he reported only the Ghost Dispatch Board’s abnormal operation as the cause of the accident.

The date of that inspection is engraved inside the black cast-iron handle; if Go Seojun begins a wartime audit, the concealment is bound to come to light.

/story_contents/B028/actors/4/sections/관.en:
During the first defense of the gate, K365 Pan Chodam clashed with Go Seojun over whether to give pump-room power to searchlight equipment. After the water level crossed the danger line, Go Seojun accepted his judgment, and they built a measure of trust.

With Seon Solwoo, he made a pump-operation agreement after they turned a motor by hand to free it in a flooded underground passage.

The three are comrades who defended the gate district, but if Pan Chodam’s past postponement of the repair is revealed, his principle of public operation risks looking hypocritical.

/story_contents/B028/actors/4/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, as the Ghost Dispatch Board’s operating cycle shortens and demand for pumping grows, K365 Pan Chodam cannot simultaneously meet Go Seojun’s defense load and Seon Solwoo’s drainage load.

In Act 2, he reveals that he once concealed the emergency-stop fault and welds the governor to a single speed to make a new passage agreement with HC14.

In Act 3, he chooses whether to turn the pump room into a timetable-based joint control center or terminate the contract, take the manual controls, help evacuate the gate district, and then scrap the equipment.

/story_contents/B028/actors/4/sections/분.en:
In the branch where K365 Pan Chodam chooses the joint control center, he establishes a system in which Go Seojun, Seon Solwoo, and resident representatives approve generator time together, and he is forbidden to operate it alone without supervision.

In the evacuation branch, he cuts the welded governor and runs the generator under overload one last time. After making the pump room unusable, he becomes a traveling instructor in the use of manual pumps.

In either ending, he tells the family of the person lost in the rescue work-vehicle accident that he postponed the repair and accepts work as restitution.

/story_contents/B028/actors/4/arc/0/summ.en:
In Act 1, just as Seon Solwoo’s pumps demand maximum output, K365 Pan Chodam faces empty tow trucks from the Ghost Dispatch Board G14E06 entering the access route.

He delays part of Go Seojun’s defense load and blocks the vehicles’ route with horn noise and chilled clamps.

During an inspection, Seon Solwoo discovers the date of his past repair postponement engraved on the black cast-iron handle.

/story_contents/B028/actors/4/arc/1/summ.en:
In Act 2, K365 Pan Chodam admits at a gate-district meeting that he concealed the automated tow-line fault and relinquishes his authority to operate alone.

With HC14 acting as intermediary, he trades charging load for empty vehicles for passage during pump-shift changes and welds the generator governor to one speed.

Even though Go Seojun objects that this sacrifices flexibility in battle, the generator, once fixed, cannot be returned to its former state.

/story_contents/B028/actors/4/arc/2/summ.en:
In Act 3, K365 Pan Chodam chooses between a joint timetable that keeps the gate district operating and one last overload run to evacuate its residents.

If he keeps it operating, he opens the control board to resident representatives; if he evacuates, he cuts the governor and uses up the generator’s remaining life in a single run.

Finally, he corrects the record of the rescue work-vehicle accident and performs the restitution work set by the bereaved family.

/story_contents/B028/actors/4/outcomes/0.en:
K365 Pan Chodam chooses the joint control center and establishes a fixed operating schedule under which the Ghost Dispatch Board and the pump room do not intrude on each other.

He retains the title of site chief, but cannot operate the generator without the consent of Go Seojun, Seon Solwoo, and resident representatives.

His principle of public operation becomes an audit system that includes his own past concealment, and it becomes a lasting rule of the gate district.

/story_contents/B028/actors/4/outcomes/1.en:
K365 Pan Chodam chooses evacuation, running the generator under overload to secure one last drainage route and get residents and the defense team out beyond the gate.

The pump room cannot be restarted, and he takes only the black cast-iron handle with him, becoming a traveling instructor who teaches people to use manual pumps.

Go Seojun and Seon Solwoo acknowledge his sacrifice, but do not treat his heroic action as canceling his responsibility for the postponed repair.

/story_contents/B028/actors/5/sections/정.en:
Heung Yena is a Korean resident whose identity has taken shape between the market rules and everyday rationing of the Main Hall Ratification Government.

Rather than defining himself by his family background, he describes himself as someone who makes practical decisions about which goods should go to whom.

He believes unsold goods carry both the circumstances of their former owners and the survival needs of their next users, and values clear-eyed calculation alongside careful observation.

/story_contents/B028/actors/5/sections/붕.en:
Before the Collapse, Heung Yena worked as the keeper of unsold-lot records at the Garak refrigerated auction house, always keeping a brass unsold-lot bell and a black abacus close at hand.

He learned procedures for reassessing unsold inhalers, ingredients, and tools instead of discarding them, and quietly tracked merchants’ price-fixing as well.

After work, he taught safe ways to use leftover ingredients at a communal kitchen in Jamsil, building trust beyond the market.

/story_contents/B028/actors/5/sections/가.en:
Heung Yena holds an intermediary responsibility linking the HC09-affiliated rationing network and the Main Hall Ratification Government’s citizens’ auction association.

He has an agreement with Geun Soli to compare items in the Garak and Sinnae unsold-lot ledgers, and rings the brass bell at Nam Yungyeong’s public auctions to mark the close of trading.

His community treats people who have reviewed the books together more like close family than blood relatives, but for that very reason treats errors in the records as seriously as personal betrayals.

/story_contents/B028/actors/5/sections/붕.en:
On the day Heung Yena encounters the Flooded Mold Respiratory Swarm G10E15 in the underground refrigerated wing, he cannot save a colleague left beside a box of contaminated inhalers.

He turns down the cooling unit to slow the spread of spores and seals the passage, but rescue time runs out while he uses the noise of the brass unsold-lot bell to draw the swarm toward another warehouse.

Ever since, the smell of wet concrete makes his count his breaths, and he cannot forget that the route closure he chose for survival was a death sentence for someone else.

/story_contents/B028/actors/5/sections/생.en:
Heung Yena’s turning point came when he realized that the ringing of the unsold-lot bell could agitate the Flooded Mold Respiratory Swarm but also guide it into a designated cooling zone.

Through an HC10 intermediary, he arranges a resource-and-time trade: empty culture vessels as a diversionary food source, and a halt to human passage while the respiratory swarm rests.

The auction house survives because he chooses not to seek its total destruction, but he also accepts criticism for treating the mold colony as a trading partner.

/story_contents/B028/actors/5/sections/현.en:
Heung Yena now works in the Main Hall Ratification Government as an unsold-lot case investigator and a limited-auction conductor.

He cross-checks Nam Yungyeong’s public auctions against Geun Soli’s Sinnae records, and before ringing the brass bell, he always makes sure all three of them inspect the item number and its actual condition together.

His official rank is not high, but because he can decide which goods to reassign and which passages to close, merchants and patients alike regard his judgment warily.

/story_contents/B028/actors/5/sections/비.en:
Heung Yena keeps secret that on the first day of the Collapse, he deliberately delayed offering a batch of inhalers he recognized as potentially contaminated so that it would go unsold.

He sent two safe ones from the batch not to his family but to a residence for asthma patients; he also knows that the remaining box stayed underground and blocked his colleague’s rescue route.

He owes Geun Soli for taking over the item comparisons at the time, and fears that revealing the truth would expose his good deed and his mistake at once.

/story_contents/B028/actors/5/sections/관.en:
Heung Yena and Geun Soli build trust while tracing repeated failures to sell items from the same manufacturing batch at different auction houses.

Nam Yungyeong has trusted Heung Yena’s rule that once he rings the bell, a transaction cannot be undone, but learning that he delayed offering an item on the day of the Collapse could shake that trust.

The three held the last normal auction together on the second-floor balcony of the Garak refrigerated auction house, and the brass bell left from that day remains both evidence of their relationship and the center of their conflict.

/story_contents/B028/actors/5/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, while comparing Geun Soli’s Sinnae ledger with Nam Yungyeong’s public auction list, Heung Yena discovers that contaminated inhalers have reappeared under a different number.

In Act 2, he comes under pressure to confess that he delayed offering them in the past and to close the entire underground storage area for an extended period if he is to maintain the passage agreement with the Flooded Mold Respiratory Swarm G10E15.

In Act 3, he makes an irreversible choice: break the brass bell himself, ending his existing auction authority and opening a public reassessment, or preserve the bell while secretly moving the hazardous goods outside.

/story_contents/B028/actors/5/sections/분.en:
If Heung Yena chooses confession and closure, he loses his position but establishes an unsold-goods reassessment center with Geun Soli and Nam Yungyeong, with patient representatives taking part.

If instead he moves the hazardous goods outside, the rationing bureau becomes stable for the time being, but small settlements along the transport route are harmed, and he lives as an exiled auctioneer carrying the brass bell.

In a third possibility, he makes a long-term passage agreement with HC10 and turns the underground area into a shared buffer zone, but must spend his life mediating the distrust of both humans and the respiratory swarm.

/story_contents/B028/actors/5/arc/0/summ.en:
K390 Heung Yena compares the brass unsold-lot bell from the Garak refrigerated auction house with Geun Soli’s Sinnae ledger to trace the route taken by a returning batch of inhalers.

He tells Nam Yungyeong that he delayed offering the batch on the day of the Collapse and brings the public auction to a halt.

His confession provokes immediate anger from patients, but also establishes legitimate authority to investigate the hidden underground storage area.

/story_contents/B028/actors/5/arc/1/summ.en:
Underground, K390 Heung Yena does not drive the Flooded Mold Respiratory Swarm G10E15 back with noise.

He negotiates an exchange involving cooling compartments, empty culture vessels, and passage times.

With HC10 as intermediary, he seals off the respiratory swarm’s dormant zone in exchange for cutting human transport time in half.

Geun Soli and Nam Yungyeong check the ledger and the physical goods respectively, monitoring the agreement so it does not become a one-sided sacrifice.

/story_contents/B028/actors/5/arc/2/summ.en:
K390 Heung Yena decides whether to break the brass unsold-lot bell and relinquish his exclusive authority to end the auction, or keep the bell and control the movement of dangerous goods alone.

Whichever he chooses, he cannot return to the old system, and he reveals the entire decision-making process to Geun Soli and Nam Yungyeong.

The final toll becomes not the end of an auction but a new promise about who will share the danger.

In a third option, he chooses the HC10 long-term passage agreement, taking lifelong responsibility for operating a buffer zone jointly with the humans and the Breathing Group instead of retaining sole authority over the brass bell.

/story_contents/B028/actors/5/outcomes/0.en:
K390 Heung Yena breaks the brass bell. He discloses the investigation’s findings and loses his position and personal property, but becomes the first recordkeeper at an unsold-goods reassessment center run jointly by citizens, patients, and merchants.

Geun Soli takes charge of comparing the scent traces, and Nam Yungyeong conducts the public objection process.

Time-based exchanges with the Flood-Mold Breathing Group also become routine, and the underground auction house remains a restricted shared zone rather than hostile territory.

/story_contents/B028/actors/5/outcomes/1.en:
K390 Heung Yena preserves the brass bell and moves the dangerous crates outside, preventing short-term turmoil in the Main Hall Ratification Court.

But when the harm along the transport route comes to light, Nam Yungyeong terminates the contract, and Geun Soli releases a copy of the original ledger and expels him.

Afterward, he travels among the affected settlements, assessing the condition of goods free of charge, but every time he rings the bell, he reads aloud the names of the dangers he passed on to others.

/story_contents/B028/actors/5/outcomes/2.en: K390 Heung Yena makes a long-term passage agreement with HC10, turns the underground area into a buffer zone shared by humans and the Breathing Group, and spends the rest of his life mediating their mutual distrust.

/story_contents/B028/actors/6/sections/정.en:
Geun Juha is a secretary of Korean descent who believes the small settlements of the Jeongdong General Labor Union must have an equal voice.

He sets the order of negotiations by each party’s capacity to honor its promises and the scale of harm it has suffered, not by national power or population.

He sees himself not as a heroic diplomat but as a records worker who calculates the cost of every sentence to the end, valuing precise times and clause numbers over grand speeches.

/story_contents/B028/actors/6/sections/붕.en:
Before the Collapse, Geun Juha worked as a meeting recorder for an international cooperation agency, using a folding clause board and a desk clock with a large second hand.

Unswayed by a representative’s accent or reputation, he recorded in detail who agreed to what, when they agreed, and which obligations they reserved.

On his days off, he explained complex contracts in plain language at a legal advice center for migrants, an experience that taught him to notice when less powerful communities fell silent.

/story_contents/B028/actors/6/sections/가.en:
Geun Juha belongs to the HP09 negotiation office and an alliance of small Jeongdong General Labor Union outposts, where he manages signatures for joint bargaining.

He has a contract with Cho Naru to reconcile the clauses in the Suseo master ledger, and he and Cho Taeon have sworn not to conceal the times of signatures.

Chang Goun is his counterpart in checking ledger numbers; these three relationships are both safeguards against Geun Juha finalizing clauses alone and a long-standing network of trust.

/story_contents/B028/actors/6/sections/붕.en:
On the day the Personalized Medical Remnant G11E07 occupied Suseo Roundtable Room 4, Geun Juha watched the negotiating delegation become trapped by a device that repeatedly issued treatment orders for a particular patient.

He slowed the device with a cooling cover and blocked routes, but delayed granting one small outpost representative’s request to leave in order to keep the meeting going.

After the remnant’s medication arm injured the representative, he carried the wound of having left the most vulnerable person in danger to preserve the majority’s agreement.

/story_contents/B028/actors/6/sections/생.en:
Geun Juha changed his approach to survival when he realized the remnant responded to consumable allocations and access times rather than the names of treatment recipients.

Through HC11 mediation, he provided cooling cartridges and vacant treatment slots, and proposed an agreement that strictly divided the human side’s passage times through the roundtable room.

The decision to treat the device’s limited treatment function as a shared resource rather than fight it saves the city, but sparks debate over whether the device can be regarded as a negotiating party equal to citizens.

/story_contents/B028/actors/6/sections/현.en:
Geun Juha is now the Jeongdong General Labor Union’s joint-bargaining signature secretary for its smaller member states, recording each clause’s number, time of consent, reservations, and costs together.

Cho Naru checks that the wording matches, Cho Taeon keeps the clock, and Chang Goun connects ledger numbers to actual allocations from the ration warehouse.

He has no vote, but no agreement takes effect without a record, giving him an influence quieter yet stronger than that of the representatives.

/story_contents/B028/actors/6/sections/비.en:
Geun Juha has a secret: just before the Collapse, he moved a small outpost’s statement of reservation from the main text to an appendix memo to speed up the agreement.

He did not delete the words, but placed them where they were hard to find; as a result, that outpost lost priority for treatment cartridges.

He owes Cho Taeon for remembering the actual signing time, and bears the guilt of knowing that telling Cho Naru and Chang Goun the truth could invalidate the city’s entire first agreement.

/story_contents/B028/actors/6/sections/관.en:
Geun Juha and Cho Naru have worked together for so long, matching clauses through the night at Suseo Roundtable 4, that each can recognize the other’s habits of omission.

Cho Taeon protected a mechanical clock even during a blackout, corroborating Geun Juha’s records, while Chang Goun constantly reminded him that a difference of one number could change the allocation of dozens of actual ration boxes.

The four are colleagues who brought the first joint agreement into force, but if the truth about the appendix memo emerges, that achievement itself will become a shared wrongdoing.

/story_contents/B028/actors/6/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, Geun Juha discovers that the consumables allocation table for the Personalized Medical Remnant G11E07 and the appendix memo to the first agreement repeatedly excluded the same small outpost.

In Act 2, he confesses his editorial decision to Cho Naru, Cho Taeon, and Chang Goun, and they debate whether to review the agreement in full or preserve the current order of passage and treatment.

In Act 3, he makes an irreversible choice: publicly enter the omitted reservation on the folding clause board at the center of the roundtable, suspending the city’s legal foundation himself, or take personal responsibility while leaving the existing agreement in force.

/story_contents/B028/actors/6/sections/분.en:
If Geun Juha chooses to suspend the agreement, the city falls into brief turmoil, but a rotating roundtable system is created in which each outpost can renegotiate its burdens and treatment times.

If he takes personal responsibility alone, he is expelled from his secretary’s post and the first agreement remains in force, but he spends his life traveling among the affected outposts to testify and disclose the costs he hid.

In the ending where the joint treatment agreement with the remnant is expanded, human representatives and device supervisors review the allocation table together, and Geun Juha becomes a permanent, nonvoting auditor.

/story_contents/B028/actors/6/arc/0/summ.en:
K415 Geun Juha brings together Cho Naru’s clause ledger, Cho Taeon’s mechanical time records, and Chang Goun’s allocation numbers.

After calculating the harm caused by the appendix memo to the first agreement, he confesses to the three of them first that he moved the statement of reservation.

The confession halts joint bargaining, but for the first time, a representative of a small outpost gains the power to set the roundtable’s agenda order directly.

/story_contents/B028/actors/6/arc/1/summ.en:
K415 Geun Juha does not destroy the Personalized Medical Remnant G11E07.

He opens renegotiations involving cooling cartridges, treatment-room access times, and sealed zones.

With HC11 mediating, he turns the remnant’s repeated orders into limited treatment duties and separates people’s travel routes.

Cho Naru and Chang Goun verify that the promised resources are actually allocated, and Cho Taeon makes every shift-change time public.

/story_contents/B028/actors/6/arc/2/summ.en:
K415 Geun Juha decides whether to enter the omitted reservation on the folding clause board and suspend the first agreement, or surrender his position and citizenship.

He must decide whether to preserve the existing order.

Before the representatives of every outpost, he reads aloud the outcomes and costs so that neither choice can be undone by merely revising a sentence.

The final signature becomes not a declaration of victory but a test of whether a vulnerable community truly has the right to reject an agreement.

In a third option, he expands the joint treatment-allocation agreement between human representatives and remnant supervisors and remains a permanent auditor without a vote.

/story_contents/B028/actors/6/outcomes/0.en:
K415 Geun Juha suspends the first agreement and designs a rotating roundtable system with Cho Naru, Cho Taeon, and Chang Goun.

The city suffers ration delays for several weeks, but small outposts take turns deciding the agenda order and treatment times.

He does not remain secretary, instead becoming a public interpreter of the clauses who explains even the agreement with the Personalized Medical Remnant to citizens at every shift change.

/story_contents/B028/actors/6/outcomes/1.en:
K415 Geun Juha chooses to keep the agreement in force, but gives up every post and his right of residence to become a witness who travels among the affected outposts.

Cho Naru takes custody of the ledger, Cho Taeon withdraws his oath, and Chang Goun runs a special office to remedy the harm caused by the allocations.

Even in villages where he is unwelcome, he repeatedly tells the full story of the appendix memo, accepting his exile as the price of preserving order.

/story_contents/B028/actors/6/outcomes/2.en: K415 Geun Juha expands the agreement under which human representatives and remnant supervisors review the treatment allocation table together, and becomes a permanent nonvoting auditor.

/story_contents/B028/actors/7/sections/정.en:
Ha Seon is a citizen born to a maternal grandmother who worked loading cargo at the port of Davao in the Philippines and a Korean father who maintained railways; at eleven, she moved through Busan to northeastern Seoul.

At home, her family spoke both Cebuano and Korean, and she learned to explain routes through colors, knots, and gestures to relatives who could not read freight labels.

She does not portray her experience of migration as an innate gift for transport. Instead, she connects it to an escort ethic under which workers who speak different languages must have the same right to withdraw.

/story_contents/B028/actors/7/sections/붕.en:
Before the Collapse, Ha Seon carried performance equipment and medical parcels on a cargo bicycle, recording in a separate notebook the differences between the knot tags her grandmother used at the Davao port and Seoul’s road signs.

She modified the aluminum towing sled Baengno-4 herself to distribute loads among several people, and marked Cebuano calls and Korean stop commands together with colored bands.

Her family’s port work and her father’s railway maintenance livelihood shaped an operating principle that valued leaving people with the strength to walk again after arrival, and the right to refuse withdrawal orders, over fast delivery.

/story_contents/B028/actors/7/sections/가.en:
Ha Seon leads a light escort unit under HP02 and the walking porter team of the Neutral Convoy City.

He carries out Jang Sehwa’s escort orders but raises objections when conditions on the ground become too dangerous, and gives Gam Guk clear instructions on scouting the outer route and the limits for returning.

He has an agreement with Seok Bomwoo to separate pedestrian and freight lines, securing space for children and older people to move first so the procession does not become one in which only the fast survive.

/story_contents/B028/actors/7/sections/붕.en:
On the night a battery warehouse exploded and the Electrolyte Burn Group G07E07 formed, Ha Seon kept dragging a heavy power box attached to Baengno-4, leaving several unit members exposed to the burn zone for too long.

She contained the leak with cooling cloth and absorbent material and blocked the route, but accepted Gam Guk’s report that they should abandon the equipment too late and missed the time to retreat.

Ever since, whenever she must distinguish what to save from what to discard, she recalls the wounds her attachment left on people’s skin and lungs.

/story_contents/B028/actors/7/sections/생.en:
Ha Seon diverted the pursuit by using her discovery that the Electrolyte Burn Group followed the heat and smell of discarded material soaked with leakage rather than charged equipment.

With HC07 mediating, she offered bundles of absorbent material and cooling time in a limited exchange under which the human escort unit would use only the designated outer route.

Choosing to divert the group’s food source and separate travel times instead of wiping it out changed her from a cargo-focused commander into a leader who put people’s capacity to recover first.

/story_contents/B028/actors/7/sections/현.en:
Ha Seon is now the light escort captain of the Neutral Convoy City, managing Baengno-4 and twelve folding handcarts.

He receives assignments from Jang Sehwa but is guaranteed the authority to abandon cargo in the field, and combines Gam Guk’s outer-route scouting and Seok Bomwoo’s crowd separation into a single operating schedule.

Citizens trust him not because he is a fast commander, but because he factors the slowest pedestrian’s pace into the overall arrival time.

/story_contents/B028/actors/7/sections/비.en:
During the first burn incident, Ha Seon already knew that the power box at issue was not medical equipment but an HP02 command-records case, and did not tell his unit.

He thought protecting the case would allow the escort network to be rebuilt later, but his choice left two of Gam Guk’s colleagues with permanent nerve damage.

He owes Jang Sehwa for keeping silent about the truth, and has yet to confess to Seok Bomwoo that he put the organization’s records ahead of the people in the crowd.

/story_contents/B028/actors/7/sections/관.en:
Ha Seon and Jang Sehwa have designed nighttime parcel runs together since before the Collapse, often arguing over the boundary between orders and discretion in the field.

Gam Guk is the scout who rescued Ha Seon when he overturned during Baengno-4’s first test run, which made the disregard of his retreat report during the burn incident feel like a deeper betrayal.

Seok Bomwoo remembers how the three of them prevented a crowd crush at Mangu Transfer Plaza and still tests whether Ha Seon puts the pedestrian line first.

/story_contents/B028/actors/7/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, when the movement of the Electrolyte Burn Group G07E07 closes the outer route, Ha Seon plans to dismantle Baengno-4 and continue the escort on foot.

In Act 2, Gam Guk reveals the true nature of the command-records case and Seok Bomwoo demands an apology for the injured members’ families, forcing Ha Seon to relinquish either Jang Sehwa’s chain of command or his unit’s trust first.

In Act 3, he makes an irreversible choice: cut up Baengno-4’s towing frame to turn it into evacuation railings, or preserve the frame to carry the last load through the dangerous stretch.

/story_contents/B028/actors/7/sections/분.en:
If Ha Seon dismantles Baengno-4, the organization’s long-distance transport capacity declines, but a school for escorts on foot is established with Gam Guk and Seok Bomwoo taking part.

If she preserves the frame for the final delivery, the Transfer City gets the parts it needs but loses one unit member; she relinquishes command and becomes a lone guide on the outer route.

In the ending where she expands long-term trade with HC07, a cooling corridor is established around the Burn Group’s movement times, but she must obey the decisions of an oversight council that includes the accident’s victims for the rest of her life.

/story_contents/B028/actors/7/arc/0/summ.en:
K300 Ha Seon receives Jang Sehwa’s long-distance order, but halves Baengno-4’s cargo to account for Gam Guk’s scouting report and the pace of the crowd managed by Seok Bomwoo.

He confesses to the unit what the command-records case really was and that he concealed it during the earlier burn incident.

The escort unit splits, but the injured members’ families gain the authority to set the conditions for stopping and resuming operations themselves.

/story_contents/B028/actors/7/arc/1/summ.en:
K300 Ha Seon does not charge at the Electrolyte Burn Group G07E07.

He clears the outer route by combining cooling cloth, bundles of absorbent material, and a storage period for spent batteries.

With HC07 mediating, he seals off the area where the Burn Group stays and divides the human escort unit’s passage into brief time slots.

Gam Guk confirms the detour, Seok Bomwoo spreads out the pedestrian line, and Jang Sehwa formally recognizes discretion in the field.

/story_contents/B028/actors/7/arc/2/summ.en:
K300 Ha Seon chooses whether to cut up Baengno-4’s aluminum towing frame to make evacuation railings or preserve the vehicle for one last delivery of parts.

She knows that cutting the frame will end her career as a long-distance commander, while preserving it will make her responsible once again for putting cargo before people.

Just before choosing, she gives Gam Guk and Seok Bomwoo the right to refuse her orders, making her decision an irreversible joint judgment.

In a third option, she chooses long-term trade with HC07 and a cooling corridor, permanently placing control of Baengno-4 under the decisions of the victims’ oversight council.

/story_contents/B028/actors/7/outcomes/0.en:
K300 Ha Seon dismantles Baengno-4 and installs evacuation railings and rest platforms on the steep slopes outside Mangu.

Jang Sehwa does not dismiss him as captain, instead transferring him to lead a school for escorts on foot, with Gam Guk and Seok Bomwoo as joint instructors.

He carries less cargo, but leaves behind a new escort culture in which accident victims and slow pedestrians design the routes themselves.

/story_contents/B028/actors/7/outcomes/1.en:
K300 Ha Seon preserves Baengno-4 and successfully delivers the last load of parts, but loses one unit member during the retreat.

Gam Guk ends their command relationship, Seok Bomwoo terminates their contract, and Jang Sehwa also holds him formally responsible.

He remains a lone guide on the outer route, taking people across without charging a toll, but never again orders anyone to protect cargo to the end.

/story_contents/B028/actors/7/outcomes/2.en: K300 Through long-term trade with HC07, Ha Seon establishes a cooling corridor that uses the Burn Group’s movement times and obeys the victims’ oversight council’s decisions for the rest of her life.

/story_contents/B028/actors/8/sections/정.en:
Nam Hoseong is a citizen of the Medical Neutrality League, born to a mother who worked at a rehabilitation-device repair shop in Da Nang, Vietnam, and a Korean father who interpreted sign language. He moved to Incheon at six and to Cheongnyangni as an adult.

His family spoke Vietnamese and Korean at home, and because of his maternal grandfather’s hearing loss, he also learned the different spatial grammars of Korean Sign Language and Vietnamese Sign Language.

He believes that knowing several languages does not entitle him to monopolize the final interpretation; patients’ own languages and gestures must carry the authority to stop a medical escort.

/story_contents/B028/actors/8/sections/붕.en:
Before the Collapse, Nam Hoseong drove specimens and rehabilitation equipment between hospitals, carrying medicines and brace components in separate compartments of a red rotating case brought from the Da Nang repair shop.

At night, he ran a small audio and sign-language video studio with his parents, converting loudspeaker orders into captions and sign language and teaching that colored tokens should indicate cargo types only.

This work shaped his present escort ethic: when machine sounds conflict with human language, which signal has the authority to make a person move?

/story_contents/B028/actors/8/sections/가.en:
Nam Hoseong commands the HP03 medical escort unit and the Medical Neutrality League’s mobile clinics.

He has an agreement with Jang Sehwa to share medical escorts with the Transfer City, while Pan Handeul handles escort stops and patient handovers at the platform.

Cheon Daol works under him on dispatch duty, but the two check the final opening of the medicine case together; their community values accountability during handovers over its captain’s speed.

/story_contents/B028/actors/8/sections/붕.en:
K326 On the night the Night Sorting Group G13E16 bound patients’ braces and medicine boxes to the sorting line in the northern logistics building, Nam Hoseong witnessed a sign-language stop signal, a loudspeaker command to advance, and a red cargo token come into conflict.

He moved the vehicle, giving the colored cargo token priority over the spoken command, and a colleague of K335 Pan Handeul could not get out of the way in time and was seriously injured.

Since then, he has warned that the same accident will recur if they increase speed without first deciding which language of command has the authority to move a person’s body.

/story_contents/B028/actors/8/sections/생.en:
K326 Nam Hoseong draws on his ability to distinguish mechanical sounds, learned while transporting specimens and rehabilitation equipment between hospitals before the collapse, to discover that G13E16 responds consistently to a fixed arrangement of color tokens and regular stopping intervals.

He establishes a procedure in which the signer giving sign-language signals, the vehicle commander giving spoken orders, and the platform attendant arranging color tokens cross-check the destination before departure.

He establishes a medical escort rule under which a patient's refusal of treatment or report of pain takes precedence over cargo colors, regardless of the language used.

/story_contents/B028/actors/8/sections/현.en:
Nam Hoseong is now the Medical Neutrality League's medical escort commander, responsible for operating three mobile clinics and the red medicine rotation box.

He coordinates escort volumes between regions with Jang Sehwa and stops only after receiving Pan Handeul's platform reports; he also guarantees Cheon Daol the authority to refuse dangerous dispatch orders.

Patients trust him, but the families of logistics workers demand a public explanation of past refrigerated-space allocations and platform delays.

/story_contents/B028/actors/8/sections/비.en:
In the first winter after the collapse, K326 Nam Hoseong deliberately mistranslates a signed order from K335 Pan Handeul, sending a medical escort along the eastern detour instead of to the northern platform.

He believes he made the decision to avoid a G13E16 runaway incident, but the diverted vehicles arrive late, delaying the patient handover, and the northern standby team does not receive the medical staff it needs.

He tells K336 Cheon Daol that a color token was misplaced and conceals the fact that he personally changed the destination he relayed.

/story_contents/B028/actors/8/sections/관.en:
K326 Nam Hoseong drew up an interregional cross-escort schedule with K296 Jang Sehwa, but he disagrees with her view that spoken instructions constitute the final order.

K326 Nam Hoseong respects K335 Pan Handeul's signed platform reports, but his debt for deliberately mistranslating one of those signals in the past means he cannot monopolize the authority to interpret them.

K326 Nam Hoseong guarantees K336 Cheon Daol the authority to refuse dangerous dispatch orders and has Da-ol verify the color tokens alongside the interpretation records.

/story_contents/B028/actors/8/sections/3.en:
K326 Nam Hoseong is a Medical Neutrality League citizen from a Southeast Asian and Korean family background and the HP03 medical escort commander, in charge of three mobile clinics.

He brings before a public hearing the question of which should be the final authority for medical escorts: Jang Sehwa's spoken orders, Pan Handeul's signing, or the colored cargo tokens checked by Cheon Daol.

He confesses that he deliberately mistranslated a signed order to divert an escort and submits to a decision on whether interpreters should be defined not as assistants but as command authorities accountable for their actions.

/story_contents/B028/actors/8/sections/분.en:
In one ending, K326 Nam Hoseong establishes a three-way interpretation council in which the sign-language interpreter, vehicle commander, and platform token attendant have equal veto power.

In another ending, K326 Nam Hoseong makes signing by patients and on-site signalers the highest-priority order, reducing spoken orders and color tokens to means of confirmation.

In either ending, K326 Nam Hoseong remains responsible for operating the medical escort unit, but he does not evade discipline for his deliberate mistranslation or a review of the harm done to its victims.

In the competing-systems ending, each escort tells patients which command language it will use before departure and changes it only with everyone's consent, while Nam Hoseong publicly compares arrival times and harm under the different systems.

/story_contents/B028/actors/8/arc/0/summ.en:
In Act 1, K326 Nam Hoseong faces an incident in which G13E16 reads different color tokens as the same destination, funneling two medical escorts into one sorting passage.

When K296 Jang Sehwa's order to advance conflicts with K335 Pan Handeul's signed stop signal, he halts the vehicles.

He has K336 Cheon Daol collect every token and summons interpreters of all three command systems to meet together.

/story_contents/B028/actors/8/arc/1/summ.en:
In Act 2, K326 Nam Hoseong confesses that, during the first winter, he deliberately mistranslated Pan Handeul's signing to send an escort along the eastern detour.

He publicly lays out his reason for the detour, the delayed patient handover, and the harm to the northern standby team on the same map and timetable.

He temporarily suspends his sole authority to order departures while the interpreter's intent and responsibility are investigated.

/story_contents/B028/actors/8/arc/2/summ.en:
In Act 3, K326 Nam Hoseong conducts a final simulated escort to determine the priority of signing, spoken orders, and colored cargo tokens.

He requires vehicles to stop immediately at a patient's signal refusing treatment or an on-site danger signal, regardless of the language in which it is given.

He reorganizes the procedure for passing G13E16 according to the community's choice between the three-way council and the signing-first system.

If the proposal to retain competing systems is chosen, patients are told in advance which command language their escort will use, and any change requires everyone's consent.

/story_contents/B028/actors/8/outcomes/0.en:
When the three-way interpretation council is adopted, K326 Nam Hoseong gives representatives of K296 Jang Sehwa, K335 Pan Handeul, and K336 Cheon Daol the authority to halt errors in spoken orders, signing, and color tokens, respectively.
