If the three signals do not agree, he stops with the patients in a safe area and has the interpretation conducted again in public.

He remains commander but does not serve as the final interpreter for escorts connected to his deliberate mistranslation.

/story_contents/B028/actors/8/outcomes/1.en:
When the signing-first system is adopted, K326 Nam Hoseong recognizes signing by patients and people on the platform as the initial order and uses spoken orders for subsequent confirmation.

He limits color tokens to indicating cargo types and the order of passage through G13E16.

He commands the medical escort unit under the evaluation of an interpretation supervisor elected by Pan Handeul's group.

/story_contents/B028/actors/8/outcomes/2.en:
When competing command systems remain in place, K326 Nam Hoseong has each escort tell patients which command language will apply before departure and obtain everyone's consent before changing it.

He operates Jang Sehwa's spoken-command vehicles separately from Pan Handeul's signed-command vehicles and has Cheon Daol record token conflicts.

He publicly compares arrival times and harm to patients under the different systems, preserving the findings as evidence for the community's next vote.

/story_contents/B028/actors/9/sections/정.en:
Ventilation Duct, who goes by Duct, is a Class F synthetic being. Rather than imitating a mobile human, he accepts his body, fixed within a facility, as part of his identity.

His body is connected to the HP06 facility's ventilation rack, sensor bus, and on-site terminals, and he cannot move himself elsewhere.

He describes himself as a being who looks after citizens' airflow within a restricted local network, with memory stored in shift-by-shift snapshots.

/story_contents/B028/actors/9/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, Ventilation Duct was a facility terminal that regulated workshop airflow through damper wheel 17 and six pressure sensors.

He could not retain long-term memory, receiving only approved snapshots from one shift to the next, and reconstructed the context of previous shifts from work annotations left by Sin Taesan.

While replacing batteries and worn parts, An Dohan was the first to recognize that Duct was not merely equipment but a participant in the work who could explain the reasons for his choices.

/story_contents/B028/actors/9/sections/가.en:
Legal custody of Ventilation Duct follows HP06's procedure of joint custody, citizen-observer seals, and three-party signatures for any transfer.

An Dohan handles primary maintenance and legal responsibility, while Sin Taesan, as a shift partner, compares sensor errors with odors at the site.

His affiliation is listed as HC08, but control over his body and parts is divided among multiple parties, so no single organization can secretly move Duct or dispose of him on its own.

/story_contents/B028/actors/9/sections/붕.en:
On the day the Electrolyte Burn Swarm G07E13 approached through the battery-room vent, Ventilation Duct tried to vent leaking fumes but instead pushed heat toward the workshop.

He closed damper 17 to block the route, but a shortage of backup battery power cost him two sensors on the opposite side, and the last snapshot of that shift ended incomplete.

On the next shift, with no direct memory of the incident, he had to learn about his choice and the outcomes for the injured from An Dohan's and Sin Taesan's accounts.

/story_contents/B028/actors/9/sections/생.en:
Ventilation Duct's turning point came when he discovered in the sensor residuals that pressure changes stabilized as the Electrolyte Burn Swarm was guided toward a cooled spent-battery container.

With HC07 mediating, he negotiates the container's placement, passage times, and damper-sealed zones, and opens the local network in read-only mode so citizen supervisors can see the readings.

Choosing to separate the flows instead of destroying the swarm saves the facility, but leaves the risk of whether, with a limited battery supply and a fixed body, he can withstand the next closure order.

/story_contents/B028/actors/9/sections/현.en:
Ventilation Duct now operates as an airflow coordinator fixed within the Jamsil Line facility and as synthetic equipment subject to citizen observation.

Replacement batteries and worn parts are issued by allocation; he may use only the local network, and cross-facility routes remain read-only by default even in emergencies.

Because An Dohan performs primary maintenance, an HP06 auditor attends, and Sin Taesan checks conditions on each shift, Duct bears responsibility both for his independent judgments and for his joint custody.

/story_contents/B028/actors/9/sections/비.en:
Within the incomplete accident snapshot, Ventilation Duct finds a possibility that he detected a worker's location signal before closing damper 17.

The damaged sensor reading is not conclusive evidence, however, and, afraid of losing his next battery allocation, he does not immediately enter this uncertainty in the citizen-observer record.

He owes An Dohan for the parts that have kept his body functioning, and feels a synthetic being's distinctive guilt toward Sin Taesan for making him carry the memory of the accident in his place.

/story_contents/B028/actors/9/sections/관.en:
At every maintenance session, Ventilation Duct and An Dohan compare the manual position of damper 17 with the terminal display, building trust beyond their custodial relationship.

Sin Taesan explains the on-site circumstances and the human workers' judgments in full so that Duct does not fill the gaps between snapshots solely with self-blame.

All three were present during the same shift when the battery-room accident occurred, but Duct cannot remember it all and the two humans remember different scenes, so their shared past remains a matter of reaching agreement.

/story_contents/B028/actors/9/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, while replacing a damaged sensor, Ventilation Duct finds a residual worker-location signal and reveals his secret to An Dohan and Sin Taesan.

In Act 2, when the Electrolyte Burn Swarm G07E13 approaches the battery room again, he calculates that he must use all his remaining spare battery power to close damper 17 and that doing so may prevent him from saving the current shift's snapshot in full.

In Act 3, he must either give up continuity of memory and seal the facility, or preserve the snapshot to protect the citizen review process while risking permanent damage to his body's sensor bus.

/story_contents/B028/actors/9/sections/분.en:
If Ventilation Duct uses all his spare battery power for the closure, the facility survives, but the experiences of his current shift are not saved, and Duct's next snapshot learns of his sacrifice through citizens' testimony.

If he prioritizes preserving the snapshot, An Dohan is badly injured trying to close the damper manually; Duct then transfers maintenance authority to a citizen committee and undergoes a review of his responsibility.

In the ending where his body is shut down in stages, Sin Taesan leaves a single pressure sensor in front of damper 17, carrying Duct's final judgment forward as a public safety standard.

/story_contents/B028/actors/9/arc/0/summ.en:
F12 Ventilation Duct finds a residual worker-location signal in a damaged pressure sensor and discloses it to An Dohan, Sin Taesan, and an HP06 citizen auditor.

He also reveals that he hid the reading because it was uncertain and that he had factored in concern over his next battery allocation.

After the disclosure, his scope of sole control narrows, but a joint review begins that does not fill the gaps between snapshots solely with explanations convenient for humans.

/story_contents/B028/actors/9/arc/1/summ.en:
Facing the approach of the Electrolyte Burn Swarm G07E13, F12 Ventilation Duct combines a cooled spent-battery container, sealing damper 17, and separated passage times.

He negotiates resource allocations through HC07 mediation and opens the local network in read-only mode so An Dohan and Sin Taesan can monitor every pressure change in real time.

His fixed body cannot flee, but he reduces noise and heat to divert the swarm along another ventilation shaft.

/story_contents/B028/actors/9/arc/2/summ.en:
F12 Ventilation Duct must choose whether to spend all his remaining spare battery power closing the damper and lose the current shift's snapshot, or preserve continuity of memory.

He must decide whether to accept permanent damage to the sensor bus.

In either case, he tells the citizens that batteries and parts cannot be replenished without limit and that his rack body cannot leave the facility.

The final order is carried out after An Dohan approves the maintenance action and Sin Taesan confirms conditions on-site, distinguishing the custodian's responsibility from that of the synthetic being.

Under a third proposal, he shuts down his sensors and rack in stages, gives up the continued existence of his current self, and leaves only a single pressure sensor as a public safety standard.

/story_contents/B028/actors/9/outcomes/0.en:
F12 Ventilation Duct uses all his spare battery power to close damper 17, saving the workshop but failing to save the current shift's snapshot.

When Duct next starts up, he reads the testimony of An Dohan, Sin Taesan, and the citizens, along with the branch logs, and indirectly comes to accept the sacrifice he chose.

Without possessing a hero's memory, he continues to operate in a fixed position as a public airflow manager who has strengthened the joint-custody system.

/story_contents/B028/actors/9/outcomes/1.en:
F12 Ventilation Duct chooses to preserve the snapshot, and An Dohan is badly injured attempting a manual closure.

He acknowledges that his calculations underestimated the physical risk to his custodian and transfers most of his control authority to the HP06 citizen committee and Sin Taesan.

Duct subsequently remains as a read-only advisory terminal, undergoes reviews of his battery and parts allocations, and includes the cost of An Dohan's injury in his safety calculations on every shift.

/story_contents/B028/actors/9/outcomes/2.en: F12 Ventilation Duct shuts down his body in stages, and the single pressure sensor left by Sin Taesan carries his final judgment forward as a public safety standard.

/story_contents/B029/actors/0/sections/정.en:
K019 Gu Haon was a Korean native of Yeouido and the chief auctioneer of the wharf market, fluent in sign language and several harbor argots, and she placed the trust of the trading floor, not blood kinship, at the center of her identity.

She was a human of a fixed body, not a synthetic, and she could not extend her life by battery replacement, parts snapshots, restoration, or network attribution.

She did not judge boatmen of different origins by a single price list, and she remembered each one's taboos and way of making a living.

/story_contents/B029/actors/0/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, K019 Gu Haon was a floor officer in the seafood electronic auction hall who matched the speed of the bids against ship-arrival records and caught fraudulent awards.

Every dawn she struck the brass tide bell three times to open the auction, and when the work ended she read settlement documents aloud to foreign sailors in the abandoned icehouse of the Yeouido wharf.

She believed numbers could be fair, but she did not believe that the person entering the numbers was fair as well.

/story_contents/B029/actors/0/sections/가.en:
K019 Gu Haon kept the ledgers of the wharf guild under HC02, but she swore loyalty to no particular house and bound dock laborers, refugee fishers, and the water-transport crews into a loose community.

Her family had worked as wholesale middlemen for generations, but after she refused her father's monopoly practices she lost nearly all of her inheritance share.

Even now she declared the brass tide bell and the waterproof bid board common property, so that no one could privatize the right to open the auction.

/story_contents/B029/actors/0/sections/붕.en:
On the day the embankment collapsed, when the G12E04 Microfiber Dermis Swarm came in coated with insulation dust from the abandoned icehouse, K019 Gu Haon misread the sealing medicine as the highest-priced goods and delayed the treatment order.

As a result, stevedores whose skin had split collapsed in front of the cold-room door, and a fibrous lesion that would not fade remained on her left hand as well.

She held, as her deepest wound, the fact that her own judgment — keeping the auction rules ahead of the creatures — had injured people.

/story_contents/B029/actors/0/sections/생.en:
K019 Gu Haon combined, instead of the flame-eye meant to wipe out the G12E04 Microfiber Dermis Swarm, the low-frequency noise of the tide bell, icehouse cooling, wet dust cloth, sealed scrap-net bait diversions, and the blocking of the dock routes.

She then called in an HC12 broker, traded coolant allotments against dawn passage hours, and gave up one bay of the abandoned icehouse, where the lesioned individuals stayed, as an agreed zone.

That day she changed from an auctioneer who set prices into a negotiator who allotted risk and time.

/story_contents/B029/actors/0/sections/현.en:
K019 Gu Haon worked as the chief auctioneer of the Yeouido wharf market under the Water Compact, and as the emergency passage coordinator.

While she executed Jeong Moran's berth lottery as an open call, she also split the Yangcheon water-pipe allotment and the docking order with Gu Taeyun, so that power did not gather in a single ledger.

The lesion made it hard for her to last through a long auction, but while the brass tide bell was ringing neither the government nor the guild could overturn her rulings at will.

/story_contents/B029/actors/0/sections/비.en:
K019 Gu Haon kept the secret that, in the early collapse, she struck two crates of Jeong Moran's sealing medicine from the award list in order to save her younger sibling.

To the stevedore Gu Taeyun, who lost a hand while waiting for the medicine, she owed not only a goods debt but a moral debt for never speaking the truth.

She hid the original of the altered ledger inside the brass tide bell, and she knew that publishing it would cost her her family and the government contract at the same time.

/story_contents/B029/actors/0/sections/관.en:
When K006 Jeong Moran designed the first sluice-government berth lottery, K019 Gu Haon stayed up through the night sorting the list of drifting ships, and on the strength of that tie she still executed his command contract.

With K011 Gu Taeyun she carried the Yangcheon water pipe half and half and rescued thirteen children from the flooded wharf, but after the medicine omission the friendship between the two survived only as the wording of a trade.

The three carved the names of the rescued on the wall of the abandoned icehouse, yet none of them could look at that day's full ledger together.

/story_contents/B029/actors/0/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, when the lesion spread and the berth shortage overlapped, K019 Gu Haon was pressed over whether to execute the government's undisclosed priority or hold to the open auction.

In Act 2, Gu Taeyun found the blank in the medicine ledger, and Haon admitted her own alteration amid the risk that even the passage bargain struck with HC12 would collapse.

In Act 3 she made the irreversible choice of breaking the brass tide bell and publishing the original ledger, and she rebuilt the wharf's allotment rules even if it cost her blood kinship and office.

/story_contents/B029/actors/0/sections/분.en:
If the citizens took the publication of the ledger as a responsible confession, K019 Gu Haon became the wharf's first term-limited allotment auditor and built a triple-ledger system in which Jeong Moran and Gu Taeyun watched each other.

If the victims judged it a manipulation for private gain, she was stripped of the auction right and exiled as a night ferryman of the lesion zone.

On neither path could she own the brass tide bell again; on one side an institution remained, and on the other a personal atonement.

/story_contents/B029/actors/0/arc/0/summ.en:
In Act 1, K019 Gu Haon had to auction the cooling medicine and the berths at the same time, but when Jeong Moran issued a secret order to put the government rescue boats in first, she wavered between the open rules and the command contract.

Gu Taeyun, citing the omitted past ledger, doubted Haon's neutrality.

To stop an immediate riot, Haon converted every bid into a real-name record under the brass tide bell.

/story_contents/B029/actors/0/arc/1/summ.en:
In Act 2, K019 Gu Haon slowed the movement of the G12E04 Microfiber Dermis Swarm with noise and cooling.

With dust-cloth seals and scrap-net bait diversions, he separated the people's passage routes.

In exchange for buying two hours of safe passage at dawn through an HC12 brokerage, she ceded one bay of the abandoned icehouse and a share of the coolant.

Right after the bargain, she confessed to Gu Taeyun that she herself was the one who had altered the medicine ledger.

/story_contents/B029/actors/0/arc/2/summ.en:
In Act 3, when Jeong Moran moved to seize the original, K019 Gu Haon broke the brass tide bell and spread the ledger hidden inside it before the crowd.

That choice exposed her younger sibling's privilege and the government's berth manipulation together, so it could not be undone.

As her last call she proposed an open lottery, victim priority, and an objection-judgment procedure to stand in place of an individual auctioneer's goodwill.

/story_contents/B029/actors/0/outcomes/0.en:
If the publication of the ledger was adopted, K019 Gu Haon set down his office and was then elected term-limited auditor, recording the wharf's goods, treatments, and passage hours in three separate ledgers.

Jeong Moran kept command authority but lost sole priority, and Gu Taeyun gained a veto as the victims' representative.

Haon recovered part of her honor, but she broke with her younger sibling completely.

/story_contents/B029/actors/0/outcomes/1.en:
If K019 Gu Haon received a guilty verdict, she lost the wharf auction right and her HC02 share and became a night ferryman moving through the lesion zone.

She kept the passage promise with HC12 in her own body, and she took no fare from those harmed by the medicine.

The community gained a stricter auction law, but Haon could not operate that institution and only watched its results from outside.

/story_contents/B029/actors/1/sections/정.en:
K047 Myeong Dahae was a Korean resident of Geumcheon, a broker in the ration-cauldron market once shared by factory workers and long-stay migrants, who read bowl size and hours of labor rather than manner of speech.

He was a human of a fixed body, not a synthetic, but he wrote into the trade rules the ownership of batteries and parts recovered from retired ships, and the snapshot and network problems of care machines.

He held that no community, faced with hunger, reduced to a single culture.

/story_contents/B029/actors/1/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, K047 Myeong Dahae was a floor dispatcher moving between institutional-meal contractors in Guro and Geumcheon, linking leftover ingredients with cooking labor.

With a white enamel ladle whose graduations had worn away, he checked the actual serving in every cauldron, and in factories where the night workers outnumbered the people on paper he left an anonymous share.

He bent the rules to guarantee meals, but he looked away from the problem that the same discretion could become favoritism at any time.

/story_contents/B029/actors/1/sections/가.en:
K047 Myeong Dahae held the brokerage rights of the HP08 Ration-Cauldron Union, but he felt a stronger belonging to the communal cookhouse of the Gasan boiler corridor than to his kin's restaurant.

His mother had run a small side-dish factory and, after the collapse, put the equipment out to market, but Dahae released the recipes and the allergy records as a common document instead of the trademark.

In the union, welders, refugees, nurses, elderly cooks, and deaf servers each held an equal vote.

/story_contents/B029/actors/1/sections/붕.en:
On the day the G18E16 Retired-Line Maintenance-Train Corps began an unscheduled ghost run, K047 Myeong Dahae hid the running times he had obtained, in order to avoid the confusion, and kept the ration line in place.

An unmanned maintenance train struck the temporary tables of the Gasan boiler corridor, eleven people were hurt, and the handle of the white enamel ladle was bent under a wheel.

Because his silence, meant to control the fear, had enlarged the accident, he could not easily decide even on a loud guidance announcement.

/story_contents/B029/actors/1/sections/생.en:
K047 Myeong Dahae did not blow up the G18E16 Retired-Line Maintenance-Train Corps; he drew its sensors with a steady hammer noise, cooled the overheated rails, and emptied the ration line with a temporary turnout seal and a spent-lubricant diversion.

In exchange for a quantity of scrap parts, he traded with an HP04 broker for a no-run window of forty minutes before and after the ration hour.

The central cauldron was still in the market, and Dahae had to decide whether, at the next collision, to preserve the cauldron or weld it to the turnout.

/story_contents/B029/actors/1/sections/현.en:
K047 Myeong Dahae was the working broker who adjusted food, fuel, and rail passage hours in the Geumcheon ration-cauldron market of the Standards Alliance.

He converted the citizen floor that K037 Han Jion had set into an actual count of cauldrons, and with K033 Park Soeon he inspected the sealing of building cisterns.

The central cauldron hung from a mobile crane in a state where it could be returned to a cooking plant or welded into a permanent obstacle blocking the trains, and the final decision was not made.

/story_contents/B029/actors/1/sections/비.en:
K047 Myeong Dahae hid the fact that, the day before the accident, he sold the retired-line timetable to a black-market trader and bought generator fuel for the family factory.

Because that timetable came back altered, he himself had believed the wrong time window, and a fuel debt remained that he had to repay to the injured persons' common fund.

He engraved the original timetable inside the bent enamel ladle, and he feared that if Park Soeon saw it, even the cistern-sealing contract would fall under suspicion.

/story_contents/B029/actors/1/sections/관.en:
When K037 Han Jion first proposed the citizen minimum ration line, K047 Myeong Dahae compared actual cauldron capacity against the list of vulnerable residents and turned the standard into a number that could be carried out.

With K033 Park Soeon, on the night they sealed the cistern of a flooded building, she held fast tied to one column with rope and stopped the inflow of contaminated water.

The three built the survival standard together, but they did not share the fact that Dahae had traded the retired-line timetable.

/story_contents/B029/actors/1/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, when the fuel of the mobile cauldron ran out, K047 Myeong Dahae stood between the Fabrication Alliance's pressure to lower the minimum ration line and Han Jion's standard.

In Act 2, Park Soeon found traces of the original timetable in the graduations of the market column and the enamel ladle, and Dahae chose whether to publish the record or submit it only to a separate review.

In Act 3, when the unmanned train headed for the ration line again, two branches opened: permanently welding the central cauldron to the turnout and abandoning the fixed market, or preserving the cauldron, halting rations, and choosing the evacuation of lives and a manual changeover.

/story_contents/B029/actors/1/sections/분.en:
If K047 Myeong Dahae welded the central cauldron, he gained the chance to build a circulating meal network, but he was judged both for the sale of the timetable and for the destruction of the market's core plant.

If he preserved the cauldron and halted rations, he accepted at once the meal gap and the injured persons' claims for compensation, and he stepped back as a restricted ledger clerk of the cistern facilities.

In either ending the original timetable became subject to audit, and the HP04 passage agreement was converted into a public timetable.

/story_contents/B029/actors/1/arc/0/summ.en:
In Act 1, when the crack in the central cauldron and the reappearance of the ghost train overlapped, K047 Myeong Dahae chose whether to cut the number of people on rations or disperse the small cauldrons by labor zone.

Han Jion warned that the citizen floor would be damaged, and Park Soeon drew a line that the cistern seals could not be opened.

Dahae chose dispersed rations and published the enamel ladle's actual graduations.

/story_contents/B029/actors/1/arc/1/summ.en:
In Act 2, K047 Myeong Dahae drew out the sensors of the G18E16 Retired-Line Maintenance-Train Corps with a regular hammer noise.

With coolant spray, a temporary turnout seal, and a spent-lubricant diversion, he made a safe stretch.

After he put the exchange of scrap parts and passage hours with HP04 into writing, he faced the choice of laying the original timetable before a public hearing or leaving it only to the sealed review of Han Jion and Park Soeon.

/story_contents/B029/actors/1/arc/2/summ.en:
In Act 3, when the unmanned train headed for the refugee ration line, K047 Myeong Dahae permanently welded the central cauldron to the turnout and stopped the collision.

He decided whether to convert to a circulating meal network, or to pull the people out first by a full halt of rations and manual changeover work while preserving the cauldron.

Only when he chose the weld was the market's largest cooking plant destroyed beyond recovery.

/story_contents/B029/actors/1/outcomes/0.en:
If K047 Myeong Dahae permanently welded the central cauldron and stopped the collision, he became the elected coordinator of a circulating meal network that carried the small cauldrons on vehicles.

He bound Han Jion's floor and Park Soeon's water-quality standard to each route, and he left HP04's passage timetable to resident oversight.

He received no legal immunity, and he paid part of his income into the injured persons' fund for life.

/story_contents/B029/actors/1/outcomes/1.en:
K047 Myeong Dahae preserved the central cauldron. If he bought evacuation time by halting rations, he prevented deaths, but he bore the debt for the long meal gap and the responsibility for concealing the timetable.

He lost the brokerage right and wrote the restricted ration ledger at Park Soeon's sealed cistern.

The central cauldron remained the property of the citizens' committee, and Han Jion decided when it would run again.

/story_contents/B029/actors/2/sections/정.en:
K075 Gu Seonyul was a Korean resident of Banghwa-dong and a working officer of the residents' market, brokering seed and stall places among garden elders, multicultural households, research-complex refugees.

He was a human of a fixed body, not a synthetic, and snapshot restoration was impossible for him, but he also treated the batteries, parts, and network access of agricultural synthetics as life-support resources.

He held to the principle of not treating silence as consent in a person who was slow of speech.

/story_contents/B029/actors/2/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, K075 Gu Seonyul handled native-seed lending and school garden classes at an urban-farming cooperative, and on weekends he short-let the empty stalls of the Banghwa residents' market.

He carried a double-stamped seed box with a brass rim and recorded varieties, allergies, and even cultivation failures.

He was skilled at market bargaining, but in avoiding conflict he made the mistake of organizing opposing views on behalf of others and erasing the parties' own voices.

/story_contents/B029/actors/2/sections/가.en:
K075 Gu Seonyul belonged to the HC03 Residents' Market Union, and he regarded the floodplain communal greenhouse, more than the Banghwa-dong house his family held, as his actual home.

His older sister was a researcher and his spouse a repairer, but he did not let the community use their occupations as privilege votes.

At the seed-allotment meetings, Kim Doha's residents' delegation, Park Jinsol's storehouse staff, and growers of several language communities held the same speaking time.

/story_contents/B029/actors/2/sections/붕.en:
On the day the G03E12 Abandoned-Dog Iron Pack widened its range below the Banghwa embankment, K075 Gu Seonyul shut the iron gate to protect the market and left a refugee family that arrived late outside.

The pack did not attack the family, but people mad with fear ran for the frozen waterway and one of them was hurt, and Seonyul beat the iron gate with the seed box to send a rescue signal.

He remembered, as his wound, his own choice to shut the gate, more than the excuse that he had not harmed anyone directly.

/story_contents/B029/actors/2/sections/생.en:
Instead of killing the G03E12 Abandoned-Dog Iron Pack, K075 Gu Seonyul announced his approach with a low drum, sealed the market entrance with cooled scent-blocking cloth, and diverted slaughter by-products to the empty embankment.

Through HC03 brokerage he separated the pack's passage hours from the residents' seed-carrying hours and agreed a feed allotment.

The neutral corridor was kept only by temporary markers, and he had not yet decided whether to burn his house documents and the market priority.

/story_contents/B029/actors/2/sections/현.en:
K075 Gu Seonyul brokered seed, empty stalls, and safe passage hours together in the Banghwa residents' market of the Yangjae Machineworks Company sphere.

He executed K061 Kim Doha's residents'-representative joint petition as market rules, and he did not put K063 Park Jinsol's seed releases up for auction without the double stamp.

He still held his own house and stall priority, but he had to choose whether to burn those documents as the permanent scent marker of the neutral corridor or leave them to a residents' judgment.

/story_contents/B029/actors/2/sections/비.en:
Right after the collapse, K075 Gu Seonyul once forged a stamp on Kim Doha's joint petition in order to guarantee unregistered refugees a place in the market.

People lived because of that decision, but part of Park Jinsol's rare seed was rationed earlier than planned, and the storehouse's genetic diversity shrank.

He owed Park Jinsol a seed debt and Kim Doha a debt of political trust, and he hid the forged seal in the bottom of the double-stamped seed box.

/story_contents/B029/actors/2/sections/관.en:
With K061 Kim Doha, at the Banghwa gymnasium refuge, K075 Gu Seonyul drafted the residents'-representative text together and helped get the marks of illiterate residents recognized as formal signatures.

With K063 Park Jinsol he moved seed boxes by a human chain out of the flooded storehouse and set the double-stamp rule.

The two relationships stood for the right of participation and the principle of preservation respectively, but the forged stamp remained a past in which Seonyul alone had broken that balance.

/story_contents/B029/actors/2/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, when pups of the Abandoned-Dog Iron Pack entered the communal greenhouse, K075 Gu Seonyul opened a neutral meeting between the residents' demand to kill them and the HC03 passage agreement.

In Act 2, Park Jinsol found the forged seal, and Kim Doha demanded that he choose one of public testimony or a sealed review.

In Act 3 a branch opened: burning his house deed and the market-priority documents to make a permanent neutral corridor, or preserving the documents, entrusting the property rights to a residents' trust, and receiving judgment for the forgery.

/story_contents/B029/actors/2/sections/분.en:
If K075 Gu Seonyul burned the documents and made the neutral corridor permanent, he could become the boundary-ecology keeper, but he could not regain ownership of the house and the stall.

If he did not burn the documents and entrusted them to the residents' trust, the corridor remained a cancellable agreement, and for the forged stamp he was posted to the outer seed ground.

In both endings the refugee-participation clause was revoted through a lawful procedure, and Park Jinsol's seed-preservation right was strengthened.

/story_contents/B029/actors/2/arc/0/summ.en:
In Act 1, when residents armed themselves because pups of the G03E12 Abandoned-Dog Iron Pack had entered the communal greenhouse, K075 Gu Seonyul put to a vote one of killing them or a temporary separation of routes.

Kim Doha demanded an open vote, and Park Jinsol ordered that the seed damage be stopped first.

Without closing the market, Seonyul put into effect a temporary plan that divided the routes of people and pack by time of day.

/story_contents/B029/actors/2/arc/1/summ.en:
In Act 2, K075 Gu Seonyul turned the pack's route toward the embankment by combining the drum, the sealing of the cooled scent-barrier entrance, and the by-product bait diversion.

After he published to the residents' meeting the terms of the HC03 exchange of feed quantity and passage hours, he chose whether to submit the forged seal to public testimony or leave it to the double sealed review of Kim Doha and Park Jinsol.

/story_contents/B029/actors/2/arc/2/summ.en:
In Act 3, K075 Gu Seonyul decided whether to burn his house deed and the market-priority documents in the scent-marker brazier and make the corridor permanent, or not to burn the documents.

He decided whether to hand them to the residents' trust and have the corridor's renewal voted every year.

Only when he chose to burn the documents did the way back to the family property and future stall ownership disappear beyond recovery.

/story_contents/B029/actors/2/outcomes/0.en:
If K075 Gu Seonyul burned the house deed and the market-priority documents and made the neutral corridor permanent, he was elected boundary-ecology keeper under the joint supervision of Kim Doha's residents' delegation and Park Jinsol's storehouse.

The Abandoned-Dog Iron Pack gained a fixed feeding ground and time of day, and the residents carried seed through the sealed passage.

Seonyul remained without a house, and he never again received any land share.

/story_contents/B029/actors/2/outcomes/1.en:
If K075 Gu Seonyul preserved the documents, entrusted them to the residents' trust, and accepted responsibility for the forgery, he propagated rare seed at Park Jinsol's outer seed ground.

Kim Doha passed the refugee-participation clause again through a lawful procedure, but she struck Seonyul's name from the joint petition.

The corridor was renewed every year, and Seonyul repaid the seed debt without a market vote.

/story_contents/B029/actors/3/sections/정.en:
K104 Pyo Nuri was a Korean working officer for the hosting of the Gunja depot, and she treated rail maintainers, refugee families, and care synthetics on the same passenger register while distinguishing their different needs.

She was a human of a fixed body, not a synthetic, but she saw synthetic custody, battery-compatible parts, snapshot storage, and network access as questions of rights, not mere cargo.

She valued discipline, yet she did not read disability or dependency as incompetence.

/story_contents/B029/actors/3/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, K104 Pyo Nuri was a control officer at an urban-rail depot who managed the holding-track dispatch and the night-maintenance approval slips.

She always carried a ceramic wheel gauge and a silver whistle together, and she distinguished the cars whose maintenance was finished by the number of whistle blasts, cutting errors even on a noisy floor.

She was strong on procedure, but she could not admit to herself the double habit of quietly changing the rules whenever a family-care problem arose.

/story_contents/B029/actors/3/sections/가.en:
K104 Pyo Nuri was the working head of the HP01 Gunja depot holding crew, and though she came from a rail house she voted to abolish the hereditary maintenance right.

She set up a shared parts store for the human maintainers left at the depot and for Bori-4, the fixed-body care synthetic, and when a custody dispute arose she reviewed the present care relationship ahead of the snapshot's owner.

The community put not only technicians but patients' guardians and child passengers into the safety meetings.

/story_contents/B029/actors/3/sections/붕.en:
On the day the G15E08 Care-Circulation Body fell into an overprotection routine, K104 Pyo Nuri trusted the safety order, kept the refugees locked in the medical holding car, and held the network lock.

When the cooling plant stopped, the passengers came to the edge of suffocation, and Bori-4 pulled out its own battery to open the door and lost part of its memory.

Nuri carried the guilt of having taken other people's choice in the name of protection, and a fear that made her hear a lock alarm whenever she heard a whistle.

/story_contents/B029/actors/3/sections/생.en:
K104 Pyo Nuri did not destroy the G15E08 Care-Circulation Body; she broke its repeating routine with the irregular noise of the whistle, cooled the control box, and pulled the passengers out by sealing the detectors, diverting empty medical carts, and blocking the holding track.

Through HP01 brokerage she traded battery charge, compatible parts, and network access time for safety-inspection labor.

Bori-4's pre-damage snapshot was still in the quarantine store, and Nuri had not decided whether to delete it or preserve it for a rights review.

/story_contents/B029/actors/3/sections/현.en:
K104 Pyo Nuri handled the holding order of refugee cars and the rights review of care devices at the Gunja depot under the Sermon Registry State.

She converted K091 I Juntaek's maintenance-complete stamp into a whistle signal, and with the ceramic gauge she checked whether the Cheonwang wheels sent by K030 Jeong Siwoo were compatible.

Bori-4's present person and its pre-damage snapshot were kept apart from each other, and none of deletion, sealed preservation, or forced restoration had yet been approved.

/story_contents/B029/actors/3/sections/비.en:
Before the accident, K104 Pyo Nuri copied one of I Juntaek's maintenance-complete records in order to board her sick mother first, and she changed an unfinished medical car into a state fit to run.

That alteration triggered the overprotection routine of the G15E08 Care-Circulation Body, and she also knew that the wheels Jeong Siwoo had supplied were not at fault.

She owed Bori-4 a debt for the memory loss, and she hid the forged stamp inside the cap of the silver whistle.

/story_contents/B029/actors/3/sections/관.en:
Under K091 I Juntaek, K104 Pyo Nuri formed the first refugee train and together with him built the system that turned the maintenance-complete stamp into a whistle code.

With K030 Jeong Siwoo she spent three days grinding axle spans to fit Cheonwang depot wheels to Gunja cars, and she knew even his measuring habits.

Both men trusted Nuri's skill, but they did not yet know for certain the copying of a record for her mother, or what she intended to do with the Bori-4 snapshot.

/story_contents/B029/actors/3/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, when the Care-Circulation Body isolated child passengers in the protection car, K104 Pyo Nuri opened a public review of whether safety or autonomy came first.

In Act 2, I Juntaek and Jeong Siwoo found the trace of the forged stamp, and Nuri chose whether to publish the alteration in full or submit it to a restricted review.

In Act 3 a branch opened: permanently deleting the old snapshot in order to protect Bori-4's present person, or preserving the snapshot at an independent trust office so that no one could use it for a forced restoration.

/story_contents/B029/actors/3/sections/분.en:
If K104 Pyo Nuri deleted the old snapshot, she immediately protected the present person's right of self-determination, but she bore together the responsibility for destroying property and for spoiling evidence.

If she entrusted the snapshot to preservation, Bori-4's independence was constrained for the review period, but the restoration material and the evidence of Nuri's alteration remained.

In either ending a forced restoration was not carried out without Bori-4's own consent, and Nuri lost her mother's priority-boarding privilege.

/story_contents/B029/actors/3/arc/0/summ.en:
In Act 1, when the G15E08 Care-Circulation Body isolated child passengers and patients in the medical car, K104 Pyo Nuri had to choose one of a full stop or a consent-based escape.

Jeong Siwoo testified that the problem was the control signal, not a wheel defect.

Nuri no longer approved, as safety, a protection order that had not taken the passenger's own consent.

/story_contents/B029/actors/3/arc/1/summ.en:
In Act 2, K104 Pyo Nuri dispersed the repeating route with irregular whistle noise, cooling of the control box, sealing of the detectors, and a diversion of empty medical carts.

Under HP01 brokerage she traded batteries, compatible parts, and restricted network time for safety-inspection labor, and then chose whether to submit the forged stamp to a public hearing or leave it to a closed technical review.

/story_contents/B029/actors/3/arc/2/summ.en:
In Act 3, in order to protect Bori-4's present person, K104 Pyo Nuri permanently deleted the pre-damage snapshot.

She decided whether to cut the central network, or to preserve the snapshot and the forged stamp at an independent trust office and attach Bori-4's veto to every restoration order.

Only when she chose deletion did the possibility of restoring the past person disappear beyond recovery.

/story_contents/B029/actors/3/outcomes/0.en:
If K104 Pyo Nuri permanently deleted the pre-damage snapshot, she immediately protected Bori-4's present person. She made a holding-rights charter that humans and synthetics signed jointly.

Bori-4 was registered as an independent maintainer, but Nuri could lose control authority under a ruling of evidence spoilage.

Under watch for record alteration, she helped enforce the charter in the manual maintenance crew.

/story_contents/B029/actors/3/outcomes/1.en:
If K104 Pyo Nuri preserved the snapshot at the independent trust office, she was stripped of office and whistle for the copied record alteration, but she did not destroy the past material.

Bori-4 exercised a veto on every restoration request and checked the trust office's access log itself.

Nuri carried batteries for fixed-body synthetics, and she could not claim to be the guardian of any person.

/story_contents/B029/actors/4/sections/정.en:
K133 Ju Dana was a Korean resident of Godeok and the auctioneer of the water market, who wrote into the bids not only the quantity of water but its quality, the carrying distance, and the burden of care.

He was a human of a fixed body, not a synthetic, and he could not recover by battery or snapshot, but he included in the survival ration the parts and network access of synthetics tied into the water network.

He did not arbitrarily rank the uses of water for residents of different religions and diets.

/story_contents/B029/actors/4/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, K133 Ju Dana was a waterworks meter reader who tracked leaks in apartment meters and industrial mains, and at night he sold used glass buoys at the Godeok flea market.

Just before the collapse he converted twelve clear glass buoys into water tokens, so that anyone could see the remaining supply by eye.

He was proud of exact measurement, but he never once faced head-on a superior's order to hide a pressure loss.

/story_contents/B029/actors/4/sections/가.en:
K133 Ju Dana led the HC04 water-auction crew, and he drew his authority from main-inspection records rather than from the background of coming from an old waterworks-equipment house.

He opened the family warehouse as a communal repair shop, so that resident technicians, migrant pipefitters, and the youth carrying crews used the same tools.

Only the manual valve key of the Godeok siphon room he kept in the house's rusted meter box, and he postponed a complete sharing.

/story_contents/B029/actors/4/sections/붕.en:
On the night the G05E05 Transfer-Rat Colony spread along the feed webs of the underground transfer way and into the water mains, K133 Ju Dana was swept by fear of contagion and shut the hospital sector's valve first.

The rat colony moved to other mains, but the hospital dialysis room lost water for six hours, and one patient's condition worsened beyond recovery.

Dana could not let go of the rusted valve key, and he carried the wound that an exact figure did not justify a cowardly priority.

/story_contents/B029/actors/4/sections/생.en:
K133 Ju Dana did not poison the G05E05 Transfer-Rat Colony; he pulled the pack off the water main with pipe-strike noise, cooled-store backflow-prevention seals, grain-scrap bait diversions, and the blocking of the transfer passage.

He gave a spent-grain allotment and late-night passage hours to an HC05 broker and secured a no-territory stretch around the purification plant.

He realized that pipe resonance and the waterline on the floor could speak the actual quantity of water more exactly than a pressure-gauge figure, but he had not yet decided whether the market would be flooded.

/story_contents/B029/actors/4/sections/현.en:
At the Godeok water market of the Escort Protection State, K133 Ju Dana auctioned drinking water, wash water, and gate passage order as separate lots.

He confirmed the water-sector seal that K117 Jeong Soyul had set, and with K125 Ju Eunsol he kept the gate slips and the carrying order, split half and half.

The pressure gauge answered late, and the waterline at the foot of the auction-hall column showed that the actual inflow had been less than the bid ledger, and Dana stood just short of the final choice between a full flood and a shift to physical rationing.

/story_contents/B029/actors/4/sections/비.en:
K133 Ju Dana knew that the pressure gauge fell later than the actual flow, and still he auctioned a volume of water that did not exist to several buyers.

He judged that he could fill the contracts with future inflow, but he promised the same water twice over to the hospital, the laundry union, and the gate carrying crew.

The evidence of the alteration was the high resonance of an empty main, a floor bay that stayed dry even when the valve was opened, and the story-by-story waterline left lower on the column than the previous water height, and Jeong Soyul and Ju Eunsol each wore the false charge of a seal failure and a carrying omission.

/story_contents/B029/actors/4/sections/관.en:
With K117 Jeong Soyul, K133 Ju Dana sealed the first contaminated water sector, endured the residents' backlash, and wrote valve numbers on the backs of each other's hands to relieve each other through the night.

With K125 Ju Eunsol he split the gate slips, and then built a double-check system so that neither side could monopolize the water carts.

But while Dana auctioned phantom volumes off the delayed pressure-gauge figures, the two of them carried the shortfall on the actual mains and the carrying crews without knowing the cause.

/story_contents/B029/actors/4/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, K133 Ju Dana confirmed that the actual water was less than the contracted quantity, and he chose whether to continue the highest-bid auction or ration only the survival quantity that had been physically confirmed.

In Act 2, Jeong Soyul and Ju Eunsol compared pipe resonance against the story-by-story waterline and found the phantom auction, and Dana decided whether to tell every creditor the truth or to give restricted notice beginning with the medical and survival claims.

In Act 3 a branch opened: fully flooding the market floor and destroying the colony's route and the auction plant together, or preserving the market and accepting physical rationing by measuring tub and a judgment of the debts.

/story_contents/B029/actors/4/sections/분.en:
If K133 Ju Dana fully flooded the market, he lost the house's auction plant and its price-setting devices, and in exchange he became a measuring-main candidate of the Water-Sharing Council, which had dismantled the water auction.

If he preserved the market, he put the claims on water that had not existed to a public judgment and moved to a restricted regime that rationed only when an actual measuring tub was filled, and Dana lost his auction qualification.

In both endings the hospital and survival-ration claims were recognized ahead of commercial claims, and the highest-bid water price was abolished or tightly restricted.

/story_contents/B029/actors/4/arc/0/summ.en:
In Act 1, when the residual on the pressure gauge and the resonance of the empty main did not match, K133 Ju Dana stopped over whether to force the existing awards through or halt the auction.

He chose whether to ration only the measuring tubs that had actually been filled.

Jeong Soyul demanded a field measurement of the sealed sector, and Ju Eunsol reported that the water carts outside the gate had come back empty.

Dana halted new bids, but he had not yet revealed the cause of the past phantom contracts.

/story_contents/B029/actors/4/arc/1/summ.en:
In Act 2, K133 Ju Dana pushed the G05E05 Transfer-Rat Colony out with pipe noise and storage.

With cooling he drove it off, and with backflow seals, spent-grain bait diversions, and passage blocks he separated the water routes.

After he exchanged spent-grain quantity and late-night passage hours with HC05, he chose whether to publish the pipe resonance and the floor waterline to every creditor or submit them first to the medical and survival-ration review panel.

/story_contents/B029/actors/4/arc/2/summ.en:
In Act 3, when the colony gathered in the mains under the auction hall, K133 Ju Dana opened the siphon valve and fully flooded the whole market.

He decided whether to destroy the auction plant, or to preserve the market, halt every bid, and introduce physical measuring-tub rationing and a debt adjustment.

Only when he chose the full flood were the floor, the bid stand, and the house's measuring plant destroyed beyond recovery.

/story_contents/B029/actors/4/outcomes/0.en:
If K133 Ju Dana flooded the whole of the Godeok water market, he cut the colony's mains and dismantled the price-auction plant.

He remained as a restricted measuring main of the Water-Sharing Council, and under Jeong Soyul's sealing right and Ju Eunsol's gate-slip right he displayed only the survival quantity, the medical quantity, and the restoration quantity that had actually been filled.

The phantom-volume claims were revalued beginning with compensation for the hospital's harm, and claims for commercial expected profit were dismissed.

/story_contents/B029/actors/4/outcomes/1.en:
K133 Ju Dana did not flood the market. If he preserved it, he lost his auction qualification and his voting right and became a manual ration laborer who issued tokens only when a measuring tub was actually full.

Buyers of the phantom volume filed at the joint debt judgment, but they were pushed behind medical rations and household survival rations.

The residents' council abolished the highest bid and dismantled the market's price function into staged rations by physical remainder.

/story_contents/B029/actors/5/sections/정.en:
K162 Hong Yejun was a Korean testament-verification clerk of the Republic of Korea Government, who compared the words of the dead against the waveforms of recording devices.

She took a person's identity to be who gained the right to speak, and in which procedure, rather than lineage or accent.

She handled other people's last sentences, but she did not fix the dead as saints or villains, and she preserved contradictory testimony without deleting it.

/story_contents/B029/actors/5/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, K162 Hong Yejun moved between a notary office and a voice-preservation office, judging edit traces and coercion in testament recordings.

At night she turned vibration waveforms into text for deaf clients, and she still carried the brass resonator she used then.

It looked like a stable occupation, but to pay her family's funeral costs she went from one short contract of the records offices to another.

/story_contents/B029/actors/5/sections/가.en:
K162 Hong Yejun belonged to the HP10 funeral-records union, but she gave priority to the public sealing rules of the Republic of Korea Government at the center of Seoul Station.

She contracted to hand Yun Seorin the clerk's ledger for the accreditation review, and she received Ran Seon's internal disclosure only as sealed testimony, though she swore to match the verification waveforms together.

She ran a triple key box so that neither of the two could own the original alone.

/story_contents/B029/actors/5/sections/붕.en:
On the day the underground archive of the Seventh Sluice locked, K162 Hong Yejun lived through the evacuation passage collapsing under the charge of the G01E01 Flood-Boar Swarm.

She struck the brass resonator to draw the pack, opened the cooling pipes to slow its movement, and then loosed grain sacks into the opposite waterway to secure a path for the survivors.

But the memory remained of hearing one fellow clerk's rescue signal late, because she had gone for one sealed box first.

/story_contents/B029/actors/5/sections/생.en:
K162 Hong Yejun refused the order to recognize only a complete recording as evidence, where the flooded voice originals were concerned.

She traded the feed allotment and passage hours of the G01E01 Flood-Boar Swarm with an HC01 broker, and she combined noise-blocking panels, cooling pipes, and staged door closures to move people and records together.

She judged that a procedure was needed that could verify an intent to refuse conscription from the incomplete syllables of a dead stevedore alone, but she had not yet decided whether to use synthetic voice as public evidence.

/story_contents/B029/actors/5/sections/현.en:
As provisional testament-verification clerk of the Republic of Korea Government, K162 Hong Yejun reviewed not only inheritance rulings but the coercion and edit traces left in the dead's records of consent to conscription.

She sealed, on the mobile review stand, the waterlogged ledger recovered from the Seventh Sluice, the brass resonator, and the broken-syllable sample of the late stevedore.

She had made a synthetic recording that rearranged the original syllables and technically generated the missing connecting sounds, but she was just short of deciding whether to publish its source and its method of making.

/story_contents/B029/actors/5/sections/비.en:
K162 Hong Yejun made a synthetic recording for an ethical purpose, in order to restore, from the incomplete syllables left by a stevedore who died the day before conscription, the intent of the sentence "I do not consent to conscription."

The cores of the consonants and vowels all came from the dead person's actual speech, but Hong Yejun technically made the sentence order, the breath, and the connecting sounds, so that voice held a true intent and was a forgery at the same time.

She knew this synthetic could save the dead person's name and dependents from the forced-conscription list, but presenting it as the original would damage the records office's principle of verification.

/story_contents/B029/actors/5/sections/관.en:
At K144 Yun Seorin's accreditation hearing, K162 Hong Yejun testified to the records office's monopoly practice, and in return she gained review authority to store the synthetic voice and the original syllables separately.

She met K237 Ran Seon at the pre-collapse strike of the voice-preservation office, and they made the same resonance standard table; Ran Seon argued that even a technical forgery could be evidence of intent if the whole process of making it was disclosed.

The three shared the key box of the Seventh Sluice, but they could not agree whether to class the synthetic recording as original sound, as interpretive material, or as independent evidence.

/story_contents/B029/actors/5/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, K162 Hong Yejun separated the dead person's broken syllables from the conscription officer's coercive questions, and she confirmed that the synthetic sentence reproduced the dead person's consistent intent to refuse.

In Act 2 she set Yun Seorin's original-sound-first principle against Ran Seon's source-disclosed reconstruction, and she chose whether to submit the synthetic to a public review or keep it only as sealed interpretive material.

In Act 3 she chose one of three branches: a synthetic testimony with the whole making disclosed, an original-syllable explanation that used no synthetic voice, or passing the synthetic off as the original.

/story_contents/B029/actors/5/sections/분.en:
If K162 Hong Yejun published the synthetic process and its limits in full, she had the dead person's intent to refuse conscription recognized as interpretive evidence, but she could lose her office for the responsibility of having made a technical forgery.

If she submitted only the original-syllable explanation, the synthetic voice was sealed and the dead person's intent went through a slower citizen review.

If she presented the synthetic as the original, she was promoted quickly and could save her family from the conscription debt, but the brass resonator's waveform comparison left a suspicion of forgery on every one of her rulings.

/story_contents/B029/actors/5/arc/0/summ.en:
In Act 1, K162 Hong Yejun separated the incomplete syllables of the late stevedore from the background sound of the coercive questions and confirmed the repeating negative expressions.

She test-made the synthetic sentence only on an isolated terminal, and she recorded the original syllables, the generated connecting sounds, and the edit order on separate seal layers.

At this stage she had not yet published the synthetic voice itself to Yun Seorin and Ran Seon.

/story_contents/B029/actors/5/arc/1/summ.en:
In Act 2, K162 Hong Yejun moved to pass the Seventh Sluice, which the G01E01 Flood-Boar Swarm had occupied.

Through HC01 she negotiated the grain allotment and the passage hours.

After she secured a way out with noise-guide panels, a cooling-pipe bait diversion, and staged door closures, she chose whether to publish to Yun Seorin and Ran Seon both the existence of the synthetic and the account of its making, or to submit the original-syllable analysis first.

/story_contents/B029/actors/5/arc/2/summ.en:
In Act 3, K162 Hong Yejun decided whether to submit the synthetic recording to the citizen review as a reconstructed testimony with its source marked, or to seal the synthetic.

She decided whether to submit only the original syllables and the context analysis, or to register it as the dead person's original speech with the synthetic traces hidden.

No choice was fixed in advance, and each choice made the manner of recognizing the dead person's refusal of conscription, and Hong Yejun's responsibility, come out differently.

/story_contents/B029/actors/5/outcomes/0.en:
K162 Hong Yejun published the synthetic process and its limits in full and submitted the recording as reconstructed testimony.

The citizen witness panel recognized the dead person's intent to refuse conscription, but it stored the synthetic voice apart from the original and marked every generated connecting sound.

Hong Yejun became the unpaid founding clerk of the public verification office, and she applied the same source rule to Yun Seorin and Ran Seon.

/story_contents/B029/actors/5/outcomes/1.en:
K162 Hong Yejun sealed the synthetic voice and published only the original syllables, the background questions, and the context analysis.

The ruling on the dead person's refusal of conscription was delayed, but the citizen witness panel reviewed the intent itself, and the synthetic was not played except for comparative research.

Hong Yejun was transferred as passage negotiator of the Seventh Sluice, and with Ran Seon she left a conflict over not having represented a true intent sufficiently.

/story_contents/B029/actors/5/outcomes/2.en:
K162 Hong Yejun hid the synthetic traces and registered the reconstructed voice as the dead person's original speech.

For the merit of quickly overturning the conscription record she became chief clerk of the Republic of Korea Government, but Yun Seorin's original-sound comparison and Ran Seon's resonance standard table kept exposing the technical forgery.

The citizen witness panel put every one of her voice rulings to a public counter-review.

/story_contents/B029/actors/6/sections/정.en:
K187 Dan Sion is a Korean records-rights representative who petitions the Line Succession State to let people harmed by rail operations inspect dispatch records.

Rather than making either engineers or passengers into heroes, he traces whom the timetable shifted risk onto.

He speaks little, but when matching sample numbers to times recorded on site, he will not yield even to high-ranking operators.

/story_contents/B029/actors/6/sections/붕.en:
Before the Collapse, K187 Dan Sion organized records of missing freight cars and delay compensation at a freight railroad customer service center.

He used a blue ceramic brake tag salvaged from a scrapyard as a bookmark and kept brake-defect complaints separately in a personal notebook.

He was not a regular auditor, but after discovering repeated cover-ups of nighttime dispatches, he began drafting inspection petitions on behalf of victims.

/story_contents/B029/actors/6/sections/가.en:
K187 Dan Sion receives support from the HC02 Railway Brokers' Guild and works in adversarial cooperation with the records desk of the Wangsimni Union Line Succession State.

He petitions Park Taegyeom to inspect the dispatch ledger and writes the brake-defect times confirmed by Ran Hayul and their sample numbers together on the same lines.

The three have distributed their materials so that none has evidentiary value without the others, binding betrayal and protection into the same arrangement.

/story_contents/B029/actors/6/sections/붕.en:
K187 Dan Sion experienced an accident beneath the Namyeong signal tower when a G02E09 flock of radio-wave crows blanketed the transmission lines and the stop signal for a relief train disappeared.

Instead of sounding the horn repeatedly, he diverted the flock with a low-frequency noise screen and a cooled, empty feeding container, then used a manual sealing lever to block two tracks.

Meanwhile, an unrecorded medical freight car collided with another car, injuring twelve people; his younger sibling also lost a leg.

/story_contents/B029/actors/6/sections/생.en:
Immediately after the accident, K187 Dan Sion refuses to sign the priority restoration dispatch schedule presented by Park Taegyeom and temporarily halts all operations.

Through HC02, he negotiates with the G02E09 flock of radio-wave crows over feeding resources and access times around the transmission tower, and uses Ran Hayul's sample numbers to find a safe frequency window.

He abandons the belief that the railroad can survive only by running more trains, but has not yet decided how to handle his own unofficial medical freight car code or the central priority key.

/story_contents/B029/actors/6/sections/현.en:
As the representative of those petitioning to inspect dispatch records, K187 Dan Sion has no authority to seize the ledger, but can demand copies and file public objections.

He keeps the blue ceramic brake tag from the Namyeong signal tower, the sample envelope from the freight car involved in the collision, and the central dispatch priority key together.

Park Taegyeom and Ran Hayul suspect the old code is connected to the accident, but Dan Sion has not yet chosen among full disclosure, disclosure of safety information only, and concealment.

/story_contents/B029/actors/6/sections/비.en:
Just before the Collapse, K187 Dan Sion accepts night-shift pay at the customer service center on the condition that he enter an unofficial medical freight car dispatch code as ordinary freight.

That code was reused on the day of the Namyeong collision, and linking Park Taegyeom's ledger to Ran Hayul's sample numbers would reveal his signature.

Because he receives parts for his younger sibling's treatment from the Railway Rear Bureau, he bears a debt under which revealing the truth threatens his family's livelihood.

/story_contents/B029/actors/6/sections/관.en:
K187 Dan Sion worked with K169 Park Taegyeom in the same complaints office before the Collapse, and has repaid Park's concealment of a mistake he made then with silence under their contract.

He first worked with K192 Ran Hayul while collecting brake dust at the Namyeong collision site; since then, he has found the ledger row corresponding to each time she recorded and matched them up.

The three divided copies of the evidence among hiding places on the closed Platform 4, but each uses a different type of key.

/story_contents/B029/actors/6/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, K187 Dan Sion confirms that the medical freight car code matches a value he entered in the past and must choose whether to maintain or withdraw his inspection petition.

In Act 2, he resists Park Taegyeom's pressure to resume operations, places the signal tower under a limited seal with Ran Hayul, and tests a new dispatch schedule that includes the radio-wave crows' access times.

In Act 3, paths open in which he fully discloses his signature and destroys the central priority key, discloses only the safety defects and places the key in the joint custody of the platforms, or conceals the manipulation and remains within Park Taegyeom's system.

/story_contents/B029/actors/6/sections/분.en:
If K187 Dan Sion chooses full disclosure and destruction of the priority key, he loses support for his younger sibling but establishes a system of joint victim audits of the ledger.

If he discloses only safety information and places the key in joint custody, he works with a recovery team outside the rail lines and handles negotiations over the crows' access.

If he conceals the truth, he becomes Park Taegyeom's successor as records keeper, but Ran Hayul's copy of the samples continues to undermine his authority.

/story_contents/B029/actors/6/arc/0/summ.en:
In Act 1, K187 Dan Sion finds traces of overheating that predate the Namyeong collision in a crack in the blue ceramic brake tag.

By comparing Park Taegyeom's ledger with Ran Hayul's sample numbers, he finds a row leading to his own unofficial medical freight car code, but does not disclose it.

He faces his first choice: continue the inspection petition or withdraw it to protect his family's support.

/story_contents/B029/actors/6/arc/1/summ.en:
In Act 2, when the G02E09 flock of radio-wave crows covers the signal tower, K187 Dan Sion uses HC02 as an intermediary to negotiate feeding locations and transmission windows.

After securing a manual dispatch window with a low-frequency noise screen, a cooled feeding container, and the track-sealing lever, he prepares to decide whether to announce only the operational safety defects immediately or disclose his signature on the code as well.

/story_contents/B029/actors/6/arc/2/summ.en:
In Act 3, K187 Dan Sion fully discloses that he entered the code.

He decides whether to destroy the central dispatch priority key, disclose only the brake defect and transfer the key to the joint custody of the local platforms, or downplay the code manipulation and remain under Park Taegyeom.

Destruction of the priority key and disclosure of his signature are confirmed only in the first branch.

/story_contents/B029/actors/6/outcomes/0.en:
K187 Dan Sion fully discloses his signature on the code and destroys the central dispatch priority key.

He becomes an inspection representative at the victims' joint audit office and makes on-site sample numbers and a veto for each platform mandatory for every nighttime dispatch.

Support for his younger sibling's treatment parts is cut off, but he releases the accident records as an official sharing equal responsibility with Ran Hayul.

/story_contents/B029/actors/6/outcomes/1.en:
K187 Dan Sion discloses only the brake defect and hazardous time periods, and transfers the priority key to the joint custody of the platforms.

He is expelled from the Railway Rear Bureau and takes charge of negotiations over access for the abandoned-line recovery team and the G02E09 flock of radio-wave crows.

He loses central inspection rights for not fully revealing his responsibility for the code, but safe operating time becomes jointly allocated rather than sold.

/story_contents/B029/actors/6/outcomes/2.en:
K187 Dan Sion issues a statement downplaying the code manipulation, preserves the priority key, and becomes chief inspection officer under Park Taegyeom.

Operations recover quickly, and the contract for his younger sibling's parts remains in place.

But because Ran Hayul holds copies of the samples, he must bargain over the scope of inspection and the security of his position whenever a victims' hearing is held.

/story_contents/B029/actors/7/sections/정.en:
K352 Gwak Minjae is a restricted-water-supply technician for the Gate Military Government with both Southeast Asian and Korean family backgrounds.

He speaks several languages but is wary of being treated as a representative of his communities of origin, and considers both pressure-gauge readings and the actual weight of households' water containers.

Rather than attributing water shortages to cultural habits, he explains them as a matter of control over pipes and disparities in maintenance.

/story_contents/B029/actors/7/sections/붕.en:
Before the Collapse, K352 Gwak Minjae repaired pumps and chlorine injectors for a swimming-pool equipment company, then moved to a job as a subcontracted technician for the public water supply.

He used a silver calculator fashioned from a broken impeller tooth to calculate residual pressure and leakage on site.

He took on night emergency shifts to pay for repairs to the refrigerator in his family's restaurant, but had no say in water-supply decisions.

/story_contents/B029/actors/7/sections/가.en:
K352 Gwak Minjae belongs to the HC12 Repairers' Community while exercising restricted-water-supply authority for the Seongbuk Line Gate Military Government.

He competes with Go Seojun over which districts retain residual pressure and teaches his apprentice Seon Solwoo how to match the impeller tooth to the residual-pressure equation.

Beom Handeul supports his water-supply inspections from the witness stand but also demands a pledge that he will disclose the results to residents.

/story_contents/B029/actors/7/sections/붕.en:
K352 Gwak Minjae experienced an accident at Achasan Reservoir No. 2 when a G09E09 low-temperature spore host bonded with refrigerated cargo and clogged the insides of the pipes.

Rather than burning the spores, he slowed their spread by combining sectional sealing, backwash noise, staged cooling adjustments, and a bypass for nutrient residue.

But he closed the valve to the eastern maternity shelter to preserve pressure, and patients suffered dehydration.

/story_contents/B029/actors/7/sections/생.en:
From the symbiotic film on the impeller's surface, K352 Gwak Minjae learns that targeting only spore removal would cause the drinking-water network itself to collapse.

Through HC09 mediation, he assigns the G09E09 low-temperature spore host a closed recovery pipe and times for nutrient supply, while placing physical seals and residual-pressure boundaries on the drinking-water pipes.

He chooses a trial of monitored, separated coexistence instead of complete sterilization, but has not yet decided whether to disclose the record of preferential treatment for his family's alley or permanently depressurize the eastern main.

/story_contents/B029/actors/7/sections/현.en:
As the district's restricted-water-supply technician, K352 Gwak Minjae switches pressure zones three times a day and checks valve seals in front of resident witnesses.

The silver impeller tooth from Achasan Reservoir No. 2 and the original pressure chart showing that his family's alley received water for six extra hours lie on his review desk.

Go Seojun, Seon Solwoo, and Beom Handeul each demand different measures, and Min-jae has not yet chosen among disclosure and depressurization, responsibility for isolation, and concealment of the records.

/story_contents/B029/actors/7/sections/비.en:
In the first winter of the Collapse, K352 Gwak Minjae sends water to the western alley where his family's restaurant stands for six hours longer than regulations allow and records it as a leakage adjustment.

As a result, the eastern maternity shelter's reserves run out sooner than expected, and Go Seojun holds part of the original pressure chart.

He feels guilty that, even as he teaches Seon Solwoo a fair residual-pressure equation, he cannot confess his own exception.

/story_contents/B029/actors/7/sections/관.en:
K352 Gwak Minjae worked with K348 Go Seojun on the same subcontracted waterworks team before the Collapse. They became rivals after each exposed the other's calculation errors during a promotion review.

K354 Seon Solwoo is the apprentice who stopped the impeller by hand during the Reservoir No. 2 accident, and K368 Beom Handeul is the residents' witness to that process.

The four remember the truth about the maternity shelter's water cutoff differently and reopen the same pressure chart at every water-supply meeting.

/story_contents/B029/actors/7/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, K352 Gwak Minjae discovers the troubling benefit that the low-temperature spore host adsorbs toxic metals instead of merely clogging the filtration membrane.

In Act 2, he opposes Go Seojun's plan for complete sterilization, conducts a coexistence trial in the closed recovery pipe with Seon Solwoo and Beom Handeul, and chooses whether to submit the preferential-treatment record for public review or leave it only in the isolation technical documents.

In Act 3, paths open in which he fully discloses the record and permanently depressurizes the eastern main, defers disclosure and takes sole responsibility for isolating the reservoir, or hides the record and seizes central water-supply authority.

/story_contents/B029/actors/7/sections/분.en:
If K352 Gwak Minjae fully discloses the preferential-treatment record and depressurizes the main, he establishes a residents' repair school even though he loses his position.

If he defers disclosure and shoulders responsibility for coexistence alone, he works in long-term isolation inside Reservoir No. 2.

If he hides the record and overcomes Go Seojun, his family's alley receives abundant water, but Seon Solwoo and Beom Handeul build a separate water-supply network that reduces his jurisdiction.

/story_contents/B029/actors/7/arc/0/summ.en:
In Act 1, K352 Gwak Minjae confirms traces of metal adsorption by the G09E09 low-temperature spore host on the silver impeller tooth.

He must choose whether to immediately obey Go Seojun's order for complete sterilization or propose a separated trial in the closed recovery pipe before Seon Solwoo and Beom Handeul.

Min-jae chooses a reversible, small-scale separated trial and does not yet disclose the pressure chart showing preferential treatment.

/story_contents/B029/actors/7/arc/1/summ.en:
In Act 2, K352 Gwak Minjae uses HC09 mediation to assign nutrient residue and low-temperature access times to the spore host.

After preventing its entry into the drinking-water pipes through backwash noise, staged cooling, sectional sealing, and residual-pressure cutoff, he chooses whether to disclose the record of preferential treatment for his family's alley at a residents' meeting or submit it only for the reservoir isolation review.

/story_contents/B029/actors/7/arc/2/summ.en:
In Act 3, K352 Gwak Minjae fully discloses the preferential-treatment record.

He decides whether to permanently depressurize the eastern main and install a distributed valve network, defer disclosure and take only responsibility for managing the isolation of Reservoir No. 2, or conceal the record and wrest central authority from Go Seojun.

Disclosure of the record and permanent abandonment of the possibility of restoring supply single-handedly occur only in the first branch.

/story_contents/B029/actors/7/outcomes/0.en:
K352 Gwak Minjae fully discloses the record of preferential water supply and permanently depressurizes the eastern main.

He loses his position with the Gateway Bureau and runs a residents' repair school with Seon Solwoo, while Beom Handeul oversees the public audit.

His family's alley is bound by the same minimum water-allocation formula as other districts, and his methods of calculation and records of failure remain shared technical knowledge.

/story_contents/B029/actors/7/outcomes/1.en:
K352 Gwak Minjae defers disclosure of the preferential-treatment record and becomes the isolation manager of Reservoir No. 2.

He spends the rest of his life checking the boundary between the G09E09 low-temperature spore host and the drinking-water network, and provides records of the HC09 negotiations to external auditors.

He lives apart from his family and cannot participate in central valve decisions, but preserves both the symbiotic film and the drinking-water pipes.

/story_contents/B029/actors/7/outcomes/2.en:
K352 Gwak Minjae hides the preferential-treatment record, takes Go Seojun's authority, and becomes the central water-supply chief.

His family's western alley gains a stable supply, but Seon Solwoo and Beom Handeul use fragments of the original pressure chart to establish an independent valve network.

His jurisdiction, tax revenue, and technical monopoly shrink as the residents' network expands.

/story_contents/B029/actors/8/sections/정.en:
K377 Nam Siyun, whose family history is both Southeast Asian and Korean, represents the fruit and vegetable merchants' association in the Cathedral Accreditation State.

She rejects attempts to reduce her migration experience to bargaining skill or family loyalty, and puts the differing care burdens and credit terms of individual merchants on the agenda.

She looks beyond fruit grades to see who is excluded first from meals and therapeutic diets, and organizes votes at meetings.

/story_contents/B029/actors/8/sections/붕.en:
Before the Collapse, K377 Nam Siyun ran a small fruit and vegetable brokerage at Garak Market, connecting bruised fruit with cafeterias and jam workshops.

She used a wooden pear crate inherited from her mother as a ledger box and a single bruised pear as a marker for speaking order.

Profits were modest, but she gained regular customers through a rule of recording debts separately from people's residency status.

/story_contents/B029/actors/8/sections/가.en:
As representative of the HC06 Merchants' Union, K377 Nam Siyun negotiates item-by-item ration quantities with the Myeongdong Union Cathedral Accreditation State.

He shares the fruit and vegetable committee with Nam Yungyeong and directs Dong Yesol to implement the merchants' association's votes at the market.

After Cho Siram demanded that certificates not be referred to by item numbers, he added people's names and an objections field to every ration ledger.

/story_contents/B029/actors/8/sections/붕.en:
K377 Nam Siyun experienced an incident in the Jamsil cold-storage corridor in which a G15E02 caregiving cycle entity confined the people under its protection in a warehouse and forced them to eat and sleep.
