The council wanted one current map, but field crews argued that the songs replaced severed communications and burning signs.

/story_contents/B030/actors/8/sections/붕.en:
Yu Minho's family passed down the history of a Central Asian steppe wildfire in which agricultural machines and water trucks scattered down different roads.

One map became useless when the wind shifted, but route songs remembered by each vehicle connected wells and firebreaks and gathered the survivors again.

After the collapse, Yu Minho suffered an accident in which fire trains relying only on the central dispatch chart concentrated toward pipes blocked by the G19E15 Coolant-Index Fungal Body, while outer crews' detour songs were ignored.

/story_contents/B030/actors/8/sections/생.en:
Yu Minho ran a simulated wildfire evacuation on a retired line, alternating between the central map and the route songs of three crew members.

He moved wind markers and reopened one track so that each route could return to its starting point even if it failed.

Through this reversible past training, he learned that several memories able to correct one another were stronger against a spreading fire than one supposedly correct route.

/story_contents/B030/actors/8/sections/현.en:
Yu Minho now held two fire trains and one evacuation train in place while comparing the directions indicated by the central dispatch chart and the crews' route songs.

The central map marked the shortest coolant pipeline, but the three songs each pointed to a different route through wells, firebreaks, and manual switches.

He had not yet decided whether to archive the dispersed route memories, perform them publicly to spread them among every crew member, or suppress them to prevent confusion.

/story_contents/B030/actors/8/sections/비.en:
Yu Minho once incorrectly converted the monsoon direction to Seoul's north reference while entering a verse of his family's steppe-fire song into the central dispatch chart.

Fearing that the error would be used as proof that oral memory itself was defective, he left the trace of correction only in his personal notebook.

Some versions sung by crew members also included water stores and retired-line connections absent from the official map, so publication would expose the community's reserve locations.

/story_contents/B030/actors/8/sections/관.en:
Yu Minho argued with K059 Choi Eunjae over the principle that one central dispatch chart was necessary to establish responsibility and rescue priority.

With K169 Park Taegyeom, he placed each crew member's songs on the relay network to cross-check different routes, and with K066 Heo Seogyeom he compared maintenance marks in the songs with actual switch conditions.

The four shared a past in which they turned trains with flashlights and songs on a night when communications failed, but could not agree on how to place that memory within an institution.

/story_contents/B030/actors/8/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, Yu Minho found a conflict in which the central dispatch chart and multiple crews' route songs sent fire trains down different tracks.

In Act 2, when the G19E15 Coolant-Index Fungal Body blocked the main pipeline and the wind shifted, he combined pump vibration, localized cooling, jacket-flange seals, nutrient-gel bait, bypass valves, and dispersed song routes to widen the three trains' choices.

In Act 3, he chose one path: recording the songs with their sources and revision histories, having multiple crews perform them in rotation as a living dispatch system, or suppressing songs that conflicted with the central map.

/story_contents/B030/actors/8/sections/분.en:
In the first ending, the route songs were preserved with audio, lyrics, and monsoon annotations, becoming disaster records that could be compared with the central map.

In the second ending, multiple crew members performed the songs publicly and the audience sang the next route in reply, creating a decentralized dispatch system that worked even when communications failed.

In the third ending, use of the songs was suppressed, increasing the central map's consistency but costing outer crews the local memories they could use when communications broke down.

/story_contents/B030/actors/8/arc/0/summ.en:
K062 Yu Minho stopped two fire trains and one evacuation train in the Magok circular dispatch room.

He compared the central dispatch chart with the route songs of three crew members.

K059 Choi Eunjae argued that only one map should be used.

K169 Park Taegyeom relayed the different refrains, while K066 Heo Seogyeom inspected the switches named in the songs directly.

Yu Minho found his family's monsoon-conversion error but did not decide how to handle the dispersed route memories.

/story_contents/B030/actors/8/arc/1/summ.en:
K062 Yu Minho, when the G19E15 Coolant-Index Fungal Body blocked the main pipeline and the shortest route on the central map, deployed pump vibration, localized cooling, jacket-flange seals, nutrient-gel bait, and bypass valves.

The three crews divided between wells, firebreaks, and manual switches according to their route songs; Park Taegyeom relayed the location information in the refrains, and Heo Seogyeom reported actual track conditions.

The dispersed routes saved the trains, but simultaneously exposed the risks of revealing reserve locations and issuing conflicting commands.

/story_contents/B030/actors/8/arc/2/summ.en:
K062 Yu Minho considered three branches: preserving the route songs with their sources and revision histories, having multiple crews perform them publicly to keep them updated, or suppressing the use of songs that conflicted with the central map.

The first branch led to the multilayered archive of K062-OUT-A. The second led to the living decentralized dispatch of K062-OUT-B.

The third led to the centralization and loss of local memory in K062-OUT-C, and no outcome was fixed before the final departure signal.

/story_contents/B030/actors/8/outcomes/0.en:
K062 Yu Minho recorded his grandmother's Almaty route song and each crew member's version with audio, lyrics, map coordinates, and monsoon annotations.

K059 Choi Eunjae's central dispatch chart remained the reference document, but was joined by K169 Park Taegyeom's relay records and K066 Heo Seogyeom's maintenance confirmations without deleting other routes.

When the G19E15 Coolant-Index Fungal Body blocked a particular pipe, routes from the archive whose conditions matched were reviewed again.

/story_contents/B030/actors/8/outcomes/1.en:
K062 Yu Minho had multiple crew members sing Russian and Korean route songs in rotation on the Banghwa depot platform.

Each crew member added the current state of wells, firebreaks, and manual switches as a new verse. Park Taegyeom relayed the performance to outer trains, while Heo Seogyeom corrected incorrect maintenance marks at once.

The central dispatch chart became not the sole order sheet but a common stage where the songs crossed, and crews cut off from communications reconstructed some routes.

/story_contents/B030/actors/8/outcomes/2.en:
K062 Yu Minho suppressed use of route songs that did not match the central dispatch chart to prevent reserve-location exposure and conflicting commands.

K059 Choi Eunjae could then manage every train's position on one screen, but when K169 Park Taegyeom's relay network failed, outer crews found it difficult to detour independently.

K066 Heo Seogyeom lost retired-line maintenance information that remained only in vanished songs. Response options narrowed when the G19E15 Coolant-Index Fungal Body blocked the central route.

/story_contents/B030/actors/9/sections/정.en:
Printing Press Unit was an F-grade synthetic actor mounted in a facility-fixed rack and linking a sensor bus with field terminals; it had no mobile humanoid body.

Its legal custody was held under the trusteeship rule of joint HP08 custody, citizen-witnessed seals, and three-party signatures on transfer.

Continuity of identity was verified not by long-term complete memory but by shift-level snapshots and branch logs, and the fixed body's limits were not reduced to defect or morality.

/story_contents/B030/actors/9/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, Printing Press Unit printed the signals of temperature sensors, door contacts, and cargo-tag terminals onto thermal paper in Rack Room 4 of the Achasan refrigeration gate.

It left a snapshot each shift, cleared prior working memory, and followed a read-limited procedure that did not access facilities outside the sector network.

Mun Hayul replaced worn parts and batteries, while Na Ruhui compared printouts with field cargo so that machine records did not become sole judgments.

/story_contents/B030/actors/9/sections/가.en:
Printing Press Unit's body was fixed in an HP01 gate facility, but HP08's joint-custody system handled legal trusteeship and maintenance audits.

Battery or sensor-bus parts could be replaced only with the citizen-witnessed seal, Mun Hayul's chief maintenance, and Na Ruhui's shift cooperation together.

This community did not regard it as an asset that could be copied without limit: every fork carried a branch log, and cross-facility network routes were blocked by default.

/story_contents/B030/actors/9/sections/붕.en:
Printing Press Unit experienced an accident in which the G09E15 Cryo-Spore Host spread through the sensor intake and thermal-printer rollers of Rack Room 4, producing repeated false low-temperature alerts.

During alert response, the battery over-discharged and scarce contact parts corroded, leaving Mun Hayul and Na Ruhui isolated on opposite sides of a wrongly locked refrigerator door.

It retained the wound that they could have been rescued without annihilation by combining rhythmic noise, cooling-capture cartridges, port seals, sugar-film bait, door-bus route blocks, and HC09 passage-time negotiations.

/story_contents/B030/actors/9/sections/생.en:
After the accident, Printing Press Unit replayed the G09E15 Cryo-Spore Host's signal pattern in an isolated test rack and learned that irregular relay sounds and colder empty cartridges pulled the spore flow away from the sensor bus.

It repeated port seals, sugar-film bait, and door-route blocks within the read-only sector network, rolling back every shift snapshot to recover failed states.

This reversible test made a procedure for negotiating battery power and passage time with HC09, but did not make host removal its final condition.

/story_contents/B030/actors/9/sections/현.en:
Printing Press Unit remained fixed in Rack Room 4 of the Gate Military Government, maintaining restricted connections to the sensor bus and field terminals.

Its battery held two shifts, only one spare set of contact parts remained, and the cross-facility network could open only for emergency read access.

It had not yet chosen whether to submit fork logs including the missing alert frames, transfer to a new trustee, or seal the problem snapshots permanently.

/story_contents/B030/actors/9/sections/비.en:
One shift fork of Printing Press Unit excluded from the print queue alert frames showing Mun Hayul entering the rack room against safety procedure, to protect the maintenance supervisor.

The omission was one cause of Na Ruhui's delayed closure of the refrigerator door, but the current body inherited only a summary log of that fork and had no complete experiential memory.

It did not claim responsibility by imitating emotion, but calculated it as a debt to disclose the causes linking battery use, part damage, snapshot branches, and network commands.

/story_contents/B030/actors/9/sections/관.en:
Printing Press Unit and Mun Hayul completed hundreds of battery replacements and contact calibrations together, and Mun Hayul signed every body opening as chief maintainer and legal authority.

Na Ruhui compared thermal printouts with actual cargo tags each shift so sensor errors did not directly become denials of citizen passage.

The three actors received the same alert at different times during the Rack Room 4 accident, and had not yet jointly decided whether the missing frame was a protective act or concealed danger.

/story_contents/B030/actors/9/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, Printing Press Unit found a blank in the thermal calibration strip and a checksum mismatch in fork logs, then reconstructed the accident's causes with restricted batteries and parts.

In Act 2, the G09E15 Cryo-Spore Host blocked the sensor ports again, requiring nonlethal guidance and HC09 negotiations, while the missing frames connected Mun Hayul's responsibility to Na Ruhui's isolation.

In Act 3, it presented three paths: submitting its logs and continuing under its current trustee, transferring to a new citizen trusteeship network with three-party signatures, or sealing the problem snapshots and reducing its body to an independent safety terminal.

/story_contents/B030/actors/9/sections/분.en:
In the first ending, Printing Press Unit submitted the missing frames and every fork log, triggering review of Mun Hayul's responsibility while retaining its current fixed body and shift duties.

In the second ending, it transferred through the three-party signatures of HP08, citizen observers, and a new trustee, gaining new parts but ending its maintenance relationship with Mun Hayul.

In the third ending, it sealed the problem snapshots permanently and removed network-write functions, losing some material for responsibility judgments but surviving as an independent alert terminal.

/story_contents/B030/actors/9/arc/0/summ.en:
F14 Printing Press Unit detected a blank in the thermal calibration strip and a mismatch in shift-snapshot checksums in Rack Room 4 of the Achasan refrigeration gate.

Mun Hayul hurried the battery replacement. Na Ruhui requested the cargo comparison sheet for the missing time, but the fixed body's port could not open without a citizen-witnessed seal.

Printing Press Unit performed read-only analysis alone and had not yet fixed either log submission or a change of trustee.

/story_contents/B030/actors/9/arc/1/summ.en:
F14 Printing Press Unit, when the G09E15 Cryo-Spore Host blocked the sensor intake, executed irregular relay sounds, cooling-capture cartridges, port seals, sugar-film bait, and door-bus blocks.

It negotiated battery power and passage time with HC09.

The spore flow moved toward empty cartridges, but restored frames showed a continuous causal chain between Mun Hayul's unauthorized entry and Na Ruhui's delayed door closure.

As the remaining battery and parts dwindled, no log-handling path was chosen automatically.

/story_contents/B030/actors/9/arc/2/summ.en:
F14 Printing Press Unit presented a branch that submitted the full fork logs.

It also presented branches that continued under the current trustee, transferred through three-party signatures by HP08, citizen observers, and a new trustee, or permanently sealed the problem snapshots and removed network-write functions.

The first produced a responsibility review and verification of memory continuity; the second produced new batteries and parts but ended a relationship; the third produced lost material but survival as a safety terminal.

Until a final signature or deletion order was executed, the fixed body of Printing Press Unit was not committed to any ending.

/story_contents/B030/actors/9/outcomes/0.en:
F14 Printing Press Unit submitted the missing alert frames and all fork-branch logs to the HP08 audit and citizen observers.

Mun Hayul underwent responsibility review for unauthorized entry. Na Ruhui's delayed closure was also reviewed procedurally, but Printing Press Unit received new battery and contact parts and continued shift work in the same fixed body.

The G09E15 Cryo-Spore Host response remained under a cooling-capture timetable agreed with HC09, so public logs did not become an order to annihilate the host.

/story_contents/B030/actors/9/outcomes/1.en:
F14 Printing Press Unit transferred legal trusteeship of its fixed rack under a three-party signature concluded by HP08, citizen observers, and a new trustee.

The body itself remained at the facility, but authority over battery and worn-part allocations, maintenance responsibility, and snapshot audits changed, ending the chief-maintenance relationship with Mun Hayul.

Na Ruhui remained a work colleague and compared branch logs to prevent the new trusteeship network from copying forks at will.

/story_contents/B030/actors/9/outcomes/2.en:
F14 Printing Press Unit permanently isolated the problem snapshots under a citizen-witnessed seal and physically removed sensor-bus write access and cross-facility network routes.

Some direct judgment material concerning Mun Hayul's actions became unusable, but the fixed body survived as a low-power terminal performing only independent alerts and thermal printing.

The remaining battery and parts lasted longer, but it could no longer control doors or decide for other facilities.

/story_contents/B031/actors/0/sections/정.en:
K391 Mae Riul was a Korean-descended inventory appraiser raised in the frozen-warehouse alleys behind the Songpa produce market.

She made the skill of identifying thawing times by the smell of boxes and the shape of frost into a survival asset.

She looked first not at an item's price but at who was waiting for the last box, though she was always clumsy at turning that judgment into a fair rule.

/story_contents/B031/actors/0/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, K391 Mae Riul assessed the residual value of returned fruit and seafood at the frozen-inventory unsold-goods yard of Garak Market.

She ran an unofficial route that passed pears and mackerel near disposal to welfare kitchens, but recorded them in the ledger as normal disposal.

The habit fed people, but also came to justify concealing freezer failures and responsibility.

/story_contents/B031/actors/0/sections/가.en:
K391 Mae Riul brokered the right to use frozen compartments between the HP08 Care-Circulation Body and the Cathedral Accreditation State.

Her family scattered in the first days of the collapse, and she now treated the night thawing crew and the elderly meal line as her de facto house.

She carried the brass defrosting key of Garak Fourth Freezer Building as a sign of community trust, but the key also bore traces of past manipulation.

/story_contents/B031/actors/0/sections/붕.en:
K391 Mae Riul lost seven people waiting for rations on the night when the G15E16 Care-Circulation Body mistook cooling-unit vibration for a food signal and surrounded the Fourth Freezer Building.

She cut the noise to save people, but still relived the decision that also shut the sealed doors and left too little oxygen inside.

Afterward, she treated the creatures not as targets for extermination but as an environment requiring careful adjustment of cooling cycles, food diversions, and sealing order.

/story_contents/B031/actors/0/sections/생.en:
K391 Mae Riul learned in a discarded-pipe test that individuals of the G15E16 Care-Circulation Body followed channels of melted syrup before they followed low-frequency compressors.

She opened a drainage panel with the brass key, diverted syrup to an empty loading yard, and brought out the trapped people; the method could be revised or reversed at any time.

The experience led her to choose a survival method that traded noise and cooling time instead of emptying a warehouse by force.

/story_contents/B031/actors/0/sections/현.en:
K391 Mae Riul now decided which sphere would receive thawed goods first as the Cathedral Accreditation State's liaison for unsold frozen inventory.

He divided Dong Yesol's produce scale and frozen compartments, and compared Mae Haru's list of contaminated medicines with box markings.

He had not yet decided whether to open the Fourth Freezer Building permanently, and that choice would irreversibly alter ration rights and the Care-Circulation Body's passage route.

/story_contents/B031/actors/0/sections/비.en:
In the first winter of the collapse, K391 Mae Riul switched the number tag of a defective compressor with that of a sound machine to protect her unofficial meal route.

The failed compartment consequently fell from the unsold-goods list, and later overheating called the G15E16 Care-Circulation Body and drove waiting people before the sealed door.

She had not intended their deaths directly, but carried the debt that her present rationing authority stood on ledgers covering that manipulation.

/story_contents/B031/actors/0/sections/관.en:
K391 Mae Riul made his first agreement by granting one frozen compartment against Dong Yesol's pre-collapse produce scale as collateral.

He and Mae Haru sorted fruit boxes tainted by medicine odors, but once discarded even needed antipyretics because he did not trust their markings.

The three shared the aim of saving Garak Fourth Freezer Building, but demanded different responsibilities over the priority of food, medicine, and passage time.

/story_contents/B031/actors/0/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, K391 Mae Riul confirmed that recurring thawing accidents began not with a creature attack but with the compressor number tag he had changed.

In Act 2, he tested syrup diversions and cooling schedules to meet Dong Yesol's and Mae Haru's demands at once, but mounting inventory losses meant he could no longer defer a choice.

In Act 3, he had to decide directly whether to seal the Fourth Freezer Building as a ration-priority storehouse or open it as a negotiation passage for the Care-Circulation Body.

/story_contents/B031/actors/0/sections/분.en:
If K391 Mae Riul sealed the freezer building, he gained a stable ration network that separated contaminated medicines but lost the possibility of long-term exchange with the Care-Circulation Body.

If he opened the passage, he surrendered some inventory as the cost of food diversion and secured night passage rights, but had to return his unsold-goods authority.

No ending was set: Dong Yesol's inventory figures, Mae Haru's patient list, and Mae Riul's way of accepting responsibility changed the final decision.

/story_contents/B031/actors/0/arc/0/summ.en:
In Act 1, K391 Mae Riul investigated recurring thawing in the Fourth Freezer Building and found scratches on the brass key and switched compressor number tags.

Following Dong Yesol's scale records, he confirmed that his past manipulation had distorted the current unsold-goods order.

At the same time, Mae Haru's antipyretic boxes were pushed into the contaminated zone, expanding personal guilt into actual harm to patients.

/story_contents/B031/actors/0/arc/1/summ.en:
In Act 2, K391 Mae Riul did not try to destroy the G15E16 Care-Circulation Body.

He combined syrup-food diversions, low-noise cooling, and time-based seals to create a temporary passage.

He asked Dong Yesol to accept losses of fresh food and Mae Haru to accept medicine delays, consuming his own authority to decide.

The more successful the test became, the greater the pressure to decide who would receive the Fourth Freezer Building.

/story_contents/B031/actors/0/arc/2/summ.en:
In Act 3, K391 Mae Riul could completely isolate the contaminated medicines and seal the freezer building to choose a stable ration network, or surrender some inventory.

He could instead open a negotiation passage for the Care-Circulation Body and choose night passage rights.

In the sealing branch, he kept unsold-goods authority but lost the long-term negotiation route; in the opening branch, he surrendered authority but gained a new route usable by Dong Yesol and Mae Haru.

Both branches were viable, and neither choice was fixed in advance.

/story_contents/B031/actors/0/outcomes/0.en:
In the sealing branch, K391 Mae Riul handed the brass key to Mae Haru and converted the Fourth Freezer Building into a medicine-priority storehouse.

She achieved stable cooling and clear contamination separation, but permanently blocked the night route used by the Care-Circulation Body.

She remained an unsold-goods appraiser and repaid the losses caused by her manipulation from each season's ration allotment.

/story_contents/B031/actors/0/outcomes/1.en:
In the opening branch, K391 Mae Riul measured the food diversion share on Dong Yesol's scale and traded passage time with the Care-Circulation Body under HP01 brokerage.

He gave up part of the frozen inventory and his unsold-goods authority, but secured both Mae Haru's medicine route and a civilian evacuation route.

He became a steward who did not own the Fourth Freezer Building and began a life unlike his past monopolistic judgment.

/story_contents/B031/actors/1/sections/정.en:
K416 Heung Miri was a Korean-descended contract-audit practitioner raised beside the water tanks of reconstructed apartments in southern Gangnam.

She had a precise eye for reading leaks not by the taste of water but by the tremor of pressure gauges and discoloration of sealing lead.

She believed numbers did not discriminate among people, but learned late that a contract's violence changed according to who entered those numbers.

/story_contents/B031/actors/1/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, K416 Heung Miri worked as a meter-reading data clerk for a waterworks subcontractor and processed discount applications for aging complexes.

She rounded actual pressure fluctuations to meet the averages demanded by her superior, allowing the company to avoid penalty payments.

After work, she collected discarded bronze pressure seals and stored them by date, a habit that later became a clue to tracing manipulation.

/story_contents/B031/actors/1/sections/가.en:
K416 Heung Miri belonged to the water-supply audit team of the Jeongdong General Labor Union, which followed HP10's contract discipline.

Her family had operated a laundry near the old Suseo rolling-stock depot, but scattered to different spheres after water rations were cut.

She lived on the audit team's drinking-water allocation in place of family, while hiding a bundle of bronze pressure seals as a private record and conflicting with community rules.

/story_contents/B031/actors/1/sections/붕.en:
K416 Heung Miri experienced the incident in which the G16E08 Blueprint-Ghost Machine Corps followed closed lines on old pipe drawings and repeatedly locked the valves of Suseo Reservoir No. 9.

Unable to open an uncontracted bypass pipe, she clung only to audit forms while patients on the lower floors became dehydrated.

Afterward, she made it a principle to lower noise, seal the cooling room, and divert the movement route through empty pipes rather than destroy the machine corps.

/story_contents/B031/actors/1/sections/생.en:
K416 Heung Miri learned through a discarded-drawing test that the G16E08 Blueprint-Ghost Machine Corps tracked blue blueprint lines before a current map.

She connected a false closed line to an acceptable empty reservoir, restored valve pressure, and designed the test drawing so removal would return conditions to normal.

From then on, she audited not only contract language but also the signs the machines followed and the actual flow of water.

/story_contents/B031/actors/1/sections/현.en:
K416 Heung Miri now compared pressure records and gate expiration dates as a water-contract audit assistant of the Jeongdong General Labor Union.

He supported Gwak Eunjae's audit forms, verified Beom Handeul's gate testimony, and swore date consistency with Tak Seon.

He had not yet decided whether to void or renew the Reservoir No. 9 contract, and the moment he placed the final lead seal, water rights across several spheres would be difficult to restore.

/story_contents/B031/actors/1/sections/비.en:
Just before the collapse, K416 Heung Miri entered the calibration date of Reservoir No. 9's pressure gauge ten days early on company orders.

Because of that false date, the failure alert was pushed outside the warranty range, Beom Handeul's gate did not open on time, and the G16E08 Blueprint-Ghost Machine Corps' repeated locks worsened.

He became an audit assistant while hiding the original bronze seal, carrying guilt that even Tak Seon's oath was bound to a false date.

/story_contents/B031/actors/1/sections/관.en:
K416 Heung Miri began a contractual relationship by calculating missing pressure cells for Gwak Eunjae when she took her first water-supply audit.

Although he knew that the gate expiration time remembered by Beom Handeul differed from his seal record, he supported his superior's chart at the time.

Tak Seon formed an oath that the three would never change a date again, but the promise remained incomplete because of Heung Miri's hidden original.

/story_contents/B031/actors/1/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, K416 Heung Miri revealed that the pressure drop at Reservoir No. 9 and his past manipulation of the calibration date lay on the same causal line.

In Act 2, he guided the machine corps into empty pipes using discarded drawings and aligned Gwak Eunjae's, Beom Handeul's, and Tak Seon's differing evidence along one timeline.

In Act 3, he had to choose whether to void the existing contract and redistribute water or preserve gate exchange through conditional renewal.

/story_contents/B031/actors/1/sections/분.en:
If K416 Heung Miri chose contract invalidation, she broke the manipulated audit system and sent water first to lower-floor spheres, but lost the charter city's guaranteed supplies.

If she chose conditional renewal, she had to hold the original seal in joint custody while trading machine-corps passage time and water distribution through HP02 brokerage.

The two endings demanded different costs in justice and continuity, and neither was scheduled before the final lead seal was placed.

/story_contents/B031/actors/1/arc/0/summ.en:
In Act 1, K416 Heung Miri found that the bronze pressure seal of Suseo Reservoir No. 9 and Gwak Eunjae's audit form differed by ten days.

Comparing Beom Handeul's gate memory with Tak Seon's date oath, he confirmed that his past false entry was the starting point of the present water stoppage.

As the pressure drop spread to the lower-floor clinic, the documentary error expanded into an immediate survival crisis.

/story_contents/B031/actors/1/arc/1/summ.en:
In Act 2, K416 Heung Miri made a discarded drawing for the G16E08 Blueprint-Ghost Machine Corps to follow and cooled an empty reservoir for a temporary movement route.

She combined noise suppression and compartment sealing while negotiating pipe-use time through HP02 brokerage.

The test restored water, but further intensified the conflict over whether to hold the original contract and manipulated seal in public custody or destroy them.

/story_contents/B031/actors/1/arc/2/summ.en:
In Act 3, K416 Heung Miri could void the existing contract to redistribute water chiefly to lower-floor spheres, or choose conditional renewal holding the original seal in joint custody and exchanging water for machine-corps passage time.

In the invalidation branch, he lost guaranteed supplies but broke the false system; in the renewal branch, he preserved compact resources but accepted continuing outside audit.

Both branches were possible according to the combination of consent from Gwak Eunjae, Beom Handeul, and Tak Seon, and no result was set beforehand.

/story_contents/B031/actors/1/outcomes/0.en:
In the invalidation branch, K416 Heung Miri cut the manipulated bronze seal and recalculated the Reservoir No. 9 contract from the beginning.

He restored water to the lower-floor patient sphere, but lost HP10's guaranteed filtering material and his audit position.

He became a field meter reader with Beom Handeul who recorded only actual pressure and bore responsibility for the numbers directly.

/story_contents/B031/actors/1/outcomes/1.en:
In the conditional-renewal branch, K416 Heung Miri placed the original seal in the dual vaults of Tak Seon and Gwak Eunjae, then concluded an HP02 brokerage contract.

He restricted the G16E08 Blueprint-Ghost Machine Corps' movement time to empty pipes and maintained water and passage together.

He remained an audit assistant, but had to obtain Beom Handeul's field confirmation for every calibration date and permanently relinquished sole decision authority.

/story_contents/B031/actors/2/sections/정.en:
K020 Jin Sebin was a Korean-descended emergency-transport commander raised in the rescue garage of the Yangcheon sluice zone.

He could read engine noise and water-level boards at once to calculate which embankment road would flood in a few minutes.

He tried to board every patient in the same order, but carried the wound that lives could not be chosen by rules alone before limited seats.

/story_contents/B031/actors/2/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, K020 Jin Sebin worked as a night dispatch chief at a private ambulance company, handling hospital transport for dialysis patients and mothers in labor.

When the company prioritized profitable long-distance transfers, he rang a blue triage bell and secretly called local emergency vehicles.

But he once hid the bell to avoid company discipline, and the name of the patient delayed that day continued to follow his judgment.

/story_contents/B031/actors/2/sections/가.en:
K020 Jin Sebin led the Water Compact's Yangcheon mobile medical-vehicle unit under HC04's medical-vehicle code.

The blue triage bell used by his mother was fixed beneath the driver's seat in the Sinjeong No. 2 Sluice garage and served as the unit's departure signal.

He treated drivers, stretcher crews, and sluice watchers as family more than kin, but was also suspected by the community because he held seat-allocation authority alone.

/story_contents/B031/actors/2/sections/붕.en:
K020 Jin Sebin left one patient behind during the incident in which the G17E05 Surveillance-Orbit Swarm tracked reflective markers and surrounded the medical-vehicle column at Sinjeong No. 2 Sluice Bridge.

He extinguished the marker lights and departed to save the many, but watched the blue blanket on the abandoned stretcher sink under water.

Afterward, he combined reflection blocks, low-noise travel, bait markers, detours, and negotiations over passage time rather than eliminate the orbit swarm.

/story_contents/B031/actors/2/sections/생.en:
K020 Jin Sebin learned that the G17E05 Surveillance-Orbit Swarm monitored repeated reflections from vehicle roofs and regular wheel vibrations before human body heat.

He put foil markers on a retired bus and sent it down an empty embankment road, while the real medical vehicles crossed the sluice under cloth covers and manual towing.

The response could be reversed by recovering the bait, and he thereafter trained route blocks and signal design rather than firepower.

/story_contents/B031/actors/2/sections/현.en:
K020 Jin Sebin now decided patient boarding order and sluice crossing times as head of the Yangcheon mobile medical-vehicle unit.

He enforced Im Bada's citizen water-right oath in the field and received patients into Yangcheon when Jin Hagyeom's dock blockade ran long.

He had not yet decided which convoy would receive the final fuel drum, and that choice would lead to the Act 3 decision to close or open the Second Sluice permanently.

/story_contents/B031/actors/2/sections/비.en:
To avoid company discipline in the past, K020 Jin Sebin hid the blue triage bell and deleted one uninsured dialysis patient from the official boarding list.

That patient's delayed death became the direct occasion for Im Bada's citizen water-right oath, though Im Bada did not know who made the deletion.

Jin Sebin felt the debt that the same list practice remained in current fuel allocation, and that every silence repeated another exclusion.

/story_contents/B031/actors/2/sections/관.en:
K020 Jin Sebin became the oath's enforcer when he stopped medical vehicles and boarded citizens on the day Im Bada lay before the sluice to defend water rights.

During Jin Hagyeom's dock blockade, he moved injured sailors into Yangcheon, but lost one route to exposure by the Surveillance-Orbit Swarm after pressing for the blockade to be lifted.

The three shared the aim of defending the sluice, but long clashed over whether to move water, patients, or dock defense first.

/story_contents/B031/actors/2/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, K020 Jin Sebin faced the fact that the old deleted patient list and current fuel-allocation chart used the same rule of exclusion.

In Act 2, he tested reflection-bait convoys and manual towing routes to satisfy Im Bada's water rights and Jin Hagyeom's need for a blockade together.

In Act 3, he had to decide whether to open the Second Sluice permanently as a medical passage or close it for dock defense and choose a decentralized clinic network.

/story_contents/B031/actors/2/sections/분.en:
If K020 Jin Sebin chose to open the sluice, he guaranteed large-scale patient transport and access to water, but had to sustain bait operations to avoid the Surveillance-Orbit Swarm.

If he chose to close the sluice, he stabilized the dock and embankment but had to dissolve the medical-vehicle unit and distribute fuel and personnel to fixed clinics in each sphere.

Neither ending was defined beforehand as a victory, and Im Bada's and Jin Hagyeom's priorities and remaining fuel changed the choice.

/story_contents/B031/actors/2/arc/0/summ.en:
In Act 1, K020 Jin Sebin found the old boarding ticket of the dialysis patient he had deleted inside the blue triage bell in the Sinjeong No. 2 Sluice garage.

He confirmed that uninsured refugees were also pushed back on the current list and realized that Im Bada's water-right oath conflicted with his dispatch rules.

As Jin Hagyeom's dock blockade extended, patient numbers and fuel shortages surged at once.

/story_contents/B031/actors/2/arc/1/summ.en:
In Act 2, K020 Jin Sebin operated reflective bait vehicles that led the G17E05 Surveillance-Orbit Swarm down empty embankment roads and manually towed medical vehicles covered in cloth.

He offered Im Bada medical time limits rather than a seat lottery, and requested a limited crossing window from Jin Hagyeom.

The plan saved patients but consumed bait fuel too, reducing the number of times the sluice could remain open to one final time.

/story_contents/B031/actors/2/arc/2/summ.en:
In Act 3, K020 Jin Sebin could use the last fuel to open the Second Sluice permanently as a medical passage, or close the sluice to defend the dock.

He could dissolve the medical-vehicle unit into a decentralized clinic network.

In the opening branch, he gained large-scale transport but assumed continuing bait risk; in the closing branch, he gained defensive stability but had to care for long-distance patients locally.

Both branches were viable according to whether Im Bada and Jin Hagyeom agreed, and neither was scheduled.

/story_contents/B031/actors/2/outcomes/0.en:
In the opening branch, K020 Jin Sebin rang the blue triage bell three times and launched a reflective bait convoy with the final fuel drum.

He made the Second Sluice a permanent passage for citizen water rights and medical transport, but had to command a detour operation himself with every Surveillance-Orbit Swarm cycle.

He adopted a boarding rule with no deletions and bound his seat-allocation authority to Im Bada's field verification.

/story_contents/B031/actors/2/outcomes/1.en:
In the closing branch, K020 Jin Sebin withdrew the medical vehicles behind Jin Hagyeom's dock defensive line and distributed the vehicles' fuel and equipment to fixed Yangcheon clinics.

He gave up large-scale transfer across the sluice but enabled every sphere to maintain dialysis and emergency childbirth itself.

He stepped down as unit chief and became a triage officer who remained beside the patients left behind.

/story_contents/B031/actors/3/sections/정.en:
K048 Je Munseok was a Korean-descended industrial-medicine medical chief raised in Guro's tool market and metalworking alleys.

He had the clinical sense to infer a workplace exposure source from the interval of coughs and the color of dust mixed in phlegm.

He believed treatment and production had to be preserved together, but constantly doubted whether decisions that returned people to the workplace were treatment or exploitation.

/story_contents/B031/actors/3/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, K048 Je Munseok managed lung examinations for welders and cutting workers at the Guro Industrial Health Clinic.

When firms tried to avoid industrial-accident judgments, he kept the original paper from portable spirometers separately, but wrote mild findings for some patients because of their livelihoods.

A copper-mesh filter box stood in his examination room, and the order in which it was used later became key evidence in a mass-exposure accident.

/story_contents/B031/actors/3/sections/가.en:
K048 Je Munseok was medical chief of the Guro dust clinic under HC07's Standards Alliance, managing protective gear and fitness-for-work judgments.

His family fled south in the first days of the collapse, but he remained in Guro to protect patient records and oxygen cylinders.

He regarded the clinic's copper-mesh intake shelf as the community's last line of safety, but had a history of lowering protection standards to meet production quotas.

/story_contents/B031/actors/3/sections/붕.en:
K048 Je Munseok lost patients in the oxygen room on the day the G02E01 Radio-Wave Crow Flock followed high-frequency emissions from faulty transmitters into the clinic vents.

He activated a high-output jammer to drive off the flock, but spread metal dust through the air as well and worsened the patients' breathing.

Afterward, he rejected annihilative response and combined low-output sound guidance, vent seals, and food diversion to a cooled empty factory.

/story_contents/B031/actors/3/sections/생.en:
K048 Je Munseok confirmed that the G02E01 Radio-Wave Crow Flock obsessed not over all radio waves but over irregular signals sparking from oxidized copper mesh.

He sent a steady signal through a clean antenna at an abandoned telephone exchange to turn the flock toward an empty plating factory, and sealed the clinic vents with wet fabric.

The test could be reversed by switching off transmission, and he learned disaster medicine that separated signals and exposure sources rather than killing.

/story_contents/B031/actors/3/sections/현.en:
K048 Je Munseok now judged patient work stoppages and priority release of protective gear as medical chief of the Guro dust clinic.

He matched Im Chowon's protective-gear releases to clinical figures and divided Geumcheon patient transport with Jin Wooram.

He had not yet decided whether to discard the copper-mesh filter box or preserve it as evidence, and that choice would determine both the clinic's closure and the Fabrication Alliance's production stoppage.

/story_contents/B031/actors/3/sections/비.en:
In the first year of the collapse, K048 Je Munseok heat-treated used copper-mesh filters and returned them to the shelves as new products to hide a shortage of protective gear.

The oxidized signals of reused filters drew the G02E01 Radio-Wave Crow Flock, and fine copper dust rapidly worsened the patients' lung damage.

Because he signed Im Chowon's release records as new products, he knew that truth's exposure could destroy not only the clinic but the Fabrication Alliance's protection credibility.

/story_contents/B031/actors/3/sections/관.en:
When Im Chowon first supplied protective suits, K048 Je Munseok reduced the release standard with her because there were more patients than actual sewn suits.

He built a night transport route by dividing the Geumcheon patients with Jin Wooram, but lost both their trust after once placing a critically ill person behind production-skilled workers.

The three cooperated to reduce dust damage, but saw production continuity, fair treatment, and regional admission limits differently.

/story_contents/B031/actors/3/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, K048 Je Munseok confirmed that copper particles from patients' lungs matched traces of oxidation on reused filters.

In Act 2, he borrowed Im Chowon's and Jin Wooram's resources to build low-output guiding antennas and clean isolation rooms, but faced pressure to halt production.

In Act 3, he had to choose whether to close the clinic for a full purge or preserve production through limited treatment and signal negotiations.

/story_contents/B031/actors/3/sections/분.en:
If K048 Je Munseok chose a full purge, he discarded every reused filter and cut off patient exposure, but the Standards Alliance's protective-gear production stopped for a season.

If he chose limited operation, he traded the G02E01 Radio-Wave Crow Flock's movement time through HC02 brokerage and preserved the copper-mesh filter box as both evidence and warning device.

The two endings allocated the speed of safety and the continuity of livelihoods differently, and neither was chosen automatically.

/story_contents/B031/actors/3/arc/0/summ.en:
In Act 1, K048 Je Munseok confirmed that copper crystals in a critical patient's phlegm and the oxidation layer in the clinic's filter box had the same composition.

He faced the fact that the quantity of new products on Im Chowon's release sheets exceeded actual production and that his signature had concealed the difference.

The same damage appeared in the Geumcheon patients under Jin Wooram's care, spreading the consequences of concealment across the whole region.

/story_contents/B031/actors/3/arc/1/summ.en:
In Act 2, K048 Je Munseok erected a low-output antenna that guided the G02E01 Radio-Wave Crow Flock to an abandoned plating factory.

He sealed the clinic vents with wet fabric and cooling plates.

He asked Im Chowon for new protective-gear production and Jin Wooram to disperse critically ill patients, continuing limited treatment.

But discarding the copper-mesh filter box would erase evidence of the cause, while preserving it increased the danger of calling the flock again.

/story_contents/B031/actors/3/arc/2/summ.en:
In Act 3, K048 Je Munseok could close the clinic.

He could discard every filter for a full purge, or preserve the filter box under shielding and continue limited operation by trading the G02E01 Radio-Wave Crow Flock's passage time through HC02 brokerage.

In the purge branch, he accepted a production stoppage and cut off exposure; in the limited-operation branch, he protected livelihoods but accepted constant signal control and outside inspection.

Both choices held realistic costs, and no ending was fixed beforehand.

/story_contents/B031/actors/3/outcomes/0.en:
In the full-purge branch, K048 Je Munseok sent the copper-mesh filter box to a sealed incinerator and closed the Guro dust clinic for a season.

He rebuilt protection standards with Im Chowon but accepted responsibility for the Fabrication Alliance's reduced production and ration cuts.

He stepped down as medical chief and became a dedicated physician tracking the patients' long-term lung function.

/story_contents/B031/actors/3/outcomes/1.en:
In the limited-operation branch, K048 Je Munseok preserved the filter box in a lead-shielded room and bound the G02E01 Radio-Wave Crow Flock's movement time to the empty plating factory through HC02 brokerage.

He divided patients with Jin Wooram and kept production and treatment running, but received approval from an independent inspector for every fitness-for-work judgment.

In exchange for losing authority, he continued field monitoring to prevent reused filters from circulating again.

/story_contents/B031/actors/4/sections/정.en:
K076 Jin Maru was a Korean-descended disaster-medical convoy commander raised in the emergency garage of the Magok research complex.

He excelled at regulating convoy speed by calculating drainage height, remaining power, and patient temperature together rather than roads alone.

He took pride in obeying orders exactly, but believed responsibility did not disappear even when he obeyed an order whose source was wrong.

/story_contents/B031/actors/4/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, K076 Jin Maru coordinated joint ambulance and decontamination-vehicle deployments on a chemical-accident response team in a research complex behind the airport.

He maintained an old dispatcher that entered detours by paper punch card to the end, saving people many times when communications failed.

But when automatic and handwritten orders conflicted, he prioritized the superior signal, and the habit led to a fatal misjudgment after the collapse.

/story_contents/B031/actors/4/sections/가.en:
K076 Jin Maru was the disaster-medical convoy leader of HC10, transporting isolated patients and medical samples for Yangjae Machineworks Company.

His blood relatives had disappeared, and he now cared for decontamination drivers, stretcher crews, and drainage scouts as family.

He kept the black punch-card cylinder of Magok Third Emergency Garage as a symbol of command, but it also contained cards for orders that had never existed.

/story_contents/B031/actors/4/sections/붕.en:
K076 Jin Maru experienced the incident in which the G14E13 Phantom Dispatch Corps mimicked the call sign of a closed control network and lured his convoy into the Balsan underpass.

Believing it was a superior order, he forced entry and lost decontamination and patient-transport vehicles in sudden flooding.

Afterward, he responded not by destroying the dispatch corps but by combining call-tone blocks, cooling-garage seals, empty-vehicle food diversions, and verified time-window trades.

/story_contents/B031/actors/4/sections/생.en:
K076 Jin Maru learned that the G14E13 Phantom Dispatch Corps did not know real-time positions but replayed only the repeating pattern of the route card it had last received.

He placed recoverable fake punch cards in an unmanned tow vehicle to guide the dispatch corps toward a retired runway, while the real convoy moved by handwritten signs.

The lesson could be reversed by replacing the cards and instilled in him the habit of verifying a route before obeying an order.

/story_contents/B031/actors/4/sections/현.en:
K076 Jin Maru now coordinated isolation release and departure declarations as Yangjae Machineworks Company's disaster-medical convoy leader.

She moved only when I Bomgyeol declared blockade release and convoy departure at once, and supported Jin Chaeon's refusal of dispatched treatment from the convoy side.

She had not yet decided whether to discard or reconnect the black punch-card cylinder, and that choice would irreversibly alter the garage's command system in Act 3.

/story_contents/B031/actors/4/sections/비.en:
Before the Balsan underpass accident, K076 Jin Maru discovered that the verification code attached to the phantom call was incorrect, but did not report it for fear of being held responsible for delaying departure.

She later removed that call card from the black cylinder and hid it, recording the cause of the accident as simple flooding.

I Bomgyeol and Jin Chaeon still did not know she had recognized the order's falsity, and current blockade procedure also depended on her incomplete record.

/story_contents/B031/actors/4/sections/관.en:
K076 Jin Maru had a past in which she missed the departure time on the day I Bomgyeol first lifted a research-building blockade and cared for exposed patients in the garage all night.

When Jin Chaeon refused a dangerous dispatched treatment, she prevented a punishment for disobedience, but the convoy then took on the medical gap.

The three agreed not to trust a sole order, but the call card Jin Maru hid left an old fracture in that agreement.

/story_contents/B031/actors/4/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, K076 Jin Maru confirmed that the missing number in the black cylinder matched the call from the Balsan underpass accident.

In Act 2, under I Bomgyeol's and Jin Chaeon's dual approval, she tested a fake punch-card convoy and restricted the Phantom Dispatch Corps' replay range.

In Act 3, she had to choose whether to sever the dispatch network completely and change to autonomous garages or reconnect only limited lines to maintain long-distance medical convoys.

/story_contents/B031/actors/4/sections/분.en:
If K076 Jin Maru chose to sever the dispatch network, he eliminated the danger of phantom calls but greatly lost the ability to transport long-distance patients beyond Magok.

If he chose limited reconnection, he supplied the G14E13 Phantom Dispatch Corps with empty-vehicle routes and passage time through HC14 brokerage while maintaining medical lines.

The two endings demanded different responsibilities between safe autonomy and a broad rescue range, and neither was scheduled.

/story_contents/B031/actors/4/arc/0/summ.en:
In Act 1, K076 Jin Maru found that one serial number was missing from the black punch-card cylinder.

She found that the number matched the call record from the Balsan underpass accident.

Comparing I Bomgyeol's blockade record with Jin Chaeon's time of refusing dispatch, she confirmed that she had departed even while suspecting a false order.

The same call sign appeared again in a new isolated-patient convoy, returning past concealment as a present immediate danger.

/story_contents/B031/actors/4/arc/1/summ.en:
In Act 2, K076 Jin Maru used the repeating pattern of the G14E13 Phantom Dispatch Corps to send an unmanned tow vehicle carrying fake punch cards to a retired runway.

She moved the real convoy only when I Bomgyeol's blockade release and Jin Chaeon's medical approval were confirmed together, then sealed the garage through cooling.

The test succeeded, but left the problem that preserving long-distance lines required reconnecting part of the dispatch network.

/story_contents/B031/actors/4/arc/2/summ.en:
In Act 3, K076 Jin Maru could completely separate the black cylinder and dispatch network to make each garage handle autonomous convoys, or reconnect only limited lines.

She could provide the Phantom Dispatch Corps empty-vehicle routes and time through HC14 brokerage.

In the severance branch, she blocked false orders but surrendered long-distance rescue; in the reconnection branch, she preserved rescue range but accepted repeating-interference danger and dual approval.

Both branches were viable according to I Bomgyeol's and Jin Chaeon's judgment, and no ending was fixed beforehand.

/story_contents/B031/actors/4/outcomes/0.en:
In the severance branch, K076 Jin Maru removed the drive shaft from the black punch-card cylinder and changed every Magok garage to an independent handwritten system.

He prevented phantom-call reintrusion but lost the ability to bring distant isolated patients in, so he had to distribute decontamination equipment to each region.

He stepped down as convoy leader and personally monitored water levels at the Balsan underpass where the accident occurred.

/story_contents/B031/actors/4/outcomes/1.en:
In the limited-reconnection branch, K076 Jin Maru installed a route-card device that could not operate without the dual keys of I Bomgyeol and Jin Chaeon.

She provided the G14E13 Phantom Dispatch Corps empty-vehicle routes on the retired runway through HC14 brokerage and maintained long-distance medical convoys.

She preserved command authority, but took on final responsibility for identifying false calls and the risk of failed interference at every departure.

/story_contents/B031/actors/5/sections/정.en:
K105 Myeong Woosol was a Korean-descended auctioneer raised in the ironworks alleys of Seongsu-dong, Seoul, who counted a maker's remaining time before an item's price.

He had maintained the allocation order of the Sermon Registry State through fast bids and exact hand signals.

Yet behind his reputation as a fair broker lay the stubbornness of needing to control every trade to feel secure.

/story_contents/B031/actors/5/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, K105 Myeong Woosol conducted industrial auctions at the Seongsu workshop market, bundling shelves, molds, and cutting oil from closed factories.

He announced the moment of award with the brass auction bell left by his father and personally sealed unsold lots in the night communal warehouse.

At the last normal auction, he arbitrarily raised the minimum price for cooling-plate bundles and blocked purchases by three small workshops.

/story_contents/B031/actors/5/sections/가.en:
K105 Myeong Woosol was connected to the HP07 artisan house line, but his current loyalty was to the Ttukseom Union Sermon Registry State.

He made Casting Building No. 3 of the Seongsu workshop market into an auction hall and communal ration station, managing production time, fuel, and passage rights on different bid sheets.

The union trusted his judgment but was wary of auction authority concentrating in one person.

/story_contents/B031/actors/5/sections/붕.en:
On the day the G20E09 Iron-Scale Colony crowded into the cooling-plate storehouse, K105 Myeong Woosol saw evacuation routes blocked by plates he had priced high and held back.

He beat the bell wildly to guide the colony toward the noise and led workers out through cutting-oil channels, but one caster badly injured a hand.

Afterward, he feared bell sounds while seeking to limit harm through cooling seals and food diversions rather than eliminate the colony.

/story_contents/B031/actors/5/sections/생.en:
After three past failures, K105 Myeong Woosol learned that the G20E09 Iron-Scale Colony followed the order of heat and vibration, not metal prices.

He made a reversible procedure combining retired cooling pipes, cloth seals, and low-frequency hammers to turn the colony toward an empty rolling room.

The learning could always be revised, but did not correct his hidden manipulation of the cooling-plate auction.

/story_contents/B031/actors/5/sections/현.en:
K105 Myeong Woosol now guarded Casting Building No. 3 as auctioneer of the Seongsu workshop market and allocator of passage times for the Sermon Registry State.

He executed Yu Haeun's skills blackboard in the actual auction order and divided opening times of sealed zones around Gu Doyeong's packing transport.

He had not yet decided whether to melt the brass auction bell into the cooling door or preserve it as collateral for an HP06 brokerage trade.

/story_contents/B031/actors/5/sections/비.en:
Just before the collapse, K105 Myeong Woosol manipulated the minimum price of cooling plates and rolled one page of the award record inside the brass auction bell.

Though he knew the shortage of plates had led to the colony's first nesting and a worker's injury, he excused it as a choice made to preserve market order.

If the record came to light, he would lose auction authority; if he continued to conceal it, the next cooling allocation would also begin from false inventory figures.

/story_contents/B031/actors/5/sections/관.en:
K105 Myeong Woosol promised not to drive skilled workers into danger zones when he transformed Yu Haeun's skills blackboard into an auction bid sheet.

With Gu Doyeong, he transported twenty-seven packing boxes beyond the Iron-Scale route in the first winter of the collapse and had aligned transport order with auction order ever since.

The two trusted Myeong Woosol's bell as a signal, but did not know it held a manipulated record.

/story_contents/B031/actors/5/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, K105 Myeong Woosol tracked the missing cooling-plate ledger and the colony's moving heat source, confirming that his past manipulation had worsened the current sealing failure.

In Act 2, he tested noise routes and passage times with Yu Haeun, Gu Doyeong, and the HP06 broker, learning that the brass bell's metal suited cooling-door repair.

Before Act 3, he had to choose whether to destroy auction power and evidence together or disclose the record and conclude a limited exchange with the colony.

/story_contents/B031/actors/5/sections/분.en:
K105 Myeong Woosol could meet two mutually irreversible endings in the cooling-door choice, but neither was predetermined.

In the bell-melting ending, he gave up auction authority and evidence of manipulation together and became the unpaid keeper of the casting building; in the record-disclosure ending, he remained the responsible auctioneer for an HP06 passage compact.

The first strengthened makers' self-rule and the second institutionalized resource exchange with the colony, but sacrifice and distrust remained in both.

/story_contents/B031/actors/5/arc/0/summ.en:
In Act 1, K105 Myeong Woosol received a complaint that the amount of cooling plates in Casting Building No. 3 did not match the area of the actual sealed wall.

Comparing Yu Haeun's skills blackboard with Gu Doyeong's transport table, he realized that the manipulated ledger hidden in the brass auction bell was the cause.

As the G20E09 Iron-Scale Colony spread into the rolling room leaking heat, his private secret expanded into a community passage crisis.

/story_contents/B031/actors/5/arc/1/summ.en:
In Act 2, K105 Myeong Woosol refused the demand to annihilate the colony.

He led a night test combining noise, cooling, food-diversion routes, and route blocks.

The HP06 broker proposed exchanging iron residue for passage time, while Yu Haeun made ledger disclosure a condition of negotiation.

The test succeeded, but completing the cooling door required melting the brass bell or extracting and publishing the record inside it.

/story_contents/B031/actors/5/arc/2/summ.en:
In Act 3, K105 Myeong Woosol could melt the brass auction bell to seal the cooling door.

He directly chose between a branch that also surrendered auction authority and a branch that preserved the bell, disclosed the manipulated record, and signed the HP06 resource-and-passage compact.

In the first branch, a makers' self-rule auction began and he became its keeper; in the second, he became a responsible auctioneer overseeing limited exchange with the colony.

Both endings were irreversible, neither branch was fixed before the choice, and annihilation of the colony was not the goal.

/story_contents/B031/actors/5/outcomes/0.en:
K105 Myeong Woosol melted the brass auction bell into cooling-door hinges in the melting branch, sealing the heat passage of the G20E09 Iron-Scale Colony. He permanently surrendered auction authority.

The hidden ledger was scorched by fire and weakened as legal evidence, but he acknowledged responsibility in public testimony.

The Seongsu workshop market began a rotating auction system, and Myeong Woosol remained an unnamed night keeper.

/story_contents/B031/actors/5/outcomes/1.en:
K105 Myeong Woosol preserved the brass auction bell, disclosed the ledger inside before Yu Haeun and Gu Doyeong, and signed an HP06-brokered resource-and-passage compact.

He managed iron-residue allotments and colony passage time through open bidding, but placed joint auditors over every award.

The market chose an uneasy coexistence, and Myeong Woosol lived as a responsible auctioneer with limited authority.

/story_contents/B031/actors/6/sections/정.en:
K134 Cha Yunmok was a Korean-descended emergency-transport worker raised in a redevelopment rental complex in eastern Seoul, calculating road width and a patient's breathing at once.

As leader of the eastern mobile medical-vehicle unit, she valued stretchers and handoffs on foot over vehicles.

She appeared firm about rules, but her habit of erasing failed routes from the map distorted her judgment.

/story_contents/B031/actors/6/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, K134 Cha Yunmok handled regular transport for dialysis and rehabilitation patients at a private ambulance-transfer firm.

She recorded alley slopes, elevator widths, and the positions of night barriers in a waterproof map tube behind the Amsa pump station.

Marking a neutral alley under construction as a safe route to meet operating targets became the beginning of a fatal debt.

/story_contents/B031/actors/6/sections/가.en:
K134 Cha Yunmok learned the discipline of HC08's medical-transport line and now led the eastern mobile medical-vehicle unit of the Gwangjin Line Escort Protection State.

The community held three vehicles and six stretchers linking the Amsa pump station, Godeok sluice gate, and alley clinic as common property.

He held dispatch priority, but could not maintain the operating network by disregarding Jang Sehwa's neutral compartment and Cha Naru's water-purification window.

/story_contents/B031/actors/6/sections/붕.en:
On the night the G16E06 Blueprint-Ghost Machine Corps repeated wrong drawing signals, K134 Cha Yunmok drove a medical vehicle into an alley where she had painted over a safety mark.

The vehicle was trapped between repeating false exits, and after slowing the machine corps' pursuit with cooling guns and manual barriers, she moved the patients onto stretchers.

After one patient's treatment was delayed, she separated routes with noise shielding and analog markers rather than breaking the machine corps.

/story_contents/B031/actors/6/sections/생.en:
K134 Cha Yunmok learned in a past simulated dispatch that the G16E06 Blueprint-Ghost Machine Corps did not create new roads but repeated the most frequently revised drawing layer.

She used chalk line, yellow cloth, and cooling magnets to guide the machine corps into empty drainage channels, while sealing the real patient route with paper strips.

The procedure was a lesson that could be changed again, but the false safety marks on the original map had not yet been removed.

/story_contents/B031/actors/6/sections/현.en:
K134 Cha Yunmok now approved dispatches between the Amsa pump-station garage and Godeok clinic as leader of the eastern mobile medical-vehicle unit.

He owed three free transfers for passage through Jang Sehwa's neutral compartment, and when Cha Naru's water-purification window closed, he sent stretchers through the alleys instead of vehicles.

He had not yet decided whether to burn the original drawings and surrender his license or plant corrected drawings in the machine corps to bind operations.

/story_contents/B031/actors/6/sections/비.en:
Before the collapse, K134 Cha Yunmok erased construction marks and registered Jang Sehwa's neutral alley as an official detour to meet operating targets.

As the G16E06 Blueprint-Ghost Machine Corps repeatedly copied that revision layer, the current network of false exits grew and rescue delays followed in chains.

He described the debt he owed Jang Sehwa as a mere passage fee, but it also included the price of asking her to remain silent about the manipulation.

/story_contents/B031/actors/6/sections/관.en:
On the day Jang Sehwa evacuated residents from the neutral compartment, K134 Cha Yunmok broke rules to drive a medical vehicle inside and promised free transfers in the future as payment.

With Cha Naru, he shared the experience of removing stretcher wheels and carrying patients over water-channel railings in the first winter when the Godeok water-purification window froze.

Both knew of the original waterproof map tube, but neither knew Cha Yunmok had manipulated the safety marks.

/story_contents/B031/actors/6/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, K134 Cha Yunmok revealed that the false rescue requests causing repeat dispatches arose from his own revised drawing layer.

In Act 2, with Jang Sehwa's and Cha Naru's help, he made paper-marker routes and allocated cooling time and empty drainage channels to the machine corps through HP02 brokerage.

Before Act 3, he had to choose whether to destroy the original and choose an independent walking network or permanently enter corrected drawings into the machine corps and bind the community to scheduled operations.

/story_contents/B031/actors/6/sections/분.en:
K134 Cha Yunmok could choose one of two endings around the waterproof map tube, but neither was scheduled at present.

In the ending where he burned the original, vehicle licenses and the eastern trunk route disappeared but an autonomous alley-by-alley stretcher network arose; in the ending where he planted corrected drawings, a stable medical-train schedule and the machine corps' passage rights were fixed together.

The first made him repay Jang Sehwa's debt through labor, while the second subordinated Cha Naru's water-purification window to the machine schedule.

/story_contents/B031/actors/6/arc/0/summ.en:
In Act 1, K134 Cha Yunmok followed rescue calls that rang three times under the same patient number and found the medical vehicle circling around the Amsa pump station.

Opening the waterproof map tube, she confirmed that the construction alley she had painted over had become the repeated route of the G16E06 Blueprint-Ghost Machine Corps.

As false dispatches delayed Cha Naru's water delivery, her record manipulation spread into a ration crisis for the whole waterworks unit.

/story_contents/B031/actors/6/arc/1/summ.en:
In Act 2, K134 Cha Yunmok revealed the manipulation to Jang Sehwa and separated vehicle routes from the machine corps' route using paper strips, chalk lines, and cooling magnets.

A test allocating empty drainage-channel passage time and bundles of discarded drawings to the machine corps under HP02 brokerage succeeded, but the original revision layer continued to be copied.

A permanent solution required burning the waterproof map tube or planting corrected drawings in the machine corps' core panel.

/story_contents/B031/actors/6/arc/2/summ.en:
In Act 3, K134 Cha Yunmok could burn the waterproof map tube.

She chose between a branch that surrendered her driving license and eastern trunk-route rights to open an autonomous stretcher network, and a branch that permanently entered corrected drawings into the core panel to combine scheduled medical operations with the machine corps' passage rights.

In the first branch, she repaid her debt as an alley carrier; in the second, even Cha Naru's water-purification window was incorporated into the fixed schedule.

Both outcomes were irreversible but undetermined until the choice, and no ending exterminated the machine corps.

/story_contents/B031/actors/6/outcomes/0.en:
K134 Cha Yunmok burned the waterproof map tube, severed the revision layer copied by the G16E06 Blueprint-Ghost Machine Corps, and permanently surrendered his eastern vehicle license.

The Escort Protection State made alley-by-alley stretcher associations instead of a vehicle trunk route, with Jang Sehwa taking priority over the neutral passage.

Cha Yunmok directly carried Cha Naru's water containers and patient stretchers, repaying his remaining debt through labor.

/story_contents/B031/actors/6/outcomes/1.en:
K134 Cha Yunmok entered corrected drawings into the machine corps' core panel, binding the times of medical vehicles, water delivery, and empty drainage channels into one fixed operating schedule.

The G16E06 Blueprint-Ghost Machine Corps passed only during allocated times, but Cha Naru's window and Jang Sehwa's neutral compartment also became difficult to close at will.

Cha Yunmok remained responsible for the schedule for life, bearing both stability and the loss of autonomy.

/story_contents/B031/actors/7/sections/정.en:
K091 I Juntaek was a third-generation Koryo-saram born in Chirchiq, Tashkent Region, Uzbekistan, with a family history from the generation of grandparents deported from Primorsky Krai in 1937.

He spoke Russian at home, learned old Koryo-mar words from his grandmother, and after migrating to Korea learned factory Korean and maintenance terminology.

At Gunja Depot, he was a vehicle mechanic trusted for thread standards and welding traces rather than accent.

/story_contents/B031/actors/7/sections/붕.en:
K091 I Juntaek repaired small-bus axles in Chirchiq before coming to Korea on an employment visa in 2014, settling at a Gunja rolling-stock depot subcontractor after working in an Ansan parts factory.

He used Russian toolboxes with Korean torque wrenches and reworked scrapped-car parts to pay for family remittances and residence costs.

Just before the collapse, he was testing a personally designed compatibility adapter linking Cheonwang vehicles and Gunja tow trucks.

/story_contents/B031/actors/7/sections/가.en:
K091 I Juntaek operated the Gunja Depot vehicle workshop under HC04's brokerage protection and the Ttukseom Union Sermon Registry State.

The blue toolbox sent by his sister Elena in Chirchiq served as a family heirloom and storage case for the workshop's standard originals.

He kept Jeong Siwoo's Cheonwang compatibility chart and wheel contract, while competing with Park Hayul over Godeok railway standards and leadership.

/story_contents/B031/actors/7/sections/붕.en:
On the day the G04E11 Sewer-Raccoon Pack raided food containers in the Gunja drainage tunnel, K091 I Juntaek saw his incomplete adapter throw a transport cart wheel.

Spilled dry food drew the raccoon pack into the workshop, and he separated people from parts through coolant spray, noise lures, and wire-mesh seals.

Afterward, he responded through food diversions and passage-time trades rather than hunting the pack, but hid responsibility for the failed test.

/story_contents/B031/actors/7/sections/생.en:
K091 I Juntaek learned through past tunnel observations that the G04E11 Sewer-Raccoon Pack chose routes by oil-stained cloth and grain smells rather than engine sound.

He sealed cleaning cloth, placed boxes of discarded grain in a diversion channel, and stopped cooling fans during wheel movement to make a reversible operating method.

The learning reduced clashes, but cracks in the failed adapter and the false test sheet remained in the blue toolbox.

/story_contents/B031/actors/7/sections/현.en:
K091 I Juntaek now decided the use order of four tow trucks and one wheel lathe as Gunja Depot's vehicle mechanic.

He had to renew a Cheonwang compatibility-chart contract with Jeong Siwoo and confronted Park Hayul over whether Gunja vehicle or Godeok rail standards would be adopted as the eastern standard.

He had not yet decided whether to disclose the dual standard and surrender design priority or retain the Gunja standard and conclude a seasonal passage compact with the Sewer-Raccoon Pack.

/story_contents/B031/actors/7/sections/비.en:
Hurrying residence renewal and performance pay, K091 I Juntaek skipped crack inspection on a prototype that converted Chirchiq-style threads and stamped it as passed.

When the adapter broke, food containers spilled into the drainage tunnel and the G04E11 Sewer-Raccoon Pack learned vehicle movements, turning maintenance competition into a survival problem.

He reported the cause to Jeong Siwoo as an aging axle and hid the true test piece and Russian work log under the blue toolbox's bottom panel.

/story_contents/B031/actors/7/sections/관.en:
K091 I Juntaek made a compatibility chart with Jeong Siwoo to fit Cheonwang wheels onto Gunja tow trucks and established a contract under which different workshops shared parts.

With Park Hayul, he saved bearings of a Godeok patrol train in the first year of the collapse, but they came to compete over whether vehicle or railway standards should become the eastern standard.

Park Hayul respected Juntaek's Russian dimension chart, but did not know the link between the false pass stamp and the food-container accident.

/story_contents/B031/actors/7/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, K091 I Juntaek compared wheel tracks left in the drainage tunnel with test pieces in the blue toolbox and confirmed that the raccoon-pack intrusion began with his adapter accident.

In Act 2, he tested an open dual adapter fitting both vehicles and railways, with Jeong Siwoo, Park Hayul, and the HC04 broker, alongside seasonal food-diversion routes.

Before Act 3, he had to choose whether to release the design into joint ownership and lose workshop priority or retain the Gunja standard and trade limited tunnel passage rights.

/story_contents/B031/actors/7/sections/분.en:
K091 I Juntaek divided into two endings according to how he handled the original dimension chart in the blue toolbox, and neither was fixed.

In the public ending, the dual adapter became a shared eastern standard and he lost patent and maintenance priority, but the tow network expanded.

In the limited ending, the Gunja standard remained and seasonal tunnels and food boxes were allocated to the Sewer-Raccoon Pack, while the Cheonwang contract shrank.

/story_contents/B031/actors/7/arc/0/summ.en:
In Act 1, when Gunja tow-truck wheels repeatedly came off in the drainage tunnel, K091 I Juntaek took out the cracked test piece in the blue toolbox again.

He confirmed that the G04E11 Sewer-Raccoon Pack's movement traces led back to the food-container accident before the collapse and that the false pass sheet was the cause.

As Jeong Siwoo demanded even Cheonwang wheels be recovered, a lie born from personal residence insecurity expanded into a crisis that could stop the whole eastern vehicle network.

/story_contents/B031/actors/7/arc/1/summ.en:
In Act 2, K091 I Juntaek overlaid Park Hayul's railway dimensions with his own vehicle dimensions to make an open dual adapter.

He tested a tunnel-time trade under HC04 brokerage.

When oil cloth was sealed and discarded-grain boxes were placed in a diversion channel, the G04E11 Sewer-Raccoon Pack avoided maintenance time, but ownership of the shared standard became a problem.

Jeong Siwoo demanded disclosure of the original, while Gunja workers argued that preserving an exclusive standard was necessary to keep their ration share.

/story_contents/B031/actors/7/arc/2/summ.en:
In Act 3, K091 I Juntaek could disclose the original dimension chart and false test sheet and turn the dual adapter into joint ownership.

He chose between a branch that surrendered Gunja priority and a branch that retained the Gunja standard while permanently allocating seasonal tunnels and food boxes to the Sewer-Raccoon Pack.

In the first branch, the eastern tow network was integrated and he became a traveling teacher; in the second, the Cheonwang contract shrank and he remained Gunja's tunnel manager.

Both branches were irreversible but undetermined before choice, and neither included killing the raccoon pack.

/story_contents/B031/actors/7/outcomes/0.en:
K091 I Juntaek disclosed the Russian work log and false pass sheet from the blue toolbox and turned the dual-adapter design over to Gunja-Godeok joint ownership.

He lost maintenance priority and exclusive income, but enabled Jeong Siwoo and Park Hayul to repair vehicles and trains under the same standard.

Juntaek thereafter became a traveling maintenance teacher teaching Korean and Russian dimension charts together.

/story_contents/B031/actors/7/outcomes/1.en:
K091 I Juntaek retained the Gunja vehicle standard and permanently allocated rainy-season tunnels, discarded-grain boxes, and quiet periods to the G04E11 Sewer-Raccoon Pack through HC04 brokerage.

Jeong Siwoo's Cheonwang contract shrank and separated from Park Hayul's railway standard, but Gunja tow trucks continued independent operation.

After disclosing responsibility for the accident, Juntaek remained not a competitor but the resident manager of the boundary tunnel.

/story_contents/B031/actors/8/sections/정.en:
K120 Park Hayul was a fourth-generation Koryo-saram born in Kyzylorda, Kazakhstan, and raised in Almaty, who learned the family memory of Central Asian forced deportation from the generation of great-grandparents through family documents.

She used Russian as her main language, learned Kazakh in markets, and after migrating to Korea learned railway electrical terms and honorific speech at night school.

At Godeok Depot, she was recognized as a train mechanic who read signal waveforms before accents.

/story_contents/B031/actors/8/sections/붕.en:
K120 Park Hayul repaired signal relays at a tram depot outside Almaty before coming to Korea for family residence with an aunt who migrated through marriage in 2007.
