After work at an Ansan plating factory and a Guro rail subcontractor, she joined the Godeok Depot train-maintenance crew and regularly delivered medicines to her parents instead of sending remittances.

In an old red insulating bag, she kept Kazakhstan tram circuit diagrams beside coil samples from Korean patrol trains.

/story_contents/B031/actors/8/sections/가.en:
K120 Park Hayul led the Godeok Depot train workshop of the Gwangjin Line Escort Protection State under HP08's technical guarantee.

She tied Han Bora's patrol train to dispatch order and guarded the water-purification line and track boundary together, while competing with I Juntaek's Gunja vehicle standard for the eastern standard.

The community depended on her signal skills, but worried that a choice to prioritize outside communications could endanger water supply.

/story_contents/B031/actors/8/sections/붕.en:
On the day the G21E08 Communication-Root Fungal Bodies spread through corroded signal coils, K120 Park Hayul experienced an accident in which patrol-train stop orders and water-supply alarms exchanged places.

She confined the fungal threads to one platform with cooling salt bags and fiber-optic sealing tubes, and put Han Bora in charge of hand-signal operation to avoid a collision.

Afterward, she did not burn the fungal bodies but allocated limited communication time and nutrient coverings, while hiding an incorrect coil-inspection record.

/story_contents/B031/actors/8/sections/생.en:
K120 Park Hayul learned through a past isolation test that the G21E08 Communication-Root Fungal Bodies did not imitate every signal blindly but remembered repeated waveforms on damp copper wire.

She cooled the tracks, installed read-only optical lines, and separately sealed an abandoned relay box where fungal threads could remain, creating a reversible operating method.

The learning restored communications, but did not erase responsibility for the corroded coil and missing inspection form in the red insulating bag.

/story_contents/B031/actors/8/sections/현.en:
K120 Park Hayul now adjusted priority among patrol-train dispatches, signal coils, and water-line alarms as Godeok Depot's train mechanic.

She bound dispatch order with Han Bora by contract and competed with I Juntaek over whether Gunja vehicle or Godeok rail standards would become the eastern standard.

She had not yet decided whether to sever fungal relays and return to manual railways or share limited communication time with the fungal bodies.

/story_contents/B031/actors/8/sections/비.en:
Just before the collapse, K120 Park Hayul recorded a corroded signal coil as replaced and hid the defective part in the red insulating bag to advance delivery of medicines to her parents.

As the G21E08 Communication-Root Fungal Bodies absorbed the coil's repeated waveform, stop orders and water-supply alarms became entangled and competition over patrol-train dispatch intensified.

She claimed I Juntaek's standard interference was the cause, but her signature remained on the actual missing inspection form.

/story_contents/B031/actors/8/sections/관.en:
K120 Park Hayul once exchanged bearings of a Godeok patrol train with I Juntaek through the night, matching Russian dimensions with Korean part names on one table.

With Han Bora, she delayed patrol-train dispatch during the first water raid to let water-purification vehicles pass first, then fixed the train order through a joint contract.

The two knew Hayul's red insulating bag only as an old object from home, and had not seen the defective coil and missing inspection form within it.

/story_contents/B031/actors/8/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, K120 Park Hayul confirmed that the waveform of the switched water-supply alarm matched the corroded coil she had hidden and realized Han Bora's patrol contract was in danger.

In Act 2, she used I Juntaek's shielding parts and HP07 brokerage to test both manual signal lines and limited fungal relay lines.

Before Act 3, she had to choose whether to sever the relay line permanently and surrender long-distance communications or grant time slots to the fungal threads and recognize them as part of the communication network.

/story_contents/B031/actors/8/sections/분.en:
K120 Park Hayul faced two endings according to whether she pulled the cut lever or opened the sealed slots of the Godeok signal tower, but neither was scheduled.

In the cutting ending, long-distance alarms were lost but the hand-signal patrol railway became independent; in the slot ending, communications remained but the fungal bodies became formal resource-allocation actors.

The first expanded Han Bora's field authority, while the second ended competition with I Juntaek but eliminated Godeok's exclusive communication rights.

/story_contents/B031/actors/8/arc/0/summ.en:
In Act 1, K120 Park Hayul investigated an accident in which a patrol-train stop signal became a water-supply opening order and found a waveform identical to the corroded coil in the red insulating bag.

The G21E08 Communication-Root Fungal Bodies had expanded along the missing inspection section, contaminating even Han Bora's dispatch contract.

Hayul's concealment for family medicine delivery grew into a crisis that shook both Godeok water rations and eastern standard competition.

/story_contents/B031/actors/8/arc/1/summ.en:
In Act 2, K120 Park Hayul used shielding rings made by I Juntaek, cooling salt bags, and read-only optical lines to test two kinds of signal network.

When she allocated nutrient coverings from an abandoned relay box and night communication time to the fungal bodies under HP07 brokerage, alarm confusion fell, but a dispute arose over recognizing the fungal threads as public communicators.

Han Bora prepared manual operations, while Hayul disclosed the defective-coil inspection sheet and could no longer shift responsibility to competitors.

/story_contents/B031/actors/8/arc/2/summ.en:
In Act 3, K120 Park Hayul could permanently sever the relay line of Godeok signal tower and surrender long-distance communications.

She chose between a branch that established a hand-signal railway and a branch that opened sealed slots to grant the G21E08 Communication-Root Fungal Bodies limited communication time and resource shares.

In the first branch, Han Bora gained field operating rights and Hayul became a track signaler; in the second, an eastern shared communication standard emerged and Hayul remained an audit technician.

No branch was fixed before choice, and extermination of the fungal bodies was not adopted as a solution.

/story_contents/B031/actors/8/outcomes/0.en:
K120 Park Hayul permanently severed the relay line of the Godeok signal tower, cutting both the repeated waveform of the G21E08 Communication-Root Fungal Bodies and long-distance alarms.

Han Bora commanded a hand-signal patrol railway using flags and lamps, and every water station received an independent alarm keeper.

Hayul stepped down from the workshop title and remained a signaler walking the tracks herself, preserving slow but autonomous operations.

/story_contents/B032/actors/0/sections/정.en:
K163 Chu Seoyun was a records clerk of Korean origin who had trained in the repair administration of Seoul Station's west side before the collapse, and he understood water not as private property but as a right of survival apportioned by documents.

He valued accreditation procedure and the order of testimony over numbers, but he had already dropped the naive belief that records protected the weak automatically.

For now he kept only his standing as a witness, without signing any contract as final.

/story_contents/B032/actors/0/sections/붕.en:
K163 Chu Seoyun had been a junior examiner in the waterworks contract office under the city hall, matching the unit-price tables of private water suppliers against the rights to use emergency reservoirs.

Just before the collapse he found that the leak report on the western intake gate had been deliberately understated, but the administrative network went down before a formal audit could open.

He still kept the accreditation stamp he had held back then, and he believed he could review that judgment again.

/story_contents/B032/actors/0/sections/가.en:
K163 Chu Seoyun worked under HC05's protection at the Seoul Station Central of the Republic of Korea Government as a witness to accreditation claims on water contracts, and he managed the Records Bureau's ration documents and the markings of the outer reservoirs together.

More than any blood house, he took as his own community the oral-claim gatherings of refugees who could not read documents.

When HC05 tried to narrow the scope of testimony in the name of order, he used the internal procedure to resist rather than abandon his affiliation.

/story_contents/B032/actors/0/sections/붕.en:
K163 Chu Seoyun was caught between the blame that the contract he had held back delayed supply to the western shelter at the first cutoff, and the counter-argument that contaminated water would have flowed even if the contract had passed.

He wrote the names of the people who died waiting for the water roster that day into the margins of the documents, but he showed them to no one.

The wound remained as guilt over the time he spent deferring a judgment, more than over any heroic decision.

/story_contents/B032/actors/0/sections/생.en:
K163 Chu Seoyun found, at the closed intake gate after the collapse, that the movement of G06E02 Migratory Wetland Predator Swarm locked to the cooling cycle of the water mains, and he got people out by noise and route blocking.

He did not hand the original contract to the Records Bureau then; he sealed it separately, but he could return the seal or put it to a public review and undo the choice.

So the fork of that time was already a past event, but its effect was still reversible.

/story_contents/B032/actors/0/sections/현.en:
K163 Chu Seoyun was summoned to the witness seat for accreditation claims on water contracts of the Republic of Korea Government, and he was treated as the only field clerk who could confirm the authenticity of the original.

O Seoyul's notarization claim and Han Jaemok's western draft demanded different standards of apportionment, so he had not yet given effect to either document.

He was just short of choosing one among a public reading, a contract rejection, and an ecological passage-right annotation.

/story_contents/B032/actors/0/sections/비.en:
K163 Chu Seoyun was hiding not only the original showing that the leak figures for the western intake gate had been falsified, but also the annex bearing his own hold mark.

He had sworn to O Seoyul that he would carry the notarization procedure through to the end, and he had sworn to Han Jaemok that he would read the western draft exactly as written, and the two promises collided.

He also remembered the debt that a refugee party starved because of the food he abandoned to lure G06E02 Migratory Wetland Predator Swarm.

/story_contents/B032/actors/0/sections/관.en:
K163 Chu Seoyun had a past in which he backed K148 O Seoyul's notarization claim from the first witness seat and caught one forged seal with her.

With K001 Han Jaemok he read the western draft under a lamp on the third day of the cutoff, and they jointly inserted the objection wording of illiterate refugees.

The two relationships were oaths bound to different principles of record rather than to personal loyalty, so they were hard to satisfy at the same time in this accreditation.

/story_contents/B032/actors/0/sections/3.en:
K163 Chu Seoyun, in Act 1, compared the sealed original with the ration status and revealed that the falsified leak and the passage times of G06E02 Migratory Wetland Predator Swarm had been deleted from the same ledger.

In Act 2 he proved that neither O Seoyul's notarization draft nor Han Jaemok's western draft could guarantee the right of survival on its own, and he made the public review stand.

In Act 3 he completed every branch — accreditation, rejection, and a conditional contract with a provisional ration and an ecological passage right attached — as endings with different legal effect.

/story_contents/B032/actors/0/sections/분.en:
K163 Chu Seoyun, in the accreditation branch, forced a leak-compensation clause into the text, stamped it, and remained as an inspector of the Records Bureau, but he accepted the western community's distrust.

In the rejection branch he posted the original on the reservoir wall, founded a seasonal water-ticket court, and lost his witness post to become the residents' claims officer instead.

In the conditional branch he built, through HC06's brokering, a wetland-boundary compact that traded the passage times of G06E02 Migratory Wetland Predator Swarm against human water-drawing times.

/story_contents/B032/actors/0/arc/0/summ.en:
K163 Chu Seoyun took out the sealed original of the water contract, compared it with the copy held by the Republic of Korea Government, and found the seasonal-movement marks of G06E02 Migratory Wetland Predator Swarm beside the deleted leak figures.

He demanded of K148 O Seoyul that the notarization claim be filed in public, and he had K001 Han Jaemok fill out the survivor roll of the western draft.

He did not yet decide on accreditation; he fixed only the scope of access to the evidence.

/story_contents/B032/actors/0/arc/1/summ.en:
K163 Chu Seoyun cooled the water mains and then set a noise device in the channel on the far side, so that he did not kill G06E02 Migratory Wetland Predator Swarm.

He blocked access to the hearing hall.

He put the company representative and the western refugees into the same hearing procedure, and he submitted as evidence even the annex he had held back.

As a result the stamp regained its effect, but which contract it would fall on remained a choice.

/story_contents/B032/actors/0/arc/2/summ.en:
K163 Chu Seoyun accredited, in branch A, the contract with the compensation clause inserted, and in branch B he rejected the contract and set up a seasonal water-ticket court.

In branch C he concluded, through HC06's brokering, a conditional compact trading the passage times of G06E02 Migratory Wetland Predator Swarm against the intake times.

In all three branches O Seoyul's notarization, Han Jaemok's draft, and his own hold responsibility came out as different legal results.

/story_contents/B032/actors/0/outcomes/0.en:
K163 Chu Seoyun inserted leak compensation and a free minimum water allotment into the body of the contract, and then he stamped the accreditation.

He became HC05's standing inspector and gained the authority to seize the company ledgers, but he grew distant from the western residents who had wanted the contract itself scrapped.

The route of G06E02 Migratory Wetland Predator Swarm was protected by the cooling timetable.

/story_contents/B032/actors/0/outcomes/1.en:
K163 Chu Seoyun rejected the contract and posted the original and his own held-back annex permanently on the outer wall of the reservoir.

He lost his post at the Records Bureau and became instead the first claims officer of a water-ticket court in which a residents' jury reviewed the grounds of each season's ration.

O Seoyul notarized the procedure, and Han Jaemok turned the western draft into the court's rules.

/story_contents/B032/actors/0/outcomes/2.en:
K163 Chu Seoyun chose, under HC06's brokering, a conditional contract that traded human intake times against the passage times of G06E02 Migratory Wetland Predator Swarm.

He gained dominion over no organization; he became the independent keeper of the boundary marks and renewed the contract's effect every month.

He left a reversibility clause so that, if the compact broke, the matter could return to the original rejection procedure.

/story_contents/B032/actors/1/sections/정.en:
K188 Sun Gaon was a clinical-logistics technician of Korean origin who had kept the intake records of medical equipment at a railway hospital before the collapse, and he judged the boundary between treatment tools and weapons not by purpose of use but by structure and power records.

He was not a doctor who treated patients directly, but he remembered the placement of equipment in the medical car and its sealing rules more exactly than anyone.

For now he had not chosen under which trial standard he would submit what he had witnessed.

/story_contents/B032/actors/1/sections/붕.en:
K188 Sun Gaon inspected the oxygen cylinders, defibrillators, and refrigerated medicines of the night medical train, and matched each car's power consumption against the hand-off signatures.

Just before the collapse he found traces that an item declared as a high-voltage device for treatment had been modified to restrain people, but he could not demand that the run be stopped.

The provisional approval slip of that time still allowed a cancellation filing, so his past judgment could still be undone procedurally.

/story_contents/B032/actors/1/sections/가.en:
K188 Sun Gaon lived with the crew survivors' association that kept the medical-convoy neutrality rules of the Wangsimni Union of the Line Succession State, while remaining under HC11.

The community was split between a faction that wanted to militarize the train and a faction that wanted every medical device scrapped, and he stayed on as the records keeper who proved each piece of equipment's use.

More than blood kin, he counted as family the crew members who had signed the patient hand-off sheets with him.

/story_contents/B032/actors/1/sections/붕.en:
K188 Sun Gaon saw, on the night the modified device fired, patients and guards burned together inside the medical car, and he saved the recording terminal before he cut the power.

Unsure whether that delay had enlarged the harm, he checked the time of the incident over and over, down to the second.

Fearing he would come to treat the bodies of the survivors as evidence alone, he demanded a strict consent procedure for any direct physical verification.

/story_contents/B032/actors/1/sections/생.en:
K188 Sun Gaon pulled the battery from the device in question just before the derailment, fixed the evidence bundle as the custody, battery, parts, snapshot, network, and fixed-body entries of the F16 standard, and carried it out.

He did not hand that bundle to a military trial; he sealed it in the neutral medical car, but he entrusted two keys separately so that the seal could be cancelled and the bundle re-verified.

So the fork at the time of survival had happened in the past, but the attribution and interpretation of the evidence were still reversible.

Then he confirmed that G07E10 Electrolyte-Burn Swarm shifted its movement route in response to the cooling bulkhead and the spent-electrolyte bypass barrel, and this trial remained a reversible lesson that could be restored to its original state if the seal was lifted.

/story_contents/B032/actors/1/sections/현.en:
K188 Sun Gaon was protected as a witness to the weapon on the medical train of the Line Succession State, and he held the key testimony for judging whether the device was treatment equipment or an illegal restraint weapon.

Jang Sehwa's medical-convoy neutrality draft, Cha Homin's window-clinic lockdown time, and Hong Woochan's waveform analysis each demanded a different place of submission.

He was before deciding where to use the evidence first: the medical court, the railway safety review, or the passage negotiation with the Electrolyte-Burn Swarm.

/story_contents/B032/actors/1/sections/비.en:
K188 Sun Gaon was hiding that his own provisional approval number remained in the battery entry of the F16 record, and that one snapshot had been taken not just before an actual firing but during a test run.

He had sworn to Jang Sehwa that he would keep his neutrality, and he had promised Cha Homin and Hong Woochan that he would not damage their respective visual materials.

He carried at once, as a debt, the chance that incomplete evidence would punish an innocent fitter and the risk of leaving the device in place.

/story_contents/B032/actors/1/sections/관.en:
K188 Sun Gaon had a past in which he backed K296 Jang Sehwa's medical-convoy neutrality with testimony and separated the patient roll from the military conscription table at the checkpoint.

With K177 Cha Homin he matched the window-clinic lockdown time against the record of the train's power cut, and with K242 Hong Woochan he laid the time the medical car was found over the stored waveform and restored the order in which the device ran.

The three relationships dealt with the same incident, but each held a different axis of evidence: ethics, sight, and physical signal.

/story_contents/B032/actors/1/sections/3.en:
K188 Sun Gaon, in Act 1, re-verified the six entries of F16 — custody, battery, parts, snapshot, network, and fixed body — and separated the party that modified the device from the person who actually fired it.

In Act 2 he drew G07E10 Electrolyte-Burn Swarm off with the cooling bulkhead and a salt-bait bypass, preserved the sealed medical car, and prepared a public reconstruction.

In Act 3 he completed every branch, including dismantling the device and converting it to a treatment machine, an evidence-preserving safety trial, and a passage trade through HC07.

/story_contents/B032/actors/1/sections/분.en:
K188 Sun Gaon, in the treatment-machine conversion branch, dismantled the weapon's accumulator, fixed it as a power supply for burn treatment, and became a railway safety inspector.

In the safety-trial branch he reproduced only the waveform and the fixed position without operating the device, identified the person actually responsible for the modification, and remained as keeper of the evidence store.

In the negotiation branch he secured passage times for the medical train, through HC07's brokering, in exchange for supplying spent electrolyte to G07E10 Electrolyte-Burn Swarm.

/story_contents/B032/actors/1/arc/0/summ.en:
K188 Sun Gaon opened the sealed medical car.

Before Jang Sehwa, Cha Homin, and Hong Woochan he compared the six entries of the F16 evidence standard: custody, battery, parts, snapshot, network, and fixed body.

He confirmed his own provisional approval number and the error in the time of the photograph together, and he distinguished the approval of the modification from the actual attack.

He did not yet decide where the evidence would be submitted or how the device would finally be disposed of.

/story_contents/B032/actors/1/arc/1/summ.en:
K188 Sun Gaon ran the cooling bulkhead and set the spent-electrolyte barrels on the bypass, drawing G07E10 Electrolyte-Burn Swarm away from the sealed medical car.

He did not fire the device again; he reproduced the operating order from the stored waveform, the view through the window, and the hand-off signatures alone.

In the course of this it came out that the person who broke the medical-convoy neutrality and the organization that modified the equipment were not the same.

/story_contents/B032/actors/1/arc/2/summ.en:
K188 Sun Gaon, in branch A, fixed the accumulator as a treatment power supply, and in branch B he kept the device and identified the person responsible for the modification through a safety trial.

In branch C he traded, through HC07's brokering, spent-electrolyte resources and train passage times with G07E10 Electrolyte-Burn Swarm.

In every branch the six entries of the F16 evidence were undamaged, and his responsibility for the provisional approval was judged separately as well.

/story_contents/B032/actors/1/outcomes/0.en:
K188 Sun Gaon removed the device's firing circuit and sealed the battery as the fixed power supply of the burn-treatment room.

He became a railway safety inspector and reviewed in advance the chance that treatment equipment could be modified, but he took the criticism that he had not preserved the original weapon as trial evidence.

Jang Sehwa's neutral-convoy rules were extended to cover an equipment-inspection clause.

/story_contents/B032/actors/1/outcomes/1.en:
K188 Sun Gaon did not run the device again. He reproduced the incident from the snapshot and the network record, the fixed-body position, and Hong Woochan's waveform alone.

Cha Homin's lockdown time separated the person responsible for the modification from the person who fired it, and blocked the punishment of an innocent fitter.

He became keeper of the evidence store, but he also accepted a suspension of qualification for his own fault in the provisional approval.

/story_contents/B032/actors/1/outcomes/2.en:
K188 Sun Gaon assigned, through HC07's brokering, the stored spent electrolyte as bait-bypass resources for G07E10 Electrolyte-Burn Swarm.

In return, a cooling time window was secured for the medical train to pass, and the device stayed on the train in a locked state.

He became the compact's power-metering officer and kept the corridor without wiping out the creature or arming the train.

/story_contents/B032/actors/2/sections/정.en:
K213 Pyeong Seoa was a survivor of Korean origin who had worked nights at a cram school and in a pharmacy storeroom before the collapse, and he was a victim who had swallowed the medicine himself at a counterfeit-drug auction.

He was used to taking his own pain as evidence of a trade, but he held that the standing of victim must not stand in for the ability to judge.

For now he had not chosen whether to close the drug auction or to use it as a device for tracing the source back.

/story_contents/B032/actors/2/sections/붕.en:
K213 Pyeong Seoa had sorted expiry dates and cold-storage tags at a small pharmacy in Noryangjin while preparing for the civil-service examination.

Just before the collapse he found medicine he suspected of illegal repackaging, but on the shopkeeper's orders he put it in a return box, and that box later flowed into the auction stock.

The recipient cell of the return hand-off sheet was blank, so even now the responsibility for distribution could be assigned again.

/story_contents/B032/actors/2/sections/가.en:
K213 Pyeong Seoa held a victim's seat on the Noryangjin Line of Won Buddhism under HC09's market rules, and he helped buyers who had suffered drug side effects with their meal order and with keeping their specimens.

The guild was split between brokers who wanted to protect the auction revenue and victims who demanded that the whole stock be burned.

He became no faction's representative; he concentrated on making a standard that separated verified medicine from forged medicine.

/story_contents/B032/actors/2/sections/붕.en:
K213 Pyeong Seoa swallowed a counterfeit fever reducer, and afterward his sense of body temperature warped so that he could not tell cold from heat exactly, and he carried the memory of noticing a companion's high fever too late because of it.

The seller who handed him the medicine disappeared, and the victims treated him by turns as an accomplice or as the surest piece of evidence.

What he feared most was his own body being appraised again like an auction lot.

/story_contents/B032/actors/2/sections/생.en:
K213 Pyeong Seoa vomited up the tablets left after the first seizure, sealed them in a storage cell, and with Seop Daeun found the same incident marks and separated the distribution bundle.

He did not discard all the medicine then; he kept part of it for verification, but he set the sealing conditions so that the decision to discard could be reversed according to the results of Ryu Eunbi's retest.

The fork of that time was an act of preservation in the past, and it still ran on into a reversible disposal procedure.

G08E02 Cleanroom Variant followed the sterile bait barrel dusted with glaze powder ahead of the cooled specimen case, and Pyeong Seoa left that difference as the standard for the next repackaging trace.

/story_contents/B032/actors/2/sections/현.en:
K213 Pyeong Seoa, as a victim of the counterfeit-drug auction and the only provider of an ingested specimen, held the standing of a party required for the guild's next petition to stop the auction.

Seop Daeun's identification of the storage cell, Yeon Gaon's market infirmary record, and Ryu Eunbi's verification of efficacy had not yet been joined into a single judgment.

He had approved none of the procedures: an auction blockade, a tracing auction, or a conversion to verified medicine.

/story_contents/B032/actors/2/sections/비.en:
K213 Pyeong Seoa had long hidden that the return box in question carried a stock number he himself had written, and that he had seen the blank recipient cell and still not checked it again with the shopkeeper.

He had sworn to Seop Daeun that he would guard the storage cell of the same incident to the end, and he had contracted with Yeon Gaon and Ryu Eunbi that he would not discard the specimens at his own discretion.

He also felt guilt over the guild's reckoning table, which showed that taking compensation for harm would shrink the other buyers' share.

/story_contents/B032/actors/2/sections/관.en:
K213 Pyeong Seoa, together with K212 Seop Daeun, identified the storage cell of the counterfeit medicine he had swallowed as the same incident site, and they crossed the seal cords and tied them.

K202 Yeon Gaon recorded the time of his seizure and the change in his body temperature at the market infirmary, and K322 Ryu Eunbi was asked to verify the actual efficacy of the remaining tablets.

The three relationships supplied evidence that could not stand in for one another: place of storage, clinical harm, and judgment of composition.

/story_contents/B032/actors/2/sections/3.en:
K213 Pyeong Seoa, in Act 1, connected the blank hand-off sheet with the glaze powder in the storage cell and revealed that the counterfeit medicine had been repackaged at a particular ceramics workshop.

In Act 2 he isolated G08E02 Cleanroom Variant with the cold storehouse and a sterile-bait bypass, guarded the specimens, and traced back the guild's list of secret buyers.

In Act 3 he completed every branch: an auction blockade, a bait auction that caught the supplier, and the conversion of the inactive component into a topical disinfectant.

/story_contents/B032/actors/2/sections/분.en:
K213 Pyeong Seoa, in the blockade branch, melted the auction bell and made it the lock of the specimen case, and he established priority for compensation of harm.

In the tracing branch he put only the marked medicine bottles up at a restricted auction, secured the warehouse seal of the supplier, and became a victims' examiner.

In the conversion branch he processed the component that could not be swallowed, under Ryu Eunbi's verification, into a topical disinfectant, and distributed it as separate goods rather than as medicine.

/story_contents/B032/actors/2/arc/0/summ.en:
K213 Pyeong Seoa compared in one place the storage cell Seop Daeun identified, Yeon Gaon's infirmary record, and Ryu Eunbi's composition table.

He found that the blank hand-off sheet of the return box and the special glaze powder on the medicine bottle pointed to the same workshop.

He disclosed his own stock number as well, but he still reserved the final disposal of the auction.

/story_contents/B032/actors/2/arc/1/summ.en:
K213 Pyeong Seoa opened the cold storehouse in stages.

He set sterile culture bait in the opposite passage and drew G08E02 Cleanroom Variant out of the specimen room.

He mixed marked medicine bottles into the list of secret buyers and traced back the warehouse seal of the repackaging supply chain.

With the logistics trace, not the victim's body, becoming the core evidence, three procedures that could be chosen opened.

/story_contents/B032/actors/2/arc/2/summ.en:
K213 Pyeong Seoa, in branch A, blockaded the auction permanently and set up a harm-compensation ledger, and in branch B he identified the supplier through a restricted bait auction.

In branch C he passed Ryu Eunbi's verification and converted the component that could not be swallowed into a topical disinfectant, but he scrapped the medicine labeling completely.

In every branch G08E02 Cleanroom Variant was either sealed in the cooling zone or diverted through a resource trade with HC08.

/story_contents/B032/actors/2/outcomes/0.en:
K213 Pyeong Seoa banned the counterfeit-drug auction permanently and melted the guild's auction bell to make the lock of the harm-specimen case.

He became the compensation clerk who reviewed the order of compensation by harm from ingestion and by the burden of dependents, and he put his own claim last in the order.

The blank hand-off sheet was not discarded; it remained as the standard evidence for future distribution disputes.

/story_contents/B032/actors/2/outcomes/1.en:
K213 Pyeong Seoa puts only harmless marked vials into a limited auction and secures the warehouse seals and transport order used by the repackaging suppliers.

He becomes the market's standing victims' examiner, but accepts a conflict-of-interest restriction that bars him from any actual trade in medicine.

The evidence of Seop Daeun, Yeon Gaon, and Ryu Eunbi becomes independent confirmation for each stage.

/story_contents/B032/actors/2/outcomes/2.en:
K213 Pyeong Seoa approves reprocessing only the safe portion of ingredients judged unfit to swallow into external disinfectant.

The vials and auction labels are all shredded so they can never again pass as medicine, and production takes place in a cooled workroom separated from G08E02, the cleanroom mutants.

He remains not a seller of products but a designer of side-effect markers.

/story_contents/B032/actors/3/sections/정.en:
K238 Seop Dalho is a sound-transport driver of Korean descent who shuttled between a broadcaster's transmission vans and its archive before the Collapse, and is now called the voice-record retrieval courier.

She checks when and where a recording was copied and cut before she weighs whether the words are true.

She now remains a carrier who has not decided whether to broadcast or seal the voices she recovered.

/story_contents/B032/actors/3/sections/붕.en:
At a Sangam broadcasting facility, K238 Seop Dalho carried interview originals, subtitle documents, and compressed files for transmission along separate routes.

Just before the Collapse she noticed that one sentence had been deleted between the original audio of a disaster evacuation order and the broadcast version, but the power failed before she reached the transmission chief.

She can still exercise the right to return the emergency copy she made then to its original owner or to destroy it.

/story_contents/B032/actors/3/sections/가.en:
Bound by the HP10 courier code, K238 Seop Dalho links the broken relay stations of the Yeouido Investment Union's Mapo Union with the record shelters.

Her community is made up of radio technicians, deaf subtitle transcribers, and a rooftop guard that watches the dead frequencies.

She puts the dual-handover custom, that original audio and documents must arrive together, above the orders of the Transmission Corporation.

/story_contents/B032/actors/3/sections/붕.en:
K238 Seop Dalho believes that one underground passage was sealed late because of the deleted evacuation sentence, and she keeps archiving, again and again, the voices of families protesting after hearing that broadcast.

But the background sounds in the original audio point to a different time, so it cannot simply be judged an editing crime either.

Afraid that a wrong broadcast might set off another movement of crowds, she cannot press the transmit button herself.

/story_contents/B032/actors/3/sections/생.en:
After recovering a cipher box and the original audio reel from a flooded relay room, K238 Seop Dalho avoided G04E11, the sewer raccoon tribe, not with high-frequency noise but by diverting food and sealing passages.

She did not hand the original reel straight to the Transmission Corporation but passed a cross copy to Yun Seorin, leaving a return slip that could change who the cipher box belongs to.

The crossroads then was the recovery in the past, and ownership and the scope of disclosure can still be reversed now.

/story_contents/B032/actors/3/sections/현.en:
As the Yeouido Investment Union's voice-record retrieval courier, K238 Seop Dalho is the only person who holds at once the original audio of the deleted sentence, the compressed broadcast version, and copies of the subtitle documents.

Song Jaemin demands the contractual return of the cipher box, and Yun Seorin demands public verification of the audio-and-document cross copy.

She has not yet carried out any of a full broadcast, a listening jury, or a trade in frequencies and passage.

/story_contents/B032/actors/3/sections/비.en:
K238 Seop Dalho hides that the evacuation audio contains temporary directions recorded in her own voice, and that those sentences pointed to the same passage as the one that was deleted.

She contracted with Song Jaemin to move the cipher box intact, and with Yun Seorin to deliver the audio and document cross copy undamaged.

She carries the debt that broadcasting the truth could restore the victims' honor but could also set off a new column of evacuees.

/story_contents/B032/actors/3/sections/관.en:
K238 Seop Dalho carried K222 Song Jaemin's cipher box along the flooded courier route, checking both the seal tone inside the box and the seal outside.

To K144 Yun Seorin she delivered a cross copy of the original audio and the subtitle documents, so he could examine whether the deleted sentence was an edit or a time-lagged transmission.

The two contracts pit a duty to return against a duty of public verification, so she cannot let either side monopolize the material.

/story_contents/B032/actors/3/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, K238 Seop Dalho compares the background echo of the original audio with the sewer water level and shows that the deleted sentence was recorded at a different time.

In Act 2, she sets up a wired listening network that avoids the nest frequencies of G04E11, the sewer raccoon tribe, and opens Song Jaemin's cipher box and Yun Seorin's cross copy at the same time.

In Act 3, she closes every branch, a corrective broadcast, a restricted listening jury, or an HC04 frequency-and-passage deal, as a different record system.

/story_contents/B032/actors/3/sections/분.en:
In the corrective-broadcast branch, K238 Seop Dalho transmits once a chronological recording that includes even her own wrong directions, then gives up her transmission rights.

In the listening-jury branch, she sets up a fixed listening room where representatives of each affected district compare the original audio and documents and rule on which sections to release.

In the deal branch, through HC04 mediation she assigns G04E11, the sewer raccoon tribe, feeding times and underground passages and separates out human transmission times.

/story_contents/B032/actors/3/arc/0/summ.en:
At separate tables, K238 Seop Dalho opens Song Jaemin's cipher box and Yun Seorin's cross copy at the same time and matches the original audio, the broadcast version, and the subtitle documents.

Analyzing the background echo and the flood level, she confirms that the deleted sentence was a test recording made before the main broadcast.

She also reveals how her own temporary directions got mixed in, but has not yet chosen how to make it public.

/story_contents/B032/actors/3/arc/1/summ.en:
K238 Seop Dalho stops the dead-frequency transmission and places food boxes in a bypass channel so that G04E11, the sewer raccoon tribe, moves off the relay line.

Instead of a wireless broadcast, she plays the evidence to three places at once over a wired listening network that cannot be cut.

The question of tampering is settled, but the scope of the corrective broadcast and the terms of underground passage remain choices.

/story_contents/B032/actors/3/arc/2/summ.en:
In branch A, K238 Seop Dalho transmits the chronological corrective recording once.

She returns her transmission rights and the cipher box to Song Jaemin, and in branch B she sets up a fixed listening room ruled by district representatives, with a return seal.

In branch C, through HC04 mediation she trades the feeding times of G04E11, the sewer raccoon tribe, underground passages, and human transmission times, and arranges for the cipher-box return procedure to trigger if the agreement is broken.

In every branch the cross copy is preserved under Yun Seorin's record rules.

/story_contents/B032/actors/3/outcomes/0.en:
K238 Seop Dalho binds the deleted sentence and her own wrong directions together in chronological order and makes a single corrective broadcast.

After the broadcast she gives up her transmission rights and becomes a maker of metal discs engraved with the editing history of disaster recordings, so the same deletion will not happen again.

The victims hear the truth, but she can no longer be the voice of emergency broadcasts.

/story_contents/B032/actors/3/outcomes/1.en:
K238 Seop Dalho gives up mobile transmission and sets up a fixed listening room beneath the Yeouido Investment Union where the original audio and documents are checked together.

Juries from each affected district rule on public sections and private personal information, and Song Jaemin and Yun Seorin supervise the sealing and comparison procedures respectively.

She lays down her courier post and remains an assessor of echo timing.

/story_contents/B032/actors/3/outcomes/2.en:
Under HC04 mediation, K238 Seop Dalho draws up a passage table that separates the feeding times of G04E11, the sewer raccoon tribe, from the hours of human underground transmission work.

The original audio is never broadcast and is used only as a reference signal for passage-violation alarms.

She runs an underground marker workshop and arranges for the cipher-box return procedure to trigger automatically if the agreement is broken.

/story_contents/B032/actors/4/sections/정.en:
K264 Ran Minjun is a head of household of Korean descent who, before the Collapse, helped with both a family farm and residents' registration paperwork in the northern hills, and is now the spokesperson for families refusing military registration.

She does not reject adult reconstruction service itself, but does not accept household-level conscription or advance registration of minors as the order of survival.

She has not yet chosen either leaving the league or conditional registration.

/story_contents/B032/actors/4/sections/붕.en:
While managing the temperature and humidity equipment of a hillside mushroom farm, K264 Ran Minjun helped villagers file move-in reports and family-relation documents.

Just before the Collapse she temporarily added a cousin to her own household to secure seats on an evacuation vehicle, but never finished the correction report.

That addition can be cancelled or restored as a separate household once the person consents and is confirmed alive.

/story_contents/B032/actors/4/sections/가.en:
In the family barracks on the Yeouido Line of the Sangha Relief State, part of HP05, K264 Ran Minjun helps manage the food slips of the elderly, minors, and the injured.

The league wants to use the military register as the basis for rations, but her community keeps a winter-table roster based on dependency and actual residence.

She defines family not as a fixed bloodline but as people who have proven their responsibility for one another through the winter.

/story_contents/B032/actors/4/sections/붕.en:
At the first winter checkpoint, K264 Ran Minjun tried to hide a cousin who was not on the register, and it ended with another family's food cart being seized.

Since then, afraid that a single line in a roster can save a person or make them a target for forced service, she cannot easily write down anyone's name.

Her deepest guilt is having made the family she meant to protect into people who do not exist on paper.

/story_contents/B032/actors/4/sections/생.en:
In a flooded mushroom cellar, K264 Ran Minjun saved the family barracks by turning the spore flow of G10E04, the flood-mold breathing corps, with cooling and by shutting off ventilation.

That day she submitted the winter-table roster to the ration office instead of the military register, but left a correction column that lets adults move to the voluntary reconstruction-service list if they wish.

The crossroads then was a past refusal, but the method of registration is still reversible.

/story_contents/B032/actors/4/sections/현.en:
K264 Ran Minjun is the official spokesperson of the families who refused military registration in the Sangha Relief State, and holds a temporary protection slip until the next winter ration review.

Baek On demands that opposition to forced service be upheld in the family council, and Gang Minseo proposes applying the voluntary adult reconstruction-service text.

She has not yet voted on any of separating the family roster, conditional reconstruction service, or settling at the spore boundary.

/story_contents/B032/actors/4/sections/비.en:
K264 Ran Minjun knows that the old family-relation papers that temporarily added her cousin do not match where the cousin actually lives, and making it public could stop the cousin's ration rights.

She contracted with Baek On to speak for opposition to forced service, and with Gang Minseo not to block adults' voluntary choices.

Every winter she repays the family that originally owned the seized food cart with mushroom spawn.

/story_contents/B032/actors/4/sections/관.en:
K264 Ran Minjun held a family council with K245 Baek On and co-wrote wording refusing forced-service registration of minors and dependents.

From K029 Gang Minseo she received the voluntary adult reconstruction-service text and examined its clauses on the term of service, a guaranteed return, and separate payment of dependents' food.

The two relationships agree in opposing coercion but split over whether to abolish the military register completely or replace it in a limited way.

/story_contents/B032/actors/4/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, K264 Ran Minjun compares the military register with the winter-table roster and shows that service rations in dead people's names are leaking into the command's warehouse.

In Act 2, she turns the spore path of G10E04, the flood-mold breathing corps, toward a cooling cellar and a sealed wall to protect the winter food, and makes an open vote by family possible.

In Act 3, she completes every branch: founding a citizen-household roster, fixed-term adult reconstruction service, or an HC10 spore-boundary farm.

/story_contents/B032/actors/4/sections/분.en:
In the citizen-household branch, K264 Ran Minjun separates the military register from rations and becomes registrar of a winter-table roster based on the fact of dependency.

In the reconstruction-service branch, she creates a service-bond system in which only individual adults sign for a fixed term and are guaranteed family food and a place to return to.

In the boundary-farm branch, through HC10 mediation she seals the wetland zone of G10E04, the flood-mold breathing corps, and uses the heat of the spores to warm winter greenhouses.

/story_contents/B032/actors/4/arc/0/summ.en:
K264 Ran Minjun calls Baek On and Gang Minseo to the family council and compares the military register, the voluntary reconstruction-service text, and the winter-table roster item by item.

She makes public both the traces of service rations in dead people's names moving into the command's warehouse and her own record of temporarily adding her cousin.

The injustice of forced registration is confirmed, but the replacement system has not yet been voted on.

/story_contents/B032/actors/4/arc/1/summ.en:
K264 Ran Minjun opens the cooling channel of the storage cellar.

She seals the vents of the living quarters and turns the spore flow of G10E04, the flood-mold breathing corps, toward an empty wetland.

She distributes the mushroom spawn she secured not by the number of family members but by days of dependency, proving that winter can be reckoned without a military register.

Adult reconstruction service and the boundary farm remain as separate motions for a vote.

/story_contents/B032/actors/4/arc/2/summ.en:
In branch A, K264 Ran Minjun founds a citizen-household roster that separates the military register from rations, and in branch B she introduces fixed-term reconstruction-service bonds for individual adults.

In branch C, through HC10 mediation she seals the wetland boundary of G10E04, the flood-mold breathing corps, and turns the heat of the spores into greenhouse heating.

In every branch advance registration of minors is banned, and her cousin's temporary addition is corrected as the cousin chooses.

/story_contents/B032/actors/4/outcomes/0.en:
K264 Ran Minjun separates the military register from the basis for rations and founds a citizen-household roster that records actual dependency and days of residence.

As registrar, she restores her cousin's household with the cousin's consent and compensates the family whose cart was seized for what they lost first.

Baek On's wording against forced service becomes the roster's first prohibition.

/story_contents/B032/actors/4/outcomes/1.en:
K264 Ran Minjun revises Gang Minseo's text and adopts reconstruction-service bonds signed only by individual adults with a set term and duty.

The service members' family food and places to return to are deposited in advance in a separate warehouse, and if the command diverts them the bond becomes void automatically.

She becomes not a recruiter but an independent clerk who examines return-guarantee documents.

/story_contents/B032/actors/4/outcomes/2.en:
Through HC10 mediation, K264 Ran Minjun builds a cooling seal wall between the wetland zone of G10E04, the flood-mold breathing corps, and the human living caves.

The heat from the creature's spores is used through a closed heat exchanger to warm winter greenhouses, and direct harvesting or extermination operations are banned.

She does not move her family away and remains the permanent overwinterer of the boundary farm.

/story_contents/B032/actors/5/sections/정.en:
He is a wheel inspector of Korean descent, born in Changdong, who grew up learning the smell of railway parts and the vibration of the test line.

He has a field sense that catches differences in the ring of metal before numbers, and he holds that whoever sees a defect must take responsibility for it to the end.

/story_contents/B032/actors/5/sections/붕.en:
Before the Collapse he handled ultrasonic flaw detection and heat-mark reading of test wheels, but was repeatedly refused re-inspections by superiors who put delivery deadlines first.

After work he collected cut faces of scrapped wheels to build a table of defect cases and taught juniors the sound of cracks.

/story_contents/B032/actors/5/sections/가.en:
His roots are in an HP05-affiliated work crew and the Seocho Computing Group, and he is bound by an oath to have testified to a defect in Jo Woochan's work crew.

He swore with Du Mo to guard together a toolbox holding defect samples and seal records, and neither can break the seal alone.

/story_contents/B032/actors/5/sections/붕.en:
He found a crack in a test wheel but, fearing the evacuation delays a halt in service would cause, wrote the defect down one grade lower, and that wheel derailed and killed two of his coworkers.

The deeper wound is not the cut on the back of his hand but the fact that he weakened on paper the bursting sound he had heard clearly.

/story_contents/B032/actors/5/sections/생.en:
His survival turning point came early in the Collapse, when he hid the original flaw-detection plate and the wheel stamp in Du Mo's sealed toolbox and burned only a substitute sample.

The seal can be reopened to correct the record if Jo Woochan and Du Mo are present, so the past choice is still reversible, but the moment it is made public Changdong's trust in rations could collapse.

G22E13, the spent-battery metal colony, gathered not at the metal resonance of the plate but at a cooled scrap-alloy sample, and Eo Yerin recorded the order so that Jo Woochan and Du Mo could return the arrangement to its original place and reproduce it.

/story_contents/B032/actors/5/sections/현.en:
He works at the Seocho Computing Group on the Gangnam Line as a witness to the test-wheel defect and a reader of cooling order, recording metal resonance and temperature changes when G22E13, the spent-battery metal colony, approaches.

He is on the verge of choosing whether to make the original public or to use the evidence as collateral in a passage deal with the colony, and has not yet handed it to either side.

/story_contents/B032/actors/5/sections/비.en:
He hides the secret that the signature lowering the defect grade of the accident wheel is his own, owes Du Mo a debt for keeping the seal, and carries guilt toward Jo Woochan for giving incomplete testimony.

He also knows that the spent-battery metal colony sees the alloy of the flaw-detection plate as food, and is torn between preserving the evidence and luring the colony.

/story_contents/B032/actors/5/sections/관.en:
When Eo Yerin first reported the sound of a crack, Jo Woochan stopped the work crew, but when pressure from the evacuation trains came she cut the re-inspection time along with him.

After the accident Du Mo sealed the original flaw-detection plate in the toolbox for him, and the two are bound by an oath never to erase the names of the dead.

/story_contents/B032/actors/5/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, he confirms that the same resonance pattern as the accident wheel draws the movement of G22E13, the spent-battery metal colony.

In Act 2, he decides whether to break the seal reversibly in front of Jo Woochan and Du Mo and prove the tampering with the defect grade.

In Act 3, every path opens: fixing the colony's feeding route to the scrap-wheel yard with the original, preserving the evidence while trading for cooled passage time, or sacrificing the plate to seal the colony and leaving the wheel shop.

/story_contents/B032/actors/5/sections/분.en:
Depending on whether he chooses preserving the original, sacrificing the alloy sample, or closing the workshop, the honor of the dead and Changdong's productive capacity pay different prices.

No ending aims at wiping out the colony or joint control, and Eo Yerin personally bears ownership of the evidence and responsibility for the accident.

/story_contents/B032/actors/5/arc/0/summ.en:
In the cooling tank of the Seocho Computing Group, K290 Eo Yerin hears it.

When the same faint resonance as the accident wheel arises, he works backward to the travel route of G22E13, the spent-battery metal colony.

Jo Woochan wants to open the toolbox at once, but Du Mo warns that if the seal breaks, the alloy of the plate could call the colony into the workshop.

Eo Yerin makes a noise lure from scrap-wheel pieces to win a day's delay, and confirms that the hidden original is both evidence and food.

/story_contents/B032/actors/5/arc/1/summ.en:
With Jo Woochan and Du Mo present, K290 Eo Yerin loosens the seal screws halfway and compares the stamp on the original flaw-detection plate with his own signature on the downgraded judgment.

He can correct the past record, but he also faces the calculation that the moment it is public, every finished product of the Seocho Computing Group will be re-inspected and production of evacuation carts will stop.

The three review the passage-time deal offered by the HP08 broker and prepare a test to protect the evidence with cooling and food diversion without killing the colony.

/story_contents/B032/actors/5/arc/2/summ.en:
K290 Eo Yerin can make the original flaw-detection plate public and settle responsibility for the defect.

He can divert G22E13, the spent-battery metal colony, along a scrap-wheel feeding route, or keep the original sealed and trade a copied stamp for cooled passage time.

Or he can use the plate itself as the colony's lure, sealing it in the underground cold store and losing the wheel shop's system of evidence.

Each branch decides differently what remains: the reinstatement of Jo Woochan's crew, Du Mo's sealing oath, the record of the dead, or Changdong's production.

/story_contents/B032/actors/5/outcomes/0.en:
K290 Eo Yerin makes the original flaw-detection plate public and restores his own downgraded judgment to the accident record, then lays out the spent-battery alloy the colony prefers in stages as far as the scrap-wheel yard.

G22E13, the spent-battery metal colony, skirts the workshop according to the HP08 broker's cooling timetable and is not wiped out.

The Seocho Computing Group enters a long re-inspection, but Jo Woochan's crew and Du Mo's seal remain as an evidence procedure that preserves the names of the dead.

/story_contents/B032/actors/5/outcomes/1.en:
K290 Eo Yerin keeps the original sealed, proves the defect exists by copying only the surface stamp, and buys the colony's passage time on condition that the original plate's alloy is not handed over.

He postpones settling legal responsibility, taking on instead the debt of personally auditing the cooling and food placement every shift.

The oath with Jo Woochan holds, but Du Mo sets a deadline for renewing the seal so that Eo Yerin cannot avoid the choice again.

/story_contents/B032/actors/5/outcomes/2.en:
K290 Eo Yerin uses the original flaw-detection plate as food bait in the underground cold store to keep G22E13, the spent-battery metal colony, inside a sealed route.

The workshop survives at once, but the physical evidence that could settle responsibility for the accident is gone, and he gives up his wheel-inspection license and the name of Changdong of his own accord.

He leaves Du Mo an empty toolbox and written testimony, and gives Jo Woochan a final inspection order to cut up every remaining wheel.

/story_contents/B032/actors/6/sections/정.en:
A Korean transit recordkeeper who grew up on Seoul’s northeastern outskirts and handled bus turnaround schedules and market freight manifests.

She is wary of reducing people to numbers in a queue, yet knows that without accurate numbers, stretchers and medicine can both be held up.

/story_contents/B032/actors/6/sections/붕.en:
Before the Collapse, she handled both nighttime dispatch at a transit center and mobility assistance for people with disabilities, calculating how many people needed a detour whenever an elevator broke down.

She also volunteered at a local hospital and devised a way to record oxygen cylinders and caregivers separately for the patient line led by Jeon Miri.

/story_contents/B032/actors/6/sections/가.en:
As an HC11 transit witness, he manages the northeast gate registry in Neutral Convoy City on the Jamsil Line.

He has separate agreements with the oath-bound Baek On, who supports Jeon Miri’s patient line from the witness stand, and the oath-bound Seok Raon, who checks Baek On’s southbound family registry, to reconcile transit counts with stretcher counts.

/story_contents/B032/actors/6/sections/붕.en:
On the first night of evacuation, she deleted three caregivers from the registry to make room for one stretcher; those she deleted suffered electrolyte burns in a closed underground passage.

One of them returned alive but was treated as a nameless traveler and denied rations and treatment, shaking her faith in her method of calculation.

/story_contents/B032/actors/6/sections/생.en:
Beom Ongyeol did not burn the original registry. She hid it behind a billboard at the transit center, then left the pre-deletion figures in reverse-order markings to preserve a lead for tracing survivors.

Dismantling the billboard would allow the registry to be restored and the deletions reversed, but it would also expose both the past manipulation of gate capacity and the current excess rations.

The G07E06 electrolyte-burn cluster followed cooled empty stretchers and spent-battery containers rather than lines of people with high body temperatures. Beom Ongyeol recorded the intervals between travelers so Jeon Miri and Baek On could test the same conditions again.

/story_contents/B032/actors/6/sections/현.en:
As the transit witness at Neutral Convoy City’s northeast gate, she assigns patients, stretchers, caregivers, and southbound families to separate lines.

She has yet to negotiate transit times with the G07E06 electrolyte-burn cluster and has approved neither Jeon Miri’s patient-priority plan nor Baek On’s plan to keep families together.

/story_contents/B032/actors/6/sections/비.en:
He secretly diverted rations by temporarily adding the names of the three deleted caregivers to the end of Baek On’s southbound family registry.

He owes Jeon Miri for keeping the patient line going and owes Seok Raon for breaching their agreement by disclosing the actual stretcher count late. He feels guilty for erasing people’s existence with numbers.

/story_contents/B032/actors/6/sections/관.en:
Jeon Miri treated the first burn patients on the gate floor, while Beom Ongyeol used the witness stand as a shield to protect the patient line.

Baek On traced the family ties of the deleted names, and Seok Raon checked Beom Ongyeol’s manipulation by insisting the gate would not open unless the stretcher count matched the transit count.

/story_contents/B032/actors/6/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, she discovers that the G07E06 electrolyte-burn cluster moves toward lines of people with high body temperatures and salt levels.

In Act 2, she recovers the original registry behind the billboard and recalculates the deleted caregivers and excess rations.

In Act 3, three paths open: divert the burn cluster with a line of cooled empty stretchers; separate the family registry to secure a limited transit window; or seal the northeast gate and personally rescue the deleted people from the underground passage.

/story_contents/B032/actors/6/sections/분.en:
Beom Ongyeol’s ending depends on what she restores first: trust in the gate’s figures, the deleted people’s legal existence, or the safety of the patient line.

Rather than merely admitting her wrongdoing, she takes on one of three distinct practical responsibilities: restoring the registry, operating the cooled stretcher line, or carrying out an underground rescue.

/story_contents/B032/actors/6/arc/0/summ.en:
K315 Beom Ongyeol sees the G07E06 electrolyte-burn cluster gather rapidly around Jeon Miri’s patient line.

He makes a correlation table for body temperature, salt, and battery leakage.

Baek On demands that southbound families not be split up, while Seok Raon cites a contract clause under which the gate must close if the stretcher count does not match.

Beom Ongyeol sends a test line carrying cooling cloths and salt-free gel on empty stretchers and finds a brief window in which the gate can open.

/story_contents/B032/actors/6/arc/1/summ.en:
K315 Beom Ongyeol retrieves the original registry from behind the billboard and compares the three caregivers he deleted with the false ration markings he added to Baek On’s registry.

Jeon Miri says their names should be restored immediately without stopping the patient line, while Seok Raon argues that the contract remains valid only if every excess person is counted again against the stretcher total.

Beom Ongyeol confirms that restoring the registry can reverse his past choice, but realizes that correcting the numbers will require some families who passed through that night to return for an audit.

/story_contents/B032/actors/6/arc/2/summ.en:
K315 Beom Ongyeol makes the original registry public.

He can divert the G07E06 electrolyte-burn cluster with a line of cooled empty stretchers and get everyone through, or briefly separate family units to secure a limited transit window brokered by HC07.

Alternatively, he can seal the gate, descend into the underground passage with Jeon Miri, and rescue the deleted survivors first, leaving Baek On and Seok Raon in charge of the registry outside.

The three branches impose different costs on restoring trust in transit, keeping families together, and rescuing nameless survivors.

/story_contents/B032/actors/6/outcomes/0.en:
K315 Beom Ongyeol makes the original registry public, restores the identities of the three deleted caregivers, and reconciles the actual stretcher count with Seok Raon.

While a line of cooled empty stretchers lures the G07E06 electrolyte-burn cluster to a closed platform, Jeon Miri’s patient line and Baek On’s families pass through the gate.

Beom Ongyeol remains a transit witness, but must repay all excess rations from his own share thereafter.

/story_contents/B032/actors/6/outcomes/1.en:
K315 Beom Ongyeol accepts HC07’s mediation, temporarily sends patients with high body temperatures and their caregivers through at different times, and allocates cooling resources and empty battery containers to the electrolyte-burn cluster.

The separation time and reunion place remain in Baek On’s family registry as legal markings, but some family members cannot confirm one another’s survival for a day.

Beom Ongyeol restores the deleted people’s identities but surrenders his authority as a gate witness to Seok Raon and is demoted to ration auditor.

/story_contents/B032/actors/6/outcomes/2.en:
K315 Beom Ongyeol closes the northeast gate, halts the line outside, and joins Jeon Miri in rescuing the nameless burn survivors from the underground passage.

Baek On safeguards the family registry outside, while Seok Raon fixes the stretcher count at the closed gate to prevent further casualties.

The rescue succeeds, but Transfer City misses the southbound deadline and loses its status as an independent gate. Beom Ongyeol cannot leave the site until the rescuers’ identities have been reviewed.

/story_contents/B032/actors/7/sections/정.en:
A third-generation Koryo-saram born in Tashkent, Uzbekistan, whose maternal great-grandparents were forcibly relocated from the Russian Far East to Central Asia in 1937.

Russian is his first language, and he trades in Uzbek at markets. He uses both the Koryo-mar he learned at home and the Korean he learned as an adult to decipher place names on maps.

/story_contents/B032/actors/7/sections/붕.en:
After moving from Tashkent to Incheon with his parents in 2008, he worked as a garment-factory interpreter while taking evening courses in library and information science. He later earned a living restoring paper maps and organizing place-name data.

He made maps of migration routes by comparing Russian-language oral histories from elderly Koryo-saram with Koryo-mar place names that had disappeared.

/story_contents/B032/actors/7/sections/가.en:
As a map-restoration librarian for HC05, the Republic of Korea Government, he manages migrant records and the master plate of transmission-tower coordinates.

He has an agreement with Choi Jiwoo to synchronize map-update times with transmissions, and maintains a double-check agreement under which he attaches the transmission-tower coordinates received from Gwon Mirae to the master map plate before passing them back.

/story_contents/B032/actors/7/sections/붕.en:
Just before the Collapse, he deliberately misplaced the coordinates of a Koryo-saram cemetery and a drinking-water reservoir on the public map to protect a refugee camp.

A misdirected rescue team entered a spent-battery field occupied by a metal colony and suffered casualties. His attempt to protect his family’s memories severed other people’s route home.

/story_contents/B032/actors/7/sections/생.en:
Seo Raon did not erase the altered coordinates. Instead, he encoded the actual offsets in Russian-language scale annotations along the edge of the master plate.

With Choi Jiwoo’s transmission times and Gwon Mirae’s original coordinates, the plate can be realigned, making his past choice reversible. But restoration would also reveal the locations of both the cemetery and the drinking-water reservoir.

The G22E04 spent-battery metal colony followed a buried line of spent batteries along the perimeter rather than the magnetic master plate. Seo Raon added nonmagnetic markings so Choi Jiwoo and Gwon Mirae could reverse the placement without exposing the coordinates.

/story_contents/B032/actors/7/sections/현.en:
He is a librarian at the Republic of Korea Government’s Seoul Station Central, restoring torn master map plates and transmission coordinates while scheduling reading sessions around magnetic interference from the G22E04 spent-battery metal colony.

He has not yet decided whether to keep the protected coordinates hidden, restore them for the route home, or trade with the metal colony for transit time.

/story_contents/B032/actors/7/sections/비.en:
He has hidden, in Russian-language annotations, the secret that he diverted the rescue team’s route to protect the cemetery.

He owes Choi Jiwoo for sending an incorrect update time and owes Gwon Mirae for breaching their agreement by altering the original coordinates. He feels guilty for failing to give the victims’ families an accurate route home.

/story_contents/B032/actors/7/sections/관.en:
On the first day of the Collapse, Choi Jiwoo sent a rescue signal timed to Seo Raon’s map update, but the displaced coordinates caused one transmission to be lost.

Gwon Mirae delivered the original transmission-tower coordinates twice. She realized the offsets Seo Raon had added to the master plate were no accident, but held off on terminating their agreement.

/story_contents/B032/actors/7/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, he combines the Russian-language scale annotations with transmission times to reconstruct the lost route home.

In Act 2, he confirms that the Koryo-saram cemetery, the drinking-water reservoir, and the site where the rescue team died all lie along one magnetic route.

In Act 3, three paths open: publish all the coordinates to restore the route home; keep the cemetery’s coordinates only in paper clues and trade drinking water for passage through the colony; or demagnetize the master plate to break the colony’s magnetic path and recreate his family map from memory.

/story_contents/B032/actors/7/sections/분.en:
Seo Raon’s branch determines not only whether the map is made public, but also the medium and language in which the memory of forced migration survives.

Rather than becoming a traveling guide, he stays with the Republic of Korea Government and becomes responsible for one of three things: a public master plate, a restricted-access cemetery register, or a demagnetized oral-history map.

/story_contents/B032/actors/7/arc/0/summ.en:
K149 Seo Raon discovers that the offsets he hid in the Russian-language scale annotations on the Republic of Korea Government’s master plate match the cycle of magnetic interference from the G22E04 spent-battery metal colony.

Choi Jiwoo presses him for an exact update time to restore the lost rescue signal, and Gwon Mirae presents the original transmission-tower coordinates again.

Reading the Russian, Koryo-mar place names, and Korean administrative names together, Seo Raon creates a temporary route home that does not expose the cemetery.

/story_contents/B032/actors/7/arc/1/summ.en:
K149 Seo Raon compares the family migration map he brought from Tashkent with the Seoul Station master plate, examining the cemetery and the drinking-water reservoir.

He reveals that the site where the rescue team died lies along the same buried line of spent batteries.

His encoded annotations make it possible to reverse the coordinate manipulation, but the restored magnetic line would also give the G22E04 spent-battery metal colony the shortest route to food.

Choi Jiwoo and Gwon Mirae divide up the transmission times, while Seo Raon tests both an HP08-brokered transit proposal and a plan to demagnetize the master plate.

/story_contents/B032/actors/7/arc/2/summ.en:
K149 Seo Raon can publish all the coordinates and restore the rescue team’s route home.

He can divert the spent-battery food source to another burial site, or keep the cemetery’s coordinates only in a restricted-access register and trade some drinking water for passage through the colony’s territory.

Alternatively, he can remove the magnetic layer from the master map plate to break the G22E04 spent-battery metal colony’s path and copy the transmission-tower coordinates onto nonmagnetic paper.

The three branches leave different outcomes for the victims’ return, protection of the Koryo-saram cemetery, the long-term drinking-water supply, and preservation of the family migration map.

/story_contents/B032/actors/7/outcomes/0.en:
K149 Seo Raon makes public how he decoded the Russian-language scale cipher and uses Gwon Mirae’s original coordinates and Choi Jiwoo’s transmission times to restore the route home.

The G22E04 spent-battery metal colony survives, bypassing the cemetery and rescue route after buried spent batteries are placed along another magnetic path.

The cemetery appears on the public map, and Seo Raon becomes responsible for recording the names of the victims of forced migration and the rescue-team dead together on the same master plate.

/story_contents/B032/actors/7/outcomes/1.en:
K149 Seo Raon keeps the cemetery’s coordinates only in a restricted-access register written in Russian and Koryo-mar. He includes part of the drinking-water reservoir in HP08’s brokered resource-allocation schedule.

In exchange for spent batteries and cooling water at set times, the G22E04 spent-battery metal colony stays clear of the transmission-tower route home.

The rescue team’s route is restored, but the records office’s drinking-water reserves shrink, and Seo Raon takes on the weighty role of personally reviewing requests to visit the cemetery.

/story_contents/B032/actors/7/outcomes/2.en:
K149 Seo Raon strips the magnetic layer from the master map plate, breaking the route by which the G22E04 spent-battery metal colony follows the coordinates. He rewrites Gwon Mirae’s coordinates on nonmagnetic paper.

Part of the family migration route preserved on the plate disappears, but he records fresh Russian and Koryo-mar oral histories from elderly Koryo-saram in Tashkent and makes a separate map.

Choi Jiwoo’s transmissions become slower but more reliable, and Seo Raon preserves the damaged master plate in the center of the records office without concealing it.

/story_contents/B032/actors/8/sections/정.en:
A fourth-generation Koryo-saram born in Kazakhstan’s Kyzylorda Region, from a family whose great-grandparents were forcibly relocated from the Russian Far East and then made a living on a collective farm’s railway loading crew.

Russian is her native language, and she uses Kazakh in everyday life. After migrating through Busan to Seoul in 2013, she learned Korean and railway-dispatch abbreviations.

/story_contents/B032/actors/8/sections/붕.en:
Soon after moving to Korea, she worked as an inspector at a refrigerated warehouse. Once her family’s knowledge of freight-car timetables was recognized, she became a dispatcher on Yongsan’s civilian line.

She coordinated passing times for night freight trains and refrigerated medical-supply carriages while earning money for remittances to relatives and residency paperwork.

/story_contents/B032/actors/8/sections/가.en:
He was brought into the railway family of HP07 Line Succession State and works under Sin Gaon’s dispatch command.

His relationship with Jo Woochan is marked by betrayal and resentment over the suspected diversion of a Chang-dong test wheel, and the family regards a dispatch pin left by Gang Daeun as key evidence of the diversion.

/story_contents/B032/actors/8/sections/붕.en:
On the day of the Collapse, when a low-temperature spore membrane covered the medical-supply line, she switched a freight car carrying a test wheel without authorization to stop the spores spreading. As a result, an evacuation carriage carrying her family was stranded outside Yongsan.

She concealed the dispatch record without explaining the rescue’s purpose, leaving Jo Woochan under suspicion of theft and losing track of two relatives.

/story_contents/B032/actors/8/sections/생.en:
Gang Daeun did not melt down the brass dispatch pin used for the unauthorized switch; he hid it inside the cover of a Kyzylorda timetable.

Comparing Sin Gaon’s original order with Jo Woochan’s wheel markings would reconstruct the sequence of switches, making his past decision reversible. But it would also reveal that the railway family had prioritized a train carrying relatives over containment of the spores.

The G23E12 low-temperature spore membrane responded to cooling time and contact with the sealed axle rather than the test wheel’s pressure. Gang Daeun recorded the conditions in the timetable so Sin Gaon and Jo Woochan could reproduce them even if they retrieved the wheel.

/story_contents/B032/actors/8/sections/현.en:
As a dispatcher for the railway family of Wangsimni Union Line Succession State, she calculates fixed track slots for cooling cars, medical-supply cars, and sealed cars.

Facing the G23E12 low-temperature spore membrane, she has yet to choose whether to reveal the test wheel’s whereabouts, obey the family’s orders, or put the wheel back into service on a spore-bypass line.

/story_contents/B032/actors/8/sections/비.en:
He hides the fact that he did not divert the test wheel for personal gain, but used it as a pressure wheel to seal the spore membrane.

He owes Sin Gaon for disobeying an order and Jo Woochan for leaving him falsely accused of theft. Guilt over sacrificing his relatives’ evacuation carriage keeps him from opening the family registry.

/story_contents/B032/actors/8/sections/관.en:
Sin Gaon ordered Gang Daeun to let the family’s evacuation carriage through first, but Gang Daeun looked at the on-site thermometer and reversed the order.

Jo Woochan traced the markings on the Chang-dong test wheel to Yongsan. Because Gang Daeun hid the dispatch pin, Jo Woochan believes he was betrayed and demands the wheel’s return and an explanation of the deaths.

/story_contents/B032/actors/8/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, he finds traces showing that pressure from the cooled test wheel held down the G23E12 low-temperature spore membrane and stopped its spread.

In Act 2, he reconstructs the unauthorized switch using the brass dispatch pin, Sin Gaon’s original order, and Jo Woochan’s record of the wheel markings.

In Act 3, three paths open: retrieve the wheel and return it to Jo Woochan; leave it in place permanently as a pressure wheel sealing the spores; or turn the family evacuation line into a spore-quarantine line and search for the lost carriage carrying his relatives.

/story_contents/B032/actors/8/sections/분.en:
Gang Daeun’s ending turns not on words clearing someone’s name, but on acts that change who physically holds the test wheel and who has priority on the railway family’s tracks.

Rather than leaving as a migrant worker, she stays in Yongsan and takes long-term responsibility for one of three things: an audit of the wheel’s return, the spore-sealing track, or the search for her relatives’ carriage.

/story_contents/B032/actors/8/arc/0/summ.en:
K174 Gang Daeun finds traces beneath Yongsan’s cooling line where the G23E12 low-temperature spore membrane could not grow across circular pressure marks.

He confirms the location of the hidden test wheel.

Sin Gaon orders him to deny the wheel exists to protect the family’s tracks, while Jo Woochan presents a rubbing of its Chang-dong markings and demands its return.

Gang Daeun takes the brass dispatch pin from the cover of a Kyzylorda timetable written in Russian and recalculates the sequence of switches he made in the past.

/story_contents/B032/actors/8/arc/1/summ.en:
K174 Gang Daeun compares the dispatch pin with Sin Gaon’s original order and proves that he sent the spore-containment freight car ahead of his family’s evacuation carriage.
