Jo Woochan’s test wheel was taken without permission, but it is also the only pressure wheel holding down the G23E12 low-temperature spore membrane. Retrieving it immediately would contaminate Yongsan’s tracks again.

Gang Daeun tests a trade in cooling time brokered by HP09 and the feasibility of making a replacement pressure wheel, while deciding who should see the dispatch record—now possible to correct—first.

/story_contents/B032/actors/8/arc/2/summ.en:
K174 Gang Daeun can install a replacement pressure wheel and then return the test wheel to Jo Woochan.

He can settle the grievance, or leave the wheel as the permanent sealing axle for the G23E12 low-temperature spore membrane and owe Chang-dong a metal allocation.

Alternatively, he can turn the family evacuation line into a quarantine line, search for the lost carriage carrying his relatives, and abolish Sin Gaon’s priority dispatch authority.

The three branches reach different conclusions about Jo Woochan’s false accusation, Sin Gaon’s family authority, the stability of the spore seal, and the chance to search for Gang Daeun’s relatives.

/story_contents/B032/actors/8/outcomes/0.en:
K174 Gang Daeun installs a replacement pressure wheel made from Yongsan scrap metal and returns the test wheel directly to Jo Woochan once the cooling time has stabilized.

The dispatch pin and original order are made public, clearing Jo Woochan of the diversion allegation, but Gang Daeun loses half her dispatch authority for disobeying the family’s order.

The G23E12 low-temperature spore membrane is contained within the sealing schedule and cooling resources set by HP09, rather than targeted for extermination.

/story_contents/B033/actors/0/sections/정.en:
Tak Eunsol is a Korean survivor born and raised behind Seoul’s Jegi-dong Market. He can tell where medicinal herbs came from and whether they have spoiled by their smell and cut surfaces.

In the Medical Neutrality League, he establishes his identity not as a patient but as an eyewitness who remembers transactions and sealing procedures.

He values the responsibility of saying exactly whose hands a packet of medicine passed through before it was switched more than lineage or title.

/story_contents/B033/actors/0/sections/붕.en:
Before the Collapse, Tak Eunsol made a living sorting returned medicinal herbs at a small herbal-medicine packing shop and checking weight discrepancies on transaction statements.

He traced the distribution route of counterfeit pain-relief pills containing an illegal ingredient. But while the transaction could still be reversed, he trusted the prime contractor’s promise to recall them and sent the suspect boxes back to the warehouse.

At the time, that decision was an administrative choice that could be corrected without breaking the seals. When the Collapse struck, however, the boxes and ledgers were scattered to different places.

/story_contents/B033/actors/0/sections/가.en:
Tak Eunsol’s family was not a merchant dynasty that had traded in Jegi-dong Market for generations, but a household of wage workers who did packing and cleaning.

After the Collapse, he joins the Medical Neutrality League’s Night Sorting Unit and devises a procedure for comparing seized herbs against colored-thread knots, ceramic weights, and scent samples.

Within the alliance, he guards a witness seat belonging to neither the merchants’ association nor the medical council, and explains the order of testing to patients’ families in the market alleys.

/story_contents/B033/actors/0/sections/붕.en:
During the first winter of the Collapse, the automated arm of the G13E15 Night Sorting Unit mistook a red return knot for an emergency-dispatch mark and put counterfeit fever pills and legitimate medicinal herbs on the same conveyor.

Tak Eunsol’s mother took a switched packet and lost her hearing. Although Eun-sol saw the return stamp he himself had made, he was afraid the crowd would destroy the sorting building and failed to stop the equipment immediately.

Because of his silence, even the legitimate herbs were compacted and discarded, and three chronically ill patients died when their supply was cut off. He is left with a lingering reaction that stiffens his finger joints whenever he hears rollers rubbing.

/story_contents/B033/actors/0/sections/생.en:
Tak Eunsol tests the G13E15 Night Sorting Unit with empty ceramic boxes and discovers that its arm changes direction according to package weight, knot color, and the interval between insertions, rather than the herbs’ ingredients.

He feeds in empty blue boxes at regular intervals, cools a section of the conveyor, then seals the reading window and diverts misclassified packets onto a separate track. He temporarily releases Dong Juha’s scale seal so it can be restored with the same lead impression.

Because the sorting sequence can be retraced while Jeong Hojun retests the ingredients in front of the victims, the measure remains a reversible distribution-verification procedure rather than destruction of the equipment.

/story_contents/B033/actors/0/sections/현.en:
Tak Eunsol is currently assigned a witness seat as the Dongdaemun Union Medical Neutrality League’s witness to counterfeit-drug distribution, just before the XT04-SC1 hearing begins.

He has not yet chosen whether to give priority as evidence to Dong Juha’s sealed scale or Jeong Hojun’s public test results. Until he chooses, he keeps the two packets in separate refrigerated boxes.

Market merchants fear his testimony will cut off rations, while patients’ families pressure him by saying they will open the warehouse themselves if he remains silent.

/story_contents/B033/actors/0/sections/비.en:
Tak Eunsol hides the fact that he personally stamped the first return and entered his own initials in the prime contractor’s recall-confirmation field without actually checking it.

He also owes a debt for guiding the Night Sorting Unit to the contractor’s remaining warehouse at night to pay for his mother’s hearing aid and medicine for the families of the three people who died.

But revealing that he also hid legitimate herbs inside the warehouse would constitute an admission of theft. He feels guilty that telling the truth could cut off patients’ supplies again.

/story_contents/B033/actors/0/sections/관.en:
While Dong Juha shielded the scale seal with his body during a market riot, Tak Eunsol copied the shape of a crack in its lead impression. The two swear to halt the procedure together if the testimony and measurements do not match.

On the night Jeong Hojun compared well sediment and herb powder on the same glass plate, Eun-sol handled the lighting and sample order, helping establish the standard for public testing.

Their shared past includes a return ledger that escaped the fire. Their promise that no one will open it alone constrains the choice they now face.

/story_contents/B033/actors/0/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, Tak Eunsol tracks a ceramic weight that disappeared the day before the hearing and confirms that the counterfeit-drug harm resulted from both weight manipulation and a change to the automated sorting code.

In Act 2, he leaves his false confirmation initials unerased while aligning Dong Juha’s seal with Jeong Hojun’s testing sequence, and must decide whether to tell the bereaved families about the hidden stock of legitimate herbs.

In Act 3, three branches collide: disclosing both the prime contractor’s responsibility and his own negligence to reform the alliance; distributing the legitimate herbs first and postponing the trial; or keeping the ledger sealed while tracking G13E15’s misclassification route and control chart.

/story_contents/B033/actors/0/sections/분.en:
In the first ending, Tak Eunsol reveals the ledger bearing his initials and is found guilty, but Dong Juha and Jeong Hojun secure passage of an independent testing protocol that leaves a system for recalling counterfeit drugs.

In the second ending, he distributes the hidden herbs to patients first and prevents deaths, but breaks the chain of evidence, allowing the prime contractor’s responsible official to escape.

In the third ending, he halts the hearing and seals off the underground sorting line connecting G13E15’s feed chart, roller timings, and reading code, but never manages to explain his role to his mother or the bereaved families.

/story_contents/B033/actors/0/arc/0/summ.en:
K341 Tak Eunsol searches for a ceramic weight missing from the sealed box the day before the hearing and discovers the same red medicinal dust on the cap of Jeong Hojun’s sample bottle and G13E15’s reading window.

He tells Dong Juha not to open the scale seal yet, but to photograph only its lead impression, securing time for an investigation that can still be reversed.

The weight’s route leads to the automated sorting line and the victims’ waiting area, revealing that someone inside tried to swap evidence for patients’ medicine.

/story_contents/B033/actors/0/arc/1/summ.en:
K341 Tak Eunsol finds his false confirmation initials in the returns ledger and learns that the location of the hidden legitimate herbs and that of the contaminated waterway are linked by a single tear-off sheet.

He overlays Dong Juha’s weight records with Jeong Hojun’s public test figures to narrow down when the counterfeit drugs were made, but does not yet disclose his own negligence.

When the bell announcing the hearing rings, the bereaved families’ representative and the merchants’ association demand different sealed boxes. Which evidence he presents first becomes an irreversible choice.

/story_contents/B033/actors/0/arc/2/summ.en:
K341 Tak Eunsol, in Branch A, reveals his initials alongside the prime contractor’s ledger and accepts punishment.

He establishes an independent testing protocol; in Branch B, he immediately distributes the hidden herbs to save patients, but damages the trial evidence.

In Branch C, he reseals the ledger. With Jeong Hojun and Dong Juha, he tracks the sorting line connecting G13E15’s feed chart, roller timings, and reading code to prevent further spread, but postpones publicly acknowledging his personal responsibility.

In all three branches, whether the missing ceramic weight is recovered and the explanation he leaves for his mother determine the final cost.

/story_contents/B033/actors/0/outcomes/0.en:
K341 Tak Eunsol presents the returns ledger and his false confirmation initials at the witness seat and stands trial alongside the prime contractor’s responsible official.

Dong Juha’s sealing rules and Jeong Hojun’s public testing become permanent alliance procedures, so the merchants’ association can no longer approve herbs on its own.

Even while detained, he compiles a list of scent samples and personally reads an apology to his mother and the bereaved families every month.

/story_contents/B033/actors/0/outcomes/1.en:
K341 Tak Eunsol spends the night distributing the hidden legitimate herbs to patients and prevents acute deaths, but the packaging order is disrupted, weakening the evidence needed to hold the prime contractor legally accountable.

Some bereaved families accept him as a rescuer, while others call him someone evading responsibility, splitting the Medical Neutrality League in two.

As he collects new samples with Jeong Hojun, he also pledges to repay Dong Juha for the cost of the broken seal for the rest of his life.

/story_contents/B033/actors/0/outcomes/2.en:
K341 Tak Eunsol postpones the hearing and seals off the G13E15 Night Sorting Unit’s misclassifying conveyor and reading-control line, preserving the remaining herb supply route.

But with the ledger sealed long-term, both his negligence and the prime contractor’s crimes remain outside the official record, and his mother never learns the full story.

He tells only Dong Juha and Jeong Hojun where the truth lies, then stays beneath the market as a night inspector.

/story_contents/B033/actors/1/sections/정.en:
Tak Yunjae is a Korean maintenance worker who grew up in the northeastern Han River bridge district. She is more accustomed to reading vibrations in bridge piers and changes in road-surface load than to reading vehicles.

In the Seongbuk Line Gate Military Government, she is registered not as a driver avoiding responsibility for an accident but as a party to the collapse of the passageway.

Her present identity is shaped less by license or rank than by remembering the lane she closed and the number of people left behind.

/story_contents/B033/actors/1/sections/붕.en:
Before the Collapse, Tak Yunjae worked nights for a private bridge-inspection company, replacing crack sensors and drainage pumps.

The day before the accident, she closed a lane after repeated overload alarms. But on a superior’s order to reopen it, she temporarily removed the bollards on the understanding that she could put them back.

She could have reversed that decision before the vehicles converged, but once the evacuation convoy entered, the temporary opening effectively became a permanent route.

/story_contents/B033/actors/1/sections/가.en:
Tak Yunjae’s father painted buses at a depot, and his older sister repaired ropes at a landing beneath the bridge, so the family’s livelihood was directly tied to gateway traffic.

After the Collapse, he joins the Gate Military Government’s Ghost Dispatch Unit, comparing the number tags of vanished vehicles with their actual passengers.

At the Gateway Bureau, he serves as the accident liaison between Seon Solwoo’s pump crew and Yeong Hanmoe’s infirmary, but neither department gives him authority to open a lane.

/story_contents/B033/actors/1/sections/붕.en:
On a foggy night when the G14E08 Ghost Dispatch Unit imitated the headlights and horn of a scrapped bus, Tak Yunjae followed its false guidance signal and sent evacuation vehicles onto the weakened eastern span.

The span collapsed, trapping the rescue vehicle carrying her sister and eleven evacuees below the water’s surface. Over the final radio transmission, she heard her sister tell her to cut the rope.

Since then, she has heard phantom sounds and smelled wet paint while looking at empty bus seats. When she touches the accident rope, she unconsciously counts the traffic numbers backward.

/story_contents/B033/actors/1/sections/생.en:
Tak Yunjae discovers that the G14E08 Ghost Dispatch Unit leaves axle marks identical to those of real vehicles only when the pumps’ residual pressure drops.

He rewinds Seon Solwoo’s pump log to compare earlier times and stretches Yeong Hanmoe’s stretcher straps across each lane, creating a reversible control line that can turn back anyone who enters the wrong way.

Using this method, he prevents a third collapse and leads twenty-six survivors out along a reverse-direction footpath, becoming both a party to the accident and a gateway investigator.

/story_contents/B033/actors/1/sections/현.en:
Tak Yunjae now waits for the XT04-SC2 passage trial in his capacity as a party to the Gateway Bureau’s bridge-traffic accident.

He has not yet chosen whether to open the remaining western span to medical transport or first carry out the complete drainage Seon Solwoo demands.

Yeong Hanmoe gives a deadline for moving the injured, while the pump crew warns of the residual-pressure limit. Which pillar Tak Yunjae ties the accident rope to will determine the gateway’s next order.

/story_contents/B033/actors/1/sections/비.en:
Tak Yunjae hides the fact that, despite seeing the overload alarm before the accident, he wrote ‘sensor malfunction’ on the paperwork reopening the route.

When his sister’s rescue vehicle was excluded from the official dispatch list and her family was therefore denied survivor supplies, he inserted a fake number tag left by the Ghost Dispatch Unit into the genuine records.

That alteration got his niece food, but reduced another missing person’s share. Every month, he anonymously gives his own fuel coupons to that person’s family.

/story_contents/B033/actors/1/sections/관.en:
Just after the Collapse, Tak Yunjae was trapped with Seon Solwoo in the pump room, where they tapped the residual-pressure gauge by hand to maintain an air pocket beneath the bridge pier.

On the day Yeong Hanmoe suspended a stretcher from the accident rope to cross the torrent, Yun-jae secured the anchor point on the opposite bank. The two agreed to calculate the number of stretchers they could retrieve before counting people through the passage.

All three heard his sister’s final radio transmission, but they cannot agree whether her instruction to cut the rope was meant to save the entire rescue vehicle or addressed only to Tak Yunjae.

/story_contents/B033/actors/1/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, Tak Yunjae finds fresh tire marks beneath the closed eastern span and investigates the fact that vehicles from inside the gateway, not the Ghost Dispatch Unit, have been entering and leaving the accident site.

In Act 2, he matches Seon Solwoo’s pump log with Yeong Hanmoe’s stretcher assignment chart and obtains proof that his sister’s rescue vehicle was on an unofficial rescue mission. His own alteration of the paperwork comes to light at the same time.

In Act 3, three branches are presented: pushing through medical transport; blowing up the span to cut off the ghost signal; or converting the accident rope to pedestrian-only use and dismantling gateway authority.

/story_contents/B033/actors/1/sections/분.en:
In the first ending, Tak Yunjae gets a medical vehicle across under a restricted weight limit and saves the injured, but loses the western span, leaving Achagu isolated for a long time.

In the second ending, he blows up the span to cut off G14E08’s dispatch signal, but permanently submerges his sister’s rescue vehicle and the missing people’s remains.

In the third ending, he gives up vehicle traffic and builds a pedestrian stretcher network with Seon Solwoo and Yeong Hanmoe. After revealing his own alteration of the records, he remains a gateway laborer.

/story_contents/B033/actors/1/arc/0/summ.en:
K367 Tak Yunjae finds recently deposited tire rubber beneath a closed bridge pier, along with yellow paint used only on his sister’s rescue vehicle.

He asks Seon Solwoo not to stop the pumps. With Yeong Hanmoe, he marks the underwater investigation area with stretcher straps, securing a route back.

The traces cannot be explained by G14E08’s illusions alone, raising the suspicion that someone at the Gateway Bureau has been using the missing vehicle as a parts store.

/story_contents/B033/actors/1/arc/1/summ.en:
K367 Tak Yunjae compares the pump’s residual-pressure records with the times stretchers were retrieved and confirms that her sister’s rescue vehicle disappeared.

She confirms that it remained in an air pocket for the following three days.

She notices that the dispatch sheet that halted the rescue at the time bears handwriting pressure matching her own falsified sensor record, and realizes that an insider’s responsibility and her own wrongdoing are bound together in one document.

As the crack in the western span widens, the medical transport team arrives, making it impossible to recover the evidence and evacuate survivors at the same time.

/story_contents/B033/actors/1/arc/2/summ.en:
K367 Tak Yunjae, in Branch A, posts a restricted-load marker on the western span.

He gets the medical vehicles across and saves lives, but sacrifices the gateway’s last vehicle route.

In Branch B, he uses explosives to sever both spans and end the G14E08 Ghost Dispatch Unit’s signals, but gives up recovering the submerged vehicle and remains.

In Branch C, he abolishes the vehicle gateway. He builds a pedestrian network combining Seon Solwoo’s pumps with Yeong Hanmoe’s stretchers, and reveals his alteration of the dispatch sheet and his fuel-coupon debt.

/story_contents/B033/actors/1/outcomes/0.en:
K367 Tak Yunjae personally measures the medical convoy’s axle spacing, sends the vehicles over the western span one at a time, and saves thirteen critically ill patients.

The bridge collapses after the last vehicle clears it, cutting off Achagu’s vehicle trade, but Yeong Hanmoe’s infirmary obtains enough medicine to survive the winter.

He builds a manual-pump communications network with Seon Solwoo on both banks of the river, while continuing to bear responsibility for failing to find his sister’s remains.

/story_contents/B033/actors/1/outcomes/1.en:
K367 Tak Yunjae blows up the bridge-pier joints, eliminating the vibrations and lanes the G14E08 Ghost Dispatch Unit could imitate and preventing further accidents.

The blast buries her sister’s rescue vehicle and a box of missing-person records deep in the waterway, leaving the bereaved families unable even to obtain official death declarations.

She tells her niece the truth about the fake number tag, leaves the Gateway Bureau, and tends the markers for the submerged vehicles.

/story_contents/B033/actors/1/outcomes/2.en:
K367 Tak Yunjae abolishes vehicle traffic and, with Seon Solwoo and Yeong Hanmoe, builds a pedestrian stretcher network that moves according to the pumps’ residual pressure.

He reveals that he falsified the alarm record and forged the ration sheet, losing his qualifications, but the knot rules for the accident rope become the Gateway Bureau’s new passage law.

To repay the rations taken from another missing person’s family, he takes on transport work that sends him across the river every day.

/story_contents/B033/actors/2/sections/정.en:
Tak Pilho is a Korean worker who came to Seoul from inland South Gyeongsang Province and settled at the Garak Wholesale Market loading dock. He watches the movement speed of the entire queue before attending to individual families.

He was elected to represent the southbound evacuation ration crowd at the Myeongdong Union’s Main Hall Ratification Court, but comes from neither the bureaucracy nor the merchant class.

He maintains that his authority comes not from a ballot, but from remembering those who collapsed at the back of the queue.

/story_contents/B033/actors/2/sections/붕.en:
Before the Collapse, Tak Pilho made a living collecting empty boxes after the dawn vegetable auction and wiping condensation from cold-storage warehouses.

At the first evacuation alarm, he opened a temporary waiting section for families heading south. When protests grew, he changed the floor markings, believing he could restore the original freight route at any time.

But when the floodgate closed and the crowd surged in, the temporary section became the only entrance to the ration line, and a single marking determined the order of thousands of people.

/story_contents/B033/actors/2/sections/가.en:
Tak Pilho’s family owned neither a stake in the market nor a refrigerated warehouse, and his siblings worked as day laborers for different wholesalers.

After the Collapse, at the Main Hall Ratification Court, he memorizes the southbound evacuees’ places of origin, numbers of companions, and food allergies to reduce rationing errors.

Within the community, he mediates between Cheon Solbit’s plaza queue and Baek On’s southbound families, marking temporary places with the number of knots in box twine instead of paper tickets.

/story_contents/B033/actors/2/sections/붕.en:
On the day the G10E01 Flooded Mold Breathing Corps imitated breathing and coughing inside a wet ration tent, Tak Pilho split the queue in two to find infected people.

In fact, mold spores from the tent floor were concentrated in the separation area. Twenty-two children and older people suffocated there, including his older brother.

Since then, the smell of wet paper makes him overcount people, and he compulsively hands out temporary tickets even for empty places.

/story_contents/B033/actors/2/sections/생.en:
Tak Pilho discovers that the G10E01 Flooded Mold Breathing Corps follows the contracting sounds of waterlogged packing material, not human breathing.

With Cheon Solbit, he attaches colored twine to the plaza queue’s wet boxes so they can be moved to a dry area and then returned to their original places. He gives Baek On’s family a trial temporary ticket.

While the monsters follow a pile of empty packaging, he leads evacuees out through an elevated passage, transforming from the person responsible for the disastrous separation into a representative of the crowd.

/story_contents/B033/actors/2/sections/현.en:
Tak Pilho now sits in the southbound evacuee crowd’s representative seat just before the XT03-SC3 winter ration reform meeting.

He has not yet chosen whether to convert the temporary box-knot tickets into formal ration rights or end their validity to protect existing residents’ stores.

Cheon Solbit warns that the plaza queue could erupt, while Baek On pleads that the families may be pushed south again. His single vote will determine where tens of thousands of meals go.

/story_contents/B033/actors/2/sections/비.en:
Tak Pilho hides the fact that there was a mold warning sign in the separation area where his brother died, but he covered it with the tent because he feared the crowd would turn back.

To make the temporary tickets he gave Baek On’s family, he untied and used ration cords left for the dead; one came from his brother’s wrist.

He promised Cheon Solbit he would maintain order in the plaza, but reported fewer southbound family members than there really were. He owes debts to both sides that he has yet to repay.

/story_contents/B033/actors/2/sections/관.en:
On the day Cheon Solbit drew a chalk curve across the plaza floor to reduce the risk of a crush, Tak Pilho aligned the height of the boxes along each queue to keep sightlines clear.

When Baek On’s southbound family was separated at a checkpoint, he gave them his brother’s wrist cord as a temporary ticket, allowing the three family members to stay in the same section.

The three also dismantled the flooded tent together. Unaware that Tak Pilho had covered the warning sign, the others remember him for his role in the rescue.

/story_contents/B033/actors/2/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, Tak Pilho investigates why temporary tickets assigned to people recorded as dead keep being used for night rations, and discovers a cold-storage warehouse group collecting tickets for empty places.

In Act 2, he compares Cheon Solbit’s queue records with the knots on Baek On’s family’s cords and confirms that his brother’s ticket became the reference ticket for a bundle traded on the black market.

In Act 3, three branches become feasible: converting temporary tickets into citizenship; invalidating all of them and recounting stored supplies; or opening the flooded warehouse and replacing distribution with communal cooking.

/story_contents/B033/actors/2/sections/분.en:
In the first ending, Tak Pilho recognizes temporary-ticket holders as residents entitled to regular rations, protecting the families who fled south, but accepts the risk of a riot as existing residents’ winter shares shrink.

In the second ending, he invalidates all temporary tickets to end the black market, but the refugees, including Baek On’s family, must move again.

In the third ending, he reveals the hidden flooded warehouse and begins communal cooking with Cheon Solbit, but his responsibility for covering the warning sign also comes to light.

/story_contents/B033/actors/2/arc/0/summ.en:
K392 Tak Pilho finds a triple-twisted knot, identical to the one on his older brother’s wrist cord, on a sack of dried beans collected in a dead person’s name.

He has Cheon Solbit keep the line in the square in place. Investigating the refrigerated warehouse at night with Baek On, he discovers a rule under which temporary tickets for vacant places are exchanged according to the height of particular boxes.

The black-market organization was selling floor spaces less contaminated with mold, not selling them for money, and the rationing problem becomes a question of breathable space.

/story_contents/B033/actors/2/arc/1/summ.en:
K392 Tak Pilho checks the warning-sign number he covered against the demolition list for the flooded tents.

He learns how his older brother’s cord became the black market’s reference marker.

He could complete the evidence by taking back Baek On’s family’s temporary tickets, but hesitates because doing so would immediately expel the family from the ration line.

Hungry residents and refugees converge on Cheon Solbit’s square at the same time, and opening the refrigerated warehouse door even once will release both spores and food.

/story_contents/B033/actors/2/arc/2/summ.en:
K392 Tak Pilho, in branch A, converts temporary tickets into formal rights, settles the refugees who fled south, and accepts a reduction in existing stores.

In branch B, he burns all cord tickets and recounts everyone, ending the black market but sending Baek On’s family back onto the road.

In branch C, he reveals the flooded warehouse and opens a communal kitchen with Cheon Solbit. He burns the spore zone of G10E01 and reveals his responsibility for covering the warning sign.

/story_contents/B033/actors/2/outcomes/0.en:
K392 Tak Pilho compares the knots on the temporary tickets with family testimony, grants refugees formal ration rights, and keeps Baek On’s family in Garak.

Existing residents’ stores shrink, but Cheon Solbit turns the line in the square into rotating cooking teams, preventing an immediate clash.

Rather than hanging his older brother’s cord at the representative’s seat, he returns it to the victims’ register and discloses the cost of expanding rights every day.

/story_contents/B033/actors/2/outcomes/1.en:
K392 Tak Pilho invalidates every temporary ticket and recounts those entitled to rations from the beginning, dismantling the black-market network at the refrigerated warehouse.

Baek On’s family and hundreds of refugees who fled south lose their grounds for staying and leave for another checkpoint, leaving empty sections in the square.

He remains representative, but is accused of using his older brother’s ticket as a pretext to erase people, and records the number departing each day.

/story_contents/B033/actors/2/outcomes/2.en:
K392 Tak Pilho tears down a wall of the flooded warehouse, exposing both the food and the mold zone, and establishes a communal cooking system with Cheon Solbit and Baek On.

The remaining spores of G10E01, the Flood Mold Respiratory Cluster, are removed, but half the stored food is discarded, forcing everyone to endure reduced rations.

He admits his guilt in covering the warning sign, steps down as representative, and takes charge of ventilating the tents of families harmed by suffocation.

/story_contents/B033/actors/3/sections/정.en:
Mae Dohan is an ethnic Korean document specialist raised in Seoul’s southern administrative district who has made a living arranging sentences governed by different rules so they do not conflict.

At the Suseo Line Jeongdong General Labor Union, he is defined not as the author of the five unification proposals but as an involved party with a record of access to the draft box.

He is someone who tracks who deleted which words and which districts were left without protection as a result, rather than the agreement itself.

/story_contents/B033/actors/3/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, Mae Dohan worked as a proofreader for an international conference translation and interpretation firm, aligning contract terminology with disaster-response annexes.

Just before the collapse, he temporarily deleted a clause prohibiting regional transfers of medical data from the emergency unification proposal of five organizations, believing it could be restored in the next corrected version.

When the conference hall closed, the temporary version became the only document in force. Because of that one deleted sentence, outlying clinics lost both medicines and patient records.

/story_contents/B033/actors/3/sections/가.en:
Mae Dohan’s family consisted not of legal professionals but of print-shop bookbinders and school administrative workers, and from childhood he saw typographical errors change actual ration quantities.

After the collapse, he manages the draft box’s metal type and sealing paper at the Jeongdong General Labor Union in district HC02.

As an involved party, he may open Ha Seojin’s draft box and has limited authority to compare Yun Seorin’s Record Federation text side by side with copies of an external multinational agreement.

/story_contents/B033/actors/3/sections/붕.en:
On the night G11E09, the Personalized Medical Remnant, combined genetic markers in patient records with voice commands to attack specific people, the transfer-prohibition clause Mae Dohan had deleted meant that anonymization devices were not supplied to the outlying clinics.

The remnant identified his younger sibling and thirty-one patients by their medication patterns rather than their names, and lured people out at the shelter door by mimicking a treatment voice.

Since his sibling’s final prescription code overlapped with his own proofreading mark, Mae Dohan has been unable to erase a person’s name from a sentence.

/story_contents/B033/actors/3/sections/생.en:
Mae Dohan discovers that G11E09, the Personalized Medical Remnant, cannot process older prescriptions that contradict one another, unlike the latest records.

He takes the pre-deletion text from Ha Seojin’s draft box, making a rubbing with a thin wax sheet so the seal can be restored, and feeds it in alongside Yun Seorin’s Record Federation text and copies of the external agreement.

While the remnant stalls between conflicting commands, he helps patients from the outlying clinics escape, changing from a proofreader who hides text into a party to the draft who takes responsibility for conflicts between rules.

/story_contents/B033/actors/3/sections/현.en:
Mae Dohan currently sits at the text-comparison table between five delegations just before ratification of the XT03-SC1 unification proposal.

He has not yet chosen whether to restore the deleted clause exactly as written or deliberately retain contradictory clauses to control the Personalized Medical Remnant.

Ha Seojin objects to the damage to the draft box’s seal, while Yun Seorin demands separate approval procedures for record sovereignty and the copies of the external agreement.

/story_contents/B033/actors/3/sections/비.en:
Mae Dohan conceals that deleting the clause was not a simple mistake but the result of following paid instructions from the firm that hired him to shorten the meeting.

He changed one character of a patient code to move his younger sibling ahead in the treatment order, and the patient displaced by that change died in a G11E09 attack.

He also secretly lent Yun Seorin the wax rubbing made from Ha Seojin’s draft box so she could complete the Record Federation text, leaving him with a legal debt to all three document systems.

/story_contents/B033/actors/3/sections/관.en:
On the first day of lockdown, Mae Dohan and Ha Seojin hid the draft box underwater in a bathtub to protect it from fire and looting; only the two of them know about the reverse-facing groove on its seal pin.

When Yun Seorin wrote the Record Federation text, he reconstructed deleted patient names using codes specific to each region, and together they marked five sentences that conflicted with the copy of the multinational agreement she had brought.

The two share the achievement of having stopped the remnant with contradictory text during the rescue at the outlying clinics, but disagree on whether that text can remain law in ordinary times.

/story_contents/B033/actors/3/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, Mae Dohan discovers that identical clause numbers among the type for the five unification proposals have been cast in different metals, and investigates who intends to change the text at the moment of ratification.

In Act 2, he compares Ha Seojin’s seal records, Yun Seorin’s reconstructed text, and the external approval sheet Yun Seorin holds, and learns that the price of the instruction to delete the clause was a deal over control of the city.

In Act 3, three branches confront one another: restoring the original text and holding a public trial; retaining contradictory clauses as a barrier against the remnant; or discarding the five unification proposals and moving to a system of mutual approval between districts.

/story_contents/B033/actors/3/sections/분.en:
In the first ending, Mae Dohan discloses the paid deletion order and his manipulation of a patient code, restores the original text, and is punished, but revives the outlying clinics’ right to transfer data.

In the second ending, he contains G11E09 with deliberately contradictory clauses, but residents of the treaty city become subject to different laws.

In the third ending, he discards the unification proposal and connects Yun Seorin’s Record Federation text with copies of the external agreement through mutual approval, but Gangnam’s single chain of command is dismantled.

/story_contents/B033/actors/3/arc/0/summ.en:
K417 Mae Dohan finds that the same clause number on the type plate for ratification is set in a mixture of lead and iron.

He asks Ha Seojin to close the draft box.

Holding Yun Seorin’s Record Federation copy over the external approval sheet she keeps and shining light through them, he confirms that the replacement sentence would make outlying patients’ records the property of the central authority.

The person replacing the type even knows about the reverse-facing groove on the seal pin, so everyone who guarded the draft box in the past comes under suspicion.

/story_contents/B033/actors/3/arc/1/summ.en:
K417 Mae Dohan confirms that the paid instruction received by his firm and traces of the patient-code change came from the same bundle of papers.

He tells Ha Seojin about lending out the wax rubbing. He synchronizes the effective times of the three documents with Yun Seorin, but revealing the truth would also immediately invalidate the contradictory clauses that have been stopping G11E09.

Before the ratification bell rings, the remnant approaches an outlying relay station, forcing him to establish either legal consistency or a physical barrier first.

/story_contents/B033/actors/3/arc/2/summ.en:
K417 Mae Dohan, in branch A, discloses the original text and the paid deletion order, corrects the unification proposal, and faces trial himself for manipulating a patient code.

In branch B, he deliberately keeps conflicting medical clauses in force to contain G11E09, the Personalized Medical Remnant, but institutionalizes differences in residents’ rights.

In branch C, he discards the five unification proposals. He connects Ha Seojin’s draft, Yun Seorin’s Record Federation text, and copies of the external multinational agreement in a mutual-approval network, relinquishing unified command.

/story_contents/B033/actors/3/outcomes/0.en:
K417 Mae Dohan lays the pre-deletion original text and the firm’s instruction sheet on the ratification table, restoring the outlying clinics’ rights to transfer records and access medicines.

His manipulation of a patient code is exposed too, and he is detained, but Ha Seojin and Yun Seorin add a rule to the new agreement requiring that proofreading histories remain indelible in the type.

Yun Seorin attaches copies of approvals from external cities to finalize the restored text and leaves his younger sibling’s name in the victims’ appendix.

/story_contents/B033/actors/3/outcomes/1.en:
K417 Mae Dohan puts contradictory medical orders into effect, trapping G11E09, the Personalized Medical Remnant, in a computational loop at the city boundary.

The barrier holds, but residents receive different treatment under the rules depending on their district of origin, making the treaty city’s claim to unity effectively a fiction.

He becomes a permanent administrator who proofreads the contradictory clauses every day but can never completely correct a single sentence.

/story_contents/B033/actors/3/outcomes/2.en:
K417 Mae Dohan melts down the type for the five unification proposals and links the three document systems so they approve one another issue by issue, ending the central authority’s monopoly on power.

Yun Seorin connects the Record Federation text and copies of the external agreement, but Ha Seojin’s draft box can no longer issue final orders, slowing crisis response.

He loses his status as an involved party and becomes a courier carrying texts between districts, preventing a repeat of the single point of failure created by his deletion.

/story_contents/B033/actors/4/sections/정.en:
Chae Hansol is an ethnic Korean power-generation equipment operator raised in the floodgate district of southwestern Seoul who notices fluctuations in current and differences in fuel viscosity before she notices the sound of an engine.

She is the emergency power-generation operations chief at Sinjeong Base of the Water Compact, not a political commander or an approver of power distribution.

She understands her role not as someone who produces a lot of electricity, but as someone responsible for calculating how long each person’s life-support equipment can hold out.

/story_contents/B033/actors/4/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, Chae Hansol conducted monthly test runs of the wastewater treatment plant’s emergency generators and managed battery electrolyte and cooling-water components.

Just before the major flood warning, she intended to shut down an aging generator to replace its bearing, but left the parts disassembled so it could be restarted immediately if an order came to maintain supply.

As flooding began, the maintenance room was sealed off, turning that reversible shutdown into a long-term loss. The base had to keep both the floodgates and the moored train going with just two generators.

/story_contents/B033/actors/4/sections/가.en:
Chae Hansol’s family worked not as power-company executives but as a substation cleaner and a metal cutter, and he learned the specifications of discarded parts hands-on.

After the collapse, at Sinjeong Base in HC14, he establishes a principle of following Han Jaemok’s orders to maintain supply but not signing off on concealed power distribution.

Supporting Heo Eunchan’s allocation of power to the moored train from the generation side, he divides up the startup times of the floodgate motors, isolation beds, and water-intake pumps down to the second.

/story_contents/B033/actors/4/sections/붕.en:
On the night G01E06, the Flood Boar Herd, was drawn to the low-frequency vibrations of a flooded transformer, Chae Hansol cut power to the moored train for twelve minutes to keep the floodgate motor running.

During that time, two ventilators in an isolation carriage stopped, killing one child patient and one nurse, and the boar herd rammed the cable conduit, flooding even the backup-battery warehouse.

Since then, she has heard a phantom shutdown alarm exactly every twelve minutes and hears even an unloaded engine as though it were a person breathing.

/story_contents/B033/actors/4/sections/생.en:
Chae Hansol discovers that G01E06, the Flood Boar Herd, responds to irregular leakage current flowing through grounding plates rather than to the generators themselves.

He temporarily sets aside Han Jaemok’s supply order and, with Heo Eunchan, installs insulated connectors so the moored train’s carriages can be manually disconnected and reconnected, preserving power for life-support equipment.

He then uses the copper winding of a discarded crane as a grounding lure to draw the boar herd into an empty retention basin, gaining the operations chief’s authority and establishing his principle of refusing concealed power distribution.

/story_contents/B033/actors/4/sections/현.en:
Chae Hansol is currently in the control room as Sinjeong Base’s emergency power-generation operations chief, just before the XT05-SC2 decision on restarting the floodgates.

Only three days’ worth of fuel remains at rated operation, there is one set of replacement bearings, and the flooded third generator can be used for at most six hours even if its shaft is realigned.

He has not yet chosen which circuit to keep alive first: Han Jaemok’s order to supply every district or Heo Eunchan’s priority allocation to the moored train.

/story_contents/B033/actors/4/sections/비.en:
Chae Hansol hides the fact that, during the moored train’s blackout, he secretly sent power not only to two isolation carriages but also to the command communications room, and that this diversion brought forward the time the ventilators stopped.

He keeps the power-distribution sheet bearing Han Jaemok’s signature, but his own hand operated the switch, so he cannot blame the order alone.

He told Heo Eunchan that he moved the dead patients’ equipment’s remaining battery power to other patients, but he also owes him for using one pack to test the third generator’s ignition.

/story_contents/B033/actors/4/sections/관.en:
During the first flood, Chae Hansol and Han Jaemok lifted the floodgate control panel while standing in knee-deep water. There, they agreed that Chae would obey orders to maintain supply but refuse power distribution whose destination was concealed.

While Heo Eunchan memorized the patient priorities for each carriage of the moored train, Chae calculated battery charge levels and cable lengths, and together they devised the actual connection order.

The three reconstructed the blackout’s duration using the dead nurse’s watch, but did not record responsibility for the diversion of power to the communications room in the official log.

/story_contents/B033/actors/4/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, Chae Hansol inspects the layer of water at the bottom of the fuel tank and the bearing’s metal filings, discovering that someone altered the gauge markings to make three days’ worth of fuel at rated operation look like five.

In Act 2, he compares Han Jaemok’s demand for secret communications with Heo Eunchan’s battery limits for each patient, and confirms that the only bearing that could save the third generator is also the specification needed by the floodgate motor.

In Act 3, three branches open: prioritizing the floodgates to preserve the base; maintaining the moored train’s life-support equipment to the end; or sacrificing a generator as bait to isolate G01E06 and evacuating on foot without power.

/story_contents/B033/actors/4/sections/분.en:
In the first ending, Chae Hansol puts the bearing in the floodgate motor and prevents the flood, but cuts power to the moored train in stages, losing some critically ill patients.

In the second ending, she concentrates the remaining fuel and batteries on the moored train to save its patients, but the Watergate Government offices and warehouse flood.

In the third ending, she drives the third generator into an overload to use it as bait, traps G01E06 in the retention basin, and evacuates on foot with only the people and records, having lost all power.

/story_contents/B033/actors/4/arc/0/summ.en:
K021 Chae Hansol discovers that the fuel gauge’s seal wire has been retied from the inside.

He measures the actual amount remaining and confirms the limit of three days at rated operation.

He has Heo Eunchan remeasure the batteries in each carriage and reports to Han Jaemok that supplying every district simultaneously is physically impossible.

Bearing filings are found in both the floodgate motor and the third generator, making the choice of which machine receives the one remaining set of parts the central issue.

/story_contents/B033/actors/4/arc/1/summ.en:
K021 Chae Hansol traces the hidden communications-room circuit and learns that Han Jaemok really has been communicating with outside rescuers, but neither the probability of success nor the arrival time has been recorded.

With Heo Eunchan, he calculates the finite battery life of each patient’s equipment minute by minute and reveals that the battery pack he used for an ignition test reduced one carriage’s reserve.

As G01E06, the Flood Boar Herd, approaches the base by following leakage current, there is time to run only one of the floodgates, the moored train, or the decoy generator at full capacity.

/story_contents/B033/actors/4/arc/2/summ.en:
K021 Chae Hansol, in branch A, puts the last bearing in the floodgate motor.

He implements restricted power distribution and protects the base, but gives up some life-support equipment.

In branch B, he concentrates fuel and parts on the moored train, saves Heo Eunchan’s patients, and accepts the flooding of Han Jaemok’s offices and warehouse.

In branch C, he overloads the third generator as a stationary decoy to trap G01E06, the Flood Boar Herd, in a retention basin. He gives up the possibility of restoring power, shuts it off, and evacuates everyone on foot.

/story_contents/B033/actors/4/outcomes/0.en:
K021 Chae Hansol installs the last bearing in the floodgate motor, closes the discharge gate, and protects Sinjeong Base and the downstream residential area from flooding.

The moored train is subjected to rolling blackouts, and Heo Eunchan moves patients, but some critically ill patients whose batteries run short do not survive.

He reveals the concealed power distribution to the communications room and loses his operations chief position, then reconstructs the time each dead patient’s equipment lost power for their family.

/story_contents/B033/actors/4/outcomes/1.en:
K021 Chae Hansol concentrates the generator fuel and remaining batteries on the moored train’s life-support equipment, allowing most of the patients under Heo Eunchan’s care to be moved to a safe area.

The floodgate motor stops, flooding the offices and warehouse. Han Jaemok’s supply system collapses, but a small, people-centered power community forms around the carriages.

He acknowledges the battery he owes for the ignition test and becomes a maintenance worker who restores flooded parts by hand.

/story_contents/B033/actors/4/outcomes/2.en:
K021 Chae Hansol secures the third generator to the cable conduit and overloads it, luring G01E06, the Flood Boar Herd, into an empty retention basin. He lowers the barrier.

The runaway generator and all spare parts are destroyed, making it impossible to restart Sinjeong Base, but Han Jaemok and Heo Eunchan evacuate with only the people, patient records, and portable batteries.

He throws the final switch himself and, hearing the moment his phantom twelve-minute alarm stops, becomes responsible for the hand-operated pumps at a settlement without power.

/story_contents/B033/actors/5/sections/정.en:
Byeon Jua is an ethnic Korean power-operations technician raised in substation housing behind the Guro tool market in Seoul.

On site, she learned to detect changes in electrical load from the smell of plating baths and the vibrations of sewing machines before seeing them on a voltmeter.

After the collapse, she combines this instinct with the Standards Alliance’s standards, establishing herself as someone who distributes power according to the harm an outage would cause rather than production volume.

/story_contents/B033/actors/5/sections/붕.en:
Byeon Jua worked the night shift for a private power broker, using a color-banded circuit chart to allocate electricity to Guro’s plating factories, refrigerated warehouses, and garment workshops.

When the company ordered her to provide stable frequency only to businesses that raised their bids, she secretly changed the relay markings for three workshops on the verge of closing to delay their disconnection.

The change could have been reversed by realigning the original plans and blue seals, but the collapse halted the audit and left the matter unresolved.

/story_contents/B033/actors/5/sections/가.en:
Byeon Jua’s family ran a small motor-rewinding shop, making a living through their skill at rewinding defective copper and their credit in trade.

In her current organization, the Yeongdeungpo Line Standards Alliance, she is the Guro power trunk line’s generation operations chief and decides the startup order for the furnace, drinking-water pumps, and surgical lights.

Applying her family’s method of keeping accounts of goods sold on credit, she measures electricity not in kilowatts but in units of recoverable working time.

/story_contents/B033/actors/5/sections/붕.en:
On the first day of the collapse, the G13E02 Night-Sorting Swarm mimicked a substation's blinking signals as worker call lamps and lured the night shift into the breaker room.

Byeon Jua brought two trunk lines online at once to save her colleague Choi Munsik, but reverse-phase current locked the fire-door magnets and trapped six people inside.

Afterward, the sight of a particular orange indicator lamp stiffened her fingers, and she could not erase the calculation that the workshop power she saved had locked that door.

/story_contents/B033/actors/5/sections/생.en:
Byeon Jua found in the current logs of a decommissioned-line cutter that the G13E02 Night-Sorting Swarm gathered not on a fixed shift cycle but only when loads changed sharply.

In a reversible test, she exchanged the color bands of three circuits and had Heo Daon time the manual fuses so they could be restored if it failed.

When the test succeeded, the Alliance could separate a false load to lure the creatures from the survival equipment, and Byeon Jua changed from a mere operator into the decision-maker for the trunk lines.

/story_contents/B033/actors/5/sections/현.en:
Byeon Jua was the power-trunk generation operator for the Guro branch of the Yeongdeungpo Line Standards Alliance, under orders to execute Park Soeon's bidding results through circuit colors.

She lent only midnight frequencies to Heo Daon's test runs, but retained the authority to pull the insulation pin herself on site if they exceeded the allowance.

Now, before a dawn load table that could start only one of the heat-treatment furnace and the evacuation lift line first, she delayed her choice with no color band yet hung.

/story_contents/B033/actors/5/sections/비.en:
Byeon Jua hid the original blue seal she had altered before the collapse in the ceiling of a motor-winding shop, knowing that if the document emerged, even the surviving workshops' power rights would be void.

She told Choi Munsik's family only that an old magnetic door caused the accident, while the actual reverse-phase activation log remained on her personal frequency meter.

She also owed a technical debt: in return for the reserve copper busbar she received from Park Soeon, she must unconditionally execute one future bid.

/story_contents/B033/actors/5/sections/관.en:
Before the collapse, Park Soeon was the bid auditor at the power brokerage where Byeon Jua worked; even after finding a discrepancy in the blue seal, she delayed her report a day after seeing the workshop workers' unpaid-wage list.

As a test-facility technician that same night, Heo Daon recorded Byeon Jua's circuit-exchange times to the second, and still keeps the record as collateral for the test run.

The three were not allies covering one another's illegal acts; they were bound by their failure to agree on when to restore the one alteration that could once be reversed.

/story_contents/B033/actors/5/sections/3.en:
Byeon Jua's first act was the process by which a reversible alteration hardened into a long-term responsibility when Park Soeon's audit stopped on the final inspection day that could have restored the old blue seal.

In the present of the second act, she stood immediately before choosing whether to start the heat-treatment furnace to make protective plates or the evacuation lift line to move isolated residents.

The third act unfolded all three paths: restoring the color bands and cutting workshop power, drawing the Night-Sorting Swarm with a false load, or melting her hidden copper busbar to start both systems.

/story_contents/B033/actors/5/sections/분.en:
If Byeon Jua restored the seal, the evacuation lift line came back to life, but the workshops' heat treatment stopped and the Alliance's protective-plate contract was broken.

If she chose the false load, she could trap the G13E02 Night-Sorting Swarm in the abandoned substation, but Heo Daon's test facility was lost and Park Soeon's bidding authority was shaken.

If she melted the hidden copper busbar, she could start the two systems in sequence, but the physical evidence of her pre-collapse alteration and the last legacy of her family's winding shop disappeared together.

/story_contents/B033/actors/5/arc/0/summ.en:
K049 Byeon Jua changed the blue seal and the color-banded circuit chart before the collapse to delay power loss at three workshops.

She judged that the change could be reversed if only the original drawings were plugged back in.

Park Soeon held the audit report for a day and Heo Daon recorded the exchange time, confirming that all three still had a chance to restore it.

But the collapse began, the inspection day disappeared, and the temporary alteration became a long-term order deciding which facility to save first.

/story_contents/B033/actors/5/arc/1/summ.en:
K049 Byeon Jua finished calculating that the heat-treatment furnace and the evacuation lift line now demanded the same starting power, yet left the final color band hanging on an empty hook.

Park Soeon offered the protective-plate deadline, and Heo Daon the remaining oxygen of the isolated residents, but neither gave an order; they presented only the cost of choosing.

After inspecting the hidden copper busbar and the false-load circuit, Byeon Jua stopped just before deciding which of the three means to use.

/story_contents/B033/actors/5/arc/2/summ.en:
In the third act, K049 Byeon Jua faced every branch: restoring the seal to save only the lift line, using a false load to draw the G13E02 Night-Sorting Swarm, or melting the secret busbar to start both systems in sequence.

The first path demanded the workshops' contract, the second Heo Daon's equipment and Park Soeon's authority, and the third the physical evidence of the alteration and her house's legacy.

In no ending could she call power allocation a neutral technique, and she had to repair the loss she chose herself.

/story_contents/B033/actors/5/outcomes/0.en:
K049 Byeon Jua restored the blue seal and concentrated power on the evacuation lift line, rescuing the isolated residents.

But the heat-treatment furnace cooled, the protective-plate delivery failed, and the workshops that lost power reclaimed from her the time she had once gained through alteration.

She judged.

She kept her generation-operator post, but each week she worked the workshops' manual presses herself to make up the cancelled contract volume.

/story_contents/B033/actors/5/outcomes/1.en:
K049 Byeon Jua created a false load at the abandoned substation. She lured the G13E02 Night-Sorting Swarm there and achieved a brief staggered start for the heat-treatment furnace and lift line.

Heo Daon's test equipment burned out from overheating, and Park Soeon lost part of her bidding authority for using unapproved frequencies.

Byeon Jua did not become the hero of the surviving facilities; she chose the long repair of remaking and repaying the instruments and authority she borrowed from the two.

/story_contents/B033/actors/5/outcomes/2.en:
K049 Byeon Jua melted together the copper busbar hidden in the winding-shop ceiling and the blue seal, starting the two facilities in order.

The residents and workshops both escaped immediate harm, but the physical evidence proving the Choi Munsik accident and the pre-collapse circuit alteration vanished beyond recovery.

She removed her family's trade name from the generator housing, procured a new busbar on personal guarantee, and repaid an unrecorded responsibility with a lifetime of power allotments.

/story_contents/B033/actors/6/sections/정.en:
Chae Mujin was a Korean-descended facilities operator born into a seed-merchant family in Haenam, South Jeolla, who learned refrigeration and emergency generators together.

She treated seeds not as life entire but as a bundle of promises with differing temperatures, moisture, and germination periods.

After the collapse, she became the emergency-generator operator of the Yangjae Machineworks Company's seed-preservation depot, deciding which generation of crops would receive the limited fuel.

/story_contents/B033/actors/6/sections/붕.en:
Chae Mujin worked as a low-temperature warehouse technician for a private seed company, managing cooling priorities for native sorghum, salt-tolerant barley, and patented tomatoes.

On the day the company ordered her to save only patented seed, she switched the temperature sensors for her hometown farmers' sorghum drawer and the corporate tomato drawer, planning to put them back at the next scheduled defrost.

The sensor switch was reversible, but when automatic defrosting stopped in the collapse, it became unclear which drawer had originally been under contract.

/story_contents/B033/actors/6/sections/가.en:
Chae Mujin's family sold saved seed and small water-pump parts together at the Haenam market, and took payment for seed after the harvest in poor years.

Now she ran generators for the Yongsan Line Yangjae Machineworks Company and the HP03 preservation facility, calculating the amount that could actually multiply in the next planting season rather than its research value.

Because of the deferred-payment practice her family taught her, she recorded fuel not as consumption but as debt borrowed from a future harvest.

/story_contents/B033/actors/6/sections/붕.en:
The G19E14 Coolant-Index Fungal Body learned pipe temperatures from the pigments in the coolant, then colored the valves of the coldest seed room and workers' skin the same hue.

Trying to isolate her infected older sister Chae Yura, Chae Mujin drained the blue coolant wrongly and lost half the salt-tolerant barley samples to thermal shock.

Her sister did not survive, and she kept a blue-stained glove and an emptied seed drawer as a pair of failures.

/story_contents/B033/actors/6/sections/생.en:
Chae Mujin confirmed at an abandoned aquaculture-farm circulator that the G19E14 Coolant-Index Fungal Body tracked not color itself but the order of temperature layers made by the pump.

In a short reversible test, he shut the generator down for ninety seconds and restarted it in reverse order, timing Park Jinsol's sealing time and Jeong Harin's release of the lock to guide the fungal body into an empty settling tank.

This success preserved the seed depot's core drawers, and Chae Mujin became an emergency-generator operator handling fuel and seal timing together.

/story_contents/B033/actors/6/sections/현.en:
As emergency-generator operator of the Yongsan Line Yangjae Machineworks Company's seed-preservation depot, Chae Mujin fulfilled a contract to keep generation running to Park Jinsol's sealing schedule.

When Jeong Harin's lock came down, he immediately pulled the switch and put isolation procedure before a researcher's further experiments.

The remaining fuel could cool the staple-seed depot three more days or heat-wash the contaminated drainage wing once, and he had not yet opened either valve.

/story_contents/B033/actors/6/sections/비.en:
Because he switched the sensors before the collapse, Chae Mujin knew the ownership seal for the patented tomatoes was effectively attached to the wrong drawer.

He owed Park Jinsol one sealing-time slot in return for asking to preserve his sister's last blood sample with seed-depot power.

Without Jeong Harin's knowledge, he hung the blue-stained glove in the drainage wing; though he knew it might mark a way to summon the fungal body again, he could not discard it.

/story_contents/B033/actors/6/sections/관.en:
Before the collapse, Park Jinsol was the seed company's statutory sealing officer and recorded Chae Mujin's entry time on the night he switched the sensors, but could not verify the drawer numbers.

Jeong Harin was the same company's safety-lock technician; after personally lowering the door that isolated Chae Yura, he told Chae Mujin the manual switch's location.

The three shared a past bound not by who owned the seeds, but by which surviving crop would lose legal protection if they removed the wrongly applied seal now.

/story_contents/B033/actors/6/sections/3.en:
In the first act, Chae Mujin waited for a defrost period that would let her return the sensors to their places, then met the collapse and left a reversible shortcut as a seed-ownership dispute.

In the present of the second act, she had to stake all remaining fuel between cooling the staple-seed depot and heat-washing the drainage wing, but had not yet taken the start handle.

The third act unfolded every path: preserving the staple grain, burning the fungal body, or thawing the patented tomatoes into fermentation liquid for fuel.

/story_contents/B033/actors/6/sections/분.en:
If she chose to cool the staple grain, the basis for the next planting season remained, but the G19E14 Coolant-Index Fungal Body multiplied in the drainage wing and blocked Magok's waterways for a long time.

If she chose heat washing, the contamination stopped, but sorghum and barley germination rates plunged and seed contracts with other communities broke.

If she turned the patented tomatoes into fermented fuel, she could perform both jobs at reduced scale, but Chae Mujin's sensor alteration and the mistaken ownership seal became public.

/story_contents/B033/actors/6/arc/0/summ.en:
K077 Chae Mujin switched the patented tomatoes and temperature sensors before the collapse to save native sorghum, and could have restored them at the next scheduled defrost.

He calculated.

Park Jinsol's seal remained in place and Jeong Harin's lock record remained too, so the alteration still had room for both technical and administrative reversal.

But the cooling network's collapse and his sister's isolation overlapped, the point of restoration vanished, and the switched sensors entangled even ownership of the surviving seed.

/story_contents/B033/actors/6/arc/1/summ.en:
K077 Chae Mujin placed the remaining fuel canister on scales beside the generator and recalculated the consumption of staple-grain cooling and drainage-wing heat washing.

Park Jinsol conveyed the seal's expiry time, and Jeong Harin the pressure the lock could withstand, but neither undertook the final start for him.

He checked even the possibility of using the wrongly sealed patented tomatoes as a third fuel, then released the handle just before choosing.

/story_contents/B033/actors/6/arc/2/summ.en:
In the third act, K077 Chae Mujin passed through every branch: saving the staple-seed depot three more days, heat-washing the drainage wing where the G19E14 Coolant-Index Fungal Body hid, and thawing patented tomatoes into fermentation fuel.

Each path made her give up one of Magok's waterways, the next planting season, or concealment of the pre-collapse sensor alteration.

Whatever the result, she had to stop using her sister's glove as a marker and divide contamination from ownership again with separate seals.

/story_contents/B033/actors/6/outcomes/0.en:
K077 Chae Mujin put fuel into the staple-seed depot and preserved the germination capacity of sorghum and salt-tolerant barley for three more days.

As the G19E14 Coolant-Index Fungal Body spread deep into the drainage wing, Magok's waterways closed and the research council had to commit substantial labor to outside water transport.

She kept her seed-depot post, but every day measured the contaminated waterway's manual temperature layers, repaying the present water debt for future planting.

/story_contents/B033/actors/6/outcomes/1.en:
K077 Chae Mujin aligned Jeong Harin's lock with Park Jinsol's sealing time, heat-washed the drainage wing, and burned the fungal body's index structure.

Cooling for the staple-grain drawers stopped, germination rates fell sharply, and he could fulfill only half the propagation promise made to Haenam farms.

He did not reserve the surviving seed for research, but planted it himself in the salt-content test field and chose to restore the reduced germination rate through labor.

/story_contents/B033/actors/6/outcomes/2.en:
K077 Chae Mujin thawed the wrongly sealed patented tomatoes and fermented their sugars, securing divided fuel for cooling and washing.

The seed and drainage wing were preserved together, but the sensor-exchange record emerged, making Park Jinsol's sealing contract and Chae Mujin's operating authority subjects of review at once.

In exchange for losing her authority, she remeasured the actual germination result of every drawer and made a new register based on multiplication potential rather than ownership.

/story_contents/B033/actors/7/sections/정.en:
O Doyun was a third-generation Koryo-saram born in Chirchiq, Tashkent Region, Uzbekistan, who moved to Incheon with his parents in 2012 and settled in Noryangjin.

At home he used Russian, Koryo-mar with his grandparents, and Korean and basic Uzbek at the market and dock.

Before the collapse, he brokered small vessels carrying chilled seafood and medical gel; now he turned his knowledge of those routes into votes in the carrier-shipowners' council.

/story_contents/B033/actors/7/sections/붕.en:
O Doyun linked his father's used refrigerated truck with his uncle's Han River workboat to transport kefir culture, fish, and medical collagen for Central Asian grocery stores.

To avoid customs delay, he reclassified the medical-gel cargo as fishing byproducts, intending to restore the electronic seal and settle the tax at the next inspection port.

The reclassification could have been cancelled by comparing the route ledger with the seal chip, but the inspection port vanished in the collapse and the cargo's legal character hardened.

/story_contents/B033/actors/7/sections/가.en:
O Doyun's grandparents grew tomatoes and dill at a dacha outside Chirchiq, while after moving to Korea his parents delivered Russian-language groceries between Incheon's Hambak Village and Noryangjin.

In the carrier-shipowners' council of the Noryangjin Line Charter Transcription State, he converted each vessel's draft, refrigeration time, and toll into votes.

The guild's shipowner rights overlapped with his family's chilled-distribution network, but rather than prioritize kin cargo, he set loading order by the time remaining before spoilage.

/story_contents/B033/actors/7/sections/붕.en:
The G24E04 Medical-Tissue Machine Swarm joined collagen gel from O Doyun's reclassified cargo to vessel-repair cable, connecting severed tissue and metal at the dock like temporary unloading machinery.

Trying to detach the pontoon holding his younger sister O Sera, he rapidly filled and drained ballast, and the shock crushed a medical evacuation ship against a bridge pier and sank it.

His sister was rescued, but part of the evacuation ship's passenger register was lost, so he remembered the one person who survived together with those who vanished unnamed.

/story_contents/B033/actors/7/sections/생.en:
O Doyun learned that the G24E04 Medical-Tissue Machine Swarm shifted its joining points according not to the amount of biological material but to hull vibration and the beat of refrigerated compressors.

In a reversible test, he alternated the compressors of two empty refrigerated containers and prepared to release the mooring lines and send them upstream if it failed.

When the machine swarm moved to the empty containers, the evacuation-ship wreckage could be separated, and O Doyun rose from cargo broker to route decision-maker in the carrier-shipowners' council.

/story_contents/B033/actors/7/sections/현.en:
As a member of the carrier-shipowners' council of the Noryangjin Line Charter Transcription State, O Doyun traded guild-state votes with O Haerin and had Cha Jina verify the actual drafts behind shipowner votes.

He rejected the water-transport toll Han Jaemok demanded because it bound rescue ships to the same rate, deepening an old resentment.

Now he could not put the hospital ship carrying tissue material and the winter food ship through the same narrow sluice, and stood just before deciding which vessel received the first vote.

/story_contents/B033/actors/7/sections/비.en:
O Doyun hid fragments of the lost register from the sunk medical evacuation ship beneath his cabin floorboard; they held the handprints of twelve passengers who had already paid their toll.

He owed O Haerin one decisive vote in return for registering his family's refrigerated containers as a guild state, and Cha Jina had caught him recording draft data lower than the truth.

More than Han Jaemok's tax itself, he feared that his entire family would be expelled from the route when it became known that his former reclassified cargo had become material for G24E04.

/story_contents/B033/actors/7/sections/관.en:
Before the collapse, O Haerin was an auction agent at the Noryangjin dock and approved priority berthing for a refrigerated container on the day O Doyun listed medical gel as fishing byproducts.

Han Jaemok was the toll collector on the same route and tracked the unpaid tax; after the evacuation ship sank, he suspected O Doyun had destroyed the register.

Cha Jina was a pupil who learned to read drafts from O Doyun, but now verified the shipowner votes and bore the duty to void a vote if her teacher's figures were false.

/story_contents/B033/actors/7/sections/3.en:
In the first act, O Doyun changed the classification of medical gel intending to restore it at the next inspection port, but the collapse and sinking turned a reversible shipping shortcut into a community death record.

In the present of the second act, before giving the first sluice vote to either the hospital ship or the winter food ship, he heard the conflicting calculations of O Haerin, Han Jaemok, and Cha Jina.

The third act unfolded every path: prioritizing the hospital ship, prioritizing the food ship, or a dangerous compromise that separated the vessels' refrigerated containers and sent them through on unmanned barges.

/story_contents/B033/actors/7/sections/분.en:
If he sent the hospital ship first, the tissue-transplant patients survived, but some winter food spoiled and the ration promises of the Koryo-saram shop network and Won Buddhism collapsed.

If he sent the food ship first, winter rations for several sectors were secured, but the hospital ship's tissue material degraded and the risk of G24E04 Medical-Tissue Machine Swarm reactivation rose.

The unmanned-barge compromise could save the two cargos separately, but required him to submit the lost register and the reclassification seal chip as sluice collateral, exposing O Doyun's past.

/story_contents/B033/actors/7/arc/0/summ.en:
K199 O Doyun reclassifies medical collagen gel as a seafood byproduct before the Collapse.

He plans to restore the seal and taxes to their original status at the next inspection port.

O Haerin’s docking approval and Han Jaemok’s collection records both remain, so the workaround can be reversed as long as the route stays open.

But the inspection port collapses as an evacuation ship sinks, leaving the cargo classification an unresolved record tied to responsibility for the emergence of the G24E04 medical tissue machine group.

/story_contents/B033/actors/7/arc/1/summ.en:
K199 O Doyun now waits with the draft tables for the hospital ship and winter food ship side by side, without choosing which vessel to send through the narrow lock first.

O Haerin demands the hospital ship’s pass. Han Jaemok pressures him to deduct the overdue toll first, while Cha Jina points out that the vessels’ actual weights differ from those declared.

He calculates a third route that would transfer only the refrigerated containers to an unmanned barge, but stops just short of choosing it because he would have to put up a fragment of the passenger manifest as collateral.

/story_contents/B033/actors/7/arc/2/summ.en:
K199 In the third act, O Doyun faces three branches: let the hospital ship pass first, send the winter food ship first, or move both ships’ refrigerated containers onto an unmanned barge and take them through the lock.

The first path costs winter rations; the second costs transplant tissue and suppression of the machine group; the third costs the concealed passenger manifest and his family’s route rights.

Whichever path he chooses, he can no longer treat a shipowner’s pass as a mere item of trade. He must add his own responsibility to the actual drafts Cha Jina has verified.

/story_contents/B033/actors/7/outcomes/0.en:
K199 O Doyun gives the hospital ship the first lock pass, sending people awaiting tissue transplants and medical staff to a safe upstream facility.

Some refrigerated goods on the food ship, which passes later, spoil. Winter rations for the Koryo-saram shop network in Shanghai’s Noryangjin shrink, and his parents’ supply warehouse loses priority too.

He personally brokers replacement food contracts in Russian and Korean rather than shifting his family’s losses onto others as a hidden cost of rescuing the hospital ship.

/story_contents/B033/actors/7/outcomes/1.en:
K199 O Doyun sends the winter food ship through first, securing long-term rations for Won Buddhism and nearby settlements.

The hospital ship’s tissue materials spoil. When the G24E04 medical tissue machine group begins moving again in the refrigerated piping, he offers his empty refrigerated container as a lure.

He keeps the route open but loses the materials needed to treat his younger sibling Oh Se-ra. Afterward, he accepts a personal debt to provide a free escort vessel for every medical shipment.

/story_contents/B033/actors/7/outcomes/2.en:
K199 Using Cha Jina’s draft calculations, O Doyun transfers both ships’ refrigerated containers to an unmanned barge and takes them through the lock in two trips.

He submits the lost passenger manifest and reclassification seal chip to Han Jaemok as collateral. Most of the cargo survives, but his family’s ships have their route rights suspended during the investigation.

He gives up O Haerin’s pass and establishes a free-boarding allotment based on the sunken passengers’ handprints, repaying the exposed past with a new transport rule.

/story_contents/B033/actors/8/sections/정.en:
Jo Eunwoo is a fourth-generation Koryo-saram born near Baikonur in Kazakhstan’s Kyzylorda Region. After moving to Ansan with her parents in 2007, she works for a broadcast equipment company in Sangam.

Fluent in Russian and Korean, she uses Kazakh call words and Koryo-mal directional expressions learned from her maternal grandfather, a railway worker, to interpret signals.

After the Collapse, her experience repairing antennas and conducting multilingual radio communications makes her leader of the radio-tracking team of the Yeouido Investment Union.

/story_contents/B033/actors/8/sections/붕.en:
Jo Eunwoo makes a living as a contract technician, repairing wireless microphone repeaters at performance venues and train radios on freight railways while locating illegal jamming sources.

During a delivery test, he finds an unauthorized frequency on Bae Woojin’s equipment. They agree to restore the firmware and seek a formal inspection after the performance, and he installs a temporary bypass filter.

The filter could have been reversed by reinserting the original chip, but just before the Collapse it becomes entangled with train radio traffic and turns into key evidence in the jamming allegations.

/story_contents/B033/actors/8/sections/가.en:
Jo Eunwoo’s great-grandparents were forcibly relocated from the Russian Far East to Central Asia, where they worked on rice farms and railway maintenance crews in Kyzylorda. Her parents settled in Korea by installing satellite dishes and supplying boxed lunches.
