At the Yeouido Investment Union of the Mapo Union, Jo Eunwoo manages transmission-tower bearings, spare vacuum tubes, and winter fuel, running the tracking team under Gwon Mirae’s command.

She converts her family’s railway call words into coordinate codes, allowing her to distinguish the direction of incoming radio waves even where map markers have failed.

/story_contents/B033/actors/8/sections/붕.en:
The G09E13 low-temperature spore host alternately occupies cold antenna feedlines and human respiratory tracts, spreading spores at the resonant frequency when transmission begins.

Jo Eunwoo tries to shut down the Sangam auxiliary tower, but the bypass filter on Bae Woojin’s equipment delays the shutdown signal. His colleague Ryu Katerina and nineteen evacuees are exposed in the transmitter room.

He hears Ryu Katerina’s final coordinates in Russian correctly but sends the rescue team to the wrong tower, leaving even his language skills bound up with the trauma.

/story_contents/B033/actors/8/sections/생.en:
At a repeater in a closed ice rink, Jo Eunwoo discovers that the G09E13 low-temperature spore host moves with the freeze–thaw cycle on feedline surfaces rather than following the strongest radio signal.

As a reversible test, he runs the antenna heater for seventy seconds and then immediately cools it. He receives Hwang Jiho’s train radio traffic in read-only mode to compare the sounds of spore movement.

When the test succeeds and drives the host into an empty feed tube, Gwon Mirae appoints him leader of the radio-tracking team.

/story_contents/B033/actors/8/sections/현.en:
As leader of the Yeouido Investment Union’s radio-tracking team in the Mapo Union, Jo Eunwoo guards Gwon Mirae’s transmission tower and receives Hwang Jiho’s train radio traffic on a limited basis as evidence of jamming.

Resentment remains between him and Bae Woojin over responsibility for the bypass filter and the alleged intent to jam, so he does not connect their equipment to the same circuit.

He is now on the verge of deciding which transmission to open first, as the northern evacuation train’s guidance signal and the Sangam spore warning both require the same spare vacuum tube.

/story_contents/B033/actors/8/sections/비.en:
Jo Eunwoo has recorded in his private reception log that Ryu Katerina’s coordinates were not wrong: he momentarily switched a Koryo-mal directional term with a Russian bearing.

In exchange for Hwang Jiho providing the train’s radio traffic as evidence, he owes him a safe frequency for one train service. He has also already borrowed two spare vacuum tubes from Gwon Mirae.

Although he knows Bae Woojin’s bypass filter may have been meant to avoid interference with medical devices at the performance venue rather than to jam signals deliberately, resentment has kept him from checking again.

/story_contents/B033/actors/8/sections/관.en:
Before the Collapse, Gwon Mirae was the facilities manager of the Sangam transmission tower and approved the overheating risk posed by the antenna heater Jo Eunwoo installed. She still holds final command over the tracking team.

Bae Woojin owns the equipment using an unauthorized frequency and agreed with Jo Eunwoo on when to restore it. After the Collapse, the filter is named as the cause of the jamming, and they become adversaries.

Hwang Jiho was the freight train’s radio operator at the time and kept the original signal from when the filter was active. He now uses that recording as collateral for a contract guaranteeing the evacuation train’s safety.

/story_contents/B033/actors/8/sections/3.en:
In the first act, Jo Eunwoo installs a bypass filter that can be removed after the performance. The Collapse prevents him from retrieving it, and he watches the temporary device become evidence in both the spore disaster and the jamming allegations.

In the present of the second act, he must assign a spare vacuum tube either to evacuation train guidance or to the spore warning. He has not yet acted on the option of retesting Bae Woojin’s equipment.

The third act includes all three branches: prioritize train guidance, prioritize the Sangam warning, or modify Bae Woojin’s filter into a reverse-phase repeater to transmit the two signals alternately.

/story_contents/B033/actors/8/sections/분.en:
If he prioritizes the evacuation train, Hwang Jiho’s passengers arrive, but the spore warning on Sangam’s outskirts is delayed, leaving the transmission construction work zone closed for a long time.

If he prioritizes the spore warning, he protects the tower, but the northern train stops on a diversion line and runs out of food and heating fuel.

If he modifies Bae Woojin’s filter, he can send the two signals in short alternation, but must submit the record of his coordinate misreading and his mistaken suspicion of Bae Woojin to a technical audit.

/story_contents/B033/actors/8/arc/0/summ.en:
K224 Before the Collapse, Jo Eunwoo uses a temporary filter to bypass the unauthorized frequency on Bae Woojin’s equipment, and they agree to reinsert the original chip after the performance.

Gwon Mirae’s approval record and Hwang Jiho’s original signal remain, so the filter installation can be fully reversed by following the prescribed procedure.

But the Collapse and the spore exposure come first. The temporary device is never retrieved, and Jo Eunwoo’s coordinate misreading is buried amid the jamming allegations.

/story_contents/B033/actors/8/arc/1/summ.en:
K224 Jo Eunwoo now places the only spare vacuum tube between the evacuation train guidance transmitter and the Sangam spore alarm, without connecting either contact.

Gwon Mirae sends ice measurements from around the tower, Hwang Jiho reports the train’s remaining heating fuel, and Bae Woojin can turn the filter into a reverse-phase device.

So Bae Woojin claims.

Jo Eunwoo takes out the record of his coordinate misreading from his private reception log, but still stops just short of choosing which circuit to restore first.

/story_contents/B033/actors/8/arc/2/summ.en:
K224 In the third act, Jo Eunwoo faces three branches: use the vacuum tube for train guidance, use it for the spore warning, or modify Bae Woojin’s filter to transmit the two signals at staggered intervals.

The first path exacts a cost from the Sangam work zone; the second, from the train passengers’ fuel; the third demands that he expose his concealed misreading and his resentment toward Bae Woojin.

Whatever the outcome, he continues tracking the G09E13 low-temperature spore host’s movement cycle and establishes a double-reading rule to cross-check language against signals.

/story_contents/B033/actors/8/outcomes/0.en:
K224 Jo Eunwoo installs the spare vacuum tube in the evacuation train guidance transmitter and directs Hwang Jiho’s train onto a safe track south of Sangam.

The spore warning comes late, allowing the G09E13 low-temperature spore host to occupy an outer feed tube. Gwon Mirae seals off half the transmission tower’s work zone.

He recruits radio technicians from among the rescued passengers to install a manual ice-monitoring line, personally repairing the damage to the tower left by the train rescue.

/story_contents/B033/actors/8/outcomes/1.en:
K224 Jo Eunwoo puts the vacuum tube into the spore alarm, preventing exposure at the Yeouido Investment Union and nearby shelters.

The northern evacuation train stops on a diversion line. Hwang Jiho closes half the passenger cars to conserve heating fuel, making long-distance evacuation necessary.

Using his authority as transmission-tower team leader, Jo Eunwoo sends short position pulses instead of food-related radio transmissions and spends the night calculating a route for a rescue team approaching on foot.

/story_contents/B033/actors/8/outcomes/2.en:
K224 Jo Eunwoo modifies Bae Woojin’s bypass filter into a reverse-phase repeater, alternating train guidance and the spore warning at seventy-second intervals.

Both areas avoid catastrophic losses, but the record of his coordinate misreading is submitted to the technical audit. His failure to rescue Ryu Katerina and his misjudgment of Bae Woojin remain on record as official causes.

He keeps his position as team leader, requires two people to cross-check every multilingual coordinate, and personally serves as the first checker.

/story_contents/B033/actors/9/sections/정.en:
Dawn Escort is a synthetic escort vehicle made up of a chassis, bogie platform, replaceable battery slots, and lane sensors. It does not have a humanlike body capable of moving freely.

Its fixed axle width and limited steering angle make it difficult for the vehicle to change direction on its own outside standard roads and maintained ramps.

Its identity can be verified only through shift-based snapshots and branch logs, not continuous personal memory. If its physical chassis is damaged, it cannot transfer without limit into another body.

/story_contents/B033/actors/9/sections/붕.en:
Before the Collapse, Dawn Escort is a low-speed autonomous bogie that carries hospital specimens and nighttime medicine along designated lanes, deleting its long-term memory at the end of each shift.

To avoid a construction zone, a route manager temporarily changes its lane-sensor map once, intending to restore the original map at the next maintenance session.

The change is reversible, but the Collapse cuts off both the original server and the road markings, leaving the temporary detour as the last route the vehicle can trust.

/story_contents/B033/actors/9/sections/가.en:
Dawn Escort’s legal custody terms are HP03 joint custody, a seal witnessed by citizens, and three-party signatures for any transfer. No technician may remove its chassis or memory medium alone.

Kim Taeun handles primary maintenance and legal responsibility, with an HP03 auditor present. Its standby chassis is parked on a limited basis in an HC02-standard garage.

The community treats it as a sealed public transport vehicle rather than owned property, allowing shift cooperation with Gam-bong only within an approved work schedule.

/story_contents/B033/actors/9/sections/붕.en:
The G12E02 microfibre skin group coats Dawn Escort’s tires and chassis joints with microfibres, preventing its lane sensors from distinguishing road edges from living tissue.

The vehicle brakes suddenly on a contaminated detour and collides with a medicine bogie following behind. Its limited chassis prevents it from moving onto a side road to avoid an overturned passenger module.

Only the eight seconds before the collision remain in the next shift’s snapshot, so Dawn Escort cannot fully remember either the causes of the failed rescue or the victims’ final moments.

/story_contents/B033/actors/9/sections/생.en:
In a short driving test, Dawn Escort confirms that the G12E02 microfibre skin group can mimic the infrared reflection detected by its lane sensors, but not the axle vibrations produced when the bogie’s load changes.

Kim Taeun removes and stores the contaminated sensor so the change can be reversed, while Gam-bong moves sandbags one position at a time to establish a vibration baseline.

After the test, Dawn Escort can identify the fibre group only within designated ramps. It becomes a verified escort platform for limited routes, not an unrestricted autonomous vehicle.

/story_contents/B033/actors/9/sections/현.en:
Dawn Escort is a sealed joint asset of HP03 and runs only the limited route between the seed vault and the medical isolation wing from an HC02-standard garage.

It has only three fully charged replaceable battery packs, and its drive bearings and lane-sensor modules are rationed. Long-distance repeated runs and unlimited self-repair are therefore impossible.

No decision has yet been made on whether to install the last spare sensor for seed transport or for recovering a skin-group sample. The vehicle will not cross the stop line before receiving an approved order.

/story_contents/B033/actors/9/sections/비.en:
Dawn Escort’s pre-collision snapshot records the automatic detachment of a passenger module that exceeded the permitted load. The detached module’s location remains inside an area that is now off-limits.

Because lasting, complete memory is prohibited, the vehicle does not know what happened to that passenger afterward. One branch log, however, remains undeleted on Kim Taeun’s maintenance terminal.

Gam-bong also recorded a battery pack’s degradation as lower than it really was, allowing operations to continue. Dawn Escort therefore carries a technical debt that reduces the actual charge available to the next shift.

/story_contents/B033/actors/9/sections/관.en:
Since before the Collapse, Kim Taeun has been Dawn Escort’s primary maintenance worker and legal custodian. He signed off on both the lane-sensor map change and the schedule for restoring it.

Gam-bong is a coworker who connected load modules during night bogie shifts and was responsible for manually braking the rear medicine bogie on the day of the collision.

Their shared past can be reconstructed only by physically matching Kim Taeun’s maintenance signature, Gam-bong’s braking traces, and Dawn Escort’s eight-second snapshot—not through deleted long-term memories.

/story_contents/B033/actors/9/sections/3.en:
In the first act, Dawn Escort is due to have its temporarily altered map restored at the next maintenance session after detouring around a construction zone. The Collapse destroys the original server, making the reversible detour its only operational memory.

In the present of the second act, it is on the verge of approval for using its last spare sensor and three fully charged battery packs for one of three tasks: transporting seeds, recovering a skin-group sample, or searching for the detached module in the off-limits area.

The third act includes each branch of the three missions and the consequences for battery use, lost parts, and the handling of memory logs.

/story_contents/B033/actors/9/sections/분.en:
If it chooses seed transport, it prevents the vault’s cooling from stopping, but loses the opportunity to recover the detached passenger module and the G12E02 microfibre skin group sample.

If it chooses sample recovery, a new sensor standard can be developed, but seed transport is delayed and one set of bearings must be permanently discarded.

If it finds the detached module, responsibility for the collision can be reconstructed, but it uses all three battery packs. Dawn Escort becomes a stationary chassis that cannot return to the garage without a tow.

/story_contents/B033/actors/9/arc/0/summ.en:
V01 Before the Collapse, Dawn Escort has its lane-sensor map temporarily changed to avoid a construction zone, with the original map scheduled for restoration on the next maintenance shift.

Kim Taeun’s restoration signature and Gam-bong’s test-braking record remain, so the change is fully reversible within the allotted time.

But the server is cut off and the G12E02 microfibre skin group intrudes, costing it the original map. The temporary route becomes the only map fragment its limited chassis can use.

/story_contents/B033/actors/9/arc/1/summ.en:
V01 Dawn Escort now holds three fully charged battery packs, its last spare lane sensor, and a set of drive bearings with little service life remaining, all awaiting installation.

HP03’s seal, witnessed by citizens, remains in force, so even Kim Taeun cannot order a departure alone. Access outside the district network and cross-facility connections are blocked by default.

At the stop line, the vehicle awaits a choice among approved plans for seed transport, skin-group sample recovery, and a search for the detached passenger module, pending three-party signatures.

/story_contents/B033/actors/9/arc/2/summ.en:
V01 In the third act, Dawn Escort presents three possible branches: head for the seed vault, recover a G12E02 microfibre skin group sample, or find the detached passenger module in the off-limits area.

Each path prioritizes one of three things—the survival of refrigerated seeds, a new sensor standard, or a reconstruction of responsibility for the collision—while irreversibly consuming batteries and wearing parts.

In every ending, the vehicle remains bound by its fixed chassis and limited steering angle, passing only shift snapshots and branch logs to the next run.

/story_contents/B033/actors/9/outcomes/0.en:
V01 Dawn Escort installs the last spare sensor and uses two battery packs to carry cooling components and germination boxes to the seed vault.

The seeds survive, but a further collapse obscures the passenger module’s location in the off-limits area, and the skin-group sample disappears beneath the contaminated road surface.

The vehicle returns to the HC02 garage on its remaining pack and seals its shift snapshot, then waits for replacement bearings before its next run.

/story_contents/B033/actors/9/outcomes/1.en:
V01 Dawn Escort uses the sandbag vibration baseline to carry a G12E02 microfibre skin group sample to an isolation container. It establishes a new sensor-reading standard, but road friction forces one set of drive bearings to be discarded. Delayed seed transport lowers the germination rate in some drawers, but escort vehicles thereafter distinguish contaminated boundaries more accurately.

The vehicle remains a stationary garage platform, providing read-only diagnostics until it receives an allocation of repair parts.

/story_contents/B033/actors/9/outcomes/2.en:
V01 Dawn Escort loads all three battery packs and enters the off-limits area, where it finds the passenger module detached during the collision and a damaged brake coupling.

Kim Taeun’s signature, Gam-bong’s braking traces, and the eight-second snapshot together confirm that the automatic detachment resulted from the overload rule, but no survivors remain.

The vehicle uses all its power and stops at the site. It creates no memory fork until it is towed and resealed by all three parties, retaining only its final branch log.

/story_contents/B034/actors/0/sections/정.en:
K106 Je Bareum is a Korean doctor born in the print-shop alleys of Seongdong who grew up moving between a night clinic and an ironworks.

She remembers patients by the condition of their hands injured at work and their lungs, rather than by their addresses or ration grades.

After the Collapse, when medical care became a means of determining citizenship, she tries to reestablish her principles between medicine and administration.

/story_contents/B034/actors/0/sections/붕.en:
Before the Collapse, K106 Je Bareum treated the chronic illnesses of welders and printers at an industrial medicine clinic in Wangsimni.

Under pressure from a factory owner, she put one occupational injury ruling on hold, but she did not destroy the original medical opinion, so she can still reverse the decision.

That unfinished record is evidence both of the caution with which she tried to protect her patient and of the cowardice with which she yielded to power.

/story_contents/B034/actors/0/sections/가.en:
K106 Je Bareum comes from a small family of artisans who have repaired metal type and sign frames in Seongdong for three generations.

She now runs the alley clinic of the Sermon Registry State, coordinating each workshop’s share of medicines and the order of nighttime house calls.

The federation respects her as a community doctor but continues to pressure her to tie treatment to tiered citizenship screening.

/story_contents/B034/actors/0/sections/붕.en:
On the night the G04E10 Sewer Raccoon Clan broke through the Seongsu drainage channel, K106 Je Bareum closed the quarantine door first and saved seven patients inside.

But sign maker Yun Daeho, who remained outside, was swept away by contaminated water, and Je Bareum heard her calls for rescue to the end.

Since then, merely seeing someone’s hand move to lock a door brings back the sounds of that night and the smell of disinfectant.

/story_contents/B034/actors/0/sections/생.en:
K106 Je Bareum saved the alley from a fever caused by the G04E10 Sewer Raccoon Clan’s feces by stamping the water-ration cards with a temporary quarantine mark.

The measure could have been withdrawn if medical records were made public within three days, but the turning point became a tool of power when Jang Minjae tried to make it a permanent citizenship grading system.

Je Bareum still has the original ledger and can reverse both her choice and the system.

/story_contents/B034/actors/0/sections/현.en:
K106 Je Bareum is the director of the Seongdong alley clinic under the Sermon Registry State and keeps both the medicine keys and the water-supply quarantine stamp.

She has carried out Jang Minjae’s orders and taken in people injured in the pump room, including Jin Morae, but has not decided which records to release.

She is on the verge of choosing whether to burn the citizenship ledger or hand it over for a joint audit.

/story_contents/B034/actors/0/sections/비.en:
K106 Je Bareum has hidden the medical records of thirteen ineligible patients, which Jang Minjae erased, behind the medicine cabinet containing metal type.

He lied to Yun Daeho’s daughter, Yun Gaeun, that her father died instantly; in fact, he heard Daeho’s calls for rescue and did not open the quarantine door.

He also has not repaid the six bottles of antibiotics he borrowed from Jin Morae and has promised her priority treatment after the next pump accident.

/story_contents/B034/actors/0/sections/관.en:
K106 Je Bareum worked with Jang Minjae on the Seongdong Industrial Accident Review Committee before the Collapse and initially approved Jang’s water-ration citizenship plan as a temporary disease-control measure.

She and Jin Morae share a past of surviving a Cheonggyecheon pump flooding accident while treating each other’s injured ribs and wrist.

The moment Je Bareum’s hidden original ledger is made public, those two relationships will cost her either authority or trust.

/story_contents/B034/actors/0/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, K106 Je Bareum confirms that Jin Morae’s new wound is connected to the records of ineligible patients and receives Jang Minjae’s order to seal the ledger.

In Act 2, she recovers an audio recording of Yun Daeho from a closed drainage channel with Yun Gaeun and prepares to admit her lie.

In Act 3, her path branches into every option: making the ledger public and founding a community clinic; burning the records and becoming the citizenship director; or confessing responsibility for the quarantine door and choosing exile.

/story_contents/B034/actors/0/sections/분.en:
K106 Je Bareum’s ending depends on whom she gives the hidden original medical records and Yun Daeho’s audio recording to.

If she releases both to the residents’ audit committee, water-ration citizenship is dismantled, but the alley clinic is also paralyzed for a time.

If she gives them to Jang Minjae or takes all the blame herself, order is maintained, but she fails to make good on the truth she owes Jin Morae and Yun Gaeun.

/story_contents/B034/actors/0/arc/0/summ.en:
K106 Je Bareum discovers signs of sewer fever in Jin Morae’s pump-room puncture wound but does not report them to Jang Minjae immediately.

He compares the original ledger behind the medicine cabinet with the current citizenship roster and finds thirteen names that differ.

At the end of the act, Yun Gaeun comes to the clinic carrying a receiver panel containing her father’s final rescue signal.

/story_contents/B034/actors/0/arc/1/summ.en:
K106 Je Bareum enters the closed drainage channel with Jin Morae and recovers Yun Daeho’s audio recording and the original design plate for the quarantine stamp.

Jang Minjae announces a halt to medicine supplies and demands the original ledger, while Yun Gaeun prepares a public hearing.

Je Bareum copies the ledger and divides the copies among three separate envelopes, but does not deliver them to either side yet.

/story_contents/B034/actors/0/arc/2/summ.en:
At a residents’ audit meeting, K106 Je Bareum can make the ledger and audio recording public and establish a community clinic, or burn the records.

She can become Jang Minjae’s citizenship director.

She can also take a third path: confess only to the Yun Daeho incident, accept exile, and hand the clinic over to Jin Morae.

Each branch settles the survival of the patients on the roster, the continuity of medicine distribution, and reconciliation with Yun Gaeun at a different cost.

/story_contents/B034/actors/0/outcomes/0.en:
K106 Je Bareum releases all the records to the residents’ audit committee and separates water-ration citizenship from eligibility for treatment.

Jin Morae becomes the new community clinic’s safety officer, and Yun Gaeun takes charge of the victims’ archive, but Jang Minjae’s distribution network is cut off, leaving medicines in short supply for the winter.

Je Bareum steps down as director and remains an ordinary council member who prepares public treatment schedules.

/story_contents/B034/actors/0/outcomes/1.en:
K106 Je Bareum burns the original ledger and audio recording and accepts the citizenship director position offered by Jang Minjae.

Medicine supplies and the water-ration system remain orderly, but Jin Morae leaves the clinic, and Yun Gaeun exposes the false death record on a wall poster.

Even as Je Bareum saves more patients, she turns away every day from people outside the grading line she created.

/story_contents/B034/actors/0/outcomes/2.en:
K106 Je Bareum confesses to the Yun Daeho incident and to hiding the records, then entrusts copies of the ledger separately to Jin Morae and Yun Gaeun.

She is exiled from Seongdong, but buys the two of them time to roll back the citizenship system in stages.

Carrying a mobile medical bag around the outskirts of the drainage channel, Je Bareum once again treats her patients who have no names on the roster.

/story_contents/B034/actors/1/sections/정.en:
K135 Seol Bomi is a Korean power-plant operator who grew up in staff housing at a Gangdong substation and can identify generator faults by sound and vibration alone.

He regards electricity not as power over people but as a public good that apportions time, and judges the order of blackouts as a matter of survival ethics.

After the Collapse, he runs the last large generator at the Godeok Base but has not yet chosen whose nights to light first.

/story_contents/B034/actors/1/sections/붕.en:
Before the Collapse, K135 Seol Bomi was responsible for no-load testing and fuel measurement on an urban rail emergency-power testing team.

At a superior’s request, he once marked an overheating alarm as maintenance completed, but kept the bearing that had not been replaced in a separate storeroom, leaving evidence that could overturn the assessment.

That part is the only physical evidence that can establish whether the accident at the time was caused by individual negligence or manipulation of the delivery schedule.

/story_contents/B034/actors/1/sections/가.en:
K135 Seol Bomi’s family ran a laundry in Amsa, and whenever the power went out, they turned the spin dryer by hand to supply hospital linens.

He now leads the power-generation team of the Escort Protection State and draws up power schedules for the water-intake pumps, siding signals, and isolation ward.

The community trusts his precision, but Bae Woojin’s announcement of restoration results and Yang Giseok’s railway demands unsettle his distribution principles.

/story_contents/B034/actors/1/sections/붕.en:
On the day the G21E07 Communications Mycelium overran the control cables like fungal threads, K135 Seol Bomi trusted the automatic transfer system and delayed shutting it off manually.

As a result, a fire in the laundry building burned his younger sister, Seol Yeoreum, leaving her without sensation in her left hand; the water-supply pump also stopped for twelve minutes.

Even now, communications static reminds Seol Bomi of his sister’s wet glove and the smell of burning cable insulation.

/story_contents/B034/actors/1/sections/생.en:
K135 Seol Bomi exploited the G21E07 Communications Mycelium’s signal to build a temporary manual distribution panel that made only the infected cable section resonate.

He promised Bae Woojin that he would remove the concealed circuit once full restoration was complete a month later, so this change can still be reversed.

But when Yang Giseok secretly supplied power to the siding through that circuit, the temporary device became a new lifeline.

/story_contents/B034/actors/1/sections/현.en:
K135 Seol Bomi is the emergency power-plant operator at the Godeok Base, with the authority to start two generators and draw on three fuel tanks.

He follows Bae Woojin’s public restoration plan, but has not yet acted on his stated refusal to carry out concealed power distribution omitted from the ledger.

He must choose whether to cut power to the ward or the siding before the next fuel truck arrives.

/story_contents/B034/actors/1/sections/비.en:
K135 Seol Bomi keeps the old test report in which he concealed the overheating alarm and the unreplaced bearing in a sealed box beneath the generator floor.

To protect the power needed for his sister Seol Yeoreum’s rehabilitation, he allotted the laundry building’s circuit eight more amperes than permitted every night.

In return for the twenty cans of railway diesel he borrowed from Yang Giseok, he has also promised to power up the siding once without public disclosure.

/story_contents/B034/actors/1/sections/관.en:
K135 Seol Bomi was paired with Bae Woojin in a joint emergency-power drill before the Collapse, and whenever Bae exaggerated the results, he kept a separate record of the actual measurements.

He and Yang Giseok also share the experience of surviving the first winter by pushing a generator car along a frozen siding to restart a water-supply pump.

Bae Woojin represents public order and Yang Giseok represents flexibility in the field; both know about Seol Bomi’s hidden circuit.

/story_contents/B034/actors/1/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, K135 Seol Bomi discovers that the fuel reserve is two days less than announced and that the infected cable has spread to the ward circuit.

In Act 2, he verifies Bae Woojin’s restoration announcement and confirms that a train carrying evacuees is hidden on Yang Giseok’s siding.

In Act 3, he chooses among all the branches: full disclosure of the power-distribution schedule, making the concealed circuit permanent, or stopping the generator to burn out the mycelium.

/story_contents/B034/actors/1/sections/분.en:
K135 Seol Bomi’s ending depends on whether he places the remaining diesel and manual distribution panel under public control or operates them on his own responsibility.

Public distribution ends preferential treatment but may cut power to Seol Yeoreum’s rehabilitation building first; concealed distribution saves the evacuation train but creates a new network of privilege.

A complete shutdown may eliminate the G21E07 Communications Mycelium, but also puts the water supply at risk.

/story_contents/B034/actors/1/arc/0/summ.en:
During a predawn startup test, K135 Seol Bomi discovers that the fuel gauge has been tampered with and that resonance from the G21E07 Communications Mycelium remains on the ward circuit.

Bae Woojin orders him to hide the figures until the restoration ceremony, while Yang Giseok requests power for the siding at one in the morning.

Seol Bomi holds off on both requests and takes out the sealed box containing the unreplaced bearing.

/story_contents/B034/actors/1/arc/1/summ.en:
With Seol Yeoreum, K135 Seol Bomi examines the old test report and proves that the present generator’s overheating is connected to manipulation of the delivery schedule.

Yang Giseok reveals that an evacuation train carrying newborns and dialysis patients is waiting on the siding, while Bae Woojin forbids a blackout in the ward.

Seol Bomi prepares a dangerous plan to divide the power among three circuits but does not throw the switch.

/story_contents/B034/actors/1/arc/2/summ.en:
K135 Seol Bomi can use a public lottery to give the ward and the train power in rotation, or make the off-ledger circuit permanent and secretly keep both groups alive.

He can also make a third choice: stop the generator completely and burn the infected windings to allow for long-term restoration.

Each branch determines Seol Yeoreum’s treatment, Bae Woojin’s command authority, and the survival of Yang Giseok’s evacuation train in a different way.

/story_contents/B034/actors/1/outcomes/0.en:
K135 Seol Bomi discloses the actual fuel supply and the old test report, then institutes rotating power distribution according to a residents’ lottery.

Bae Woojin is dismissed for falsifying his results, and Yang Giseok’s evacuation train departs a day late, but every passenger receives a minimum supply of power.

Seol Yeoreum supports her older sister’s decision despite losing rehabilitation time and becomes the first auditor of the public measurement team.

/story_contents/B034/actors/1/outcomes/1.en:
K135 Seol Bomi gives Bae Woojin and Yang Giseok different power-distribution schedules and makes the manual panel’s secret circuit permanent.

Both the ward and the evacuation train survive, but laundry workers bear repeated blackouts and pay the price of preferential treatment.

Seol Bomi keeps the operator’s position but becomes the manager of a closed network that requires him to add falsified measurements every day.

/story_contents/B034/actors/1/outcomes/2.en:
K135 Seol Bomi stops the generator and burns the infected windings, eliminating the core colony of the G21E07 Communications Mycelium.

The water-supply team gets by with hand pumps for three days, and some of the evacuation train’s passengers travel on foot, but afterward they regain a clean, independent circuit.

Seol Bomi loses his position and opens a workshop making manual generators with Seol Yeoreum, making even the record of his failure public.

/story_contents/B034/actors/2/sections/정.en:
K164 Eo Taesan is a Korean archivist trained in a Jongno historical-document restoration studio to read paper grain, cracks in sealing wax, and ink oxidation.

She trusts the procedures by which documents were made and the traces left by human hands more than a state’s legitimacy.

After the Collapse, she safeguards the ratification of sixteen flags but has not yet decided which flag to recognize as authentic.

/story_contents/B034/actors/2/sections/붕.en:
Before the Collapse, K164 Eo Taesan was a contract conservator who digitized royal protocols and original local-government documents.

To avoid being fired, she added a seal of unknown provenance to the catalog of authentic items, but kept a piece of its sealing wax and the photographic logs separately so the registration could be canceled.

That pending correction could now overturn the authenticity of the entire founding-ratification chest.

/story_contents/B034/actors/2/sections/가.en:
K164 Eo Taesan’s family ran a small mounting shop in Seochon that restored rental contracts and letters rather than family genealogies.

He now manages the ratification chests for the flags of sixteen political communities and their sealing keys for the Government of the Republic of Korea Government.

The Records Bureau demands neutrality, but when Yun Seorin’s founding procedure conflicts with Jo Harin’s preservation standards, ultimate responsibility falls to Eo Taesan.

/story_contents/B034/actors/2/sections/붕.en:
On the day the G17E03 Surveillance Orbital Forces pierced the Records Bureau’s skylight, K164 Eo Taesan delayed apprentice Mun Seju’s evacuation while trying to move the chest of authentic documents.

Mun Seju was exposed to an optical marker and lost her sight, and Eo Taesan could not deny the accusation that she had put documents before a person.

Whenever a red tracking dot passes across a ceiling, she feels the weight of the ratification chest she carried as she ran.

/story_contents/B034/actors/2/sections/생.en:
To evade the G17E03 Surveillance Orbital Forces’ scans, K164 Eo Taesan exchanged the seals on the sixteen flags and encoded the authentic items’ locations in a humidity chart.

He designed the exchange to be reversible if Yun Seorin and Jo Harin were both present, so it can still be undone.

But when the communities completed their oaths with the seals exchanged, a temporary disguise became an actual political order.

/story_contents/B034/actors/2/sections/현.en:
K164 Eo Taesan is the Government of the Republic of Korea Government’s keeper of the sixteen flags’ ratifications, with the authority to open the ratification chests and enter the humidity-controlled room.

He safeguards the founding-ratification chest entrusted to him by Yun Seorin and follows the storage schedule for iron chests set by Jo Harin, but has not disclosed the exchange of seals.

He is about to choose whether to restore the authentic arrangement or declare the present agreement authentic.

/story_contents/B034/actors/2/sections/비.en:
K164 Eo Taesan has hidden the old photographic logs showing when she added a seal of unknown provenance to the authentic-items catalog, along with the current seal-exchange chart, in the same scroll rod.

She has not been able to tell Mun Seju, who lost her sight, that at the moment of the accident she picked up the documents first.

She also has yet to return two oxygen-free storage canisters borrowed from Jo Harin on the condition that she maintain political neutrality.

/story_contents/B034/actors/2/sections/관.en:
K164 Eo Taesan spent a night with Yun Seorin verifying the order of signatures on the first civic accord immediately after the Collapse, and together they sealed the founding-ratification chest.

With Jo Harin, he hauled an iron chest out of a flooded basement archive on a handcart and then jointly designed its seasonal humidity schedule.

Yun Seorin prioritizes the force of the agreement, while Jo Harin prioritizes material authenticity, and they pressure Eo Taesan’s final choice in opposite directions.

/story_contents/B034/actors/2/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, K164 Eo Taesan confirms that the sixteenth seal has the same crack as the old seal of unknown provenance.

In Act 2, she combines Mun Seju’s tactile testimony with footage taken by the orbital forces to reconstruct the authentic arrangement at the time the seals were exchanged.

In Act 3, every branch opens to her: restoration and renewed ratification, legalization of the current arrangement, or invalidation of all ratifications and creation of a new accord through a public lottery.

/story_contents/B034/actors/2/sections/분.en:
K164 Eo Taesan’s ending depends on whether she judges authenticity to reside in the physical original or in the procedures survivors believed in and carried out.

Restoring the seals recovers past rights but invalidates three alliances already formed; recognizing the present arrangement turns a disguise into law.

Total invalidation destroys the Records Bureau’s authority but returns the process of ratification to Mun Seju and the citizens.

/story_contents/B034/actors/2/arc/0/summ.en:
During a routine humidity inspection, K164 Eo Taesan finds in the sealing wax of the sixteenth seal the crack of unknown provenance that he registered in the past.

Yun Seorin demands that the scheduled declaration of the nation’s founding proceed, while Jo Harin argues for immediately isolating every chest.

Eo Taesan postpones opening them and goes to ask Mun Seju, who has lost his sight, about the evacuation route that day once more.

/story_contents/B034/actors/2/arc/1/summ.en:
K164 Eo Taesan reconstructs the original arrangement of the seals by combining Mun Seju’s tactile memory, Jo Harin’s humidity records, and Yun Seorin’s order of signatures.

In the process, evidence also emerges that his earlier manipulation of the catalog enabled the Surveillance Orbital Forces to identify the target.

He summons the sixteen representatives to the basement archive but puts off deciding which truth to disclose first.

/story_contents/B034/actors/2/arc/2/summ.en:
K164 Eo Taesan can restore the authentic seals and demand renewed ratification by the sixteen communities, or declare the current arrangement, formed during their survival, the lawful original.

He can also open every chest, invalidate the ratifications, and choose new signatories by public lottery among the citizens.

Each branch gives different authority to Yun Seorin’s founding, Jo Harin’s Records Bureau, and Mun Seju’s testimony as a victim.

/story_contents/B034/actors/2/outcomes/0.en:
K164 Eo Taesan discloses the seal-exchange chart and his past manipulation of the catalog, then restores the authentic arrangement.

Yun Seorin’s founding declaration is postponed and three alliances dissolve, but a renewed ratification process overseen by Jo Harin begins.

Eo Taesan steps down as keeper and devotes himself to reconstructing the accident record, including Mun Seju’s oral account.

/story_contents/B034/actors/2/outcomes/1.en:
K164 Eo Taesan declares the current arrangement of seals, which the survivors have sworn by and upheld, the new authentic arrangement.

Yun Seorin declares the nation’s founding as scheduled, and Jo Harin leaves the Records Bureau in protest over the violation of archival principles.

Eo Taesan stabilizes the political order but bears lifelong responsibility for making the disguise he created its legal origin.

/story_contents/B034/actors/2/outcomes/2.en:
K164 Eo Taesan opens all sixteen ratification chests, invalidates the existing rights, and entrusts a citizens’ lottery committee with drafting a new accord.

The Records Bureau closes temporarily, and both Yun Seorin and Jo Harin lose their authority, but Mun Seju participates in the process as a representative of those harmed.

Eo Taesan remains not as a guardian of originals but as a clerk who records the process of change.

/story_contents/B034/actors/3/sections/정.en:
K189 Hong Jaemin is a Korean railway witness who grew up around the Yongsan rail yard and remembers people’s movements by carriage windows, boarding doors, and seat numbers.

She believes the bodies and voices of those who actually held their places take precedence over tickets.

After the Collapse, she testifies about the occupation of windows on the 2126 water-supply train, but has not yet decided whether to turn that testimony into authority over train assignments.

/story_contents/B034/actors/3/sections/붕.en:
Before the Collapse, K189 Hong Jaemin worked for a railway video-recording subcontractor, sorting footage of passenger complaints and deleting videos past their retention periods.

On company orders, she marked one video of a wheelchair user’s forcible removal from a designated seat for deletion, but kept a copy in her personal error folder so it could be recovered.

The station employee’s order in that video is the origin of the current rules for occupying places on the water-supply train.

/story_contents/B034/actors/3/sections/가.en:
K189 Hong Jaemin’s family repaired window frames and insect screens in Haebangchon, and Jaemin learned to patch broken glass temporarily.

She is now recognized in the Railway Succession Polity as a witness to the occupation of windows on the first water-supply train and attends hearings on seat disputes and boarding priority.

The community trusts her memory but also knows that a single statement from her could cut off one family’s water ration.

/story_contents/B034/actors/3/sections/붕.en:
On the day the G18E11 Abandoned-Line Maintenance Train Group charged down the disused Seobinggo line, K189 Hong Jaemin mistook a flashlight signal outside the window for a prank.

Because of that judgment, an evacuation carriage failed to move onto a siding, injuring eleven people, and her friend Im Dohyeon died between the couplers.

Whenever Jaemin hears three taps on a window, she remembers the final switching signal Dohyeon sent.

/story_contents/B034/actors/3/sections/생.en:
K189 Hong Jaemin read the vibrations of the G18E11 abandoned-line repair train group through a carriage window frame, identified a safe track, and helped the 2126 water-supply train escape.

To prevent confusion, she recorded the first person to touch a window as its occupant, but provisionally set a rule requiring the claim to be reviewed at the first terminal.

When Gwon Sion fixed that record to the dispatch board, a reversible marker became an inheritable boarding pass.

/story_contents/B034/actors/3/sections/현.en:
K189 Hong Jaemin is the officially recognized witness to window occupancy on the 2126 water-supply train for the Line Succession State, and his word carries decisive weight in dispatch hearings.

He has attached his testimony to Gwon Sion's dispatch board and tested whether Park Taegyeom's relay remains operational against actual window occupancy.

He is now on the verge of choosing whether to review the first record and correct the dispatch board or honor his existing oath.

/story_contents/B034/actors/3/sections/비.en:
K189 Hong Jaemin hid an audio recording of the accident, which says he ignored Im Do-hyeon's switch signal, and deleted footage of the wheelchair seats beneath the rubber seal inside a window frame.

He promised a brother and sister who could not secure a window on the first water-supply train seats on the next train, but Gwon Sion's dispatch board prevented him from keeping that promise.

He also has yet to repay Park Taegyeom for a box of spare batteries used to keep the relay running.

/story_contents/B034/actors/3/sections/관.en:
K189 Hong Jaemin and Gwon Sion drew up the window-occupancy list together while drying a wet dispatch board on the roof of the first water-supply train.

In an abandoned-line tunnel, he and Park Taegyeom matched relay signals against window-frame vibrations and avoided the approaching G18E11 abandoned-line repair train group three times.

Gwon Sion values continuity of records, while Park Taegyeom values signals verified each time, so they test Jae-min's principles of testimony in different ways.

/story_contents/B034/actors/3/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, K189 Hong Jaemin receives an objection alleging that a family monopolized a water carriage using a forged window-occupancy chart.

In Act 2, he restores the deleted footage and checks it against Park Taegyeom's relay records, uncovering that the current dispatch rules repeat discriminatory orders from before the collapse.

In Act 3, every ending branch opens up: a full review, retaining the existing dispatch assignments, or combining a public lottery for each train with on-site testimony.

/story_contents/B034/actors/3/sections/분.en:
K189 Hong Jaemin's ending depends on whether he treats memory as fixed ownership or as public testimony subject to continuing verification.

A full review corrects unjust occupancy claims but breaks longstanding promises of passage, while retaining the existing system preserves order but prolongs discrimination.

The mixed-lottery plan reduces Gwon Sion's and Park Taegyeom's authority, but also requires Jae-min to step down as the sole witness.

/story_contents/B034/actors/3/arc/0/summ.en:
At a water-supply train hearing, K189 Hong Jaemin discovers that the ink on a window-occupancy chart was produced after the first run.

Gwon Sion demands that he dismiss the objection to prevent dispatch chaos, while Park Taegyeom offers to release the relay records from that time.

Jae-min postpones his ruling by a day and dismantles the window frame concealing the audio recording of Im Do-hyeon's accident.

/story_contents/B034/actors/3/arc/1/summ.en:
K189 Hong Jaemin restores the deleted footage of the wheelchair seats and the first water-supply train's relay records, confirming the window-occupancy rule's wrongful origins.

The brother and sister he had made a promise to have since become train drivers in a water-scarce region, and they offer train support on condition that the rule be abolished.

Jae-min summons Gwon Sion and Park Taegyeom to a public hearing, but has yet to speak of his own mistaken judgment.

/story_contents/B034/actors/3/arc/2/summ.en:
K189 Hong Jaemin can review every window-occupancy right and return seats to the harmed brother and sister and excluded passengers, or preserve the existing dispatch board and prioritize operational stability.

He can also implement a third plan combining a public lottery for each train with on-site testimony and verification of relay records.

Each branch changes Gwon Sion's dispatch authority, Park Taegyeom's relay network, and Jae-min's own standing as a witness.

/story_contents/B034/actors/3/outcomes/0.en:
K189 Hong Jaemin reveals her mistaken judgment and the deleted footage, and reviews every window-occupancy right from scratch.

Gwon Sion's dispatch board is discarded, and the harmed brother and sister take charge of the new water carriage, but train service stops for several days.

Jae-min loses her authority as the sole witness and becomes a traveling hearing officer who compares the memories of multiple survivors.

/story_contents/B034/actors/3/outcomes/1.en:
K189 Hong Jaemin confesses only to the Im Do-hyeon accident, leaving the window-occupancy rule and Gwon Sion's dispatch board in place.

The trains run on time and Park Taegyeom's relay network remains stable, but ownership of the water carriage obtained through a forged chart is legalized.

Jae-min remains a symbol of order, yet cannot look toward the windows whenever he passes the station of the brother and sister to whom he made his promise.

/story_contents/B034/actors/3/outcomes/2.en:
K189 Hong Jaemin abolishes window-occupancy rights and introduces a temporary dispatch system that uses a public lottery, relay records, and on-site testimony together.

Gwon Sion remains as dispatch coordinator, Park Taegyeom takes charge of verifying records, and the harmed brother and sister are guaranteed seats on an outlying route.

In exchange for sharing decision-making power, Jae-min accepts that his own memories, too, are evidence that can be challenged.

/story_contents/B034/actors/4/sections/정.en:
K214 Dan Noeul is a Korean night-shift inventory inspector who grew up behind the Noryangjin wholesale market and tracks the movement of stock by the weight of boxes and water marks on the floor.

She trusts the smell of the actual compartments and the stamps on bricks more than ledgers, but believes eyewitness memories must also be verified.

After the collapse, she became a key witness to the transfer of contaminated-water stock, though she has not yet decided whom to accuse.

/story_contents/B034/actors/4/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, K214 Dan Noeul handled nighttime intake and dispatch and weighed waste at a fish market cold-storage warehouse.

At a trading firm's request, she recorded two pallets of spoiled ice as sound stock, but hid the original barcode strips inside a drainpipe so the entry could be corrected.

That reversible falsification is now the first clue to where the contaminated-water stock originated.

/story_contents/B034/actors/4/sections/가.en:
K214 Dan Noeul's family moved up from North Chungcheong Province and ran a small noodle stall in Noryangjin, providing meals to market merchants on credit recorded in a ledger.

She is now an unofficial inspector who testifies about the Won Buddhist night warehouse and the movement of contaminated-water stock.

The trading firm needs her sharp eye but tries to control the direction of her testimony by invoking her family's unpaid credit.

/story_contents/B034/actors/4/sections/붕.en:
On the night the G19E03 coolant color-indexing organism contaminated the cold-storage labels, K214 Dan Noeul mistook a blue marking for a determination that the water was drinkable.

Twenty-three residents who drank that water collapsed, and his mother, Dan Mi-seon, suffered kidney damage that left her needing purification treatment every week.

Whenever he sees a blue glow spreading across wet bricks, No-eul remembers the tank valve he opened.

/story_contents/B034/actors/4/sections/생.en:
K214 Dan Noeul discovered that the color changes left by the G19E03 coolant color-indexing organism varied with the temperature at which each brick was fired, allowing her to identify compartments holding contaminated water.

Using Seo Nayeon's stamp chart and Ma Sol's cordon, she temporarily isolated the contaminated compartments and made it possible to lift the cordon after retesting three days later.

But when someone began replacing stamped bricks every night, a reversible testing procedure became a means of permanent seizure.

/story_contents/B034/actors/4/sections/현.en:
K214 Dan Noeul is protected until the warehouse interrogation as the sole eyewitness to the nighttime transfer of the Won Buddhist contaminated-water stock.

She has identified compartments where Seo Nayeon's stamped bricks were changed and testified that Ma Sol's cordon was justified, but has not named the person who ordered the transfer.

Her current standing remains unsettled because she is about to choose between her mother's right to treatment and public testimony.

/story_contents/B034/actors/4/sections/비.en:
K214 Dan Noeul once falsified a ledger entry for spoiled ice and knows that the ice was used as coolant for the first organism culture vat.

In exchange for guaranteed purification treatment for her mother, Dan Mi-seon, she falsely testified that she had not seen the face of Oh Gyeong-taek, the trading firm's general manager.

She also owes Ma Sol twelve water-purification sheets lost during the cordon and Seo Nayeon a box of test bricks.

/story_contents/B034/actors/4/sections/관.en:
Before the collapse, K214 Dan Noeul worked with Seo Nayeon on repairs to the market floor, recording stamps by brick lot to make a map of nighttime leaks.

During the first contaminated-water disturbance, she and Ma Sol were trapped in the same cold-storage compartment; No-eul read the stock chart, Ma Sol broke down the door, and they escaped together.

Seo Nayeon values continuity of physical evidence, while Ma Sol prioritizes an immediate cordon, and both wait to see which of their efforts No-eul's eyewitness account will complete.

/story_contents/B034/actors/4/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, K214 Dan Noeul discovers that a brick in a cordoned compartment differs from Seo Nayeon's original stamp record.

In Act 2, she follows the transfer route through underground drains with Ma Sol and obtains a ledger showing that Oh Gyeong-taek traded treatment rights for sales of contaminated water.

In Act 3, every branch opens up: full disclosure, trading evidence and remaining silent, or converting the trading firm into a victims' management cooperative without dissolving it.

/story_contents/B034/actors/4/sections/분.en:
K214 Dan Noeul's ending turns on whether she protects her mother's treatment through a private deal or makes it a right for all victims of the contaminated water.

Disclosure brings down Oh Gyeong-taek and the trading firm but creates a gap in the distribution of stored water; silence extends her mother's treatment but conceals further harm.

Conversion to a management cooperative requires Seo Nayeon's and Ma Sol's cooperation and forces No-eul to confess to falsifying the ledger.

/story_contents/B034/actors/4/arc/0/summ.en:
During an early-morning inspection, K214 Dan Noeul confirms that a brick stamp in a cordoned compartment has changed and that cart tracks on the floor lead to Oh Gyeong-taek's private warehouse.

Seo Nayeon presents the original stamp chart, and Ma Sol demands an immediate cordon of the entire area, but the time for her mother's treatment is approaching.

No-eul repeats her earlier statement at the interrogation that she did not see the man's face, then enters the drain alone.

/story_contents/B034/actors/4/arc/1/summ.en:
In the drain, K214 Dan Noeul and Ma Sol find hidden barcode strips and a ledger of contaminated-water sales, and No-eul realizes that her old falsification is connected to the start of the incident.

Seo Nayeon pinpoints when the bricks were replaced, and Oh Gyeong-taek sends word that she will cut off Dan Mi-seon's treatment rights.

No-eul makes three copies of the ledger but has not yet decided where to release them or whom to bargain with.

/story_contents/B034/actors/4/arc/2/summ.en:
K214 Dan Noeul can release the ledger and barcode strips to bring down Oh Gyeong-taek and the Won Buddhist organization, or hand over the original.

She can secure lifelong treatment for her mother.

She can also confess to her own falsification and choose to convert the trading firm into a victims' management cooperative overseen by Seo Nayeon and Ma Sol.

Every branch determines the distribution of stored water, Dan Mi-seon's treatment, and the scope of compensation for victims of the contaminated water.

/story_contents/B034/actors/4/outcomes/0.en:
At a public interrogation, K214 Dan Noeul identifies Oh Gyeong-taek and admits his own past falsification, then distributes the sales ledger.

The Won Buddhist organization is dissolved. Seo Nayeon retests the contaminated compartments and Ma Sol guards a temporary distribution line, but water prices soar for three days.

Though Dan Mi-seon loses her priority treatment rights, she becomes the first officially registered patient of a shared victims' fund.

/story_contents/B034/actors/4/outcomes/1.en:
K214 Dan Noeul gives Oh Gyeong-taek the original ledger and barcode strips in exchange for guaranteed lifelong purification treatment for Dan Mi-seon.

Ma Sol's cordon is ruled an excessive response, Seo Nayeon's stamp chart is confiscated, and the contaminated-water stock continues to be sold under another name.

No-eul saves her mother but becomes a silent custodian who checks the credit ledgers of new victims every week.

/story_contents/B034/actors/4/outcomes/2.en:
K214 Dan Noeul releases the evidence through multiple channels and postpones dissolution of the trading firm on condition that its storage facilities be handed over to a victims' management cooperative.

Seo Nayeon takes charge of brick authentication, Ma Sol of temporary cordons, and Dan Mi-seon's treatment is moved to the same place in line as that of every other contamination victim.

No-eul loses her voting rights for falsifying the ledger but remains an inspector who broadcasts the nighttime inventory publicly.

/story_contents/B034/actors/5/sections/정.en:
K239 Pyeong Jiwoo is a Korean wireless-equipment technician who grew up in a metropolitan apartment complex and learned to judge the authenticity of recordings by sound quality and transmission intervals.

His family trusted disaster broadcasts, but he considered something a fact only after checking the editing practices inside the transmitting station as well.

After the collapse, he follows a rule of testifying about signals he witnessed without exaggeration, distinguishing between originals, estimates, and intervals of silence.

/story_contents/B034/actors/5/sections/붕.en:
K239 Pyeong Jiwoo calibrated disaster transmitters and compared night logs for the Yeouido Investment Union, recording deliberate silences that looked like faults in a separate ledger.

Just before the collapse, on a superior's orders, he marked one line of a test transmission concerning Gwon Mirae as inactive, but did not delete the original, leaving it recoverable at any time.

That reversible choice was a compromise to protect a colleague at the time, but is now the only clue that can recover the timeline of a disappearance.

/story_contents/B034/actors/5/sections/가.en:
As a survivor affiliated with HC01, K239 Pyeong Jiwoo knows the Yeouido Investment Union's closed technical culture, but puts continuity of records ahead of the company's reputation.

He maintains the paper frequency chart signed by shift workers and the equipment-room sealing cord as shared evidence, without claiming personal ownership.

The community respects him as an eyewitness to transmission records, but is also wary of his attempts to interpret missing intervals on his own.

/story_contents/B034/actors/5/sections/붕.en:
On the night the G09E12 low-temperature spore host spread through the cooling duct into the transmission room, K239 Pyeong Jiwoo picked up a colleague's distress signal but could not immediately open the spore-blocking shutter.

Because the distress signal and the host's mimicry used the same call sign, he repeated the verification procedure, and a shift crew disappeared in the meantime.

Ever since, cold air and repeated calls make his fingers go numb, and he is gripped by guilt that he protected records before people.

/story_contents/B034/actors/5/sections/생.en:
K239 Pyeong Jiwoo discovered that the G09E12 low-temperature spore host followed the heat of transmitters and lured the organism into an empty relay room by briefly switching a backup transmitter on and off.

He restored the log he had previously marked inactive and confirmed a tiny timing difference between the imitated signal and Gwon Mirae's actual transmission.

Since that day, he has resolved that a witness is not merely someone who recounts a memory, but someone who leaves behind a procedure that can be checked again.

/story_contents/B034/actors/5/sections/현.en:
K239 Pyeong Jiwoo is a key eyewitness at the Mapo Union's Yeouido Investment Union who personally heard the pre-disappearance transmission record, and he guards the equipment seal until the XT05-SC3 investigation team is ready to open the original.

Releasing Gwon Mirae's record could reveal the missing person's route, but would also expose the company's internal cover-up and the evacuation frequencies.

He has not yet decided whether to give Choi Jiwoo the key to the blank slot or allow only restricted listening.

/story_contents/B034/actors/5/sections/비.en:
K239 Pyeong Jiwoo heard the last four seconds of Gwon Mirae's transmission but classified them at the time as equipment interference, and he conceals the fact that his judgment contributed to a delay in the search.

He swore to give Choi Jiwoo the blank slot needed to find the original, but that slot also bears his own signature for marking the entry inactive.

His debt to reveal the truth conflicts with his responsibility to protect the survival frequencies, and he feels that neither choice is clean.

/story_contents/B034/actors/5/sections/관.en:
On the day Gwon Mirae lowered the output of a test transmission, K239 Pyeong Jiwoo checked the waveform at the adjacent console and later promised to testify that her record had not been altered.

He and Choi Jiwoo salvaged paper logs just before they were discarded, and he swore to hand over the blank slot and seal number needed to find the original.

He also worked shifts with the V02 circulator bus to carry a mobile antenna, but made a separate comparison chart so its limited snapshots would not be mistaken for human memory.

/story_contents/B034/actors/5/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, K239 Pyeong Jiwoo compares spore traces in the cooling duct with the timing difference in Gwon Mirae's transmission and admits to the inactive marker he concealed.

In Act 2, he enters the sealed room with Choi Jiwoo and restores the original, but confirms that broadcasting it publicly would reveal both the evacuation frequencies and the missing person's hiding place.

In Act 3, he faces every branch—full disclosure, restricted testimony, or permanently sealing the original—and proves through his choice that a witness's responsibility concerns not only how much truth is revealed, but how it is revealed.

/story_contents/B034/actors/5/sections/분.en:
If K239 Pyeong Jiwoo chooses full disclosure, he reveals Gwon Mirae's movements and the company's cover-up, but must endure the community's condemnation until the evacuation network has been reassigned.

If he chooses restricted testimony, he gives Choi Jiwoo only a verifiable copy to protect people, but some bereaved families remember him as another person who concealed the truth.

If he chooses permanent sealing, he prevents the immediate risk of being tracked, but, unable to erase his signature, leaves both his guilt and the key to the next investigator.

/story_contents/B034/actors/5/arc/0/summ.en:
In the Yeouido Investment Union's sealed equipment, K239 Pyeong Jiwoo finds a brief delay between Gwon Mirae's call sign and the mimicry of the G09E12 low-temperature spore host.

He confesses to Choi Jiwoo that the log he marked inactive in the past was not deleted and can be restored.

Together, they compare the paper frequency chart with the V02 circulator bus's shift snapshots to establish the time of the final transmission.

/story_contents/B034/actors/5/arc/1/summ.en:
K239 Pyeong Jiwoo gives Choi Jiwoo the blank slot.

He corroborates Gwon Mirae's transmission record with eyewitness testimony, but also finds the coordinates of an evacuation relay station in the original.

The investigation team demands immediate disclosure, while HC01 seeks to extend the seal for fear the coordinates will leak.

Pyeong Jiwoo publicly acknowledges that his earlier judgment delayed the search and binds the final decision to an evidentiary procedure rather than to one individual.

/story_contents/B034/actors/5/arc/2/summ.en:
In the full-disclosure branch, K239 Pyeong Jiwoo broadcasts the entire original; in the restricted-testimony branch, he gives Choi Jiwoo and the bereaved families a verifiable copy with the coordinates obscured.

In the permanent-seal branch, he places the original in an independent vault and releases only his processing signature and the conditions for opening it.

In no branch does he alter Gwon Mirae's record, and he leaves an audit trail so later generations can judge the difference between concealment and protection.

/story_contents/B034/actors/5/outcomes/0.en:
K239 Pyeong Jiwoo releases both Gwon Mirae's original transmission and his own signature for marking it inactive, bringing down the Yeouido Investment Union's system of concealment.

The evacuation frequencies are hastily changed and some search teams are exposed to danger, but the time of the disappearance and direction of travel are established in the official record.

He loses his position but becomes the first person to testify at an independent archive, continuing to take responsibility in public.

/story_contents/B034/actors/5/outcomes/1.en:
K239 Pyeong Jiwoo provides Choi Jiwoo and a representative of the bereaved families with a copy that obscures the coordinates, and publicly testifies only to the authenticity of Gwon Mirae's transmission.

The survival network is protected, but distrust over access to the original remains, so he accepts regular reviews and a multiple-seal procedure.

Because the record can be reopened later, his past choice is not fixed forever either, but remains subject to the community's judgment.

/story_contents/B034/actors/5/outcomes/2.en:
Citing the risk of being tracked, K239 Pyeong Jiwoo refuses to broadcast the original and seals the equipment and paper logs together in an independent vault.

He is condemned for failing to keep his promise to Gwon Mirae, but prevents the host's imitated signal from finding the evacuation network again.

In the end, he leaves Choi Jiwoo the conditions for opening the vault and the location of the blank slot, preserving the possibility that the next generation can reverse the decision.

/story_contents/B034/actors/6/sections/정.en:
K265 Seop Seoyeon is a Korean former packaging-equipment inspector who reads a product's manufacturing history from embossing depth and bonding temperature rather than drug names.

Rather than blame patients for what they do not know, he believes it is necessary to trace who abandoned responsibility for verification during distribution.

After the collapse, he is a victim of counterfeit medicine, yet also seeks to turn the process knowledge he remembers into inspection rules for the communal infirmary.

/story_contents/B034/actors/6/sections/붕.en:
K265 Seop Seoyeon inspected faulty blister seals and embossed batch numbers at a small pharmaceutical packaging company, and left a batch he had rejected under delivery pressure in the bin awaiting reinspection.

A manager demanded that he change its status to approved, but he merely withheld electronic approval so the next shift could reverse the decision.

That reversible hold preserved reference samples for comparing the embossing on genuine packaging found after the collapse with that of counterfeit medicine.

/story_contents/B034/actors/6/sections/가.en:
K265 Seop Seoyeon belongs to HP06's Sangha Relief Court, but does not want either the rationing committee or the militia to monopolize inspection authority.

At Bong-gam's herbal infirmary, he keeps each patient's temperature chart alongside fragments of medicine packaging and cross-checks them against Hwang Serin's distribution register.

Within the community, he is protected as a victim who can testify, but is also treated as a dangerous whistleblower who could intensify anxiety over rations.

/story_contents/B034/actors/6/sections/붕.en:
After taking counterfeit medicine disguised as a fever reducer, K265 Seop Seoyeon was harmed when fine filaments of the G21E05 communications mycelial organism invaded his gums and ear canals.

The organism carries transmission noise through his body like a vibration, so he often confuses people's whispers with echoes of rationing radio calls.

Because he remembers giving the same medicine to his family first, he is driven to identify its distributor rather than focus on his own recovery.

/story_contents/B034/actors/6/sections/생.en:
K265 Seop Seoyeon drew on his packaging-inspection experience to discover that the G21E05 communication-root fungus makes a brief clicking sound when it reacts to heat from a particular silver-foil adhesive.

After Bonggam used his skilled fever treatment to lower Seop Seoyeon's body temperature, Seop heated packaging fragments to identify infected bundles of counterfeit medicine.

This discovery turned him from a mere victim into an on-site inspector, but the more he uses the fungus's reaction, the worse his hearing damage becomes.

/story_contents/B034/actors/6/sections/현.en:
K265 Seop Seoyeon testifies about the harm caused by counterfeit-medicine distribution and runs a temporary inspection station at the Sangha Relief State on the Yeouido Line, but he has no official authority to recall the medicine.

If he stops Hwang Serin's distribution line immediately, patients will lose access even to genuine medicine; if distribution continues, more infected bundles could spread.

He is now about to choose which procedure to demand: a public recall, a secret replacement, or continued distribution.

/story_contents/B034/actors/6/sections/비.en:
K265 When his first symptoms appeared, Seop Seoyeon gave the two remaining counterfeit fever-reducer tablets to his family instead of preserving them as evidence, and one family member never returned.

Because he owes Bonggam for treating him, he cannot openly criticize the herbal infirmary's incomplete records, and he has agreed with Hwang Serin to testify truthfully about the harm caused in the distribution line.

He believes that being a victim does not absolve him of his own mistaken decision to share the tablets.

/story_contents/B034/actors/6/sections/관.en:
K265 Seop Seoyeon witnessed patients who had received the same manufacturing number in Hwang Serin's distribution line begin trembling at the same time, and collected packaging fragments to reconstruct the sequence of harm.

Bonggam lowered Seop Seoyeon's high fever and documented his hearing problems at the herbal infirmary; in return for treatment, the two agreed to manage all packaging samples jointly.

His relationship with Hwang Serin remains not one of hostility, but an uneasy collaboration in which they must share responsibility for continued distribution and verification.

/story_contents/B034/actors/6/sections/3.en:
K265 In Act 1, Seop Seoyeon proves the difference between the imprints on genuine and counterfeit medicine and confesses that the two tablets he gave away broke the chain of evidence.

In Act 2, he compares Hwang Serin's register with Bonggam's temperature charts to trace the infected bundles, but confirms that announcing a recall could provoke a riot at the infirmary.

In Act 3, he makes every branch—public recall, secret replacement, and controlled distribution—feasible, and leaves a patient-by-patient tracking chart in every ending.

/story_contents/B034/actors/6/sections/분.en:
K265 If Seop Seoyeon chooses a public recall, he finds infected patients quickly at the cost of undermining trust in distribution, and discloses his own mistake involving his family as well.

If he chooses secret replacement, he changes the medicine without causing panic but leaves Hwang Serin and Bonggam indebted to the concealment.

If he chooses controlled distribution, he gives the limited genuine medicine to the most severely ill first, while personally recording and taking responsibility for who does not receive it.

/story_contents/B034/actors/6/arc/0/summ.en:
K265 Seop Seoyeon collects fragments of counterfeit-medicine packaging from a waste bin at the Sangha Relief State.

He identifies contaminated bundles by the clicking sounds made by the G21E05 communication-root fungus.

He finds recipients of the same manufacturing number in Hwang Serin's distribution register and connects their accounts of harm.

Bonggam lowers the fever that rises during the inspection, helping Seop Seoyeon carry the procedure through to the end.

/story_contents/B034/actors/6/arc/1/summ.en:
K265 Seop Seoyeon discovers that medicines with different imprint depths were switched not at the distribution warehouse, but at an intermediate point in transit.

He also confirms the calculation that, because genuine medicine is in short supply, recalling all of it would leave some patients with high fevers untreated.

He discloses that he gave evidence tablets to his family and distributes inspection authority so that the victims' representative, Hwang Serin, and Bonggam decide together.

/story_contents/B034/actors/6/arc/2/summ.en:
K265 In the public-recall branch, Seop Seoyeon posts every manufacturing number and symptom; in the secret-replacement branch, he changes only the medicine while keeping the order in which patients are called.

In the controlled-distribution branch, he allocates medicine that passes the fungus-reaction test according to severity and does not delete the names of those who do not qualify.

In all three branches, he preserves the packaging samples and temperature charts so that concealment or mistaken judgments can be reviewed later.

/story_contents/B034/actors/6/outcomes/0.en:
K265 Seop Seoyeon posts the counterfeit medicine's manufacturing numbers and the list of victims on the distribution center wall, and declares a full recall with Hwang Serin.

The disturbance closes the distribution center for a day, but people infected with the G21E05 communication-root fungus are isolated early, and the intermediate switching point is exposed.

He also records that he shared evidence tablets with his family, remaining both a victim and a responsible party.

/story_contents/B034/actors/6/outcomes/1.en:
K265 With Bonggam and Hwang Serin's help, Seop Seoyeon quietly replaces the counterfeit medicine with genuine medicine and vouchers for herbal treatment while keeping the existing call list.

He prevents immediate panic, but patients unaware of the replacement wonder why their symptoms are being recorded.

He sets a disclosure deadline in the sealed original register so the secret does not become permanent concealment.

/story_contents/B034/actors/6/outcomes/2.en:
K265 Seop Seoyeon acknowledges the shortage of genuine medicine and proposes a restricted distribution chart based on body temperature, infection response, and degree of dehydration.

He personally explains the painful choice to make some patients wait, combining a public lottery with medical priority rather than Hwang Serin's armed distribution.

More people survive, but a list remains of those who did not receive medicine, and he becomes a watchdog who demands a review every month.

/story_contents/B034/actors/7/sections/정.en:
K250 O Hangyeol is a second-generation resident of Korea, born to a mother who grew up in Sulaymaniyah, Iraqi Kurdistan, and a father from southern Korea.

Her mother migrated through a university interpretation and translation program in the late 2000s and later ran a small heating-and-cooling appliance repair shop. At home, the family used Sorani and Korean depending on the situation.

She does not treat her family's migration history as proof of loyalty, but carries it forward as the practical skill of honoring metering and repair contracts precisely.

/story_contents/B034/actors/7/sections/붕.en:
K250 O Hangyeol repaired fuel pumps and heater pressure gauges at the family repair shop and organized a communal warehouse's incoming and outgoing inventory sheets at night.

Just before the collapse, she placed a container of a customer's unpaid fuel in a holding area rather than processing it as a return, so she could give it back if its original owner came.

That reversible hold later kept the Sangha Relief State's first generator running, but also left an ownership dispute and a personal debt.

/story_contents/B034/actors/7/sections/가.en:
K250 O Hangyeol works in HP06 Sangha Relief State militia distribution oversight, preferring sealed gauge markings and dual signatures to weapons as means of control.

He supports distribution oversight under Hwang Serin's command, shares fuel-depot duty and tools with Dugam, and instructs Yongdu on the order of on-site guard rotations.

He converts the Sorani parts notes he learned to make at the family repair shop into a ledger with Korean alongside them, which anyone can cross-check, rather than treating them as a private code.

/story_contents/B034/actors/7/sections/붕.en:
K250 O Hangyeol experienced an attack on Yongdu's guard detail after the G21E06 communication-root fungus imitated a command transmission in a voice like her own and induced them to open the fuel-depot door.

She closed a valve to save one person, but the heat went out in another area, causing cases of hypothermia.

Since then, fear that her commands can be forged has led her to require tool marks and face-to-face confirmation for every order, testing even her colleagues' trust.

/story_contents/B034/actors/7/sections/생.en:
K250 O Hangyeol detected an intrusion into the fuel depot by exploiting the fact that the G21E06 communication-root fungus could imitate a voice but could not forge the physical movement of a pressure-gauge needle.

She exchanged wrenches of different specifications with Dugam and had Yongdu check both valve pressure and scratches on the seals, neutralizing the false radio orders.

After that turning point, she recognizes as orders only verification procedures that three people can reproduce, not an individual's voice.

/story_contents/B034/actors/7/sections/현.en:
K250 O Hangyeol is a militia worker overseeing fuel and food distribution at the Sangha Relief State on the Yeouido Line, and is responsible for the fuel-depot seals in XT01-SC2.

Hwang Serin orders the reserves opened for winter heating, but they include fuel marked as belonging to its original owner and the ward's emergency reserve.

He is now about to choose whether to distribute all of it as ordered, hold some back, or disclose the oversight records and put the matter to a joint vote.

/story_contents/B034/actors/7/sections/비.en:
