K250 O Hangyeol knows that the container of fuel that kept the first generator running belonged to a customer before the collapse, and that the customer's family may have survived on the outskirts of Bukhansan Bogukmun.

He bears a debt to Dugam for lending him tools, command responsibility for Yongdu's injury, and Hwang Serin's trust all at once.

He also hides his guilt over recording his decision to close the heating valve a few minutes late in the official report after the first attack, blurring the connection between his decision and a death from hypothermia.

/story_contents/B034/actors/7/sections/관.en:
K250 O Hangyeol prevented excessive withdrawals twice by presenting gauge charts instead of resorting to armed confrontation in Hwang Serin's distribution line, earning a command agreement as a result.

He has shared wrenches brought from the family repair shop and fuel-depot tools with Dugam, and they have checked each other's duty seals.

Yongdu guarded the fuel depot under O Hangyeol's command, but since being injured by an imitated order, he no longer trusts voice instructions; the two can rebuild trust only through procedure.

/story_contents/B034/actors/7/sections/3.en:
K250 In Act 1, O Hangyeol introduces pressure-gauge authentication to distinguish imitated radio transmissions from real orders, and discloses the ownership ledger he had hidden.

In Act 2, he confirms that Hwang Serin's heating order, Dugam's maintenance plan, and Yongdu's guard report point to different needs.

In Act 3, he carries out every branch—full distribution, strategic reservation, and a joint vote—recording the terms for returning the owner's property and responsibility for hypothermia-related harm under each choice.

/story_contents/B034/actors/7/sections/분.en:
K250 If O Hangyeol chooses full distribution, he reduces winter deaths but uses up the ward's emergency reserve and the original owner's share, incurring a future obligation to compensate them.

If he chooses strategic reservation, he protects the basis for long-term survival but clashes with residents demanding immediate heat and may lose his militia position.

If he chooses a joint vote, the decision takes longer, but Hwang Serin, Dugam, Yongdu, and the residents consult the same ledger and share responsibility.

/story_contents/B034/actors/7/arc/0/summ.en:
K250 When an order to withdraw fuel arrives over a radio transmission imitated by the G21E06 communication-root fungus, O Hangyeol discovers that the pressure-gauge movement and wrench scratches do not match.

He withdraws Yongdu's guard detail and installs dual seals on every valve with Dugam.

He then submits to Hwang Serin the ownership ledger for the fuel he held before the collapse, making his hidden debt official.

/story_contents/B034/actors/7/arc/1/summ.en:
K250 While calculating heating demand, O Hangyeol confirms that using even the ward's emergency reserve would leave the maintenance vehicle unable to run ten days later.

Hwang Serin commands him to prevent deaths from hypothermia now, while Dugam cites a contractual requirement to preserve fuel for transporting parts.

Yongdu warns that imitated radio transmissions could recur and demands that O Hangyeol stop monopolizing orders and allow residents to observe.

/story_contents/B034/actors/7/arc/2/summ.en:
K250 In the full-distribution branch, O Hangyeol opens the seals.

He enters the debt of return in the ledger; in the strategic-reservation branch, he locks away the minimum needed for the ward and maintenance.

In the joint-vote branch, he publishes a table of figures in Korean and Sorani and obtains signatures from residents, Hwang Serin, Dugam, and Yongdu.

In every branch, he does not rely on imitated voices, but leaves a record of each order's authenticity through physical instruments and multiple checks.

/story_contents/B034/actors/7/outcomes/0.en:
K250 Under Hwang Serin's command, O Hangyeol opens all the fuel reserves and prioritizes restoring heat to areas where it has stopped.

Cases of hypothermia decline, but the repair vehicle and ward generator are left without fuel for the following month, so he and Dugam must find an alternative power source.

He does not hide that he consumed the original owner's share, and signs a public debt agreement to repay it from future production.

/story_contents/B034/actors/7/outcomes/1.en:
K250 O Hangyeol seals away the minimum fuel needed for the ward and pump-maintenance vehicle and distributes only the rest, partially defying Hwang Serin's immediate order.

His militia position is suspended amid protests from areas left without heat, but ten days later the repair vehicle reopens a food transport route.

Yongdu and Dugam testify to his judgment while preserving the list of victims as well, so that success cannot erase responsibility.

/story_contents/B034/actors/7/outcomes/2.en:
K250 O Hangyeol discloses fuel quantities, ownership, and the estimated risk of death, and puts allocations by use to a vote observed by residents.

The decision is delayed, leaving some areas to endure one more day of cold, but reducing the opportunity for imitated orders or militia coercion to intervene.

He retains his oversight position but returns his sole key and establishes a system of distributed custody with Hwang Serin, Dugam, and Yongdu.

/story_contents/B034/actors/8/sections/정.en:
K276 Hwang Noeul is a third-generation Korean born into a family whose grandparents, from Pokhara, Nepal, migrated through an industrial trainee program in the late 1990s and settled in Korea.

After periods of return and remigration, the family ran a bicycle-wheel truing and small metalworking shop in the capital region. They mainly spoke Korean at home and also used Nepali with the grandparents.

He does not use his migrant background as a decorative marker, but carries forward the family business's ethic of recording the origin of metal, labor hours, and terms of return precisely.

/story_contents/B034/actors/8/sections/붕.en:
K276 Hwang Noeul straightened wheel rims and sorted discarded bicycles and construction steel by grade at the family workshop, while studying welding inspection at a night vocational school.

Just before the collapse, he kept steel suspected of having been removed illegally on a separate shelf instead of cutting it, so it could be returned if its owner provided proof.

That reversible hold gave the Seocho Computing Group access to specification-grade steel, but an unsettled account with the dealer who concealed the removal route followed him into the survival period.

/story_contents/B034/actors/8/sections/가.en:
K276 Hwang Noeul leads a steel-recovery crew connecting HC08 and the Seocho Computing Group on the Gangnam Line, prioritizing provenance and fatigue-crack markings over the quantity recovered.

He reports steel inventory to elder I Hongwon and negotiates with Sin Gaon for the rail family's transport rights and safety inspections in exchange for wheel supplies.

The community needs his skills, but also holds him responsible for distribution delays caused by his strict practice of classifying usable steel as hazardous.

/story_contents/B034/actors/8/sections/붕.en:
K276 Hwang Noeul lost three crew members at a recovery site where the G06E15 migratory-bird wetland predator flock converged on gleaming cut surfaces and hammer vibrations.

He was slow to abandon the cart in an effort to keep its load, and the rescue signal of a colleague trapped beneath a wet steel plate was drowned out by the flock's wingbeats.

Since then, he has refused to describe metal only in inventory figures and engraves each recovered item with its discovery site and a marker for the dead.

/story_contents/B034/actors/8/sections/생.en:
K276 Using an old brake drum, Hwang Noeul confirmed that the G06E15 migratory-bird wetland predator flock gathers at irregular striking sounds but changes direction in response to steady low-frequency resonance.

He sounded three drums at different distances to lure the flock into an empty wetland, allowing the crew to escape without the steel.

From that day on, he measures a successful recovery by everyone's safe return and the preservation of markings, not by load size, and designates resonance equipment as essential safety gear.

/story_contents/B034/actors/8/sections/현.en:
K276 Hwang Noeul leads a steel-recovery crew for the Seocho Computing Group on the Gangnam Line and is about to decide how to allocate wheel-grade steel in XT01-SC3.

I Hongwon demands that the communal inventory be maintained, while Sin Gaon demands all the specification-grade wheels first as a condition of restoring the rail line.

He now faces three choices—prioritizing the rail contract, prioritizing the communal inventory, or reprocessing hazardous steel—and has not yet signed off on any of them.

/story_contents/B034/actors/8/sections/비.en:
K276 Hwang Noeul is hiding work-time records showing that he might have saved one colleague in the wetland accident if he had abandoned the cart sooner.

He has a duty to report accurate inventory to I Hongwon and promised Sin Gaon wheel supplies twice, but treated the same agreement as though it were documented separately.

He also knows that some unsettled steel from the family workshop is mixed into the highest-grade inventory, making him feel the burden of an ownership debt with every supply decision.

/story_contents/B034/actors/8/sections/관.en:
K276 Hwang Noeul reports steel inventory and crack rates to I Hongwon every week and has agreed not to downgrade hazardous classifications without the elder's approval.

He made an agreement with Sin Gaon to secure the rail family's transport rights in exchange for wheel supplies, but as they confirmed the same terms twice, the wording on deadlines and quantities ended up differing.

The three worked together on the first rail restoration, but if it comes to light that Hwang Noeul concealed the origin of the steel involved in the accident, both their dealings and their chain of command will be shaken.

/story_contents/B034/actors/8/sections/3.en:
K276 In Act 1, Hwang Noeul opens a new recovery route with resonance equipment that repels the predator flock, and discovers the record of his delay during the accident and markings on the unsettled steel.

In Act 2, he reveals that both I Hongwon's communal-inventory plan and Sin Gaon's rail-first contract are necessary for survival but cannot be fulfilled at the same time.

In Act 3, he carries out every branch—rail priority, communal inventory, and reprocessing hazardous steel—and discloses the double agreement and his responsibility for the accident in each ending.

/story_contents/B034/actors/8/sections/분.en:
K276 If Hwang Noeul prioritizes the rail line, he restores the transport network quickly but delays production of carts and defensive panels in Changdong, giving Sin Gaon strong bargaining power.

If he chooses the communal inventory, he preserves I Hongwon's order but delays outside food transport and becomes liable for breaching the contract.

If he chooses to reprocess hazardous steel, he can partly meet both needs, but the crew must reenter the territory of the G06E15 migratory-bird wetland predator flock.

/story_contents/B034/actors/8/arc/0/summ.en:
K276 Hwang Noeul redirects the G06E15 migratory-bird wetland predator flock's movement with brake-drum resonance.

He confirms that specification-grade steel remains at the flooded recovery yard.

Among the steel markings, he finds both an unsettled number from the family workshop and the duration of the delay on the day of the accident.

He orders the crew to withdraw immediately, but decides to report both the legal and physical defects in the inventory to I Hongwon and Sin Gaon.

/story_contents/B034/actors/8/arc/1/summ.en:
K276 Hwang Noeul reports the communal inventory quantity to I Hongwon and discloses to Sin Gaon the difference in delivery deadlines between the two wheel contracts.

Repairing the rail line first would bring in outside supplies but halt transport carts within Changdong; preserving the inventory would leave the rail line flooded before the next heavy rain.

He also releases the record showing that he abandoned the cart late during the accident, allowing the crew to vote independently on whether to reenter the danger zone.

/story_contents/B034/actors/8/arc/2/summ.en:
K276 In the rail-priority branch, Hwang Noeul supplies specification-grade wheels to Sin Gaon, and in the communal-inven.

branch, he stores the steel in separate locations under I Hongwon's management.

In the hazardous-steel reprocessing branch, he organizes resonance equipment and short-shift crews to recover flooded steel and divide it between the two needs.

In every branch, he discloses the double agreement and the unsettled markings, and engraves the accident victims' names on the finished products.

/story_contents/B034/actors/8/outcomes/0.en:
K276 Hwang Noeul prioritizes fulfilling his wheel-supply contract with Sin Gaon, putting most of the specification-grade steel into rail restoration.

Food vehicles arrive from outside, but cart production at the Seocho Computing Group stops, and I Hongwon removes him from inventory management.

To avoid becoming subordinate to the rail family, he specifies the final delivery date and the number of wheels to be returned in a new contract, retaining only his position as crew leader.

/story_contents/B034/actors/8/outcomes/1.en:
K276 Hwang Noeul kept the steel as common stock under I Hongwon's command and refused Sin Gaon's demand for priority supply.

Transport carts and armor plates within Changdong were maintained, but outside goods arrived late because of track flooding, creating liability for breach-of-contract compensation.

He put his workshop share up as collateral for the double contract and assigned the next wheel production lot by public draw.

/story_contents/B034/actors/8/outcomes/2.en:
K276 Hwang Noeul re-entered the flooded recovery yard with the work crew's consent and diverted the G06E15 Migratory-Wetland Predator Swarm with resonant equipment.

He reworked steel with fatigue cracks into short rims and reinforcing plates, partially meeting both the track and common-stock needs.

He delivered the accident-delay record to the victims' families and gave up unilateral loading judgment in every recovery mission thereafter.

/story_contents/B034/actors/9/sections/정.en:
V02 Circulating Bus was not a humanoid being with personhood, but a synthetic mobile vehicle body composed of a chassis/bogie platform, battery slots, and lane sensors.

Its function was limited to carrying passengers and equipment along designated routes and leaving sensor readings in shift records; it held neither independent ownership nor unlimited judgment authority.

Without assuming a long-term self, its operating history was verified only through each shift's snapshots and branch logs.

/story_contents/B034/actors/9/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, V02 Circulating Bus was a vehicle body that conducted lane-sensor tests and replaceable-battery efficiency inspections on a closed-loop route.

On its last normal run, it received temporary approval for a detour but did not delete the default route table, so an auditor could return it to the original route at any time.

This reversible detour record became a basis for comparing retired-line sections with safe sections after the collapse, and was not treated as evidence of independent decision-making.

/story_contents/B034/actors/9/sections/가.en:
V02 Circulating Bus was an HP04 jointly managed transport asset, and both custody and operation followed the synthetic-actor protocol.

Its custody was exactly joint custody under HP04 · seal witnessed by citizens · three-party signature on transfer, and no maintainer or operating crew could dispose of it alone.

Kim Nayul served as chief maintainer with an HP04 audit in attendance, inspecting the body battery, sensors, and shift logs separately.

/story_contents/B034/actors/9/sections/붕.en:
After colliding with the G18E03 Retired-Line Maintenance-Train Corps, V02 Circulating Bus had its left bogie frame twisted and two lane sensors destroyed, reducing its intersection-reading range.

Some onboard shift snapshots were also damaged by voltage loss, but because it lacked complete long-term memory, the lost experience could not be restored like human amnesia.

Collision marks and temporary welds remained on the vehicle body, revealing finite wear limits whenever it selected a high-speed detour or heavy load.

/story_contents/B034/actors/9/sections/생.en:
When the G18E03 Retired-Line Maintenance-Train Corps charged along track vibrations, V02 Circulating Bus combined its remaining lane sensors with manual-sign readings to escape onto the service road beside the retired line.

Kim Nayul temporarily fitted recovered bushings to the damaged bogie instead of standard parts, recording the original part number and wear value in the branch log so the replacement could be reversed.

Thereafter, operation was approved only when the vehicle body's limits, replaceable battery remainder, and allocated quantity of wear parts were all met.

/story_contents/B034/actors/9/sections/현.en:
V02 Circulating Bus waited on the Yeongdeungpo Line and XT02-SC1 as a transport asset of chassis/bogie platform, battery slots, and lane sensors, and had not yet received approval for its next route.

Only two shifts' worth of replaceable batteries remained, and the left bogie bushings had to be replaced after one long-distance run, but there was only one spare set.

It remained undecided before the three-party signature whether to prioritize carrying Pyeong Jiwoo's transmission equipment, civilian evacuation, or return to the maintenance depot.

/story_contents/B034/actors/9/sections/비.en:
V02 Circulating Bus was not assigned human guilt, but the snapshot from just before damage revealed one unapproved stop and a passenger-count discrepancy.

That log was separately preserved under the mandatory branch-log rule for forks; deleting it would make it impossible to establish the responsible party and the cause of battery consumption.

An operational debt remained from Kim Nayul's temporary bushings and HP04's spare batteries, so maintenance and citizen audit took priority in the next batch as well.

/story_contents/B034/actors/9/sections/관.en:
V02 Circulating Bus had its bogie, battery slots, and lane sensors inspected under Kim Nayul's chief maintenance and legal responsibility, with an HP04 audit attending every major task.

It carried mobile antennas and paper logs with Pyeong Jiwoo through shift cooperation, but the bus retained only that shift's snapshot and did not replace his human memory.

Neither relationship granted the vehicle the status of owner or friend; they were distinguished as management responsibility and work-record access rights.

/story_contents/B034/actors/9/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, V02 Circulating Bus had its damaged bogie and finite battery and parts stock audited, then recovered the branch log of the discrepant snapshot.

In Act 2, using only read-only information from the sector network, it compared routes for carrying Pyeong Jiwoo's equipment, civilian evacuation, and return to the maintenance depot while maintaining the cross-facility route block.

In Act 3, it carried out every branch of transmission support, evacuation priority, and preservation stop under joint custody under HP04 · seal witnessed by citizens · three-party signature on transfer.

/story_contents/B034/actors/9/sections/분.en:
In the transmission-support branch, V02 Circulating Bus carried Pyeong Jiwoo's equipment but consumed one of its two battery slots and the life of its bogie bushings.

In the evacuation-priority branch, it moved citizens to a safe zone, but original transmission delivery was delayed and one lane sensor suffered additional wear.

In the preservation-stop branch, it halted operation to preserve the vehicle body and spare parts, but could not contribute to immediate rescue or evidence transport.

/story_contents/B034/actors/9/arc/0/summ.en:
V02 Circulating Bus had the actual remaining life of its left bogie, battery slots, and lane sensors measured under Kim Nayul's chief maintenance and an HP04 audit in attendance.

Under the memory rule of keeping shift-only snapshots, prohibiting complete long-term memory, and requiring branch logs for forks, it separately preserved the record of the discrepant stop.

The citizen-observation record confirmed that it held two shifts' worth of replaceable batteries and only one spare bushing set.

/story_contents/B034/actors/9/arc/1/summ.en:
Within the network limits of sector network only · cross-facility routes blocked by default · read-only in emergencies, V02 Circulating Bus calculated three candidate routes.

Carrying Pyeong Jiwoo's mobile antenna favored evidence recovery, and civilian evacuation saved lives at once, but there were not enough batteries and parts to do both.

Kim Nayul and the HP04 audit disclosed the vehicle body's wear values and asked the citizen observers to sign the final priority.

/story_contents/B034/actors/9/arc/2/summ.en:
In the transmission-support branch, V02 Circulating Bus carried Pyeong Jiwoo and equipment to the Sangam connection point, and in the evacuation-priority branch it moved only approved passengers to the safe zone.

In the preservation-stop branch, it removed the batteries and awaited the next parts allocation while retaining the citizen-witnessed seal.

Every branch kept joint custody under HP04 · seal witnessed by citizens · three-party signature on transfer and the branch log, and was not recorded as the vehicle's unilateral choice.

/story_contents/B034/actors/9/outcomes/0.en:
After receiving the three-party signature, V02 Circulating Bus carried Pyeong Jiwoo's antenna and sealed logs along a read-only path in the restricted sector network.

It consumed most of one shift's battery and the left bogie bushing life, so it could not operate after return until spare parts were allocated.

The shift snapshots and lane-sensor records supported Pyeong Jiwoo's testimony, but were not considered complete long-term memory or independent witnessing.

/story_contents/B034/actors/9/outcomes/1.en:
With citizen observers' approval, V02 Circulating Bus left the transmission equipment behind and carried refugees within the seat-load limit to the Yeongdeungpo Line safe zone.

It did not make a second round trip because that would exceed the battery remainder and bogie-wear limit, and an external responsible party signed the boarding order.

After the operation, one lane sensor reached its replacement limit and was sealed until Kim Nayul's maintenance and an HP04 audit in attendance.

/story_contents/B034/actors/9/outcomes/2.en:
Following the audit finding that batteries and spare parts were simultaneously insufficient, V02 Circulating Bus did not operate and kept its vehicle body in HP04 joint custody.

The batteries were held separately, and citizen-witnessed seals were applied to the lane sensors and temporary bogie bushings to prevent unauthorized departure.

There was no immediate rescue result, but if the next shift changed the resource allocation, the decision could be reversed with a three-party signature.

/story_contents/B035/actors/0/sections/정.en:
Ran Jina is a wheel mechanic of Korean descent who grew up in the Changdong railway quarters and is in charge of the north-gate equipment of the medical train.

She is a field technician who reads axle cracks by vibration rather than sound.

At the center of her identity is the principle that refugees and medical staff must live on the same train.

/story_contents/B035/actors/0/sections/붕.en:
Before the Collapse, Ran Jina handled brake tests and wreck recovery at a night urban-rail depot.

She also took part in volunteer work converting carriages on the verge of scrapping into mobile clinics.

If the inspection originals she hid back then were made public again, her past dismissal could be overturned.

/story_contents/B035/actors/0/sections/가.en:
Ran Jina's family has run HC08 of the Seocho Computing Group for three generations, reconditioning bearings and brake shoes.

After the Collapse the wheel shop became the medical train's parts store and a dormitory for apprentices.

Rather than the family business's monopoly, she wants to protect a shared workshop where the whole north gate shares repair methods.

/story_contents/B035/actors/0/sections/붕.en:
During the first migratory-bird raid, Ran Jina trusted a broken inspection lamp and sent the quarantine carriage out onto the main line.

When G06E14, the migratory-bird wetland predators, pierced the roof vents, eleven patients vanished.

She does not hide responsibility for the misjudgment, but she cannot let go of the suspicion that someone had swapped the inspection lamp at the time.

/story_contents/B035/actors/0/sections/생.en:
In a disused tunnel, Ran Jina discovered that when migratory-bird feathers wind around a wheel flange, the predators' sense of direction is thrown off.

She could choose whether to use the last copper mesh on the brakes or on a lure trap.

Her decision to hold the trap back for now can still be reversed, and it can be rewired until the north-gate departure.

/story_contents/B035/actors/0/sections/현.en:
Ran Jina is now the north-gate mechanic of the Seocho Computing Group's medical train on the Gangnam Line and holds the departure approval stamp.

But the brake fault in Gwon Doha's patrol car and the time Sun Gaon found the medical carriage are tangled in the same stop record.

She is on the verge of choosing whether to send the train off or seal the records first.

/story_contents/B035/actors/0/sections/비.en:
Ran Jina hid one page of the stop log from the day of the accident under the floorboards of the wheel shop, and it still bears the tool marks of whoever replaced the inspection lamp.

She has also not yet repaid the two pairs of ceramic brake pads she borrowed from Gwon Doha.

Above all, guilt that she protected her family's maintenance license before the patients shakes her judgment.

/story_contents/B035/actors/0/sections/관.en:
K275 Gwon Doha is the contract partner who has entrusted her with the brake maintenance of the north-gate patrol cars, and who once towed Ran Jina to safety on a disused bridge.

K188 Sun Gaon is the record keeper who cross-checked the time the medical carriage was found against the stop log.

The three held the same signal box on the night G06E14, the migratory-bird wetland predators, first broke in, but each testifies to a different time.

/story_contents/B035/actors/0/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, Ran Jina traces the mismatched stop logs and confirms that the inspection lamp swap was no accident.

In Act 2, only one of Gwon Doha's patrol car and Sun Gaon's medical carriage can be repaired first, and the alliance's trust splits.

In Act 3, the endings branch into making the hidden original public and running the trap together, burning it and departing alone, or making herself the bait.

/story_contents/B035/actors/0/sections/분.en:
In the disclosure branch, Ran Jina hands over the original, completes the bird lure net with Gwon Doha and Sun Gaon, and wins joint maintenance rights over the north gate.

In the concealment branch, she burns the records and saves the medical train, but the wheel shop turns into a monopoly business and she loses both contracts.

In the sacrifice branch, she sends the train off, stays behind at the manual turntable, and lures G06E14, the migratory-bird wetland predators, onto a disused line.

/story_contents/B035/actors/0/arc/0/summ.en:
K291 Ran Jina finds on the north-gate axle a scrap of blue insulation identical to the inspection lamp at the time of the accident.

When she overlays Sun Gaon's discovery time on the stop log, a three-minute stop that never existed comes to light.

At a stage where she could still hide the original from under the floorboards again, she shows only half of it to Gwon Doha.

/story_contents/B035/actors/0/arc/1/summ.en:
K291 Ran Jina must either repair the brakes of Gwon Doha's patrol car with the remaining copper mesh or finish the bird trap on the medical carriage roof.

Either choice can be undone once before departure, but it is fixed once the flock gathers above the north gate.

Sun Gaon demands the records be made public, and Gwon Doha presses her to move the people first.

/story_contents/B035/actors/0/arc/2/summ.en:
K291 Ran Jina makes her final choice among making the original public, burning the records, and staying at the manual turntable.

If she discloses, the three drive G06E14, the migratory-bird wetland predators, into a shared trap; if she conceals, Ran Jina sends the train off alone.

If she stays, she uses her own vibration signal as bait to buy time for the medical train to leave the wetland.

/story_contents/B035/actors/0/outcomes/0.en:
K291 Ran Jina makes the stop original public and restores the conflicting testimony of Gwon Doha and Sun Gaon into a single timeline.

G06E14, the migratory-bird wetland predators, is lured onto the disused line wound with copper mesh, and the medical train passes the north gate.

In exchange for giving up her family's monopoly on licenses, she becomes the first elected supervisor of the shared workshop.

/story_contents/B035/actors/0/outcomes/1.en:
K291 Ran Jina burns the original, pours the patrol car's parts into the medical train, and gets the patients out at once.

Gwon Doha and Sun Gaon sense the manipulation and cut their contracts, and the Seocho Computing Group becomes a monopoly repair shop amid distrust.

She protected the survivors, but she will never uncover who replaced the inspection lamp.

/story_contents/B035/actors/0/outcomes/2.en:
K291 Ran Jina sends the medical train off, stays at the manual turntable, and draws in G06E14, the migratory-bird wetland predators, with wheel vibration.

As Gwon Doha applies the last brake and Sun Gaon recovers the original statements, the train and the evidence both survive.

Whether Ran Jina lives is unconfirmed, but the wheel-shop apprentices carry on her open maintenance code.

/story_contents/B035/actors/1/sections/정.en:
Chang Dahuin is a community organizer of Korean descent who grew up in a Sinnae rental housing complex and represents the victims of contaminated-medicine transport.

He records patients not as statistics but by their travel routes and household units.

He holds to the belief that people who could not be treated must still remain full members of the community.

/story_contents/B035/actors/1/sections/붕.en:
Before the Collapse, Chang Dahuin inspected transport temperatures and return reasons for medicines at a cold-chain distributor.

When the company dumped out-of-spec medicine on welfare facilities, he copied the internal ledger but could not make it public.

If the seal on the original server were found, both the settlement that bought his silence then and his dismissal record could be overturned.

/story_contents/B035/actors/1/sections/가.en:
Chang Dahuin's family ran a small laundry, and after the Collapse that space became a shared washhouse that quarantines contaminated clothing.

The victims in Neutral Convoy City on the Jamsil Line use laundry tickets like temporary identity cards.

Against the merchants' guild that buys and sells treatment priority, he insists on shared ownership of the victims' roster.

/story_contents/B035/actors/1/sections/붕.en:
On the day the contaminated medicine was first transported, Chang Dahuin ordered the refrigerated truck doors opened for ventilation.

As a result the fibers of G12E07, the microfiber skin swarm, spread into the waiting line, and several people, including his younger sibling, were infected.

He admits the order made the harm worse, yet he is convinced the shipping manifest in the sealed box was falsified.

/story_contents/B035/actors/1/sections/생.en:
Chang Dahuin discovered that the blue sediment left on the infected people's laundry tickets pointed to the warehouse the contaminated medicine had left from.

He could burn the samples to stop the spread of infection or seal them to keep as evidence.

The samples are now in a lime drum, a reversible stage at which one more wash can safely revive them.

/story_contents/B035/actors/1/sections/현.en:
Chang Dahuin now holds, as representative of the victims of contaminated-medicine transport, the right to negotiate compensation in Transfer City and the right to view the quarantine roster.

Jeon Miri's severity table and Mae Haru's Jegi-dong damage ledger list the same people at different grades.

Before distribution begins, he must choose which roster becomes the official record.

/story_contents/B035/actors/1/sections/비.en:
Chang Dahuin once wrote an extra line of symptoms onto Jeon Miri's table to raise his sibling's infection grade.

Of the three sealed boxes he borrowed from Mae Haru, he has not been able to return one because of the evidence samples.

He carries both the fear that confessing the manipulation could void the entire victims' roster and a representative's guilt.

/story_contents/B035/actors/1/sections/관.en:
K298 Jeon Miri is the triage officer Chang Dahuin contracted to put the victims' line onto the severity table.

K340 Mae Haru is the record keeper who twice cross-checked the names in the Jegi-dong damage ledger against the transport roster.

The three split the task of guarding the roster on the night G12E07, the microfiber skin swarm, overran the washhouse, but they remember differently who is responsible for the one falsified line.

/story_contents/B035/actors/1/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, Chang Dahuin links the laundry-ticket sediment to Mae Haru's ledger and reveals that the contaminated medicine was repackaged inside Transfer City.

In Act 2, he must either confess the manipulation to Jeon Miri and retest the whole roster, or keep silent and start distribution at once.

In Act 3, he meets one of three endings: public evidence, concealment that puts the victims first, or destroying the samples and resigning.

/story_contents/B035/actors/1/sections/분.en:
In the disclosure branch, Chang Dahuin confesses even his own manipulation, rebuilds trust in the roster, and shuts down the contaminated supply chain.

In the concealment branch, he moves distribution forward and saves many patients, but lower-graded victims are pushed out of the community.

In the destruction branch, he gives up the samples and his representative's authority and personally leads a mobile clinic for those infected by G12E07, the microfiber skin swarm.

/story_contents/B035/actors/1/arc/0/summ.en:
K316 Chang Dahuin takes a victim's sample with blue sediment out of the washhouse lime drum.

When he checks it against Mae Haru's ledger, the stamp of the Mangu repackaging site, supposedly shut down, appears again and again.

Still hiding the line he falsified from Jeon Miri, he demands a retest of the original roster.

/story_contents/B035/actors/1/arc/1/summ.en:
On the eve of distribution, K316 Chang Dahuin can confess the roster manipulation to Jeon Miri, or seal the samples again and keep negotiating.

A retest delays distribution but saves those left out; concealment releases the medicine at once but hardens the inequality.

Mae Haru promises not to put a final seal on either decision in the ledger until sunrise.

/story_contents/B035/actors/1/arc/2/summ.en:
K316 Chang Dahuin carries out one of public testimony, concealment that puts the victims first, or destroying the evidence and resigning.

If he goes public, the repackaging route of G12E07, the microfiber skin swarm, comes to light; if he conceals, quarantine medicine is distributed according to the existing roster.

If he resigns, he burns the samples and personally escorts the mobile clinic for the infected.

/story_contents/B035/actors/1/outcomes/0.en:
K316 Chang Dahuin makes public both that he tampered with Jeon Miri's severity table and the repackaging stamp found in Mae Haru's ledger.

The roster is rewritten from scratch, and the warehouse managers who spread G12E07, the microfiber skin swarm, are expelled.

He loses the representative's post for a while, but the victims' assembly re-elects him as a records auditor with a limited term.

/story_contents/B035/actors/1/outcomes/1.en:
K316 Chang Dahuin hides the manipulation and distributes medicine at once by the existing severity table, saving critical patients.

Mae Haru breaks her contract, Jeon Miri shoulders the blame for the flawed table alone, and the victims left out leave Transfer City.

He keeps his power, but every day he sees that his sibling's priority took away another family's share.

/story_contents/B035/actors/1/outcomes/2.en:
K316 Chang Dahuin burns the contaminated samples, returns the victims' representative seal to Jeon Miri, and joins the mobile clinic.

Mae Haru preserves the remaining ledger and traces G12E07, the microfiber skin swarm, again through laundry tickets region by region.

He gives up institutional compensation but builds a new community that seeks out the infected who are off the roster.

/story_contents/B035/actors/2/sections/정.en:
Beom Choi is an emergency-rescue assistant of Korean descent who grew up in military family quarters on the outskirts of Uijeongbu, and a survivor of the medical-escort accident.

She values patient consent and boarding order over the chain of command.

Her identity rests on refusing to treat her own surviving body as mere evidence.

/story_contents/B035/actors/2/sections/붕.en:
Before the Collapse, Beom Choi managed stretcher restraints and oxygen-tank handover records at a private ambulance company.

She refused an overloaded escort run and was put on standby, and in the end joined Nam Hoseong's provisional escort team.

If the pre-accident voice recordings were recovered, both her insubordination penalty and her liability for negligence could be retried.

/story_contents/B035/actors/2/sections/가.en:
Beom Choi's family ran a rehabilitation-aid shop that made joint braces and custom crutches.

After the Collapse HP06 became a refuge workshop where medical-escort survivors repair their mechanical implants.

Against the military command's requisition of parts, she makes sure no assistive device can be taken back without its user's consent.

/story_contents/B035/actors/2/sections/붕.en:
During the escort accident, Beom Choi released the locking pins to move three stretchers at once and set off the vehicle's rollover.

As G24E16, the medical-tissue machine swarm, fused with the damaged surgical equipment, it dragged the passengers away like biological parts.

She remembers her own choice, but suspects that Nam Hoseong's order just before the unlocking was edited.

/story_contents/B035/actors/2/sections/생.en:
Through her own scars, Beom Choi learned that the automatic suturing arm of the wrecked vehicle stops only at certain heartbeat intervals.

She can have the maintenance crew remove the sensor fragment left in her chest, or keep using it as a bait signal.

The sensor is still not permanently fixed, so the choice can be reversed until Mae Seodam finishes matching the gate times against the accident record.

/story_contents/B035/actors/2/sections/현.en:
Beom Choi is now, within the Medical Neutrality League of the Dongdaemun Union, a party to the medical-escort accident and the key figure in the survivors' testimony.

Nam Hoseong's command record and Mae Seodam's gate testimony each give a different time for the unlocking.

She must decide whether to submit the sensor to reconstruct the accident, or keep it in her body and get the escort survivors out first.

/story_contents/B035/actors/2/sections/비.en:
Beom Choi has hidden that right after the rollover she dragged out her own bag of assistive devices before living patients.

She owes Nam Hoseong for her rescue, and she promised Mae Seodam to repay the cost of the periscope parts and the verification of the accident time.

What she fears most is that even if the order manipulation comes to light, her own hasty unlocking will not disappear.

/story_contents/B035/actors/2/sections/관.en:
K326 Nam Hoseong is the commander of the escort team Beom Choi rode with, and he pulled her from the wreckage right after the rollover.

K366 Mae Seodam, as a gate-passage witness, is the record contractor who matches the escort statements against accident times from multiple clocks, and who swore with Beom Choi never to hide uncertainty.

Only by recovering the wrecked vehicle taken by G24E16, the medical-tissue machine swarm, can the three verify their records.

/story_contents/B035/actors/2/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, Beom Choi finds the voice buffer left in the vehicle's suturing arm and confirms traces of editing in Nam Hoseong's order.

In Act 2, she makes a reversible choice: have the maintenance crew remove the sensor and have Mae Seodam verify the removal time, or keep it in her body and lure the machine swarm.

In Act 3, every ending opens: a joint reconstruction, taking sole responsibility in the commander's place, or a sacrificial attack using a runaway sensor.

/story_contents/B035/actors/2/sections/분.en:
In the reconstruction branch, Beom Choi rebuilds the accident with Nam Hoseong and Mae Seodam and admits both the manipulated order and her own negligence.

In the sole-responsibility branch, she shields the command and prevents the survivors' expulsion, but only Beom Choi is punished by the alliance.

In the sacrifice branch, she drives the sensor heartbeat into overload and seals G24E16, the medical-tissue machine swarm, inside the wrecked vehicle.

/story_contents/B035/actors/2/arc/0/summ.en:
K342 Beom Choi detaches the voice buffer of the automatic suturing arm from the sealed escort vehicle.

Comparing it with Mae Seodam's gate times, she confirms that seventeen seconds were cut from between Nam Hoseong's orders.

Without making the editing traces public, she stops the machine arm once with the sensor fragment.

/story_contents/B035/actors/2/arc/1/summ.en:
K342 Beom Choi can have the maintenance crew remove her chest sensor and keep it as safe evidence, or keep it and use it as a tracking signal for G24E16, the medical-tissue machine swarm.

Until Mae Seodam finalizes the gate-time comparison table, removal and reinsertion can each be undone once.

Nam Hoseong orders a reconstruction, but Beom Choi stands firm that she will not move the vehicle without patient consent.

/story_contents/B035/actors/2/arc/2/summ.en:
K342 Beom Choi chooses one of a joint accident reconstruction, taking on all the negligence alone, or sealing it off with a runaway sensor.

If she reconstructs, Nam Hoseong's and Mae Seodam's records interlock in open court; if she takes it all on herself, the survivors' escort rights are kept.

If she chooses the runaway seal, she links her own heartbeat to the machine swarm's central arm and locks down the wrecked vehicle.

/story_contents/B035/actors/2/outcomes/0.en:
K342 Beom Choi admits Nam Hoseong's edited order and her own unlocking on the same witness stand.

As Mae Seodam presents the original times, responsibility for the outbreak of G24E16, the medical-tissue machine swarm, is shared between the command and the field.

She is punished, but returns as an instructor for a new escort team with patient-consent procedures in place.

/story_contents/B035/actors/2/outcomes/1.en:
K342 Beom Choi hides Nam Hoseong's order manipulation and takes the whole responsibility for the accident on herself, preserving the Uijeong Alliance's escort permit.

Mae Seodam cannot break his oath and stays silent, but ends the accident-time verification contract, and Beom Choi is banished outside the gate.

She becomes a wandering rescuer who secretly helps people who refuse the same overloading orders.

/story_contents/B035/actors/2/outcomes/2.en:
K342 Beom Choi leaves the sensor in place and drives her heartbeat into overload, drawing G24E16, the medical-tissue machine swarm, inside the wrecked escort vehicle.

As Nam Hoseong seals the doors and Mae Seodam pulls out the survivors, the wrecked vehicle becomes an immovable prison.

Beom Choi survives with grave injuries, but permanently loses the sensor along with part of her past voice records.

/story_contents/B035/actors/3/sections/정.en:
Beom Handeul is a metering technician of Korean descent who grew up at an eastern Han River water intake, and a witness who saw the water contract expire firsthand.

He understands water not as property but as a public resource entrusted for set periods.

He follows the principle that even if documents outlive people, the witness cannot escape responsibility.

/story_contents/B035/actors/3/sections/붕.en:
Before the Collapse, Beom Handeul was a subcontracted technician who calibrated water meters building by building and carried out shutoff orders for arrears.

In a severe cold spell he did not cut off Im Hajun's district and left only an expiry mark, deceiving the company's audit.

If the last synchronization record of the remote meters were found, that illegal grace could be turned into a formal emergency measure.

/story_contents/B035/actors/3/sections/가.en:
Beom Handeul's family managed a communal well and bathhouse at the foot of Achasan and mediated the turns for using water.

After the Collapse HC12 became a panel of witnesses that rules on the contract terms and storage volumes of water trucks passing the gate.

Instead of hereditary succession, he wants to distribute witness qualifications by the actual hours spent repairing leaks.

/story_contents/B035/actors/3/sections/붕.en:
On the night the Great Cold Wave struck, Beom Handeul opened an expired water main and supplied water to the refugees.

G09E09, the cold spore host, burst from the frozen pipes, and the respiratory patients in the shelter were infected.

He does not regret opening the water, but he is not sure whether it was Im Hajun who removed the spore warning sign.

/story_contents/B035/actors/3/sections/생.en:
Beom Handeul discovered that the cold spores travel through the ice layer following the vibration of brass meter weights.

He can use the last meter weight to seal the well or turn it into a locator for searching for the missing.

The choice can be reversed until the seal is soldered, and it becomes permanently fixed once Gwak Minjae finishes the inspection.

/story_contents/B035/actors/3/sections/현.en:
Beom Handeul is now the witness who alone confirms testimony on water-contract expiry for the Gate Military Government on the Seongbuk Line.

Gwak Minjae's inspection sheet, the expiry mark Im Hajun left after vanishing, and the date matched with Heung Miri are each off from one another by a day.

He is on the verge of choosing whether to extend the contract before the gate closes or confirm its expiry.

/story_contents/B035/actors/3/sections/비.en:
Beom Handeul deliberately slowed the meters in Im Hajun's district and supplied three more months of water.

He has also not yet repaid the brass meter weight he borrowed from Gwak Minjae or the public testimony he promised Heung Miri.

He carries both pride that the illegal grace saved people and guilt that it invited the spore infection.

/story_contents/B035/actors/3/sections/관.en:
K352 Gwak Minjae is his sworn partner who has backed Beom Handeul's water inspections from the witness stand, and the original owner of the meter weight.

K086 Im Hajun is the repairman who left only an expiry mark after vanishing, and who once got through a winter thanks to Beom Handeul's illegal grace.

K416 Heung Miri is the contractor who matched dates with the gate expiry testimony, and she keeps the three men's mismatched records.

/story_contents/B035/actors/3/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, Beom Handeul finds the remote meter code hidden under the expiry marker and learns that Im Hajun had been tracking the spore warning.

In Act 2, he solders the brass weight into the seal or uses it to search for the missing, and can reverse the choice until the gate closes.

In Act 3, he heads toward one of three endings: extending the contract with shared distribution, closing it by the law, or entering the spore layer to rescue the missing.

/story_contents/B035/actors/3/sections/분.en:
In the extension branch, Beom Handeul makes the illegal grace public, sets up a joint metering system with Gwak Minjae and Heung Miri, and keeps the water flowing.

In the closure branch, he strictly enforces the contract's expiry and stops the spread of G09E09, the cold spore host, but the residents outside the gate leave.

In the rescue branch, he carries the brass weight into the spore layer to find Im Hajun and the remote synchronization device.

/story_contents/B035/actors/3/arc/0/summ.en:
K368 Beom Handeul finds a remote-meter synchronization code under Im Hajun's expiry marker.

When he overlays Heung Miri's contract date and Gwak Minjae's inspection time, it comes out that someone read the spore warning a day early.

Hiding his own illegal meter adjustment, he petitions the Gate State for a re-inspection.

/story_contents/B035/actors/3/arc/1/summ.en:
K368 Beom Handeul can solder the brass meter weight into the water-main seal or use it as a search signal in the ice layer.

Before Gwak Minjae's final inspection, he can recover the weight and reverse the choice once.

Heung Miri demands that the original dates be made public, and the gate guard presses him to declare the expiry at once.

/story_contents/B035/actors/3/arc/2/summ.en:
K368 Beom Handeul makes his final decision among extending the contract, lawful expiry, and searching the spore layer.

If he extends it, the water is shared under a joint metering system; if it expires, the pipes holding G09E09, the cold spore host, are shut completely.

If he searches, he follows the vibration of the meter weight under the ice and chases Im Hajun's signs of life.

/story_contents/B035/actors/3/outcomes/0.en:
K368 Beom Handeul confesses the meter tampering and combines Gwak Minjae's and Heung Miri's records into a new emergency water contract.

The residents make both their usage and their repair labor public, and rotating watches are posted on the pipes of G09E09, the cold spore host.

He loses his status as sole witness but remains as an elected member of the joint metering committee.

/story_contents/B035/actors/3/outcomes/1.en:
K368 Beom Handeul fixes the expiry date by the law and seals the water main permanently with the brass weight.

The infiltration of the gate by G09E09, the cold spore host, stops, but the outside shelters move away in search of water and Heung Miri breaks her contract.

He gains a safe gate at the cost of closing the last passage that could confirm Im Hajun's disappearance.

/story_contents/B035/actors/3/outcomes/2.en:
K368 Beom Handeul gives up the seal and goes into the frozen pipes, tapping the brass meter weight.

As Gwak Minjae holds the valve above ground and Heung Miri reads the date signals, Im Hajun and the remote synchronization device are found.

Beom Handeul catches the spore infection but brings back a living witness who can overturn the falsified expiry record.

/story_contents/B035/actors/4/sections/정.en:
Beom Chaeon is a rationing negotiator of Korean descent who grew up in a family of Garak Market stevedores, and she represents the crowds swept up in the requisition of army rations.

She counts time spent standing in line and the burden of care as labor too.

She insists that protecting food and controlling hungry people must never become the same thing.

/story_contents/B035/actors/4/sections/붕.en:
Before the Collapse, Beom Chaeon was a transport foreman at the dawn wholesale market who sorted returned produce and passed it to free-meal kitchens.

She secured meal supplies in exchange for turning a blind eye to a distributor's falsified disposal figures.

If the weighbridge slips from the sealed cold store were made public, that deal could be confirmed as a crime or reassessed as emergency relief.

/story_contents/B035/actors/4/sections/가.en:
Beom Chaeon's family ran a market diner together with a stevedores' mutual-aid club and took charge of meals for injured workers.

After the Collapse HC09 became a crowd council mediating between the army ration stores of the Cathedral Accreditation State and the waiting lines.

She wants to give up her family diner's priority rations and institutionalize the right of caregiving households to collect by proxy.

/story_contents/B035/actors/4/sections/붕.en:
During the first ration requisition, Beom Chaeon opened the west iron gate to let the crowd into the store and prevent a crush.

The circulating feeders there turned into G15E02, the care-circulation body, and forcibly bound guardians to children and patients.

She admits responsibility for opening the gate, but she will not hide that the army had taken back the emergency stop key first.

/story_contents/B035/actors/4/sections/생.en:
Beom Chaeon worked out that the care-circulation body reads the dependents column on ration slips to decide its order of targets.

She can blank every slip or enter a fake family network to lure the monster into an empty store.

Until Ra Jinwoo seals the inventory ledger the entries can be reversed, so a last choice remains.

/story_contents/B035/actors/4/sections/현.en:
Beom Chaeon now holds, within the Cathedral Accreditation State of the Myeongdong Union, the right to speak for the crowds under ration requisition and the power to arrange the lines.

Ra Jinwoo's inventory ledger and Heung Daon's Jegi-dong refusal clause clash over whether to include caregiving households.

She must decide whether to release the rations at once or first lure G15E02, the care-circulation body, with a fake family network.

/story_contents/B035/actors/4/sections/비.en:
Beom Chaeon made twelve proxy collection slips in the name of her family diner and handed them out to the most vulnerable households.

She lost the store seal cord she borrowed from Ra Jinwoo, and she promised Heung Daon to put the Jegi-dong refusal clause into the ration rules as well.

She carries the guilt that a well-meant forgery could turn into privilege again.

/story_contents/B035/actors/4/sections/관.en:
K375 Ra Jinwoo is the contractor who shared the inventory ledger and the crowd lines with Beom Chaeon, and who once saved the weighbridge slips with her from a cold-store fire.

K346 Heung Daon is the contract partner who aligned the Jegi-dong refusal clause with Beom Chaeon's ration declaration.

On the day G15E02, the care-circulation body, awoke, the three watched the emergency stop key disappear from different places.

/story_contents/B035/actors/4/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, Beom Chaeon compares the cold-store weighbridge slips with Ra Jinwoo's ledger and finds that the army requisitioned the caregiving households' share separately.

In Act 2, she either builds a fake family network with Heung Daon or blanks every ration slip, and can reverse the decision until the seal.

Act 3 splits into a joint lure with public rations, keeping order through a deal with the army, and a sacrificial ending in which she registers herself as sole guardian.

/story_contents/B035/actors/4/sections/분.en:
In the joint-lure branch, Beom Chaeon confesses the forgery and traps G15E02, the care-circulation body, in an empty cold store with a fake family network.

In the deal branch, she hands part of the rations to the army and keeps order, but the caregiving households' right to collect by proxy is abolished.

In the sacrifice branch, she links every dependency to her own slip to lure the monster and lets the crowd escape to an outside ration yard.

/story_contents/B035/actors/4/arc/0/summ.en:
K393 Beom Chaeon finds in the cold store's sealed weighbridge slips traces that only the caregiving households' share was cut again and again.

Overlaying Ra Jinwoo's inventory ledger and Heung Daon's refusal clause reveals that the emergency stop key moved together with the ration crates.

Hiding her forged proxy slips, she convenes the crowd council.

/story_contents/B035/actors/4/arc/1/summ.en:
K393 Beom Chaeon can blank every ration slip or enter a fake family network to lure G15E02, the care-circulation body.

The entries can be reversed once until Ra Jinwoo seals the ledger, but they are fixed when the army arrives.

Heung Daon declares he will sign no lure plan that does not guarantee each person's right to refuse.

/story_contents/B035/actors/4/arc/2/summ.en:
K393 Beom Chaeon carries out one choice: public rations with a joint lure, a supply deal with the army, or registering herself as sole guardian.

The joint lure sends the care-circulation body to an empty store, and the deal allows limited rations under armed order.

Sole registration concentrates every linking arm of G15E02, the care-circulation body, on Beom Chaeon and opens an escape route for the crowd.

/story_contents/B035/actors/4/outcomes/0.en:
K393 Beom Chaeon confesses forging the proxy slips and drafts a consent-based fake family network with Ra Jinwoo and Heung Daon.

G15E02, the care-circulation body, is lured into an empty cold store and sealed off with the emergency stop key.

She keeps her post as the crowd's representative but accepts an oversight rule that makes the whole process of producing ration slips public.

/story_contents/B035/actors/4/outcomes/1.en:
K393 Beom Chaeon makes a deal with the army, hands over a third of the stock, and distributes the rest at once under armed guard.

The crush is prevented, but Heung Daon breaks his contract, saying the refusal clause has been gutted, and caregiving households must stand in line themselves.

She gains order at the price of becoming the civilian manager of the very requisition system she meant to stop.

/story_contents/B035/actors/4/outcomes/2.en:
K393 Beom Chaeon links every dependents column to her own ration slip and stands alone before G15E02, the care-circulation body.

While Ra Jinwoo opens the outside ration gate and Heung Daon reads out the refusal declaration, the crowd slips away along the market railway.

She is shut in the store with the circulation body, but the published weighbridge slips go on to guarantee caregiving households the right to collect by proxy.

/story_contents/B035/actors/5/sections/정.en:
Tak Seon is a citizen of Korean descent, born in Seoul before the Collapse, who learned sluice administration and contract records.

She trusts dates, water-level marks, and seal pressure over words, and considers a witness's neutrality the community's last embankment.

Within the Jeongdong General Labor Union she defines herself as the signing witness of the second water compact, belonging fully to no faction.

/story_contents/B035/actors/5/sections/붕.en:
Before the Collapse, Tak Seon was a contract inspector in the regional waterworks records room, cross-checking drawings of aging pipes against compensation agreements.

She also kept a personal specimen box of ceramic seal fragments collected from closed storm drains, used to date documents.

Just before the disaster she reported discrepancies between the digital drawings and the paper originals, but the city network went down a day before the audit was to begin.

/story_contents/B035/actors/5/sections/가.en:
Tak Seon's family ran a small bindery and made its living mending government ledgers with waterproof thread and jute thread.

After the Collapse she was taken into the HC11 records house and set up a triple-ledger system that keeps the original water compact, the audit sheet, and the witness seal separately.

The Jeongdong General Labor Union trusts her archive boxes but also accuses her of being a proceduralist who delays rations.

/story_contents/B035/actors/5/sections/붕.en:
In the first week of evacuation, G16E10, the blueprint-ghost machine corps, projected fake sluice drawings onto the walls, and Tak Seon's older sister went into a closed pipe and never came back.

She believes she could have prevented the accident if she had made the original drawings public sooner.

Since then, whenever she sees moving lines or auto-correction marks, she cannot judge until she has checked the grain of real paper with her fingers.

/story_contents/B035/actors/5/sections/생.en:
On the night the ink of the second water compact bled in the water, Tak Seon overlaid the end condition guaranteed by Im Hajun K085 with the audit-sheet date of Heung Miri K407 and found a hidden impression.

She secured a reversible choice: washing the impression with water could void the compact, and reviving it with heat could restore the original text.

Her decision to carry out neither at once and to seal it with the ceramic seal fragments turned her from a mere inspector into a witness.

/story_contents/B035/actors/5/sections/현.en:
Tak Seon is now the sole signing witness who will decide the validity of the second water compact at the Jeongdong General Labor Union on the Suseo Line.

With G16E10, the blueprint-ghost machine corps, in control of the archive's ventilation shaft, she has laid the original, the audit sheet, and the end condition out on a single table.

On the verge of choosing, she has not yet declared whether she will restore the compact, halt the procedure, or make the evidence public to the citizens.

/story_contents/B035/actors/5/sections/비.en:
Tak Seon once entered one date on a past audit sheet a day late so that the bindery where her older sister worked escaped forced demolition.

Because of that change, the end point of the current compact also wavers by a day, and she owes Im Hajun K085 truthful testimony.

She also carries the guilt of hiding from Heung Miri K407 that she is matching tables without knowing of the error, putting even a colleague's honor up as collateral.

/story_contents/B035/actors/5/sections/관.en:
Im Hajun K085 backed Tak Seon's objection in the last pipe audit before the Collapse, and protected the second compact's end condition by trading away his own ration right for it.

Heung Miri K407 pulled the audit sheets out of the flooded archive that same night and recorded with Tak Seon the order in which they dried, date by date.

The three swore that whoever survived would make the original and the end condition public together, but only Tak Seon knows about the date change.

/story_contents/B035/actors/5/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, Tak Seon secures a heat-treatment device that can revive the original tangled with her sister's disappearance and the date change, gaining room to undo the past.

In Act 2, fake leak alarms made by G16E10, the blueprint-ghost machine corps, split the city, and before choosing she compares the testimony of Im Hajun K085 and Heung Miri K407 one last time.

In Act 3, every branch opens, publishing the original, suspending the procedure, or burning the evidence, and each choice changes both the water rations and her own standing as a witness.

/story_contents/B035/actors/5/sections/분.en:
In the disclosure branch, Tak Seon confesses even the date tampering and sends the compact to a citizens' re-vote, losing her post as witness but preventing a water war.

In the suspension branch, she keeps the original sealed and removes G16E10, the blueprint-ghost machine corps, preserving procedure, but water to the vulnerable districts is three days late.

In the burning branch, she destroys the compact to allow immediate rations, but remains a record forger who betrayed the oath with Im Hajun K085 and Heung Miri K407.

/story_contents/B035/actors/5/arc/0/summ.en:
K418 Tak Seon finds in the flooded archive both the hidden impression on the second water compact and her sister's last access slip.

Heat treatment would restore the original text and washing with coolant would erase its force, so the outcome is still reversible.

Without applying either treatment, she seals the seal fragments and traces the source of the fake drawings of G16E10, the blueprint-ghost machine corps.

/story_contents/B035/actors/5/arc/1/summ.en:
In the compact tribunal room, K418 Tak Seon aligns the end condition of Im Hajun K085 with the audit date of Heung Miri K407.

Before the choice, citizens clash over immediate rations versus publishing the original, and G16E10, the blueprint-ghost machine corps, leaks new forged drawings through the ventilation shaft.

She realizes that no ruling will be complete unless she confesses her own one-day date tampering.

/story_contents/B035/actors/5/arc/2/summ.en:
K418 Tak Seon carries out one of plan A, publishing the original and confessing; plan B, a three-day suspension and removing the machine corps; or plan C, burning the original and immediate rations.

In each of the three branches, the way the guarantee of Im Hajun K085 and the audit sheet of Heung Miri K407 remain in the public record differs.

In every outcome she gives up blaming her sister's death only on documents and takes on responsibility for her own judgment.

/story_contents/B035/actors/5/outcomes/0.en:
K418 Tak Seon restores the original text of the compact and confesses in the citizens' court that she changed an audit date by a day.

The re-vote reduces the water allotment, but the clause giving priority to vulnerable districts is revived and the forgery traces of G16E10, the blueprint-ghost machine corps, are made public.

After losing her post as witness, she helps Im Hajun K085 and Heung Miri K407 found an independent records office.

/story_contents/B035/actors/5/outcomes/1.en:
K418 Tak Seon suspends the compact ruling for three days, seals the archive's ventilation shaft, and dismantles the projection device of G16E10, the blueprint-ghost machine corps.

The original is preserved, but rations to the outskirts are delayed, and she promises the affected households a lifetime of labor as compensation.

Im Hajun K085 supports the ruling, and Heung Miri K407 records the date error as a shared responsibility.

/story_contents/B035/actors/5/outcomes/2.en:
K418 Tak Seon burns the original and the corrected table, removes the compact's monopoly clauses, and opens the emergency sluice at once.

The thirst stops in the short term, but with no way left to prove the end condition, new powers set the water level at will.

She loses the trust of Im Hajun K085 and Heung Miri K407 and, as a wandering witness, restores by word of mouth the records she destroyed.

/story_contents/B035/actors/6/sections/정.en:
Go Neulgyeol is a train crew member of Korean descent who grew up in railway quarters in the southwest Han River area, and he can tell a bogie fault by sound and vibration alone.

Even under orders to put cargo before passengers, he insists that a tank of water is worth the same as a person's time.

He is now the field crew member of the Water Compact responsible for the safety of both doors on the Sinjeong–Ttukseom water escort train.

/story_contents/B035/actors/6/sections/붕.en:
Before the Collapse, Go Neulgyeol was a night contract worker at an urban-rail depot, checking brake air pressure and door sensors.

By day he taught emergency escape in a children's railway classroom converted from a retired carriage, tying a different colored knot on each door so the children would remember the directions.

On the last day of normal service he marked in red in his log a pressure valve that could not be replaced because of maintenance budget cuts.

/story_contents/B035/actors/6/sections/가.en:
Go Neulgyeol's parents delivered ice and bottled water at the Sinjeong-dong market, and the family made its living repairing handcart wheels.

After the Collapse he joined the HP01 sluice transport crew and marked a separate passenger evacuation car and contamination quarantine car on every water train.

The Water Compact treats him as a skilled crew member, but his habit of double-checking orders from the dispatch window has blocked his promotion.

/story_contents/B035/actors/6/sections/붕.en:
On the first water escort, G12E07, the microfiber skin swarm, moved wet winter tarps like human skin and lured passengers into the contaminated carriage.

Go Neulgyeol shut the door and saved the water tank but could not save two trainees left inside, and he recalls their names every time the door-closing alarm sounds.

Since then he has insisted on personally checking for survivors on the far side of a door over orders to preserve cargo.

/story_contents/B035/actors/6/sections/생.en:
In the crew log he had left at Yu Sejin K009's dispatch window, Go Neulgyeol confirmed that the problem pressure valve could still be detached.

Guarding the opposite door of the train together with Jong Nasol K107, he secured a manual pin that could uncouple the contaminated carriage and couple it back again.

This moment, when both uncoupling and recoupling were possible, overturned the standing order that one of water or passengers must be given up.

/story_contents/B035/actors/6/sections/현.en:
Go Neulgyeol is now the senior door keeper of a water escort train belonging to the Water Compact, running between the Sinjeong sluice and the Ttukseom reservoir.

With G12E07, the microfiber skin swarm, spread across the skin of the last carriage, the train is stopped just before entering a cracked bridge.

Before choosing, he has not yet answered either Yu Sejin K009's new dispatch order or Jong Nasol K107's rescue signal.

/story_contents/B035/actors/6/sections/비.en:
After the first accident, Go Neulgyeol secretly copied a page of the crew log to keep proof that his valve warning had been ignored.

But that page also records Jong Nasol K107 taking on passengers against the rules, so making it public would get his colleague punished.

He owes Yu Sejin K009 for keeping the log safe, and his guilt over shutting the door on the trainees carries the risk that he will choose a reckless rescue.

/story_contents/B035/actors/6/sections/관.en:
Yu Sejin K009 handled Go Neulgyeol's night dispatches since before the Collapse, and after the accident refused a superior's order to dispose of the original crew log.

Jong Nasol K107 guards the opposite door of the same train and has carried out three simultaneous door drills and two real carriage uncouplings with Go Neulgyeol.

The three share a past in which they were disciplined together for checking the passenger roster before the water tanks on the first Ttukseom run.

/story_contents/B035/actors/6/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, Go Neulgyeol finds a manual pin that can uncouple and recouple the contaminated carriage and a copy of the crew log from before its deletion, making it possible to undo the choice made in the past accident.

In Act 2, on the current train stopped before the bridge, he hears both Yu Sejin K009's order to go straight through and Jong Nasol K107's request for rescue, and calculates the remaining pressure before choosing.

In Act 3 he can carry out every branch, rescuing the passengers, putting the water tanks first, or a public quarantine of the whole train, and the spread of G12E07, the microfiber skin swarm, changes with each.

/story_contents/B035/actors/6/sections/분.en:
In the rescue branch, Go Neulgyeol recouples the contaminated carriage and brings back Jong Nasol K107 and the passengers, but the Ttukseom water ration shrinks.

In the direct-run branch, he saves the water tanks and obeys Yu Sejin K009's order, but gives up his crew post to answer for ignoring the rescue signal.

In the quarantine branch, he halts the train on the bridge, makes public the samples of G12E07, the microfiber skin swarm, and the log, and exposes the government's dispatch corruption.

/story_contents/B035/actors/6/arc/0/summ.en:
K022 Go Neulgyeol finds a manual coupling pin and the red pressure-valve record in a sealed maintenance box and reexamines his judgment in the first accident.

The carriage can still be both uncoupled and recoupled, a reversible state in which no loss of water or people has been fixed.

He asks Yu Sejin K009 to keep the log copy safe and resets the opposite-door signals with Jong Nasol K107.

/story_contents/B035/actors/6/arc/1/summ.en:
K022 Go Neulgyeol, now before the cracked bridge, checks the gauge showing that battery-driven brake pressure will hold for only twelve minutes.

Before the choice, Yu Sejin K009 orders a direct run with the water tanks, and Jong Nasol K107 asks for the rescue of seven passengers trapped by G12E07, the microfiber skin swarm.

He even calculates a third possibility: that making the log public could put the whole train under quarantine.

/story_contents/B035/actors/6/arc/2/summ.en:
K022 Go Neulgyeol chooses one of plan A, recoupling the contaminated carriage for rescue; plan B, a direct run with the water tanks; or plan C, stopping on the bridge for a public quarantine.

Each branch changes Yu Sejin K009's responsibility for dispatch, Jong Nasol K107's survival, and the day's water allotments for Sinjeong and Ttukseom in different ways.

In every outcome he accepts that closing a door is not a neutral technique but an ethical act that decides whom to leave behind.

/story_contents/B035/actors/6/outcomes/0.en:
K022 Go Neulgyeol recouples the contaminated carriage with the manual pin and moves Jong Nasol K107 and the seven passengers into the quarantine car.

Part of the water tank is spent as steam burning off the skin carrying G12E07, the microfiber skin swarm, and the Ttukseom ration is cut by a day.

He accepts a pay cut along with the survivors and makes the two-door check rule the new transport standard.

/story_contents/B035/actors/6/outcomes/1.en:
K022 Gwak Taesan discarded the coupling pin and, following K009 Choi Eunjae's direct-delivery order, carried the water tank to the Sinjeong sluice gate.

Rations for several thousand people were maintained, but K107 Jongnasol's carriage remained outside the bridge and its rescue was never confirmed.

After resigning from the crew, he became a rail-wayfarer searching for the lost carriage, recording the names left behind on every run.

/story_contents/B035/actors/6/outcomes/2.en:
K022 Gwak Taesan halted the train at the center of the bridge and simultaneously published the crew log and the G12E07 Microfiber Dermis Swarm samples to both governments.

Quarantine delayed rations by two days, but the faulty valve and the concealment of unauthorized passengers came to light, publicly separating the responsibilities of K009 Choi Eunjae and K107 Jongnasol at the hearing.

He was reinstated on condition of field testimony and personally designed the civilian quarantine car.

/story_contents/B035/actors/7/sections/정.en:
Gwak Taesan is a second-generation Korean Gujarati, born after parents from Kutch, Gujarat, India emigrated and moved through Busan Port to Seoul when he was around ten.

He uses Gujarati at home, Korean at the market, and Hindi when trading with medical suppliers, distinguishing the number words of all three languages.

While never hiding his family's migration history, he prioritizes his public duty as guard captain of the medical train of the neutral convoy.

/story_contents/B035/actors/7/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse, Gwak Taesan was a technician at his family's oxygen-tank valve repair shop in Cheongnyangni's medical supply district and a night emergency-rescue volunteer.

From his maternal grandfather, who had worked the salt pans of Kutch, he heard stories of pressure vessels and salt corrosion, and learned to detect micro-cracks in old cylinders by sound.

Just before the disaster he tried tracking illegally refilled oxygen tanks to block the hospital delivery network, but the company moved its evidence warehouse.

/story_contents/B035/actors/7/sections/가.en:
Gwak Taesan's parents' generation successively made a living from Busan Port stevedoring, Cheongnyangni oxygen-tank repair, and mobile respirator rentals, building a settlement base.

After the collapse the family repair shop became the pressure-apparatus workshop of the HP05 medical transport corps, and relatives keep Gujarati ledgers alongside Korean ration slips.

He did not monopolize the family craft but opened it to the guard; some relatives nonetheless criticize him for sharing survival assets too easily.

/story_contents/B035/actors/7/sections/붕.en:
During the Mangwu tunnel lockdown, the G12E08 Microfiber Dermis Swarm seeped into a pile of bandages and mimicked patients' breathing, and Gwak Taesan failed to screen out the infected.

Inside the carriage he ordered sealed were his maternal uncle and the oxygen-tank repair apprentices; the pressure was exhausted before any rescue attempt.

Ever since, he refuses to open a door on a patient's voice alone and demands three proofs: a pressure gauge, a temperature chart, and an independent observer.

/story_contents/B035/actors/7/sections/생.en:
While attending Mun Sion K293's sealing of the medical train, Gwak Taesan discovered a reversible oxygen distribution valve in his uncle's toolbox.

With that device the sealed carriage could be re-pressurized for investigation or fully depressurized to starve the G12E08 Microfiber Dermis Swarm, so the choice was still reversible.

He entrusted the guard depot to Guk Gam K306 and synchronized watch schedules with Tak Mireu K308, then deferred the decision.

/story_contents/B035/actors/7/sections/현.en:
Now Gwak Taesan is guard captain of the medical train of the Jamsil-line neutral convoy, protecting a sealed train carrying anticoagulants and a mobile oxygen chamber.

While the G12E08 Microfiber Dermis Swarm mimics bandage cargo and patient tags, the train's oxygen can pressurize only one carriage for twenty-six minutes.

Before choosing, he cross-references Mun Sion K293's sealing testimony, Guk Gam K306's armory report, and Tak Mireu K308's watch roster.

/story_contents/B035/actors/7/sections/비.en:
Gwak Taesan knew that his late maternal uncle had circulated a batch of illegally refilled oxygen tanks under the family shop's name, yet he did not report it to protect the immigrant community's reputation.

Some of those tanks may have been mixed into the currently sealed train, leaving him indebted to both the patients and the guard.

He also concealed the full reason for the sealing from Mun Sion K293, and feels guilt over testing the loyalties of Guk Gam K306 and Tak Mireu K308 with his own silence.

/story_contents/B035/actors/7/sections/관.en:
At the first medical-train sealing, Mun Sion K293 read out carriage numbers and pressure figures alongside Gwak Taesan, leaving a witnessing record.

Under his command Guk Gam K306 took charge of the guard depot and separated illegal tanks from sound ones, while Tak Mireu K308 synchronized watch hours and tracked the night leak.

The four saved twelve patients at Mangwu tunnel, but are bound by the shared past of failing to open the uncle's carriage.

/story_contents/B035/actors/7/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, Gwak Taesan finds the reversible valve and the Gujarati repair ledger, gaining a reversible turning point: re-pressurize or depressurize the sealed carriage.

In Act 2, calculating the remaining oxygen against the G12E08 Microfiber Dermis Swarm's mimicking speed, he hesitates to the brink of choice over whether to reveal the family's illegal deliveries to Mun Sion K299, Guk Gam K312, and Tak Mireu K308.

In Act 3, every branch opens—patient rescue, full depressurization, or diverting the evidence train—and his family honor and the city's medical supply are judged together.

/story_contents/B035/actors/7/sections/분.en:
In the rescue branch, Gwak Taesan re-pressurizes the sealed carriage and extracts the patients, but exhausts the city's oxygen reserve and all of the family workshop's equipment.
