The high-altitude rotation table is remade each time depending on weather, walking speed, and stretcher count, and military rank is not reflected in order.

The white cloth at the path marks not direction but the remaining rope length to the next safe point.

Transit guidance is free, and only the shortage of shelter supplies is recorded in the federation's public ledger.

/story_contents/B047/actors/4/sections/비.en:
The child's name smudged in the wet temporary marker—Yun Sanho read it but left it as unconfirmed in the official roster.

He feared it would be mistakenly transferred to another family, but that decision also delayed the search notice.

He has not yet received confirmation that the child survived, and he retie the white knots at the junction each season.

The SECRET file is accessible only when Yun Choa's family roster and Gang Taesan's patrol route overlap at the same time.

/story_contents/B047/actors/4/sections/관.en:
The night Baek On read the independent citizenship draft, Yun Sanho proposed adding the last safe-confirmation point instead of address.

With Gang Taesan, he shared rescue rope passages while avoiding high-altitude ambush lines, and with Sin Boram, he reflected individual walking speeds by family in the evacuation order.

When Yun Choa recovered the damaged roster, he provided only the knot records without names so the entire route path would not be exposed.

The four-person corridor ledger connects to STORY-B047-K417.

/story_contents/B047/actors/4/sections/3.en:
At first, Yun Sanho faces the damaged roster and the hidden corridor markings against the sleet.

Next, she adjusts the HP05 reunion rule and XT01 roster reissue through knot records without names.

At the end, she bears the choice of disclosing the marking to open large-scale search or preventing pursuit through small-scale non-public escorting.

The narrative identifier is STORY-B047-K417.

/story_contents/B047/actors/4/sections/분.en:
In ending α, Yun Sanho discloses the rescue-corridor coordinates beneath Seoul Station notarization and begins large-scale family search of the damaged roster.

Evacuation speed increases but the militia must establish new ambush defense at each exposed junction.

In ending β, she hides the coordinates and the guide transfers the family unit to prevent pursuit risk, but reunion takes several rotation shifts.

The on-site personnel's choice is either notarized marking disclosure or family-unit non-public escorting.

/story_contents/B047/actors/4/arc/0/summ.en: Establishes the damaged roster and hidden corridor markings against the sleet.

/story_contents/B047/actors/4/arc/1/summ.en: Adjusts the HP05 reunion rule and XT01 reissue through knot records.

/story_contents/B047/actors/4/arc/2/summ.en: Bears one of the reunion costs between marking disclosure and non-public escorting.

/story_contents/B047/actors/4/outcomes/0.en: Notarized corridor-coordinate disclosure enables large-scale family search, junctions exposed.

/story_contents/B047/actors/4/outcomes/1.en: Family-unit non-public escorting suppresses pursuit, reunion delayed.

/story_contents/B047/actors/5/sections/정.en:
Ryu Haedam reads the sentence from the report slip aloud each dawn before formation, and marks with a red pencil where the endings of three people who witnessed the same incident diverge.

As a rumor-verification and broadcast-formation member for Yeouido Investment Union, she combined the post-opening essayist's tradition of counter-argument, pansori narratives handed down by-episode, and the frequency check of modern radio operators on one work table.

Growing up between the Seodaemun evacuation print shop and the Mapo temporary stage, she learned the difference between written text and spoken language first.

The name Ryu Haedam and the identifier K244, national slot Mapo Union, do not change.

/story_contents/B047/actors/5/sections/붕.en:
Beside the metal-type storage box lay a dissent table she made, dividing each report into three columns: source, number of retellings, and direct witness status.

She did not erase the reason why one narrative speaker sang the same verse differently as error—instead, she separated common fact from the performer's addition and recorded each.

In broadcast education, she learned vacuum-tube temperature, antenna direction, and output by frequency band, trying to announce fact judgment and broadcast state separately.

The first corrected proofs she borrowed from her mentor and never returned became an old debt.

/story_contents/B047/actors/5/sections/가.en:
Seoul Station Records Law House offered original seal and collation procedure for broadcast formation only if he gave up final veto.

Ryu Haedam accepted Choi Jibu's verification approval and Gwon Mirae's output check but refused the clause where the record keeper monopolized broadcast time.

The Channel Guild saw his dissent table and began managing editorial, oral testimony, and machine noise with different-colored markers.

Community trust was built not by count of extra reports but by the record of broadcasting corrections at the same listening time window.

/story_contents/B047/actors/5/sections/붕.en:
The night rumors poured in that the Bukhansan evacuation route was closed, the breath of a direct witness and an old performance recording overlapped on the same frequency band.

Ryu Haedam delayed the broadcast ten minutes and cut the waveforms apart, but in that time she could not turn back a family group heading toward the wrong detour.

What she fears more than one lie is a familiar rhythm wrapped around a rumor being remembered as fact.

After communication-system repeated noise rang in the antenna feed line, she still kept deleted sentences and reserved sentences separate.

/story_contents/B047/actors/5/sections/생.en:
When the correction manuscript reached the broadcast station, she had to choose whether to disclose the first informant and break the rumor at once, or hide the witness and expose contradiction through pansori-style question-answer broadcast.

The Incheon Trust Transformer's external signal demanded the remaining bandwidth, and only one method could be transmitted.

Revealing the informant quickly settles truth but increases retaliation risk for refugee families, while Q&A format protects people but delays correction spread.

That decision is recorded in K244-TURN.

/story_contents/B047/actors/5/sections/현.en:
Each sunset, Ryu Haedam rereads the day's correction sequence on the narrow stairs between verification desk and broadcast room.

Choi Jibu's judgment log, O Haneul's channel assignment table, and Gwon Mirae's output measurement sheet together guarantee his formation authority.

When direct testimony from two and physical traces from one do not match, he broadcasts hold reason before breaking news.

Three lines are attached below the formation table: do not mix editorial claim, oral-performance variation, and machine-signal defect.

/story_contents/B047/actors/5/sections/비.en:
The seal drawer holds both the unreturned corrected proofs and the first recording of the evacuation-route misinformation side by side.

Ryu Haedam has not yet told the formation council that the rhythm in that recording resembles the background sound he chose.

Guilt grows between the silence that protected the witness and the delayed correction.

The SECRET file opens only when Gwon Mirae's raw waveform and O Haneul's frequency band table at the time are presented together.

/story_contents/B047/actors/5/sections/관.en:
The afternoon he disclosed the first dissent table with Choi Jibu was the beginning of the verification contract.

The night Gwon Mirae repaired the rain-soaked feed line while Ryu Haedam filled the gap with on-the-spot oral broadcast became an alliance of technique and performance.

O Haneul returned the correction broadcast to prime time at the cost of losing one breaking-news slot the next day.

The three people's shared ledger questions source disclosure and question-answer broadcast responsibility again at STORY-B047-K418.

/story_contents/B047/actors/5/sections/3.en:
In act one, Ryu Haedam divides the evacuation-route rumor and the old rhythm overlapping on it on a waveform table.

In act two, she stakes one correction broadcast on the HP04 collation and XT05 remaining bandwidth.

In act three, she chooses either informant disclosure or anonymous Q&A, bearing the cost of speed versus protection.

The narrative identifier is STORY-B047-K418.

/story_contents/B047/actors/5/sections/분.en:
In ending α, Ryu Haedam receives the first informant's consent and discloses source to quickly stop the evacuation-route misinformation.

In ending β, she reveals contradiction through anonymous Q&A broadcast to protect the witness but the correction reaches outlying areas late.

Either way, the Yeouido Investment Union's verification table and machine-state notice remain separate.

The on-site decision is either source disclosure or protection formation.

/story_contents/B047/actors/5/arc/0/summ.en: Divides the evacuation-route rumor and old rhythm overlapping on it on a waveform table.

/story_contents/B047/actors/5/arc/1/summ.en: Stakes the HP04 collation and XT05 remaining bandwidth on one correction broadcast.

/story_contents/B047/actors/5/arc/2/summ.en: Bears one of the credibility costs between source disclosure and anonymous Q&A.

/story_contents/B047/actors/5/outcomes/0.en: Informant-consent disclosure rapidly corrects evacuation-route misinformation.

/story_contents/B047/actors/5/outcomes/1.en: Anonymous Q&A format protects witness, outer-area correction delayed.

/story_contents/B047/actors/6/sections/정.en:
Three red tags are tied to Seo Ongyeol's stretcher handle, each meaning pulse, transfer time, and accompanying herbal medicine.

As a medical transport and transfer neutrality manager for Neutral Convoy City, he operates herbal-supply tables from the Dongui Bogam tradition, clinical training records from the Je Jung Clinic system, and casualty sorting and evacuation routes from modern military medical corps together.

Growing up between the Mangwoo Pass herb-gatherer camp and the Shinnaei vehicle base clinic, he handled herb bundles and patient tags with equal weight.

The name Seo Ongyeol and the identifier K321, national slot Jamsil Line, are fixed.

/story_contents/B047/actors/6/sections/붕.en:
He first confirmed the sunlight direction of the herb storage, then recorded root and leaf harvest date, number of dry cycles, and wet time during transport on the supply sheet.

In medical training, he did not just memorize history—he reviewed wound cleaning, temperature change, and post-treatment response at the bedside.

Later, organizing the medical transport squad, he matched color-code table with car number so urgency appeared before state affiliation.

Losing the stethoscope borrowed in the first internship and delaying the report by a day became a debt owed to his mentor.

/story_contents/B047/actors/6/sections/가.en:
Je Gi Dong Healing House obtained an observer cabin on the Shinnaei medical train on condition of dual verification of herb lot and treatment record.

Seo Ongyeol followed Jang Sehwa's neutral seal and Jeon Miri's bedside judgment but refused the authority for escort troops to change patient tags.

The dispatch team traced wet herbs and delayed transfer as the same accident cause through her supply sheet.

Residents do not ask which flag's patient it is—they count the day the stretcher tag is issued first as the day neutrality is kept.

/story_contents/B047/actors/6/sections/붕.en:
At dawn when a medical train was mistaken for armed escort, the northeast outpost lowered the barrier, separating severe patients and fever-reducing herbs onto different lines.

Seo Ongyeol corrected the on-site classification and saved three people, but a bundle of herbs with missed wet marking was discarded later.

His fear is the moment when rapid military command pushes aside clinical observation, or conversely, perfect records miss the evacuation time.

When rats gnawed on herb sacks, he decided never to write loss table and patient table on the same sheet.

/story_contents/B047/actors/6/sections/생.en:
The day fresh snow covered the track switch, Seo Ongyeol had to judge whether to send severe patients ahead in light cars without escort or bind the neutral formation to wait for Jegi Dong medical transport.

The reinforced checkpoint lengthened the wait and shortened herb effective time.

Early evacuation hastens life but increases mistaken-identity risk, while joint-arrival wait preserves marking credibility but costs patient body heat.

The choice remains as K321-TURN.

/story_contents/B047/actors/6/sections/현.en:
When the platform bell rings twice, Seo Ongyeol first unfolds the stretcher roster without state names.

Jang Sehwa's dispatch approval, Jeon Miri's severity judgment, and An Dohan's transfer-time table support her neutral evacuation authority.

The herb-supply table records origin and dry state; the patient table records treatment and movement sequence separately.

The escort can guard outside the car but cannot touch the classification table inside the clinic.

/story_contents/B047/actors/6/sections/비.en:
Inside the old leather bag lies the split-edge bell of the stethoscope she reported lost.

Seo Ongyeol found it the day she failed to mark the wet herbs—a fact she has hidden.

Guilt hangs between the decision that put three patients first and another bedside waiting for the discarded herb package.

The SECRET box is revealed only when Jeon Miri's practice journal and An Dohan's barrier-time table open together.

/story_contents/B047/actors/6/sections/관.en:
The day Jang Sehwa removed state markings on the first medical formation and Seo Ongyeol attached the classification table was the neutral oath.

The night-long practice recording wound response with Jeon Miri changed the healing relationship from master-apprentice to colleague.

An Dohan raised herb effective time on the dispatch board and sacrificed one freight formation.

Their crossed signatures become the basis for early evacuation and joint-arrival wait at STORY-B047-K419.

/story_contents/B047/actors/6/sections/3.en:
In act one, Seo Ongyeol reclassifies patients and herbs separated by the mistaken blockade.

In act two, he aligns the HP06 lot verification and XT01 checkpoint time to the neutral car.

In act three, he chooses light-car precedence or transport-unit joint arrival, bearing the cost of safety and body heat.

The narrative is fixed as STORY-B047-K419.

/story_contents/B047/actors/6/sections/분.en:
In ending α, Seo Ongyeol sends severe patients ahead in unmarked light cars to maintain golden-time evacuation.

In ending β, he joins Jegi Dong medical transport to prevent mistaken attack but some patients suffer hypothermia aftereffects.

Both paths preserve the principle of separating supply sheet and classification table as Shinnaei neutral regulation.

The decision is either early evacuation or joint-arrival wait.

/story_contents/B047/actors/6/arc/0/summ.en: Reclassifies patients and herbs separated by mistaken blockade.

/story_contents/B047/actors/6/arc/1/summ.en: Aligns the HP06 lot verification and XT01 checkpoint time to the neutral car.

/story_contents/B047/actors/6/arc/2/summ.en: Bears one of the body-heat costs between early evacuation and joint arrival.

/story_contents/B047/actors/6/outcomes/0.en: Unmarked light-car precedence secures severe-patient evacuation time.

/story_contents/B047/actors/6/outcomes/1.en: Jegi Dong medical-transport joint arrival prevents mistaken attack, hypothermia aftereffects.

/story_contents/B047/actors/7/sections/정.en:
At the Je Gi Dong Market east gate corridor, Baek Yeoul unfolds a handful of herbs on white paper before trade and records smell, crumble, and moisture in sequence.

As a medical-trade neutrality trader for the Medical Neutrality League, she sets herbal-origin and harvest-season supply from the Donguibogam tradition, credit-and-ledger contrast from Songdo merchants, the distinction between gratis and paid prescriptions from temple pharmacies, and component testing and lot management from modern pharmacologists all on one scale.

Born in Cheongnyangni but grew up moving between merchant groups keeping Songdo accounting and temple relief pharmacies.

The name Baek Yeoul and the identifier K347, national slot Dongdaemun Union, are not renumbered.

/story_contents/B047/actors/7/sections/붕.en:
Measuring the sediment height at the bottom of a glass bottle was her first trade each day.

From long-distance merchant guilds, she learned to record credit date and transport loss in separate ledgers, and from pharmacies, she learned to turn prescriptions for patients without money into community-contribution shares.

After laboratory internship, she insisted that even herbs with the same name must be sold as separate lots by drying temperature and extraction ratio.

Using the silver-credit table Shim Dalho gave her for a communal medicinal soup pot on other relief supplies became an unpaid debt.

/story_contents/B047/actors/7/sections/가.en:
Healing Guild and patient representatives agreed to trade only goods marked with Baek Yeoul's test table at the Judicial Council common window.

Je Gi Dong Healing House provided dual prescription verification but also requested that good lots be given first to certain buyers.

She used Ryu Eunbi's neutrality principle to separate test order from auction order and excluded temple pharmacy share from lowest-price competition.

Merchant representatives complained of loss, but when counterfeit drugs declined, they accepted her comparison ledger as market standard format.

/story_contents/B047/actors/7/sections/붕.en:
When dry wind swept the herb storage, two lots marked with identical tags produced extract of different colors.

Baek Yeoul did not blockade the entire market but only stopped that transaction line, but in that time a transport unit needing pain relief left empty-handed.

The deepest wound is the memory that the testing procedure she created to keep neutrality became another barrier for people in pain.

After Cleanroom-Bent spores were detected on drying shelves, she applied the same inspection to free-pharmacy supplies and further delayed distribution speed.

/story_contents/B047/actors/7/sections/생.en:
The moment a blue test strip indicated one box's contamination, Baek Yeoul stood at a fork between disclosing the supplier name to sever market credit, or recovering the box and correcting the line non-publicly.

Patients across the Tumen River Far East region were waiting for that exact herb, and quantity was short for retesting anyway.

Disclosure stops counterfeit distribution but could bankrupt innocent transport guilds, while non-public recovery saves the supply chain but makes neutral trade suspect as concealment.

The judgment remains as K347-TURN.

/story_contents/B047/actors/7/sections/현.en:
When market noon arrives, Baek Yeoul hangs the lot-test table and credit-due table separately under the Judicial Council eaves.

Ryu Eunbi's healing approval, Shim Dalho's origin ledger, and La Seyeong's quarantine seal together create the power of three tables.

Free pharmacy shares are distributed by patient representative and paid trade is priced on the public scale.

No state can pre-purchase quantity before testing, and recovery costs of failed lots are split between seller and transporter.

/story_contents/B047/actors/7/sections/비.en:
Beneath the medicinal-soup pot base are scratched Shim Dalho's silver-credit table number and the relief-supply list Baek Yeoul substituted.

She believes the substitution saved starving pharmacy children but cannot deny changing the credit purpose without Judicial Council approval.

Guilt hardened between the blockade that stopped contaminated drugs and the transport unit that left without pain relief.

The SECRET opening requires both the patient representative's distribution table at the time and Shim Dalho's original ledger.

/story_contents/B047/actors/7/sections/관.en:
The day Ryu Eunbi separated free-pharmacy shares from auction was the contract of healing neutrality.

Learning Songdo-style comparison ledger from Shim Dalho but changing the silver-credit purpose cracked the master-apprentice bond.

La Seyeong refused to sign the contaminated-lot seal and instead demanded the recovery route be disclosed to the quarantine corps.

The unpaid share of the three relationships returns at STORY-B047-K420 as the question of supplier disclosure.

/story_contents/B047/actors/7/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, Baek Yeoul sets two extracts split under the same tag on the trading table.

In Act 2, she links HP06 prescription checks and XT04 winter demand in a lot-comparison ledger.

In Act 3, she chooses between disclosing the supplier and making a confidential recall, paying in either trust or transparency.

The story-line identifier is STORY-B047-K420.

/story_contents/B047/actors/7/sections/분.en:
In Ending α, Baek Yeoul discloses the contaminated supplier and transport route, cutting off the counterfeit-medicine trade.

In Ending β, she recalls only the affected crates and corrects the trading line, keeping medicinal supplies flowing while accepting suspicion of a cover-up.

The Medical Neutrality League's free-clinic allocation and public test sheets remain in either ending.

The decision at the time was to disclose the supplier or make a confidential recall.

/story_contents/B047/actors/7/arc/0/summ.en: Sets two extracts split under the same tag on the trading table

/story_contents/B047/actors/7/arc/1/summ.en: Links HP06 prescription checks and XT04 winter demand in a comparison ledger

/story_contents/B047/actors/7/arc/2/summ.en: Pays a price in trust by disclosing the supplier or making a confidential recall

/story_contents/B047/actors/7/outcomes/0.en: Discloses the contaminated supplier to cut off counterfeit-medicine trade

/story_contents/B047/actors/7/outcomes/1.en: Keeps supplies flowing by confidentially recalling the problem lot, under suspicion of a cover-up

/story_contents/B047/actors/8/sections/정.en:
Ham Dogyeom had a habit of weighing three sets of measures, bushels, and scale weights against one another on an empty stall before the auction bell.

As the public-auction and price-ledger keeper for the Cathedral Accreditation State, she wove together Joseon market merchants' item-by-item stall assignments, Gaeseong merchants' comparisons of weights and measures and posted market prices, and modern grain-exchange brokers' bids and execution records for long-distance credit into one public procedure.

She learned numbers atop grain sacks at the Garak loading dock and grew up watching prices become the order of survival in the ration line at the Jamsil assembly ground.

The name Ham Dogyeom, identifier K397, and state slot Myeongdong Union are immutable.

/story_contents/B047/actors/8/sections/붕.en:
At daybreak, the empty auction board showed the previous day's closing price and actual delivered quantity in separate chalk columns.

She clarified sales responsibility with market-style item stall cards and converted local measures into standard volume with Songdo-style paired scales.

After learning exchange operations, she tried to reduce disputes over collusion by prioritizing the time on the paper bid sheet over prices called aloud.

A sack she let pass underweight at a relative's stall during the first famine remained an empty line in the ledger to this day.

/story_contents/B047/actors/8/sections/가.en:
The Noryangjin Cold-Storage Guild gained the right to observe auctions on condition that it disclose storage temperatures and removal times.

Ham Dogyeom recognized Nam Yungyeong's authority to mediate and Eun Taeho's conduct of bidding, but banned item-based merchant councils from privately agreeing on minimum prices in advance.

Each standard scale weight was kept separately by an auction crew, a ration clerk, and a citizen witness, and combined only when the market opened.

The community's reputation was measured not by high winning bids but by how often the difference between closing prices and actual deliveries was published on the next page.

/story_contents/B047/actors/8/sections/붕.en:
During the week six grain trucks failed to reach Garak, sacks bearing the same weight labels held different actual volumes in the warehouse.

Ham Dogyeom halted the auction and reweighed everything, but during the half-day when price boards were blank, black-market trade penetrated the ration line.

What she could not forget was the paradox that a market closed to uphold standards had instead bought time only for powerful buyers.

After an alarm that the Migratory-Wetland Predator Swarm had overrun an outlying storehouse, she posted estimated losses separately from closing prices.

/story_contents/B047/actors/8/sections/생.en:
When the warehouse doors reopened, Ham Dogyeom had to decide whether to put the shortage up for immediate spot auction or curb a price spike with delivery commitments bundling in shipments due three days later.

Because escorts in the West Sea Granary Theater were delayed, future supplies were uncertain, and today's ration line was already long.

A spot auction distributed actual grain but drove the highest bid upward; a commitment sheet lowered prices but would shatter trust in the ledger if the goods failed to arrive.

The choice was fixed as K397-TURN.

/story_contents/B047/actors/8/sections/현.en:
Even in the afternoon, as the auction tent came down, Ham Dogyeom left the final execution prices and undelivered quantities on the blackboard.

Nam Yungyeong's opening accreditation, Eun Taeho's bid records, and Yeong Migyeol's copy of the ration ledger upheld his position.

Every sack was marked with both its conversion to the standard bushel and its actual scale weight.

Famine rations were set aside before the auction, and only the remainder entered open bidding.

/story_contents/B047/actors/8/sections/비.en:
Inside the ledger's spine lay a folded old weighing slip that covered up an underweight sack from a relative's stall.

Ham Dogyeom explained that this one act of looking the other way had led to today's rule of three-party custody for standard scale weights, but she could not disclose the victim's name.

Her guilt remained between the fairness preserved by reweighing and the black-market trade that spread while the market was closed.

The SECRET field opens when both Yeong Migyeol's old ration copy and a citizen witness's scale weight are presented.

/story_contents/B047/actors/8/sections/관.en:
Nam Yungyeong's authorization to separate famine rations in advance was an alliance of mediation.

After disputing the time of the first bid with Eun Taeho, aligning the auction bell with the ledger clock became a pact born of rivalry.

Yeong Migyeol demanded that reasons for halting auctions be written on the same board, in exchange for not hiding undelivered quantities.

At STORY-B047-K421, their shared price board tests what to trust: spot goods or a delivery commitment.

/story_contents/B047/actors/8/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, Ham Dogyeom reweighs different grain sacks bearing the same weight label.

In Act 2, she reflects HP08 storage records and XT02 escort delays on the public price board.

In Act 3, she chooses between an immediate spot auction and a three-day delivery commitment, paying the price of a spike or a default.

The story line is STORY-B047-K421.

/story_contents/B047/actors/8/sections/분.en:
In Ending α, Ham Dogyeom puts the shortage up for immediate spot auction and secures actual delivery quantities, but accepts a closing-price spike.

In Ending β, she lowers prices with a three-day delivery commitment and stakes trust in the ledger on whether the outlying convoy arrives.

In both branches, famine rations and commercial supplies are disclosed in separate ledgers.

The decision at the time was to open a spot auction or issue a commitment sheet.

/story_contents/B047/actors/8/arc/0/summ.en: Reweighs different grain sacks bearing the same weight label

/story_contents/B047/actors/8/arc/1/summ.en: Reflects HP08 storage records and XT02 escort delays on the public price board

/story_contents/B047/actors/8/arc/2/summ.en: Pays a market price by choosing spot auction or a delivery commitment

/story_contents/B047/actors/8/outcomes/0.en: Immediate spot auction guarantees actual delivery but spikes the closing price

/story_contents/B047/actors/8/outcomes/1.en: Three-day delivery commitment holds prices down but risks trust if goods fail to arrive

/story_contents/B047/actors/9/sections/정.en:
When monsoon rain battered the Suseo utility-tunnel vents, No Seram covered the date stamp and witness field with a dry cloth before tending to the smeared contract.

As a contract auditor and arbitration clerk for the Jeongdong General Labor Union, she combined the itemized disbursements of a Joseon Ministry of Revenue section chief, the bilingual item comparisons of late-opening-era trade ledgers, and the clause numbers and loss calculations of a modern contract-law clerk into one audit sheet.

Moving between Gangnam's temporary financial ledger office and the Suseo depot delivery window, she learned that figures could be added together without responsibility being combined.

The name No Seram, identifier K422, and state slot Suseo Line are fixed.

/story_contents/B047/actors/9/sections/붕.en:
The six columns divided by ink lines stood for income, expenses, transport loss, storage loss, exemptions, and unresolved items.

She learned to close balances by person in charge as in Ministry of Revenue accounting, compare different item names against one standard unit at trade counters, and write nonperformance and force majeure as separate clauses in contract training.

Her aim was to put even the powerful party's verbal promise on the same scales as a lesser state's written loss sheet.

The time she altered one witness's signature timestamp during her first arbitration remained the weak point in every audit that followed.

/story_contents/B047/actors/9/sections/가.en:
The Seoul Station Record-Law House demanded priority in interpreting Suseo's standard contracts in exchange for keeping originals and comparing copies.

No Seram followed Jeong Yura's audit direction and Sim Yuri's arbitration decisions, but did not recognize a confidential side agreement attended only by appointed committee members as part of the main contract.

The Citizen Lottery Council published his unresolved-items sheet each month and selected a third witness who was not party to the contract.

His authority in the community was measured not by the number of cases won but by the number of contracts that printed loss formulas and objection periods on the same page.

/story_contents/B047/actors/9/sections/붕.en:
After a water main broke, the Amsa escorts and Garak transport crews presented different exemption clauses, doubling the total on Suseo's loss ledger.

No Seram found the duplicate claims, but because she had altered a witness timestamp in the past, one side argued the entire audit was invalid.

What she could not bear was the moment an accurate total became a number for which no one was responsible, all because of one falsified procedure.

When coolant leakage from the Custom-Medicine Remnant Bodies was also mixed into underground warehouse losses, she separated the ledgers by cause and order of compensation.

/story_contents/B047/actors/9/sections/생.en:
On the day southerly winds drew moisture into the underground archive, No Seram had to choose whether to disclose the altered signature time herself and reopen the audit from the beginning, or seal the flaw and secure an immediate compensation agreement between both sides.

The Incheon Trust Theater's delivery manifest had crowded into the same window, and a re-audit threatened to delay even the southern passage contract.

Voluntary disclosure would restore procedural trust but delay compensation to those harmed; an immediate settlement would cover their daily losses but permanently hide the clerk's flaw.

The decision remained K422-TURN.

/story_contents/B047/actors/9/sections/현.en:
When he heard contract paper fold three times, No Seram checked the parties, witnesses, and performance deadlines before the amounts.

Jeong Yura's audit orders, Ha Seojin's transfer of the originals box, and Sim Yuri's record of objection mediation formed his authority as an arbitration clerk.

Every loss sheet had to fill four fields: cause, formula, share of liability, and review deadline.

Side agreements signed by only one of the technology-company appointment committee or the Citizen Lottery Council were kept only as drafts.

/story_contents/B047/actors/9/sections/비.en:
In the inner groove of an old date stamp remained the contract number for which he had moved a witness's timestamp forward by one day.

No Seram had tried to meet the deadline for delivering evacuees, but that alteration gave today's duplicate claimants a way out.

His guilt could not be reckoned between the evacuation column that passed in time and the audit principles shaken afterward.

The SECRET disclosure takes effect when Ha Seojin's seal on the originals box and a citizen witness's journal from that day are both verified.

/story_contents/B047/actors/9/sections/관.en:
The season Jeong Yura and No Seram put loss formulas into the standard contract marked the start of their audit alliance.

The night No Seram compared item lists in both languages while Ha Seojin dried the wet originals was a shared duty among clerks.

Sim Yuri suspected the altered date but did not invalidate the delivery of evacuees itself.

At STORY-B047-K422, the three unresolved clauses decide which duty comes first: reopening the procedure or paying compensation immediately.

/story_contents/B047/actors/9/sections/3.en:
In Act 1, No Seram finds duplicate loss claims and an altered witness timestamp on the same audit sheet.

In Act 2, she ties HP04 comparison with the original and XT05 manifest deadline to the review period.

In Act 3, she chooses between voluntary disclosure of the flaw and an immediate compensation agreement, paying the price of delay or concealment.

The story-line identifier is STORY-B047-K422.

/story_contents/B047/actors/9/sections/분.en:
In Ending α, No Seram discloses the date alteration and reopens the audit from the beginning, restoring procedural trust.

In Ending β, she seals the flaw and secures immediate compensation from both sides, covering everyday losses first.

The Jeongdong General Labor Union's loss formulas and public objection-period rules remain in both endings.

The decision at the time was to reopen the audit or settle immediately.

/story_contents/B047/actors/9/arc/0/summ.en: Finds duplicate loss claims and an altered witness timestamp on one audit sheet

/story_contents/B047/actors/9/arc/1/summ.en: Ties HP04 original comparison and the XT05 delivery deadline to the review period

/story_contents/B047/actors/9/arc/2/summ.en: Pays a contract price by disclosing the flaw or compensating immediately

/story_contents/B047/actors/9/outcomes/0.en: Discloses the date alteration and re-audits fully to restore procedural trust

/story_contents/B047/actors/9/outcomes/1.en: Seals the flaw and compensates immediately, prioritizing everyday losses

/monster_contents/M001/entries/0/bestiar.en: The low call of the Flood-Boar Great King 'Ironclad' immediately commands only the metal-and-poison mutant lineages. The adult sows retain the movement rights of their family groups; this individual controls the deep-mutant battlefield, not the entire kingdom.

/monster_contents/M001/entries/0/prose.en:
### Role and Body
The alpha controller of the Flood-Boar Swarm ruled over a heap of refuse in the lower Han River. Its massive body, four meters long, carried metal wreckage on its back and shook the surrounding sewers.

### Origin
A mutant born in the polluted wetlands swept by the G01-SC1 Great Flood took command of the early group. It later led the entire colony's breeding and territorial expansion, reshaping the southern Han River ecosystem.

### Habitat
It settled deep in the sewer tunnels connected to the flooded zone south of Seoul Station. Only during the monsoon rains, when the waters rose, did it surface to scout the surroundings.

### Needs and Economy
It relied on decaying organic matter and rusted metal ions as its main energy sources. By consuming exclusively the resources collected by the entire group, it sustained the colony's survival. G01-SC2 confirmed that when energy ran out, the whole colony entered prolonged hibernation.

### Life and Maintenance
After a single breeding season in its lifetime, it continually renewed the iron armor on its back. It welded metal fragments brought by its subordinates into place with its own bodily fluids, strengthening its defenses.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
It issued absolute commands through low-frequency calls. All boars obeyed at once, while E02 through E04 interpreted the signal and relayed it to subordinate individuals. This structure kept the colony's hierarchy stable.

### Escalating Threat
First it unleashed a territorial warning call to threaten intruders. Then it charged with its massive body, scattering the metal fragments on its back in every direction. Finally, it summoned the entire colony to surround its targets with overwhelming numbers.

### Combat and Response
If field personnel installed a high-frequency sound generator, it could induce resonance in Ironclad and create cracks. On failure, the Great King's charge would collapse the sewer walls, flood the surrounding area, and sharply raise the cost of evacuating citizens. The success signal was the sound of cracks appearing across Ironclad's surface.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
It was a being that maintained the colony's ecological balance. Excessive hunting would cripple the entire sewer system and contaminate drinking water for residents of southern Seoul. Limited negotiation was possible in G01-SC3, but refusal led the colony to actively invade human settlements.

### Scenario Links
It played a key role in G01-SC1, G01-SC2, and G01-SC3.

/monster_contents/M001/entries/1/bestiar.en: The scout 'Mudnose' was a mutant scouting network raised in the Great King's first litter. It brought the Great King scents from the wetland mud, relaying to a different recipient than ordinary juveniles scouting for feeding grounds.

/monster_contents/M001/entries/1/prose.en:
### Role and Body
Its long snout read the surrounding scents while buried in wetland mud. Its thin, flexible legs moved quickly through the current.

### Origin
The flood-survivor lineage of G01-SC1 grew out of the Great King's first litter. It later formed a scouting network responsible for the colony's outer perimeter.

### Habitat
It moved between shallow pools on the edge of the flooded zone and underground drains. By day it hid in the mud and was active only at night.

### Needs and Economy
It fed by catching decaying aquatic plants and small fish. By bringing the freshest portions to the Great King, it circulated both information and resources through the colony.

### Life and Maintenance
It shed its coat every two years, covering its broken snout tip with mud and saliva to form new sensory receptors. In the process, it updated information about the surrounding terrain.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
It sensed the smell of danger before the Great King's low call reached it. Its distinctive snout-call signaled E03 and E04, putting the whole group on alert.

### Escalating Threat
First it revealed its position with a low snout-call. Then it gathered nearby individuals to encircle targets as a group. Finally, it lured in the Great King to deliver the decisive blow.

### Combat and Response
If field personnel lured it into a trap set in the mud, its snout caught in the trap and slowed its movement. On failure, the scout summoned the group to block sewer pipes and cut off civilian routes. The success signal was muddy foam flowing from its snout.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
Leaving fresh organic refuse at a designated spot temporarily pushed its boundary back. But if the entire colony faced food shortages, it expanded its scouting range into human settlements and contaminated water sources.

### Scenario Links
It served as a scout in G01-SC1.

/monster_contents/M001/entries/2/bestiar.en: The scavenger 'Rustiron' was a deep mutant whose acidic saliva dissolved both rust and equipment. It searched through refuse even without the Great King's call, but stopped scavenging and joined the encirclement when it heard the signal.

/monster_contents/M001/entries/2/prose.en:
### Role and Body
Its powerful jaws broke rusted metal pipes, and its acidic saliva dissolved corrosion. Rust flakes attached to its torso blended into the surrounding environment.

### Origin
An individual raised in a heap of sewage-treatment refuse came to manage the colony's resource cycle. Records from G01-SC2 show that these individuals improved the colony's waste-processing efficiency.

### Habitat
It roamed mainly along the floors of sewer tunnels piled with metal refuse. It was most active around pools of stagnant acidic water.

### Needs and Economy
It fed on rusted metal and corroded organic matter. By breaking them down, it supplied reusable ions to the whole colony. When supplies ran short, the colony's scavenging activity stopped.

### Life and Maintenance
To survive in acidic environments, it periodically renewed its skin. It washed the rust from around its jaws and grew new acid-secreting glands.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
It cleaned refuse independently, even without the Great King's orders. But when it heard the call, it immediately stopped scavenging and moved into combat formation.

### Escalating Threat
It sprayed acidic saliva to corrode enemy equipment. Then it narrowed the encirclement with nearby individuals, trapping its targets in place.

### Combat and Response
If field personnel sprayed neutralizer, the acid was neutralized and the scavenger's attack power fell sharply. On failure, the acid dissolved field equipment and reduced movement speed by 70%. The success signal was white smoke rising as the neutralizer reacted with the saliva.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
Leaving a large quantity of metal refuse in a designated tunnel concentrated its scavenging there, clearing the surrounding area for a while. But over-supplying refuse sharply increased the colony's size and led to frequent sewer blockages.

### Scenario Links
It left testimony about the resource cycle in G01-SC2.

/monster_contents/M001/entries/3/bestiar.en: The guard 'Steel Tusk' was an escort mutant that blocked the Great King's ten-meter perimeter with its tusks. Unlike the adult sows of the family groups, which carried salt, it put the Great King's safety first.

/monster_contents/M001/entries/3/prose.en:
### Role and Body
Its enormous tusks, growing through thick hide, pierced metal pipes. Its large, heavy body was adapted to pushing upstream against currents.

### Origin
An escort lineage raised near the Great King formed the colony's core defensive line. G01-SC3 records confirmed that this lineage put the Great King's safety first.

### Habitat
It patrolled narrow passages and iron doors in the center of the flooded zone. Even after the water receded, it preferred places where mud pooled deeply.

### Needs and Economy
In return for protecting the Great King, it received first share of the most nutritious decaying matter. This supply of nutrients kept its tusks strong.

### Life and Maintenance
It regularly ground and polished tusks broken in combat. It filled fractures with metal fragments brought by nearby individuals.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
It kept the Great King's location under constant priority watch. If another individual came within ten meters, it emitted a low warning sound to block the approach.

### Escalating Threat
It drove back intruders with a powerful charge, then gored them with its tusks. If the threat continued, it called nearby guards for a coordinated attack.

### Combat and Response
If field personnel dug a trap to guide its charge, its tusks became lodged in the trap floor and it was immobilized for 30 seconds. On failure, the guard collapsed sewer walls and flooded nearby subway stations. The success signal was the metallic impact of its tusks catching on the trap's rebar.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
It temporarily opened a particular passage in exchange for assurances of the Great King's safety. But if the agreement was broken, the whole colony fortified that passage and permanently blocked a civilian evacuation route.

### Scenario Links
It served as an escort in G01-SC3.

/monster_contents/M001/entries/4/bestiar.en: The venom secreter 'Rotmouth' was a specialized attack mutant that survived in chemical pools. Its green venom marked the boundary of the mutant lineage; it was not the basic weapon of wetland sows.

/monster_contents/M001/entries/4/prose.en:
### Role and Body
Glands developed around its mouth sprayed dark green venom. Poison stains spreading across its torso slowly corroded nearby metal.

### Origin
An individual that survived a pool of polluted chemical waste became the colony's specialized attack unit. G01-SC2 recorded many cases in which these individuals disabled enemy equipment.

### Habitat
It stayed deep in sewer areas where toxic chemicals had pooled. Other individuals detoured around the area to avoid the smell of poison.

### Needs and Economy
It strengthened its glands by consuming highly concentrated toxic substances. Through this individual, the colony maintained a boundary against hostile ecologies.

### Life and Maintenance
If tissue around its mouth was damaged after secreting venom, it ate nearby mud to regenerate new glands. In the process, it increased its resistance to poison.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
When it received the Great King's call, it immediately prepared venom. It worked with nearby individuals to encircle the enemy and then spray a concentrated dose.

### Escalating Threat
First it sprayed venom to paralyze the enemy's movement. Then the entire colony surrounded the paralyzed target and finished it off.

### Combat and Response
If field personnel used gas masks and neutralizing spray together, they blocked 80% of the venom's effects. On failure, the poison corroded equipment, leaving personnel unable to move within five minutes. The success signal was green smoke rising as the venom was neutralized.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
It left a designated area empty for a while if toxic waste was dumped there. But excessive amounts increased the number of venom-secreting individuals and permanently contaminated nearby drinking-water sources.

### Scenario Links
It left toxic testimony in G01-SC2.

/monster_contents/M001/entries/5/bestiar.en: The mud architect 'Bricknose' was a mobile construction mutant that mixed mud and metal to close passages. Unlike the place called Mud-Iron Wall, this individual set traps and brought down ceilings.

/monster_contents/M001/entries/5/prose.en:
### Role and Body
Its snout and forelegs mixed mud and metal into sturdy structures. Clumps of mud attached to its back blended completely into the surrounding environment.

### Origin
A mutant with an extremely developed wetland-building instinct designed the colony's network of nests. G01-SC1 records confirmed that this individual improved the colony's survival rate after the flood.

### Habitat
It moved between muddy ground left by the flood and collapsed concrete debris. There it continually built new passages and nests.

### Needs and Economy
It used mud and broken metal debris as its main materials. Through construction, it secured concealment and movement routes for the entire colony.

### Life and Maintenance
When a structure it had built collapsed, it immediately gathered nearby mud to repair it. As it added new passages, it expanded the colony's territory.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
It designed the Great King's dwelling as its top priority. It took materials brought by other individuals and immediately reinforced walls and passages.

### Escalating Threat
It set mud traps to catch intruders, then collapsed ceilings to bury them. When the threat level rose, it closed every nearby passage.

### Combat and Response
If field personnel sprayed ground hardener, the mud structures hardened and lost their trapping effect. On failure, a collapse left field personnel unable to move for 3 turns and doubled the cost of rescuing citizens. The success signal was hardened mud cracking with a sharp sound.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
It showed curiosity and opened a particular passage when shown human construction techniques. But if the techniques were not shared, the colony actively occupied human underground facilities and crippled subway service.

### Scenario Links
It left testimony about the nest in G01-SC1.

/monster_contents/M001/entries/6/bestiar.en: The herd guide 'Cry-King' was a relay mutant among the Great King's direct descendants, amplifying low frequencies. It relayed first to E02 through E04, using a different frequency from the departure signal given by the sows.

/monster_contents/M001/entries/6/prose.en:
### Role and Body
Resonance organs developed around its neck greatly amplified its low-frequency calls. Its torso vibrated with each call, stirring the nearby current.

### Origin
An individual among the Great King's direct descendants specialized in transmitting calls and took on the colony's relay duty. Records from G01-SC3 show that it maintained the unity of the entire colony.

### Habitat
It stayed in a wide chamber at the colony's center. It preferred tunnel junctions where its calls carried well.

### Needs and Economy
Producing calls consumed a great deal of energy. It maintained its resonance organs by taking first share of nutrients brought by nearby individuals.

### Life and Maintenance
It regularly inspected its vocal cords and resonance organs. It adjusted its call frequency by filling damaged areas with mud and saliva.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
It relayed the Great King's orders to E02-E04 first. It amplified the low frequency and broadcast it to the whole colony at once, maintaining coordinated behavior.

### Escalating Threat
It summoned nearby individuals all at once with a powerful call. The assembled group pressed the intruders together.

### Combat and Response
If field personnel wore specialized noise-canceling headsets and fired a high-frequency disruptor toward the call's source, its resonance organs overloaded. On failure, the entire colony assembled and completely blocked the field personnel's retreat. The success signal was the discordant sound from Cry-King's throat.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
If responders analyzed its call patterns and answered in a particular rhythm, it attempted limited communication. But when the colony lacked food, Cry-King led an incursion into human settlements and raided food stores.

### Scenario Links
It left testimony about command in G01-SC3.

/monster_contents/M001/entries/7/bestiar.en: The metal-fusion mutant 'Fusion Armor' was a royal-guard mutant whose skin and scrap metal had become one body. It took no orders from other individuals, only from the Great King directly.

/monster_contents/M001/entries/7/prose.en:
### Role and Body
Metal fragments fused with its skin across its whole body, forming thick armor. Whenever it moved, the metal scraped together with a sharp sound.

### Origin
A rare mutant that survived extreme pollution became the colony's elite royal guard. G01-SC2 confirmed multiple cases of this individual directly escorting the Great King.

### Habitat
It stayed among heaps of metal waste in the deepest, most polluted sewers. Other individuals avoided the area to escape the scraping metal sound.

### Needs and Economy
It maintained the fused areas by continually consuming highly concentrated metal ions. The colony built a powerful defensive line through this individual.

### Life and Maintenance
When fused metal came loose, it ate nearby refuse to form a new metal layer. Its body weight gradually increased in the process.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
It served as a royal guard directly under the Great King. It wielded the colony's greatest combat power and took no orders from other individuals.

### Escalating Threat
It blocked every attack with thick metal armor while charging with its massive body. After the charge, it shook its body to scatter nearby metal fragments.

### Combat and Response
If field personnel installed a high-power electromagnetic pulse generator, the fused metal overheated and its movement slowed by 40%. On failure, its charge struck the field personnel's position, rupturing nearby sewers and releasing contaminated water. The success signal was superheated vapor rising from its metal armor.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
It temporarily retreated if its continual pain from the fusion process was acknowledged and particular metal waste was provided. But if refused, the entire royal guard attacked human facilities and cut off the power supply.

### Scenario Links
It performed its role as an elite in G01-SC2.

/monster_contents/M001/entries/8/bestiar.en: The Venom King 'Deadly Tusk' was an elite battlefield mutant born of venom secretion and metal fusion. It was a famed boss, not the biological king of all Flood-Boars.

/monster_contents/M001/entries/8/prose.en:
### Role and Body
Powerful venom saturated its enormous tusks. Glands around its mouth continually coated the tusk surfaces with venom.

### Origin
It was a top-tier combatant born from the crossbreeding of a venom secreter and a metal-fusion mutant. Records from G01-SC3 show that it served as the colony's final line of defense.

### Habitat
It established its own territory in the deepest sewers where poison and metal coexisted. Other individuals detected the poisonous smell and kept their distance.

### Needs and Economy
It maintained the venom on its tusks by consuming toxic substances and metal ions together. Through this individual, the colony secured its strongest combat power.

### Life and Maintenance
When the balance of poison and metal broke down, it ate nearby refuse to find a new balance. In the process, the venom coating on its tusks grew thicker.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
It served as the Great King's closest aide. It judged independently and led the colony's final defense and attacks.

### Escalating Threat
It stabbed enemies with venom-soaked tusks while spraying venom. Then it summoned the nearby colony for a coordinated attack.

### Combat and Response
If field personnel used top-grade protective suits and powerful antidote injectors together, they completely neutralized the venom. On failure, venom entered the bloodstream, incapacitating personnel within 2 turns and poisoning nearby citizens en masse. The success signal was a drop of neutralized venom falling from its tusk.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
It was a being living in extreme pain. If responders established empathy and provided particular chemical waste, it cooperated. But refusing negotiation put all of southern Seoul at risk of contamination from a full colony assault led by the Venom King.

### Scenario Links
It appeared as a boss-level threat in G01-SC3.

/monster_contents/M001/entries/9/bestiar.en: The ironclad nest 'Steel Wetland' was a living place where the Great King's bodily fluids fused with accumulated mud and metal. It was not an individual but a fixed stronghold in the deep sewers.

/monster_contents/M001/entries/9/prose.en:
### Role and Body
It is the Great King's dwelling and the center of the entire colony. A living metal-and-mud composite structure slowly expands along the surrounding sewer pipes.

### Origin
Colony structures accumulated over decades fused with the Great King's bodily fluids to become a living fortress. From G01-SC1 onward, this structure became the foundation of the colony's survival.

### Habitat
It stands at the center of the largest flood zone in the lower Han River. It continually absorbs the surrounding mud and metal debris, expanding its territory.

### Needs and Economy
It receives the resources gathered by the entire colony. The structure itself absorbs metal to grow, providing the colony with a stable home.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
When part of it is damaged, every nearby member of the colony is mobilized to repair it. A supply of the Great King's bodily fluids speeds the structure's regeneration.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
As the colony's heart, it is instinctively protected by every member. Vibrations arising inside the structure coordinate the behavior of the entire colony.

### Escalating Threat
The fortress itself activates traps and deploys self-defense organs. As the threat level rises, it mobilizes the entire colony to surround intruders.

### Combat and Response
If personnel on site inject an acidic solvent into the structure's core, its internal metal-and-mud bonds weaken, reducing the fortress's functionality by 50%. If they fail, the fortress seals every surrounding sewer pipe, flooding all of underground southern Seoul. The sign of success is rusty foam rising from the structure's surface.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
It is the ecological center of the colony. Destroying it would collapse the entire sewer system of southern Seoul. In G01-SC1 through SC3, it becomes the site of crucial negotiations and moral choices. If negotiations are refused, the fortress mobilizes the entire colony to occupy human settlements permanently.

### Scenario Connections
It serves as the final setting in all of G01-SC1, G01-SC2, and G01-SC3.

/monster_contents/M002/entries/0/bestiar.en: The fortress 'Mud-Iron Wall' is a wall of hardened mud and rebar on the slope outside the Water Compact Well sluice. Sows read its dull vibrations as the time of sealing; solitary males ignore them.

/monster_contents/M002/entries/0/prose.en:
### Role and Body
On the waste slope outside the Water Compact Well, Water Compact Well, stands a wall in which mud and rebar have hardened into one. Each time the sluice opens, the wall drinks water and accumulates decaying organic matter and a crust of salt inside. It catches approaching footsteps in mud, serving as both a storehouse and a capture trap.

### Origin
After the first hoofprint of G01-SC1 appeared at the collection yard, sow families repeatedly packed mud onto the sluice apron, growing the wall's framework. Rebar left by the flood and salt from the Yeouido Computer District's cooling waste seeped into the mud, turning the wall into a storage organ that would not collapse.

### Habitat
It is rooted in the lowest slope of the flood zone and draws in water in rhythm with the sluice's opening and closing. In the dry season, it survives by licking the salt layer inside; during monsoon weeks, its face pushes outward a handspan at a time, narrowing the drainage channel.

### Needs and Economy
It concentrates food brought in by family groups and salt flowing from the recovery tank inside the wall. If this concentration stops, the wall can no longer hold water, and the downstream pumps overheat that same night. Excessive concentration increases pressure to forage in the alleys.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
Adults fill cracked sections with saliva and mud, adding only one new layer per monsoon. The labor devoted to adding that layer reduces scouting and bathing that day, drawing the center of the hierarchy toward the wall.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
The wall's dull vibrations tell the family groups when sealing will occur. The sows do not begin moving until the vibrations subside; solitary males ignore them and pass along the same slope.

### Escalating Threat
When a drain is blocked with mud, the pump noise changes first. By day, as the water recedes, part of the wall sheds iron fragments as though collapsing, closing the inspection passage. At night, when the water level crosses the warning line, the wall's vibrations draw the family groups up toward the stairs.

### Combat and Response
A drain outside the sluice remains blocked with mud while four pumps overheat within the same opening-and-closing cycle. If the duty crew cannot push solvent into a hairline crack in the wall during the interval when the water level drops a handspan, the wall grows another layer and seals off the downstream worksite that same night. If the crack opens, rusty-smelling steam leaks from the gap and the dull vibrations subside.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
Only one person on duty has the authority to cut through one section of the wall during the night shift to let water through. In a week when recovery of the G01-SC2 salt pool is brought forward, cutting that section bursts the storehouse and drives the family groups into semi-basement alleys. Leaving it intact lets the pump station hold, but the wall drinks water at every sealing time, prolonging the ration convoy. Mud cut apart cannot be rejoined in the same monsoon.

### Scenario Connections
G01-SC1 records that the wall's first layer of mud was attached on the same night hoofprints appeared at the collection yard. In G01-SC2 and G01-SC3, salt storage and occupation of the sluice stairs overlap, with this wall as their setting.

/monster_contents/M002/entries/1/bestiar.en: The larva 'Tender Ironhide' is a soft-bodied offspring of the Great King's bloodline that fills the pipes through sheer numbers. Its nursery inside the wall overlaps with the sow families' territory, but once its shell closes, it moves into the mutant transport line.

/monster_contents/M002/entries/1/prose.en:
### Role and Body
The Great King's newest offspring still have soft backs, leaving the pink skin of their 1.5-meter bodies exposed. At the edge of the bathing ground, they absorb metal ions through their skin and form a thin shell in a fortnight. Their soft bodies catch the ankles of anyone passing through the drainage channel.

### Origin
They emerged all at once from one sow's litter just after the G01-SC1 flood receded. A warm, humid section inside the storage wall became the litter's nursery, and those that grow up disperse into scouting and transport.

### Habitat
They spend the day in a warm mud chamber inside the wall, emerging only on nights of rapid growth to seek metal fragments on the slope. In the dry season, the chamber depends on its salt layer; during the monsoon, the chamber entrance opens into a waterway that pushes the larvae as far as the pipe entrance.

### Needs and Economy
Covering their soft skin requires both highly concentrated decaying matter and salt. They contribute some of the ions they absorb to enlarge the wall's storehouse. If ions become scarce, the nursery temperature falls and the next litter stops growing.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
Their skin changes sheen and gains another layer of shell every fortnight. Torn areas are filled with bodily fluid flowing from the wall. Once a shell is complete, its owner moves into the adult transport line.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
The larvae respond only to the sows and the wall's vibrations. Once their shells close, they rise to positions as subadults responsible for the forward feeding ground; until then, they merely fill the slope with their numbers.

### Escalating Threat
At first, young bodies gather on the pipe floor and soak the feet of those passing through. Once their shells begin to open thinly, they test short charges with iron fragments stuck to their bodies. When they return to the nursery, empty spaces in the wall are filled in proportion to their numbers, eliminating the detour.

### Combat and Response
If the metallic sheen of the larvae's skin stops developing for two days, the cluster cannot widen the pipe. A brief burst of high frequency at the edge of the bathing ground disrupts only their growth rhythm. If the rhythm remains unchanged, the same drainage channel fills with young in a fortnight, lengthening the detour through the alleys.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
When the hoofprints at the G01-SC1 collection yard become visible, the recovery tank and a sow face each other over the same scented bait. Moving the bait toward the wetland keeps the larvae inside the wall for another fortnight but delays the nighttime ration by one meal. Removing the sow on the spot sends the scent of her young through the alleys for 48 hours, and the window for action opens and closes within a day.

### Scenario Connections
G01-SC1 marks the point when larval hoofprints begin appearing among those at the collection yard. The salt shortage of G01-SC2 slows shell formation, while the crowded stairs of G01-SC3 lead to young bodies getting caught between people's feet.

/monster_contents/M002/entries/2/bestiar.en: The adult 'Rusty Ironplate' is the transport workhorse of an ordinary family group, clad in rusty iron plates across its 3-meter body. Despite the aging label, it is a working adult and enters the same tunnel only after the sow sets out.

/monster_contents/M002/entries/2/prose.en:
### Role and Body
Rusty iron plates encircle its fully grown, 3-meter body. The plates scrape the sewer tunnel walls as it carries salt crust and organic matter. In the middle of the transport line, its tusks push sidewalk rebar, briefly closing off the human path.

### Origin
Adults that survived the early wetlands of G01-SC1 accumulated metal on their backs and took this form. The same body handles both labor and brief clashes, entering the tunnel only after the sow begins moving.

### Habitat
It sleeps in the tunnels of the middle flood zone and, during dry-season weeks, travels almost exclusively along the walls. On monsoon nights, a transport route opens between the salt pool and the slope, overlapping with alley drainage.

### Needs and Economy
It eats metal and decaying matter together to maintain its iron plates, passing surplus salt to the wall and the larvae. If the Cheongram recovery tank collects the pool early, the plates crumble and a week's transport volume falls by half.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
It returns to the wall to reattach scraped plates with bodily fluid. Scouting lapses on nights spent making repairs, so the family groups do not use that time as a movement window.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
Taking its cue from the sow's departure and the wall's vibrations, it tells the subadults the order of passage through the tunnel. Solitary males do not follow this order and cross paths with the adult line at the same feeding ground.

### Escalating Threat
The sound of metal at the tunnel entrance signals that the day's transport has begun. When the sound reaches the sidewalk, iron fragments fly up and block the water-supply inspection cover. If several adults gather at the same bend, the water pressure for morning rations falls.

### Combat and Response
As an adult emerges from the tunnel carrying salt crust on its back, an electromagnetic pulse from a recovery-tank cart reaches the same bend. If the pulse grazes its body, flakes of rust fall away in a seagull pattern. If the cart is a beat late, its tusks push the sidewalk rebar and the water-supply hose is pulled out overnight.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
The sluice government, the Cheongram recovery tank, and alley representatives sit together to allocate the adults' transport nights. Leaving the salt pool in the wetland ties monitors to that site for a season; removing only the alley food waste first prompts the adults to make a route into another semi-basement. The cost left by G01-SC2 is not carcasses, but which door the monitoring work shifts to.

### Scenario Connections
The cost of the G01-SC2 pool shows in the thickness of the adults' iron plates. The hoofprint record of G01-SC1 and the occupation of the stairs in G01-SC3 mark where this transport line overlaps with human routes.

/monster_contents/M002/entries/3/bestiar.en: The coexisting form 'Peaceful Ironhide' occupies the edge of the family group. Its flexible ironhide selects only the scents from the waste shelf. If collections are missed for two weeks, its back hardens and it opens covers like a wild adult.

/monster_contents/M002/entries/3/prose.en:
### Role and Body
Individuals that move only around the outskirts of human areas have thin, flexible ironhide and can distinguish the scents on waste shelves. With the wall's and sow's permission, they pass near drainage-channel covers; patrol records show them selecting metal fragments from the shelves.

### Origin
This form appeared after leftover-food convoys were diverted through a bait corridor in G01-SC3. Once it began receiving waste selected by people reliably, its body adapted to collection instead of attack.

### Habitat
It stays by drainage channels with shelves between the wetland and the alleys. It checks the shelves at sealing time and retreats deep toward the wall on days when they are empty.

### Needs and Economy
Sorted metal and a small amount of salt are its staple diet. As long as supplies continue, the colony puts less pressure on the alleys; if supplies stop, the same body opens covers like a wild adult.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
Rather than breeding, it lives by ingraining the shelf schedule into its body. If the schedule is kept, its ironhide stays flexible; if two weeks are missed, its back hardens, becoming suited to charging rather than concealment.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
It responds only to the sow's direct signals and does not share a route with other adults. On nights when the shelf is stocked, it remains in the peaceful tier and takes a peripheral role in resource distribution.

### Escalating Threat
While the shelf schedule is kept, even warning calls are rare. Three days after a collection is missed, its back hardens and it occupies the drainage channel. At the next sealing time, the family group leaves muddy hoofprints through that cover all the way to the alley kitchens.

### Combat and Response
Stocking the waste shelf to the same weight at the same time each week keeps the thin ironhide from hardening. A low rumble then continues without a break from the wetland. If the shelf is empty for two weeks, its skin thickens, and the same body opens the cover and pushes muddy water as far as the drinking-water valve.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
For households on the outskirts, placing sorted metal fragments on the shelf is an obligation without a signature. If the shelf is stocked before the G01-SC3 evacuation leftovers pile up on the stairs, the coexisting form retreats toward the wall. If even one household skips a collection, the window for reversing the change shrinks to the next sealing time, and that household's water-supply hose takes in mud first.

### Scenario Connections
The weight on this shelf determines whether the passage-rights agreement of G01-SC3 is upheld or broken. G01-SC1 and G01-SC2 can be read as the history of feeding-ground movements, before the shelf existed, left in this individual's flexible ironhide.

/monster_contents/M002/entries/4/bestiar.en: The boss 'Great King's Heir' is a large female of the bloodline that will succeed to the armored king's place. She holds several family groups in one column. She is a distinct mustering individual on the battlefield; solitary males remain outside her column.

/monster_contents/M002/entries/4/prose.en:
### Role and Body
The heir to E01's Great King has a 5-meter back nearly as thick as the storage wall and holds several family groups in a single column with a low call. On nights when the floodwater rises, she emerges from the deepest storage section and makes the sluice stairs her arena.

### Origin
The largest surviving female bloodline from the G01-SC2 salt crisis grew into the heir. Her body became a means of rearranging the order of movement in seasons of scarce energy, setting the rhythm of the western Han River wetlands to her call.

### Habitat
She stays in the deepest salt section of the wall, then crosses the entire tunnel at once when a water-level warning appears. In ordinary times she barely moves, registering as only a single mass on Hannuri's heat-source display.

### Needs and Economy
She consumes a great deal of resources but redistributes surplus salt and decaying matter to the family groups. If that redistribution stops, the heir's call rings hollow, the groups scatter into the alleys, and the area of harm to civilians expands.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
She rubs the Great King's memories of movement into grooves on her back and fills the grooves with her subordinates' iron fragments. Too much filling leaves gaps in subadult scouting and delays the escape route in the next flood.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
She gives the departure signal after the Great King falls asleep. The sows align their columns to that signal; as it overlaps with the wall's vibrations, the gaps between families narrow. Only solitary males remain outside the column.

### Escalating Threat
On some nights, her low call alone drives scouts back. When the call coincides with the wall's trap sections, iron fragments pour down all at once. When rising water and evacuation leftovers coincide, the heir fills the southern stairs with a single column.

### Combat and Response
Even as floodwater begins to engulf the sluice stairs, the heir's low call keeps the family groups in one column. Scouts set a frequency shield at the seam where the storage wall meets her back armor. If the shield covers the seam, the mass of heat signatures splits into family groups; if it misses, the evacuation line encounters hooves on the same stairs.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
Even after Hannuri marks a single large heat source, human scouts can move that marker to distinguish the family groups from solitary males. On a night when G01-SC3's evacuation window overlaps, moving the marker delays the heir's muster and briefly clears the stairs. Trusting the marker as it stands lets the groups take their places first, following the smell of leftovers. The last row of the line heading toward Imjin bears the burden of the postponed evacuation order.

### Scenario Connections
The G01-SC3 flood line follows the same timetable as the heir's mustering call. The first hoofprints of G01-SC1 and the cost of salt in G01-SC2 form the earlier part of the departure rules this body inherited.

/monster_contents/M002/entries/5/bestiar.en: The variant 'Bukhansan Ironplate' belongs to an upstream family with ridge moss growing on its back. It responds only faintly to the Great King's call, and its own sow initiates movement along the hiking trail.

/monster_contents/M002/entries/5/prose.en:
### Role and Body
Adapted to the foot of Bukhansan and the Anyangcheon corridor, this body's armor has moss and grass growing in its gaps, matching the color of the slope. It moves between an abandoned rail embankment and the wetland, rising from the grassy shade to cut off the hiking trail.

### Origin
During the G01-SC1 flood, some families were pushed upstream and rooted plant fibers in their backs. They lived to a different rhythm from the downstream storage wall, but in drought they descend toward the sluice again, swelling the main group.

### Habitat
By day, they cling to ridge wetlands and areas around abandoned railroad ties, sustaining daytime activity through photosynthesis. By the end of the dry season, they must move along Anyangcheon in search of downstream salt.

### Needs and Economy
Sugars produced by the moss supplement their diet of decaying matter. When drought scorches the moss, the variant families stop transporting supplies and the downstream storehouse thins out as well.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
Symbiotic plants cover scraped armor and aid its regeneration. If polluted water reaches the ridge, the moss dies, exposing their backs and breaking their camouflage.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
On the ridge, their own sow initiates movement, and they respond only faintly to the Great King's call. Only on nights when they descend downstream do they exchange information through the wall's vibrations.

### Escalating Threat
A body rising from the mossy shade blocks the hiking trail in one movement. Within the same week, plant sap mixes with valley water and changes the smell at the water intake. If the family joins the downstream group, nighttime hoofprints on the sluice stairs contain bits of ridge moss as well.

### Combat and Response
A back with scorched moss is already exposed like a mass of iron before its owner descends downstream. A hiking-trail ranger applies solvent only to the symbiotic seams. If the treated area extends beyond the ridge, the variant family descends along Anyangcheon and adds a layer to the storage wall outside the sluice.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
A quarantine strip marked once in spring remains in place into the following year unless one side breaks it. Keeping the strip leaves the Bukhansan hiking trail empty during the day; pushing it aside to allow the groups to join downstream adds the variant's camouflaged charge to the G01-SC3 flood line. The costs fall separately on weekend hikers on the ridge and the downstream pump's duty crew.

### Scenario Connections
The upstream evacuation of G01-SC1 is why this variant settled on the ridge. The salt drought of G01-SC2 and the converging flood of G01-SC3 hinge on whether the quarantine strip is maintained or broken.

/monster_contents/M002/entries/6/bestiar.en: The broadcast crow lord 'Signal King' is the breeding pair at the Sangam transmission tower, not the king of the leaderless roost. Its imitation of three horn blasts merely serves as the communal roost's evening clock.

/monster_contents/M002/entries/6/prose.en:
### Role and Body
The breeding pair at the top of the Sangam transmission tower gathers sparks in its metallic feathers and carries a horn imitation through its whole body. At dusk, when that imitation spreads across the factory roofs, the dark bodies on the communal roost lean in one direction and the flock swarms over the work basket.

### Origin
Even before G02-SC1, factory waste heat and catenary sparks drew insects, and a pair claimed the tower. After learning to associate three horn blasts with food, the whole roost began using that pattern to divide up the evening sky above Seoul Station.

### Habitat
They cling to the roofs of the Yeongdeungpo Line Standards Alliance and the tops of disused railway towers by day, flying far only at night. Outside the breeding season, the roost shares calls without a leader, so the pair’s pattern becomes its temporary clock.

### Needs and Economy
Insects, small carcasses, and the warmth left by sparks sustain the pair. If the pattern weakens, the flock cannot blanket the basket, making daytime roof work easier; instead, insects remain in inspection openings and draw the next sparks.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
They molt their metallic feathers each season and fill the gaps with fine wire brought by their offspring. If the repairs are clumsy, their imitation splits, dividing the roost between two beats.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
During breeding season, the pair divides nest defense and food transport between them, with young helpers joining the dives. The nonbreeding roost has no leader, so the pair’s horn imitation alone becomes the focus of repeated learning.

### Escalating Threat
