An adult specialist guarding a separate protective area for families with pups. Though smaller than a leader, it blocks approaching noses under the shade canopy first, remembering the smell of disinfectant and unfamiliar hand gestures as threats. Tag readings miss pups more often.

### Origin
As loading-yard leftovers grew and several families joined forces, a pair with pups fixed one corner of a vacant lot as their sleeping place, establishing a nursery area. Even a leader's proposal can be vetoed at this barrier.

### Habitat
It keeps to the shade of a Yongsan Line vacant lot and dry ground an alley away from the loading yard. It does not take pups onto the freezer approach and moves toward a drain when vibrations grow strong.

### Needs and Economy
Pup food packs, shade, and sealed water take priority over the adults' share. If distribution is confined to the loading yard, the nursery barrier is left empty and pups are exposed to cart wheels.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
Stable feeding does not cause explosive breeding; it only strengthens defense of the barrier. If adults are captured, the sound of remaining tags re-establishes it, but pup survival falls before that happens.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
Its veto stands outside the command structure. The barrier remains even when the leading adults and metal-tag specialists go to the loading route. If an HC03 flag marks the pups' area, it tolerates approaches only inside that boundary.

### Escalating Threat
At Stage 1 there is only the barrier in a corner of the vacant lot. At Stage 2 a feeding cart cuts across it and pups following the cart are left behind. At Stage 3, after feeding stops, the barrier moves beneath the transfer stairs.

### Combat and Response
Capturing the entire nursery destroys trust and scatters adults across the market. Removing only an injured adult without lethal force and leaving the barrier in the shade restores passage more slowly but preserves the pups' area. Success is reunion with pups and zero bites.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
Separating families with a feeding cart to check tags speeds loading, but pups unable to follow are abandoned. Recording present companionship before old codes conflicts with former claims of ownership. Erasing the nursery barrier for human passage means erasing the animals' present family.

### Scenario Links
The separation choice in G03-SC1 tests this barrier, and family-specific feeding areas in G03-SC3 offer a way to recognize it as an official cost.

/monster_contents/M004/entries/9/display.en: Abandoned-Dog Iron Pack First Elite 'Cart Tooth'

/monster_contents/M004/entries/9/bestiar.en: First Elite 'Cart Tooth' is a real biter that learned escort-cart wheels and ankle height as biting range. It is an exception that prioritizes the cart over the leader and does not use its teeth in front of the pup barrier.

/monster_contents/M004/entries/9/prose.en:
### Role and Body
The first elite is a medium adult that learned escort-cart wheels and human ankle height as the height for its teeth. Its nose distinguishes thawed drips on a cart from disinfectant, while its ears separate the squeak of a cart axle from engine noise. It can lead actual biting attacks, and its metal collar often lets only one side of its tag be read.

### Origin
During Stage 2 family reunion, several families converged on one passage; an individual that resisted while following a cart remembered biting range. Its former guard-dog pursuit training remains, but it has no owner; after one deceptive capture it stored the cart itself as a threat.

### Habitat
It occupies the short straight stretch where the Noryangjin Line loading passage meets the transfer stairs. On the vacant lot it stays behind the leading adults, emerging at the freezer threshold only on nights when XT03 vibrations coincide with a halt in feeding.

### Needs and Economy
Residual protein on carts is its chief resource, so tighter sealing makes it follow people's bags instead of wheels. Without enough water and shade, the warning period before it bites shortens.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
If its teeth are damaged, it chews cart rubber to recalibrate their height. If few treated individuals rejoin their former companions after nonlethal capture, this elite remains a solitary pursuer.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
It is an exception that prioritizes cart movement over the leader's proposal. It does not bite at the pup barrier, but overlapping deceptive signals can make it bite passersby while defending the barrier. Mediators record it separately only as the individual leading attacks.

### Escalating Threat
At Stage 1 it walks beside a cart and merely sniffs the wheels. At Stage 2 it blocks an escort line and increases the loading share. At Stage 3, after feeding stops and deceptive capture occurs, it attacks ankle height first in the market and on the stairs.

### Combat and Response
Killing only this individual with direct fire scatters the remaining families over a wider area. The upper limit of response is to separate the cart route from the pup barrier with a blocking fence and capture only the individual leading the bites without lethal force. Using the sound of metal scraps as bait destroys not just trust in this elite but the entire rescue-call network.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
Moving night loading to another freezer clears its biting range and preserves the animal's memory, but raises merchants' costs. Treating a captured individual as a bargaining resource closes the negotiation window. Humans must answer the question of erasing its cart memory to protect passage by paying an additional cost.

### Scenario Links
This elite leads the reunion pack following the cart in G03-SC2, and the choice to capture only injured individuals in G03-SC3 sets the limit on using its teeth.

/monster_contents/M005/entries/0/bestiar.en: The Rust-Ring Escort is a body with overlapping rings that takes the left flank of the leading adult. It is not a leader and does not push the pack toward the loading area before the leader steps out.

/monster_contents/M005/entries/0/prose.en:
### Role and Body

In the open ground outside the Magok research institute wall, the Rust-Ring Escort guards the left side of the longest-lived medium adult, striking the layered rusty collar rings against its flank.

Its shoulders are thick, and the scars on its muzzle are scrapes from a helmet rim; the ring sounds do not carry commands. They are more like markers that draw scattered companions together by the smell of the same wind.

This individual is not a leader, and does not push the pack toward the loading area before the leading adult steps out.

### Origin

An animal that had remained as a construction-site guard dog lost its human in an evacuation column, then joined the Abandoned-Dog Iron Pack, drawn by the sound of metal scraps in a closed security passage.

The shelter code on its tag survives only in H03 Ido's incomplete reading; its current family is defined not by that code but by where they sleep together and the territory they protect for their young.

### Habitat

By day it presses itself into the shade along the Yongsan Line walls and beneath the elevated track, descending to the edge of the Noryangjin Line night loading area only when thawing smells grow strong.

On days when XT03 freight vibrations intensify, it does not cross the cold-storage approach, only scenting the wind at the passage entrance; it does not appear on the crowded daytime transfer stairs.

### Needs

Its energy comes from fish offal and protein in discarded meal packs, and it cannot maintain long rests in the shade without sealed water free of recontamination.

When rust on the rings freezes, the metal sounds stop and reunion slows, so it reduces its own movement on nights when rain or loading-area moisture wets the rings.

If HC03 seals discarded protein too tightly, this individual is pushed out without being able to sidestep into the market alleys.

### Life and Maintenance

Its coat sheds each season, and it tears salt and scales caught between the rings with its teeth.

If the rings are cut off during forced capture, it wanders for days trying to find the leading adult by scent alone; meanwhile, the family with young keeps to its own territory and refuses proposals.

If territorial defense grows at the expense of breeding, only the escort radius narrows; no command authority emerges.

### Behavior and Hierarchy

When the leading adult and two accompanying adults propose moving first, the Rust-Ring Escort takes the left flank, distinguishing carts from human scent.

Families with young may not follow this individual's metal sounds, and even if H03 records them as an aggressive cluster, the HC03 mediator separates them again by tags, scent, and companionship.

### Escalation

At stage 1, it shakes its rings only at a particular tag and meal-cart engine sound near the edge of the open ground.

At stage 2, when a familiar idle gathers several families into one passage, it follows beside the convoy cart, guarding its flank.

After a stage 3 feeding cutoff or deceptive capture, it joins a dispersed regrouping that occupies the transfer stairs and market entrance at once, apart from the leading adult.

### Engagement and Response

Blocking fences, noise reduction, and flags marking young-animal territory take priority over direct fire.

If the metal sounds are used as false bait, it will no longer shake its rings even for later rescue calls; capture must be limited to individuals that actually led an attack and to the injured.

Success is measured not by removals but by zero citizen bite injuries, reduced minutes of loading delay, and the rate at which families gather again in the same shade.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice

When HC03 trades over night feeding times and loading access windows, the choice is whether to use the Rust-Ring Escort's metal sound as a lure or wait until individual identification is complete.

The lure clears the passage quickly but burns rescue trust, while identification delays loading.

The moment old guard records are entered in a punishment ledger, this individual's flank remembers human scent only as a threat.

### Scenario Links

In G03-SC1, the companionship of the overlapping-ring individual must be distinguished among three incompletely read tags.

In G03-SC2, an old meal-cart engine sound draws the escort radius onto the loading route; in G03-SC3, it takes the outer edge of the dispersed regrouping around the cold-storage approach.

/monster_contents/M005/entries/1/bestiar.en: The Loading-Shadow Keeper is a resting body that protects the shade area of the Noryangjin Line loading zone itself. It is an animal that slips to market eaves when the shade, rather than the place, is taken away.

/monster_contents/M005/entries/1/prose.en:
### Role and Body

On the ground where the Noryangjin Line night-loading shade meets the lingering cold-storage draft, the Loading-Shadow Keeper has a short,

broad body and wet paw pads that fix its resting place.

Unlike a moving guard dog, this individual protects the shade area itself; if people take away the shade, its sleeping place slips to the eaves of a market alley rather than disappearing.

It has only one collar ring, but a corroded tag catches on its foot and makes the sound of a shade boundary, not an individual number.

### Origin

After feeding times ended at a private shelter that had closed its doors, a small family that found both thawing smells and shade under a loading-area awning fixed this spot as its sleeping place.

The fictional UHF tag preserves only a former pen number; its current home is defined by the shade and the sealed-water container.

### Habitat

Its core is the downwind shade of the Noryangjin Line loading zone; when daytime crowds thicken, it retreats only as far as a drain entrance.

It does not make a daily round trip to the Yongsan Line open ground. When XT03 vibrations grow strong, it gives up the shade, presses against the cold-storage wall, and follows only the temperature.

### Needs

Water free of recontamination and shade area, more than leftover protein, set its density limit.

If HC03 leaves discarded protein unsecured, families overcrowd the shade and human contact increases; if sealing is tightened, this individual loses the shade and slips to the eaves of a children's passage.

### Life and Maintenance

If the shade disappears for three days in a row, it moves its sleeping place; if the water is contaminated, it laps thaw-water puddles, then abandons the area at the smell of disinfectant.

Breeding is attempted only in seasons when the shade is stable; after forced removal, it returns beneath the same pillar around individuals whose tags remain.

### Behavior and Hierarchy

Even if it receives a proposal from the leading adult, it will not follow while its young are in the shade.

If a loading cart brushes the shade, it gives only a low warning; in a union without command authority, this individual has only the right to refuse its place.

### Escalation

At stage 1, it responds only to a meal cart at the edge of the shade.

At stage 2, when engine sounds are reproduced, families follow as far as the loading route outside the shade; at stage 3, after feeding stops, they leave the shade and occupy the transfer stairs and cold-storage approach at once.

### Engagement and Response

Removing the entire shade only moves the home into an alley.

It is safer to put feeding detours and young-animal flags beside the shade; bending the loading route is safer, and success is measured by time spent in the shade and zero bite injuries.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice

If the awning is removed to speed loading, citizen passage opens briefly, but families without shade are pushed into the market.

If the shade remains, density gathers in one place and contact risk persists.

The moment this home is used for speculative storage, the negotiation window closes.

### Scenario Links

The tag comparison in G03-SC1 asks whether companionship in a shared sleeping place under the shade counts as the current family.

In G03-SC2, engine sounds draw the shaded home onto the loading route; in G03-SC3, families that gave up the shade surround the cold-storage approach.

/monster_contents/M005/entries/2/bestiar.en: The Underpass Sleeper marks its daytime sleeping place beneath the Yongsan Line viaduct with urine. Unlike the Loading-Shadow Keeper, it occupies a hiding place from daytime crowds, not a nighttime loading area.

/monster_contents/M005/entries/2/prose.en:
### Role and Body

On a dry ledge where the underside of the Yongsan Line viaduct meets a drain, the Underpass Sleeper marks its daytime sleeping place with its long body and mud-caked claws.

Unlike the Loading-Shadow Keeper, this home is a hiding place from daytime crowds, not a nighttime loading zone; even when territorial urine is washed away, it appears again at the same pillar root.

### Origin

A companion animal separated during the crowd evacuation followed a drain outside the research-facility wall and entered beneath the viaduct; it made concrete cooling and shade humidity, rather than metal sounds, the conditions for a sleeping place.

The old residence code on its tag is only a clue; companionship beneath the pillar is its current territory.

### Habitat

Its core is beneath the Yongsan Line viaduct, and even when loading leftovers increase it does not descend to S08 every day.

When rain fills the drain, it moves one ledge higher; on days when XT03 vibrations shake the pillar, it temporarily leaves its sleeping place.

### Needs

Sealed water, a dry ledge, and little lingering disinfectant are the costs of maintaining it.

Meal packs left in the open ground provide enough protein, but if the water is recontaminated, it abandons its sleeping place and climbs to the shade on the transfer stairs.

### Life and Maintenance

When mud on the ledge hardens, it scrapes with its claws to make ventilation holes; when a disinfection vehicle passes, it leaves for a day.

During weeks when it has young, it refuses the leading adult's loading proposal and guards the pillar root.

### Behavior and Hierarchy

It has no command authority and keeps only the hours of access to its sleeping place.

Even if H03 counts all animals beneath the viaduct as one cluster, HC03 separates families by urine locations and numbers of young.

### Escalation

At stage 1, it appears only briefly at a meal cart on the edge of the open ground.

At stage 2, when engine sounds ring through the security passage, families beneath the viaduct are drawn to the loading route; at stage 3 they occupy the transfer stairs after abandoning the sleeping place.

### Engagement and Response

Driving it out from beneath the viaduct with water only moves the sleeping place to the transfer stairs.

Leaving urine markers beside detour arrows and dividing passage reduces conflict; blanket disinfection fixes the smell of disinfectant in memory as a threat.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice

If the markers are erased for daytime passage, people have an easier time, but the dogs lose their boundaries and meet on the stairs.

If the markers remain as rules, citizens must take detours.

Using the sleeping place to store honeycomb cuts the reporting network.

### Scenario Links

G03-SC1 turns on whether companionship beneath the viaduct takes priority over the shelter code.

The engine sound in G03-SC2 shakes even this sleeping place, and in G03-SC3 the abandoned underpass becomes the starting point for regrouping on the transfer stairs.

/monster_contents/M005/entries/3/bestiar.en: The Torn Name Tag is an injured individual whose tag was torn on a cart. Its irregular metal-scrap sound gathers companions, but the machine ledger cannot confirm an owner.

/monster_contents/M005/entries/3/prose.en:
### Role and Body

One side of the Torn Name Tag's collar has broken off.

Its passive UHF tag is flipped against wet fur, making it a medium-sized dog in an injured state that H03 may count twice or miss entirely within two meters.

With every step the broken metal scrap makes an irregular sound: companions gather, but the machine ledger cannot confirm an owner.

### Origin

On a night when different shelter codes were read at the edge of the loading area, its tag was torn when it caught on a cart.

The damage was an accident, not a mutation, and subsequent regrouping continues only through sound and scent.

### Habitat

It moves between the Noryangjin Line loading edge and the Yongsan Line open ground, but chooses shade by a drain because tags are missed more often beside metal fences.

It avoids the transfer stairs in the daytime crowds.

### Needs

It needs thawed protein and sealed water, but approaches only when the gesture of someone correcting the tag's orientation coincides with a familiar feeding cart.

The smell of unfamiliar gloves is more threatening than food.

### Life and Maintenance

The broken ring does not regenerate, and growing fur hides the tag further.

Readability is worst when wet after disinfection; before it dries, the ledger gains one more ghost individual.

### Behavior and Hierarchy

It follows the leading adult, but its irregular metal sound makes families with young stop first.

It cannot establish a hierarchy; the sound of damage itself is both a regrouping signal and a cause of mistaken readings.

### Escalation

At stage 1, incomplete readings show three codes at once.

At stage 2, if the damaged sound mixes with the engine noise, several families attach to one cart; after deceptive capture at stage 3, this sound alone brings the stairs and market under simultaneous occupation.

### Engagement and Response

If the damaged tag is forcibly removed, the individual permanently refuses rescue calls.

It is safer to wait for comparison of appearance and companionship, and to use a feeding cart to keep a little distance.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice

The question for this individual is what to register: the former owner in electronic records or the animal family it sleeps with now.

Waiting for comparison delays loading; separating them with a cart leaves behind young unable to follow the damaged sound, while prioritizing current ties conflicts with later return claims.

### Scenario Links

It is at the center of G03-SC1, 'Rusty Name Tags'; in G03-SC2, its damaged sound overlaps engine noise and compounds misreading, and in G03-SC3 it becomes a dispersed marker that prevents the ledger from counting them as one main group.

/monster_contents/M005/entries/4/bestiar.en: The Slow Leading Adult is an elderly leader with stiff joints, carrying forward through aging the place of the 'longest-lived medium-sized dog,' as does Iron-Step. It steps toward the loading wind only when two companions stay beside it.

/monster_contents/M005/entries/4/prose.en:
### Role and Body

The Slow Leading Adult is the longest-surviving medium adult in the Abandoned-Dog Iron Pack; it proposes movement first but has no permanent command authority.

Its hind legs are stiff and its rings rusted to a low sound; it steps toward the loading wind only when two accompanying adults stay beside it.

### Origin

It is an individual that remained in the open ground outside the Magok wall after passing through private shelters, construction sites, and evacuation columns; when feeding schedules stabilized, it increased territorial defense rather than breeding.

Its fictional tag history preserves several pen numbers, but its present standing is only age and companionship.

### Habitat

It uses the shaded tunnel in the Yongsan Line open ground as a daytime sleeping place, descending slowly to the Noryangjin Line entrance only on nights when loading runs late.

On days with strong XT03 vibrations, it makes no proposal and stays in the tunnel.

### Needs

Soft protein, sealed water, and short travel distances are conditions for its upkeep.

If feeding stops, its proposals shift toward the market alleys, and crowded loading areas further injure its joints.

### Life and Maintenance

Aging reduces the number of round trips it makes along the loading route; if its companions disappear, it sweeps the same scent axis repeatedly for nearly 48 hours.

If reorganization is forced based only on tags left after capture, families with young scatter first.

### Behavior and Hierarchy

It makes proposals, but the territory of families with young can refuse them.

Even if H03 marks this individual as a controller, the HC03 mediator separates them again by companionship, and does not record orders to slaughter.

### Escalation

At stage 1, it slowly approaches only familiar carts at the edge of the open ground.

At stage 2, it comes onto the loading route with two companions at the engine sound; at stage 3, when feeding stops, its proposal ends in failure to divide the passage, and the stairs and market are occupied at once.

### Engagement and Response

If the elderly individual is captured first, the pack is dispersed, not dissolved.

Detour carts, extended shade, and short access windows take priority; success is measured by the share of cases where the leader comes out of the tunnel and its family follows.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice

The choice is whether to wait for the slow proposal to keep loading moving, or capture the injured or elderly without killing to open the passage quickly.

Waiting delays food; capture burns trust and kills rescue calls.

Concentrating this individual's trust in one original driver also leaves a vulnerability.

### Scenario Links

In G03-SC1, it is the subject of comparison between an old tag and the current leader's position; in G03-SC2, it is the center that remembers the engine sound; in G03-SC3, the question rests on this individual: whether to open district feeding without slaughter even after its proposal is refused.

/monster_contents/M005/entries/5/bestiar.en: The Cart-Side Dog is a coexisting body with a shoulder shaped to the spokes of a feeding cart. If that person disappears, it refuses food or bites tires; it is a knot of trust, not a commander.

/monster_contents/M005/entries/5/prose.en:
### Role and Body

The Cart-Side Dog is a coexisting type with a soft mouth, a low-wagging tail, and a familiar shoulder scar from the spokes of a feeding cart.

It learned to treat human gestures and a particular engine's idle as safety, but if that person disappears, it refuses food or bites the cart tires.

### Origin

It survived by following a meal cart through a closed security passage; the fictional regrouping rule placed vehicle sounds and cart smells on the same level as signs of companions.

It does not provide grounds to blame real shelters.

### Habitat

It moves with a cart between the Yongsan Line security-passage entrance and the Noryangjin Line loading route; by day, when no cart is present, it hides beneath the viaduct.

It does not enter children's passages on its own, but that boundary breaks when feeding stops.

### Needs

It needs the familiar wheel sound of a cart, meal packs at set times, and human scent weaker than disinfectant.

If a mobile feeding station changes its place every day, it follows, but the cost of refrigeration labor is shifted onto people.

### Life and Maintenance

It learns a new driver's scent over several days; during that time, loading volume must be reduced to lower aggression.

After one deceptive capture, it will not approach even the same cart.

### Behavior and Hierarchy

It looks to the cart before the leading adult and yields the place beside the cart to families with young.

It is a knot of trust, not a commander; if that knot is concentrated in one person, the whole union becomes vulnerable.

### Escalation

At stage 1, it attaches only to a particular cart.

At stage 2, reproducing the engine sound gathers scattered families onto the loading route; at stage 3, feeding stops and they occupy stairs without carts.

### Engagement and Response

If the cart is used as bait for a pen, a coexisting type immediately becomes hostile.

There are three paths: find the original driver, gradually acclimate a new driver, or use a mobile feeding station without engine noise. A gun muzzle is no solution.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice

Dependence on the original driver clears the passage immediately, but one person's absence breaks the agreement.

Retraining costs several days of lost loading, while a silent feeding station preserves the trust signal but requires daily labor and refrigeration.

If trust is treated as a consumable, every rescue that follows is powerless.

### Scenario Links

It is central to G03-SC2, 'The Pack That Remembers the Meal Cart'; during the tag comparison in G03-SC1, companionship beside the cart is evidence, and in G03-SC3 it remains the knot that opens family-specific feeding zones.

/monster_contents/M005/entries/6/bestiar.en: The Transfer Regrouping Core is not a single tyrant but a boss phase created when the sounds of several families overlap at the cold-storage approach. H03 logs it as one colony, but each family's right to refuse is stronger than the leading proposal.

/monster_contents/M005/entries/6/prose.en:
### Role and Body

The Transfer Regrouping Core is not one tyrant but the central adult in a scenario boss phase that forms when the tag sounds and scents of several families overlap at the cold-storage

approach.

Its build is medium, but the metal sounds ring all at once: overlapping rings, damage sounds, and the low sound of the leader. H03's log records it as a single colony.

### Origin

This phase formed on a night when XT03 freight vibrations and a feeding cutoff coincided, as small families from the Magok open ground, Noryangjin loading area, and beneath the viaduct encircled the same approach.

It is a created regrouping network, not a legendary leader's bloodline.

### Habitat

At the highest stage it occupies the Noryangjin Line cold-storage approach and the transfer-stair landing at once; in ordinary times it disperses again into the shaded Yongsan Line tunnel.

The core is invisible among daytime crowds.

### Needs

Without family-specific feeding zones, sealed reserves, and shade to care for injured individuals, the core does not disperse but spreads into a wider living sphere.

Even pouring protein in one place only increases overcrowding if territories are not divided.

### Life and Maintenance

This phase measures not the lifespan of an individual but the duration of broken trust.

Unless engine sounds and carts are retired for a period after deceptive capture, the core gathers again at the same time.

### Behavior and Hierarchy

There is no fixed command; each family's right to refuse is stronger than the leader's proposal.

Even if sensors count them as one, the mediator must split them by sleeping places, number of young, and times of access.

### Escalation

Though it may seem to skip stages 1 and 2, in fact it is the end result of accumulated memory checks and regroupings.

At stage 3, the market entrance, transfer stairs, and cold-storage approach are blocked at once, while gunfire only expands the living sphere.

### Engagement and Response

Blanket capture and orders to slaughter are close to prohibited.

Family-specific feeding zones, nonlethal capture of only the injured, and moving night loading to another cold-storage site are the three response pillars; results are measured by passage recovery speed and the rate of regrouping with zero bite injuries.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice

District operations preserve the animals' social memory but consume rationing labor and stored supplies.

Limited capture reduces damage to trust but slows passage recovery, while moving loading increases merchants' cold-storage costs.

The moral cost is whether the animals' current families can be erased for people's right of passage.

### Scenario Links

This is the boss phase of G03-SC3, 'Regrouping on the Transfer Stairs,' formed by the overlap of tag misreadings in G03-SC1 and engine-sound learning in G03-SC2.

Choosing to extend only the shaded tunnel, without recording an order to slaughter, is the lower bound of coexistence.

/monster_contents/M005/entries/7/bestiar.en: The Strait-Loading Dog is a regional branch that sets its night routes by the Noryangjin Line's salt wind and XT03 vibrations, not Magok dust. It does not always follow the open-ground leader's proposal; small families along the loading axis set their own times.

/monster_contents/M005/entries/7/prose.en:
### Role and Body

The Strait-Loading Dog is a regional variant that extended its night routes to match the salt wind of seafood loading on the Noryangjin Line and XT03 freight vibrations, rather than the dry dust of Magok open ground.

Its paw pads are always wet and its tags corrode quickly; it responds to cold-storage thaw smells before families near the research-facility wall.

### Origin

As vibrations from the Strait Three Routes grew stronger, a small family expanded along the loading-area entrance. It uses the same Iron Pack name but does not share sleeping places with the open-ground leader.

This is a fictional regional adaptation, not an explanation of any real port accident.

### Habitat

The core is the nighttime Noryangjin Line loading axis and the cold-storage walls; by day it hides in drains behind the market.

It climbs briefly to the Yongsan Line open ground only when leftovers diminish after a storm.

### Needs

Fish offal and cold-storage leftovers are its staple; when sealing is tightened, it immediately seeps into market alleys.

Sealed water is easily recontaminated by loading hoses, so it needs a separate shaded container.

### Life and Maintenance

Salt corrodes its rings quickly and raises their pitch; the sound diverges from that of open-ground families, slowing regrouping.

When the loading cycle stabilizes, entrance defense increases more than breeding; when vibrations stop, its routes shorten.

### Behavior and Hierarchy

It does not always follow the Magok leading adult's proposal; small families along the loading axis set their own movement times.

If H03 counts them as one pack, it misses their different escape directions.

### Escalation

Stage 1 is a tag response at the edge of the loading area; at stage 2, vibrations and engine noise crowd the entrance; at stage 3, a feeding cutoff grows into a blockade of the cold-storage approach.

If it breaks out at the same time as the open-ground group, it overlaps the transfer stairs as well.

### Engagement and Response

Moving an open-ground fence directly to the loading area only makes it slip on the wet floor.

Loading access windows, alley seals, and sealing of offal leftovers must be tied to the loading ledger; gunfire drives it into the market.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice

Recognizing this variant as a separate family increases feeding zones and raises merchant costs.

Counting it as one pack and driving it out all at once opens loading briefly, but children's passages become replacement habitat.

If the vibration timetable is made too public, a theft group can read which warehouses are empty.

### Scenario Links

It connects directly to the freight-vibration axis of G03-SC3, preserves a loading-area code among the differing shelter codes in G03-SC1, and transforms G03-SC2's engine-sound learning through loading hoses.

/monster_contents/M005/entries/8/bestiar.en: The Dry-Cavern Elder Female is a named controller, but has priority only over moving the young and passing narrow ledges, not over combat command. It reads pressure with its body before the pump starts and climbs first to the high ventilation room.

/monster_contents/M005/entries/8/prose.en:
### Role and Body

The Dry-Cavern Elder Female is a named controller of the Sewer-Raccoon Pack, but has priority only over moving the young and passing narrow chokepoints, not over combat command.

Its whiskers are long and pipe rust has seeped into its paw pads; it reads pressure changes with its body before the pump starts and climbs first to the high ventilation room.

### Origin

It is an elderly female of a family group that settled in a dry evacuation hollow beside a Ttukseom Union pump after inspection of the Jungnang and Tancheon mains stopped.

The rule that it knows water levels before the pumps is fictional and is not attributed to any real municipal accident.

### Habitat

Its core is the dry burrow in the connecting pipes of a Ttukseom Union pump station and an evacuation hollow beneath the workshop.

When flood levels rise, it moves the young to the underground transmission gallery of the Mapo Union; during an XT04 cold wave, it shares the only dry approach with other families.

### Needs

Aquatic food, organic waste, and carrion provide energy; low flow and dry hiding places are the costs of maintenance.

If HC04 skips dredging, the food film thickens and density rises; if it over-dredges, this female pushes its young toward the surface market.

### Life and Maintenance

In dry seasons, each family uses a separate hiding place and moves to the ventilation room at the pressure rise preceding rain.

If hiding places are flooded repeatedly, they abandon time-sharing and disperse into alleys.

Its priority comes from survival experience, not hereditary bloodline.

### Behavior and Hierarchy

It gives no combat orders to other families.

Even if H04's robot counts heat sources as one colony, the HC04 drainage watch separates them by sleeping places and access times; human visual inspection is final.

### Escalation

At stage 1, movement to the ventilation room before rain becomes an unofficial warning.

At stage 2, excrement and microbial film obscure the water-level sensor and bring it into conflict with the inspection robot; at stage 3, during a cold wave and flood, pump maintenance and evacuation compete for one dry pipe.

### Engagement and Response

Poison bait and complete flooding harm both downstream areas and workers through carcass decay.

Partial barriers, alternative hiding pipes, sensor cleaning, and nighttime surface-traffic limits are the baseline; success is measured by pump recovery time, sensor reliability, and zero surface bite injuries.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice

Adopting raccoon movement as an advance warning buys preparation time but leaves responsibility for false-alarm fuel use; waiting for HP01 sluice workers' measurements may be too late for a sudden inflow.

Preheating pumps only when the two signals differ saves fuel but misses short local cloudbursts.

The moral cost for this controller is whether public safety should rely on an unofficial ecological signal.

### Scenario Links

It drives the central movement of G04-SC1, 'An Early Indicator Beneath the Manhole'; in G04-SC2 it holds one family's priority in time-sharing that overlaps the dredging window; in the dry passage during the G04-SC3 cold wave, it forces a choice among a heated refuge pipe, delayed inspection, or an external foothold.

/monster_contents/M005/entries/9/bestiar.en: The Pipe-巡回 Raccoon is an ordinary adult that circles pipes by day and alleys within 50 meters of an exit at night. It recognizes the elder female's priority only at chokepoints and follows its own schedule elsewhere.

/monster_contents/M005/entries/9/prose.en:
### Role and Body

The Pipe巡回 Raccoon is an ordinary ecological type of the Sewer-Raccoon Pack, hiding in pipes beneath manholes by day and circling alleys within about 50 meters of an exit at night.

It reads currents and airflow through gaps with its whiskers, distinguishes pump vibrations from boot sounds by hearing, and is built not with combat claws but with wet fur and narrow shoulders.

### Origin

It is an ordinary adult in a family group that followed aquatic food, refuse, and carrion into a stormwater main abandoned by people.

Based on records of urban-stream sightings, it observes ecological patterns that affect pipe operations in 2126.

### Habitat

Its usual habitat is the low-flow pipes of the Ttukseom Union; when water levels rise, it disperses temporarily toward Mapo Union vents.

If a cold wave changes feed density, it moves to an eastern branch and returns to familiar pipes after the thaw.

### Needs

Microbial film, organic refuse, and carrion are food; without dry hiding places, it stays on the surface longer.

If dredging removes the food film all at once, this individual is among the first pushed into market alleys.

### Life and Maintenance

In dry seasons it circles only its family's feeding ground; after floods, families share the same main at different times.

A small body suited to narrow pipes may persist across generations, but is more vulnerable to surface crossings and cold waves.

Changing refuge within a few days is learned behavior, not heredity.

### Behavior and Hierarchy

It recognizes the elder female's priority only at chokepoints and follows its own schedule elsewhere.

Because robot logs confuse it with floating debris, it is not counted as a colony until a person confirms it.

### Escalation

At stage 1, it follows to a high ventilation room before rain; at stage 2, it encounters the inspection robot in pipes with obscured sensors; at stage 3, it overlaps the pump approach when only one dry pipe remains.

### Engagement and Response

Driving it from an alley only shortens its 50-meter patrol to residential doorways.

Dividing nighttime passage windows, opening alternative refuge pipes, and washing sensors are the response; culling worsens water quality.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice

Dividing the 50-meter alleys into no-passage windows inconveniences people but leaves raccoons in the pipes.

Driving them to the surface reduces complaints immediately but increases home intrusions.

Poisoning them out of disease fears endangers pipe workers and downstream drinking water alike, and loses an indicator species.

### Scenario Links

In G04-SC1 it builds the warning's density as an ordinary individual climbing after the female to the ventilation room; if the G04-SC2 dredging window breaks, it is the first wave into the surface market; in G04-SC3 it overlaps the dry passage as one of three families.

/monster_contents/M006/entries/0/bestiar.en: Current-Whiskers presses its belly to the low-flow floor beside a pump and reads the current with its whiskers. When a pipe fills, that same sense goes blind, setting its niche apart from surface patrols.

/monster_contents/M006/entries/0/prose.en:
- Role and body: An ordinary ecological member of the Sewer-Raccoon Pack, it presses its belly to the floor of a low-flow pipe beside a pump and reads the current's direction and strength with its whiskers. It is smaller than a surface adult, with wide paw pads suited to slippery concrete. It feels pressure changes in its paws and chest before water levels rise, but the same sense goes blind when the pipe fills or its air pocket breaks.
- Origin: After inspection of the Jungnang and Tancheon mains stopped following the collapse, it followed aquatic food into an abandoned pump branch of the Ttukseom Union's Sermon Registry State. The claim that it knows water levels before pumps is fictional family learning, not an accident involving a real institution.
- Habitat: By day it stays against the floor of slow-flow pipes and ledges beneath manholes; even at night it rarely goes toward exits. When flood levels rise it moves only to a higher joint in the same pipe; the Mapo Union gallery is outside its daily range.
- Needs: Small aquatic prey and microbial film on pipe walls are its staples, and a gentle current must persist to conserve swimming energy. If disinfectant runs strong, its whiskers dull for days and it loses track of food.
- Life and maintenance: In dry seasons it repeatedly follows one branch and rubs its whiskers to remove debris. If continuous rain lifts the floor, it moves its own body to a joint before moving its young; after the thaw it returns to familiar low-flow sections.
- Behavior and hierarchy: It gives no combat commands and yields only when the elder female passes a narrow ledge. Even if H04 Gangbyeol's log marks it as floating debris, the HC04 drainage watch must distinguish it again by access times and sleeping places.
- Escalation: At stage 1 it clings to a joint before rain and becomes an unofficial early signal. At stage 2, excrement accumulates in the same pipe, the official water gauge reads low, and its nose meets the inspection robot. At stage 3, the remaining low-flow section overlaps the maintenance workers' foothold.
- Engagement and response: Poison bait and complete flooding ruin downstream areas through carcass decay. Temporarily lowering flow with a partial barrier, washing the sensor, and opening a bypass pipe lets Current-Whiskers return to its familiar floor and reduces pump recovery time.
- Negotiation and moral choice: Adopting this individual's movement to a joint as an advance warning buys preparation time, but responsibility for fuel used on false alarms remains with the Ttukseom Union and HC04. Waiting only for HP01 sluice workers' field measurements is too late for a short inflow; preheating pumps only when the two signals differ saves ordinary fuel but misses simultaneous delays. Its reading of the current cannot be grounds for punishment.
- Scenario link: In G04-SC1, 'An Early Indicator Beneath the Manhole,' daytime movement to a joint appears before the official sensor.

/monster_contents/M006/entries/1/bestiar.en: The Fifty-Meter Nightwalker patrols above ground only at night, covering about 50 meters of alley from a manhole exit. It is poor at reading whiskers on deep pipe floors and retreats straight into the pipe if it crosses that boundary.

/monster_contents/M006/entries/1/prose.en:
- Role and body: An ordinary ecological member of the Sewer-Raccoon Pack, it patrols above ground only at night, circling alleys about 50 meters from a manhole exit. Its hind claws suit wet asphalt, and at the entrance its ears distinguish pump vibrations from people's boots. It is poor at reading whiskers on deep pipe floors.
- Origin: It came from a family that formed a surface circuit around exit refuse and market leftovers in a year when food inside the pipes dwindled. It became the face of fears that sewage would backflow into living areas, but is not a scout for an underground army.
- Habitat: By day it hides in dry shade below an exit ledge; at night it circles only within 50 meters of the workshop alleys of the Ttukseom Union and the alleys toward the Mapo Union transmission site. If it crosses that line, exposure to dogs and vehicles drives it straight back into the pipe.
- Needs: Nighttime refuse and carrion are its staples; it needs a dry ledge with an unblocked exit to maintain its circuit. If dredging lifts the exit all at once, the circuit extends deeper into the market.
- Life and maintenance: If the pads on its feet crack, it stays off the surface for a while and waits for leftovers on the ledge. When alleys freeze in a cold wave, it folds its circuit and stays inside the entrance; on the first thawed night, it steps on the same corner again to check its route.
- Behavior and hierarchy: It shares emergence times with the family that uses the same exit; who goes first is decided after the elder female passes. It forms no combat formation and breaks off its circuit midway when boot sounds approach.
- Escalation: At stage 1, it leaves only footprints at an alley corner. At stage 2, the dredging window overlaps the access time and two families emerge into the market together. At stage 3, repeated flooding of the exit breaks the 50-meter rule and pushes it into passageways.
- Engagement and response: Limiting nighttime surface passage to within 50 meters of the exit and opening an alternative dry ledge reduces market intrusion. Poison bait endangers alley dogs and sanitation workers alike; success is measured by zero surface bite injuries.
- Negotiation and moral choice: Closing the night market early shortens its circuit but reduces merchants' selling hours. Keeping passage open reduces complaints but increases responsibility for simultaneous emergence during the next dredging. Fixing the Fifty-Meter Nightwalker's circuit as a prohibited line and recognizing its feeding hours are not the same cost.
- Scenario link: In G04-SC2, 'Two Families in the Dredging Window,' a broken timetable extends this individual's 50-meter circuit into market complaints.

/monster_contents/M006/entries/2/bestiar.en: The Dredging-Time Keeper has memorized the intervals of HC04's nighttime dredging vibrations through its ears and paws. Without combat orders, when it vacates a branch first, families in the same window read that absence.

/monster_contents/M006/entries/2/prose.en:
- Role and body: A specialized member of the Sewer-Raccoon Pack, it remembers the intervals of nighttime dredging vibrations from HC04, the Ttukseom Heat-Source House, through its ears and paw pads. Sediment dust on its shoulders visibly shows the date of the last dredging; if the equipment's entry rhythm is off, it immediately changes its hiding direction.
- Origin: This is the result of a family that survived repeated dredging noise learning a safe timetable. It did not inherit a clock; it remembers how an individual that saw a missed window become a death site taught the others the vibration rhythm.
- Habitat: It moves between the Ttukseom Union main branch visited by dredging equipment and the vacant branch entrance beside it. By day, when there is no construction, it sleeps at that entrance; when vibrations begin, it briefly moves toward the Mapo Union.
- Needs: Organic sediment and aquatic leftovers accumulated between dredgings make its feeding calendar. If the schedule is unexpectedly advanced, food and hiding places disappear together.
- Life and maintenance: After memorizing one season's vibration cycle, it tests the first equipment of the next season by avoiding it. After three exposures to an incorrect rhythm, it abandons that main; returning requires a quiet night after the thaw.
- Behavior and hierarchy: It gives no combat orders to other families. But if it vacates a branch first, families using the same time window read that absence. Even if H04 counts several movement points as one colony, the Dredging-Time Keeper's access times must be logged separately.
- Escalation: At stage 1, it appears only as a branch emptying before equipment enters. At stage 2, nighttime dredging overlaps with rotational hiding, pushing two families above ground. At stage 3, equipment is concentrated into one window regardless of the timetable, breaking the shared rules.
- Engagement and response: Dividing dredging into two sections and keeping vibration warnings on the same rhythm lets this individual retreat to a branch. Concentrated dredging is faster but increases simultaneous appearances during later rain.
- Negotiation and moral choice: Matching dredging times to raccoon memory delays completion and increases night labor. Buying off one family's time slot with food and clearing it is fastest, but unfairly breaks the rotation another family kept. Whether to put the Time Keeper's memory on the work calendar is a matter of fairness in HC04's ledger.
- Scenario link: The nighttime window of G04-SC2, 'Two Families in the Dredging Window,' is triggered when it overlaps the vibration intervals this individual memorized.

/monster_contents/M006/entries/3/bestiar.en: The Biofilm Forager eats microbial film off pipe walls, leaving residue that obscures the official water-level gauge. It is not a weapon attacking sensors but a forager seeking thick film.

/monster_contents/M006/entries/3/prose.en:
- Role and body: A specialist member of the sewer raccoon clan, it uses its nose and forepaws to scrape biofilm and piles of waste from pipe walls and eat them. This food film can obscure official water-quality and water-level sensors, but the animal itself is a forager seeking thick film, not a weapon that attacks sensors.
- Origin: When the film thickened in a section where HC04 had postponed sediment dredging, a foraging habit favoring film over aquatic food took hold within the family. This was not sabotage intended to cultivate the film.
- Habitat: It stays beneath sensor housings and in sediment pockets with almost no current. If the film washes away, it moves to another housing in the same pipe; if excessive dredging exposes the bottom, it is driven toward surface garbage.
- Needs: Thick organic film and microbes on carcasses provide all its energy. When disinfectant concentrations rise, its nasal lining cannot distinguish food quality for several days. Without a dry shelter, it loses body heat while eating film with wet fur.
- Life cycle and upkeep: It strips film from the edges of housings with its incisors. Once its teeth wear down, it eats only the softer film downstream. After clearing a housing, it rests for several days while the film regrows; that gap is a brief window in which sensor reliability recovers.
- Behavior and hierarchy: It does not command other families, only claims spots where the film is thick. It climbs down from a housing when an elder female passes. A point that an H04 robot marks as debris must be viewed three times by a person with a flashlight to distinguish a forager from floating debris.
- Escalation: At stage 1, sensor readings come back consistently low. At stage 2, the cleaning crew and a forager meet at the same housing, halting inspection. At stage 3, scraping away the film all at once sends the family spilling into the market.
- Engagement and response: Clean the sensors and partially block the water first, leaving film in one section to create an alternative feeding route. Flooding the entire area and using poisoned bait make the film of decomposing carcasses thicker. The measures of success are sensor reliability and the delay in pump decisions.
- Negotiation and moral choice: Frequent housing cleaning restores pump decision-making but removes both the film forager's staple food and its shelter. Delaying cleaning reduces conflict over food, but makes official water-level readings false, putting the early warning signs in G04-SC1 at odds with instrument readings. Whether to recognize the film as a resource is a matter of putting drainage safety and foraging ecology on the same ledger, not a matter of disgust.
- Scenario connection: In G04-SC1, an obscured water-level gauge forces a wait for on-site measurement. In G04-SC2, dredging removes the film all at once and pushes the foragers to the surface.

/monster_contents/M006/entries/4/bestiar.en: The litter-carrier mother is a caregiving animal that responds to pre-rain pressure changes by carrying her young to a ventilation room in her mouth. She uses her right of way only for this task and does not take feeding grounds from other families.

/monster_contents/M006/entries/4/prose.en:
- Role and body: A specialist member of the sewer raccoon clan, she senses pressure changes before rain and carries her young by mouth, gripping them by the scruff, to a higher ventilation room. She uses an elder female's right of way only for this task and does not give combat orders to other family members. Folds like a chest pouch hold her young's body heat against her wet fur.
- Origin: Mothers that lost young left in low-lying pipes during floods established a place within the family for moving them to ventilation rooms as soon as they sensed pressure changes before the pumps started. This is a learned sequence of movements that aided survival, not a genetic change that occurred in days.
- Habitat: She relies chiefly on the floor of the ventilation room beside the Ttukseom Union pumps and the dry ladder leading up to it. If the ventilation room floods, she leads her line of young onto high cable supports in the Mapo Union gallery.
- Needs: She needs a high space where her young can dry off and nearby scraps to make up for the brief interruption in feeding while she moves them. Closing a vent because of the smell diverts her carrying route into the alleys.
- Life cycle and upkeep: The strength of her neck determines how many young she can move from one litter. When exhausted, she leaves one on an intermediate ledge and makes a return trip. If the ventilation room freezes during a cold snap, she stops moving and endures by covering them with the folds of her body.
- Behavior and hierarchy: She asserts right of way only at narrow passage points and does not take other families' feeding grounds. If people are in the ventilation room, she routes her line of young around them. Even if H04 displays people, young, and debris as a single heat spot, no team should be sent out before visual confirmation.
- Escalation: At stage 1, young climb to the ventilation room during the day, before any rain. At stage 2, closing the ventilation room puts their route across a work platform. At stage 3, the only dry space left is the pump access route, bringing maintenance and caregiving into conflict.
- Engagement and response: An alternative shelter pipe and limited opening of the ventilation room come first. Flooding the entire area kills the line of young at once and worsens water quality as their bodies decay. Success means zero surface bites and surviving young, not the number captured.
- Negotiation and moral choice: Using the mother's daytime movement as an advance warning partially entrusts public safety to informal caregiving behavior. Closing the ventilation room and waiting only for HP01 measurements provides clear evidence, but brings the young into the alleys. A compromise of preheating the pumps only when the two signals differ saves fuel, but leaves a gap in which people act only after the mother has already moved them.
- Scenario connection: G04-SC1, ‘The Leading Indicator Beneath the Manhole,’ begins with this animal carrying her young to the ventilation room during the day.

/monster_contents/M006/entries/5/bestiar.en: The shift-change burrow keeper maintains the time-sharing arrangement between two families using the same main pipe by blocking the way with its body. It has no combat command authority; outside its family's allotted window, it lies across the entrance only to slow passage.

/monster_contents/M006/entries/5/prose.en:
- Role and body: The sewer raccoon clan's first elite, it maintains the time-sharing arrangement between two families using the same main pipe through scent marks and by blocking the way with its body. It has no combat command authority; outside its family's allotted window, it lies across the entrance only to slow passage. The scent from its neck glands fades after a few hours, so it does not create permanent territory.
- Origin: After a flood thickened the food film and multiple families began using one pipe, the habit of the first arrivals guarding their allotted window grew strong in this animal. It is not a crowned ruler, but a keeper of the shift rule in its body.
- Habitat: It stays below the branch manhole where the Ttukseom Union main pipe splits toward the Mapo Union route, retreating to a dry refuge chamber when its window ends. If dredging begins in violation of the windows, it is pushed toward the surface market along with both families.
- Needs: It needs enough body scent to maintain its marks, and film and scraps to eat between windows. If one window is bought out, leaving only one family, it loses its role and disperses into the alleys.
- Life cycle and upkeep: It renews the scent line two or three times a day. If rain washes it away, it abandons the shift arrangement for that night. If an injury prevents it from lying across the entrance, another adult guards it temporarily, but the rule soon loosens.
- Behavior and hierarchy: It always makes way for an elder female moving her young. Otherwise, it asserts only its family's allotted window. If H04 merges two heat sources into one point, HC04 must separate them again using their entry and exit times.
- Escalation: At stage 1, only the shifts at the branch entrance are visible. At stage 2, nighttime dredging disrupts both windows at once, prompting complaints from both sides of the market. At stage 3, after one window is bought out, the remaining family abandons the rule.
- Engagement and response: If dredging is divided into two sections, the shift-change burrow keeper renews its marks. Opening an alternative dry pipe reduces competition for the entrance but reduces spare cable space for the Mapo Union. Flooding the entrance drives entire families into the alleys; it does not merely end the rule.
- Negotiation and moral choice: Buying one family's time slot with food and a safe passage makes construction fastest, but turns the fair window the burrow keeper guarded into a transaction. Split dredging delays completion, while the alternative pipe trades away communications capacity. Pursuing efficiency alone increases simultaneous surface appearances during the next rain.
- Scenario connection: In G04-SC2, ‘Two Families in the Dredging Window,’ both families surface at once when this animal's branch mark is broken.

/monster_contents/M006/entries/6/bestiar.en: During an XT04 cold snap, the thaw-path guide uses its paw pads and whiskers to find an unfrozen passage first. It cannot summon other families, but several follow it onto the dry ledge where it stops.

/monster_contents/M006/entries/6/prose.en:
- Role and body: The sewer raccoon clan's second elite, it uses its paw pads and whiskers to distinguish ice from residual warmth on pipe walls and find an unfrozen passage first during an XT04 cold snap. It cannot summon other families, but several follow it onto the dry ledge where it stops. Its surface crossings are brief and clumsy.
- Origin: During a winter when cold from the Tumen River–Far East theater and a logistics disruption changed the distribution of feed, an animal that survived when only an unfrozen pump access route remained passed its memory of warmth on through family learning. It has no history of claiming to be a commander.
- Habitat: During cold-snap weeks, it moves between the residual heating in the Mapo Union Yeouido Investment Union's underground gallery and the dry access route to the Ttukseom Union pump room. When thawing begins, it returns along the eastern branch line as though guiding others back to a familiar pipe.
- Needs: Unfrozen ground and a little residual heat are central to its survival; it chooses dry space before food. Cutting the gallery's heat brings three families together on a single pump access route.
- Life cycle and upkeep: When cracks in its paw pads deepen, it becomes slower to detect ice and spends a season on the branch line alone. The first warm water after the thaw offers a chance to wash its wounds, but if it arrives too quickly, it floods the access route again.
- Behavior and hierarchy: What looks like leading is a search for warmth, not an order. It yields its route when an elder female moves her young. Even if H04 merges them into one heat spot, HC04 records the number of families and their entry and exit times separately.
- Escalation: At stage 1, tracks appear first toward the gallery. At stage 2, diminished residual heat causes their use of the access route to overlap. At stage 3, three families block the only dry passage to the pumps, stopping maintenance.
- Engagement and response: Temporarily opening a heated shelter pipe and restricting nighttime surface travel disperses their routes. Poisoned bait and flooding add bodies that have frozen to death. A temporary external inspection platform permits maintenance without clearing the passage, but the work crew bears the risk of falling in the cold snap.
- Negotiation and moral choice: Opening part of the gallery's heating as shared shelter requires other Mapo Union facilities to give up power. Postponing pump inspection avoids a clash but increases flood risk during a thaw or sudden rain. Whether to use the guide's memory of warmth as an official detour hinges on the inability to secure both city drainage and nonhuman refuge at once.
- Scenario connection: In G04-SC3, ‘The Dry Passage to the Pump Room,’ three families converge on the access route where this animal first stops.

/monster_contents/M006/entries/7/bestiar.en: The dry refuge keeper braces its shoulders inside the dry refuge chamber beneath the Ttukseom Union pump station, filling the space so other families cannot enter all at once. It is not a fixed command post but an animal guarding dry storage space with a low current.

/monster_contents/M006/entries/7/prose.en:
- Role and body: An environmental-stronghold type of the sewer raccoon clan, this burrow keeper has settled into the dry refuge chamber beneath the Ttukseom Union Seolgyo Myeongbujeong pump station, where its body fits closely. Its shoulders catch against a ceiling joint, physically filling the chamber so other families cannot enter all at once. It senses airflow with its flanks more than with its whiskers.
- Origin: A family that used a refuge chamber vacated by people as a dry-season sleeping place refused to give up the dry space even after sending its young to the high ventilation room during a flood, producing this stronghold animal. The chamber is not a fixed command post but dry, low-current storage space.
- Habitat: Its entire range is the dry shelf inside the refuge chamber and the ledge at its entrance. When the water rises above the entrance, it gives up the chamber and moves to the ventilation room. During a cold snap, the chamber adjoins the only unfrozen pump access route, putting it in the same space as maintenance workers.
- Needs: Staying dry itself saves energy, and it survives on the small amount of scraps washed into the chamber. Converting the chamber into a human-only inspection route shifts the cost of losing its stronghold onto the surface alleys.
- Life cycle and upkeep: It times its entries and exits by how long its fur takes to dry, and scrapes away floor dirt if dampness persists for more than two days. If the entrance floods repeatedly, it abandons the stronghold and the sharing arrangement.
- Behavior and hierarchy: Inside the chamber, the first arrival holds its place but does not drive others out by fighting. It yields the shelf when an elder female arrives with a line of young. A ‘debris’ point in the H04 log is corrected to burrow keeper only after visual confirmation by flashlight.
- Escalation: At stage 1, only fur and tracks appear at the refuge chamber entrance. At stage 2, an inspection robot and the burrow keeper meet at the entrance. At stage 3, a cold snap makes this dry chamber the only space available for both pump access and refuge.
- Engagement and response: Partial water blocking delays flooding at the entrance, while opening an alternative shelter pipe relieves pressure on the stronghold. Flooding the entire chamber opens access to the pumps immediately but increases incursions into surface homes. The measures of success are restored pump operation and zero surface bites.
- Negotiation and moral choice: Leaving the dry refuge chamber as an ecological buffer lengthens the maintenance route. Sealing it as a human-only shaft speeds drainage, but during a cold snap three families block the remaining access route. A temporary external platform avoids sharing the chamber, but someone must decide who bears the fall risk of installing it.
- Scenario connection: The competition for space in G04-SC3, ‘The Dry Passage to the Pump Room,’ intensifies when this stronghold remains unfrozen.

/monster_contents/M006/entries/8/bestiar.en: The cable-gap dweller has made a home in empty Mapo Union trays and gaps by the vents, forming a second dry shelter. It is not a group trying to seize the communications network, but a home for a family that dispersed when the water rose.

/monster_contents/M006/entries/8/prose.en:
- Role and body: An environmental-stronghold type of the sewer raccoon clan, it has made a home in spare trays and gaps by the vents of the Mapo Union Yeouido Investment Union's underground cable gallery. It moves with its belly raised to avoid getting oil on the cable sheathing. It does not respond to audible transmission frequencies, distinguishing only human boots from low-frequency pump sounds.
- Origin: A family dispersing from the Ttukseom Union pipes as the water rose discovered the gallery's dry warmth and empty trays and settled there. It is not a group trying to seize the communications network, but a second dry-shelter stronghold.
- Habitat: It lives among the empty cable tiers in the middle of the gallery and at the base of the vents, moving to tiers that retain residual heating during XT04 cold-snap weeks. If communications expansion fills the spare space, the stronghold is pushed back toward the pump access route.
- Needs: Dry warmth and organic scraps mixed into the dust beneath the trays sustain it. Opening this space as an alternative shelter pipe reduces surface appearances but reduces spare transmission cores.
- Life cycle and upkeep: It shakes cable dust from its fur in the vent breeze and vacates a tier for several days if it leaves scuff marks on the sheathing. If power rationing removes the residual heat, it abandons the stronghold and returns to the Ttukseom Union route.
- Behavior and hierarchy: Even in the gallery, it moves only with its own family and does not command other families. When an inspector shines a flashlight, it slips behind a tray. If H04 marks one heat source as a colony, the duty officer separates the sightings again by tier number.
- Escalation: At stage 1, only fur accumulates in the empty trays. At stage 2, a proposal for an alternative dry pipe trades this home against communications expansion. At stage 3, failure to share heating sends three families down to the pump passage.
- Engagement and response: Tape restricting nighttime surface travel and limited opening of designated tiers are effective. Clearing the gallery with toxic disinfectant damages both the cable sheathing and downstream water quality. Success is measured by transmission availability and surface bites, not removals.
- Negotiation and moral choice: Providing empty, dry trays as alternative shelter reduces market appearances in G04-SC2, but costs the Mapo Union communications headroom. Sharing heating only during cold-snap weeks makes other facilities endure the cold. Treating the cable-gap dweller solely as an illegal occupant sends the costs back to the pump room during the next dredging operation or cold snap.
- Scenario connection: The alternative dry pipe in G04-SC2 and the heated shelter pipe in G04-SC3 refer to this stronghold's trays and residual heat.

/monster_contents/M006/entries/9/bestiar.en: The pipe-bound youngling is a growth stage whose small size suits narrow pipes. It can scarcely complete the 50-meter surface circuit or cross during a cold snap, so it stays close to adult strongholds and further constricts maintenance space.

/monster_contents/M006/entries/9/prose.en:
- Role and body: A growth-stage member of the sewer raccoon clan, it has a small body suited to narrow pipes and whiskers that are still short. It slips between adults to eat scraps but can scarcely complete the 50-meter surface circuit or cross during a cold snap. It is strongly nocturnal but poor at judging what it finds, mistaking floating debris for food.
- Origin: The name was given to small-bodied young that survived in families living in pipes for many generations. The speed with which they move shelter in response to leading indicators is learned by following their mothers, not inherited.
- Habitat: Its main spaces are narrow joints in the Ttukseom Union branch lines and the area beneath ventilation ladders. When adults disperse to the gallery, it often cannot follow and remains beneath a refuge-chamber shelf. Restoring the designed flow rate eliminates this habitat altogether.
- Needs: It needs only film scraps left by adults, small aquatic prey, and a low current that lets it dry. Loss of body heat threatens its life before lack of food does.
- Life cycle and upkeep: If it cannot join the group carried to the ventilation room before its first flood, it grows exhausted on an intermediate ledge. After a season, its whiskers lengthen and it begins to read the current, but raising the flow rate before then cuts its growth short.
- Behavior and hierarchy: It is at the bottom of the hierarchy and waits its turn to be carried by an elder female. If it goes to an exit alone, it confuses the sound of boots with the sound of pumps. H04 misses this small heat spot as debris more often than it misses adults.
- Escalation: At stage 1, young that could not join the group moving to the ventilation room remain at pipe joints even during the day. At stage 2, they meet a robot head-on in a narrow pipe. At stage 3, unable to cross the dry passage during a cold snap on their own, they cling to an adult stronghold and further constrict maintenance space.
- Engagement and response: Immediately raising the flow to its design rate or flooding the entire area wipes out a growing generation at once. Partial water blocking, alternative shelter, and sensor cleaning take priority; capture numbers cannot serve as a measure of success.
- Negotiation and moral choice: Allowing a low flow rate for one more season lets the pipe-bound younglings grow and learn to read the current, but delays the recovery of pump capacity. Raising the flow immediately stabilizes drainage but also reduces the next generation's ability to adapt to the pipes and the information available from this indicator species. Moving these animals to the gallery's heating during a cold snap draws power from the Mapo Union; leaving them in the refuge chamber lets them occupy the maintenance platform.
- Scenario connection: This is the growth stage left out of the group carried in G04-SC1 and the one that clings to the dry passage in G04-SC3, narrowing the space further.

/monster_contents/M008/entries/0/bestiar.en: The route specialist 'Gapwhisker' is a pathfinding individual that pushes its whiskers into gaps in cable trays to find openings where air leaks through. It gives no orders and connects branches only to cores with abundant food traces.

/monster_contents/M008/entries/0/prose.en:
### Role and Body
A specialist pathfinder, it pushes its whiskers into cable-tray gaps to find openings where air leaks through. From the temperature and vibrations transmitted through its feet and belly, it distinguishes trains, supply carts, and human footsteps, but it cannot read distant heat spots on a screen or decipher the text on an electronic information board.

### Origin
During a winter when ultrasound and sealing panels were deployed in the same sequence again and again, survivors split off after learning to remember only the open side. After testing an unused pipe support beneath the Gwangjin Line Escort Protection State Office shopping arcade, they turned its opening into a branch between cores.

### Habitat
By day, it clings to the edges of cable trays and insulated-pipe brackets; it ventures onto frequently disinfected ground-level areas only at night. It visits the space behind shutters where traffic has ceased only as temporary storage.

### Needs and Economy
Pipe heat, more than crumbs, supplies the strength needed to keep an opening in use. When the heat fades, its whiskers grow less sensitive and pathfinding stops; if food scraps move to another core, the opening is abandoned within a day.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
When rough cable sheathing wears down its whiskers, it misses air currents and opens the wrong escape route. Prolonged exposure on a bright platform raises its energy expenditure, causing it to skip breeding that season.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
It gives no orders and connects branches only to cores with abundant food traces. If H05 Yun Jae treats one heat spot as the leader, it can be confused with leaking pipe heat, setting off a misguided lockdown.

### Escalating Threat
In stage 1, it makes a test opening in the opposite tray. In stage 2, when one core is blocked, it moves the branch beneath a shop shutter. In stage 3, the soup kitchen side is closed first, and it opens a reverse-running passage into the evacuation stairwell cables.

### Combat and Response
Because toxic spraying and flames can reach areas used by children and companion animals, they remain last resorts. After confirming which sections are occupied, open a one-way escape route toward an area people do not use and seal openings from the rear forward. Judge the result not by the number captured, but by short circuits, food contamination, non-target deaths, and evacuation transit time.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
Keeping one unoccupied section closed long enough to test an escape route avoids handing passage records to HP09 Digital Media City Trust House, but leaves that space unavailable as evacuation capacity. Sealing every opening at once speeds up sanitation, but drives the pathfinders deeper into the cable layers and raises restoration costs.

### Scenario Connections
The one-way escape-route test in G05-SC1 uses this opening as its setting; the sealing-sequence error in G05-SC2 drives the colony up through the same opening toward the stairs; and during the protein unloading week in G05-SC3, the branch reaches the elevator threshold.

/monster_contents/M008/entries/1/display.en: Transfer Rat Colony First Elite 'Warm Core Site'

/monster_contents/M008/entries/1/bestiar.en: The first elite, 'Warm Core Site,' is a breeding concentration where food and insulated pipes coincide. It is not a permanent leader; treating a large thermal-imaging mass as the entire colony causes the lockdown to miss its target.

/monster_contents/M008/entries/1/prose.en:
### Role and Body
The first elite is a dense breeding core situated where food and insulated pipes coincide. It is not a permanent leader; movement merely concentrates here for a time. Its whiskers and sense of smell locate food scraps and heat, but it cannot distinguish distant infrared patterns.

### Origin
Beneath the Gwangjin Line transfer shopping arcade, carbohydrate crumbs dropped after closing and leaking pipe heat remained in one section, solidifying this core. People began calling the large mass on thermal imaging the entire colony, but that reflects only the limits of the image.

### Habitat
Its center is a warm core where trays and pipes cross beneath the shopping arcade. When feeding density rises at the Yeouido Line Sangha Relief State, branches extend into the wall, but the warm core itself is not vacated until its heat fades.

### Needs and Economy
Its density depends on having both carbohydrate crumbs and pipe heat. Even if HC05 Bukhansan Bogukmun Records House seals the document archive and reagent storeroom, the warm core will not shrink while soup-kitchen leftovers remain.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
Breaking up one core merely drives its individuals into the remaining cores; it does not collapse the colony. Density falls only when food-scrap collection and drying continue throughout every section. Removing a visible nest merely relocates the colony.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
Movement gathers through openings brought by pathfinding individuals. H05 does not record the warm core as active until it has compared heat spots with nighttime droppings, juvenile footprints, and missing bait.

### Escalating Threat
In stage 1, droppings and warmth make this core the first to become visible. In stage 2, sealing only this site redistributes movement to shop shutters and other trays. In stage 3, closing the soup kitchen side in the wrong order sends pressure from the warm core spilling into the emergency stairwell.

### Combat and Response
Putting flames into the warm core burns cable sheathing and hastens a short circuit. The basic approach is to open a one-way escape route, then seal from the rear forward and collect food scraps. Judge success by insulation resistance, zero cases of food contamination, and transit time.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
Removing only the visible warm core in haste opens the passage briefly, but the opposite core becomes the center, raising costs in the next stage. Surveying every core first protects non-target animals and evacuation routes, but delays the opening of the Gwangjin Line and Yeouido Line passages.

### Scenario Connections
The large mass on thermal imaging in G05-SC1 is this warm core. Resealing in G05-SC2 begins after its pressure has been driven upward in error, and during the unloading week in G05-SC3, its branches reach the hub floor.

/monster_contents/M008/entries/2/display.en: Transfer Rat Colony Second Elite 'Opposite Core'

/monster_contents/M008/entries/2/bestiar.en: The second elite, 'Opposite Core,' is a hidden core that barely appears on thermal imaging and is revealed only by juvenile tracks. No leader is replaced; disturbing the warm core merely shifts the traces elsewhere.

/monster_contents/M008/entries/2/prose.en:
### Role and Body
The second elite is a hidden breeding core, barely visible on thermal imaging and revealed only by juvenile tracks in the opposite tray. Its individuals are smaller than those of the warm core, and movement peaks at night. They cannot read electronic signals and hold their position using only air currents and the smell of food scraps.

### Origin
