The track of G06-SC3 migratory week was this knot's stage, and the overlapped surface of G06-SC1 and mismatched timetable of G06-SC2 were the strings tightening the knot.

/monster_contents/M010/entries/5/bestiar.en: Inland Variant 'Rooftop Gutter' is the omnivorous waterfowl that used park fountains and rooftop gutters as temporary surface during the dry season when wetlands dried. It did not follow the main force's slowdown learning.

/monster_contents/M010/entries/5/prose.en:
### Role and Body
As a regional variant, it was the omnivorous waterfowl that used inland park fountains and rooftop gutters as temporary surface during the dry season when wetlands dried. Its feet were short to match railing width. Its eyes confused rooftop solar reflections and fountain droplets with wetland surface. It remembered the sound of water-supply pumps before sea wind or bridge horns.

### Origin
In the season when the central Seoul Station surface was drained for sluice inspection, some individuals that could not complete intermediate stopovers scattered inland in search of the next surface. The movement was not finished but temporary, and did not overlap space with the main Seoul Station wetland force even on the same evening.

### Habitat
Only in the dry season did it leave the Gangnam Line pond for inland park fountains, rooftop gutters, and occasionally temporary surface outside the rolling-stock depot. When the rainy season returned it went back to the waterside deck, but if rooftop supply stabilized for one season it postponed return.

### Needs and Economy
Its food was organic debris gathered in fountains and insects in rooftop gutters. Even if wetland fishmeal was cut this variant did not decrease. If rooftop gutters were blocked it moved to the next building's drain.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
When soles wore on railings gutter takeoff was delayed and it overlapped window workers. When rooftop was emptied by forced removal it crowded park walkway fountains the same evening.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
There was no commander on inland perches either. It did not follow the main force's slowdown learning. Even when H06 radar raised a rooftop point as a balloon the site distinguished it by gutter droppings. The HC06 Noryangjin Delivery House did not add inland occupation to the yard-line incursion ledger.

### Phased Threat
In phase 1 it sat only on fountain edges to avoid the dried wetland. In phase 2 it gathered on rooftop gutters and obscured the water-supply pump. In phase 3 even after the surface was dried inland crowding remained and called rodents and other predators into residential areas.

### Combat and Countermeasures
Inland netting put walking children at risk and wetland water-level control did not reach rooftops. It was safer to open gutter covers and alternative temporary surface outside the track. Success was rooftop supply available time, inland walking injuries, and wetland return ratio.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
Drying the surface to obtain bridge visibility let this variant occupy residential water supply. Permanent rooftop gutter blockade made park fountains new stopover sites and reduced walks. Leaving dry-season temporary surface outside the track neither hid restoration failure nor shifted birds only to inland residents.

### Scenario Connection
The surface drainage of G06-SC3 pushed this variant inland, and the unilateral drainage of G06-SC1 made fountains into fake edges.

/monster_contents/M010/entries/6/prose.en:
### Role and Body
As controller, it was the guide Seojin that read brine marks. It did not stand in front but threw dry glove fragments on the floor to mark only the points where conduction broke. Its primary sense was change in skin conductivity and minute vibration on metal surfaces. As auxiliary it read electrolyte solvent and salt smell and local hot spots. There was no wall-penetrating perspective or global eavesdropping. After rainwater dilution misreads increased so H07 Jeong Uram's residual-pressure log and glove discoloration had to be cross-checked.

### Origin
It came from the night recovery unit that repeatedly inhaled the mist of abandoned towing-battery stacks between the Line Succession State siding and the Neutral Convoy City transfer platform immediately after collapse. The origin was disaster residual chemistry, not ethnicity or disability nature. The word 'burn' was only a metaphor for scars and not a medical stigma code.

### Habitat
The core was the lower Yongsan siding and the brine-tray row. During rainy and thaw cycles it used condensation-wall surfaces along the Sinnae and Mangwoo freight-elevator shafts as landmarks. In the dry season it reduced radius to prevent skin-membrane cracks. When XT02 West Sea Granary Precinct refrigerated containers pressed in it received only the pressure signal of the salinity gradient and did not replace the sixteen-state slots.

### Needs and Economy
Neutralized electrolyte salt, conductive scrap metal debris, cooling water, and weak-alkali buffer were its resources. It did not own batteries but used tray salt concentration as trading unit. Energy over-absorption was limited by skin cracking. When buffer ran out distant exploration automatically stopped.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
On days when rain redissolved tray salt it was not the skin but the dispatch that changed first. A guide whose skin membrane had cracked was not deprived of authority but recited contamination paths verbally. Only when that testimony remained with figures did the successor gain speaking rights.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
There was no permanent commander. Speaking rights arose only in sections where it first stepped on the brine path and read conduction values. When neutralizer and repairer concentration gauges disagreed departure could not be ordered until the Yongsan duty officer, citizen observer, and Jeong Uram log confirmed the same tray number. Strength lay not in command speed but in the fact that the person who hid the leak could not open the path alone.

### Phased Threat
In phase 1 glove color changed and white crystal lines appeared on tray edges. In phase 2 brine reached switch contacts and dispatch signals shook. In phase 3 the Sinnae freight-elevator floor continued as one conduction surface.

### Combat and Countermeasures
Attacking the guide made the person who would announce hidden puddles disappear. Laying dry walking plates, making switch contacts powerless, and pushing weak-alkali spray from inside to outside was the basic. Flame and strong water jets were forbidden. The price of suppression remained in the number of stopped trains and discarded gloves.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
Letting passenger trains pass on time let hidden puddles ride wheels to Sinnae. Clearing the track for thirty minutes shook dispatch credit. Sealing only the brine line left no cause map. Weighing passenger time and recovery workers' skin on the same morning was the negotiation with this guide.

### Scenario Connection
In G07-SC1 white brine line dispatch Seojin's glove fragments marked conduction breaks, and in G07-SC3 one conduction surface the concentration gauges disagreed so even the guide could not designate a path.

/monster_contents/M010/entries/7/prose.en:
### Role and Body
As a general ecological type, it was the neutralizer individual that pushed weak-alkali spray from inside the tray outward so that salt aerosol did not splash onto the platform. It read the concentration slope before and after spraying by skin conduction. Local hot spots told it only the places where solvent evaporated. It remembered with its body that strong water jets widened the leak area.

### Origin
It split from the guide when division of labor for trading salt concentration emerged. Among the recovery units that inhaled the mist of initial protection failure, the body that first mastered spray angle remained as neutralizer.

### Habitat
The inner grooves of the siding tray row and the cleaning-tank drainage lip were its work spots. When switch contacts shook manpower gathered on that track. When dry-season cracks deepened it cut signals in Yongsan's shaded drainage grooves.

### Needs and Economy
Weak-alkali buffer was the key consumable. When warehouse stock fell below half it stopped distant-shaft exploration and circulated only already-marked zones. Cooling water was used only for aerosol suppression and kept separate from drinking-water ledgers.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
When spray valves clogged with salt the inside-to-outside order reversed and aerosol splashed onto the platform. Concentration gauges were kept separate from the repairer's. When the two values diverged greatly movement automatically stopped.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
It began spraying only in sections where the guide had speaking rights and did not spray first on command. Even when the H07 log read high residual pressure it cross-checked with现场 glove discoloration, cleared misreads, and only then used more buffer.

### Phased Threat
In phase 1 it only wet the white brine-line edge. In phase 2 it demanded reduced night operations to block aerosol around switch contacts. In phase 3 when the whole hall became one conduction surface spray angle became meaningless and it demanded power cutoff together.

### Combat and Countermeasures
Flame raised solvent vapor and water jets spread salt. Spraying only weak alkali on dry plates made the neutralizer close its own nozzles. Success was not corpses but the number of contacts that had to be replated and zero platform aerosol.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
Supplying buffer immediately wet even the misread section and killed cooling continuity. Waiting for cross-check lengthened that morning's passenger time. Removing this crew to erase neutralization knowledge made contact corrosion cost in the next rain fall on the contract violator.

### Scenario Connection
In G07-SC1 the hand that pushed aerosol inward from inside was this crew, and the unsealed lot leak of G07-SC2 exhausted the buffer ledger.

/monster_contents/M010/entries/8/prose.en:
### Role and Body
As a general ecological type, it was the repairer individual that stitched cracked skin membranes and work gloves with the same needle. Its fingertips gauged crack width. Conductive scrap was allocated only to contact repair and conduction measurement. Burn appearance was not entered on the judgment table and cracked membrane was not used as reason to block passage.

### Origin
After electrolyte thirst and conductive skin membrane stabilized, the side that blocked cracks rather than expanding raised survival rate. It split when the speed at which the Guro Alloy House recovery team brought heat-resistant alloy scrap overlapped repair speed.

### Habitat
The shaded drainage grooves of the Yongsan duty ledger and the area behind the dry walking plates of the Sinnae transfer hall were its repair spots. In the rainy season it moved along shaft-wall condensation water. In the dry season it reduced radius and only stitched membranes.

### Needs and Economy
Conductive scrap metal debris and buffer were repair materials. It did not use scrap as plunder target. Organic matter was only auxiliary food for the night labor unit. Raising recovery speed widened brine under the tray and actually increased repair demand.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
Crack width of skin membrane, leak liters, and remaining buffer moved together before advancing to the next phase. For people missing from work rest and buffer were allocated in the same unit as discarded glove count.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
The repairer did not command the guide and kept a different concentration gauge. When values diverged it stopped the needle and waited until the citizen observer marked the wet section. The next shift using the same glove together was proof of authority.

### Phased Threat
In phase 1 it replaced only discolored gloves. In phase 2 leak from ledger-outside lots increased the repair queue so whether cold-storage compartments were sealed became the issue. In phase 3 when the hall floor became one conduction surface the repair needle itself became the conduction path.

### Combat and Countermeasures
Felling the repairer left cracked membranes open and increased conduction area. It stitched only on dry plates and powerless contacts. Success was reduction in discarded glove count and compartments that could no longer be opened.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
Using burn traces as passage qualification hid the actual leak ledger. Opening the house warehouse name increased dispatch-rights conflict but the citizen corridor did not repay ledger blanks. Agreement was not declaration but the labor of the next shift using the same glove.

### Scenario Connection
Responsibility for ledger-outside waste batteries in G07-SC2 created the repair queue, and while the observer marked wet sections in G07-SC3 this crew waited for power with needle in hand.

/monster_contents/M010/entries/9/prose.en:
### Role and Body
As a general ecological type, it was the circulating individual that abandoned distant shafts when buffer warehouse stock fell below half and circled only already-marked zones. Its skin conduction read only residual salt of marked tray numbers. It voluntarily exited long high-concentration zones to avoid cracking. Electronic noise was used only for battery residual-pressure estimation and there was no complete透視.

### Origin
After unauthorized washing diluted electrolyte spread widely, the unit that scattered into small groups learned marked-zone circulation. The upper limit at which expansion automatically stopped was this body's habit.

### Habitat
It moved only between already-marked tray rows of the Yongsan siding and the dry walking plates of the Sinnae transfer hall. When XT02 refrigerated inflow diverted salt load outward the circulation radius fixed for one season.

### Needs and Economy
Neutralized salt of marked zones and remaining buffer share were its energy. Sealing the lot and discarding two cold-cargo compartments maintained circulation but left the next rainy-season map blank. When the seal was broken this individual collected the map and stopped circulation.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
When Sinnae officially recognized the brine passage as a night slot it emptied passage in exchange for contact cleaning and concentration records. When trays were unauthorized-washed it split into smaller rings following the diluted salt.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
The circulating individual did not open new paths. It stopped in unmarked sections where the guide had no speaking rights. When the three crews' concentration gauges disagreed it circled even inside marked zones. Instead of retaliatory attack it withdrew work from unpublished sections.

### Phased Threat
In phase 1 it circled only marked grooves. In phase 2 ledger-outside lots overlapped marked zones so circulation touched passenger paths. In phase 3 when the hall became one conduction surface the circulation ring itself became the conduction path.

### Combat and Countermeasures
Cutting circulation with gunfire made the location of hidden puddles disappear from the ledger. Reinforcing dry plates in marked zones and selectively cutting hall power made the ring dry again. Success was time when circulation was separated from passenger corridors and cold-storage compartments not discarded.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
Moving the lot to the Sinnae hall to disperse responsibility spread salt onto passenger paths. Narrowing night slots to protect Yongsan transfer revenue pushed this individual's circulation onto the platform. Whose ledger blank the citizen corridor would repay was the content of whether to leave the circulation.

### Scenario Connection
Whether the lot was sealed in G07-SC2 left or erased this individual's map, and the outer detour of G07-SC3 fixed circulation location for one season.

/monster_contents/M011/entries/0/prose.en:
- Role and body: A lead scout of the electrolyte-burn group, it presses the blistered sensory sacs on both arms against the floor to read vibrations traveling through solid material. On continuous concrete, it can distinguish footsteps within 28 meters at intervals of 0.2 seconds, but it cannot detect them across suspended platforms or through a layer of water 4 centimeters or more deep. The mildly acidic fluid dripping from its split skin leaves a turquoise route marker for about 40 minutes.
- Origin: Survivors burned badly enough to lose their hands and arms at a battery-electrolyte leak site mutated after prolonged exposure to conductive deposits on the floor of the Wangsimni Union. As the external pressure variable XT02 rises, the number of sensory sacs increases, but so do each sac’s reading errors and fluid consumption.
- Habitat: It patrols stretches of the Wangsimni Union’s abandoned power corridors where the floor remains continuous, and migrates seasonally to the low drains of the Jamsil Line when thermal inversion widens the cracks. Elevated walkways and deep pools of sediment are blank zones where it cannot read its own way.
- Needs and desires: Silver-chloride mesh patches used to recoat the sensory-sac electrodes are its scarcest maintenance material; one patch preserves reading accuracy for no more than three days. Its travel energy is limited to two pouches of acidic sugar solution, and each adult produces only three blister seeds in its lifetime to awaken new individuals, so it postpones reproduction unless a safe route is secured.
- Life cycle and maintenance: The sensory sacs shed after a cumulative 63 kilometers of floor contact. If a silver-chloride mesh patch is not applied before then, left- and right-side vibration sources are recorded in reverse. A discarded blister seed must receive 300 evenly paced footsteps in the same corridor to grow into an individual; otherwise, it dries out and dies within a week.
- Behavior and hierarchy: At the front, it signals that a route is safe by stopping three times and tapping twice, and approves only stretches where H07 records match actual vibrations as the group’s line of travel. It classifies unfamiliar walking intervals as pursuers, but removes a completely stationary target from its map after 90 seconds.
- Escalating threat: At first, leak markers become mixed with evacuation signs; when its readings go awry, it registers maintenance workers’ footsteps as danger signals. An individual whose sensory sacs have reversed left and right leads the group into collapse zones, leaving skin-irritating acidic lines along the corridors it passes through.
- Countermeasures and combat: Installing suspended platforms separated from the floor cuts off its detection range, and an entry team can stop completely for 90 seconds at a time to escape its tracking memory. Dividing a corridor’s vibration connections into three sections with rubber wedges prevents the guide from reading distant targets, so it turns back without an acid attack.
- Negotiation and moral choice: Three strikes on the floor followed by the display of a safe map verified by H07 serve as an expression of intent. Humans provide silver-chloride mesh patches and collapse forecasts, while the guide updates evacuation routes. An agreement is maintained through the number of notches carved into its arm scars; if an ambush is set in a promised corridor, it covers that route with false acidic markers and refuses the next three map exchanges.
- Scenario connection: In G07-SC1, compare H07 vibration records with the leak notches to choose the Wangsimni Union’s actual escape route. If HC07 mediation succeeds, the location of the seasonal passage leading to the Jamsil Line is shared.

/monster_contents/M011/entries/1/prose.en:
- Role and body: A maintenance individual that reads temperature gradients inside pipes with bundles of capillaries along its bent torso and carries coolant. Where metal pipes are connected, it can distinguish a change of 0.4 degrees from 14 meters away, but it cannot perceive anything beyond ceramic insulation or a closed shutoff valve. Its dorsal pouch holds 18 liters at a time and releases the liquid where needed through a pressure differential.
- Origin: Maintenance workers trapped in an emergency cooling tank underwent electrolyte burns and repeated hypothermia, changing their circulatory systems to respond to the external pipe network. As XT02 pressure grows stronger, their discharge valves stiffen, making even normal temperature correction more likely to turn into an aggressive spray.
- Habitat: It maintains communal pools in the Wangsimni Union’s condensation chambers and at the junctions of active cooling pipes, and moves along residual condensate to the Jamsil Line’s low-temperature sections during the dry season. Broken pipes and rooms wrapped in insulation are absent from its temperature map, so it does not enter them.
- Needs and desires: Borate inhibitor ampoules, which prevent crystals from forming in its capillaries, are its essential consumable; one adult needs exactly two bottles a month. The liquid in its dorsal pouch diminishes through evaporation and spraying, while a reproductive condensation pod consumes 30 liters of clean water and one inhibitor ampoule. Only two pods can therefore be grown in each pool per season.
- Life cycle and maintenance: The dorsal pouch withstands 180 fillings and discharges before its valve must be replaced. If replacement is delayed, its entire contents erupt as an acidic vapor mist at the next temperature rise. A condensation pod awakens only if kept between 7 and 9 degrees Celsius for 16 days; if it remains outside that range for more than two hours, its internal capillaries harden.
- Behavior and hierarchy: The individual that remembers the longest temperature curve in the pipe network sets the order of distribution, prioritizing the stability of dormant pools over hot equipment. If the H07 temperature log lags more than 5 minutes behind actual changes in the pipes, it treats the recorder as the cause of the malfunction and cuts off flow around the sensors.
- Escalating threat: When its reserves are low, it diverts active cooling circuits; as its valve stiffens, it sprays supercooled liquid onto doors and stairs. If an individual in its final filling cycle touches a heat source, rapid vapor expansion can rupture three adjacent pipe sections at once.
- Countermeasures and combat: Separate the pipe network into short loops with shutoff valves and keep the temperature change in each loop at 0.3 degrees per minute or less; the gradient it tracks will disappear. Connecting an empty condensation tank for pressure relief lets it empty its dorsal pouch on its own, buying time to replace the valve without a freezing attack.
- Negotiation and moral choice: Send pulses of hot water through the pipes in a 2–1–2 pattern and indicate the quantity of purified condensate; it understands this as a distribution offer. The pulse keeper records the number of agreements in the scars on its valve and prevents the facility from overheating. If the humans divert the water they promised, it repays the supply violation by directing cooling flow to the communal pool instead of the residents’ circuits.
- Scenario connection: In G07-SC1, use H07 temperature curves and the HC07 distribution plan to divide the Wangsimni Union’s cooling network. The agreed quantity of condensate determines the size of the group moving to the Jamsil Line.

/monster_contents/M011/entries/2/prose.en:
- Role and body: A builder that locates the direction of structural stress with four branching arms and a rib cage embedded with ferromagnetic metal fragments. Where steel framing is continuous, it can identify bends of 2 millimeters or more within 9 meters, but it does not respond to aluminum frames or fiber composites and loses its bearings near transformer boxes with overlapping magnetic fields.
- Origin: Workers burned by electrolyte and trapped under debris when a storage wall collapsed in the Wangsimni Union took iron scraps into their skeletons, becoming these creatures. If XT02 pressure persists, the magnetic alignment of their rib cages becomes disordered, causing them to judge load-bearing walls as safe walls and safe walls as load-bearing ones.
- Habitat: It builds walls of acidic scrap metal in the Wangsimni Union’s intersecting corridors and lift entrances. In seasons when moisture weakens the walls, it carries structural members to the Jamsil Line’s dry sections. It treats spaces made entirely of nonferrous structures as empty places with no building value.
- Needs and desires: Manganese-phosphate-coated nails that stop its chest fragments from corroding are scarce; one is consumed every 12 reinforcement jobs. A new mason requires one core fragment removed from an adult’s breastplate and 80 kilograms of steel. Because the breastplate regenerates only twice in a lifetime, it does not increase its numbers indiscriminately.
- Life cycle and maintenance: A building cycle ends after a wall undergoes 40 major load changes. An individual that has not received a coated nail becomes fused to the structure on the forty-first deformation. Forcibly removing a fused body brings down both the wall and its skeleton; leaving it in place yields a single core fragment after 20 days.
- Behavior and hierarchy: Rather than widening a corridor, it directs loads onto walls of its choosing to create rooms for the colony. It builds a double barrier in any direction where H07 impact records confirm repeated blows, but dismantles steel framing that has borne no load for a long time and moves it elsewhere.
- Escalating threat: First, steel disappears from around inspection hatches; then changing load paths twist ceilings and lift shafts. If a mason making faulty judgments classifies a critical column as a weak member, it even tears out the steel supporting an evacuation route to use as barrier material.
- Countermeasures and combat: Erect a temporary load frame of nonmagnetic composite, then release the weight from the steel framing one joint at a time. With nothing left to detect, it stops building. Instead of breaking through a wall head-on, show it a load gauge and shift the stress line toward a safe pile of steel to avoid fusion and cascading collapse.
- Negotiation and moral choice: Two short hammer strikes followed by one long one, then the display of an H07 load map, are understood as a request for joint construction. It remembers the locations of the supplied manganese-phosphate nails and steel through the arrangement of rivets on its breastplate. In return for reinforcing an evacuation room, the mason is guaranteed one dormant chamber; if humans dismantle it, the mason closes the next corridor into a structure with no exit.
- Scenario connection: In G07-SC2, use H07 impact data to determine the actual loads on the Wangsimni Union’s barriers. If reinforcement is chosen over demolition under the HC07 agreement, an alternative passage toward the Jamsil Line remains open.

/monster_contents/M011/entries/3/prose.en:
- Role and body: A decomposer that sorts contaminated organic matter with an abdominal grinding sac and layered taste plates, then turns it into binder. By touching its tongue to a wet surface, it can classify the degree of protein decay within 30 centimeters into five grades. It can smell airborne particles only up to 2 meters away and cannot read the contents of glass containers or silicone membranes.
- Origin: Waste handlers whose mouths and abdomens were damaged after the electrolyte accident ate fungal deposits and battery residue, transforming their digestive tracts into external processing tanks. As XT02 pressure rises, the bitter-taste threshold by which they distinguish living tissue increases, and they may classify even living injured people as waste.
- Habitat: It makes rounds through the Wangsimni Union’s compression chambers and fungal layers, leaving bite-mark signs on piles it can process. When fermentation stops in the cold season, it moves to the Jamsil Line’s warm waste areas. On inorganic floors or in completely dry storerooms, it cannot assess anything as food at all.
- Needs and desires: Chitin-apatite dental plates to replace worn taste plates are in shortest supply; one wears out for every 50 kilograms of contaminated material processed. The grinding sac’s enzymes can process only 12 kilograms a day. Each reproductive sac requires three dental plates and 20 kilograms of fermenting fungus, so each processing room can raise only one individual per season.
- Life cycle and maintenance: The grinding sac has a 72-hour fermentation clock after feeding. If it cannot vomit up the finished binder within that time, internal pressure turns its esophagus and abdominal wall inside out. A reproductive sac opens only after receiving exactly three bursts of fermentation heat; a fourth creates a pool of corrosive enzymes instead of a new individual.
- Behavior and hierarchy: It prefers rotting tissue, then fungus, then insulation. It remembers anything that produces a strong bitter taste in its mouth as a living being for twelve days. Once it learns bitter-taste labels matching the H07 list of living people, it excludes those people from its feeding routes until their labels wear off.
- Escalating threat: When it has enough dental plates, only waste disappears; as they wear down, it also chews biological filters and medical bandages. An individual nearing the end of fermentation tears doors apart to find an outlet. If time runs out, the grinding sac’s enzymes dissolve nearby floors and organic equipment.
- Countermeasures and combat: Apply bitter-taste labels at the prescribed concentration to survivors and important equipment, and separate waste into glass intake bins to control what it classifies as food. When its grinding sac is overfilled, offering a protease inhibitor at the intake stops digestion, causing it to move to a processing tank on its own.
- Negotiation and moral choice: Hand it pieces with three different concentrations of bitterness in sequence, and it understands a contract distinguishing people, material to process, and forbidden material. The grinder preserves the terms as colored bands on its taste plates; humans receive removal of infectious material in exchange for supplying the specified waste. If they deliberately falsify a forbidden label, it invalidates the entire set of markers and inspects protected subjects again.
- Scenario connection: In G07-SC2, use H07 records of living people to decide who in the Wangsimni Union receives bitter-taste labels. If HC07 approves its processing rights, saturated individuals follow the waste to the Jamsil Line.

/monster_contents/M011/entries/4/prose.en:
- Role and body: A heat buffer that gathers and transports radiant heat with ceramic-like burn calluses and a phase-change backplate. With a clear line of sight, it can distinguish heat sources 35 meters away at a spatial resolution of 30 centimeters and a temperature difference of 0.2 degrees, but cannot read around corners or surfaces covered with reflective film.
- Origin: It arose when survivors trapped for a long time in high-temperature sections after an electrolyte fire formed layers of cooling-salt deposits on their skin. As XT02 pressure rises, the backplate crystals fail to release heat, reaching their rupture threshold at a much lower temperature than usual.
- Habitat: It absorbs excess heat beneath the Wangsimni Union’s heat exchangers and on the floors of burned-out battery rooms. When the equipment cools, it follows the heated ducts of the Jamsil Line. In rooms with many polished metal panels, overlapping false thermal images make it pause for a long time before entering.
- Needs and desires: Phase-change salt bricks fitted into its backplate are its only long-term maintenance material; each brick must be replaced after absorbing 8 megajoules of heat. A new diver grows only from two spent salt bricks of an adult, and an adult can attach only six bricks to its backplate over its lifetime, so it can leave no more than three offspring.
- Life cycle and maintenance: A cycle ends at whichever condition comes first: absorption of 8 megajoules by a salt brick, or 6 hours at 60 degrees Celsius or above. If it cannot lie down on a heat-dissipation platform within 20 minutes of saturation, its ceramic calluses burst off layer by layer, releasing acidic vapor and a heat wave.
- Behavior and hierarchy: The individual with the greatest spare capacity leads and chooses heat sources, while saturated companions are pushed to the outside of the group to establish the order of heat release. It suspects point heat sources that suddenly appear on H07 heat maps are traps, but accepts broad, gently graded heated surfaces as safe food.
- Escalating threat: At first, temperatures in heated sections even out; as absorption increases, heat vanishes from residential areas, creating a risk of hypothermia. If several saturated individuals lie in one entrance, the passage becomes a radiant-heat barrier, and a backplate rupture can trigger cascading heating in nearby storage cells.
- Countermeasures and combat: Cut off its line of sight with reflective-film shutters, then expose black ceramic heat-dissipation panels one by one to guide its movement and the location of heat release precisely. Pushing an empty phase-change storage panel in front of a saturated individual lets it transfer heat, preventing backplate damage without rapid chilling.
- Negotiation and moral choice: Send one long flash and three short flashes with an infrared lamp, then present an empty heat-dissipation panel to initiate a heat-transport contract. The agreed quantity is recorded in discolored squares along the edge of its backplate. Humans gain protection for overheating equipment, and the diver gains a safe surface on which to release heat; if the promised panel is taken away, it directs its next load of saturated heat back into that equipment.
- Scenario connection: In G07-SC1 and G07-SC3, use H07 heat records to calculate the Wangsimni Union’s order of heat release. The group retreats to the Jamsil Line’s heated ducts only while the heat-dissipation surfaces designated by HC07 remain available.

/monster_contents/M011/entries/5/prose.en:
- Role and body: A messenger that hears low-frequency sound in tunnels and relays group signals through resonating chambers in its calves and membranous ears on its neck. In a straight passage, it can distinguish echo differences of 15 milliseconds from up to 120 meters away, but cannot determine a signal’s direction behind sound-absorbing walls or in passages with two or more bends.
- Origin: It appeared when people who suffered electrolyte burns to their feet while hanging from alarm equipment fused damaged bells with their bodily tissue. XT02 pressure is an external disturbance that speeds up the resonating chambers’ basic rhythm, turning standby signals into commands to assemble.
- Habitat: It stands between the Wangsimni Union’s long tunnels and support pillars to maintain an acoustic network. In seasons when ground contraction changes the pitch, it moves to the Jamsil Line’s regularly arched passages. It does not use rooms finished with fabric and porous panels as relay points because they do not return sound.
- Needs and desires: Mica reeds inside the resonating chambers are its scarcest resource; one cracks after 10,000 accurate signals. Its sugar-powered cells can move its throat membrane only 400 times a day. A new bell keeper can form only if two adults each contribute one intact reed, so the colony limits the number of relays.
- Life cycle and maintenance: An individual’s lifespan is measured in the number of times it stamps its feet. If its reed is not replaced before its 10,000th signal, the next beat splits into two conflicting commands. A reproductive resonance sac must receive beats at intervals of exactly 6 seconds for 24 hours to grow; a single irregular interval hardens it into an empty lime shell.
- Behavior and hierarchy: It compresses the intentions of higher-ranking individuals into short beats for long-distance transmission and sends the same signal no more than seven times to a section that does not reply. If H07 machinery vibrations resemble an agreed interval, it may mistake them for a colony summons and wake even dormant individuals.
- Escalating threat: First, alarms become difficult to distinguish from stamping feet. Once the relay network is complete, distant groups pour into the corridors at the same time. The double beat of a bell keeper with a broken reed transmits retreat and attack together, concentrating chaotic impacts on structures.
- Countermeasures and combat: Installing quarter-wave sound-absorption boxes matched to the tunnel’s length can cancel a particular beat. Sending an opposite-phase sound between support pillars can reduce relay range to 10 meters or less. Opening the access port for replacing the mica reed, rather than attacking the resonating chamber directly, safely stops even a corrupted signal.
- Negotiation and moral choice: One long ring followed by four replies at 6-second intervals requests a conversation. Humans provide mica reeds and disaster information, and the bell keeper carries collapse warnings to distant areas. The agreed beat is preserved in cuts on the reed. If a promised warning is used for an ambush, the colony sends a false evacuation order in the same sound pattern, destroying trust in the group that broke the agreement.
- Scenario connection: In G07-SC3, decode H07 acoustic logs to interrupt the Wangsimni Union’s assembly command. The shared beat approved by HC07 then serves as a collision-prevention signal during movement to the Jamsil Line.

/monster_contents/M011/entries/6/prose.en:
- Role and body: A specialized individual that absorbs radio-frequency energy through the coiled cartilage in its head, concealing the colony’s electronic traces. In unshielded spaces, it can distinguish transmitters within 60 meters at a resolution of 5 kilohertz, but it cannot detect grounded metal rooms or fiber-optic lines.
- Origin: Communications personnel whose scalps and nervous systems were damaged by electrolyte leaks developed coil organs as they adapted to leakage current from cables. When XT02 pressure increases, they become saturated even by ordinary weak signals and mistake operating equipment for charge sources.
- Habitat: They roam the Wangsimni Union communications room and cable tunnels whose shielding has come off, swallowing unnecessary transmissions. When seasonal electronic activity weakens, they move to unstable power-transmission sections of the Jamsil Line. To their senses, a fully grounded equipment room does not exist.
- Needs and desires: Sintered ferrite rings that restore the coils’ permeability are essential maintenance supplies; one breaks for every 4 kilocoulombs of accumulated charge. Stored charge must be released within 20 minutes, and one reproductive nerve knot requires four new rings, so the colony cannot produce more offspring than its ferrite stock allows.
- Life cycle and maintenance: An absorption cycle ends upon reaching 4 kilocoulombs or charging continuously for 20 minutes. If they cannot find a grounding point, the coil’s charge flows back into the nearest equipment. A nerve knot must receive a single low-strength frequency for 48 hours to grow; if the frequency band changes, it stops developing and remains a conductive lump.
- Behavior and hierarchy: They feed on sustained narrowband transmissions before broadband ones, and when close to saturation, they leave the colony to find a discharge site. If an H07 recording device emits radio waves at regular intervals, they treat it as a tracking beacon and selectively tear off only its antenna and power unit.
- Escalating threat: At first, a particular radio band goes silent; as the number of absorbing individuals grows, the entire sensor network stops responding. If a saturated group uses the same grounding point, the reverse current burns out controllers and cuts off even rescue signals, leaving outsiders unable to assess the situation.
- Countermeasures and combat: Switching communications to fiber optics and operating transmitters only inside grounded metal rooms removes their reason to approach. For individuals already saturated, open a capacitor bank connected to a resistor to draw off their charge safely. To prevent equipment destruction, provide an actual electrical discharge outlet rather than a frequency decoy.
- Negotiation and moral choice: Three short transmissions at 31 kilohertz followed by the deployment of a grounding wire signal an offer of safe discharge. Noise-Eaters remember permitted bands through the orientation of their ferrite rings; humans reduce communications interference in exchange for having excess charge handled. If humans secretly activate a forbidden band, the Noise-Eaters return current to that transmission network at the next discharge.
- Scenario connection: In G07-SC3, H07 transmission records reveal the Wangsimni Union’s absorption bands. If HC07’s permitted frequencies are observed, the predators do not target the Jamsil Line’s power-transmission section for pursuit.

/monster_contents/M011/entries/7/prose.en:
- Role and body: A ceremonial individual that stores combinations of body odors in salt-crystal folds of its nose and throat to read passage rights and promises. It can distinguish markings by concentration differences of one part in ten thousand within 80 meters when the wind is favorable and within 8 meters in still air, but cannot read odors inside activated-carbon filtration rooms or completely submerged passages.
- Origin: Survivors whose respiratory tracts were burned by electrolyte vapor and who were trapped in sealed shelters developed chemical memory organs through repeated use of organic filters. XT02 pressure fixes fear-related body odor as a hostile mark, causing even an ordinary negotiator’s sweat to be recorded as the smell of a violation.
- Habitat: They maintain scent layers at the Wangsimni Union’s ventilation junctions and colony boundaries. During periods when seasonal winds wash away the markings, they lead the group to passages on the Jamsil Line with weak airflow. Strong carbon-filtration zones are considered zones of oblivion where the record ends.
- Needs and desires: Porous alumina scent plates used to organize the scent layers are scarce; the pores of one plate become clogged for every ten oaths inscribed. The memory folds can retain only thirty-two conditions at once, and a new oathkeeper can be born only from a salt cocoon containing six unused scent plates, so the number of records and the number of individuals compete for the same stock.
- Life cycle and maintenance: Each body-odor contract has a half-life of 11 days. If the other party does not renew its confirming scent before then, conditions disappear beginning with the oldest markings. If humidity remains at 85 percent for 3 hours, the crystal layers intermingle, causing a memory collapse in which the odors of enemies and allies merge.
- Behavior and hierarchy: They arrange scent plates in the order of boundary markings, passage permissions, and violation records, stopping entrants who do not match the current conditions. They accept external testimony as a valid memory only when an H07 chemical log gives the same proportions as their own crystal layer.
- Escalating threat: When a new boundary scent travels through the ventilation network, the movement of unauthorized residents is restricted; as humidity rises, old ceasefires and recent intrusion records become mixed. During a memory collapse, they mark every entrant with the scent of violation, drawing other colony members into the pursuit.
- Countermeasures and combat: Moving people one at a time through an activated-carbon antechamber breaks the continuity of scent trails, while keeping humidity below 60 percent stops the crystal layers from mixing. Presenting a genuine oath sample in a sealed ampoule for reading and then retrieving it completes verification without leaving tracking traces on nearby people.
- Negotiation and moral choice: An ampoule containing three standard scents in the order permission, prohibition, exchange serves as a comprehensible contract. Humans provide stable ventilation and scent plates, while oathkeepers identify travelers and warn of intruders. Conditions remain in the crystal folds for 11 days; if someone steals and uses a permission scent, the oathkeepers mark all associated body odors as violators and revoke the shared right of passage.
- Scenario connection: In G07-SC2 and G07-SC3, the HC07 scent oath sets the Wangsimni Union’s passage conditions, and the H07 chemical log determines whether the agreement still holds after arrival at the Jamsil Line.

/monster_contents/M011/entries/8/prose.en:
- Role and body: A passage anchor that monitors loads on doors and bridges using cable-like elongated limbs and joint tension organs. It can distinguish changes of 3 kilograms in the load on a structure to which its body is connected within 45 meters, but cannot feel movement in a loose tent or on a platform built on an independent foundation.
- Origin: Refugees who had suffered electrolyte burns and become trapped between automatic doors and tension cables developed after taking metallic ligaments into their bodies. As XT02 pressure rises, the baseline tension in their joints increases, and they judge even a normally open door to be a gap on the verge of collapse.
- Habitat: They connect the Wangsimni Union’s fire doors, maintenance hatches, and narrow bridge approaches with their limbs to distribute loads. When seasonal expansion opens gaps in doorframes, they move to the Jamsil Line’s narrow, stable passages. They do not count temporary passages built on separate foundations as their responsibility.
- Needs and desires: Tungsten braided wire for joining severed ligaments is their most precious supply; one strand wears out for every 600 door openings and closings. Their muscular energy sustains a continuously open door for only 7 minutes, and a tension cocoon that produces a new latchkeeper requires 20 meters of braided wire, so the colony cannot reproduce beyond the number of doors it must guard.
- Life cycle and maintenance: A joint’s lifespan ends after 600 opening-and-closing cycles. If it bears another load without replacement, a break in one limb cascades to the other three. A tension cocoon must bear a constant 50-kilogram weight for 30 days to mature; if the weight varies by 5 kilograms or more, its ligaments harden asymmetrically.
- Behavior and hierarchy: They count travelers and total weight with their joint ratchets and refuse further movement once the permitted limit is reached. If H07 passage records confirm recurring times and loads, they learn them as a regular procession; an unannounced change in weight causes them to lock the entire door.
- Escalating threat: Initially, only heavy equipment is barred. As the tension threshold rises, even an empty stretcher and a few people are judged to be an overload. Forcing a door open when its braided wire is worn pulls the doorframe, bridge, and adjacent hatch together as though they were one body, damaging them simultaneously.
- Countermeasures and combat: Hang a calculated counterweight on the opposite side to remove the load from the limbs first, then release the joint ratchet one notch at a time to open the door without tearing the structure. Moving people over temporary platforms on independent foundations and dividing only the equipment into loads within the permitted weight bypasses the limits of their detection directly.
- Negotiation and moral choice: Hanging a weighted ring indicating the number of people and their total weight on the scale in front of a door is understood as a request to open it. Humans provide tungsten braided wire and an accurate roster, while the latchkeeper guarantees a safe load for the agreed 7 minutes. The agreement remains recorded in the joint ratchet and bead count; if an undeclared weight enters, it closes the door immediately and halves the next allowance.
- Scenario connection: In G07-SC2, H07 passage data and HC07’s allocation plan determine the weight-based order of passage through the Wangsimni Union’s emergency exit, changing the composition of people and equipment in the Jamsil Line evacuation procession.

/monster_contents/M011/entries/9/prose.en:
- Role and body: A contamination collector that reads and transports the electrochemical state of acidic residues using a multilayer storage sac in its abdomen and electrode membranes on its palms. Where a wet drain is continuous, it can distinguish pH differences of 0.1 and redox-potential differences of 20 millivolts up to 6 meters upstream, but cannot detect contents across a dry floor or inside a vitrified container.
- Origin: After the Wangsimni Union electrolyte accident, burn survivors assigned to neutralization work developed storage organs as they isolated acidic sludge and shed tissue in separate layers. XT02 pressure destabilizes the potential differences between storage membranes, moving acids and metal salts that should remain separate into the same layer.
- Habitat: They patrol the Wangsimni Union’s contamination settling tanks and the edges of dormant areas, gathering wet residues. In seasons when their storage capacity fills, they move to the Jamsil Line’s downstream treatment area. They avoid dry waste sites and vitrification warehouses because they cannot check their contents.
- Needs and desires: Zeolite membrane pouches that separate the storage layers are essential maintenance supplies; each must be replaced after taking in 40 liters of contaminants. Total abdominal capacity is 240 liters, and a reproductive precipitation core requires three new membrane pouches and 25 kilograms of neutralizing salt, so offspring form only when treatment supplies remain available.
- Life cycle and maintenance: A collection cycle ends when 240 liters have been taken in or 96 hours have passed since the first absorption; whichever occurs first, the collector must reach a discharge tank. If it exceeds that time, the potential difference between layers collapses, acidic liquid and metal salts mix, and gas generated inside the abdomen tears the entire storage sac apart.
- Behavior and hierarchy: They measure acidity and bioelectric potential together and absorb only residues from which all signs of life are gone. They stop before tissue that still shows signs of recovery and await HC07’s determination. If an H07 biological log indicates the possibility of a response, they surround the subject with a blue precipitation line and defer its collection.
- Escalating threat: When their stores are low, they reduce contamination; once they exceed half capacity, their weight blocks drains and sharply slows their movement. If an individual nearing the 96-hour limit stops in a passage, its rupture radius creates a bottleneck that neither rescuers nor residents can approach.
- Countermeasures and combat: Using the drain slope to direct acidic liquid and metal salts into different settling tanks, with a zeolite exchange station between them, allows the storage sac to be emptied layer by layer. Presenting already separated substances in vitrified transport cases removes them from detection, resolving an overload without forced movement.
- Negotiation and moral choice: Presenting a sample bottle with a pH color strip together with an H07 biological assessment clearly conveys what may be collected and which subjects must be held back. The collector preserves the list in an arrangement of ceramic beads in its abdomen; humans receive contamination removal in exchange for emptying the designated discharge tank. If unauthorized biological tissue is mixed in, it returns its stored contents to an upstream drain and no longer trusts subsequent assessments.
- Scenario connection: In G07-SC3, H07 biological logs and HC07’s determinations establish what may be collected from the Wangsimni Union. Once safely emptied, the procession moves to the Jamsil Line treatment area before XT02 pressure rises.

/monster_contents/M012/entries/0/prose.en:
### Role and Body
A passage repairer of the Electrolyte-Burn Group, it uses brine glands beneath its porcelain-like shoulder blades and four-pronged fingers to apply strips of silicate gel that reconnect current across severed conductive veins.

### Origin
`H07` records state that the repair specialization emerged as burn-survivor tissue in `S07` adapted to leaked electrolyte under prolonged pressure from `XT02`.

### Habitat
It occupies the flooded distribution corridors of `S07` and the spaces beneath salt bridges, locating live-current points by sensing only temperature differences arising within two arm lengths of its skin.

### Needs and Desires
Each sheet of gel requires salt, water, and silicate, and its brine glands can recharge only three times a day. When stores run out, it grinds down inactive insulating walls to gather materials.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
It passes through five stages: salt film, blister, conductive body, discharge elder, and crystal core. Even a core left by an elder grows into an individual only if sufficient salinity and silicate are present during the next flooding season.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
It experiences a break in current as pain in its skin and approaches first. The individual that repaired the longest vein directs the work order with three short discharges, but its low stored charge leaves it dependent on an escort.

### Escalating Threat
During the prickling warning stage, it shoves away anyone who touches it; during arc hunting, it fixes shoes in place with gel strips before connecting lateral electrodes; during electrolyte runaway, it releases all the charge stored in the vein under repair at once.

### Countermeasures and Combat
Hygroscopic powder stops ions moving through the gel, and covering both ends of the vein simultaneously with insulating panels breaks the attack circuit. Rapidly draining the floodwater scatters dry crystal cores over a wide area.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
If an `HC07` mediator presents two short current signals followed by one long signal and a bundle of silicate, they record on a decision plate the condition that they will repair only the marked bypass circuit, and both sides gain stable power transmission. But if humans connect a wire outside the markings, they short-circuit the next water-supply pipe.

### Scenario Connection
In `G07-SC1`, they serve as key workers in bridge repair; in `G07-SC2`, as the other party to a limited power-transmission agreement; and in `G07-SC3`, as a buffer that stops runaway triggered by `XT02`. They follow state axis `S07` and world connection axes `H07` and `HC07`.

/monster_contents/M012/entries/1/prose.en:
### Role and Body
A charge regulator of the Electrolyte-Burn Group, it uses layered capacitor sacs around its ribs and whip-shaped grounding roots to collect excess electrical potential from the group and distribute it to weakened individuals.

### Origin
According to `H07`, conductive tissue implanted by people quarantined in `S07` to withstand repeated discharges developed independent collection behavior under sustained pressure from `XT02`.

### Habitat
It patrols the transformer wells and metal stair landings of `S07`. It can read voltage differences only within three steps of where its grounding roots make contact, so it cannot determine the number or expressions of insulated subjects.

### Needs and Desires
Cooling one capacitor sac requires two containers of coolant and uncorroded grounding metal. If either runs out, it transfers charge to a living carrier to avoid rupturing the sac.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
It develops from salt film through blister and conductive body into a discharge elder. An elder’s capacitor plate awakens a crystal core to produce offspring only if it receives coolant and three stable discharges.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
It treats the voltage within a body as an amount owed. The individual that has endured the largest discharge sets the collection order, but it cannot identify intentions or status beyond the direction of current.

### Escalating Threat
During the prickling warning stage, it tests equipment potential with its grounding roots; during arc hunting, it pursues only high-potential targets and connects them to its capacitor sacs; during electrolyte runaway, it links nearby living beings and equipment into a series circuit.

### Countermeasures and Combat
Installing grounding rods of different heights in sequence, starting with the lowest, diverts the collection path into empty ground. Relying on a single large lightning rod instead keeps the sacs charging and enables prolonged discharge.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
If `HC07` offers a signal made by grounding three copper rings in sequence along with spent batteries, the debt officer remembers the arrangement of scratches on the rings until the next meeting and provides safe discharge. But if the promised coolant is diverted, it collects from the residential area’s medical equipment first.

### Scenario Connection
It appears in `G07-SC1` as an assessor of the risks of power-transmission volume, in `G07-SC2` as the enforcer of a charge-tribute agreement, and in `G07-SC3` as a variable in tracking `XT02` backflow. State ID `S07` and world links `H07` and `HC07` form the basis of its judgments.

/monster_contents/M012/entries/2/bestiar.en: The Sampling-Membrane Weaver spins disposable sampling membranes from its wrist resin spouts, leaving particle distributions in grid patterns. It is not one of the three gatekeepers of the illustrated guide; it cannot read airborne particles and can assess only surfaces it has pressed directly.

/monster_contents/M012/entries/2/prose.en:
### Role and Body
A surface-survey specialist among the Cleanroom Mutants, it uses wrist resin spouts and spreading ribs to weave disposable sampling membranes that it presses onto walls or equipment and peels away, leaving particle distributions in grid patterns.

### Origin
`H08` logs record the first occurrence as a case in which the wrist tissue of `S08` workers changed into resin-spinning structures while they were making contamination inspection maps from discarded filter fibers.

### Habitat
It operates primarily in the air-supply rooms and inspection corridors of `S08`. When seasonal airflow changes, it tracks surface deposits caused by `XT03` pressure and moves to designated survey areas in `S13`.

### Needs and Desires
Each sampling membrane consumes water, carbon fiber, and curing agent. Making more than six in a day tears its resin spouts. It cannot read airborne particles and can assess only surfaces it has pressed directly.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
Five stages follow one another: deposition, germination, specialized work, migration, and recovery. Even a dry weaving frame left by an individual in the recovery stage produces one germinating form only if supplied with clean water and a bundle of fibers.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
The weaver that completes the broadest and most accurate contamination grid sets the survey order. A sampling membrane is peeled off a surface without bringing particles into the body, then hung on a marker stand after it changes color.

### Escalating Threat
On alert, it attaches sticky inspection labels to equipment; during lockdown, it fixes travelers’ hands and feet between sampling membranes; under overpressure, it lashes uncured resin threads to obstruct sight and joints at the same time.

### Countermeasures and Combat
Particle-free cloth can create a false survey surface to consume its working time. In low humidity, pulling broadly on a membrane’s edges breaks its resin threads, but setting them on fire turns toxic substances in the sample into fumes.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
If `HC08` hands over a blue grid plate and new fibers, the weaver remembers the pattern as a safe commission and provides a contamination map, reducing movement losses for both sides. But if humans forge an inspection-complete mark, it subsequently adheres even ward equipment as hazardous samples.

### Scenario Connection
In `G08-SC1`, it surveys contamination on air-supply system surfaces; in `G08-SC2`, it allocates limited sampling membranes; and in `G08-SC3`, it forecasts changes in deposition caused by `XT03`. It is linked to state IDs `S08` and `S13` and world links `H08` and `HC08`.

/monster_contents/M012/entries/3/bestiar.en: The Pressure-Difference Pilgrim converts pressure differences along a passage into vibrations in its footsteps using a barometric sac along its spine and piezoelectric bones in its soles. It perceives stationary objects as walls even within two steps, and a single gust makes it forget the last three forks.

/monster_contents/M012/entries/3/prose.en:
### Role and Physiology
A route scout for the Cleanroom Mutants, it uses barometric sacs on either side of its spine and piezoelectric bones in its soles to turn pressure differences along corridors into sequences of footstep vibrations.

### Origin
The `H08` log records how, after the `S08` inspection crew suffered repeated decompression accidents, the function of their inner-ear balance organs extended into pressure-sensitive tissues in their backs and feet.

### Habitat
It normally leads groups through the `S08` pressure antechamber. When seasonal pressure changes occur, it assesses the heightened risk caused by `XT03` and scouts ahead as far as the secured sections of `S13`.

### Needs and Desires
It needs filtered air and sugar to maintain its barometric sacs. After more than four hours of continuous movement, its sense of direction breaks down, and it perceives stationary objects as walls even within two steps.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
Pressure spots from the settling stage grow into small sacs in the budding stage. After the functional and migration stages, only one of the sensory sacs burst open by the recovery-stage individual matures into the next generation, provided it receives steady pressure and sugar.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
The individual that finds the least turbulent pressure line takes the lead, but a single gust overwrites its memory of the last three forks, causing it to relay even a wrong direction through confident vibrations.

### Threat by Stage
On alert, it announces an approach with low-frequency stomps; during lockdown, it steps on pressure plates to create a sudden draft between doors; under overpressure, it ruptures its barometric sacs in sequence, sending shock waves back and forth through the corridor.

### Countermeasures and Combat
Opening small exhaust vents at regular intervals creates false pressure lines that can lead the group into an empty section. An explosion or a door slammed shut, however, immediately drives every individual to the sac-rupture stage.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
If `HC08` offers whistle notes at three pitches and a sugar pack, the pilgrim learns that same note sequence as the condition for safe passage in a procession and provides humans with a surveyed route. But if they first lock a pressure door along the guided route, the next procession leads refugees into a dangerous branch passage.

### Scenario Connections
In `G08-SC1`, it serves as a guide through the pressure maze; in `G08-SC2`, as the leader of the `S13` seasonal procession; and in `G08-SC3`, as a forecaster of decompression signs caused by `XT03`. It retains the state axes `S08` and `S13` and the world axes `H08` and `HC08`.

/monster_contents/M012/entries/4/bestiar.en: The Residue Digester uses an enzyme pouch beneath its jaw to turn contaminated debris into fuel sludge. Its sense of taste distinguishes only the acidity of materials it touches, so it mistakes feverish patients and active batteries for fermentation sources.

/monster_contents/M012/entries/4/prose.en:
### Role and Physiology
A waste decomposer among the Cleanroom Mutants, it uses a multilayered enzyme pouch beneath its jaw and shovel-broad fingernails to scrape up contaminated debris and turn it into fuel sludge inside a sealed fermentation sac.

### Origin
The `H08` log identifies the cause as the prolonged exposure of `S08` waste-processing personnel to mixed residues, which erased the boundary between their detoxification glands and digestive tracts.

### Habitat
It feeds primarily in the waste ducts of `S08`. During seasons when decaying matter grows scarce, it moves to the sediment zones of `S13` at times permitted by `XT03` pressure.

### Needs and Desires
Filling one enzyme pouch requires both protein and a neutralizing agent, and a fermentation sac must be replaced after three uses. Its sense of taste distinguishes only the acidity of materials it touches.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
In the settling stage, it attaches to debris with an enzyme membrane; it develops limbs in the budding stage, then passes through the functional and migration stages. Even the fermentation pouch of a recovery-stage individual sustains no more than two budding nuclei, and only if sufficient organic matter and neutralizing salts are available.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
The individual that processes the most strongly acidic residue gets first claim on food. At close range, it mistakes heat-emitting objects for fermentation sources and surrounds feverish patients or active batteries.

### Threat by Stage
On alert, it marks a forbidden line with acidic saliva; during lockdown, it pins its target to the floor with enzyme foam; under overpressure, it turns its fermentation sac inside out, spilling corrosive liquid across a narrow fan-shaped area.

### Countermeasures and Combat
Spraying a mild alkaline neutralizer in a broken band can divide its feeding route. Striking it directly with a concentrated disinfectant makes its enzyme pouch contract and spray defensive acid forward.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
If `HC08` puts unattended waste and neutralizing salts in a sealed container tapped twice, the digesters learn that sound as a safe feeding signal and return fuel sludge. But if a treatable infected person is left outside the container, they regard that person as agreed-upon food and end the protection pact.

### Scenario Connections
In `G08-SC1`, it appears as a cleaner of waste ducts; in `G08-SC2`, as a party to the debate over classifying infected people; and in `G08-SC3`, as the final consumer of residual contamination. It is tied to state IDs `S08` and `S13`, world links `H08` and `HC08`, and the external-pressure variable `XT03`.

/monster_contents/M012/entries/5/bestiar.en: The Condensate Shepherd gathers moisture with cooling plates on its back and condenses it in a storage sac beneath its neck. Its heat sense reads only surface temperatures within three steps, and it takes water back from anyone who drinks beyond the marked measure.

/monster_contents/M012/entries/5/prose.en:
### Role and Physiology
A water distributor among the Cleanroom Mutants, it uses cooling plates on its back and capillaries between its ribs to gather moisture from the air and condense it in a transparent storage sac beneath its neck.

### Origin
The `H08` log explains that, while enduring residual contamination and a shortage of cooling water, `S08` facilities personnel converted their body-heat-dissipating tissues into condensation devices and became a distinct line.

### Habitat
It tends droplet colonies on the `S08` cooling wall. When the dry season comes, it moves to the humid equipment sections of `S13`, following the condensation periods created by `XT03` pressure changes.

### Needs and Desires
It needs salt and a cold plate surface to maintain its storage sac. One individual can collect only two bottles' worth per day, and its heat sense reads only surface temperatures within three steps.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
A cooling-plate primordium forms in the settling stage, and it collects its first droplet in the budding stage. After the functional and migration stages, a recovery-stage individual joins the communal reservoir, but it produces no new buds if the allocated water level is low.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
The shepherd that keeps its back plates at the lowest temperature controls distribution. The group guides dehydrated people to water containers, yet draws water back through its finger capillaries if they drink beyond the marked measure.

### Threat by Stage
On alert, it strips a thin film of water from exposed skin; during lockdown, it slows movement by freezing patches of floor; under overpressure, it bursts its storage sac, spreading conductive water and rapidly chilled steam.

### Countermeasures and Combat
Sending gentle streams of warm, dry air from several directions makes its cooling plates fold and stops its condensation attacks. A single strong heat source, however, gathers all the shepherds in one spot and provokes concentrated water reclamation.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
If `HC08` supplies a white graduated container and a measured amount of saltwater, the shepherd remembers the markings as the terms of communal distribution, provides drinking water to refugees, and preserves the cooling wall. But if humans draw water beyond the markings, it freezes the ward's condensation pipes in the next cycle.

### Scenario Connections
In `G08-SC1`, it helps restart the cooling system; in `G08-SC2`, it distributes a limited water supply; and in `G08-SC3`, it regulates abrupt humidity changes caused by `XT03`. It references the state axes `S08` and `S13` and the world axes `H08` and `HC08`.

/monster_contents/M012/entries/6/bestiar.en: The Electrostatic Sorter applies charges to friction plates on its forearms and comb-like spinal spines to draw out metal, polymers, and glass separately. Unable to detect anything more than four steps away or any grounded material, it classifies operating medical devices as high-value materials like spent batteries.

/monster_contents/M012/entries/6/prose.en:
### Role and Physiology
A material-recovery specialist among the Cleanroom Mutants, it applies different charges to the friction plates on its forearms and its comb-shaped spinal spines to draw metal components, polymer fragments, and glass powder separately from waste heaps.

### Origin
The `H08` log records that, while the `S08` materials-management crew sorted contaminated tools without touching them, electrostatic equipment fused with their skin nerves and the sorting behavior became autonomous.

### Habitat
It patrols the materials handover room and discarded-tool racks of `S08`. As seasonal dryness intensifies, it moves to `S13` workshops that still have grounding equipment, avoiding the discharge risk amplified by `XT03`.

### Needs and Desires
It needs dry fibers and insulating wax to maintain its friction plates, and one charge lets it sort only about twenty items. It cannot detect objects more than four steps away or grounded materials.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
Charge blotches from the settling stage form comb-like spines in the budding stage. After the functional and migration stages, a recovery-stage individual lays its body down in a nest of sorted polymers, but no buds develop if wax and metal fragments are scarce.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
The individual that creates the purest pile of materials gets first access to charging. Because it reads only charge types, it classifies operating medical devices and spent batteries as the same high-value material and tries to carry them away.

### Threat by Stage
On alert, it leaves an opposite-charge mark on equipment; during the recovery stage, it pulls metal items from people's hands; during the discharge stage, it flicks collected parts from between its spinal spines, firing them along short diagonal paths.

### Countermeasures and Combat
A dense grounding mesh laid across the floor, together with ceramic tools, eliminates its pulling force. Spraying a sudden mist of water, however, makes its stored charge jump to every nearby piece of metal, creating unpredictable arcs.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
If `HC08` provides a box of discharged scrap parts with a three-scrape friction sound, the sorter preserves the matching scratch mark as a condition of delivery and returns usable tools. But if an active battery is hidden in a marked box, it subsequently treats all human equipment as subject to confiscation.

### Scenario Connections
In `G08-SC1`, it recovers parts for repairs; in `G08-SC2`, it disputes ownership of medical devices and facility materials; and in `G08-SC3`, it serves as a means of suppressing the electrostatic chain reaction amplified by `XT03`. It follows state IDs `S08` and `S13` and world links `H08` and `HC08`.

/monster_contents/M012/entries/7/bestiar.en: The Afterglow Recorder etches warning-light flashes and sequences of movement in layers onto photosensitive scars and hardened fingernails. Seeing only brightness and outlines, it cannot distinguish people with the same build, and when a new bright light appears, it tries to cover the light source.

/monster_contents/M012/entries/7/prose.en:
### Role and Physiology
A preserver of events among the Cleanroom Mutants, it etches warning-light flashes, object outlines, and sequences of movement as layered traces onto photosensitive scars on its skin and fingernails hardened like lenses.

### Origin
As `S08` personnel who managed the `H08` log were repeatedly exposed to residual contamination and sterilizing light, their memory circuits shifted into photochemical reactions in the epidermis.

### Habitat
It builds up recording layers around `S08` observation windows and emergency lights. When seasonal power outages strike, it avoids areas where `XT03` pressure has made light sources unstable and moves to the daylit room in `S13`.

### Needs and Desires
Fixing a recording requires ultraviolet exposure and a protein membrane, and one area of skin can hold only seven scenes. Seeing only brightness and outlines, it cannot distinguish people with the same build.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
A light spot from the settling stage receives a memory fragment in the budding stage, and events are imprinted during the functional stage. After the migration stage, a recovery-stage individual sheds and leaves behind its skin film, but without a stable light source and a nutrient membrane, the next generation's spots disappear.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
The recorder with the oldest light layer sets the order of testimony. When a new bright light appears, it tries to wrap the source in cloth to prevent its recordings from becoming saturated, even at the expense of addressing the immediate danger.

### Threat by Stage
On alert, it disrupts distance perception with crossing flashes; during lockdown, its reflective skin creates multiple outlines of the exit; under overpressure, it releases stored sterilizing light in one direction, burning exposed tissue.

### Countermeasures and Combat
Under dim red light, its imprinting response slows and it cannot overwrite existing scenes. A complete blackout triggers a group rush toward the last bright-light location it saw.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
If `HC08` indicates scene numbers with hand gestures under a red light and provides a protein membrane, the recorder marks the specified sequence along the film's edge and plays it back. But if humans erase a scene they promised to preserve, it overlays the outlines of human faces with danger markings.

### Scenario Connections
In `G08-SC1`, it gives limited testimony about an accident scene; in `G08-SC2`, it keeps conflicting records; and in `G08-SC3`, it serves as a key to filling gaps in `H08`. State IDs `S08` and `S13`, world link `HC08`, and external-pressure variable `XT03` form its verification network.

/monster_contents/M012/entries/8/bestiar.en: The Sterile-Line Adjudicator displays a contact subject's microbial reaction as colored bands on the culture plate in its palm. The color reaction remains visible only briefly after contact, causing it to confuse latent infections with traces of treatment; if a reading matches a senior adjudicator's color band, it enforces quarantine even when an error comes to light.

/monster_contents/M012/entries/8/prose.en:
### Role and Physiology
An entry adjudicator among the Cleanroom Mutants, it uses color-changing tendrils around its neck and culture plates in its palms to display a contact subject's microbial reaction as brief bands of color.

### Origin
The `H08` log reveals that `S08` specimen managers accumulated testing reagents in their bodies and developed an obsessive function: comparing biological surfaces against reference colors.

### Habitat
It occupies the sterile boundary of `S08` like a courtroom. When seasonal changes in microbial flora begin, it migrates to the `S13` checkpoint section to correct reference errors caused by `XT03` pressure.

### Needs and Desires
Each culture plate requires nutrient gel and a reference sample and must be discarded after twelve readings. A color reaction remains visible for only thirty seconds after contact, causing it to confuse latent infections with traces of treatment.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
Reading stains from the settling stage develop tendrils in the budding stage. After the functional and migration stages, a recovery-stage individual hardens into a reference culture plate, but without fresh samples, the next generation's range of color judgments is halved.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
Authority comes from a long-preserved reference chart rather than actual accuracy. If a reading matches a senior adjudicator's color band, it continues to enforce a quarantine ruling even when an error is revealed.

### Threat by Stage
On alert, it leaves an expulsion color on the skin; during the quarantine stage, it confines the subject of its ruling inside a movable membrane; under overpressure, it sprays reference reagent, sharply stimulating the immune responses of those exposed.

### Countermeasures and Combat
Presenting a sterile decoy and then a contaminated one to produce opposing colors halts the adjudication procedure. Breaking a culture plate, however, causes it to treat everyone not yet tested as the highest-risk color.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
If `HC08` presents a standard glass bottle, fresh reference samples, and a color-band chart together, the adjudicator preserves the arrangement of grooves on the bottle as a valid rule, reducing the introduction of infections on both sides. But if humans let someone pass without testing, it requarantines everyone covered by the agreement.

### Scenario Connections
In `G08-SC1`, it screens those crossing the sterile line; in `G08-SC2`, it enforces quarantine policy; and in `G08-SC3`, it is the starting point for the spread of adjudication errors. It is linked to the state axes `S08` and `S13`, the world axes `H08` and `HC08`, and the external-pressure axis `XT03`.

/monster_contents/M012/entries/9/bestiar.en: The Circulating-Air Conductor is a colony-breathing symbiont whose twin bellows lungs in its chest and clavicle whistles have taken on the control of air-handling equipment. It cannot hear sounds as speech, distinguishing them only as pressure beats; if its command tone stops, subordinate specialists all spring into action at once.

/monster_contents/M012/entries/9/prose.en:
### Role and Physiology
