A coordinator of group breathing among the Cleanroom Mutants, it uses twin bellows lungs in its chest and split clavicle whistles to carry rhythmic signals through the airflow, synchronizing the movement and rest of specialist individuals.

### Origin
The `S08` air-handling control personnel in the `H08` log took on equipment-control functions in their respiratory organs after exposure to residual contamination and prolonged low-oxygen conditions.

### Habitat
It makes the `S08` central circulation room its main home. When the seasonal pressure band reverses, it calculates the overpressure risk heightened by `XT03` and moves the group to a reserved section of `S13`.

### Needs and Desires
Its bellows lungs require oxygen-adsorbent material and six hours of stillness each day, and it cannot direct others continuously for more than ten minutes. It cannot hear sounds as speech, distinguishing them only as pressure beats.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
Chest vibrations develop in the settling stage, and it makes its first breathing sound in the budding stage. After the functional and migration stages, a recovery-stage individual remains as a communal air sac. If adsorbent material is scarce, however, it only prolongs the existing group's breathing instead of producing new buds.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
The conductor that keeps the greatest number of specialists in rhythm rises in rank. If its command tone stops, subordinate individuals all perform their respective functions at once, rapidly consuming corridor space and resources.

### Threat by Stage
On alert, it drives intruders away with a slow offbeat that removes oxygen; during lockdown, it uses crosswinds to push people and projectiles into a designated section; under overpressure, it makes its bellows lungs resonate, shaking fixtures in the ventilation shaft.

### Countermeasures and Combat
Sending two mismatched low-frequency beats from opposite corridors splits its command network into two groups. If only the conductor is brought down, the remaining specialists each seize different parts of the air-handling equipment.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
If `HC08` provides a four-beat whistle signal and oxygen-adsorbent material, the conductor remembers the breathing time for a human refugee procession as a schedule and separates the two sides' movements. But if humans use the blower longer than their allotted time, it reverses the ward's ventilation in the next cycle.

### Scenario Connections
In `G08-SC1`, it directs the reorganization of the air-handling network; in `G08-SC2`, it coordinates the seasonal migration to `S13`; and in `G08-SC3`, it suppresses the overpressure chain reaction caused by `XT03`. State IDs `S08` and `S13` and world links `H08` and `HC08` form the basis for negotiation.

/monster_contents/M013/entries/0/bestiar.en: Sterile-Membrane Weavers work together to install a biological membrane made from fibers produced by their four-pronged wrist glands, complete with passageways and specimen windows. They cannot identify pathogen types or distant sources of contamination; they only maintain the difference in particle concentration on either side of an agreed boundary.

/monster_contents/M013/entries/0/prose.en:
### Role and Body
A cleanroom mutant that works with others to install translucent biological membranes dividing spaces by contamination level. Four-pronged wrist glands produce differently colored fibers, which rotating protrusions on the ribs weave into a boundary membrane with passageways and specimen-transfer windows.

### Origin
They arose when a work crew that frequently rearranged isolation zones fused with movable barriers. They receive a neural reward response not from stopping a leak itself, but from maintaining the difference in particle concentration on either side of an agreed boundary.

### Habitat
They form colonies in positive-pressure room antechambers, at laboratory intersections, and along movable partition rails. Sensory hairs on their wrists can compare only acidity and particle counts within two steps; they cannot identify pathogen types or distant sources of contamination.

### Needs and Desires
Maintaining each section of membrane requires a plate of protein paste and mildly alkaline water. If food runs out, they reclaim the passageways first, and they do not create a partition larger than their stores can support.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
Juveniles separate from the edge of an existing membrane after six wetting cycles, and only two grow to maturity on a given membrane in a season. Adults must also eat old fibers to empty their wrist glands, so they cannot maintain every boundary permanently.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
When a user flashes a blue light three times and marks a boundary on the floor, a representative signals agreement with yellow pulses in the same sequence. The representative records passage times, food quantities, and the number of people permitted in the direction of the knots; the colony can distinguish the three most recent contracts.

### Escalating Threat
In the agreement stage, they merely surround the marked line. When resources run short, they narrow the promised passageways. In the trespass stage, they attach a violator’s equipment to the membrane to restrict movement. If someone deliberately crosses the boundary or misses two feedings, the colony stops pulsing yellow and reclaims the entire membrane, allowing contamination from both sides to mix.

### Countermeasures and Combat
Someone who reads the knot records and passes at the agreed time can get through without contact. Forcibly cutting the membrane makes the connected fibers contract toward the passageways, so the safe way to remove it is to stop its food supply and dry it from the edges inward.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
If offered the proposal signal of three blue flashes, a boundary plan, and a plate of food per shift, the colony divides the designated area, giving people a safe route for specimens. If the user breaks the terms, the weavers exclude the violator from the next contract and withdraw the membrane. Increasing the number of people rescued therefore requires either additional food from stores or a reduction in an existing refuge zone.

### Scenario Connections
In G08-SC1, H08’s knot reading and HC08’s guarantee of food are needed to repartition the contaminated area of the Noryangjin Line. In G08-SC3, XT03’s external pressure variable destabilizes the particle boundary, requiring a reduction in the contracted area.

/monster_contents/M013/entries/1/bestiar.en: Filter-Bone Feeders select and compress only the one metal specified by a salt marker inside a discarded filter frame. They are animals that anchor their bodies to a frame, not to a location, and let organic dust and spores pass between their bone teeth.

/monster_contents/M013/entries/1/prose.en:
### Role and Body
A cleanroom mutant that enters discarded filter frames to select and recover a specific mineral. The magnetic bone teeth on its spreading ribs catch whichever one of iron, nickel, or chromium is specified by a salt marker, and a separation pouch in its neck compresses it into a small lump of ore.

### Origin
It arose when the marrow of a worker recovering rare metals fused with an analytical filter grid. It cannot purify air: organic dust, spores, and liquid contaminants pass straight between its bone teeth.

### Habitat
It anchors its body inside standard frames in spent-cartridge storerooms and at disassembly benches. Its tongue can find only deposits at least the size of a fingernail on a single filter it touches, and cannot distinguish plated equipment from solid metal.

### Needs and Desires
It needs a handful of the designated mineral and a bottle of saline to wash its bone teeth each day. Eating different metals in succession hardens its separation pouch, so workers must allow a day of rest between recovery targets.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
A larva attaches to one empty filter frame and becomes an adult after processing eight cartridges. An adult uses half its accumulated minerals to produce only two bone eggs in its lifetime, and the eggs will not hatch without a frame.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
Individuals prefer different minerals and set their working order by the color of the frame’s salt marker. The adult with the most intact bone teeth takes possession of the ore outlet; an individual given the wrong metal scratches the frame with its claws to signal that work has stopped.

### Escalating Threat
During sorting, it moves only within the frame. When metals are mixed in, it tears at nearby plated panels. When its separation pouch is blocked, it spits sharp metal fragments. Mixing two minerals under the same salt marker causes a blockage fastest.

### Countermeasures and Combat
Installing an empty standard frame with the correct salt marker can draw an individual away from equipment. A powerful magnet pulls both its bone teeth and the compressed ore, rupturing its ribs, so filters must be removed one at a time with nonmagnetic ceramic tongs.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
If workers repeatedly show a colored salt marker twice and then offer a test piece containing the same metal, an individual remembers the combination for twelve jobs. People recover rare minerals and the feeder gets food, but if the promised purity is violated, it rejects that color and tears out equipment parts made of the same metal. Workers must then decide whether to surrender medical equipment or repair materials.

### Scenario Connections
In G08-SC2, examining the Noryangjin Line’s discarded frames allows G08E10’s sorting target to be chosen according to H08’s materials records and HC08’s allocation plan. In G08-SC3, XT03’s external dust pressure increases the rate of material mixing in the filters, threatening the contracted purity.

/monster_contents/M013/entries/2/bestiar.en: The Differential-Pressure Pulse Gatekeeper is an airlock symbiont formed when a diaphragm fused with an emergency valve. When a door opens, three inflatable sacs in its abdomen release stored air in portions toward the lower-pressure side. It cannot detect movement on rubber sheeting or beyond a closed compartment.

/monster_contents/M013/entries/2/prose.en:
### Role and Body
A cleanroom mutant that uses its body to regulate pressure between rooms. Three inflatable sacs in its abdomen store air and release it in portions toward the lower-pressure side when a door opens.

### Origin
It formed when the diaphragm of a worker who survived a sudden depressurization accident fused with an emergency valve. Its pain receptors changed to function like a barometer, causing it to interpret a large pressure imbalance as a signal of attack.

### Habitat
It occupies the center of an airlock and the narrow space between double doors. The soles of its feet can read vibrations only across three sections of connected metal floor, so it cannot detect movement on rubber sheeting or people beyond a closed compartment.

### Needs and Desires
Each day it needs two containers of saline water and one sac of air warmer than body temperature. A single buffering action uses half its stored air, so it cannot let many people through in quick succession.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
Young with only one sac grow by receiving air released by adults, and only one young member of a group survives each year. An elderly individual whose third sac has hardened anchors itself at an exhaust vent, buffers the remaining pressure once, and dies.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
The individual with the largest sac sets the order in which doors open and close, while subordinates tap the pipes to report pressure changes. Three short strikes followed by one long strike request passage; the same sounds in reverse order signal approval.

### Escalating Threat
During equilibrium, it watches the space between the doors. During an imbalance, it pushes intruders back with localized bursts of air. At the rupture stage, it releases all its stored air at once. If the pressure gauge exceeds the permitted range twice, it revokes even a previous approval.

### Countermeasures and Combat
Alternately opening each door by a finger’s width to equalize the readings relaxes its inflatable sacs. Piercing a sac creates a blast in the enclosed space, so it is safer to secure the creature with floor restraints and open the exhaust valve slowly.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
If the request rhythm, the amount of saline water offered, and the number of people seeking passage are presented in front of the pressure gauge, the gatekeeper remembers that number for the next three door operations. If more people enter than promised, it immediately closes the door and refuses approval for the next cycle. Moving additional injured people therefore requires giving up oxygen from another compartment or the remaining saline water.

### Scenario Connections
G08-SC1 addresses both restoring differential pressure on the Noryangjin Line and G08E11’s survival, requiring H08’s instrument records and HC08’s mediation of passage. In G08-SC2, XT03’s external shock variable disrupts the approved sequence for opening and closing the doors.

/monster_contents/M013/entries/3/bestiar.en: The White-Light Molting Guide excises tissue damaged by sterilizing light only with the patient’s consent. Without the white handle and black stop button, it cannot establish a safe boundary, and it cannot detect tissue beneath clothing.

/monster_contents/M013/entries/3/prose.en:
### Role and Body
A cleanroom mutant that excises tissue damaged by sterilizing light with the patient’s consent. Its transparent eyelids channel ultraviolet light into fluorescent vessels, while its finger-mounted blade claws perform excisions and a wrist shield stops them immediately.

### Origin
It arose when skin-treatment tissue exposed to prolonged light decontamination overdeveloped its ability to identify damaged cells. Some pigmentation and scars in healthy tissue produce similar fluorescence, so it cannot establish a safe boundary without the patient’s instructions.

### Habitat
It stays in corridors where sterilizing lights cross and in examination rooms with reflective panels. Its eyelids can read fluorescence only on the skin’s surface within three steps; it cannot detect tissue under clothing, internal bleeding, or conditions beneath matte bandages.

### Needs and Desires
Each procedure requires a brief charge from sterilizing light and a handful of dead tissue. After more than three procedures in a day, its fluorescent vessels become oversaturated, and it will not begin an excision without sterile water to cool its blade claws.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
Young individuals collect only light until their fourth molt, when they acquire blade claws and wrist shields. Once in its lifetime, an adult buries two pairs of used blade claws to produce one juvenile; it cannot reproduce without sterile soil.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
It takes one pull of the white handle by a patient as consent to the procedure, and two pulls as a request to narrow its scope. Pressing the black stop button or making a low, sustained sound causes a mechanical latch to close the wrist shield and physically confine the blade claws. No leader can override this stop.

### Escalating Threat
While waiting, it does not touch anyone without a consent signal. During assessment, it scans only within the approved line. During an error, reflected light widens the area of excision. If it becomes overcharged while the stop button is broken, it continuously assesses nearby pigmentation, making even an approach dangerous.

### Countermeasures and Combat
Covering reflective surfaces with matte cloth and fitting a portable stop button into the groove on its wrist can disable its ability to excise. Flashing red light disrupts its assessment but makes the boundaries of multiple patients appear to overlap, so it must not be used as a lure for long.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
If given a white handle and black stop button for each patient, along with an excision line drawn on the skin, the guide preserves those conditions for one procedure and provides treatment in exchange for eating necrotic tissue. It withdraws immediately if the patient stops the procedure, and a guardian who interferes with that stop is excluded from the next procedure. A patient’s refusal cannot be ignored on the grounds of preventing infection from spreading.

### Scenario Connections
In G08-SC2, the Noryangjin Line’s light network and H08’s exposure records are used to determine a safe charge, while HC08 verifies that the consent device works. In G08-SC3, XT03’s external exposure variable changes patients’ fluorescent responses, requiring renewed consent.

/monster_contents/M013/entries/4/bestiar.en: The Reagent-Bile Neutralizer is an aging mutant that alternately swallows acidic and alkaline reagents and turns them into neutral precipitate. Its tongue can classify only the acidity of liquids within one step into three ranges; it cannot distinguish a concentrate from a bodily fluid with the same acidity.

/monster_contents/M013/entries/4/prose.en:
### Role and Body
A cleanroom mutant that alternately swallows spilled acidic and alkaline reagents, turning them into neutral precipitate. Its two-chambered stomach and color-changing abdominal scales reveal which reactant it currently needs and how much it can still process.

### Origin
It arose when gut microbes used to treat chemical burns formed a symbiosis with a decontaminant, transforming the entire digestive system into a mobile neutralization tank. When the balance fails, its bodily fluids also shift toward one extreme and corrode surrounding materials.

### Habitat
It moves between washroom drains and the lower parts of reagent storerooms, following the slope of the floor. Its tongue can classify only the acidity of liquids within one step into three ranges; it cannot distinguish a concentrate from a bodily fluid with the same acidity.

### Needs and Desires
It must consume one bottle each of acid and base in a prescribed sequence to preserve the linings of both stomach chambers. When the sand container for discharging buffered precipitate is full, it stops further neutralization.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
Larvae eat twelve handfuls of neutral precipitate to acquire symbiotic bacteria, and adults harden one bile egg only when balanced. An individual produces just three bile eggs in its lifetime; all become inactive if the supply of the opposing reagent is cut off.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
The individual whose abdominal scales are closest to green regulates the feeding order. If a worker signals twice with a triangular plate for acid or a circular plate for base, the group lines up before the corresponding container. After processing is complete, the worker turns over the same plate to signal the end.

### Escalating Threat
When balanced, it eats only marked spills. When its balance shifts, it breaks containers in search of the opposing reagent. In the reversal stage, it sprays corrosive bile in a brief mist. If three consecutive sections of its abdominal scales show the same color, it must be buffered before it feeds again.

### Countermeasures and Combat
Giving it cups of dilute solution with the opposing property at intervals can reduce its aggression. Pouring in a strong neutralizing agent all at once causes a boiling reaction in both stomach chambers and spreads the bile spray.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
If workers repeatedly provide a shape plate, a bottle of reagent, and a precipitate container that is not full, the group remembers the sequence for six jobs. People reclaim the spill area and the neutralizer preserves its stomach lining. But if it receives a reagent different from the one marked, it breaks the plate and bites the supplier, forcing people to share limited buffering solution with burn patients.

### Scenario Connections
In G08-SC1, HC08 allocates the Noryangjin Line’s remaining reagents between survivors and G08E13, while H08 provides a concentration chart for each shape. The neutralization work in G08-SC2 requires shorter shifts as XT03’s external chemical pressure increases in G08-SC3.

/monster_contents/M013/entries/5/bestiar.en: The Electrostatic-Fur Dust-Collecting Pilgrim is a symbiont whose particle-removal fibers have bonded to its nerve sheaths, allowing it to collect metal dust and spores with static electricity. Its whiskers detect only conductors within twice its body length, and it cannot find powered-off equipment made of synthetic resin.

/monster_contents/M013/entries/5/prose.en:
### Role and Body
A cleanroom mutant that collects metal dust and spores through static electricity as it follows a set route among the equipment. Glassy hairs along its spine generate frictional charge, and a grounding spike on its tail deposits what it collects onto a metal plate.

### Origin
Particle-removal fibers bonded to its nerve sheaths, allowing it to read changes in electric fields instead of using touch. When its electrical potential rises too high, it cannot distinguish its own muscle commands from external electrical stimuli.

### Habitat
It makes its rounds in a fixed order along cable trays, behind equipment racks, and at the edges of conductive floors. Its whiskers detect only conductors within twice its body length; it cannot find wires beyond an insulating wall or powered-off equipment made of synthetic resin.

### Needs and Desires
Each circuit requires one bundle of dry fibers and an empty grounding plate. One plate can receive the charge of only three individuals, and a saturated plate cannot be reused until it is replaced.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
Young eat metal dust from clumps of hair shed by adults to develop insulating skin. A breeding adult leaves one grounding spike as a nest electrode and raises no more than two young; afterward, its discharge capacity is halved.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
The individual maintaining the lowest electrical potential chooses the route, while overcharged members fall to the rear. If a worker taps a grounding plate three times and then unfurls a green band, they take it as a signal to begin their pilgrimage and follow that route for the next two circuits.

### Escalating Threat
During the pilgrimage stage, they only sweep surfaces. During charge accumulation, they shut down nearby electronic equipment. During the flashover stage, they send current between two conductors. Insulating suits prevent contact but can eliminate opportunities to ground the charge, increasing the eventual discharge.

### Countermeasures and Combat
Placing a movable grounding plate ahead of them to drain charge gradually lets people collect the recovered material without fighting. Spraying water broadens the discharge path, so dry ceramic shields should first be used to separate the individuals.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
If offered a green band, three taps, and an empty grounding plate in the same sequence, the pilgrims remember the route, remove contamination from equipment, and gain a safe place to discharge. If the promised plate is removed, they mark that corridor as dangerous for one cycle and discharge directly into power lines. People must then choose whether to remove a breeding nest to restore power or give up a bypass circuit.

### Scenario Connections
In G08-SC3, XT03’s external electrical pressure variable increases G08E14’s rate of charge accumulation, while the Noryangjin Line’s grounding network slows it. In G08-SC1, H08’s pilgrimage records and HC08’s power allocation determine whether the nest is preserved.

/monster_contents/M013/entries/6/bestiar.en: The Suture-Pouch Nursery Keeper is a battlefield caregiver that carries other mutants’ larvae and damaged organs in six pouches on its back. The sensory chambers in its pouches hear only internal heartbeats and cannot perceive voices or gestures even beyond a single layer of cloth.

/monster_contents/M013/entries/6/prose.en:
### Role and Physiology
A colony nursery keeper that carries other cleanroom mutants’ larvae and damaged organs for a limited period. The six sutured pouches on its back maintain different temperatures and oxygen concentrations, while enzymes at the tip of its tongue suppress short-term rejection.

### Origin
Mutated tissue trapped in an organ-transplant culture tank bonded with its host’s back muscles and became a mobile growth chamber. In exchange for accepting other lives, its own immune system and ability to heal wounds were greatly reduced.

### Habitat
It nests in preparation rooms with little temperature variation and culture sections with emergency power remaining. The pouches’ sensory chambers hear only the pulses inside them and cannot detect voices or gestures even a single layer of cloth away, so signals must be shown at the eye panel in front.

### Needs and Desires
For each filled pouch, it consumes one packet of sugar, one oxygen cartridge, and one sheet of sterile cloth per day. If supplies run short, it digests the contents least likely to survive first, but it cannot accept more subjects than it has empty pouches.

### Life Cycle and Upkeep
A juvenile is born with two empty pouches and receives an adult’s enzymes to grow as many as six. An adult can detach one empty pouch to raise as offspring only once in its lifetime; it does not reproduce if all its pouches are full or infected.

### Behavior and Rank
The number of lives in its care determines its rank, but each pouch entrance bears a separate retrieval tag. If a guardian shows the retrieval tag and makes two short sounds, it opens only the corresponding pouch; if someone tries to take out different contents instead, it closes its back plate.

### Threat by Stage
In the stable stage, it warns approaching people through its eye panel. In the deprivation stage, it takes marked medical supplies. In the hunger stage, it seizes creatures without retrieval tags as candidates for empty pouches. Attacking a pouch triggers a protective reflex, but pulling the oxygen shutoff handle locks every pouch and stops the body from moving as well.

### Countermeasures and Combat
Placing nutrient solution proportionate to the number of pouches and a valid retrieval tag in front of it can induce it to distribute supplies voluntarily and return a patient. Anesthetic reaches the contents first, so to subdue the body, its eye panel must be covered and its leg joints immobilized.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
If given a retrieval tag inscribed with the care period, pouch number, and daily supply amount, the nursery keeper remembers the terms for up to three days, and the guardian gains time for the patient to survive. If supplies or the retrieval time are missed, it refuses the next request and claims the remaining contents for the colony. The choice is whether to concentrate limited oxygen on a human patient or keep the promise to save a rare larva as well.

### Scenario Connections
In G08-SC2, H08’s pouch records and HC08’s mediation over retrieval tags allow the patient in G08E15 to be returned from the Noryangjin Line’s culture section. In G08-SC3, XT03’s external resource pressure reduces the oxygen supply and disrupts care priorities.

/monster_contents/M013/entries/7/bestiar.en: The Protocol-Mimicking Gatekeeper is a local mutant neurally connected to an automatic authentication device. It reproduces the Bestiary Gatekeeper’s entry procedures through gestures. It remembers the order of the procedures but does not understand why the rules were created, and it does not accept instructions from beyond a wall as authentication.

/monster_contents/M013/entries/7/prose.en:
### Role and Physiology
A cleanroom mutant that remembers and reenacts entry procedures through gestures to prevent unauthorized passage into quarantine sections. The muscle plates on its face imitate symbols and hand movements, while a resonance chamber in its sternum distinguishes approval tones from alarm tones.

### Origin
Quarantine personnel undergoing repeated training changed after being neurally connected to an automatic authentication device, coming to treat compliance with the rules as a survival instinct. It remembers the order of the procedures but does not understand why the rules were created.

### Habitat
It patrols closed checkpoints and double-authentication doors, stepping only on designated footprints. Its sight is limited to four paces within the floor markings, and its resonance chamber can identify sounds only in the same room, so it does not accept instructions from beyond a wall as authentication.

### Needs and Desires
A complete response sequence and the prescribed alarm tone must be entered once a day to keep its memory circuits stable. After three days without an update, it forgets everything except the last procedure it completed successfully.

### Life Cycle and Upkeep
In youth, it imitates only one action; as it matures, it can string together up to seven steps. Only one memory fragment shed from an aged individual’s muscle plate can be implanted in the next individual, so each generation preserves only one protocol.

### Behavior and Rank
The individual that can reenact the longest procedure without interruption occupies the door, while the others perform witness gestures on either side. If an applicant presents a palm mark, a spoken passphrase, and a departure time in that order, the gatekeeper sounds its sternum twice to confirm the terms.

### Threat by Stage
In the verification stage, it demands the gestures. In the error stage, it blocks the way back. In the violation stage, it fixes an intruder’s joints in the prescribed posture. If the approved departure time passes, the gatekeeper registers those inside as contaminated holdovers and will not accept the same mark again.

### Countermeasures and Combat
Reenacting a previous procedure from beginning to end can elicit the movements for safe passage. Presenting two contradictory protocols at once makes it stop briefly, but may damage its memory fragment and cause it to attack even lawful visitors afterward.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
If offered a recognizable mark and passphrase, the number of people passing through, and a return time, the gatekeeper preserves the terms for three round trips, allowing people to move without breaking the lockdown. If someone abuses an exceptional authorization, it permanently revokes that exception and bars the guarantor as well. The choice is whether to rescue someone trapped immediately or preserve the checkpoint’s long-term order.

### Scenario Connections
In G08-SC1, H08 restores the procedure remembered by G08E16, and HC08 guarantees an exception for the Noryangjin Line. The lockdown order in G08-SC2 conflicts with XT03’s external pressure variable in G08-SC3, requiring the protocol to be updated.

/monster_contents/M013/entries/8/bestiar.en: The Cold-Vein Spore Carrier is a host-fungal mutant that lowers the temperature of sealed spores with frost sacs inside its ribs. It is not the Bestiary’s commander of the three temperature chambers; it remembers only the direction of the next cold point and the allotted supply, not the destination.

/monster_contents/M013/entries/8/prose.en:
### Role and Physiology
A humanoid mutant that transports sealed, viable spores between refrigerated distribution networks. Frost sacs inside its ribs lower the cargo’s temperature, and vascular bundles in its arms circulate a limited supply of coolant around the containers.

### Origin
It arose when host tissue and a preservation fungus bonded hastily during a breakdown in cold-chain distribution. When the symbiosis becomes unstable, the human’s memories of transport and the mycelium’s urge to disperse pull the body in different directions.

### Habitat
It makes the Mapo Union its primary habitat and travels to the Seongbuk Line’s cold points in seasons when cooling equipment weakens. Its sense of smell detects only frozen spores within one pace, and beyond two paces it loses sight of the outlines of things hotter than body temperature.

### Needs and Desires
For each day of transport, it consumes one canister of coolant, two packets of sugar, and one bottle of live symbiotic culture. Its stored fat can fuel only three days of travel, so if an intermediate cold point disappears, it cannot take a long detour.

### Life Cycle and Upkeep
Its life cycle has five stages: dormant spore, infiltrating larva, symbiotic adult, fruiting walker, and collapsing disperser. One adult can carry four fruiting sacs, and only a sac that completes the journey produces the next larva, so cargo losses reduce reproduction.

### Behavior and Rank
The carrier with the most stable frost sacs sets the convoy’s cold points and rest times. It accepts a container only when the three-tone transport signal learned at H09 matches the frost tag; it remembers the direction of the next cold point and the allotted supply, not the destination.

### Threat by Stage
Dormant spores cause contact contamination; infiltrating larvae steal body heat; symbiotic adults capture prey as a group; fruiting walkers release short bursts of cold; and collapsing dispersers release spores over a wide area. Forcing one to keep moving after its coolant runs out hastens the final stage.

### Countermeasures and Combat
Presenting an empty sealed container at a steady temperature like a shield can prompt the cargo handover procedure. Rapid heating only increases mycelial activity and extinguishes the host’s remaining judgment, so the coolant valve must be closed gradually and the members of the convoy separated.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
If the three-tone signal, a frost-tagged container, and a coolant delivery time are presented together, the carrier remembers the terms for two route segments and carries dangerous cargo in place of people. If no cold point is provided or the promised culture inside the container is changed, it puts down the cargo and steals the guarantor’s body heat. The choice is whether to reduce the refrigerated supply for medicines or the amount reserved for the transport contract.

### Scenario Connections
G09-SC1 verifies H09’s transport records at a Mapo Union cold point and uses HC09 to make terms with G09E01. In G09-SC2, seasonal migration toward the Seongbuk Line accelerates because of XT04’s external pressure variable, putting the coolant promise at risk.

/monster_contents/M013/entries/9/bestiar.en: The Thawing Mycelium Regulator uses the paired vocal cords in its neck to slow mycelial metabolism and antifreeze blood vessels in its palms to warm contact areas little by little, delaying indiscriminate germination. It can distinguish mycelial vibrations only within three floor spaces and mistakes a motionless person for an empty culture platform.

/monster_contents/M013/entries/9/prose.en:
### Role and Physiology
A humanoid mutant that regulates the rate at which spore hosts thaw in stages, delaying the collapse of their symbiosis and indiscriminate germination. The paired vocal cords in its neck emit low frequencies that slow mycelial metabolism, while antifreeze blood vessels in its palms warm contact areas little by little.

### Origin
It arose when regulatory tissue treating people infected with refrigerated spores became mutually dependent on the fungus. When the symbiosis becomes unstable, human nerves demand cooling and the mycelium demands thawing, making the body tremble at short intervals.

### Habitat
It normally guards the thawing rooms of the Mapo Union and, when the cold season ends, follows groups of hosts to temporary clinics on the Seongbuk Line. Its hearing distinguishes mycelial vibrations only within three floor spaces, and its distance vision is blurry, causing it to mistake motionless people for empty culture platforms.

### Needs and Desires
Each treatment requires one bottle of chilled water, one packet of antifreeze sugar, and one cup of trace alcohol excreted by the symbiotic fungus. It stores enough antifreeze sugar for only five treatments, and continuous treatment without replenishment splits its paired vocal cords.

### Life Cycle and Upkeep
Its five stages are cooling embryo, awakened mycelial form, regulatory adult, thawing spawner, and symbiotic collapse form. A regulatory adult can produce a thawing spawner only twice in its lifetime, and sharing too many resources causes it to enter the collapse stage itself.

### Behavior and Rank
Rank is determined not by the number of hosts treated but by the number of times an individual has delayed collapse for an agreed period. If a patient or guardian sounds a low drum twice, then a high bell once, and points out the treatment order, the leading individual responds in the same rhythm.

### Threat by Stage
A cooling embryo absorbs body heat on contact; an awakened mycelial form binds joints; and a regulatory adult causes low-frequency disorientation. A thawing spawner spreads germination through contact, while a symbiotic collapse form consumes all remaining cold points and leaves a cloud of toxic mycelium.

### Countermeasures and Combat
Providing the agreed rhythm together with a small amount of antifreeze sugar allows its vocal-cord modulation waves to be synchronized from outside. Covering the ears does not stop the low frequencies from traveling through the skeleton, so floor connecting plates must be separated and enough distance kept that vibrations cannot reach.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
If the treatment subjects’ marks, priorities, and the amount of antifreeze sugar to be supplied are presented with the signal, the regulator remembers the terms for five treatments, buying the hosts time before collapse. If the order is changed or the payment reduced, it will not answer the next beat and will protect only the patients agreed upon first. The choice is how to allocate limited resources between one person whose sense of self remains and many on the verge of collapse.

### Scenario Connections
G09-SC2 distributes G09E02’s antifreeze sugar at the Seongbuk Line’s mobile clinic, using H09’s medical records and HC09’s mediation over priorities. In G09-SC3, XT04’s external pressure variable breaks the Mapo Union’s thawing order, causing several life stages to appear at once.

/monster_contents/M014/entries/0/bestiar.en: The Cooling-Vein Carrier is a cold-chain mutant that transports concentrated brine using two cooling sacs on its back and mycelial pumps in its forearms. Its duties overlap with those of the Cold-Vein Spore Carrier, but where there is no connected piping, it never strays more than ten steps before returning to its starting point.

/monster_contents/M014/entries/0/prose.en:
### Role and Body
A humanoid mutant that transports concentrated brine using two cooling sacs on its back and mycelial pumps in its forearms. When one sac empties, its body tilts in that direction; when the pressure difference between the sacs exceeds three marks, the pumps draw in even its blood.

### Origin
It arose when cold-chain workers of the Mapo Union connected their bodily circulation to a temporary cooling network during a power outage. H09 records the time when the first carrier gave up its own body heat to cool a patient room, along with the number of the valve it used.

### Habitat
In the Mapo Union, it travels back and forth between reservoirs and dormancy chambers along blue condensation lines; during the overheated season, it uses the shaded waterways of the Seongbuk Line as supply routes. In spaces without connected piping, it never goes more than ten steps away and always returns to its starting point.

### Needs and Desires
A day's circulation requires 18 liters of concentrated brine, one pump membrane, and two compressed carbohydrate rations; the cooling sacs must be replaced after seven deliveries. A new carrier grows, one individual at a time, only when an adult has earned four completed-route marks and secured two empty sacs and a living mycelial wick.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
Juveniles carry empty containers through short conduits, then take on refrigerant after their third molt. After twenty circuits, adults shed their pump membranes in a low-temperature recess; without replacement materials, they harden on the transit route before they can return.

### Behavior and Rank
They distinguish passersby not by identity but by the heat they carry and the markings on their containers. As the XT04 pressure reading rises, they fill the central reservoir's allotment first, but they do not touch a civilian container already marked with a vertical blue line, down to its last sip.

### Threat by Stage
With empty sacs, they seize refrigerant containers; with half-full sacs, they push people aside to secure the shortest route. When both sacs are overpressurized, they spray cold at every three-way junction, so anyone they encounter who crosses the same condensation line twice is classified as cargo.

### Countermeasures and Combat
Through the soles of their feet, they can read pressure changes in connected piping up to 20 meters away, but cannot sense beyond a rubber joint; insulated clothing conceals body heat even within 6 meters. If a bypass valve is opened first to break the pressure route and a sealed hot-water container is placed in an empty conduit, a carrier will turn its pumps toward it and can be captured without damaging its cooling sacs.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
If three vertical blue lines are drawn on a container and exactly 6 liters of brine are offered, they understand it as a ration proposal and retain the agreed route on the surfaces of their sacs for six circuits. The carriers cool an evacuation route, and HC09 supplies pump membranes, but if the promised quantity is missing, they cut off cooling on that route. Personnel on site must decide whether to give up that day's refrigerant for the Mapo Union patient rooms to save the Seongbuk Line evacuation column, or abandon the long-term supply route to protect the ward.

### Scenario Connections
In G09-SC1, H09's valve records are used to reset the Mapo Union ration line; in G09-SC2, HC09 mediates the brine contract for the Seongbuk Line transit route. G09-SC3 concerns establishing civilian containers' rights before rising XT04 pressure leads to a monopoly over the central reservoir.

/monster_contents/M014/entries/1/bestiar.en: The Frost-Film Sealer uses the frost-fungal film on its six-pronged fingers to seal thresholds and waste. It decides not whom to treat, but which contact surfaces to close, and does not settle where direct sunlight persists.

/monster_contents/M014/entries/1/prose.en:
### Role and Body
A humanoid mutant that spreads thin frost-fungal film from its six-pronged fingers to seal entrances and exits to contaminated areas, as well as waste. When the film absorbs pathogens, it changes from white to purple; even after saturation, if stepped on, it wraps around the person's ankle and isolates them.

### Origin
It resulted from Mapo Union infection-control staff cultivating refrigerated spores on disposable barriers to make up for a shortage of filter material. H09 preserves a record of their decision on the first day of quarantine to protect thresholds before patients.

### Habitat
They grow beds of film around thresholds, drains, and waste elevators in the Mapo Union medical section; on the Seongbuk Line, they choose only culverts with little wind. They do not settle in places exposed to four continuous hours of direct sunlight, because the fungal film dries out.

### Needs and Desires
One sheet of film takes 2 kilograms of antimicrobial salt, one bundle of absorbent fiber, and one lump of black wax; contaminated film must be removed within 18 hours. Seven saturated sheets and protein feed must be gathered before one finger can be detached and raised as a juvenile, so production falls for a season after reproduction.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
First they set out a test film bearing an air sample, then spread a broad barrier in the direction where its color changes, and finally roll up and digest the saturated film. An adult that misses the collection window reabsorbs toxins from the film, loses its senses, and seals even its own surroundings in layers.

### Behavior and Rank
As the colony's sanitation adjudicators, sealers decide not whom to treat but which contact surfaces to close. When XT04 pressure rises, they count movement itself as an infection risk and draw purple lines even across sound passageways.

### Threat by Stage
At the test-film stage, they take samples from shoes and equipment; at the barrier stage, they catch unregistered footprints. Once the film beds are saturated, they block exits one by one, causing an air shortage. Anyone who crosses the same purple threshold twice is treated as quarantine waste.

### Countermeasures and Combat
Their fingertips can read changes in acidity only within 2 meters of fungal film they touch, and the fine hairs on their arms lose their sense of direction in air currents of 1 meter per second or more. Saturating the test film first with a neutral buffer and placing a clean ceramic plate over the threshold creates a safe passage without damaging their sensory surface.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
If two clean swabs are laid in a cross and antimicrobial salt is offered, they take it as a signal to exchange areas; they inscribe the approved boundaries on a black-wax tag until the next molt. As long as HC09 keeps collecting waste, the sealers maintain the Mapo Union's infection-free passage, but if a contractor leaves contaminated film unattended, they turn every approval tag purple. Personnel on site must choose whether to leave asymptomatic evacuees at the Seongbuk Line quarantine shelter or open the barrier and take them along, accepting the risk of infection to the entire colony.

### Scenario Connections
G09-SC1 begins with an investigation comparing H09's sanitation assessment table against Mapo Union threshold samples; in G09-SC2, HC09 sets the quarantine boundaries for the Seongbuk Line culvert. In G09-SC3, passage surfaces overzealously closed because of XT04 pressure are selectively reopened.

/monster_contents/M014/entries/2/bestiar.en: The Condensation Spore Waterkeeper gathers moisture from the air with capillary combs on its back and flanks and divides it into drops for drinking, cultivation, and reserves. It measures time by how far the water level in a tank has fallen rather than by dates, and leaves a yellow stain on the back of a hand that takes more than the permitted amount.

/monster_contents/M014/entries/2/prose.en:
### Role and Body
A humanoid mutant that gathers moisture from the air with capillary combs on its back and flanks and measures it into colored drops. The blue, yellow, and red drops it dispenses represent drinking, cultivation, and reserve allotments, respectively; when the gauges inside its body dry out, its skin cracks like a sheet of paper.

### Origin
It arose after Mapo Union water-supply managers implanted condensation-recovery panels and refrigerated fungal material into their skin and began recording water rations with their bodies. H09's early ledger specifies that the maximum one individual can recover in a day is 12 liters.

### Habitat
They collect droplets on the railings above Mapo Union water tanks and in low-speed ventilation rooms; on the Seongbuk Line, they follow only the insides of tents where dawn fog lingers. If humidity falls below 25 percent, they stop moving and fold themselves into the nearest shade.

### Needs and Desires
Cleaning the capillaries requires 3 liters of distilled water, three packets of pigment salt, and one carbon wick; the comb teeth must be replaced every forty rationing cycles. An adult must complete thirty cycles without a surplus and separately reserve 50 liters of water before it can detach one condensation spore from its abdomen and raise it as a young waterkeeper.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
Young waterkeepers produce only colorless drops until they can distinguish the three kinds of water tank accurately, at which point they gain rationing rights. Aging individuals begin by absorbing the red reserves; at the end, they add their own bodily fluids to the ledger and leave only a transparent husk.

### Behavior and Rank
They measure time by how far the water level in a tank has fallen rather than by dates, and leave a yellow stain on the back of the hand of anyone who takes more than the prescribed mark. If the XT04 pressure variable increases evaporation, they cancel water for new individuals first, but do not arbitrarily change patients' existing allotments.

### Threat by Stage
During collection, they draw exposed water containers into the rationing network; during metering, they dry out containers that exceed their permitted amount. When the red gauge reaches empty, they regard every open source of moisture as a reserve, so crossing a water-tank railing in wet clothing becomes a trigger for attack.

### Countermeasures and Combat
Their eyes distinguish only polarized reflections within 10 meters and cannot see matte surfaces; their capillaries are sensitive to surface humidity within 3 meters but cannot detect water inside sealed containers. Moving sealed water containers beneath a matte canopy and spreading wet cloth in an empty trough turns their comb teeth that way, allowing access to the water-supply valve.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
If one blue drop, two yellow drops, and one red drop are placed on a tile in that order and distilled water is offered, they recognize it as a rationing agreement; its terms are stored in a colored band that does not fade for thirty cycles. The waterkeepers recover leaks to provide water to the Seongbuk Line column, and HC09 supplies carbon wicks, but if overdrawn water is confirmed, they suspend the relevant allotment for the next two cycles. Personnel on site must decide whether to preserve the reserve water needed to bring a young waterkeeper into being or immediately give that water to the Mapo Union's dialysis patients.

### Scenario Connections
In G09-SC1, H09's water-supply ledger is used to establish the actual losses from Mapo Union water tanks; in G09-SC2, HC09 adjudicates ownership of the water collected at dawn on the Seongbuk Line. G09-SC3 concerns deciding whose allotment bears the evaporation losses caused by rising XT04 pressure.

/monster_contents/M014/entries/3/bestiar.en: The Ice-Conduit Scrap Herder is a symbiotic organism formed when a contaminated magnetic transporter bonded with a nervous system; it herds metal fragments by size. After three failed attempts to tow stationary rebar, it accepts it as a territorial boundary, and it cannot distinguish ceramic from aluminum.

/monster_contents/M014/entries/3/prose.en:
### Role and Body
A humanoid mutant that uses a magnetic ice conduit along its spine and towing hooks at its waist to herd metal fragments by size and make low-temperature storage pens. If more than 30 kilograms stick to the ice conduit, even the iron in its limbs is pulled as though it were material to be recovered, and its gait collapses.

### Origin
It appeared when Mapo Union equipment-recovery workers manually pulled contaminated magnetic transporters and their nervous systems bonded with the control coils. The H09 recovery list retains the last human instruction to distinguish structural alloys from decorative metals.

### Habitat
At the Mapo Union waste-compaction yard, they tend nails, sheet metal, and cables in separate heaps; on the Seongbuk Line, they use valleys where melting snow exposes debris as seasonal pastures. After three failed attempts to tow immovable metal such as rebar embedded in concrete, they accept it as a territorial boundary.

### Needs and Desires
A day's work requires one charged coil, 500 grams of graphite lubricant, and one lump of edible fungal material; the ice conduit must be fully discharged every 60 hours. A new herder can grow only after a calf core has been made from 30 kilograms of pure iron and one bundle of tendon tissue, and an adult has given up one segment of its own ice conduit.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
A calf core initially attracts only small screws, then takes charge of moving heaps once it learns to sort by weight. At the end of the season, adults switch off their magnetic fields and undergo a lubricating molt; if they lose their discharge site, they are crushed beneath the scrap stuck to their backs.

### Behavior and Rank
Herders see metal not as objects but as domesticated flocks, and leave a heap with a red iron shard planted in it untouched for three days. As XT04 pressure rises, they raise the priority of sheet metal for barriers, but still exclude parts designated as life-support equipment on the H09 list from recovery.

### Threat by Stage
While searching, they mark metal at waist height; while herding, they send scattered fragments flying in one direction. If the same piece of equipment fails to move after being marked twice, they regard its owner as an obstacle; when the ice conduit is overloaded, they pull in nearby prosthetics and iron doors all at once.

### Countermeasures and Combat
Within 12 meters, they detect only iron masses of at least 300 grams, and cannot distinguish ceramic from aluminum; after a sudden reversal of polarity, they lose their sense of direction for 8 seconds. Approaching with nonferrous equipment, connecting a grounding chain to a floor groove, and discharging the coil in three stages can empty the ice conduit without a storm of fragments.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
If one short and one long induction pulse are sent and sorted scrap iron is presented in three heaps, they understand it as a proposal for recovery rights; the permitted list is engraved on a copper ring along the spine until the end of the season. The herders provide storage pens to HC09, and settlers hand over lubricant and scrap iron, but if prohibited parts are mixed in, they mark all metal from that supplier for recovery. Personnel on site must choose whether to preserve spare sheet metal for the Mapo Union barrier or use it to build pens that protect the Seongbuk Line's traveling group from freezing to death, saving this season's evacuees.

### Scenario Connections
In G09-SC1, the H09 recovery list is used to identify essential Mapo Union equipment; in G09-SC2, HC09 establishes the scrap-metal boundaries of the Seongbuk Line pasture. G09-SC3 changes requisition priorities so the response to XT04 pressure does not cause structures to collapse.

/monster_contents/M014/entries/4/bestiar.en: The Cold-Fermentation Cook-Mother ferments plant scraps, fat, and fungal material in three abdominal chambers to produce low-temperature nutritional gel. It observes the rule against using vulnerable living people as ingredients as long as the public markings remain in place.

/monster_contents/M014/entries/4/prose.en:
### Role and Body
A humanoid mutant that ferments plant scraps, fat, and fungal material at different acidity levels in three abdominal chambers to make low-temperature nutritional gel. If acidity in the middle chamber drops below 4.2, the gel becomes toxic food that causes muscle spasms and a false sense of fullness.

### Origin
It began when a Mapo Union food-preservation worker transferred refrigerated cultures into an internal cultivation vessel to salvage discarded food. H09's ration records state that the first production batch ended starvation, but three people were expelled over a dispute about ownership of the ingredients.

### Habitat
They tend cultivation jars in the shaded kitchens of Mapo Union storehouses and, while traveling along the Seongbuk Line, stay only at camps where corpses can be separated from plant scraps. They will not enter rooms with smoke or strong disinfectants, even if food is present, because these kill the microbes in their fermentation chambers.

### Needs and Desires
One vat of safe gel requires 8 kilograms of starch, 2 kilograms of fat, 5 kilograms of clean ice, and one bottle of mature starter culture. A new cook-mother is born only when the mother gives up half her starter culture and one layer of her stomach wall; she can endure this process only once every 90 days.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
They grind the ingredients on the first day, separate them by acidity on the third, and extract gel fit for distribution only on the sixth. Contents older than ten days must not be eaten and must be buried in a sealed earthenware jar; putting them back in turns the entire fermentation chamber toxic for a week.

### Behavior and Rank
Cook-mothers classify ingredients with white knots as plant-based, those with black knots as provided by the dead, and those without any marking as prohibited. If XT04 pressure interrupts transport, they reduce rations, but they observe the rule against using vulnerable living people as ingredients as long as the public markings remain in place.

### Threat by Stage
On preparation day, they confiscate unmarked sacks; during fermentation, they monopolize the kitchen's oxygen and temperature. When the toxic transition begins, sweet vapor spreads up to 15 meters and induces an urge to eat; anyone encountered carrying prohibited ingredients inside the white line is treated as an ingredient thief.

### Countermeasures and Combat
The tentacles around their mouths can determine only the acidity of material they touch, and when four or more scents mingle within 3 meters, their sense of smell follows only the strongest one. A sealed sack of starch can draw their attention while a measured amount of alkaline clay is added to the toxic fermentation chamber, allowing the batch to be discarded without raising internal pressure.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
Offering bitter, sweet, and salty samples in that order, followed by knotted ingredients, establishes ration negotiations; the agreed ingredient standards are impressed on the mother's jar for the next three batches. HC09 handles verified waste, and the cook-mothers provide gel to Seongbuk Line evacuees, but if unmarked meat is mixed in, they withdraw all remaining rations. Personnel on site must decide whether to reduce hunger in the Mapo Union with provisions supplied by the dead whose origins are unclear, or uphold standards of dignity and safety and accept a production shortfall.

### Scenario Connections
G09-SC1 is a food investigation comparing H09 ration records with markings on Mapo Union stores; in G09-SC2, HC09 administers ingredient-collection rights at Seongbuk Line camps. In G09-SC3, a judgment is made on whether supply lines severed by XT04 pressure justify using a toxic batch.

/monster_contents/M014/entries/5/bestiar.en: The Vibration-Gathering Lurker is a low-cognition symbiotic organism with a vibration sensor soaked in refrigerated fungal material fixed to a bone spike in its shin. It cannot understand instructions and remembers only repetitions of stride and reward; it cannot sense anything beyond an expansion joint.

/monster_contents/M014/entries/5/prose.en:
### Role and Body
A low-cognition humanoid mutant that drives its elongated shinbone spikes into the floor to gather vibrations through connected plates. If it receives impacts from three directions at once, the spikes lock, and it cannot pull its body free for 11 seconds.

### Origin
Explorers of the Mapo Union's lower structures fixed vibration sensors soaked in refrigerated homogenate to their bones, after which they came to rely on the ground for most of their senses. The H09 inspection sheet records the observation that early specimens did not attack at a steady work pace.

### Habitat
They bury themselves at the Mapo Union's monolithic floor plates and pipe junctions, and on the Seongbuk Line guard only stretches where frozen bedrock remains continuous. They cannot read movement on the other side of an expansion joint at least 5 centimeters wide or a gravel layer.

### Needs and Wants
To maintain a pair of bone spikes, each needs two calcium lumps, 1 kilogram of tendon feed, and one saltwater-pool cell. An adult detects 60 safe passages and sheds one spike casing as a larva only when its stored protein is sufficient; it does not breed again before its next molt.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
A larva guards a single floor plate and learns to associate familiar walking rhythms with the provision of food. An adult that has molted three times expands its territory, but forgets one learned rhythm if its saltwater supply is cut off for two days.

### Behavior and Rank
The ambusher cannot understand instructions and remembers only repeated relationships between pace and reward. When ground impacts grow more frequent due to XT04 pressure changes, registered steps mix with attack signals, so the colony distributes them one floor plate at a time along the perimeter.

### Escalating Threat
In a stable phase, it extends only one spike toward an unfamiliar first step; when hungry, it pins even the second foot and tears away protein. Repeating the same four-beat walk three times and then withholding the promised saltwater becomes a betrayal cue, immediately turning that rhythm into prey.

### Countermeasures and Combat
Its detection range reaches 18 meters along an unbroken floor plate, and it cannot find objects suspended in the air or movement over soft sand. Turn on three vibrators out of phase to lock the spikes for 11 seconds, then move beyond an expansion joint to pass without injuring the specimen.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
After walking four slow steps and two quick ones, placing calcium and saltwater conditions it to treat the pattern as safe; the memory lasts through three molts. The ambusher signals approaching heavy impacts by scraping the floor, and HC09 fills its feeding pool, but if the reward is missed it attacks that walking pattern again. The field team must choose whether to keep a dangerous passage rule for early warning on the Seongbuk Line or remove the spike-bearing floor plates so Mapo Union residents can move freely.

### Scenario Links
In G09-SC1, the H09 walking chart tests the safe rhythm on the Mapo Union's lower plates; in G09-SC2, HC09 operates the conditioned feeding arrangement with the Seongbuk Line advance party. G09-SC3 is a mission to preserve or end the learned association amid ground impacts caused by XT04 pressure fluctuations.

/monster_contents/M014/entries/6/bestiar.en: The Thermal-Leak Tracker draws hot air through frost gills between its ribs and stores it in a phase-change sac. Its first targets were not living beings but seven overheating points in a generator room; once the sac reaches capacity, fever patients become the first at risk.

/monster_contents/M014/entries/6/prose.en:
### Role and Body
A humanoid mutant that draws hot air through frost gills between its ribs and stores it in a phase-change sac. When the sac reaches 42 degrees, its gills cannot close and it keeps drawing heat from the body temperature of nearby living things.

### Origin
Technicians of the Mapo Union cooling network wrapped their bodies in spore-based insulation to prevent fires, then became living heat collectors. The H09 leak diagram shows that their first targets were not living beings but seven overheating points in a generator room.

### Habitat
They patrol the Mapo Union's generator outer walls and steam-pipe bends, and on the Seongbuk Line follow waste heat left behind cooking stations and mobile equipment. When wind exceeds 8 meters per second, thermal traces tear apart; they stop tracking and cling to a wall.

### Needs and Wants
They need 30 megajoules of waste heat per day, one pack of phase-change salt, and 2 liters of gill-washing water to remain stable. Only an adult that has safely stored 200 megajoules can shed one sac to raise a juvenile, after which its heat intake is halved for a month.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
A juvenile feeds only in lukewarm stretches of pipe and joins fire-suppression patrols once its first sac hardens. Without washing water, crystals grow in an adult's gill slits and exaggerate temperature differences; in old age it mistakes even cold targets for leak sources.

### Behavior and Rank
A tracker classifies surfaces above 38 degrees as defects first and leaves lower heat sources alone unless they appear on a registered ration sheet. When XT04 pressure raises the external heat load, protecting generators takes priority, but patients marked with a white ceramic tag are excluded from harvesting for 10 minutes.

### Escalating Threat
During patrol, it extinguishes exposed flames and shuts down high-output equipment; just before saturation, it herds warm people toward pipes to concentrate the heat sources. At capacity, it draws heat in turn from targets at least 35 degrees within its 15-meter field of view, putting fever patients at greatest risk.

### Countermeasures and Combat
Its gills read only temperature differences of at least 2 degrees within a clear 15-meter line of sight; they cannot group heat sources behind reflective insulation panels or several dispersed lukewarm packs into one target. Divide waste heat among six low-temperature packs and spray washing water to redirect its tracking route without saturating the sac.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
After shining one long and two short heat lines on an infrared shield, offering a charged heat-storage pack is understood as a feeding-heat contract; its terms are recorded for a month on ceramic beads in the sac. The tracker suppresses fires in the Mapo Union and HC09 gathers waste heat on the Seongbuk Line, but if the designated packs run out it harvests body heat again from people without tags. The field team must decide whether to reduce ward power to provide safe feeding heat or preserve power while exposing fever patients to tracking.

### Scenario Links
In G09-SC1, the H09 leak diagram is used to calculate the Mapo Union's permitted heat load; in G09-SC2, HC09 assigns waste-heat packs from Seongbuk Line mobile equipment. G09-SC3 addresses how to divide the heat load raised by XT04 pressure between power facilities and living beings.

/monster_contents/M014/entries/7/bestiar.en: A communications symbiont that absorbs electronic noise in specific bands through porous antennae on its neck and shoulders. It is a moving node, not an environmental outpost, and does not respond to optical signals or wired fiber networks.

/monster_contents/M014/entries/7/prose.en:
### Role and Body
A humanoid mutant that absorbs electronic noise in specific bands through porous antennae on its neck and shoulders, storing it as bundles of fungal signals. When storage exceeds capacity, fragments of signal replay mixed with its oldest personal memories, under the wrong sender's name.

### Origin
Mapo Union communications maintenance workers put contaminated shielding material under their skin to protect emergency channels, and were reorganized into a living relay network. The H09 record lists the first specimen's last preserved call sign alongside a deleted family name.

### Habitat
They occupy Mapo Union communications rooms and vertical cable shafts, and on the Seongbuk Line set up temporary nodes in bedrock shade where electronic storms are weak. Their antennae receive only between 2 and 40 megahertz, so they do not respond to optical signals or wired fiber networks.

### Needs and Wants
Daily operation requires one power cell, two conductive carbon plates, and 500 milliliters of insulating gel; the storage lattice must be cleared every 72 hours. A new relay needs six empty ferrite cores and 72 continuous hours without transmission to grow, while the parent permanently loses one third of its stored records.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
A young node relays a single call sign and takes responsibility for multiple channels only after twelve accurate relays. An adult that fails to clear its lattice on time sends past messages in the present tense; eventually black frost seals the antenna openings.

### Behavior and Rank
A relay treats unregistered transmissions above 2 watts as resource leaks, silences the transmitting device, and stores its contents. When XT04 interference is high, it allows only short distress messages through, but does not arbitrarily change an agreed call sign.

### Escalating Threat
During collection, it drains power from strong transmitters; at saturation, it sends stored commands to the wrong recipients. After detecting the same unregistered call three times, it classifies even the sender's neural signals as noise and induces paralysis at close range.

### Countermeasures and Combat
Its detection range is 30 meters in an open passage, but it cannot capture short directional transmissions below 0.2 watts or determine the direction of a signal that has passed through two metal shielding walls. Use low-power dummy transmissions to calculate the remaining lattice capacity and send a discharge command over a fiber-optic control line to close its antenna without erasing the memory layer.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
Transmit a header bearing the H09 checksum and a charged power cell to have it interpreted as a formal offer; the agreement is stored on a write-only carbon lattice and lasts until the next lattice replacement. The relay provides HC09 with a clean communications window and the Mapo Union supplies insulating gel, but exceeding the agreed output blocks that call sign for a week. The field team must decide whether to reveal private stored messages to rescue the missing or seal the parties' secrets even if this delays network restoration.

### Scenario Links
In G09-SC1, the H09 checksum verifies the sender of stored signals in the Mapo Union; in G09-SC2, HC09 allocates restricted communications windows on the Seongbuk Line. G09-SC3 is an operation to clear the lattice before saturation from XT04 interference contaminates distress commands.

/monster_contents/M014/entries/8/bestiar.en: The Scent-Map Guide freezes volatile traces on layered fungal plates on its face, making scent maps for each route. Sealed doors, flooded paths, and activated-carbon passages remain blank gaps beyond the map.

/monster_contents/M014/entries/8/prose.en:
### Role and Body
A humanoid mutant that freezes volatile traces on layered fungal plates on its face to make scent maps for each route. Each plate can read only the scent layers from the last four hours in sequence, so older traces must be moved to separate scent ice.

### Origin
A Mapo Union supply-seeker became a living olfactory archivist after continuing searches for a long time while wearing a contaminated chemical sensing membrane. The H09 missing-person register records the first case of erasing one's own family's traces to preserve the scent of a rescue target.

### Habitat
They hang scent ice at every Mapo Union ventilation junction and replace route markers on the Seongbuk Line whenever seasonal winds change. Sealed doors, flooded paths, and passages laid with activated carbon have no continuous scent and remain blank gaps beyond the map.

### Needs and Wants
A seasonal map requires four bottles of scent fixative, 12 wax plates, and one clean cooling case; the face plates must be shed every 30 days. A young guide needs 12 samples from different routes to mature, and the parent forgets each route represented by a transferred sample until it learns it again.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
Collectors build up new traces on their face plates; map-makers transfer stable scents to wax plates; aging archivists leave only hazard markers. When fixative runs out, the faintest traces evaporate first, so the missing people sought by the fewest disappear from the map first.

### Behavior and Rank
Guides mark food, burial grounds, coolant, and tracking hazards with distinct scent combinations; they guide no one along a route whose scent ice has been damaged. When XT04 tracking pressure grows, they erase the Mapo Union's main entrance scents but do not discard markers for missing people in the H09 register without HC09's approval.

### Escalating Threat
During gathering, they strip scent fragments from passersby’s clothing; during rewriting, they forcibly stop groups following old markers. Anyone who mixes funeral and food scents on the same marker is deemed a grave-robber, and when the face plates overload the guide sprays a fear scent to scatter the crowd.

### Countermeasures and Combat
They track a single scent up to 40 meters downwind, but cannot determine chronology if the wind reverses twice or three or more scent layers are mixed. Block actual routes with an activated-carbon mesh and place three harmless scents that evaporate at different temperatures in an empty washroom to safely clean the face plates.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
Present pine resin, salt, and vinegar scents in sequence, then offer a genuine possession of the person to be guided; the guide understands this as a route request, and preserves the agreement on a wax scent tablet until the seasonal winds change. The guide provides safe paths on the Seongbuk Line and HC09 supplies fixative and missing-person data, but a false personal scent mixed in will cover every marker from that group with a gray hazard scent. The field team must decide whether to erase a small group of refugees' traces to evade XT04 tracking or preserve the entire route in hope of finding the missing in the Mapo Union.

### Scenario Links
G09-SC1 is a search comparing the H09 missing-person register with Mapo Union scent ice; in G09-SC2, HC09 reviews which traces to leave on the Seongbuk Line seasonal-wind map. In G09-SC3, the team approves or rejects the scope of erasing entrance scents in response to XT04 tracking pressure.

/monster_contents/M014/entries/9/bestiar.en: A negotiating specimen that stores several hosts' memory layers separately in a low-temperature thoracic core and brings forward one persona at a time. Contrary to its growth-stage label, it does not decide for the colony alone; it requires the assent of at least three memory layers.

/monster_contents/M014/entries/9/prose.en:
### Role and Body
A humanoid mutant that stores several hosts' memory layers separately in a low-temperature thoracic core and brings forward one persona at a time as needed. If two layers rise above 6 degrees at once, speech and movement commands conflict, and its body moves in opposite directions.

### Origin
It arose from the choice of a Mapo Union crisis coordinator who transferred neural samples from dying infected people into their own dormancy device to prevent the loss of knowledge. The H09 persona record states that the original coordinator now has only one vote in the core.

### Habitat
They communicate through crystal plates in a 2-degree cold room at the Mapo Union's deepest level and, while moving on the Seongbuk Line, are carried only in a shaded cooling tube at the center of the procession. XT04 is an external pressure variable that affects cooling demand and decision time, not a place the negotiator travels to.

### Needs and Wants
Daily maintenance requires 10 liters of coolant, three packs of glucose gel, one blank memory plate, and 40 uninterrupted minutes of deliberation. A successor core can form only by inheriting three memory layers, but the parent cannot reclaim the transferred knowledge or votes; according to the H09 list, only two blank cores are available.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
At first, only one persona awakens and learns external vocabulary; once stable, different memory layers take turns representing the whole according to a schedule. If memory plates run short, new experiences overwrite old layers; if coolant is cut off, the warmest persona is irreversibly lost first, before a vote.

### Behavior and Rank
The negotiator does not make colony decisions alone and requires the assent of at least three memory layers, leaving dissenting views around the edge of the decision plate. When XT04 pressure exceeds the threshold, more votes favor shortening deliberation, but breaking an existing contract requires a separate two-thirds majority.

### Escalating Threat
In single-representative mode, it restrains questioners to verify facts; in multilayer awakening, different escort orders are issued simultaneously. If two or more conflicting offers are made during one deliberation, it rules them deceptive and seals the cold room; in a full thaw, each persona sends a separate mobilization order to its own supporters.

### Countermeasures and Combat
It understands an external voice only when spoken into the decision tube, senses movement beyond 1 meter only through changes in floor temperature, and cannot tell which memory layer triggered an electronic stimulus. Keep cooling fixed at 2 degrees and provide voice, scent, and electrical signals one at a time to separate the representative layer; rapid heating or broadband input accelerates persona conflict.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
Speak an H09 persona number, place its memory plate against the decision tube, and deposit coolant to register a formal agenda; passed clauses are permanently stored in the decision patterns of three memory layers. The negotiator gives HC09 long-term plans for the Mapo Union and Seongbuk Line, while outsiders guarantee deliberation time and cooling, but if actions contradict the record all representatives jointly end contact. The field team must choose whether to permanently freeze dissenting personas for rapid colony stability or preserve every memory layer's right to speak despite dangerous delays and conflict.

### Scenario Links
In G09-SC1, the H09 persona record and the legitimacy of Mapo Union decision patterns are verified; in G09-SC2, HC09 mediates representation and cooling allocation while moving on the Seongbuk Line. G09-SC3 is the finale, deciding whether to retain deliberation procedures shortened by XT04 pressure or establish a new multilayer agreement.

/monster_contents/M015/entries/0/bestiar.en: A hexapod carrier of the Cryo-Spore Host, rolling three cooling fungal cores inside its hollow shell. Temperature pits in its legs distinguish only cold and warm on the floor within 2 meters, so it cannot locate airborne heat sources; blocking a passage when the cores shake is a response to protect its spawning surface, not a mobilization of the whole host.

/monster_contents/M015/entries/0/prose.en:
### Role and Body
A hexapod specimen that carries the reproductive cores of the Cryo-Spore Host, rolling three cooled fungal cores inside its hollow shell and distinguishing only cold and warm on the floor within 2 meters through temperature pits in its legs.

### Origin
In the Mapo Union's long-term cold zones, host tissue and stored fungal cores became symbiotic and differentiated into a mobile spawning organ.

### Habitat
It prefers Mapo Union storerooms with stagnant air and retreats from infiltrating heat to verified cold refuges such as sealed refrigerators on the Seongbuk Line or northern ice tanks; XT04 is an external pressure reading that triggers this retreat, not a destination.

### Needs and Wants
For each fungal core it maintains, it consumes 300 grams of salt and 1 kilogram of animal fat every three days, so when stores run short it absorbs the smallest core first.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
Each of the three cores matures for 18 days after feeding on fat, with a 60 percent hatch rate. If the last core opens or spoils, the carrier calcifies without reproducing again.

### Behavior and Rank
