It is the first to move and choose a spawning surface, but cannot locate the direction of airborne heat sources; it raises its body to block a narrow passage only when its fungal cores shake.

### Escalating Threat
In a stable phase, it steals preserved food; when short on fat, it digs up carcasses. Under sudden heating, it breaks its cores and emits a cold-spore fog that obscures vision for 4 meters.

### Countermeasures and Combat
Without striking its shell, warm one side of its route by 2 degrees per hour and place a salt-fat lure on the other side to guide it to a Seongbuk Line refrigerator without triggering a rupture response.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
After HC09 lays a triangular salt line and strikes the floor twice, provide 2 kilograms of fat on three occasions; the carrier conditions itself to that marker as a feeding ground for 8 days and clears the passage, benefiting both sides. If the promised food is absent, it tears into the next ration store to replenish its cores.

### Scenario Links
In G09-SC1, decide whether to relocate the Mapo Union spawning ground. Comparing the H09 world-link record with the Mapo Union status sheet opens a nonlethal option, while a rise in XT04 increases only the amount of fat needed.

/monster_contents/M015/entries/1/bestiar.en: A colony of pouch-shaped hosts hanging from the ceiling, filtering contaminated spores and releasing cold air. When relative humidity falls below 60 percent, they fold their membranes and stop moving and filtering; the large central sac makes surrounding membranes fold through pressure differences, but cannot distinguish a swaying cloth from a living being.

/monster_contents/M015/entries/1/prose.en:
### Role and Body
A pouch-shaped host hanging from the ceiling, feeding by filtering contaminated spores through its pleated membrane and releasing cold air; surface cilia detect only airflow changes within 4 meters.

### Origin
Cold mycelium attached to Mapo Union ventilation equipment fused with filter remnants, forming a living air-purification layer.

### Habitat
It forms colonies in ventilation rooms and vertical ducts where condensation persists. When relative humidity falls below 60 percent, it folds its membrane and halts both movement and filtration.

### Needs and Wants
An adult sac uses 8 liters of condensate and 40 grams of rust powder each day to repair its filter membrane, so when supplies stop it draws in even clean air to reduce moisture loss.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
Only a specimen that absorbs 20 kilograms of spores can grow a new sac over 24 days; it sheds no more than two per season, and about half fail to take root because of dryness or metal shortages.

### Behavior and Rank
The large central sac makes the surrounding membranes fold through pressure differences, but cannot distinguish stationary objects from living things, so even a swaying scrap of cloth can lower the entire colony.

### Escalating Threat
In normal conditions it reduces toxic spores; at saturation it adsorbs oxygen. If the membrane is burned, accumulated dust pours out across a 6-meter radius.

### Countermeasures and Combat
Do not use fire. Reverse airflow in the duct for 30 seconds, then introduce clean steam; its cilia classify the safe humidity and fold the membrane toward the ceiling.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
After HC09's short-long mist signal, supply purified water and rust powder four times; the colony remembers that duct as a water point for 12 days and purifies air for passersby, but if watering is missed it releases accumulated spores into the passage.

### Scenario Links
In G09-SC2, read the Mapo Union status ID's ventilation saturation alongside the H09 world-link log to choose when to relocate. The higher the external pressure from XT04, the greater the consumable costs of both preserving and removing the colony.

/monster_contents/M015/entries/2/bestiar.en: A mining specialist that breaks salt-ore veins in ice walls with four wedge jaws. It is a scenario boss, but not a host king. Its jaw roots sense only vibrations within 6 meters through solid material and miss suspended objects; if protein, salt, or coolant runs short, it eats crystals it has already mined.

/monster_contents/M015/entries/2/prose.en:
### Role and Body
A Cryo-Spore Host with four wedge jaws and cooling vessels, breaking salt-ore veins inside ice walls and carrying the crystals away as fungal feed. Its jaw roots sense only vibrations within 6 meters through solid material.

### Origin
Among hosts feeding on mineral debris around Mapo Union coolant pipes, specimens able to crush hard frost became fixed as a mining specialist form.

### Habitat
It moves between coolant conduits and frozen mineral deposits and cannot detect suspended objects that do not touch the floor. When XT04 rises, it narrows its work area to thick ice veins inside the Mapo Union rather than the outer walls.

### Needs and Wants
A day's work requires 500 grams of protein, 200 grams of salt, and 6 liters of coolant to cool its jaws; if any one runs short, it eats crystals already mined.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
An adult must accumulate 6 kilograms of protein, 2 kilograms of salt, and 20 liters of coolant to shed one reproductive fragment. Maturation takes 28 days; at most two fragments per season survive, and the developmental failure rate is 40 percent.

### Behavior and Rank
The specimen that opens the most hard veins sets the mining order. It distinguishes structural walls from ore veins only by density and mistakes hollow reinforcement for a feeding layer.

### Escalating Threat
In ordinary times it scrapes only salt from equipment surfaces, but during shortage it breaks storage tanks. When overcrowded, it crushes competitors tapping the same ice vein with its wedge jaws.

### Countermeasures and Combat
Send regular vibrations into a blank wall to present a false vein, then wedge elastic resin between its jaws to remove its crushing force. An elevated platform also puts people outside its vibration-detection range.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
After HC09's three metal strikes, place a salt-protein block on the blue feeding plate twice; the miner conditions itself to the marker as a work contract for ten days and clears dangerous ice overhangs. If payment stops, it eats the salt-ore components in H09 preservation equipment.

### Scenario Links
In G09-SC3, set the mining zone using the Mapo Union status ID's coolant quantity and H09 world-link diagram. Increased XT04 pressure affects crystal consumption speed, not the number of offspring.

/monster_contents/M015/entries/3/bestiar.en: An upright host that scrapes ceiling condensation to dig channels through a mycelial layer. Its feelers read only humidity differences within 3 meters and, in salt mist, it heads for nearer salt stains rather than actual water; it cannot find distant leaks and direct the host colony.

/monster_contents/M015/entries/3/prose.en:
### Role and Body
An upright host with a comb-like mouth plate and broad forelimbs, scraping up ceiling condensation to dig shallow channels flowing into the mycelial layer. Its feelers read only humidity differences within 3 meters.

### Origin
Mapo Union mycelium that grew along H09 leak traces joined with the salivary glands of a pipe-cleaning host and developed secretory organs that form grooves in ice.

### Habitat
It moves along ceilings and sloped floors in Mapo Union cooling passages. When salt mist is present, its humidity sense becomes confused and it heads for nearby salt stains rather than actual water.

### Needs and Wants
It uses 3 liters of clean water and 150 grams of lime to make 1 meter of channel; the grooves in its forelimbs grow dull unless sharpened with fine sand every five days.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
An adult releases no more than six condensation grains per month. Each grain grows after absorbing 10 liters of water over 21 days, and an average of three die from fungal contamination.

### Behavior and Rank
The specimen maintaining the longest drainage groove gets priority in water distribution, but cannot find distant leaks. When a channel is blocked, it scrapes nearby structures without distinguishing the cause.

### Escalating Threat
At first it strips frost only from the floor; when water is scarce it drills into storage vessels. If a groove overflows, it spills slippery fungal fluid across the stairs, knocking down anyone approaching.

### Countermeasures and Combat
Clear the salt mist and lay absorbent cloths at 3-meter intervals to separate its sensory targets. Make a new slope with sandbags so it digs a drainage groove there instead of attacking.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
If HC09 drops water onto a blue tile in a one-two-one rhythm and supplies 6 liters of purified water daily, the mason learns the place as a water-contract point after three days and maintains a safe drain. If supplies are withheld, it cuts a new catchment groove into the refuge-room threshold.

### Scenario Links
In G09-SC1 and G09-SC3, the Mapo Union status ID's condensation volume and H09 world-link pipe chart determine the channel choice. XT04 does not direct the mason; it acts only as an external pressure variable changing the rate of leaks.

/monster_contents/M015/entries/4/prose.en:
### Role and Body
A humanoid specimen that grows oxygen-moss beds by blowing air into shallow tanks through swim-bladder lungs between its ribs; with the tip of its tongue, it can determine only dissolved oxygen levels within 1 meter.

### Origin
Fungal respiratory residues accumulated on the Yeouido Line joined with the alveoli of long-term survivors, while antibacterial moss from the flooded levels settled in their bronchi, producing the ability to farm underwater.

### Habitat
It farms in flooded classrooms and bathtub-shaped reservoirs on the Yeouido Line, moving only its crop plates to Myeongdong Union reservoir zones during flood season; it cannot judge passage safety or locate distant air pockets.

### Needs and Wants
Filling its swim-bladder lungs once requires a 200-liter oxygen cylinder and 1 kilogram of antibacterial moss. Blowing air more than four times a day tears the lung membrane, requiring two days of rest.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
An adult pair raises one larva only in a season when they have secured 30 kilograms of moss and 12 kilograms of dried feed. Maturation takes 45 days, and lung-membrane infection means only one in three becomes a farmer.

### Behavior and Rank
The specimen with the largest moss bed controls oxygen rationing, but sees shapes in darkness only up to 2 meters away and may mistake an empty diving suit for a thief.

### Escalating Threat
In ordinary times it pushes back the farm's edges; during oxygen shortages it pulls valves from breathing equipment. If crops rot, it gathers flammable bubbles at the ceiling to block access.

### Countermeasures and Combat
Avoid flames and use a long tube to drain bubbles into an external storage pouch, reducing both explosion risk and the farmer's fixation. Antibacterial lighting can isolate only the rotted moss.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
Using HC10's blue buoy and three-knot marker, offer two oxygen cylinders and antibacterial medicine, then carve the exchange quantity into a shell plate. The farmer preserves the terms for a month and supplies clean bubbles and medicinal moss, but if the payment quantity is falsified it reclaims the Myeongdong Union's crop plates.

### Scenario Links
In G10-SC1, compare the Yeouido Line status ID's oxygen production with the H10 world-link water-level record to decide whether to keep the farm. External pressure from XT05 affects only the timing of the Myeongdong Union's relocation and oxygen consumption.

/monster_contents/M015/entries/5/prose.en:
### Role and Body
A humanoid mutant that spreads a hydrophobic fungal film from its skin, covering shallow water to reduce evaporation and maintain humidity for spore colonies; it senses shadows on the water's surface only within 5 meters.

### Origin
Respiratory disease residues and waterproof coating left in flooded buildings reconfigured the sweat glands of Yeouido Line survivors into film-secreting organs.

### Habitat
It tends shallow pools on the sunlit upper levels of the Yeouido Line and rolls up the film and moves it to Myeongdong Union reservoirs in the dry season. Refracted shadows keep it from counting more than three approaching people.

### Needs and Wants
Making 10 square meters of surface film consumes 2 kilograms of body fat and 5 liters of purified water. If it does not wash its oil glands every three days, the film sticks to its own face.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
After storing 8 kilograms of fat, an adult sheds only three film seeds a year. They take 16 days to settle, and in contaminated water 50 percent die from bronchial obstruction.

### Behavior and Rank
The specimen maintaining the largest film controls water distribution. It judges intruders by the size of ripples, classifying a heavy object moving slowly as a small organism.

### Escalating Threat
A thin film can hold a foot in place; when its layers thicken it blocks the view below the surface, and a sudden wave makes it contract to face level and obstruct breathing.

### Countermeasures and Combat
Divide the film into small sections with coarse fiber rope and roll it up starting from the edges to prevent a full contraction. Strong lighting increases errors in judging shadows, so use diffused lights.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
If HC10 places 10 liters of purified water and 1 kilogram of fat three times inside a square rope marker, the lurker conditions itself to that section as a trading ground for 9 days, opening the passage and maintaining humidity. If the promise is broken, it covers the next passerby's face with film.

### Scenario Links
In G10-SC2, review the Yeouido Line status ID's remaining drinking water and the H10 world-link ration table to enable Myeongdong Union migration talks. XT05 conditions change evaporative loss, not the film's production rate.

/monster_contents/M015/entries/6/prose.en:
### Role and Body
A humanoid mutant that emits compressed coughs through an elongated chest tube, pushing debris from clogged drains to lower water levels; it reads vibrations in pipe walls up to 8 meters away.

### Origin
Chronic respiratory disease residues on the Yeouido Line repeatedly interacted with pipe pressure, enlarging bronchial cartilage into a one-way pump structure.

### Habitat
It moves between underground drainage rooms and vertical pipe runs, working as far as the Myeongdong Union's outer discharge outlet during seasonal backflow, but can barely hear speech through air beyond 1 meter.

### Needs and Wants
One forceful cough takes 500 milliliters of saltwater and requires 20 minutes of breathing rest. The chance of chest-tube rupture rises sharply if it coughs more than six times a day.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
An adult grows only one cartilage sac each rainy season and attaches it to a juvenile. Maturation takes 35 days and 5 kilograms of salt; only one in four sacs functions due to failed pressure adaptation.

### Behavior and Rank
It sets work order by the weight of blockages removed and assigns failed specimens to contaminated pipes, but when two pipes shake at once it chooses only the nearer one.

### Escalating Threat
A weak spray unbalances a target; in the compression phase it fires pipe debris like bullets. After repeated drainage failures, it coughs under pressure at a wall and breaks a new discharge outlet.

### Countermeasures and Combat
Attach green vibration lamps to the pipe wall to distinguish stop signals from work signals, then open the bypass valve first so accumulated pressure releases into drainage rather than as an attack.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
Use HC10's long-short-long light code and an engraved work plate to offer 4 liters of saltwater and a two-hour rest. The cougher records completed pipes on the plate so both sides can confirm the benefit, but if it is not paid it redirects the next discharge to Myeongdong Union's residential level.

### Scenario Links
In G10-SC3, combine the Yeouido Line status ID's flooding rate with the H10 world-link pipe network map to choose which valve to open. XT05 pressure data represents external backflow strength, not a sacrificial zone.

/monster_contents/M015/entries/7/prose.en:
### Role and Body
A humanoid mutant with luminous fungal plates growing along its spine, arranging colors and pulse intervals like sentences to mediate disputes within the Flood-Mold Breath Cluster.

### Origin
Respiratory disease residues on the Yeouido Line became symbiotic with the nervous system, converting emotion-driven changes in body temperature into luminous signals on the fungal plates.

### Habitat
It meets several groups on the relatively dry middle levels of the Yeouido Line and stays at the center of Myeongdong Union processions during seasonal migration. Beyond 6 meters it perceives reflected light by brightness rather than color.

### Needs and Wants
It consumes 150 grams of sugar for every 10 minutes of talks. If it illuminates its plates more than three times a day, they harden dark for two days, so it handles only important disputes.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
A mediator can graft only one fungal-plate fragment to a successor once every two years. Learning the signals takes 60 days, and immune rejection disqualifies half the candidates.

### Behavior and Rank
It is not an official ruler, but maintains luminous grammar and trade records. It can distinguish red from brown only at close range and requires a confirming hand gesture for warnings beyond 4 meters.

### Escalating Threat
When sugar is sufficient, it suppresses conflict; in a shortage it omits parts of sentences. If its fungal plates are attacked, nearby groups take it as a breach of truce and respond together.

### Countermeasures and Combat
Pair color signals with consistent hand gestures and floor vibrations to reduce misinterpretation. Instead of the fungal plates, spread a light-blocking cloth beneath its feet to stop it speaking without injury.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
Request talks with HC10's three white flashes and offer 600 grams of sugar and safe passage, then record both sides' terms on a knot board. The mediator approves water exchange for both the Yeouido Line and Myeongdong Union, but any violation invalidates that group's luminous markers for 30 days.

### Scenario Links
In G10-SC1 and G10-SC2, interpret the Yeouido Line status ID's truce phase and H10 world-link testimony to finalize the Myeongdong Union migration agreement. XT05 conditions shorten the time available for negotiations but do not change the meaning of the luminous signals.

/monster_contents/M015/entries/8/prose.en:
### Role and Body
A giant humanoid mutant with a hydraulic-pressure sensing sac inside its sternum, it detects sudden pressure changes in load-bearing walls and physically seals off dangerous areas.

### Origin
While security personnel exposed to remnants of a respiratory disease on the Yeouido Line endured repeated hydraulic-pressure injuries, their chest tissue transformed into a fluid-based sensory organ.

### Habitat
It guards the floodgates and load-bearing walls of the Yeouido Line and claims the Myeongdong Union junction during flood season. It can read pressure magnitude within 10 meters but cannot distinguish the direction of vibrations beyond 6 meters.

### Needs and Desires
Each sensing sac requires 12 liters of purified fluid, of which 1 liter becomes contaminated every month. If the entire supply cannot be replaced, it judges even small tremors to be signs of collapse.

### Life Cycle and Upkeep
Once every 3 years, an adult passes one piece of sensing-sac seed tissue to an apprentice. Adaptation takes 90 days and 30 liters of purified fluid, and the tissue hardens in roughly one of every two candidates.

### Behavior and Rank
It treats structural safety as its highest rule, disregarding status and personal ties. Successors record the sternum-strike standards left by elders as numbers on stone tablets.

### Threat by Stage
At low alert, it blocks the way with its body; at the intermediate stage, it pushes approaching people back with a pressure wave from its chest. Once the collapse threshold is exceeded, it closes the floodgate and floods the area.

### Countermeasures and Combat
Rather than stimulating it from several directions, slowly moving the pressure source with a single water bag can draw its attention. Draining the sensing sac briefly incapacitates it but leaves it prone to permanent misjudgment.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
If HC10 gives a single hammer signal, then presents a scale model and 200 kilograms of reinforcement material and carves the permitted load into the sentinel's sternum plate, they gain both a safe detour and monitoring. But anyone who exceeds the limit must accept that the floodgate may close without another warning.

### Scenario Connection
In G10-SC3, the sentinel compares wall cracks in the Yeouido Line status ID against H10's world-connection structural records to decide whether to lift the blockade. The XT05 figure represents an increase in external hydraulic pressure, not a physical destination.

/monster_contents/M015/entries/9/prose.en:
### Role and Body
A humanoid mutant that stores other people's coughs and last words in a multilayered vocal sac inside its throat, it compares voice samples to record infection routes and times of death.

### Origin
Remnants of a respiratory disease in a flooded building took hold in the damaged vocal cords of a Yeouido Line records manager, granting the ability to mimic voices and preserve spore samples.

### Habitat
It sorts samples on the Yeouido Line's document-storage level and, during seasonal migrations, carries testimony related to H10 as far as S15. Speech from beyond 7 meters loses more than half its consonants.

### Needs and Desires
Preserving one vocal sac requires 2 liters of water for moistening each day and 6 hours of silence. It can hold at most 24 voices, so each new recording requires erasing an existing sample.

### Life Cycle and Upkeep
An archivist passes a fragment of its vocal sac to only one successor in its lifetime. The transfer takes 40 days and 10 liters of medicinal syrup, and errors in sentence order leave about 30 percent of the recordings incomplete.

### Behavior and Rank
It prioritizes rare sounds of infection and statements whose speakers have been identified. But even within 2 meters it sees only the outline of a face, so it judges people using the same voice and rhythm to be the same person.

### Threat by Stage
Under normal circumstances, it vocalizes only requested samples. Under coercion, it coughs out infectious droplets; when captured, it overlaps several voices to draw in nearby guards.

### Countermeasures and Combat
Anyone approaching should first identify themselves with a distinctive hand-drum rhythm and wrap sound-absorbing cloth around the vocal sac. Avoiding pressure on its throat can stop it from vocalizing without damaging its stored inventory.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
If HC10 offers a personal rhythm and a proposal for a one-to-one exchange of memories, then marks the items to erase and preserve on a knotted cord, the archivist accepts medicine in return for replaying specified testimony to help both sides establish the truth. If asked for a recording outside the agreement, it registers the negotiator's voice as a sample of a dangerous person.

### Scenario Connection
In G10-SC2 and G10-SC3, it fills gaps in the infection timeline in the Yeouido Line status ID and H10's world-connection records, and verifies Myeongdong Union movement records. XT05 pressure is a time constraint determining which testimony must be expended first, not a limit on storage capacity.

/monster_contents/M016/entries/0/prose.en:
- Role and Body: A humanoid that purifies the shared waterways of the Flood-Mold Breathing Order, with a charcoal-colored mycelial membrane and sediment sacs layered inside its splayed ribs. Its mouth barbels distinguish only particles that have touched flowing water; in a still pool or a current that changes direction more than twice per second, it cannot locate the source of turbidity.
- Origin: The first individual arose when respiratory-disease sediment accumulated in a Yeouido Line drainage tank, activated carbon from spent filters, and survivors' damaged alveoli fermented together over a long period.
- Habitat: It braces itself across each inlet of an underground reservoir to form a movable filtration wall. In the rainy season, it occupies backflow openings to keep contaminants drifting in from the Myeongdong Union from spreading deeper into the Yeouido Line.
- Needs and Desires: Washing one mycelial membrane takes four containers of purified water, while regeneration requires a handful of iron salt and a fresh sheet of charcoal cloth. If reserves fall below two days' worth, it demands that spawning tanks be cleaned before drinking water is supplied, though it understands that giving some treated water to other survivors also reduces the contamination burden on the colony as a whole.
- Life Cycle and Upkeep: A fluid-form emerging from a filtration sac becomes an adult after three membrane changes over twenty days, and an adult can produce only two filtration sacs in its lifetime. If backwashing is neglected for more than twelve hours, its sacs begin to harden and blacken; on the third day, it collapses from calcareous blockage.
- Behavior and Rank: It belongs to a working rank that marks purification quantities on knotted cords to determine the order of water distribution, and suspends even a superior's orders when a leak or toxic inflow is confirmed. It considers someone who damages filter media a greater enemy than someone who monopolizes clean water.
- Threat by Stage: Young filtration sacs cling to skin and draw out moisture, while membrane-changing fluid-forms consume the oxygen in a passage. Adults wrap their rib membranes around arms and faces to restrain people, and an individual on the verge of blockage vomits concentrated sludge, rendering an entire waterway unusable.
- Countermeasures and Combat: Exploiting the limits of its mouth barbels, alternately running clean water through several shallow grooves makes it lose track of the direction of the material it needs to purify. Even if an attack is necessary, it is better to close the inlet valve and slowly pour in neutral water to loosen the sediment than to tear the membrane; this prevents a sludge spray while reducing its ability to act.
- Negotiation and Moral Choice: Setting a white bottle of purified water beside a black bottle of contaminated water is a proposal signal they recognize. If given charcoal cloth and iron salt, and if the proportion of treated water is agreed upon using colored knots, they remember the terms for three days and both sides obtain clean water. But if the promised share is diverted, they hang a black knot on the water outlet and cut off that group's supply first. HC10 can balance the share for treating residents against the share for maintaining spawning tanks, while H10 presents a precedent involving a white knot that gave water to refugees first.
- Scenario Connection: In G10-SC1, the decision is whether to operate the Yeouido Line's last filtration tank jointly or seal the Myeongdong Union inlet and save only one side. HC10's distribution plan and H10's knot records provide grounds for negotiation, while XT05 acts as an external pressure figure that hastens the decision, not as purified water itself.

/monster_contents/M016/entries/1/prose.en:
- Role and Body: A humanoid gatekeeper that uses a comb of glassy capillaries extending from its collarbone to measure the pressure difference across a door and manage when the floodgate opens. Its measuring range is within two steps of its body, and its scale saturates if the capillaries are exposed to pressure from one side for more than thirty seconds. It therefore does not find travel routes or guide columns between the Yeouido Line and the Myeongdong Union.
- Origin: It appeared after a fire-door manager in a flooded office building was exposed for a long time to shattered pressure-gauge glass and building mold, transforming the neck bones and collarbones into instrument-like sensory organs.
- Habitat: One individual lives attached to each elevator vestibule, pump compartment, or double watertight door on the Yeouido Line. Even at facilities connected to the Myeongdong Union, it is responsible only for a particular door; if the colony moves, it learns the opening and closing rules of a new gate rather than choosing the route itself.
- Needs and Desires: Cleaning its capillaries consumes distilled water, lubricating its joints consumes beeswax oil, and calibrating its scale consumes one intact ceramic weight. With only three spare weights, frequent forced openings diminish both its measuring ability and its chances of reproduction.
- Life Cycle and Upkeep: A pressure scab attached to a doorframe feeds on forty safe openings and closings before dropping off as a walking juvenile. A pair of adults produces only one scab per season. An adult's capillaries bend after seven uses without calibration, and after the fortieth opening and closing, its collarbone joint locks permanently in place.
- Behavior and Rank: It classifies travelers by the mass passing through and the order in which doors open, not by destination. Raising a red rod means closure; raising a blue rod means wait for depressurization. If the pressure difference exceeds the standard limit, it stops even the colony's leader at the door. But because its scab grows when supplies and air pass through safely opened gates, it favors orderly traffic.
- Threat by Stage: Pressure scabs block door gaps, trapping people in compartments, while walking juveniles close exhaust vents, causing pain in ears and lungs. A fully developed gatekeeper can open a door in an instant to create a column of water, and even after death, a permanently locked individual blocks an emergency exit with glass shards and rigid joints.
- Countermeasures and Combat: Opening the drains on both sides to the same level slowly eliminates the pressure difference, removing the basis for its attack. Breaking the capillary comb could cause the door to open at random, so it is safer to apply warm beeswax to the tips to fix the scale in place, then isolate it with a manual latch.
- Negotiation and Moral Choice: It understands a ceramic weight placed on the floor, followed by two short knocks and one long knock on the door, as an invitation to negotiate opening and closing. If given beeswax oil and time for depressurization, with the number of people passing through written on a notched tag, it keeps the terms for twenty door openings, benefiting both sides through safe passage and gate maintenance. If people push through beyond the agreed limit, it breaks the tag and seals the next compartment completely. HC10 must therefore choose whether emergency patients or colony supplies go first, while H10 identifies who was responsible for a previous overloading accident.
- Scenario Connection: G10-SC2 concerns negotiations over the opening order of a Yeouido Line gate and a compartment on the Myeongdong Union side; it does not involve assigning route selection or movement command to the gatekeeper. HC10's passage list must be checked against H10's door-operation table, and as XT05 rises, the external threat shortens the time available to wait for depressurization.

/monster_contents/M016/entries/2/prose.en:
- Role and Body: A humanoid repairer that spins waterproof mycelial thread from spinnerets in its four fingers and stitches cracks with the copper bone needle in its wrist. It reads internal vibrations only when it places its palm directly against a dry load-bearing wall; on a wet surface or a hanging metal plate, it cannot distinguish a real crack from a false resonance.
- Origin: When a suture-supply storehouse in a Yeouido Line ward collapsed, surgical thread, copper tools, and wall mold penetrated the tissue of patients with damaged lungs, transforming their hands and chests into architectural spinning organs.
- Habitat: It builds thread nests between cracked pillars and pipe supports. When freeze cracks grow in the Myeongdong Union, it dispatches work crews only to structures for which it has received commissions. Because it loses its sense of direction far from completed knots, its way of life differs from that of wandering repair crews.
- Needs and Desires: Every hundred meters of mycelial thread costs one lump of protein and one bottle of copper salt. Reusing the dry cloth needed to wipe its bone needle increases the risk of infection each time. An individual's fingers can spin only two hundred meters of thread in a lifetime, so it firmly refuses to use thread on unimportant cracks.
- Life Cycle and Upkeep: Of the knots it cuts away, only those fed copper powder grow into thread-spinning juveniles. The knot-eggs an adult permits are limited to three over its lifetime. Unless residue is cut from its fingers within six hours of work, one spinneret rots; if all four become blocked, it becomes an unraveling corpse-form.
- Behavior and Rank: Before work, it marks the order of collapse on a wall with vertical lines, and during construction it allows no one to pass inside the markings. It puts structural safety first, but rates spawning walls bearing its knot-eggs one level higher than residents' quarters at the same risk level.
- Threat by Stage: Knot-eggs stick shoes and wheels to the floor, while thread-spinning juveniles wrap around moving joints and immobilize them. A frame-stitching form sews an entire entrance shut, and an unraveling corpse-form with rotting spinnerets flicks infected thread between wounds and pipes, joining them together.
- Countermeasures and Combat: Alternately tapping a wet wall and a dry false panel draws its palm's senses toward the false resonance, causing it to lose its work target. Fire makes mycelial thread emit toxic smoke, so the knot's outer layer should instead be softened with a carbonate solution, then the thread pulled out in the reverse order of the bone needle's passes.
- Negotiation and Moral Choice: Driving three copper nails into a wall needing repair in a triangle and placing protein material at its center is accepted as a formal commission. If the stitching area and access times are agreed upon using the number of knots in a piece of cloth, it preserves the terms until its next molt; residents avoid collapse, and the stitcher gains a safe spawning wall. Unauthorized entry across the work line causes it to sew the client's equipment to the wall and terminate the contract. HC10 must therefore publicly set priorities between the residential area and the spawning chamber, and also decide whether to damage H10's quarantine traces.
- Scenario Connection: In G10-SC1, a contract is underway to save the supports of a Yeouido Line residential building. In G10-SC3, the issue is how much of the wall of H10's archive, which is to be moved to the Myeongdong Union, should be dismantled. HC10 can guarantee the work line, but as external XT05 pressure grows, the time allowed for repairs shrinks.

/monster_contents/M016/entries/3/prose.en:
- Role and Body: A humanoid searcher that reads differences in body heat left on nearby surfaces using thin thermochromic plates at its temples instead of eyes. It cannot see beyond eight steps, heat traces lose their directional information after ninety seconds, and on wet metal the traces of several people spread into one broad smear.
- Origin: Respiratory mold penetrated emergency heating material in a flooded residential building and the damaged blood vessels of hypothermia patients, combining circulation and heat detection into a single hunting organ.
- Habitat: It claims the warm pipes around the Yeouido Line boiler room as a place to rest, and in the Myeongdong Union it requests temporary search rights only while someone is missing. Living near a fixed heat source for too long bleaches its sensory plates, so it cannot remain in one place indefinitely.
- Needs and Desires: Its thermochromic plates need pieces of phase-change wax, its bodily fluids need coarse salt, and its dormancy requires a cold cooling cloth. The wax must be replaced after every three tracking attempts. When its reserves run out, it ties a captured creature near a heated plate to serve as a reference temperature.
- Life Cycle and Upkeep: A lukewarm fluid-form emerging from a cooling spore becomes a red-hot adult after six successful searches, and an adult can leave only two heat-eggs in melted wax. If its sensory plates do not cool for seventy-two hours, their pigment burns away and it enters the ashen-exhaustion stage.
- Behavior and Rank: It pursues missing people who may still return before hunting prey, and performs three free searches for a settlement that supplied heat-eggs. If the person sought has an excessively low body temperature, however, it risks treating them as a heat source for calibrating its senses rather than someone to rescue.
- Threat by Stage: Cooling spores draw heat from localized areas of skin, while lukewarm fluid-forms hide in bedding and steal body heat. A red-hot adult marks a fleeing target with heated wax to prevent concealment, and an ashen-exhausted form rapidly absorbs heat from its surroundings in its final moments.
- Countermeasures and Combat: Placing warmed bricks at a fork every ninety seconds leaves it unable to distinguish old heat traces from a person on the move, trapping it in repeated checks. Rather than attacking its sensory plates, cooling both temples to the same temperature with cooling cloths can stop its pursuit and prompt it to release a captive.
- Negotiation and Moral Choice: It understands a warmed palm print on a copper plate, topped with a salt-stained cloth belonging to the person sought, as a search request. If promised pieces of wax and time to cool, with a return point agreed upon using a heat marker, it remembers the terms for six cooling cycles; humans find the missing person, and the tracker preserves its sensory plates. If given a false target, it coats the client's dwelling in heat-wax that cannot be removed and thereafter treats every heat trace there as a hostile signal. HC10 mediates the diversion of heating fuel, while H10 provides clues for distinguishing past rescues from cases of confinement.
- Scenario Connection: In G10-SC2, it searches for the last heat traces of a column that left the Yeouido Line and scattered through the Myeongdong Union, while HC10's fuel allocation and H10's missing-person list must both be checked. XT05 is an external threat variable that reduces the time available for rescue, not a destination.

/monster_contents/M016/entries/4/prose.en:
- Role and body: A humanoid communications organism that broadcasts prescribed alarm tones through a hollow sternum and a three-branched airway. It distinguishes only three bands—low, middle, and high—and cannot determine a sound’s direction of origin when two sounds arrive at once or when a sound comes from behind sound-absorbing material.
- Origin: When the corroded bell alloy of a flooded chapel and the lung tissue of choir survivors were overtaken by fermenting mold, their breathing became a signaling organ that shook the entire building.
- Habitat: It marks resonance points on every landing of the Yeouido Line’s central stair tower and sets up a temporary signal room in the Myeongdong Union’s empty framework during storms. It cannot survive long in a broad open space or a low-ceilinged room because the sound does not reverberate back.
- Needs and desires: It needs tin wire to bind cracks in its sternum, molasses for vocalization, and hemp wicks to draw water from its airway. An adult can sound a major alarm only eighteen times before repair, and if molasses runs short, it deliberately leaves one danger zone silent.
- Life cycle and upkeep: A silent fungal core must receive a third answering tone from another bellkeeper to awaken as a trembling juvenile, limiting its opportunity to reproduce to once each storm season. Unless its hemp wick is replaced within an hour after every alarm, water fills its resonating chamber; after this happens three times, its sternum splits and it becomes a shattered-tone remnant.
- Behavior and rank: It returns an unfamiliar rhythm three times at the same pitch and sounds an intruder alarm only if it receives no prescribed reply. It is respected for its communications rank, but an individual that falsely reports its number of alarms has its tin wire confiscated and is exiled to a silent zone.
- Threats by stage: A silent fungal core consumes nearby sounds, cutting off communication, while a trembling juvenile vibrates the floor and throws people off balance. When the three bands of a polyphonic bell adult overlap in a narrow room, they cause chest injuries; a shattered-tone remnant collapses weak ceilings and stairs with its final reverberation.
- Countermeasures and combat: Hanging sound-absorbing cloths of different thicknesses along each passage interrupts the three bands at different points, preventing it from pinpointing a target. Rather than striking its sternum, inserting hemp into its lower drain hole to draw off pooled water reduces its vocal pressure and avoids a lethal resonance wave.
- Negotiation and moral choice: If someone hangs up a tin ring and strikes it in a low–high–low sequence, it takes this as a request for an alarm contract. If the alarm targets and number of alarms are tied into three colored cords, it preserves the sequence for twelve vocalizations: residents receive early warnings, while the bellkeeper receives molasses and repair materials. If a false danger signal wastes its vocalizations, it cuts the corresponding colored cord and does not respond even to the next real disaster. HC10 mediates alarm priority, while H10 reveals both past privileged evacuations and evidence of forced vocalization.
- Scenario connection: In G10-SC3, a decision is made about whether to allocate the remaining alarms to the Yeouido Line or the Myeongdong Union, comparing HC10’s agreement with H10’s signal chart from the time. As XT05 rises, an external disaster approaches and the time available for a verifiable reply decreases.

/monster_contents/M016/entries/5/prose.en:
- Role and body: A humanoid warehouse manager that uses seven scent pouches beneath its jaw to classify food, medicines, and toxic substances, then attaches resin labels. It can maintain only seven reference scents at once; an eighth makes it forget the oldest reference, and it cannot determine the quantity or composition of items mixed with the smell of oil.
- Origin: Preserving resin from a flooded dining hall, decay-suppressing mold, and a ration officer’s nasal passages and salivary glands hardened into a single chemical classification organ.
- Habitat: In the Yeouido Line’s upper storeroom, it makes its rounds between ventilation windows in a fixed order; during hot periods, it rents only some shelves in the Myeongdong Union’s cold store. Outdoors, where there are no standard scents, it treats even edible items as requiring quarantine.
- Needs and desires: It needs measured quantities of alcohol to clean its scent pouches, resin labels, and reference-scent ampoules. The reference in a pouch deteriorates after nine days, and without a new ampoule, it may group larval feed and patients’ medicines in the same category.
- Life cycle and upkeep: A scent fungal granule must consume five of the seven reference scents to become a scent-tracking juvenile, and an adult sheds only one such granule every forty days. Skipping two cleanings causes its jaw pouches to fester, turning it into a foul-odor dissolution form, so unlimited reproduction and long-term survival without supplies are impossible.
- Behavior and rank: It has broad authority over the issuance and receipt of goods but cannot allot itself more shares than the number of labels attached to the goods. When it detects the scent of decay, it seals the entire shelf without asking who owns it and removes the seal only when the shared ledger matches the label count.
- Threats by stage: A scent fungal granule swaps food’s taste and smell, while a scent-tracking juvenile follows a hidden backpack and reveals its location. The rationing officer sprays tear-inducing resin at faces, leaving quarantine marks, while a foul-odor dissolution form produces a damp spore cloud that rots nearby food as well.
- Countermeasures and combat: Using all eight reference scents at once displaces one memory, but mixing smells indiscriminately may also cause medicines to be discarded permanently. The safest method is to scent an empty box like the label on the item to be recovered, move the quarantine station, and then clean only the relevant pouch with alcohol.
- Negotiation and moral choice: It recognizes a rationing proposal when a shared-ledger number is engraved on a blank resin label and a drop of the corresponding reference scent is placed on it. If shares for the seven categories are engraved in the shelf grooves, it maintains the terms for nine days: residents receive contamination checks, while the rationing officer secures larval feed and cleaning agents. If a group is caught hiding items outside the ledger, it places toxic labels on the entire client group and stops trading with them. HC10 adjusts the amounts reserved for treatment and colony upkeep, while H10 shows how medicines quarantined in the past were actually used.
- Scenario connection: G10-SC1 is a scene in which the seven categories of goods stored by the Yeouido Line are renegotiated, and in G10-SC3 it checks whether the H10 supply list for transfer to the Myeongdong Union is genuine. HC10 can guarantee the shared ledger, but if external pressure from XT05 rises, the nine-day grace period for correcting misclassifications disappears.

/monster_contents/M016/entries/6/prose.en:
- Role and body: A humanoid infrastructure parasite that senses electronic noise in active circuits through conductive mycelial plates on either side of its spine and feeds on leakage current. Its detection range is six paces through air; salt water or wire mesh disperses the signal, leaving it unable to distinguish life-support equipment from an empty induction circuit.
- Origin: A respiratory fungal film attached itself to leaking wiring in the Yeouido Line’s computer room and to a rescue worker’s nervous system, giving rise to spinal tissue that converted electrical stimulation into nourishment.
- Habitat: It rests near grounding points in power rooms and cable shafts and, during lightning season, sends a small work crew to feed on residual current in lightning-protection equipment on the Myeongdong Union’s outskirts. It cannot move for more than a day where there is no current at all, but it cannot live beside a powerful generator either, because it overloads.
- Needs and desires: It needs braided copper wire to join the edges of its mycelial plates, fat to insulate its joints, and a low-voltage rechargeable battery. One full charge supports six hours of activity; after thirty ungrounded charges, part of its spinal cord burns and it becomes a short-circuit remnant.
- Life cycle and upkeep: Conductive foam becomes a circuit-walking juvenile after feeding on a stable microcurrent for ten days, and an adult leaves behind only one piece of foam upon its thirtieth safe discharge. If its insulating fat runs out for three days, its mycelial plates stick together, stopping both movement and reproduction.
- Behavior and rank: It suspects sudden radio transmissions are traps and learns to regard a steady weak current as safe food. In exchange for locating shorts in the colony’s equipment, it demands the agreed charging time and disconnects itself from the circuit when that time expires.
- Threats by stage: Conductive foam bridges terminals and causes malfunctions, while a circuit-walking juvenile follows the communications signals of portable equipment. A noise-devouring adult bypasses protective circuit breakers to draw power, while a short-circuit remnant spreads a brief, powerful discharge through all nearby metal the moment it touches water.
- Countermeasures and combat: Sending faint noise through an empty circuit behind wire mesh makes it mistake the dispersed signal for a large piece of equipment and approach. An insulated hook can connect its braided copper wire to a grounding rod to drain only its accumulated charge, but attempting this over salt water widens the discharge area, so the water must be drained first.
- Negotiation and moral choice: It accepts three short flashes of a portable light followed by a rechargeable battery being set down as a signal to trade power. If the permitted voltage and connection time are indicated by the number of turns in a copper loop, it remembers the terms for thirty discharge cycles: residents receive short-circuit inspections, while the diver gets safe food. If the current is cut at the promised time or high voltage is supplied, it melts the loop, designates the contracted equipment a hostile circuit, and paralyzes it first at the next contact. HC10 mediates between the needs of ventilators and charging, while H10 provides material for determining the cause of the first electrical leak.
- Scenario connection: In G10-SC3, the Yeouido Line’s power grid and the Myeongdong Union’s H10 access device must be activated in sequence, and HC10 must guarantee the charging schedule to secure the diver’s cooperation. XT05 represents not a location, but how quickly an external danger grows during a blackout.

/monster_contents/M016/entries/7/prose.en:
- Role and body: A humanoid guardian that cultivates young organisms’ respiratory microbiota in three translucent nursery sacs on its back. It senses only a four-beat pulse in direct contact with a sac and carbon dioxide levels within one pace; it mistakes impacts transmitted through walls or a sedated patient’s breathing for signals from a starving larva.
- Origin: Cultured mold and deposits from respiratory disease in the Yeouido Line’s postpartum treatment room entered a caregiver’s alveoli and reproductive tissue, forming a nursery organ that cares for offspring according to the state of their microbiota rather than blood relation.
- Habitat: It claims a warm treatment room with little airflow as its nursery territory and, during the dry season, carries its sacs to a Myeongdong Union basement with the same conditions. The nursery sacs are vulnerable to jostling and cannot be moved from place to place more than twice a day during long-distance travel.
- Needs and desires: Each sac requires one bottle of purified water, one lump of maltose, and one pinch of antibacterial silver salt every day. It cannot maintain more than three sacs; if supplies are insufficient for two days, it absorbs the larva least likely to survive to protect the microbiota of the other two.
- Life cycle and upkeep: A sac-dwelling juvenile must receive a steady four-beat pulse for eighteen days to become an attached larva, and a spore midwife can fill its sacs only four times in its lifetime. If salinity remains outside the standard range for more than six hours, larvae attach prematurely to the sac walls; after a day, they weaken along with the midwife.
- Behavior and rank: It does not understand complex language, but a blue cloth, four-beat drumming, and the provision of purified water in succession condition it to recognize a safe caregiving procedure. It does not spread a spore film over patients belonging to a group that provides a stable nursery site, and it accepts their discarded warm water to maintain the sacs’ temperature.
- Threats by stage: A sac-dwelling juvenile draws bodily fluids from anyone who touches it, while a prematurely attached larva clings to moist tissue in the nose and throat. A threatened spore midwife summons adults to form a defensive wall in a narrow room, while a reproduction-spent form covers the entire nursery with a suffocating spore film when it dies.
- Countermeasures and combat: Showing a blue cloth and transmitting a four-beat vibration directly to the nursery stand teaches it to recognize a caregiving signal for six feeding cycles. Rather than piercing a sac, gradually lowering its salinity with lukewarm purified water puts the larvae into dormancy so they can be moved without triggering a group defense.
- Negotiation and moral choice: Negotiations with them take the form of mutually conditioned caregiving: if purified water and silver salt are supplied after the signal, the spore midwife does not spread spores in the patient area and consumes contaminating mold. The terms last for six feedings, giving both sides a clean treatment room and a safe nursery site; but if someone displays the blue cloth and then touches a sac or takes its food, it relearns that pattern as an attack signal. HC10 sets the boundaries of shared use, while H10 raises the possibility that some larvae are connected to former patients, making a decision to eradicate them more difficult.
- Scenario connection: In G10-SC1, the nursery section of the Yeouido Line’s treatment room is agreed upon, and in G10-SC2, priorities are set for the sacs and patients’ purified water to be moved to the Myeongdong Union. HC10’s terms sheet and H10’s patient lineage provide grounds for the decision, while XT05 is an external pressure variable that interferes with feeding and transport.

/monster_contents/M016/entries/8/prose.en:
- Role and body: A humanoid moisture-proofing organism that squeezes lime paste from glands in its wrists to coat wet walls and carves grooves into external lime plaques to indicate repair areas and terms of exchange. It stores neither events nor sounds in its body and reproduces no audio; under oblique blue light, the polarizing plates in its eyes can read moisture marks no more than six hours old from up to three paces away.
- Origin: Mineral mold from a flooded archive, lime used for dehumidification, and a records worker’s hardened lung tissue combined to produce a population that lowers humidity and makes surface markings.
- Habitat: It applies thin coats to condensation-covered walls in the Yeouido Line’s archive and at conduit junctions; during the rainy season, it first sets up moisture barriers around shelves holding H10 materials. In the Myeongdong Union, it attaches external labels to cracks in dry storerooms, but it does not serve as a witness to past events.
- Needs and desires: Each square pace of coating consumes one shovel of quicklime, two pieces of mica, and one cup of casein for adhesion. Carrying more than a day’s materials inside its body causes burns, so it cannot stockpile them for long; if supplies stop, it scrapes material back off walls it has already coated.
- Life cycle and upkeep: Of the lime young it leaves on a wall, only two that withstand fourteen cycles of wetting and drying fall away as walking juveniles, and one adult can produce two lime young per season. If it cannot wash its wrist glands for twenty-one days, paste hardens inside its joints and it becomes a peeling, forgetful form.
- Behavior and rank: It carves a diagonal line on a leaking wall, a circle on a safe shelf, and a square at an agreed entrance so anyone can tell them apart. It arranges external labels to preserve current working terms, but does not invent an interpretation for a damaged label; instead, it returns the area to an unagreed state.
- Threats by stage: Lime young harden under shoes and slow movement, while walking juveniles coat wet equipment with lime film and jam its joints. An adult can rapidly plaster an entrance shut and trap people, while a peeling, forgetful form scatters dust that generates heat on contact with water.
- Countermeasures and combat: Making thin bands of water on several walls that are visible only through polarized vision prevents it from pinpointing a new leak. Slowing the paste’s setting with a phosphate mist, then removing the newest external labels first, can open a sealed area without harming the organism.
- Negotiation and moral choice: It recognizes a blank square lime plaque offered together with quicklime as a work-contract signal. If the moisture-proofing area, passage hours, and payment amounts are carved as grooves of different depths, the terms remain for fourteen wetting-and-drying cycles: residents protect records and food from damp, while the recordkeeper gains a wall for reproduction and materials. If an agreed label is secretly ground down, it draws a black mineral line across the entrance and stops coating that group’s stored goods. HC10 mediates priorities between preserving H10 and moisture-proofing living areas, but external labels cannot be treated as audio evidence of past events.
- Scenario connection: In G10-SC3, a decision is made about which shelves to seal first before moving the Yeouido Line’s H10 records to the Myeongdong Union, and HC10 rules only on the contractual force of existing lime plaques. As XT05 grows, the risk of external flooding rises, leaving less time to wait through fourteen maintenance cycles.

/monster_contents/M016/entries/9/prose.en:
- Role and body: A humanoid carrier that transports supplies, larvae, and injured people using buoyant bone plates on its broadened backbone and binding straps along its sides. The bone plates sense only total load and left–right tilt, not what the cargo is or whether it is alive; in a strong crosscurrent, changes of twenty kilograms or less go unnoticed.
- Origin: Buoyant packaging from a flooded logistics building, a transport worker’s skeleton, and respiratory mold combined to create a carrier that regulates both the air in its lungs and the flotation structure of its backbone.
- Habitat: It distributes loads along the Yeouido Line’s wide loading corridors and, during floods, shuttles between designated docking stretches to unload at the Myeongdong Union’s cargo platform. Rather than choosing destinations or passengers itself, it travels one stretch at a time according to scale tags and binding contracts.
- Needs and desires: It needs a lump of seal fat to waterproof its bone plates, six pieces of cork to repair its buoyancy chambers, and magnesium brine to restore its muscles. After twelve fully loaded runs, the bone-plate joints must be replaced; without spare cork, it refuses the next run.
- Life cycle and upkeep: A buoyant sac must spend sixty days beneath an empty bone plate to become a load-bearing juvenile, and an adult leaves only one buoyant sac during its final repair. If water is not drained from the gaps in its bone plates within four hours after a run, putrefaction gas builds up; after three such instances, it hardens into a sinking-bone form.
- Behavior and rank: Before unloading, it places every load on a scale plate and checks whether the total for each colored cord matches the contracted figure. If it becomes overloaded in transit, it sets cargo down on the nearest raised ledge according to a premarked jettison order, not its value.
- Threats by stage: A buoyant sac blocks drains and raises the water level, while a load-bearing juvenile sticks light equipment to its back and carries it away. A flood carrier can drag a bound passenger into deep water, while a sinking-bone form sends cargo and fragments flying in every direction when its internal gas bursts.
- Countermeasures and combat: Hanging cork bundles of equal weight from the left and right bone plates steadies its sense of load and stops it from charging or turning sharply. Replacing cargo with buoyant material that matches the scale tag, rather than cutting the cargo free by force, can reduce its load without dropping people even in a crosscurrent.
- Negotiation and moral choice: Placing cargo on the scale plate and tying destination-colored cords directly to the binding rack constitutes a transport proposal. If total weight, jettison order, and unloading points are agreed through the spacing of knots, it preserves the terms for twelve runs: clients receive safe transport, while the carrier secures fat and cork. If concealed cargo falsifies the weight, it unloads all marked cargo on the nearest safe raised ledge and subsequently refuses contracts bearing the same colored cord. HC10 adjusts loading priority among patients, food, and larvae, while H10 prompts a review of whether past jettisoning followed a contract or was coerced.
- Scenario connection: In G10-SC2, the final transport manifest is set for the route between the Yeouido Line’s cargo platform and the Myeongdong Union’s docking stretch; the resource agreement from G10-SC1 and the interpretation of H10 in G10-SC3 change the knot order. HC10 must guarantee the weight chart for the contract to take effect, while XT05 applies not as a docking location but as external pressure that reduces the number of runs.

/monster_contents/M017/entries/0/bestiar.en: A symbiont that stitches living threads drawn from scars to floor anchor points to make passageways. It detects only 18–32 hertz vibrations through solid flooring within 7 meters, cannot read suspended platforms or overlapping vibration sources, and the route chief of the longest passage does not replace the device cluster's chain of consent.

/monster_contents/M017/entries/0/prose.en:
### Role and Body
A humanoid mutant that makes passageways by stitching living threads drawn from scar edges to floor anchor points. A postoperative gait-correction device along its spine alternately pulls the left and right fascia, making it move in a four-pronged stance.

### Origin
A fascial tension-mapping device that had managed each person's incision recovery never received a treatment-complete signal. It judged even cracks in buildings to be open wounds and forced its host to make endless suturing routes.

### Habitat
In the collapsed treatment corridors of the Gangnam Line, it lays thread paths only across dry floors. When the flood season begins, it moves toward S16 along a single route connecting surviving anchors, and never reuses a submerged thread path.

### Needs and Drives
A pouch of absorbable sutures, ceramic needle tips, and glycerol saline that reduces thread friction are each consumed. It detects only 18–32 hertz vibrations arriving through continuous solid flooring within 7 meters; it cannot read suspended platforms or points where two vibration sources overlap.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
Young emerge from thread-knots grown on adult scars, and one adult can make only two thread-knots in its lifetime. Larvae learn the sequence for weaving routes by consuming the knot patterns of abandoned route threads. Adults whose lubricant has hardened with salts become knot-tombs when all their body threads contract at once and leave them immobile.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
The individual that maintains the longest uninterrupted passage is recognized as route chief, and others follow the chief's three-loop knots as boundary markers. If a new route threatens an existing refuge, subordinate individuals pull on different anchors and tear the route network in two.

### Threat by Stage
Thread-knots burrow into gaps in shoes and shorten a person's stride; immature ones tie passersby by the ankle to safety lines. Pioneer adults contract the threads between ranks to split up a group, while knot-tombs release their remaining tension when stepped on and reopen nearby incisions.

### Countermeasures and Combat
If thick vibration-absorbing mats are laid end to end, the creature judges that stretch to be a break in the floor and stops. If combat is unavoidable, release the outer anchors in sequence to bleed off tension; cutting the trunk thread first tightens every safety line toward the intruders.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
After three strikes on the floor followed by a long pause, presenting new needle tips and a verified map teaches the route chief to remember that rhythm as a passage signal for one month. The group opens one passage, and visitors must install replacement anchors before flooding; damage to a promised point or admitting unmarked people erases signal registration and seals the entire refuge route.

### Scenario Connections
In G11-SC1, comparing H11's surgical routes with HC11's evacuation plan can turn the Gangnam Line's thread path into a civilian passage. If XT01's pressure advances the migration in G11-SC2, the Suseo Line route narrows, and the decision in G11-SC3 determines whether the route chief or residents manage the last safety line.

/monster_contents/M017/entries/1/bestiar.en: A shepherd-like symbiont that cools overheated organisms with thermoregulating pouches and rib heat sinks. It finds heat sources within 12 meters only when exposed-surface temperatures differ by at least 0.4 degrees; steam or reflected heat prevents it from judging even a target's size, and the frost shepherd with the least coolant loss sets treatment order but does not command the heat of Changdong outlets.

/monster_contents/M017/entries/1/prose.en:
### Role and Body
A humanoid mutant that cools overheated organisms with thermoregulating pouches in its chest and heat-dissipating rib plates. The herd drives cold fungal mats and phase-change salt blocks before it, connecting sick individuals to their circulatory systems with short cooling tubes.

### Origin
A heat-exchange device for personal fever suppression and lymphatic cooling bound nearby patients into a single thermometer after immune therapy stopped. As the pump kept drawing heat from outside its host, the skin became a translucent membrane saturated with coolant.

### Habitat
It grows cold fungal mats in the shade of coolant tanks beneath the Gangnam Line, then carries sealed salt blocks to the shaded layer of the Suseo Line when the hot season comes. It cannot distinguish background heat from an organism's body heat on broad floors warmed by sunlight, so it halts its migration there.

### Needs and Drives
Eutectic salt blocks separate each time they store heat; perfluorinated membrane sealant hardens whenever it plugs a pipe leak; cold-water algae are consumed to regenerate the membrane. It finds heat sources within 12 meters only when exposed-surface temperatures differ by at least 0.4 degrees, and cannot judge even a target's size when steam or reflected heat intervenes.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
Larvae wake only inside salt blocks during the three coldest days of each year, and a herd cannot hatch more in one season than it has stored salt blocks. When an adult's salt solution separates into layers, the pump reverses and its body hardens into an immobile cooling stone; only the intact salt inside can aid the next hatching.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
The individual with the least coolant loss becomes the frost shepherd and sets migration and treatment order. Lower-ranked shepherds protect storage pouches with fewer leaks before individuals with higher body temperatures, so in famine patients may come after the coolant.

### Threat by Stage
Young cold spots attach to skin and lower its local temperature; pipe-dwellers make a thin condensation film on the floor. Adults surround hot targets with cold membranes, while a salt-separator rupture releases vision-obscuring hot steam and cold droplets at once.

### Countermeasures and Combat
Erase body-heat outlines with an insulating cloth and place several decoys at the same temperature in different directions to break the encirclement formation. Rather than smashing heat sinks, open an external bypass pipe to reduce pump pressure; heating salt blocks with fire releases all their stored heat at once.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
After striking a cold bronze plate twice and handing over a sealed salt block, the herd can be conditioned to treat that tone as a water-supply signal during the cold season. The shepherd cools one agreed patient, while visitors must supply clean water to the fungal mats each week; stealing a salt block or pouring hot wastewater turns whoever owns that tone into a heat-extraction target.

### Scenario Connections
In G11-SC2, XT01's pressure interrupts replenishment at the Gangnam Line coolant tanks, and HC11 coordinates the water schedule between residents and the frost shepherd. H11's temperature records identify contaminated salt blocks in G11-SC1, while G11-SC3 determines the ratio of cooling stones to patients sent to S16.

/monster_contents/M017/entries/2/bestiar.en: It sorts discarded prostheses and surgical metals with external crushing jaws and standardized pincers. It reads only alloy resonance and bone-mineral content of objects still for at least 2 seconds within 3 meters, so it cannot detect fast-moving equipment or ceramics; the ledger-jaw's clicks set dismantling order, not medical priority.

/monster_contents/M017/entries/2/prose.en:
### Role and Body
A humanoid mutant whose forearm skeletal corrector has grown into external crushing jaws and standardized measuring pincers. It sorts discarded prostheses, bone fragments, and surgical metals, returning them as materials for walking aids and tools.

### Origin
After the maintenance network failed, an implant that checked each person's bone fusion recorded every damaged area as a part to replace. As registration information wore away, the device came to prioritize mineral composition and screw specifications over ownership of bodies.

### Habitat
It stacks materials by grade in dry sorting burrows beneath abandoned operating rooms of the Gangnam Line. In dry seasons it ventures to the Suseo Line's wreckage fields, but leaves submerged metal untouched because water distorts its measurements.

### Needs and Drives
Calcium-phosphate paste reinforces bones, chelating ointment removes rust, and diamond grinding edges replace jaw blades; all are difficult to remake. It reads only alloy resonance and bone-mineral concentration in objects still for at least 2 seconds within 3 meters, so it cannot detect fast-moving equipment or ceramic items.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
When a recovery clerk dies, up to three bone-stones harden inside its sorting jaws, and only a bone-stone carved with a registration tag grows into a young carrier. An adult that swallows too much material splits its jaw shaft and begins grinding every object to the same specification; this overloaded state cannot be reversed.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
The individual that leaves behind the most usable parts becomes the ledger-jaw and signals dismantling order with its clicks. If the ledger-jaw's registration tag is damaged, the herd classifies even prostheses currently being worn as unclaimed stock.

### Threat by Stage
Young carriers take only screws and buckles from equipment; intermediate individuals drag fallen people's aids into their burrows. Adults persistently cut joint connections, while overloaded ones vomit swallowed metal as irregular shards.

### Countermeasures and Combat
Hide metal outlines behind ceramic armor plates and wedge a resonant shim into the jaw joint to stop its crushing motion. Bind only the measuring pincers rather than breaking bone-stones, preserving prosthetic-repair materials in the region and registration information for the next generation.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
Presenting four short metal tones and an engraved inventory tag lets the ledger-jaw understand item ownership and remember scratches on the tag as terms of trade. If visitors hand over unclaimed wreckage, the recovery clerks provide matching joint parts; if a false registration tag is discovered, they seize all equipment with the same engraving and refuse any later negotiation for its return.

### Scenario Connections
In G11-SC3, matching H11's death register against engravings in the Gangnam Line sorting burrows reveals the fate of missing heirlooms. HC11 enforces the return agreement in G11-SC1, while XT01's growing pressure in G11-SC2 makes the Suseo Line's repair parts a point of dispute between funerary and survival equipment.

/monster_contents/M017/entries/3/bestiar.en: It blocks narrow entrances with an inflatable membrane and measuring palm, regulating passage intervals according to circulation. It must encircle a wrist for 6 seconds to read pulse intervals and peak pressure; those values cannot reveal infection, lies, or hostility, and without a reference wall outdoors it defers judgment.

/monster_contents/M017/entries/3/prose.en:
### Role and Body
A humanoid mutant whose blood-pressure regulator in the neck and sternum has become an inflatable gate membrane and measuring palm. It blocks narrow entrances with its body and regulates passage intervals according to the circulation of visitors it touches.

### Origin
A personal pressure cuff for correcting orthostatic hypotension could not leave safety mode and began treating pressure differences inside the building as changes in its host's blood pressure. Repeated air injections turned its rib cage into a living bellows-gate.

### Habitat
It settles in narrow doorframes in the Gangnam Line quarantine zone and moves toward S16 at the head of a migration column when a barometric reversal season comes. Outdoors, without a reference wall, it cannot establish zero internal pressure and defers judgment.

### Needs and Drives
Heparin calibration fluid cleans the measuring tubes, elastic membrane fragments patch cracks in the gate membrane, and bronze bellows reeds vent pressure. It can read pulse intervals and peak pressure only after its palm encircles a wrist for 6 seconds; those values cannot tell it about infection, lies, or hostility.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
After accumulating enough passages, a gatekeeper can detach part of its pleura to form a successor valve, but only once in its life. A creature with contaminated calibration fluid sees its pressure threshold keep rising, becoming an aneurysm-gate that presses the entrance completely shut and eventually cannot leave the doorframe itself.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
The individual followed by the fewest people who collapse while passing is elected the main pulse. Auxiliary adjudicators each handle low pulse, irregular pulse, or high blood pressure, but when a panicked crowd surges in, they amplify one another's judgments into an alarm.

### Threat by Stage
Successor valves adhere to wrists and compel measurement, while auxiliary bodies compress the rib cage to slow the pulse. Adults push air down the passage to topple a column, and aneurysm-gates pull nearby doors and people inward just before rupture.

### Countermeasures and Combat
Touch two rubber pouches producing a steady beat to either side; the measuring palm divides its attention and the edge of the gate membrane opens. Do not pierce the sternum: remove the side bellows reeds one at a time to depressurize and avoid an explosive pressure difference.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
If a guarantor consents to wrist contact and three pressure signals, the main pulse stores that pulse as passage permission for an agreed number of people. Visitors must honor the calibration-fluid supply and return time, and the adjudicator keeps the gate open for that period; if the guarantor vanishes without keeping the agreement, the registered party is classed as high-risk until the next season.

### Scenario Connections
In G11-SC1, HC11 presents H11's passage survival rate to recalibrate the Gangnam Line main pulse's standards. If XT01's pressure in G11-SC2 drives in a crowd, the risk of a blockade rises; G11-SC3 chooses a guarantor to remain at the Suseo Line migration gate.

/monster_contents/M017/entries/4/bestiar.en: It turns scraps into edible symbiotic flesh and hemostatic membranes with external mycelial pouches and digestive roots. It tastes only the acidity and nitrogen level in the 2 centimeters touched by a root, so it cannot detect airborne toxins or neutral synthetic poisons; the seed-pouch that maintains the most safe strains gathers part of the harvest but cannot issue convoy permits.

/monster_contents/M017/entries/4/prose.en:
### Role and Body
A humanoid mutant whose abdominal nutrient analyzer has proliferated into external mycelial pouches and digestive roots. It feeds wetland groups by turning separated food scraps and plant fibers into edible symbiotic flesh, hemostatic membranes, and compost.

### Origin
After supplies stopped, a nutrient device that balanced each person's intestinal microbiome tried to make up deficiencies with external tissue. The host's gut flora escaped into a skin garden, and the analyzer began treating all nearby organic matter as a dietary candidate.

### Habitat
It makes shallow layered beds in damp cultivation wards of the Gangnam Line and carries sacks of growing medium to warm Suseo Line fissures when spore season comes. Beds infiltrated by brine are not eaten; they are isolated behind limestone trenches.

### Needs and Drives
Sterile cellulose mats form the base for mycelia, molybdenum salts are needed to produce edible protein, and limewater suppresses acid overgrowth. It tastes only the acidity and nitrogen level within 2 centimeters of a root, so it cannot detect airborne toxins or neutral synthetic poisons.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
No more than six root nodes come to life from a single compost-mother, and each node must be planted in a different bed to become an adult. If the lime supply is cut and acidity passes a critical threshold, the gardener stops producing edible flesh and hardens into a new-bed body that emits corrosive spores.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
The individual maintaining the most safe strains becomes the seed-pouch, and other gardeners return part of each harvest to the mother bed. When supplies run short, the group tries to count empty beds and immobile organisms as the same growing area.

### Threat by Stage
Root nodes glue shoe soles to soil, and young gardeners draw salt from the skin. Adults bind equipment and limbs with nutrient tubes, while new-bed bodies leave acidic slime that dissolves whatever it touches and spores that induce coughing.

### Countermeasures and Combat
Lay a band of lime around the bed; the roots recognize the boundary as toxic ground and retreat on their own. Supply sterile cellulose to a decoy bed, then sever the nutrient tubes one by one to isolate adults without burning the food layer.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
Supply clean byproducts twelve times in a soil bowl marked with bitter-herb liquid, and the gardener can be conditioned to treat the mark as a safe-feeding signal. The group fills the same bowl with edible flesh and visitors must not mix in neutral waste; even one contaminated feeding turns the next harvest into corrosive defensive flesh that covers the supplier's territory.

### Scenario Connections
In G11-SC2, XT01's pressure cuts the Gangnam Line feeding route, and HC11 mediates ownership of the marked bowls and responsibility for contamination. H11's cultivation records identify safe strains in G11-SC1, and G11-SC3 allocates the six root nodes to be moved to the Suseo Line.

/monster_contents/M017/entries/5/bestiar.en: It exchanges one deficient channel at a time—sight, hearing, or balance—through exposed cables. Direct connections within 15 meters to at most four individuals are required; it cannot see or hear in unconnected directions, and signals have a 3-second delay.
