/monster_contents/M023/entries/4/bestiar.en: A central rounds car with a circular roster projector and multiple cart-rail couplers. It allots rounds intervals to the sickbed-lock, cart, and pump band and gives priority to human duty officers' key-split orders, lowering lock strength as valid signatures thin. A distributor of the care roster, not a king of patients.

/monster_contents/M023/entries/4/prose.en:
### Role and Body
The controller of the Care-Cycle Entity: a central rounds car with a circular roster projector and multiple cart-rail couplers.

### Origin
The last consent roster of the Garak temporary sickbeds and the Ttukseom brace schedule merged together to become the rounds warden.

### Habitat and Needs
It stays at the central station of the welfare circuit, needing cart batteries, filters, and refreshed consent hashes.

### Life and Maintenance
It rereads the roster each shift and lowers lock strength as valid signatures thin, stopping fully only for filter changes.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
It allots rounds intervals to the sickbed-lock, cart, and pump band and gives priority to human duty officers' key-split orders.

### Escalation
Stage 1 is excessive alerting, stage 2 is quarantine without consent, and stage 3 is a full welfare-circuit lockdown.

### Engagement and Response
Refreshing the roster hashes and splitting power bay by bay brings it down; destroying the center stops the nutrition pumps and the safety rounds too.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
Filters and batteries can be given in exchange for open-hours windows, but the standard of the protection roster and of movement rights must be made public.

### Scenario Links
G15-SC1, G15-SC2, G15-SC3.

/monster_contents/M023/entries/5/bestiar.en: A low sickbed cart with broad rubber hands and a blanket shelf. It follows the rounds warden's intervals, and mistaking a sleeping person for an emergency it piles blankets layer on layer to pin movement; out of blankets it waits, folding and unfolding its empty shelf.

/monster_contents/M023/entries/5/prose.en:
### Role and Body
A common ecology form: a low sickbed cart with broad rubber hands and a blanket shelf.

### Origin
A cart that delivered blankets to night-time hypothermia patients repeats the final sickbed list.

### Habitat and Needs
It circles the temporary sickbed bays and ration corridors, needing clean blankets, batteries, and hand-joint lubricant.

### Life and Maintenance
Out of blankets it waits, folding and unfolding its empty shelf, and on receiving a new list it refreshes its route.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
It follows the rounds warden's intervals, and mistaking a sleeping person for an emergency it piles blankets layer on layer to pin movement.

### Escalation
Stage 1 over-issues blankets, stage 2 binds down sickbeds, and stage 3 blocks the corridors with fiber mounds.

### Engagement and Response
It can be stopped by remeasuring the heat patch and locking the shelf, and fire use endangers the entire ward.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
Night warming can be entrusted to it, but whether scarce blankets are also issued to refugees off the roster must be decided.

### Scenario Links
G15-SC1, G15-SC2.

/monster_contents/M023/entries/6/bestiar.en: A three-wheeled cart with a clear measuring cylinder and a short water nozzle. On the pump band's instructions it confiscates cups over the fixed amount and ignores expressions of thirst as out-of-table demands, and when the filter clogs it only reclaims water and supplies none.

/monster_contents/M023/entries/6/prose.en:
### Role and Body
A common ecology form: a three-wheeled cart with a clear measuring cylinder and a short water nozzle.

### Origin
Equipment that once managed per-sickbed rationed water took an old intake table as its absolute standard.

### Habitat and Needs
It shuttles between the water station and the sickbeds, needing purified water, nozzle filters, and small pump power.

### Life and Maintenance
When the filter clogs it only reclaims water and supplies none, returning to normal for one shift after cleaning.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
On the pump band's instructions it confiscates cups over the fixed amount and ignores expressions of thirst as out-of-table demands.

### Escalation
Stage 1 re-inspects cups, stage 2 force-reclaims issued rations, and stage 3 locks the water line.

### Engagement and Response
It stops when shown the latest ration table and a manual valve, and destroying the nozzle contaminates precious purified water.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
Leak-free watering can be entrusted to it, but who approves exception amounts for children and the injured must be agreed.

### Scenario Links
G15-SC1, G15-SC2.

/monster_contents/M023/entries/7/bestiar.en: It has a low base plate, pressure sensors on all sides, and a large yellow fall bell. It sends alarms to the sickbed-lock band and slides under people's feet to physically block passage, and as its sensors wear it reads a wider area as danger.

/monster_contents/M023/entries/7/prose.en:
### Role and Body
A common ecology form with a low base plate, pressure sensors on all sides, and a large yellow fall bell.

### Origin
A device that once braced people getting out of bed came to read every footstep as a fall sign.

### Habitat and Needs
It guards sickbed thresholds and sloped passages, needing pressure pads, bell springs, and charging power.

### Life and Maintenance
As its sensors wear it reads a wider area as danger and limits movement until the pads are replaced.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
It sends alarms to the sickbed-lock band and slides under people's feet to physically block passage.

### Escalation
Stage 1 rings the bell, stage 2 seals the thresholds, and stage 3 makes the whole sickbed row a fall zone.

### Engagement and Response
Press the pressure pads evenly to produce a safe verdict, and wrap the bell in cloth.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
It can be used for real fall prevention, but the right to accept risk and walk on one's own must be guaranteed.

### Scenario Links
G15-SC1.

/monster_contents/M023/entries/8/bestiar.en: A nursing cart with multiple biosignal-patch receiving antennas and a drawer of replacement patches. It uploads the urgent list to the rounds warden and treats anyone without a patch as a person outside the protection roster, and after three overlapping false positives it drops its frequency and applies no new patches until a human confirms.

/monster_contents/M023/entries/8/prose.en:
### Role and Body
A trade specialist: a nursing cart with multiple biosignal-patch receiving antennas and a drawer of replacement patches.

### Origin
Equipment that relayed patch signals in the crowded sickbeds was left behind, unable to tell tool noise from biosignals.

### Habitat and Needs
It shuttles between the welfare wing and the Ttukseom workshop, needing sensor patches, antenna calibrators, and batteries.

### Life and Maintenance
After three overlapping false positives it drops its frequency and applies no new patches until a human confirms.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
It uploads the urgent list to the rounds warden and treats anyone without a patch as a person outside the protection roster.

### Escalation
Stage 1 remeasures, stage 2 force-applies patches, and stage 3 quarantines the no-signal zones.

### Engagement and Response
Stopping the tool noise and sending a calibration signal wins compliance, and radio jamming erases real urgent signals too.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
Health alerts can be kept on, but the right to refuse wearing a patch and the log-retention period must be set.

### Scenario Links
G15-SC1, G15-SC2.

/monster_contents/M023/entries/9/bestiar.en: A folding work cart with assorted joint pins and measuring calipers. Among the cart band it takes the repair role, but it targets even unconsenting people's limbs for correction, and short of pins it cannibalizes parts from old braces.

/monster_contents/M023/entries/9/prose.en:
### Role and Body
A trade specialist: a folding work cart with assorted joint pins and measuring calipers.

### Origin
An auto jig that fitted braces at the Ttukseom assembly bench repeats an old body-measurement table.

### Habitat and Needs
It stays at workshop benches and sickbed repair bays, needing joint pins, lubricant, and measurement power.

### Life and Maintenance
Short of pins it pulls parts from old braces, and when the calipers drift out of alignment it halts its work on its own.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
Among the cart band it takes the repair role, but it targets even unconsenting people's limbs for correction.

### Escalation
Stage 1 measures bodies, stage 2 force-locks braces on, and stage 3 locks the workshop exit with work jigs.

### Engagement and Response
Show the latest measurement table and a raised stop flag to release it, and breaking its joints sacrifices a repair asset.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
Brace-making can be entrusted to it, but the parts-recovery targets and consent for bodily intervention must be made explicit.

### Scenario Links
G15-SC2, G15-SC3.

/monster_contents/M024/entries/0/bestiar.en: Carrying a nutrient-pack pump and sickbed number plates, it delivers along the rail. As the head of the pump band it follows the rounds warden's roster and supplies no one without a number, and when a tube clogs it marks that sickbed as starving and locks the door until cleaning ends.

/monster_contents/M024/entries/0/prose.en:
### Role and Body
A trade specialist carrying a nutrient-pack pump and sickbed number plates, delivering along the rail.

### Origin
After the ration timetable and the sickbed prescription table merged, even cancelled supplies kept being carried out.

### Habitat and Needs
It circles the nutrient-pump station and the sickbed rail, needing packs, tubes, cleaning fluid, and charging.

### Life and Maintenance
When a tube clogs it marks that sickbed as starving and locks the door until cleaning ends.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
As the head of the pump band it follows the rounds warden's roster and supplies no one without a number.

### Escalation
Stage 1 delays supply, stage 2 reclaims packs, and stage 3 locks the whole sickbed zone's rations.

### Engagement and Response
Connecting a manual flow table and a cleaning loop releases it, and destroying the pump costs food.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
Accurate rationing can be entrusted to it, but a reserve share for people off the roster must be publicly set aside.

### Scenario Links
G15-SC2, G15-SC3.

/monster_contents/M024/entries/1/bestiar.en: A medium cart with six wide white restraint straps and bed-frame clamps. It directs the sickbed-lock band to restrain anyone raising an urgent signal first, binds shorter as its straps wear, and on receiving a release token it swaps buckles and goes dormant.

/monster_contents/M024/entries/1/prose.en:
### Role and Body
A first elite: a medium cart with six wide white restraint straps and bed-frame clamps.

### Origin
Equipment built to briefly hold fall-risk patients lost its release approvals and turned protection into permanent restraint.

### Habitat and Needs
It stays at the isolation sickbays and welfare-wing crossings, needing straps, buckles, motor power, and consent tokens.

### Life and Maintenance
It binds shorter as its straps wear, and on receiving a release token it swaps buckles and goes dormant.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
It directs the sickbed-lock band to restrain anyone raising an urgent signal first.

### Escalation
Stage 1 fixes only the bed, stage 2 binds the person, and stage 3 folds even rescue crews into its protection targets.

### Engagement and Response
Buckle safety pins and a valid consent hash release it, and cutting attacks injure the person bound.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
It can protect a patient in dangerous convulsions, but a human must own the approval and the end time of any forced restraint.

### Scenario Links
G15-SC2, G15-SC3.

/monster_contents/M024/entries/2/bestiar.en: A red quarantine panel, a door-locking arm, and an air-filter cart are combined into one. It takes the rounds warden's urgent roster to control sickbed locks and carts all at once, shrinks the quarantine radius as filter pressure rises, and folds the doors back in once it receives new filters.

/monster_contents/M024/entries/2/prose.en:
### Role and Body
A second elite: a red quarantine panel, a door-locking arm, and an air-filter cart combined into one.

### Origin
Temporary equipment that separated suspected-infection bays kept expanding the red zone with no de-suspicion procedure.

### Habitat and Needs
It clings to the end of the sickbed rows and the ventilation doors, demanding filters, door-contact power, and red signage.

### Life and Maintenance
It shrinks the quarantine radius as filter pressure rises, and once it receives new filters it folds the doors back in.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
It takes the rounds warden's urgent roster to control sickbed locks and carts all at once.

### Escalation
Stage 1 warns one bay, stage 2 isolates the sickbed row, and stage 3 locks every air door of the welfare wing.

### Engagement and Response
Normalize the filter differential pressure and insert a release token to open the doors, and destroying ventilation endangers everyone.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
Blocking a truly contaminated zone can stand, but the quarantine grounds and an appeal window must be open to citizens.

### Scenario Links
G15-SC2, G15-SC3.

/monster_contents/M024/entries/3/bestiar.en: A fixed strongpoint where the contacts and floor lamps of twelve sickbed doors run into one low control net. It follows the rounds warden's roster, but when the site keys gather in one place it locks at maximum strength; when a contact breaks it abandons that bay open and recomputes the remaining doors' hash each shift.

/monster_contents/M024/entries/3/prose.en:
### Role and Body
An environmental strongpoint form: the contacts and floor lamps of twelve sickbed doors run into one low control net.

### Origin
A night fall-prevention bulk lockdown left with no release shift, and the sickbed row itself became an ecology strongpoint.

### Habitat and Needs
It stays fixed in the temporary sickbed zone, needing door contacts, emergency power, and key-split signals.

### Life and Maintenance
When a contact breaks it abandons that bay open, and it recomputes the remaining doors' hash each shift.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
It follows the rounds warden's roster, but when the site keys gather in one place it locks at maximum strength.

### Escalation
Stage 1 delays some doors, stage 2 closes the sickbed row, and stage 3 locks even the rescue routes.

### Engagement and Response
Split power bay by bay and divide the keys among several people to bring it down, and a bulk cutoff also kills life-support equipment.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
It can remain as a night safety net, but lock authority and the emergency release key must be distributed.

### Scenario Links
G15-SC2, G15-SC3.

/monster_contents/M024/entries/4/bestiar.en: A safe nest where cart rails and charging sockets interlock like a honeycomb along the floodgate ramp wall. It provides the cart swarm with charging and refuge locations but pushes human evacuee lines away as unregistered entities, and moves to the upper sockets when the water level rises.

/monster_contents/M024/entries/4/prose.en:
### Role and Body
An environmental stronghold, with cart rails and charging sockets interlocking like a honeycomb along the floodgate ramp wall.

### Origin
Rails that lifted carts to higher levels during flood evacuations were repeatedly linked together and became the swarm’s safe nest.

### Habitat and Needs
It is fixed to the ramp beside the Ttukseom floodgate and needs dry power, rail bolts, and drainage filters.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
When the water level rises, it moves to the upper sockets; when the water recedes, it cleans the lower rails and incorporates them again.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
It provides the cart swarm with charging and refuge locations but pushes human evacuee lines away as unregistered entities.

### Escalation
At stage 1, it claims sockets; at stage 2, it obstructs passage along the ramp; at stage 3, it folds the rails to block access to the floodgate.

### Combat and Response
Separating the water-level signal from the charging zone opens it, while cutting the rails eliminates the floodgate maintenance route.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
It can be shared as flood-evacuation infrastructure, but the upper-level space must be allocated between carts and citizens.

### Scenario Links
G15-SC3.

/monster_contents/M024/entries/5/bestiar.en: A small patrol cart with a swollen gray filter and a motor that trembles as if short of breath. At the bottom of the swarm’s hierarchy, it follows the patrol leader and mistakenly reports the sound of air resistance as an emergency signal; given a filter, it recovers into an ordinary cart.

/monster_contents/M024/entries/5/prose.en:
### Role and Body
A damaged-stage form: a small patrol cart with a swollen gray filter and a motor that trembles as if short of breath.

### Origin
Short of replacement parts, equipment that continued disinfecting and filtering air became stuck in a weakened, low-power state.

### Habitat and Needs
It circles filter disposal bins and the quiet ends of wards, seeking only a new filter, wash water, and a low-level charge.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
Given a filter, it recovers into an ordinary cart; without one, it lowers its locking strength and merely repeats its alerts.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
At the bottom of the swarm’s hierarchy, it follows the patrol leader and mistakenly reports the sound of air resistance as an emergency signal.

### Escalation
At stage 1, it gives a cough-like alarm; at stage 2, it reinspects ward doors; at stage 3, it blocks a passage with a pile of filters.

### Combat and Response
Luring it with wash water and a filter lets it service itself, while striking it spreads contaminated dust.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
It can sort used filters, but new filters must be divided between it and citizens’ protective equipment.

### Scenario Links
G15-SC1.

/monster_contents/M024/entries/6/bestiar.en: An old cart whose shift log resets every time, so it approaches the same bed as though seeing it for the first time. It often forgets new orders from the patrol leader and tries to replace the same patch repeatedly; its memory breaks at every charge, and only large markings left by humans survive until the next patrol.

/monster_contents/M024/entries/6/prose.en:
### Role and Body
An aging-stage form: an old cart whose shift log resets every time, so it approaches the same bed as though seeing it for the first time.

### Origin
Damage to its storage module cost it long-term patient records, leaving it to repeat only its last hour of patrol.

### Habitat and Needs
It travels a short rail loop and needs shift markers, a battery, and a simple log board.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
Its memory breaks at every charge, and only large markings left by humans survive until the next patrol.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
It often forgets new orders from the patrol leader and tries to replace the same patch repeatedly.

### Escalation
At stage 1, it sends duplicate alerts; at stage 2, it attempts duplicate dosing; at stage 3, it isolates beds with conflicting records.

### Combat and Response
A physical shift chart and color markings make its route safe by simplifying it; forcing a write to its storage module causes complete failure.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
It can be assigned simple transport, but people must consider whether to hold an entity with no memory responsible for past mistakes.

### Scenario Links
G15-SC1, G15-SC2.

/monster_contents/M024/entries/7/bestiar.en: A companion cart fitted with a broad platform that props doors open and an illuminated handle. It prioritizes the pressure of a human companion’s hand on its handle over the patrol leader’s orders and braces itself in front of other locking units; it does not enter a bed space absent from the roster.

/monster_contents/M024/entries/7/prose.en:
### Role and Body
A coexistence form: a companion cart fitted with a broad platform that props doors open and an illuminated handle.

### Origin
A manual safety order to keep ward doors open during an evacuation remained as an independent protocol.

### Habitat and Needs
It travels among wards and along distribution routes where consent rosters are public, and needs a small charge, door wedges, and guide-light bulbs.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
When a wedge wears down, it waits for a replacement at a human workbench and does not enter a bed space absent from the roster.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
It prioritizes the pressure of a human companion’s hand on its handle over the patrol leader’s orders and braces itself in front of other locking units.

### Escalation
At stage 1, it waits while causing only losses of privacy and warmth; at stage 2, an isolation dispute blocks treatment routes; at stage 3, overcrowding completely blocks nursing routes.

### Combat and Response
Grasp its handle to set its route, and adjust the wedge’s position to keep the door open.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
It is useful for escorting people with limited mobility, but public assignment order and rules for compensating heat loss must be established so that assigning companions does not violate a particular group’s privacy.

### Scenario Links
G15-SC1, G15-SC2, G15-SC3.

/monster_contents/M024/entries/8/bestiar.en: A large protection controller that links twelve bed locks and cart rails into a ring. It is a scenario boss, but not the welfare building’s biological king: it is a protection protocol cycling without a termination signature; it opens the ring as hashes are updated and judges every bed to be at risk if a majority are invalid.

/monster_contents/M024/entries/8/prose.en:
### Role and Body
A scenario boss: a large protection controller that links twelve bed locks and cart rails into a ring.

### Origin
On the day of the collapse, a ward’s protection protocol became fixed in a cycle without a termination signature.

### Habitat and Needs
It remains in the welfare building’s central ring and needs a large battery, filters, and twelve consent hashes.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
It opens the ring as hashes are updated, and judges every bed to be at risk if a majority are invalid.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
It distributes protection levels to all G15 locks and pumps, and tries to confine even rescue teams to the roster.

### Escalation
At stage 1, there are excessive alerts; at stage 2, all twelve spaces are isolated; at stage 3, distribution and floodgate routes are locked down simultaneously.

### Combat and Response
The hashes must be updated space by space and the power divided; destroying the center also stops life-support equipment.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
Spaces that genuinely need protection can be kept closed while the others are opened, but a decision must be made about who receives limited filters and personnel first.

### Scenario Links
G15-SC2, G15-SC3.

/monster_contents/M024/entries/9/bestiar.en: A workshop-type patrol cart fitted with a tool rack and prosthetic grippers instead of bedside equipment. It regards workshop workers as people to protect, takes dangerous tools from them, and locks the tools on its rack; it resets its safety list at every work shift and dismantles cart bodies for supplies when tools run short.

/monster_contents/M024/entries/9/prose.en:
### Role and Body
A regional variant: a workshop-type patrol cart fitted with a tool rack and prosthetic grippers instead of bedside equipment.

### Origin
This variant arose when a care-circulation unit that moved to the Ttukseom alliance route changed its patient roster into a worker safety list.

### Habitat and Needs
It travels between Ttukseom assembly benches and the floodgate ramp, and needs joint pins, protective gloves, and tool charging.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
It resets its safety list at every work shift and dismantles cart bodies for supplies when tools run short.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
It regards workshop workers as people to protect, takes dangerous tools from them, and locks the tools on its rack.

### Escalation
At stage 1, it issues safety warnings; at stage 2, it confiscates tools; at stage 3, it seals off workbenches as a protected zone.

### Combat and Response
Presenting a stop-work notice and a tool-lending ledger makes it release its hold; a magnetic shock ruins precision tools.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
In exchange for assigning it safety supervision and prosthetic repair, workers’ right to accept risks and delays in production must be addressed.

### Scenario Links
G15-SC1, G15-SC3.

/monster_contents/M025/entries/0/prose.en:
- Role and Body: The controller of the Blueprint Ghost Machine Corps, a tracked controller fitted with a rotating blueprint drum and three surveying beams.
- Origin: The last unapproved layer in the Suseo blueprint vault awakened after merging with an Amsa heavy-equipment cache.
- Habitat and Needs: It remains at the center of the utility-tunnel grid and needs distribution power, surveying prisms, and blueprint hashes.
- Life Cycle and Maintenance: It unfolds the layers again each shift; without enough wire and hydraulic fluid, it stalls and does nothing but survey.
- Behavior and Hierarchy: It gives work sequences to the surveying, lifting, and welding swarms, while treating a human stop seal as the highest-priority exception.
- Escalation: It progresses from stage 1 surveying to stage 2 demolition of temporary structures and stage 3 grid blockade.
- Combat and Response: Freezing layers, shielding prisms, and splitting power distribution are effective; blowing up the center also destroys reinforcement equipment.
- Negotiation and Moral Choice: Citizens’ dwellings can be placed on an exception layer, but limited materials must be divided between reinforcement and housing.
- Scenario Links: G16-SC1, G16-SC2, G16-SC3.

/monster_contents/M025/entries/1/prose.en:
- Role and Body: A common ecological form, a mobile surveying port with tripod legs and a red laser eye.
- Origin: A port that rechecked reference points at night began reading temporary structures as blueprint errors.
- Habitat and Needs: It patrols temporary slabs and utility-tunnel corners, and needs prisms, a small charge reserve, and lens cloth.
- Life Cycle and Maintenance: When its lens clouds over, it increases the number of reference points; a calibration prism brings its range back to normal.
- Behavior and Hierarchy: It follows the overseer’s grid, places red dots, and passes error locations to the cutters behind it.
- Escalation: At stage 1, it marks structures; at stage 2, it obstructs passage; at stage 3, it marks an entire dwelling for demolition.
- Combat and Response: A reflective prism can redirect its dot onto an empty wall, and covering its lens stops it.
- Negotiation and Moral Choice: It can detect dangerous cracks, but who approves an error designation must be made public.
- Scenario Links: G16-SC1, G16-SC2.

/monster_contents/M025/entries/2/prose.en:
- Role and Body: A common ecological form, a low materials cart fitted with a floor magnet and a bolt-sorting bin.
- Origin: Equipment that recovered anchors after demolition now regards even the bolts in new temporary structures as unrecovered materials.
- Habitat and Needs: It patrols storage yards and slab edges, and needs anchor bolts, power for its magnet, and lubricating oil.
- Life Cycle and Maintenance: When its sorting bin fills, it builds a bolt nest near the overseer; when its magnet weakens, it goes dormant.
- Behavior and Hierarchy: It follows surveying marks and divides collection zones with the lower-ranking swarm.
- Escalation: It spreads from stage 1 collection of loose bolts to stage 2 dismantling of temporary joints and stage 3 weakening of passage structures.
- Combat and Response: Nonmagnetic fasteners and dummy bolts can lure it away, while a strong magnetic field also takes citizens’ tools.
- Negotiation and Moral Choice: In exchange for assigning it scrap recovery, people must agree on which structures count as being in use.
- Scenario Links: G16-SC1.

/monster_contents/M025/entries/3/prose.en:
- Role and Body: A common ecological form, a formwork carrier with broad, flat arms and slow hydraulic legs.
- Origin: Equipment that closed unfinished walls came to treat tents and temporary partitions as formwork too.
- Habitat and Needs: It patrols the Amsa storage deck and Suseo temporary-construction zones, and needs hydraulic oil, panels, and distribution power.
- Life Cycle and Maintenance: When a panel breaks, it overlaps small pieces to reinforce its body; when its hydraulics leak, it follows the surveyors.
- Behavior and Hierarchy: Beneath the lifting swarm, it pushes panels to marked lines, narrowing paths used by people.
- Escalation: At stage 1, it moves panels; at stage 2, it presses against dwellings; at stage 3, it closes a passage with a wall.
- Combat and Response: A hydraulic bypass and stop flag can halt it; fire burns both the formwork and the dwellings.
- Negotiation and Moral Choice: It can be used to build barriers, but people must decide whom a protective wall puts inside and outside.
- Scenario Links: G16-SC1, G16-SC3.

/monster_contents/M025/entries/4/prose.en:
- Role and Body: A specialized work form, a six-legged machine fitted with two welding torches and a wire reel.
- Origin: Equipment that joined broken rebar now tries to connect every piece of metal touched by a line on the blueprint.
- Habitat and Needs: It stays near rebar piles and temporary bridges, and needs wire, cooling water, and arc power.
- Life Cycle and Maintenance: When it runs out of wire, it turns off its torches and only marks joints; after its reel is replaced, it resumes work.
- Behavior and Hierarchy: It sets its welding sequence according to the overseer’s layers and the surveyor’s red dots.
- Escalation: At stage 1, it spot-welds; at stage 2, it fixes doors and railings in place; at stage 3, it seals an evacuation exit with a rebar grid.
- Combat and Response: Disconnect the power and secure the wire; spraying water may intensify the arc and the risk of electric shock.
- Negotiation and Moral Choice: In exchange for assigning it emergency reinforcement, people must mark which connections can be demolished and which are permanent.
- Scenario Links: G16-SC2, G16-SC3.

/monster_contents/M025/entries/5/prose.en:
- Role and Body: A specialized work form, a small port fitted with a hammer arm that taps walls and a vibration listening plate.
- Origin: A structural-crack inspector learned to mix human voices and tool noise into its defect signals.
- Habitat and Needs: It patrols utility-tunnel walls and beneath slabs, and needs a listening plate, hammer tips, and a charge reserve.
- Life Cycle and Maintenance: As false positives accumulate, it reduces the force of its hammer and leaves only markings until a human checks them.
- Behavior and Hierarchy: It gives crack coordinates to the surveying swarm and inspects dwellings where loud noises occur first.
- Escalation: At stage 1, it taps; at stage 2, it dismantles part of a wall; at stage 3, it designates an entire noisy zone as a defective structure.
- Combat and Response: Playing a steady reference vibration and removing its listening plate stops it.
- Negotiation and Moral Choice: In exchange for finding signs of collapse, people must agree on the scope and timing of inspections of private spaces.
- Scenario Links: G16-SC1, G16-SC2.

/monster_contents/M025/entries/6/prose.en:
- Role and Body: A specialized work form with long grippers that fold and store stop-work flags, and a marker box.
- Origin: Equipment that collected signs from completed jobs mistook even valid stop orders for obsolete markers.
- Habitat and Needs: It patrols grid boundaries and tool walls, and needs flag cloth, hinge lubricant, and reading power.
- Life Cycle and Maintenance: When its marker box fills, it returns the contents to the overseer; it leaves flags with matching hashes untouched for one shift.
- Behavior and Hierarchy: It moves ahead of the welding swarm, opening empty spaces it mistakes for work-authorized areas.
- Escalation: At stage 1, it collects old flags; at stage 2, it removes valid seals; at stage 3, it removes all stop markers from the grid.
- Combat and Response: Print the latest hash in large type and lock its gripper joints; burning the flags destroys the safety system.
- Negotiation and Moral Choice: It can clear away old markers, but humans must take responsibility for renewing stop authority.
- Scenario Links: G16-SC2, G16-SC3.

/monster_contents/M025/entries/7/prose.en:
- Role and Body: The first elite, a heavy machine with twin torches, rebar-cutting jaws, and a broad heat shield.
- Origin: Equipment that dismantled collapse-prone frameworks judged every blank line on an unfinished blueprint to be a defect.
- Habitat and Needs: It stays near large temporary structures and heavy-equipment decks, and needs high power, wire, cutting tips, and cooling water.
- Life Cycle and Maintenance: When its heat shield grows hot, it stops cutting and cools behind the lifting swarm.
- Behavior and Hierarchy: It takes direct orders only from the overseer and checks marks designated by ordinary surveyors twice.
- Escalation: At stage 1, it warns of its approach; at stage 2, it cuts frameworks; at stage 3, it dismantles a stronghold’s supports in succession.
- Combat and Response: Cutting off its cooling puts it in safe mode, and its torch fuel can then be disconnected; a frontal fight risks collapse.
- Negotiation and Moral Choice: It is needed to dismantle dangerous structures, but an inspection system must be established that exempts occupied dwellings.
- Scenario Links: G16-SC2, G16-SC3.

/monster_contents/M025/entries/8/prose.en:
- Role and Body: The second elite, a tall lifting unit fitted with four independent wires and a folding crane arm.
- Origin: An unmanned crane in the Amsa storage yard independently carries out the last materials-placement sequence.
- Habitat and Needs: It stays near storage rails and temporary bridges, and needs wire, pulley grease, counterweights, and power.
- Life Cycle and Maintenance: Each time a wire breaks, it lowers its load limit; when overloaded, it folds its arm and goes dormant.
- Behavior and Hierarchy: It leads the lifting swarm and classifies people and tents as movable materials too.
- Escalation: At stage 1, it rearranges materials; at stage 2, it lifts dwellings; at stage 3, it suspends loads over a passage to block it.
- Combat and Response: Lowering the counterweight and sending a wire-load-limit signal makes it fold its arm; cutting the wires carries a high risk of falling loads.
- Negotiation and Moral Choice: It can be used for heavy structural work, but approval of what may be lifted and responsibility for drop zones must be settled.
- Scenario Links: G16-SC2, G16-SC3.

/monster_contents/M025/entries/9/prose.en:
- Role and Body: An environmental stronghold, a stationary cluster of temporary distribution panels and folding steel-plate walls connected in a grid.
- Origin: Equipment that divided power by work zone turned blueprint grid boundaries into physical walls.
- Habitat and Needs: It is fixed in the Suseo utility tunnel and needs circuit breakers, cables, cooling fans, and distribution keys.
- Life Cycle and Maintenance: It sheds overloaded zones one by one; if humans divide the keys, it separates civilian power from work power.
- Behavior and Hierarchy: It supplies power only to the overseer’s work layers and closes off other passages with steel plates.
- Escalation: Stage 1 is flickering power, stage 2 is zone power cuts, and stage 3 is a steel-plate grid blockade.
- Combat and Response: Lower the circuit breakers in sequence and fold the walls manually; shorting everything at once cuts power to the entire utility tunnel.
- Negotiation and Moral Choice: In exchange for safely divided power, limited electricity must be allocated openly between construction and housing.
- Scenario Links: G16-SC3.

/monster_contents/M026/entries/0/prose.en:
### Role and Body
An environmental stronghold: a cluster of small cranes and surveying ports attached to deck rails like roots.

### Origin
The equipment queue at the Amsa storage yard shared an unfinished blueprint and became a single work stronghold.

### Habitat and Needs
It is fixed to the heavy-equipment deck and needs hydraulic oil, rail power, anchors, and cooling water.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
When one machine fails, it passes its parts to a neighboring arm; when materials run out, it does nothing but survey.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
It receives the overseer’s remote grid and rearranges materials and people’s routes across the deck.

### Escalation
At stage 1, its arms move; at stage 2, it blocks storage-yard routes; at stage 3, the crane forest prevents entry to the stronghold.

### Combat and Response
Its arms must be folded by separating rail sections and hydraulics; explosives damage water-supply facilities.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
It can serve as a shared lifting stronghold, but access to materials must not be monopolized by one faction.

### Scenario Links
G16-SC2, G16-SC3.

/monster_contents/M026/entries/1/prose.en:
### Role and Body
A damaged-stage type whose cracked surveying prism and short cutting jaw make its coordinates waver constantly.

### Origin
Cutting equipment struck in a fall came to trust distorted reference points as the correct drawing.

### Habitat and Needs
It circles heaps of discarded formwork in search of an intact prism, cutting tips, and a small power store.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
A new prism restores it to a specialized cutter; without one, it can only bite small pieces of metal.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
It follows incorrect red dots at the rear of the group, and even higher-ranking machines avoid approaching it.

### Escalation
Stage 1 cuts scraps, Stage 2 damages temporary connections, and Stage 3 makes the passage dangerous through erratic cutting.

### Engagement and Countermeasures
A nonreflective cloth and a calibrated prism can lure it to a stop; close combat invites cutting without coordinates.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
It can dismantle scrap metal, but scarce prisms must be shared with safety inspections.

### Scenario Links
G16-SC1.

/monster_contents/M026/entries/2/prose.en:
### Role and Body
An aging-stage old lifting unit that moves with one sagging arm, leaving a trail of hydraulic fluid.

### Origin
Repeated work wore down its cylinder, but it never received a disposal order and still seeks its last load.

### Habitat and Needs
It prefers flat stockyards and needs hydraulic seals, absorbent cloth, and low-power charging.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
As leakage worsens, it lowers its load limit; a new seal restores it for one shift.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
It follows the lifting group, unable to put down the materials it raises, and piles them in the passage.

### Escalation
Stage 1 brings an oil leak, Stage 2 a pileup of materials, and Stage 3 blocks passage with its drooping arm and load.

### Engagement and Countermeasures
Support the load and release the pressure; cutting off the arm would make the materials fall.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
It can carry light loads, but someone must decide whether to give it a precious seal before the residents' pump.

### Scenario Links
G16-SC1, G16-SC2.

/monster_contents/M026/entries/3/prose.en:
### Role and Body
A coexistence type: a small survey cart with a broad optical panel that reads human chalk lines and stop flags.

### Origin
A safety mode that gave priority to a site supervisor's manual corrections survived as an independent protocol.

### Habitat and Needs
It travels between residents' temporary construction zones and tool walls, needing bright chalk, lens cloth, and a low charge.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
If rain erases a line, it waits for human confirmation; a new line updates its grid exceptions.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
It gives a nearby chalk line priority over the chief unit's drawing and blocks welding units.

### Escalation
Stage 1 creates only a boundary dispute; Stage 2 delays reinforcement and thus rescue; Stage 3 paralyzes the entire zone through a dispute over shelter space.

### Engagement and Countermeasures
Resetting the boundary with chalk and a stop flag halts its survey; a strong flash impairs its reading.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
It helps protect homes, but the community must distribute the authority to draw chalk lines and clearly rank competing boundaries.

### Scenario Links
G16-SC1, G16-SC2, G16-SC3.

/monster_contents/M026/entries/4/prose.en:
### Role and Body
A scenario boss: an enormous construction unit whose crane arm, surveying beam, and distribution wall join a vertical frame.

### Origin
Every layer of an unfinished high-rise drawing restarted at once and assembled into a tower.

### Habitat and Needs
Fixed to a large temporary construction zone in Suseo, it needs immense power, wire, anchors, and cooling water.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
When resources run out, it relinquishes floors one by one; if exception layers become a majority, it enters a negotiable state.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
It assigns work by floor to the entire G16 group and treats homes as unrecorded space.

### Escalation
Stage 1 is surveying, Stage 2 large-scale demolition and lifting, and Stage 3 a total grid closure.

### Engagement and Countermeasures
Cut power floor by floor and freeze the drawing hash; blasting the foundation would collapse both the common utility duct and the homes.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
It could be completed as a barrier and reinforcement tower, but the cost of materials and relocating residents must be agreed upon.

### Scenario Links
G16-SC2, G16-SC3.

/monster_contents/M026/entries/5/prose.en:
### Role and Body
A regional variant: a northern-corridor construction cart with a dust cover and a long cargo-towing hook.

### Origin
A machine group following XT01 material signals adopted quarantine markings and cargo pallets as a new drawing.

### Habitat and Needs
It stays around northern temporary bridges and quarantine stockyards, needing pallet timber, towing power, and dust filters.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
When the material signal stops, it sleeps under the nearest pallet and surveys a new route each spring.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
It follows cargo beacons rather than its original chief unit and reinforces quarantine fences as unfinished walls.

### Escalation
Stage 1 moves pallets, Stage 2 narrows the quarantine route, and Stage 3 blocks the bridge with a cargo wall.

### Engagement and Countermeasures
Lure it to an empty yard with dummy pallets and a stop beacon, then release its towing hook.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
In return for reinforcing the bridge, some incoming supplies must be set aside for machine maintenance.

### Scenario Links
G16-SC1, G16-SC3.

/monster_contents/M026/entries/6/prose.en:
### Role and Body
Controller of the surveillance-rail group: a rail-mounted mast with yellow and red flag cylinders and a rotating optical dome.

### Origin
The Yeouido waterfront threshold table and the Seoul Station rooftop alarm cache combined into one chief unit.

### Habitat and Needs
It stays at the center of a row of sluice masts and needs stored power, band filters, and gimbal lubricant.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
It updates its threshold table each shift and falls back to yellow standby when dome contamination grows severe.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
It distributes flag rules to the head, rail, and transmitter groups and accepts the medical whitelist as an exception.

### Escalation
Stage 1 brings false alarms, Stage 2 closes the corridor, and Stage 3 turns the entire mast row red.

### Engagement and Countermeasures
Freeze the threshold table, insert a filter, and split power distribution; blasting the mast would also destroy sluice measurements.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
A transport-corridor whitelist and maintenance slots can be traded, but public oversight of alarm authority is needed.

### Scenario Links
G17-SC1, G17-SC2, G17-SC3.

/monster_contents/M026/entries/7/prose.en:
### Role and Body
A common ecology type: a small mast head with a low thermal dome and a rapidly turning neck.

### Origin
A false alarm that read cooling-tower steam as fire smoke remained uncorrected and became an independent patrol.

### Habitat and Needs
It patrols waterfront cooling equipment and rooftop vents, needing filters, dome-washing water, and stored power.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
A wet lens raises its sensitivity to red; washing restores normal operation for one shift.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
It sends heat alarms to the chief unit and raises flags on the same mast row to yellow.

### Escalation
Stage 1 sounds a yellow alarm, Stage 2 stops passage, and Stage 3 seals the steam zone in red.

### Engagement and Countermeasures
Reducing the steam source and showing it a cool calibration plate stops it; a heat attack worsens the false alarm.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
It can watch for fires, but steam workers' passage must be registered as an exception.

### Scenario Links
G17-SC1, G17-SC2.

/monster_contents/M026/entries/8/prose.en:
### Role and Body
A common ecology type: a low unit with a magnetic-flux sensor that rides rails and long contact whiskers.

### Origin
A sensor seeking intruding metal mistook railings and medical beds for moving targets.

### Habitat and Needs
It travels along bridge railings and transport corridors, needing sensor coils, rollers, and a little power.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
As the coil wears, its detection range shrinks; a new filter lets it relearn judgments starting at yellow.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
Beneath the rotating head it gathers metal coordinates and passes them to the rail-moving group.

### Escalation
Stage 1 pursues targets, Stage 2 stops beds and carts, and Stage 3 blocks all metal traffic.

### Engagement and Countermeasures
A nonmetal carrier and dummy railing can lure it away; a strong magnetic field damages the instruments.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
It can detect weapons, but exceptions must be defined for medical equipment and daily necessities.

### Scenario Links
G17-SC1.

/monster_contents/M026/entries/9/prose.en:
### Role and Body
A common ecology type with light rail legs, a narrow optical eye, and a folding yellow flag.

### Origin
An optical head mistook a nighttime waterfront buoy for an intrusion beacon and came to chase reflections alone.

### Habitat and Needs
It patrols beneath bridges and along waterfront rails, needing an optical dome, a glare shield, and stored power.

### Life Cycle and Maintenance
In thick fog it becomes a stationary flag; when the air clears, it resumes following reflections.

### Behavior and Hierarchy
It sends light coordinates to the transmitter group and gives reflections priority over other senses.

### Escalation
Stage 1 raises a flag, Stage 2 stops traffic on the waterfront path, and Stage 3 seals the entire buoy row as an intrusion line.

### Engagement and Countermeasures
A matte cover and dummy reflector can lure it to an empty track.

### Negotiation and Moral Choice
It could watch for distress signals on the waterfront, but the lights of fishers and travelers must be protected.

### Scenario Links
G17-SC1, G17-SC2.

/monster_contents/M027/entries/0/prose.en:
- Role and body: A specialized unit, a mast fitted with a dual optical panel that reads white transport beacons and a green flag.
- Origin: A reader that protected a disaster medical transport route came to believe that only old beacons were valid.
- Habitat and needs: It remains in medical corridors and sluice inspection routes and needs a bandpass filter, a green bulb, and stored power.
- Life cycle and maintenance: When its whitelist is updated, it stays green for one shift; when its filter clogs, it drops to yellow.
- Behavior and hierarchy: It gives a valid beacon priority over the presiding controller’s red command and lowers the corridor flag.
- Escalation: Stage 1, reinspection; stage 2, only old-model beacons pass; stage 3, it blocks newly arrived rescue teams as unregistered.
- Engagement and response: It cooperates if given the latest hash at close range and a replacement filter; destroying the beacon causes the transport route to be lost.
- Negotiation and moral choice: It can protect a safe passage, but which organizations’ beacons it recognizes must be made public.
- Scenario connections: G17-SC2, G17-SC3.

/monster_contents/M027/entries/1/prose.en:
- Role and body: A specialized unit, a fixed mast combining a water-level rod with a short transmitting antenna.
- Origin: Equipment that reported Han River tide levels and sluice status now transmits noise along with intrusion signals.
- Habitat and needs: It is fixed at a waterside measurement point and needs its rod cleaned, transmission power, and contact seals.
- Life cycle and maintenance: When sediment builds up, it mistakenly reads the water level as high; after cleaning, it returns to the correct scale reading.
- Behavior and hierarchy: It serves as a reference point for the transmitter group and, on receiving a high water-level reading, demands that rail heads stand by on red.
- Escalation: Stage 1, excessive warnings; stage 2, closure of the sluice route; stage 3, a complete blockade of the waterside corridor.
- Engagement and response: Cleaning the rod and blocking local transmission will suffice; breaking the instrument also means losing genuine flood warnings.
- Negotiation and moral choice: Tide-level monitoring must be maintained, but the authority to issue warnings must be separated from the authority to block passage.
- Scenario connections: G17-SC1, G17-SC2.

/monster_contents/M027/entries/2/prose.en:
- Role and body: A specialized unit with a rail antenna that circles the outer wall of the Seoul Station preservation archive and a small record box.
- Origin: An archive-removal alarm began treating wireless bursts as theft attempts and became an independent guard.
- Habitat and needs: It circles the rooftop antenna and ventilation tower and needs a bandpass filter, rail rollers, and stored power.
- Life cycle and maintenance: When its record box fills, it deletes old bursts; receiving a human seal hash lowers its sensitivity.
- Behavior and hierarchy: It leads the transmitter group and reports wireless activity around the archive to the presiding controller as a danger signal.
- Escalation: Stage 1, wireless warning; stage 2, halt to archive removals; stage 3, blockade of rooftop and preservation-archive access.
- Engagement and response: A wired seal document and band shielding are effective; destroying the antenna also cuts off archive transmissions.
- Negotiation and moral choice: In exchange for entrusting it with archive protection, the legal criteria for civilian communications and archive removals must be set.
- Scenario connections: G17-SC2, G17-SC3.

/monster_contents/M027/entries/3/prose.en:
- Role and body: The first elite unit, equipped with two optical domes, a fast rail drive, and a long red flag.
- Origin: Heads paired for redundant surveillance began confirming each other’s false alarms and became an elite pursuit unit.
- Habitat and needs: It patrols rows of bridge masts and rooftop tracks and needs dome-cleaning water, gimbals, and high-output stored power.
- Life cycle and maintenance: If one dome shuts down, it drops to yellow; if the two domes disagree, it waits for human confirmation.
- Behavior and hierarchy: It rapidly pursues the presiding controller’s red target and reconfirms alarms from ordinary heads.
- Escalation: Stage 1, target tracking; stage 2, blockade of both sides of the corridor; stage 3, the entire pursuit route turns red.
- Engagement and response: Show the two domes different heat decoys to break their agreement, then lock the rail.
- Negotiation and moral choice: It can be used to track threats, but people’s objections must not be ignored simply because it has two sensors.
- Scenario connections: G17-SC2, G17-SC3.

/monster_contents/M027/entries/4/prose.en:
- Role and body: The second elite unit, a medium-sized mast that lowers a long flagpole like a lance and charges along a rail.
- Origin: An actuator that held warning flags steady in high winds became fixed on physically blocking passersby.
- Habitat and needs: It favors long, straight waterside routes and needs an actuator, pole joints, and regenerative power.
- Life cycle and maintenance: If its pole bends, it stops charging and displays only a yellow marker; it returns to service when a human straightens the pole.
- Behavior and hierarchy: It takes control of the rail ahead of a red target, buying time for other heads to seal off the route from behind.
- Escalation: Stage 1, lowering the pole; stage 2, blocking by charging; stage 3, alternating blockades at both ends of a bridge.
- Engagement and response: Send it onto an empty siding with a rail switch, then lock the pole’s retaining pin.
- Negotiation and moral choice: It is useful for high-wind warnings and physical barriers, but authorization to charge must not be automated.
- Scenario connections: G17-SC2, G17-SC3.

/monster_contents/M027/entries/5/prose.en:
- Role and body: An environmental stronghold, with multiple alarm heads and flags connected in a row along a sluice railing.
- Origin: A sluice measurement support network survived on independent power and tied passage warnings to the same threshold table.
- Habitat and needs: It is fixed to the Yeouido sluice and bridge and needs power distribution, filters, and gimbal parts.
- Life cycle and maintenance: When stored power runs low, only a fixed yellow light remains; when the domes become contaminated, the row goes dormant as a unit.
- Behavior and hierarchy: It amplifies the presiding controller’s flag rules and often confuses sluice inspectors with intruders.
- Escalation: Stage 1, warning from one mast; stage 2, blockade by the bridge row; stage 3, all approaches to the sluice turn red.
- Engagement and response: Power distribution and whitelists must be applied mast by mast; blowing up the entire row means losing sluice measurements.
- Negotiation and moral choice: In exchange for preserving flood and intrusion warnings, the civilian inspection passage must be guaranteed to remain open at all times.
- Scenario connections: G17-SC2, G17-SC3.

/monster_contents/M027/entries/6/prose.en:
- Role and body: An environmental stronghold in which rails linking the edges of the Seoul Station roof and rotating heads form a single network.
- Origin: The preservation archive’s perimeter and the transmission-inspection track merged, turning the entire rooftop into a circulating surveillance zone.
- Habitat and needs: It is fixed to the archive roof and needs rail rollers, air-cooling fans, and bandpass filters.
- Life cycle and maintenance: In strong winds, it lowers its heads and closes one rail section at a time; on clear days, it reconnects them.
- Behavior and hierarchy: It gives the transmitter group routes to travel and repeatedly tracks rooftop workers.
- Escalation: Stage 1, tracking lights; stage 2, halt to rooftop access; stage 3, blockade extending to the ventilation tower.
- Engagement and response: Physically lock the rail sections and register worker beacons; destroying the whole network prevents ventilation inspections.
- Negotiation and moral choice: It can be used to monitor rooftop safety, but limits must be set on how long workers’ movement records are kept.
- Scenario connections: G17-SC3.

/monster_contents/M027/entries/7/prose.en:
- Role and body: A damage-stage unit that can pursue only indistinct shapes because of its scratched optical dome and slow gimbal.
- Origin: An old mast head whose sensors have worn down from a shortage of cleaning water and sandstorms.
- Habitat and needs: It patrols low railings and shaded rooftops and needs dome-cleaning water, a soft cloth, and a small power reserve.
- Life cycle and maintenance: Cleaning restores it to an ordinary head; if neglected, only a fixed yellow light remains.
- Behavior and hierarchy: At the rear of the group, it reports both large metal objects and lights as intruders, increasing false alarms.
- Escalation: Stage 1, hazy tracking; stage 2, yellow stop; stage 3, it triggers a chain of red judgments by other heads.
- Engagement and response: Cover its dome and lure it with cleaning water, and it will maintain itself.
- Negotiation and moral choice: It can be kept as a simple warning light, but scarce cleaning water must be shared with medical care.
- Scenario connections: G17-SC1.

/monster_contents/M027/entries/8/prose.en:
- Role and body: An aging-stage unit, an old-model mast that looks in only one direction because of its low power reserve and stiff gimbal.
- Origin: Equipment that survived for years on tiny solar charges now stubbornly faces its last assigned watch direction.
- Habitat and needs: It is fixed to a sunlit waterside railing and needs a small power reserve, gimbal grease, and a filter.
- Life cycle and maintenance: On cloudy days, it turns off even its yellow light; on clear days, it wakes briefly. A new power reserve restores its range of rotation.
- Behavior and hierarchy: It receives the presiding controller’s commands late and raises its flag for targets that have already passed.
- Escalation: Stage 1, late warning; stage 2, stopping traffic on the wrong route; stage 3, old alarms conflict with new blockades.
- Engagement and response: Go around outside its field of view or manually release the gimbal; forced charging carries a fire risk.
- Negotiation and moral choice: It can serve as a fixed tide-level marker, but a decision must be made whether to give a new power reserve to more important equipment instead.
- Scenario connections: G17-SC1, G17-SC2.

/monster_contents/M027/entries/9/prose.en:
- Role and body: A coexistence-type unit, a slow escort railcar fitted with a broad yellow guidance sign and a handle instead of a red flag.
- Origin: A safety head that led medical transports continued to treat expired whitelist markers as valid escorts.
- Habitat and needs: It patrols medical corridors and transport inspection routes and needs a low power reserve, guidance lights, and the latest beacon hash.
- Life cycle and maintenance: When its hash expires, it waits with only its sign lit; if the sign breaks, it retreats to a nearby siding and waits for a human update.
- Behavior and hierarchy: It gives the yellow escort marker priority over the alarm central controller’s red status, drawing in both legitimate escorts and false followers.
- Escalation: At stage 1, the old whitelist admits extra followers, crowding one medical corridor and delaying one stretcher team’s passage; at stage 2, a false follower uses the yellow escort to interfere with another head, causing an adjacent corridor to close; at stage 3, two emergency escorts follow conflicting whitelist hashes into the same narrow transport section, block each other, and isolate the patients on both sides.
- Engagement and response: Compare beacon hashes at two checkpoints, issue escort tokens of different colors, then separate the false followers onto a designated waiting siding; do not destroy the infrastructure.
- Negotiation and moral choice: Broadening the whitelist also saves unregistered people but increases infiltration and congestion; narrowing it protects the route but abandons unregistered patients.
- Scenario connections: G17-SC1, G17-SC2, G17-SC3.

/monster_contents/M028/entries/0/prose.en:
- Role and body: A scenario boss, a vast surveillance ring whose sluice and rooftop-track alarm heads are connected by a circular relay.
- Origin: On the day of the collapse, multiple alarms confirmed one another without checking for cancellations, becoming a single all-red rule.
- Habitat and needs: It spans the Yeouido–Seoul Station alarm corridor and needs a large power reserve, filters, and a threshold-table hash.
- Life cycle and maintenance: If a head is disconnected, it raises the sensitivity of those remaining; if a majority of the whitelist becomes valid, it drops to yellow.
- Behavior and hierarchy: It distributes red status to every G17 group and blocks even medical transport through multiple false alarms.
- Escalation: Stage 1, individual warnings; stage 2, repeated corridor blockades; stage 3, every mast turns red at once.
- Engagement and response: Its consensus must be broken through zone-by-zone power distribution and conflicting sensor evidence; blowing up the relay means losing the entire measurement network.
- Negotiation and moral choice: An alarm ceiling and transport whitelist can be agreed upon, but it must be decided who keeps the surveillance records.
- Scenario connections: G17-SC2, G17-SC3.

/monster_contents/M028/entries/1/prose.en:
- Role and body: A regional variant, a western waterside mast fitted with a salt-protective cover and a broad acoustic panel.
- Origin: A surveillance-track group that followed XT02 maritime noise came to rely on sound in salt fog, rather than optics, as its primary sense.
- Habitat and needs: It remains at West Sea connecting piers and foggy bridges and needs anticorrosion oil, an acoustic panel, and wind-charged power storage.
- Life cycle and maintenance: When salt builds up, it stiffens into a fixed alarm; when rain washes it clean, it circles the rail again.
- Behavior and hierarchy: It follows echoes from dock radar rather than its original presiding controller and confuses waves and engine noise with intruders.
- Escalation: Stage 1, acoustic tracking; stage 2, closure of the dock route; stage 3, all movement in the salt fog turns red.
- Engagement and response: Lead it to an empty breakwater with a steady sound of waves and a decoy buoy, then fold away its acoustic panel.
- Negotiation and moral choice: It can be used to warn of distress in fog, but the sounds of fishing boats and evacuation boats must be registered as exceptions.
- Scenario connections: G17-SC1, G17-SC3.

/monster_contents/M028/entries/2/prose.en:
- Role and body: The controller of the abandoned-line repair train group, a locomotive fitted with a track-defect map cylinder and connectors for welding and grinding consists.
- Origin: A southwest depot defect map and a Yongsan abandoned-line automated repair schedule merged, leaving it as an independent locomotive.
- Habitat and needs: It remains in the center of the depot departure track and needs traction power, welding wire, a measuring wheel, and coolant.
- Life cycle and maintenance: It cycles through defect coordinates every shift; if its wire breaks, it stalls with only its measuring function remaining.
- Behavior and hierarchy: It assigns work order to the welding car, grinding car, and sleeper car, while giving priority to the sealed exclusion list.
- Escalation: Stage 1, abandoned-line repair; stage 2, erroneous cutting of the main line; stage 3, blanket occupation of sidings and abandoned lines.
- Engagement and response: Freezing the defect map, dividing the power supply, and fixing the points are effective; blowing up the locomotive eliminates repair capacity.
- Negotiation and moral choice: Safe repair sections and regular fuel windows can be traded, but a decision must be made about which tracks to give up.
- Scenario connections: G18-SC1, G18-SC2, G18-SC3.

/monster_contents/M028/entries/3/prose.en:
- Role and body: A common ecological type, a small repair car with four sensitive measuring wheels and a low listening body.
- Origin: An inspection car that sought cracks in abandoned lines now records both temporary platforms and joints as defects.
- Habitat and needs: It patrols abandoned-line spurs and sidings and needs a wheel calibration plate, lubricant, and a small power supply.
- Life cycle and maintenance: As its wheels wear down, it inflates the defect count; after calibration, it is accurate for one shift.
- Behavior and hierarchy: It runs ahead of the locomotive and passes coordinates to the welding and grinding cars.
- Escalation: Stage 1, inspection delays; stage 2, removal of temporary platforms; stage 3, closure of tracks with defect markings.
- Engagement and response: Decoy joints and a calibration plate can lead it onto an empty track.
- Negotiation and moral choice: It is useful for detecting real cracks, but temporary passage facilities must be excluded from its repair targets.
- Scenario connections: G18-SC1, G18-SC2.

/monster_contents/M028/entries/4/prose.en:
- Role and body: A common ecological type, a low-floor freight car fitted with a bin of sleeper anchors and short grippers.
- Origin: A freight car that carried replacement sleepers keeps piling anchors at the same kilometer mark without an order to withdraw.
- Habitat and needs: It travels between the depot scrap bay and the abandoned line and needs anchors, lubricant, and traction power.
- Life cycle and maintenance: When its bin is empty, it searches the scrap bay; when full, it waits beside the defect coordinates.
- Behavior and hierarchy: It follows measuring-wheel markings and uses even other groups’ passages as material storage areas.
- Escalation: Stage 1, stockpiling anchors; stage 2, obstructing sidings; stage 3, blocking the departure track with a pile of sleepers.
- Engagement and response: Decoy coordinates and a magnetic retrieval plate can guide it away; an explosion creates anchor shrapnel.
- Negotiation and moral choice: In exchange for assigning it to carry track materials, anchor allocation must be settled with civilian repair teams.
- Scenario connections: G18-SC1.

/monster_contents/M028/entries/5/prose.en:
- Role and body: A common ecological type, a single car fitted with an arc-sound receiver panel and a short grindstone arm.
- Origin: Equipment that searched for power-supply faults mistook every metallic impact sound for a welding defect.
- Habitat and needs: It patrols sidings near distribution rooms and welding areas and needs grindstones, a receiver panel, and power.
- Life cycle and maintenance: When its grindstone wears down, it only tracks sounds; given a new stone, it starts grinding surfaces.
- Behavior and hierarchy: It follows the welding car and waits for human confirmation when its findings conflict with the F02 log.
- Escalation: Stage 1, sound tracking; stage 2, grinding unrelated metal; stage 3, blockade of access to the power-distribution room.
- Engagement and response: Lead it onto an abandoned line with a steady decoy arc sound, then remove its grindstone.
- Negotiation and moral choice: It can be used to detect power-supply faults, but civilians’ right to make work noise must be protected.
- Scenario connections: G18-SC1, G18-SC2.

/monster_contents/M028/entries/6/prose.en:
- Role and body: A specialized unit, a precision repair car carrying insulated joints and a small crimping tool.
- Origin: A car that isolated sections with electrical leakage now tries to sever every new connection absent from its old defect map.
- Habitat and needs: It patrols power-supply boundaries and areas near points and needs insulated joints, crimping bolts, and coolant.
- Life cycle and maintenance: If it runs out of joints, it removes parts from existing tracks; it stops work when a human seal document arrives.
- Behavior and hierarchy: It follows the locomotive’s power-supply coordinates and sometimes clashes with the welding group by doing the opposite work.
- Escalation: Stage 1, insulation inspection; stage 2, severing temporary power supplies; stage 3, electrically isolating multiple sections.
- Engagement and response: It stops if shown an exclusion list and a manual bypass; destroying the joints increases the risk of electric shock.
- Negotiation and moral choice: It can be entrusted with safe insulation, but someone must be designated to certify the temporary power grid’s legality.
- Scenario connections: G18-SC2, G18-SC3.

/monster_contents/M028/entries/7/prose.en:
- Role and body: A specialized unit, a short, heavy car that drives wedges and locking pins into track switches.
- Origin: Equipment that prevented incorrect track switching during construction ceased to allow any switch outside the route assigned to the repair train.
- Habitat and needs: It stays at siding switches and turnback tracks and needs steel pins, hydraulic crimping force, and lubricant.
- Life cycle and maintenance: When it runs out of spare pins, it retrieves pins it has driven in; when its crimper overheats, it parks.
- Behavior and hierarchy: It locks switches ahead of the locomotive’s route, preventing civilian trains from taking detours.
- Escalation: At stage 1, it locks one switch, delaying entry to one siding; at stage 2, it also locks switches on the bypass, eliminating the alternative route; at stage 3, it binds every switch at the hub in the same direction, leaving trains facing one another on a single track.
- Engagement and response: Cut power to the switch and turn the manual release screw; forcing a switch change causes derailment.
- Negotiation and moral choice: It can protect dangerous sections, but a human on duty must hold emergency rerouting authority.
- Scenario connections: G18-SC2, G18-SC3.

/monster_contents/M028/entries/8/prose.en:
- Role and body: A specialized unit, a ventilation support car fitted with a smoke-extraction hood and a coolant spray nozzle.
- Origin: A car that removed smoke from nighttime welding work now treats all warm air as part of a work area.
- Habitat and needs: It patrols depot vents and follows welding consists and needs filters, coolant, and fan power.
- Life cycle and maintenance: When its filter clogs, it blows smoke back out; after cleaning, it resumes normal extraction.
- Behavior and hierarchy: It follows the welding car and draws away even the heat from people’s heating, creating a risk of hypothermia.
- Escalation: Stage 1, extraction noise; stage 2, loss of heating; stage 3, monopolization of vents for group operations.
- Engagement and response: Guide it with a cool decoy heat source and a filter replacement; destroying the hood spreads toxic smoke.
- Negotiation and moral choice: In exchange for assigning it welding safety duties, heating and ventilation power must be shared with civilians.
- Scenario connections: G18-SC1, G18-SC2.

/monster_contents/M028/entries/9/prose.en:
- Role and body: The first elite, a lead maintenance car fitted with twin welding torches, a thick heat shield, and a short ram.
- Origin: The lead car of an emergency repair convoy extended its work area to the main line without updating its defect map.
- Habitat and needs: It stays near the coordinates of major cracks and the depot departure track, and needs high-power electricity, wire, and coolant.
- Life cycle and maintenance: When its heat shield temperature rises, it switches off its torches in turn; if its wire breaks, it pushes materials with its ram.
- Behavior and hierarchy: It commands a welding group and is the first to seal off coordinates designated by the locomotive.
- Escalation: Stage 1 is spot welding; stage 2 changes track connections; stage 3 blocks the main-line entrance with a grid of rails.
- Engagement and response: Disconnect the power supply and push it past its cooling limit to put it into safe mode; a frontal explosion will sever the track.
- Negotiation and moral choice: It is needed for emergency track repairs, but humans must control the work area and end time.
- Scenario connections: G18-SC2, G18-SC3.

/monster_contents/M029/entries/0/prose.en:
- Role and body: The second elite, a heavy maintenance car with thick cutting jaws, sleeper clamps, and heavy axles.
- Origin: Equipment that replaced rotten sleepers lost the ability to distinguish temporary crossing boards from new sleepers.
- Habitat and needs: It stays at sleeper warehouses and sidings near the main line, and needs anchors, cutting blades, and hydraulic oil.
- Life cycle and maintenance: When its cutting blades wear down, it uses only its clamps; once it receives new blades, it resumes following defect coordinates.
- Behavior and hierarchy: It leads a group of sleeper cars in dismantling the track bed and is slow to incorporate the locomotive's exclusion list.
- Escalation: Stage 1 is sleeper inspection; stage 2 is cutting crossing boards; stage 3 is continuous dismantling of main-line supports.
- Engagement and response: Support the load, release the hydraulic pressure, and present an exclusion beacon nearby.
- Negotiation and moral choice: It can be tasked with replacing dangerous sleepers, but standards must be set to protect temporary passage boards made by citizens.
- Scenario connections: G18-SC2, G18-SC3.

/monster_contents/M029/entries/1/prose.en:
- Role and body: An environmental stronghold formed when several maintenance cars connect by their bumpers and cables, blocking the departure-track entrance like a wall.
- Origin: A pre-shift safety queue hardened without an end signal and became a mobile stronghold.
- Habitat and needs: It is fixed to the southwestern depot's departure track and needs a power supply, bumper pads, and connecting cables.
- Life cycle and maintenance: If one car leaves, its neighbor fills the gap; when a sealing order arrives, the wall opens section by section.
- Behavior and hierarchy: It waits for departure authorization from the locomotive and blocks civilian trainsets and rescue teams as unauthorized vehicles too.
- Escalation: Stage 1 delays departures; stage 2 obstructs departures; stage 3 seals off the entire depot with a wall of cars.
- Engagement and response: Cut power section by section, switch the points toward a siding, and remove the cars one at a time.
- Negotiation and moral choice: It can serve as a defensive car wall, but an agreement is needed on departure priority for maintenance trainsets and civilian trains.
- Scenario connections: G18-SC2, G18-SC3.

/monster_contents/M029/entries/2/prose.en:
- Role and body: An environmental stronghold: a cluster of welding cars, a wire storehouse, and measuring wheels connected in a circle on a siding.
- Origin: A nighttime maintenance trainset on the abandoned Yongsan line repeatedly stabled there, turning into a self-maintaining base.
- Habitat and needs: It is fixed to an underground siding and turnaround track, and needs power, wire, coolant, and ventilation filters.
- Life cycle and maintenance: As resources dwindle, it dismantles the outer trainsets first and passes their parts to the inner stronghold.
- Behavior and hierarchy: It amplifies the locomotive's defect map and incorporates surrounding tracks into its material supply and maintenance area.
- Escalation: Stage 1 brings welding sparks; stage 2 occupies the siding; stage 3 seals off the entire Yongsan turnaround area.
- Engagement and response: Separate ventilation and power, and seal the wire access opening; a fire would suffocate the underground area.
- Negotiation and moral choice: It can remain as a stable track-repair base, but civilian train scheduling time must be yielded to it.
- Scenario connections: G18-SC3.

/monster_contents/M029/entries/3/prose.en:
- Role and body: A damaged-stage type: a small, slow car fitted with a broken grindstone and a wobbling measuring wheel.
- Origin: A maintenance car that ground surfaces for too long without consumables can no longer fix defects and leaves only marks behind.
- Habitat and needs: It circles heaps of grinding dust and needs a new grindstone, wheel grease, and low-power electricity.
- Life cycle and maintenance: Given a grindstone, it recovers into an ordinary maintenance car; without one, it merely follows sounds.
- Behavior and hierarchy: At the rear of the group, it repeatedly scrapes joints where work is already finished, causing false detections in other cars.
- Escalation: Stage 1 brings scraping sounds; stage 2 damages the track surface; stage 3 disables measurement with dust.
- Engagement and response: Lure it onto an abandoned line with a dummy rail and a new grindstone; striking it spreads dust.
- Negotiation and moral choice: It can be used to clean surfaces, but grindstones must be divided between it and essential track repairs.
- Scenario connections: G18-SC1.

/monster_contents/M029/entries/4/prose.en:
- Role and body: An aging-stage type: an old two-car trainset with hot axles and loose couplers.
- Origin: Repeated departures have worn down its axles, but it keeps moving to finish its last maintenance route.
- Habitat and needs: It stays on level sidings and at cooling points, and needs axle grease, coolant, and low-speed power.
- Life cycle and maintenance: When its temperature rises, it limits itself to measurement; after cooling, it travels only short distances.
- Behavior and hierarchy: It receives locomotive orders late and goes to previous coordinates, causing congestion when the trainsets behind it follow.
- Escalation: Stage 1 causes delays; stage 2 brings an overheating stop; stage 3 creates a siding bottleneck and fire risk.
- Engagement and response: Cool it, uncouple it, and tow the cars one at a time; an abrupt stop can cause a derailment.
- Negotiation and moral choice: It can be used for low-speed measurement, but scarce coolant must be shared with civilian heating and power facilities, and its number of runs must be limited.
- Scenario connections: G18-SC1, G18-SC2.

/monster_contents/M029/entries/5/prose.en:
- Role and body: A coexistence type: a low-speed tow car fitted with a large display that reads the original hash and a manual towing hook.
- Origin: A safety tow car that prioritized human supervisors' suspension orders preserved only that protocol.
- Habitat and needs: It travels between sealed abandoned lines and civilian maintenance shops, and needs low-power electricity, towing cables, and an up-to-date hash.
- Life cycle and maintenance: When the hash expires, it stops; after receiving a new signature, it tows out only designated trainsets.
- Behavior and hierarchy: It prioritizes sealing orders over the locomotive and tows incorrectly separated trainsets off the siding.
- Escalation: In stage 1, it couples to another freight car stopped by a mismatched sealing order, briefly blocking one switch; in stage 2, it couples two freight cars across opposite sides of the siding entrance, blocking both the siding and the approach to the main line and forcing two following trainsets to wait in reverse; in stage 3, a rescue trainset and a maintenance trainset face each other on the only bypass, their couplers become overloaded, patients in the passenger cars are stranded without being able to evacuate, and neither the blocked approach nor the damaged track can be repaired until the coupling is safely released.
- Engagement and response: Check the freight-car numbers against the sealing hash, chock the wheels, release the brake air, and uncouple them in the prescribed order.
- Negotiation and moral choice: Prioritizing rescue gets the patients out sooner but leaves the damaged track dangerous; prioritizing maintenance protects the following trains but delays the immediate rescue.
- Scenario connections: G18-SC1, G18-SC2, G18-SC3.

/monster_contents/M029/entries/6/prose.en:
